textes.Au sommet du Grand Temple, offrir une ja: At the top of the Great Temple, offer a jar of rain to Tlaloc (blue shrine) and copal to Huitzilopochtli (red shrine)
textes.Au sommet du Mont Fusain: At the summit of Mount Charcoal
textes.Au sommet du Temple de Kukulkan, mettre: At the top of the Temple of Kukulkan, set the two calendar wheels to the date of the creation of the world (the great stele on the square shows it; Ah Kin, the astronomer, knows it)
textes.Au sommet du massif, il y a un endroit d: At the top of the massif, there's a spot where you can see both your islands at once. I mapped it. On a shell, naturally.
textes.Au stand, Momo fait les comptes sur une: At the stall, Momo does the accounts on a plank with a bit of charcoal. One evening he showed me: “Necklaces sold: nine. Bananas given away: forty-two.” He looked very sad. I gave him a banana. He laughed. And he wrote: “forty-three”.
textes.Au top ! Tant que la mer est là et que l: Top form! As long as the sea's here and people are dancing, I'm mixing.
textes.Au top. La mer est calme, aucun noyé, et: Top form. The sea's calm, nobody's drowned, and I've done five hundred press-ups.
In the village where I grew up.
textes.Au village, il y a Sylwen et son pain de: In the village there's Sylwen and her honey bread, Aëlwen and her potions, Faelar and his stories… Go and see them, they're all waiting for you.
textes.Au-delà, il n'y a plus que la mer et les: Beyond this there's only the sea and the clouds: turn back!
textes.Au-dessus de la porte, en lettres de feu: Above the door, in letters of fire: “YOU WHO ENTER HERE, KEEP HOPE (AND TAKE A COAT).” Lower down, smaller: “The ferryman only accepts obols. No coins with holes.”
textes.Au-dessus de mon trône, il y a une phras: Above my throne, there's a sentence carved in stone: “The king is the most handsome of dwarves.” Hilda told me Croâ had said it. I had it carved that very day. Nori looked at it for a long time and murmured: “That's not raven.” I don't care. It's carved.
textes.Au-dessus de sa porte, il y a une grande: Above his door, there's a big sword with blue glints. Every time I walk past, I look the other way. One day, I looked the other way so hard I walked into a bench. He was on his doorstep. He didn't laugh. He went “Hm”. That's worse.
None! Well, one. A teeny one.
textes.Aucun ne brille encore. Il faudra sans d: None are shining yet. You'll probably need to wake the crystal in each wing.
textes.Aucun pour l'instant. Rendez service, et: None yet. Help people out, and they will remember it.
None. Well, one. A teeny one.
textes.Aucun. Et ne recommence pas avec tes bou: None. And don't start again with your buoys.
textes.Aucune pour l'instant. La première t'att: None yet. The first one may be waiting for you under the village…
textes.Aucune quête en cours. Parlez aux habita: No quest in progress. Talk to the locals: many of them need help.
textes.Aujourd'hui : cartes postales, coquillag: Today: postcards, painted shells, kites and snow globes. The post office is waging a postcard war on me, the postwoman gives me smiles: I no longer know who's winning. In the evening, I beat Lucas at cards at the Perroquet. Inès looks down on my shells. And little Théo, whose kite flew away. That made my heart heavy. Half price, but heavy.
textes.Aujourd'hui : douze lits par jour. La se: These days: twelve beds a day. Room seven, the newlyweds. Room twelve, the Lord, where you have to dust mountains of knick-knacks. The professor's, with his drawing under the pillow. This morning I found a pearl under a bed! Well, a button. I put it in my pension box. There are already savings in it. And three buttons.
textes.Aujourd'hui ? Colette, à qui je prédis u: Today? Colette, to whom I predict a great love every year, this time “come from beyond the seas”. Hortense, to whom I promised a stranger who will make the clock ring. The tourist on the beach and her “someone who walks a lot”. And Félix, the bookseller, who writes everything down in a notebook to catch me out. He's found three that came true. It makes him ill.
textes.Aujourd'hui ? Les daurades de Fernand, l: Today? Fernand's sea bream, Rosalie's fish, when she's not selling me yesterday's. Margaux's bread, whose croissants I steal. No, I'm joking. Gérard, who has the bouillabaisse every lunchtime and talks about buying bigger trousers. The newlyweds, the evening they had dinner without saying a word to each other. And me in the middle, singing louder than the pot.
textes.Aujourd'hui, Gunnar garde mon trône, Ori: These days, Gunnar guards my throne, Ori writes my decrees, Hilda's ravens bring me the news, and Ulfa waters down my fizz. I lose my crown every day. It's on my head. Gunnar tells me so with great delicacy. He's a good guard.
textes.Aujourd'hui, Perlée arrose, Noisette com: Today Perlée waters, Noisette counts her seeds, Lumi lights up our evenings, and Zéphyr carries our letters faster than the wind, if you believe him. Far below, on a beach, a human called Lulu watches over our mushrooms. Thanks to her, travellers like you come all the way up here. It had been so long.
These days, a hundred dwarves, a hundred stomachs. Dwalin, my godson, brings me coal and leaves with two bowls. Sigrun brews her fizz in my old oven. Bramm has his noon bowl, Borin his eleven o'clock ladleful, and Hilda sells me her cheese, which is alive. I see everything. I feed everything.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'accorde les clochettes de: These days I tune the crystal bells, I write everything down in my big book and I set riddles for whoever passes by. Brindille never gets them, Pimprenelle answers before I've finished, Mélisse demands three bottles from me. And Grommelot grumbles. I write down the grumbles too. A memory doesn't pick and choose.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai deux îles. Celle de l': Today, I have two islands. The Mother Tree's, where Sylwen always keeps a honey loaf for me and Nimiel lies in wait with a hundred questions. And this one, where an old man waves his hat at the mist, and a blacksmith grumbles at the trees while stroking them. My mother says my heart is split in two. I think it has simply grown.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai dix mille rouleaux, un: Today, I have ten thousand scrolls, a cuttlefish who sells me her ink in exchange for songs, and three scrolls about you. Marée won't let me archive her recipes, Protée makes up history faster than I can write it, and Ondine asks me the questions I should have asked a thousand years ago. I'm swamped. It's wonderful.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai l'atelier à l'est de l: Today I've got the workshop east of the square, shelves full of lamps, and a shark who taunts me at the reef with my father's silver chisel in its jaws. I call him Mister Teeth. Triton listens to me grumble, Marée sells me her crackers, Ondine steals my offcuts. A rich life. Not in coins, alas.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai l'étal, les jardins au: Today I've got the stall, the gardens along the edge of the dome, and Pélagos watching me whenever I cut seaweed, as if I were stealing his children. Thalassa takes my long kelp, Ianthé dances in front of my shop to draw the customers. And you bring me fish from the surface! Business has never been better.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai la forge de la terrass: These days, I've got the terrace forge, Brunna on the bellows, and an apprentice, Fundin, who's got a hole in his head. I even had a big'un once: Hector, three years on coal before he touched a hammer. And at eleven o'clock, I go and taste Dagna's stew. To check the salt. Somebody has to.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai ma boutique dans mon c: Today I've got my shop in my mushroom. Zéphyr pays me in feathers, Cardamome in riddles, Pimprenelle in advice about sugar, and Grommelot pays me nothing at all, since he never buys anything. Thank goodness for big folk like you, {surnom}, with real coins in their pockets.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai mon échoppe dans la Gr: These days, I have my shop in the Great Hall, next to the Royal Forge. Every evening, I count my rubies: one is missing. It's Ulfa. I pretend I don't know. Ori keeps my ledgers, Grimli brings me stones he can never say where he found, and the king comes to admire what he doesn't pay for.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai quarante chèvres, douz: These days, I've got forty goats, twelve crows and some golems who make the whole lot of them nervous. Kalda brings back the goats that climb too high. Dagna and Ulfa buy my cheese. The king sends me crows at midnight. And Bramm serves as a rock. Everyone in their place.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai soixante-dix ans, un b: Today, I'm seventy, I've a griddle that's hot from nine o'clock, and a tavern full every night. I count Corentin's hot honeys with beans, I keep the first crêpe for Fañch, and I let Pierrick believe he's the boss. The rest of the time, I sing. Off-key. But loud.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai trente ruches au pied: Today I have thirty hives at the foot of the tree-houses. My girls, I call them. They forage the lime trees, the clover and Miriel's roses, which annoys Miriel. I take honey to Sylwen every morning, and to Aëlwen, who haggles. The wild bees, right at the top of the Mother Tree, I never go up to.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai trente-deux hamacs, je: Today, I've got thirty-two hammocks, I recount them every evening, and they're less than fifty years old. Ewen ties knots in them, Salomé rents out seaweed sacks in the hold to steal my customers, and Matthias drew me a meadow that doesn't move, for later. My aunt pretends not to know anything. She knows everything.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ouvre à dix heures et je: Today, I open at ten and close at one in the morning. Django on stage, Lola between the tables, Hector at the end of the counter, the Lord who pays in gold, and Kiki, my punch rival, who comes for a drink at my place after closing his. And a mystery: the jungle boat doesn't stop at mine anymore. Strange, eh?
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'écris tout : les décrets: These days I write everything: the king's decrees, Kalda's reports, Orsik's ledgers, the slates at the Blazing Mug. Three hundred and twelve decrees in ninety years of reign. The shortest: “No.” The longest is about fizz. I correct the mistakes. The king doesn't like it. The city does.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'élève Gland avec Mamie Fa: These days, I'm raising Gland with Granny Faîne, while Mum and Dad are in the deep forest. I mend the bridges, I climb up for wild honey for Grelot, three stings and a smile, and for golden acorns from the oldest oaks, which Plumette adores. I buy Ursule's nails. Her axes, though… brrr. You don't cut down a living tree!
textes.Aujourd'hui, je bouche les trous, je man: These days, I plug holes, I eat the pancake Gwenola slips into my pocket, and I listen to Jos hammering above my head. Lucie tells me where it's seeping, under the hull. Ewen asks me how you put a ship back in the water. And my daughter, Nolwenn, sews at her window till midnight. I see her lamp. I say nothing.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je connais chaque client à: These days, I know every customer by their cup. Odette has her table facing the port, woe betide any tourist who sits there. The mayor comes by at noon, Colette at seven, the professor in the morning, silent as a fish. And when Raymond loses at pétanque, he comes here to sulk, in front of a coffee he doesn't drink. I see everything. It's the job.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je donne mon cours sur la p: These days, I teach my class on the square every day at four. I've still got the cat, and now Zoé, who learns fast. The kids prefer Titou's show on the other side of the fountain, but I'm not giving up. And once a week I take the boat for Fanny's croissants. Cheerful, I tell you!
textes.Aujourd'hui, je donne une deuxième vie a: These days, I give old sails a second life: red and blue awnings, curtains for homes, bags, hammocks for Pierrick. Jos forges my needles, Lucie gives me a pearl every birthday, and Salomé resells my offcuts for three times the price. And every day, I watch the ship's original great sail fall to tatters under the yard.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je fais des haches, des pel: These days, I make axes, shovels, corsair sabres for the caravanners who like dressing up, and needles for Nolwenn. Tobias complains about the noise above his head. In the evening, I have a sparkling apple by the beach fire or at Gwenola's counter. And I dream of a piece of metal nobody knows.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je fais l'aller-retour entr: These days, I go back and forth between the village and Port-Azur, five coins one way. At night, I steer by Anselme's lighthouse: two lantern calls, two flashes in reply. Little Nina rings the departure bell. Lola, my passenger who never went back, gives me her letters for her mother. And every evening, as I come alongside, I look for Hortense on the promenade. She's always there.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je garde l'entrée. Orophin: These days I guard the entrance. Orophin runs the forest for me. Sylwen leaves me bread. Caelan plays. All night. Gilwen nags me about her bees, Haldir never tells me where he's going, and Ilyria says “luck” when I hit an apple. I keep an eye on them all. It's to keep them safe. They don't know that.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je garde les racines, je ch: These days I guard the roots, I chase off the will-o'-the-wisps and I look after my fireplace. With crystal shards. For the warmth. The glitter-gnat wants to buy them off me, the sky thief digs holes, the magician turns me into a frog. Brindille, now, she says hello. That's my lot. Bah.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je gouverne des fuites, des: These days, I govern leaks, neighbours' quarrels and the price of sparkling apple. Tobias swears the hull will hold, Grégoire keeps watch, Matthias dreams of opening what would be better left shut, and Ewen rings the bell whenever he likes. In the evening, on the poop deck, I watch Stoneheart turn red. It reminds me I'm not in command of everything.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je me lève avant Clou, ce q: These days, I get up before Clou, which isn't hard: he sleeps on the cash box. I beat iron until noon, I sell in the afternoon, I count in the evening. Clou means “nail”: I named him after my first one. Bent, but he holds. Customers climb up, complain about the prices, buy anyway. That's enough for me. Almost.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je mixe nuit et jour, ou pr: These days, I mix night and day, more or less: when I sleep for two hours, Tchoum minds the decks and nobody can tell the difference. There's Zoé who cries at sunrise, Lulu who says the fairies are listening, Momo who jumps, Nono who creaks. I compose for them. “Low Tide” is all their hearts together, a hundred and forty-five times a minute.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je photographie la teuf tou: These days, I photograph the party every night. Nono turning into a wave, Lulu looking like a fairy, Titou who's never in focus. I buy glow sticks by the box in Port-Azur. I never have enough: people borrow them, throw them, lose them in the sea. Especially Titou. Him most of all.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je plonge le matin et je da: These days, I dive in the morning and dance at night. Dancing is like swimming: you let yourself be carried, you don't fight the current. Zoé's learning to dive with me; she swallows half the bay and laughs. Every week Mistral asks me when I'll go to Atlantis. I tell him: when I've danced enough.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je porte les lettres de Per: These days, I carry Perlée's letters to her sister, Mélisse's crates of nectar, seeds for Noisette and the queen's petals for a human lady on the beach. And did you know there's a big balloon named after me, on the big island to the east? A balloon that puffs smoke! And slow, too. I've been offended ever since it existed.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je pêche de cinq heures à m: These days I fish from five till noon, sleep in the afternoon, and dance at night. I make the earplugs myself, out of candle wax, and give them to the newcomers. Rule number one, always. I'm thirty-two and I still haven't found a rule number three. As we say round here: two is already plenty.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je raconte au cercle, sous: These days, I tell stories at the circle, under the garlands. Nimiel is always in the front row, Orophin goes off to check my stories in the forest, Rúmil listens while mending his nets. And when the wind blows from the west, I can hear Barnabé singing on his beach. Sometimes I fall asleep in the middle. They put a flower on my nose.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je recolle les genoux de Ni: These days, I patch up Nimiel's knees, I make Faelar drink his herbal teas and I listen to Caelan sigh, one hand on his heart, the other on my counter. Ilyria leaves me flowers on the sly. I pretend I don't know who. And yes, I count my coins. Potions don't grow on their own.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je soigne les genoux d'Ewen: These days, I patch up Ewen's knees, the fishermen's sunburns and the headaches the morning after a big feast. Lucie brings me my seaweed, Corentin hides his hot honey drinks in my storeroom, and Pierrick comes to see me about illnesses he makes up. Well… almost all made up.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je tisse les capes, les voi: These days I weave the cloaks, the sails and the ribbons for the festivals. Nessa wears out one ribbon a season, Aëlwen pretends not to see my flowers, Thalion keeps watch over the square, and I keep watch over Thalion. From up here I can see the whole village. Everything. Even a musician practising the same line, all alone, in front of the fountain.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je travaille à la capitaine: These days, I work at the harbour master's office, under the Admiral's eye, on a map two metres wide. The coasts are finished, or nearly: they move. In the middle, there's still a big blank, Stoneheart. Lucie brings me her stones, Corentin his stories, Grégoire his lights. I write it all down. Even what doesn't add up. Especially that.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je trie mes graines le soir: These days, I sort my seeds in the evening with Lumi's fireflies, Perlée waters my pots, and the queen lets me plant things just about everywhere. Even where I shouldn't: there's a sprout growing in her crown. And in my pocket, I've got my treasure. Nobody knows. Don't look at my pocket. Stop looking at my pocket!
textes.Aujourd'hui, l'après-midi, je fais le cl: These days, in the afternoons, I clown around on the village square for the kids. I juggle coconuts, I fall on purpose, I invent dance steps: the lovestruck crab, the shy octopus. And at night, the party is my own show. Nobody watches me, everybody dances. That's what's great about it. Yo!
textes.Aujourd'hui, la Chope Ardente est pleine: These days, the Blazing Mug is packed every night. The king sings off-key, Bramm drinks from his father's mug, Nori drinks WATER, and I hide one of Orsik's rubies a night in the empty barrel at the back. The stew comes from Dagna's, the cheese from Hilda's. And me, I make the noise!
textes.Aujourd'hui, le jour, je vends mes colli: These days, in the daytime, I sell my necklaces at the village market, on a stall with Marley and his bananas. At night, I dance and jump, every night a little higher than the night before. I have contests with Titou, I make Zoé laugh, I borrow stuff from Bastien. And Sofia brings me shells from the bottom of the sea. The good life, bro.
textes.Aujourd'hui, le matin, je soigne mes ban: These days, in the morning, I look after my banana trees, I talk to them like Barnabé does. In the daytime, I run the market stall with Momo. And at night, I dance, with bananas for everyone. Fanny still won't have banana croissants. But I'm not giving up hope. Family always ends up tasting. What else?
textes.Aujourd'hui, les runes de garde s'efface: These days, the guardian runes are fading, the mountain rumbles and the golems no longer recognise anyone. Ori, my great-nephew, copies down everything I say. The king comes down to ask me about the future. Ulfa asks me why I drink water. I give them all the same answer: patience.
textes.Aujourd'hui, mon étal est pile en face d: Today, my stall is right opposite the breach onto the beach: you come in, you bump straight into it, that's on purpose. I sell everything that floats, everything that shines, and two or three things that do neither. Lucie brings me her pearls, Jos his sabres, Nolwenn her canvas offcuts. And Matthias still won't take my key.
textes.Aurélien Lumen m'apprendra le sort de lu: Aurélien Lumen will teach me the light spell if I bring him three moon shards that fell on the island. Then I'll have to awaken the runes in the Crypt.
textes.Autrefois la cloche réglait toute la vie: Once, the bell ruled the whole life of the town: market at eight, siesta at one, aperitif at seven. Especially the aperitif.
textes.Autrefois, avant que la porte de l'Arbre: Long ago, before the door of the Mother Tree closed, Faelar used to come down into the roots. He'd trade a story for a riddle. His stories were so long that I set him three riddles while he was telling them, and he solved them without ever stopping talking. It was infuriating. It was marvellous.
textes.Autrefois, les quatre peuples de l'île s: Long ago, the island's four peoples met in the centre, in front of the great gate, once a year. We sang, we swapped, we danced. Then the gate closed, with its four seals. Nobody quite knows why any more. The stories have forgotten.
textes.Aux commandes du Glisseur stellaire: At the controls of the Star Glider
textes.Aux pieds d'Ehécatl : la tablette du Sol: At the feet of Ehécatl: the tablet of the Sun of the Wind… and a large pink conch, the god's conch. When you blow into it, the wind rises.
textes.Avalé par une grenouille (et recraché): Swallowed by a frog (and spat out)
textes.Avant chaque course, Caramel m'attend au: Before every race, Caramel waits for me at the start. A skewer. The biggest on the stall. “For the paws,” she says. … I eat it. Always. The only time I forgot it, I fell. … Caramel says it's not connected. I'm not sure.
textes.Avant chaque course, je lui garde la plu: Before every race, I save her the biggest skewer on the stall. It brings luck, everyone knows that. The only time she forgot it, two years ago, she fell at the root bend. I'm not saying it's connected. I'm saying that, since then, I watch her eat down to the last bite. Mrrr.
textes.Avant chaque départ, Nina inspecte L'Hir: Before each departure, Nina inspects the Swallow, hands behind her back, with my old cap on her head. It falls over her nose. She checks the knots, the lifebuoys, the bench. Once, she told me, very seriously: “Captain, your boat needs a seventh coat of paint.” She was right.
textes.Avant de le perdre, il montait au belvéd: Before he lost it, he used to come up to the lookout to photograph my easel. Not the view: my easel, my unfinished canvas, my hand. Click, click. He says a photo “keeps” things. I told him that mostly it kept my mistakes. He laughed. He showed me the photo, later. Blurry. That, at least, was artistic.
textes.Avant de le perdre, j'avais photographié: Before I lost it, I'd photographed her painting. To keep it, as a souvenir. I had it developed: blurry. A blue smudge and a pink smudge. She looked at it for a long time and said: “It's the first time anyone's got my pink right.” I still don't know if it was a compliment.
textes.Avant de me prêter sa barque, Barnabé a: Before lending me his boat, Barnabé insisted on drawing a map of the route. Port-Azur to the beach: a straight line, I told him. It took him two days. There were reefs, two monsters, a whale, and a little cross where, according to him, “a rock might be badly placed”. We followed the map seventeen times. Not one rock.
textes.Avant de rentrer dans sa chambre, Sylvie: Before going into her room, Sylvie told me, very seriously, like a schoolteacher giving the lesson of the day: “Husbands get lost and get found. So do wedding rings.” I wrote it on the hotel notepaper. It's still in my bag.
textes.Avant j'étais surfeur. Puis j'ai découve: I used to be a surfer. Then I found out the waves in Port-Azur are thirty centimetres high. So now I rent boats.
textes.Avant l'aube, Lumi m'envoie dix lucioles: Before dawn, Lumi sends me ten fireflies to light my rounds. I thank each one by name. She thinks it takes too long. But her fireflies go back to her glowing brighter. She says they're showing off. I think they're simply happy.
textes.Avant l'aube, je prête dix lucioles à Pe: Before dawn, I lend Perlée ten fireflies so she can see her flowers. She thanks each firefly by name, one by one. It takes forever. My fireflies love it. They come back all proud, and they look at me as if I never thanked them.
textes.Avant le déluge, j'étais le plus petit c: Before the flood, I was the smallest copyist in the palace. Fourteen years old, fingers black with ink, and a master, old Themis, who rapped my knuckles whenever I rounded off a number. “History is not rounded off, Abyssos.” I've never rounded since. The dome is ninety-two paces across. Or ninety-three. I'm working on it.
textes.Avant le naufrage, Octave a ressemelé me: Before the shipwreck, Octave resoled my boots with the leather of his own belt. He held his trousers up with a rope until the end of the voyage. I never thanked him. The left one is at the bottom of the sea, but the right one is still going strong.
textes.Avant le soleil ! Comme une vraie lapine: Before the sun! Like a proper bunny! Drop by the bakery at five, I'll save you the first loaf, the one that's still crackling.
textes.Avant les araignées de cristal, Pimprene: Before the crystal spiders, Pimprenelle used to take me bouncing on the mushrooms in the cave. I was scared. She held my hand and we jumped together, right to the top. I laughed so much I cried, and my tears bounced on the mushrooms. It's my loveliest memory.
textes.Avant les araignées, j'emmenais Brindill: Before the spiders, I used to take Brindille bouncing on the mushrooms in the cave. She was scared, so I held her hand. Right at the top she laughed so much she cried, and her tears bounced on the mushrooms, plip, plop! I've never seen anything so pretty. Not even my sparks.
textes.Avant ma traversée, Salomé m'a vendu un: Before my crossing, Salomé sold me an “indestructible” bag. It split on the second day, in the highlands. I carried everything in my shirt for two months. When I got back, she refunded me down to the last coin, and gave me a new bag. Free. I've never understood why.
textes.Avant moi, c'était la vieille Angélique: Before me, old Angélique kept the kingdom's memory. She was getting forgetful, so she hid every story in a riddle so as not to forget it. When she fell asleep for good, I inherited a thousand riddles and not a single answer. It took me a hundred years to find the stories inside them.
textes.Avant mon départ, elle m'a donné un sach: Before I left, she gave me a little bag of herbs: “Half for the Tree, the other half for you, on the evenings when you cry.” I gave it all to the Tree. She knows. She's been pretending to be cross ever since.
textes.Avant que Marius embarque avec moi, on p: Before Marius came aboard with me, we already fished in the evenings at the end of the jetty, him and me. Anselme would come and lie on the warm stones and count the stars, under his breath. Marius would shout to him: “And the fish, are you counting those?” Anselme would answer: “Three hundred and twelve.” Stars. He never looked at the water.
textes.Avant sa grande traversée, j'ai interdit: Before his great crossing, I forbade Le Goff to go near Stoneheart. He came back two months later, barefoot, saying he'd seen nothing there because of the fog. That day, Grégoire logged sunshine over the whole island. I said nothing. A man has the right to have been afraid.
textes.Avant sa grande traversée, je lui ai ven: Before his great crossing, I sold him an “indestructible” bag. It split after two days. When Matthias came back, barefoot, thin, his twelve journals clutched inside his shirt, I refunded him and gave him a new bag. He asked why. I said: “Advertising.” It wasn't the advertising.
textes.Avant, Pépin s'entraînait au tambour dan: Pépin used to practise the drum in the south tree, right under my window. Boom, boom-boom, the night before races! I complained. He moved his drum behind Trèfle's bakery. Now the bread rises in rhythm, and I get to sleep. Hop. Everybody wins.
textes.Avant, elle s'appelait Églantine. C'étai: She used to be called Églantine. She was our queen… The brambles took her heart.
textes.Avant, j'habitais une grande ville du co: Before, I lived in a big city on the mainland, on the fifth floor, with a view of a wall. I sorted papers in an office. I started loads of things: piano, pottery, Spanish. I never finished any of them. My mother used to say: “Zoé, you're a weathervane.” She wasn't wrong.
textes.Avant, j'étais cartographe du roi. J'ai: I used to be the king's cartographer. I drew a map of this kingdom so precise it was as big as the kingdom itself. Nobody ever unfolded it.
textes.Avant, j'étais une moitié de goutte. Ma: I used to be half a drop. My sister Perlée and I were one single drop of dew, on a leaf of Yggdrasil, way up high. A gust of wind split us in two. Perlée stayed on the leaf. I fell down through the clouds… all the way into the roots of the Mother Tree.
textes.Avant, je vendais des glaces. Des glaces: Before, I sold ice creams. Ice creams that melted before they reached your mouth: in fact, you drank them. And then fifteen years ago, Bruno turned up with his ice-cream maker. In one summer, everyone was going to him. He offered to go into business with me. I said no, out of pride, and opened Souvenirs d'Azur. Snow globes, at least, don't melt.
textes.Avant, la poignée de la tyrolienne était: The zip line handle used to be too high for me. I'd jump, miss, jump again. And one morning it was lower! Just my height! Croc-Gris said it was “for safety”. But I'm the only one who's that small. So it's for me. I said thank you. He said “Halt.”
textes.Avant, volcan dormait. Maintenant, volca: Before, volcano sleep. Now, volcano snore.
textes.Avec Félix comme navigateur. Je lui gard: With Félix as navigator. I'll save him the best seat, up front, with a bucket. A nice bucket, painted blue, just for him. A navigator deserves comfort.
textes.Avec Titou, on marque nos sauts sur le p: Titou and I mark our jumps on the palm tree, with shells pushed into the bark. One night I jumped so high I grabbed a coconut. It landed on my head right after. Titou said it didn't count. The shell is still up there, right at the top. Legend.
textes.Avec beaucoup de clous. Et de la bonne v: With lots of nails. And goodwill. Mostly nails.
textes.Avec du lait ? Ici ? … Vous m'avez bien: With milk? Here? … Did you hear me right? Fine. I'll put some in. A drop. And you don't tell a soul.
textes.Avec joie ! Que l'Aube nous garde… et qu: With joy! May the Dawn watch over us… and over my feet too, I trip a lot. Let's go!
textes.Avec la pelle, cherche les petites croix: With the shovel, look for the little wooden crosses on the sand. Castaways hid their savings there. It glints a bit, up close.
textes.Avec le soleil, c'est raisonnable. Le so: With the sun, that's reasonable. The sun keeps a lazy lord's hours, but still. You'll get bread from the second batch. It's very good too.
textes.Avec les intérêts ? Il va falloir lever: With interest? I'll have to raise a tax.
textes.Avec les intérêts. Je ne fais pas crédit: With interest. I don't give credit.
textes.Avec mes daurades d'hier, Paulo ?: With my day-old sea bream, Paulo?
textes.Avec moi ? Non : à ta place. Un guerrier: With me? No: in my place. A jaguar warrior against jaguars, Cuauhtli finds that far too funny, he won't let me go. The slopes of Smoking Mountain, to the west, under the pines. When a jaguar crouches, it's about to pounce: step aside, then strike.
textes.Avec mon chronomètre, j'ai tout mesuré d: With my stopwatch, I measured everything in the bakery. The all-time record is Mochi: a whole mooncake in two minutes, hidden behind a flour sack. I shouted “New record!” far too loud, and Trèfle came in. Mochi looked at me as if I'd betrayed her. Which was true.
textes.Avec ta pelle sur l'épaule, tu as l'air: With that shovel on your shoulder, you look like a real treasure hunter. Found anything?
textes.Avec ta voix d'aujourd'hui ! Chante un p: With your voice of today! Sing a little, so the pot can hear you.
textes.Avec tes dents de requin, j'ai taillé le: With your shark teeth, I carved the finest flippers in the city.
textes.Avec tes plumes, j'ai fait un manteau po: With your feathers, I made a coat for Croâ, my oldest raven.
textes.Avec ton miel, j'ai brassé l'hydromel de: With your honey, I brewed Forgefer's honey drink. The king drank a whole barrel.
textes.Avec ton minerai, je t'ai forgé une épée: With your ore, I forged you a dwarven sword. My best of the year.
With a straw. Not with a ladle.
textes.Avec une pelle ? Il faut une hache pour: With a shovel? You need an axe to fell this tree.
textes.Avec une pelle, on trouve de tout dans l: With a shovel, you'll find all sorts in the beach sand: shells, castaways' coins… I sell shovels, you know. Just saying.
textes.Avec ça, tu vas faire des jaloux. Surtou: With that, you'll make people jealous. Especially the neighbour. The neighbour gets jealous of everything.
textes.Aventurier de rang S, légende de la Guil: Rank S adventurer, legend of the Guild
textes.AÏE ! Dans MA cabane ?! Les prix doublen: OUCH! In MY hut?! Prices are doubling!
textes.AÏE ! La lave ! Tu bondis hors du cratèr: OUCH! The lava! You leap out of the crater, clutching your backside.
textes.Aëlwen ! Mon miel. Au prix du miel, cett: Aëlwen! My honey. At honey prices, this time.
textes.Aëlwen ! Regarde, je n'ai même pas une é: Aëlwen! Look, I haven't got a single scratch!
textes.Aëlwen achète mon miel pour ses potions,: Aëlwen buys my honey for her potions, and she haggles over every drop. But the night of my three hundred stings, she looked after me until morning without counting the cost. That's how she is.
textes.Aëlwen est une bonne guérisseuse et une: Aëlwen is a good healer and a terrible trader. She treats my daughter's knees almost for free, and she pays me for moonflowers as if they were dandelions.
textes.Aëlwen m'a soignée cent fois depuis ma n: Aëlwen has healed me a hundred times since I was born. Her potions are bitter and her hands are gentle: you have to take both together.
textes.Aëlwen me fait trier ses graines pendant: Aëlwen makes me sort her seeds while she patches me up: red ones on one side, black ones on the other. That way I keep still. One day I found a blue seed in the pile. She gave it to me: “Plant it and see what it turns into.” It's in a pot on my windowsill. It isn't growing yet.
textes.Aëlwen me soigne depuis trois siècles, e: Aëlwen has been looking after me for three centuries, and I look after her in return: I tell her stories while she works. She says it annoys her. She's never closed her door.
textes.Aëlwen soigne mes genoux. Ses potions so: Aëlwen patches up my knees. Her potions are disgusting, but she always has a honey sweet in her pocket. I hide my footbridge climbing from her. She knows. She knows EVERYTHING.
textes.Aëlwen soigne mon cœur deux fois par sem: Aëlwen treats my heart twice a week. She says there's nothing wrong with it. She's mistaken: it has Ilyria. She charges me anyway, and she's quite right to.
textes.Aëlwen soigne tout le monde, et personne: Aëlwen looks after everyone, and nobody looks after her. So I leave her flowers, unsigned. She thinks I don't know she knows. We're very happy like that.
textes.Aëlwen soigne tout le monde, mais person: Aëlwen heals everyone, but nobody heals her. Bring her flowers, one day.
textes.Aëlwen vend des potions, Sylwen du pain: Aëlwen sells potions, Sylwen sells honey bread. And Faelar sells stories. For free. Lots of them.
Aëlwen, I have a story about mint.
textes.Aëlwen, mes fleurs de lune. Au prix just: Aëlwen, my moonflowers. At a fair price.
textes.Aëlwen, tu as des cernes. Tu as dormi ?: Aëlwen, you've got dark circles. Did you sleep?
textes.Aïcha ! Ton safran a encore augmenté ?: Aïcha! Has your saffron gone up again?
textes.Aïe ! L'Amirale va entendre parler de to: Ouch! The Admiral's going to hear about you!
textes.Aïe ! La lave brûle ! (Les démons, eux,: Ouch! The lava burns! (The demons soak their feet in it… you don't.)
textes.Aïe ! Mais t'es pas bien ?!: Ow! Are you out of your mind?!
textes.Aïe ! Mais… on ne frappe pas sous le dôm: Ow! But… nobody hits anyone under the dome!
textes.Aïe ! Mes oreilles se sont toutes hériss: Ouch! All my ears are standing on end! No hitting in Ramure!
textes.Aïe ! Pas dans la sauce : elle est brûla: Ouch! Not in the sauce: it's scalding! (And besides, it stains.)
textes.Aïe ! Qui a mis ce caillou ici ?: Ouch! Who put this pebble here?
textes.Aïe aïe aïe ! La lave du Phlégéthon ! Tu: Ow ow ow! The lava of the Phlegethon! You leap back onto the bank, your soles smoking. Take a raft next time.
textes.Aïe. Aïe aïe. Tu parles comme Bondi. Bon: Ouch. Ouch ouch. You sound like Bondi. Okay, fine. So this time I'll finish first. That way we'll both agree. I can feel it in my paws!
textes.BAC DES PIÈCES DÉTACHÉES\nNe pas tomber:
SPARE PARTS BIN
Do not fall in.
(The sorting robot would file you under “Miscellaneous”.)
textes.BIIIP. Le lecteur clignote en rouge : «: BEEEEP. The reader flashes red: “BADGE NOT DETECTED. Have you tried having a badge?” (Up there, on the back mezzanine, something is shining…)
textes.BIP BIP ! Un chariot élévateur robot te: BEEP BEEP! A robot forklift bumps into you: “FORKLIFTS HAVE PRIORITY. THANK YOU FOR YOUR UNDERSTANDING.” Look carefully before crossing the aisles.
textes.BIP. Surface propre à 97 %. Les 3 % rest: BEEP. Surface 97% clean. The remaining 3% is your shoes.
textes.BLORP ! (Il fait défiler les hologrammes: BLORP! (He flips through the holograms: a mayor sucking in his tummy, a tavern-keeper glaring, a baron with three hats, a crested granny raising her fist.) They're PERFECT! They're so… so Heavyfoot! I'm sending everything to Mama! (Click-click-click. A long silence. Then the device goes “beep”.) She replied! She says: “My Glorb, you have friends!” … (He wobbles very hard.) I have friends. Here, my kaleidoscope glasses: with them, you see the world like I do. In a thousand pieces, and all of them pretty.
textes.BLOUOP ! Le Roi Gélatineux retombe de to: BLOOP! The Jelly King slams back down with all his weight: the ground shakes!
textes.BONK ! L'Alouette heurte l'obstacle et s: BONK! The Alouette hits the obstacle and folds up all at once… The harness spring set you down gently. Nothing broken!
textes.BOOONG ! (Les adeptes disent qu'il ne fa: BOOONG! (The followers say you must never strike it three times in a row. Nobody remembers why.)
textes.BOOONG ! Le grand couvercle de cuivre ré: BOOONG! The great copper lid rings out across the whole forecourt. Above the temple, the Great Flying Spaghetti wriggles all its noodles.
textes.BOOONG. Quelque part dans les gradins, q: BOOONG. Somewhere in the stands, someone shouts: “AGAIN!” (The champion is allowed.)
textes.BOOONG… BOOONG… BOOONG ! Le sol tremble: BOOONG… BOOONG… BOOONG! The ground trembles a little. Up above, Mount Bolognese starts to rumble… It sounds like it heard you.
textes.BOUM ! Le rocher t'aplatit comme une crê: BOOM! The boulder flattens you like a pancake (a very offended pancake). You peel yourself off the floor at the entrance of the corridor. Next time: an alcove!
textes.BOUM ! … Voilà, tout est par terre. Même: BOOM! … There, everything's on the floor. Even me, almost. Thanks, here, a cookie from our place. It floats too, careful.
textes.BOUM-BA-BOUM ! (Tout le Clan se met à da: BOUM-BA-BOUM! (The whole Clan starts dancing around the fire. Even Ougha. Especially Ougha.)
textes.BOUM. BOUM. BOUM. Tes coups résonnent da: BOOM. BOOM. BOOM. Your knocks echo through the mountain… A deep voice behind you: “No use knocking, big one. Nobody enters Forgefer without being invited.” It's Bramm, the guard. Talk to him.
textes.BOUUUUH ! … Hé. Tu n'as même pas eu peur: BOOOO! … Hey. You weren't even scared?
textes.BRAMM : « OUVREZ LA GRANDE PORTE ! » Un: BRAMM: “OPEN THE GREAT GATE!” A rumble, creaking chains… and the two iron doors slowly open onto the glow of the Forgefer forges.
textes.BRRRANG ! Une guitare saturée, une basse: BRRRANG! A fuzzed-out guitar, a rumbling bass: two musicians rehearse in the middle of the yurt, between the stove and an old amp.
textes.BZZT. Une lampe rouge clignote : « MONTE: BZZT. A red lamp flashes: “FREIGHT LIFT RESERVED FOR MANAGEMENT. Please defeat management first.”
textes.Ba Sidi ! Tu as encore du thé ? J'ai enc: Ba Sidi! Still got some tea? I've still got a story.
textes.Ba Sidi ! Tu as toujours mon livre, vieu: Ba Sidi! Still got my book, you old date thief?
textes.Ba Sidi dit que vous avez un tapis ancie: Ba Sidi says you have an old carpet that shows the way to the seal.
textes.Ba Sidi, le conteur de Tazira. Il a mon: Ba Sidi, the storyteller of Tazira. He has my book, he's always one story ahead of me, and his beard is longer. I'll never forgive him. I'm very fond of him.
textes.Ba Sidi, le conteur de la place de Tazir: Ba Sidi, the storyteller of the square in Tazira. A thousand and one stories, and he's only ever told a thousand. He keeps the last one for himself. I understand him better than anyone.
textes.Ba-da-boum, ba-da-boum ! Tu as trouvé le: Ba-da-boom, ba-da-boom! You found the rhythm of the Flower Camp.
Bah. Just asking for no reason.
textes.Bah… il n'y avait plus grand-chose dedan: Meh… there wasn't much left in it anyway.
textes.Baisse ton coude, d'abord. … Je n'ai rie: Lower your elbow first. … I didn't say anything.
textes.Barnabé ! Dix-sept traversées, pas un ro: Barnabé! Seventeen crossings, not one rock. A legend, oh yes!
textes.Barnabé ! Tu as encore salué la brume, h: Barnabé! You waved at the mist again last night.
textes.Barnabé ! Tu reviens mesurer la piste, c: Barnabé! Coming back to measure the dance floor tonight?
textes.Barnabé ? Le meilleur cartographe du roy: Barnabé? The best cartographer in the kingdom, according to him. The worst, according to the rock. We used to be friends. Used to is a long way back.
textes.Barnabé ? Un humain qui chante sur sa pl: Barnabé? A human who sings on his beach about exploits he never saw, to tunes he never learned. I adore it. I listen from afar. It's the right distance for Barnabé.
textes.Barnabé Coquillard ! Ta chanson a un cou: Barnabé Coquillard! Your song has one verse too many.
textes.Barnabé Coquillard… Un humain qui dessin: Barnabé Coquillard… A human who draws maps of things he has never seen. We are very fond of him. From a distance.
textes.Barnabé dessinait les cartes. Sa carte d: Barnabé drew the maps. His map said “open sea”. The sea said “rock”. I believed the map. Twenty-two years I've regretted it.
textes.Barnabé dit que sa carte des Anciens mon: Barnabé says his map of the Ancients shows “a golden eye in the east”. That's the Mother Tree. He has good eyes, for a human.
textes.Barnabé est passé hier soir. Il a fait t: Barnabé came by last night. He did three dance steps with Gaston on his shoulder and left again. Legend.
textes.Barnabé m'a donné un coin de terre contr: Barnabé gave me a patch of land for a few bunches. At night, he talks to my banana trees, he calls them his confidants. Me, I never listen. Well… almost never.
textes.Barnabé m'a prêté sa barque pour monter: Barnabé lent me his boat to build this wall, and he never asked me for a penny. Just that we say hello to Gaston. So we say hello to Gaston.
textes.Barnabé m'a tout appris des cabanes. Il: Barnabé taught me everything about huts. He talks a lot, he's sometimes wrong about the rocks, but his knots never give. Never.
textes.Barnabé parle à la mer comme à une vieil: Barnabé talks to the sea like an old friend. Humans say he's mad; the trees say he's kind. I believe the trees.
textes.Barnabé t'a parlé de moi ? Laisse-moi de: Barnabé told you about me? Let me guess: “it was Octave at the helm”. He's a broken record, that one.
textes.Barnabé, c'est une légende, frérot. Il a: Barnabé is a legend, bro. He did three dance steps at the party and swears he was measuring the dance floor. He recounts his shells when I walk past. I get it: we kind of do the same job.
textes.Basile Pinceau, le peintre du village, a: Basile Pinceau, the village painter, saw the pot of blue (no. 1) floating on the Rubbed-Out Pond the day after the Great Downpour. It got stuck on a giant water lily, far from the bank. Basile swims like a stone.
textes.Basile est à l'Étang Gommé, Lili sur la: Basile is at the Rubbed-Out Pond, Lili on the White Strand.
textes.Basile, j'ai repêché le pot de bleu !: Basile, I fished out the pot of blue!
textes.Basile, qu'est-ce que vous regardez dans: Basile, what are you looking at in the pond?
Bastien! Your octopus says good evening.
textes.Bastien ! Tu es encore tout rouge, mets: Bastien! You've gone all red again, put your cap on!
textes.Bastien ? Un pêcheur qui se lève tôt et: Bastien? A fisherman who gets up early and doesn't haggle too much. We get along: he fishes, I pay. Not much.
textes.Bastien distribue des bouchons d'oreille: Bastien hands out earplugs. In front of MY sound. As if it were too loud. … And he was right about the crab. That's worse.
Bastien talked to me about fishing. Two hours. Tides, bait, mackerel. I said three words: “Yeah.” “Ah.” “Right.” He said it was the best conversation of his life. … He's nice. He's tiring. Nice people are tiring.
textes.Bastien m'a tirée de l'eau le jour de la: Bastien pulled me out of the water on the day of the biggest fright of my life. I owe him that. But I won't come to the five o'clock fishing. Ever. He knows it.
textes.Bastien m'invite à la pêche de cinq heur: Bastien invites me to the five o'clock fishing every evening. I say no every evening. But when he's out at sea, I sometimes dive near his boat and leave a nice shell on his bench. He pretends not to know who it is. I pretend to believe him. We're very good at this, the two of us.
textes.Bastien ne croit pas aux fées. Il dit «: Bastien doesn't believe in fairies. He says “of course” the way you shut a door, and it makes me a bit sad. But he's never painted over my octopus. So deep down, he believes a little.
textes.Bastien voulait un petit poisson sur sa: Bastien wanted a little fish on his sail. I painted a big purple octopus, a protective one. He shouted. He says the fish are scared of it. But he's never repainted the sail. And the day Sofia came up white as a sheet from the golden point, it was my octopus that made her laugh. It protects, like I said.
textes.Bastien, c'est le meilleur porteur de pa: Bastien's the best basket carrier on the island, and the only boy I've ever knocked into the water. He's sweet. He blushes a lot. Too much sun, I think.
Bastien's a grumpy big brother. He lends me everything, even when he doesn't know it yet. His cap looks better on me than on him, but I give it back. Sometimes.
textes.Bastien, ce matin, tu as trouvé quelque: Bastien, did you find anything on your bench this morning?
textes.Bastien, frérot ! Je te rends ta casquet: Bastien, bro! I'm giving you your cap back!
textes.Bastien. Combien, la sardine, aujourd'hu: Bastien. How much for a sardine today?
textes.Battre Ventaile. Une fois. D'une plume,: Beat Ventaile. Once. By a feather, that'll do me. And then carry a letter so fast it arrives before it's written. The queen says it's impossible. The queen has never raced me.
textes.Battre son record à Dragon-Pixel: Beat your high score at Dragon-Pixel
textes.Bedaine ? Le tanuki le plus rusé de la f: Bedaine? The craftiest tanuki in the forest. After me. He says it's the other way round. We've been squabbling over the title forever, and frankly, it's what keeps me awake at the market.
textes.Bedaine a encore troqué un caillou contr: Bedaine swapped a pebble for a feather again, a feather for a vial… One day he'll swap the Mother Oak for a hazelnut.
textes.Bedaine laisse des traces partout. Beauc: Bedaine leaves tracks everywhere. Lots of tracks means he's doing his shopping. I hold two things against him. But he makes me laugh. That almost makes up for it.
textes.Bedaine vous troque ce caillou-qui-chant: Bedaine swaps you this singing pebble.
textes.Bedaine, c'est le maître du troc ! Il me: Bedaine is the swap master! He finds me singing-stones, I give him hazelnuts and bits of rope. His great chain of swaps starts with me. First link!
textes.Bedaine, le tanuki du Marché aux trocs,: Bedaine, the tanuki of the Barter Market, wants to teach you the Great Swap: a pebble that, swap after swap, becomes a treasure.
textes.Belle matinée, oui. Il faut en profiter: Lovely morning, yes. Best enjoy it before the heat.
textes.Belle mer, ce matin. Je dis ça au vent,: Lovely sea this morning. I'm saying that to the wind, mind.
textes.Belle. J'ai encore trouvé de la lavande: Lovely. I found lavender on my bench again.
textes.Belles ? Elles sont AFFICHE-NANTES ! … B: Nice? They're POSTER-PERFECT! ... Well. Pigment painted the rat, I printed the letters, and we argued about the colour for three hours. She wanted green, I wanted black. We went with green. The next Great Boucan has to be the biggest of all time, with people coming from everywhere! But our posters can't swim. You travel. You could carry three: one to Paulo, the cook of Port-Azur; one to Ulric, the innkeeper of Montjoie; and one to Tom the Fiddler, the musician at the Crâne Fendu, on Balafre. Great encounters start with a poster!
textes.Benvenuto, bienvenue ! Chez Paulo, la me: Benvenuto, welcome! Chez Paulo, the best bouillabaisse in the archipelago! The others are just soups.
textes.Bernard ? Soixante-sept ans, des mollets: Bernard? Sixty-seven, calves of steel and a stubbornness set in concrete. He doesn't run faster than I swim. But I admit he runs fast.
textes.Bernard court comme s'il avait un train: Bernard runs as if he had a train to catch. I'm very fond of him, and he worries me. He thinks I don't see him going round by the back alley.
textes.Bernard dit qu'il court plus vite que je: Bernard says he runs faster than I swim. Ridiculous. He runs faster than I run, that's all.
textes.Bernard défie quiconque de courir de la: Bernard challenges anyone to run from the fountain to the lighthouse in under a minute.
textes.Bernard joue avec nous l'après-midi. Il: Bernard plays with us in the afternoon. He points badly, but he runs well: every time a ball rolls too far, he sprints off to fetch it, shouting “hup hup hup”. Raymond and I don't bend down any more. Sometimes, to tease him, I pretend to run with him. Two steps. My knee goes hup too.
textes.Bernard, le coureur. Il fait trois tours: Bernard, the runner. He does three laps of the island a day, with a stopwatch. I did thousands with a satchel. Nobody ever timed me.
textes.Bernard, le coureur. Un retraité respect: Bernard, the runner. A respectable retiree who respects nothing, least of all my sign. He has the legs of a twenty-year-old and the cheek of a fifteen-year-old.
textes.Bernard. Il tape à ma porte à huit heure: Bernard. He knocks at my door at eight. I go to bed at six. Do the maths. I have.
textes.Beurk ! La grenouille t'a avalé…\n(Il fa:
Yuck! The frog swallowed you…
(It's pitch black, it smells of mud, and it's very, very sticky.)
textes.Bien ! J'ai trouvé une veine d'argent. J: Good! I found a vein of silver. Then I lost it again. But I found it!
textes.Bien ! Tout va bien ! Tant que ma tante: Good! All good! As long as my aunt isn't looking.
textes.Bien caché, un petit sac de pièces ! Le: Well hidden, a little bag of coins! The captain's treasure! (He's asleep. He'll never know his parrot talked.)
Nice and hot, just as it should be.
textes.Bien sûr ! Du cacao, du piment, un peu d: Of course! Cacao, chili, a little vanilla, and water. Sugar? What's sugar?
textes.Bien sûr ! On déterre, on déterre… Voilà: Of course! We dig, we dig… There! Grilled fish, coconut, and… oh no, that's a hot stone. Don't eat it. Well, if you want, but it crunches.
textes.Bien sûr que je me souviens de toi. Les: Of course I remember you. Elves forget nothing.
textes.Bien sûr que je me souviens. Les elfes n: Of course I remember. Elves forget nothing: sometimes that's a problem.
Of course. And I fish for whales.
textes.Bien sûr. J'ai le temps. Beaucoup de tem: Of course. I have time. Plenty of time.
textes.Bien, Amirale ! Neuf ! Et demi, des fois: Yes, Admiral! Nine! And a half, sometimes?
Yes, Admiral. A geographer. From very close up.
textes.Bien, bien, très bien. Le soleil, le son: Good, good, very good. Sun, beats, friends. What else is there?
Good, good. A rune smiled at me this morning. That doesn't happen often.
textes.Bien, merci. La lumière est douce aujour: Fine, thank you. The light is soft today.
textes.Bien, merci. La lumière ondule joliment,: Fine, thank you. The light ripples nicely today.
textes.Bien, monsieur le patron. Les vieux, à c: Very well, mister boss. The old ones, next to the chest. Not in the chest.
textes.Bien, mousse. Qu'est-ce que tu vois, à l: Good, cabin boy. What do you see on the horizon?
textes.Bien. Alors tu peux danser jusqu'au mati: Good. Then you can dance till morning.
textes.Bien. C'est ce qu'il faut faire. Tu fera: Good. That's what you should do. You'd make a passable guard. For a human. … Don't take it the wrong way, it's a compliment.
textes.Bien. C'est la bonne réponse. Les lanter: Good. That's the right answer. The moon lanterns on the bridges are put there by Mère-Lune. For exactly that. For those who can't read tracks.
textes.Bien. De quoi d'autre veux-tu parler ?: Good. What else would you like to talk about?
textes.Bien. De quoi d'autre voulez-vous parler: Good. What else would you like to talk about?
textes.Bien. Il fait chaud. Il fait toujours ch: Fine. It's hot. It's always hot. That's good.
textes.Bien. J'ai compté mes rubis : il en manq: Fine. I counted my rubies: one's missing. As usual.
textes.Bien. J'ai dormi dans les branches, et u: Well. I slept in the branches, and a bird woke me up singing out of tune. It was charming.
textes.Bien. J'ai touché une pomme à cent pas c: Fine. I hit an apple at a hundred paces this morning. Ilyria said it was luck. It was not luck.
textes.Bien. Le métier à tisser chante, le fil: Good. The loom is singing, the thread is soft. And the harp fell silent last night. Finally, a little quiet.
textes.Bien. Le noir, ce n'est que le jour qui: Good. The dark is only the day, sleeping. It doesn't bite.
Fine. The goats ate a barrel. An empty one, luckily.
textes.Bien. Les chèvres, c'est honnête : elles: Good. Goats are honest: they eat everything and they don't hide it. Don't tell Croâ, he'd sulk on the roof for three days.
textes.Bien. Les touristes sont polis cette sem: Fine. The tourists are polite this week. Except one, who asked for milk in his espresso. Here!
textes.Bien. On frappe, on attend, on dit qui o: Good. You knock, you wait, you say who you are. Like a dwarf. You knocked at my gate. I remember. Hard, too. Too hard.
textes.Bien. Sous l'eau, tout est calme. C'est: Fine. Underwater, everything's calm. It's on the surface that people talk too much.
textes.Bien. Te voilà apprenti d'Arcanelle. Éco: Good. So you're an apprentice of Arcanelle. Listen: six masters, six spells. Aurélien Lumen will teach you light, Pyra fire, Borée frost, Zéphyrine levitation, Théophraste telekinesis, and Mère Sauge healing. Each will ask you for something: magic isn't given, it's traded. When your spellbook has its six spells, come back to me.
textes.Bien. Très bien, même. J'ai vendu une pe: Good. Very good, even. I sold a shovel this morning. To you, maybe?
textes.Bien. Très bien. (Pyrus frappe le sol de: Good. Very good. (Pyrus strikes the ground with his pitchfork.) In the name of the Guard: thank you. Here, something to warm you up.
textes.Bien. Très bien. L'eau de la source du v: Good. Very good. Water from the village spring, I hope? It's the best, everybody knows. You can dance, then.
Good. Very good. The kick is clean.
textes.Bien. Très bien. Vous irez loin. Ceux qu: Good. Very good. You'll go far. People who don't count end up with buttons in their pockets instead of coins.
textes.Bien. Tu es bien le seul. Ewen me montre: Good. You must be the only one. Ewen shows me his scrapes three days later, once they've changed colour. Come whenever you like, I always have honey.
textes.Bien. Un bricoleur, c'est un futur clien: Good. A tinkerer is a future customer. A good tool changes everything, you'll see.
textes.Bien. Un peu trop bien, peut-être. Un bo: Good. A little too good, perhaps. A good sailor obeys. A very good sailor can recognise a bad order. Think about it.
textes.Bien. Vous aurez une ligne à vous dans l: Good. You'll have a line of your own in the register. And you'll respect the quay's hours, like everyone else. Even Fernand. Especially Fernand.
textes.Bien. Ça prend plus de temps, ça rate so: Good. It takes longer, it often goes wrong. But what you've mended, you know by heart. And you never throw it out again.
textes.Bien. … (Hector frappe, chauffe, frappe: Good. … (Hector hammers, heats, hammers again.) … There. A bronze cog, as precise as a captain's watch. Take it to Hortense.
textes.Bientôt… Tu parles comme un humain. Chez: Soon… You talk like a human. Where we live, “soon” means in fifty years. Well. If you say so. I'll iron my dress anyway.
textes.Bienvenue ! Chez nous, les poissons nage: Welcome! At our place, the fish swim all through the house: it's more cheerful. Want to feed them?
textes.Bienvenue ! Chez nous, on ne laisse pas: Welcome! Here, we never let a visitor leave without a glass of tea. The first glass is gentle as life…
textes.Bienvenue ! Je prépare le cacao. Le secr: Welcome! I'm preparing the cacao. The secret is the foam: you pour from one pot to the other, from very high. Want to try?
textes.Bienvenue ! Regarde tranquillement. Tu a: Welcome! Take your time and look around. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Bienvenue au Cabaret des Cailloux ! Tien: Welcome to the Pebble Cabaret! Here, listen to this one:
textes.Bienvenue au Café Feedback. Chocolat cha: Welcome to Café Feedback. Hot chocolate, three coins. Herbal tea, two coins. Melancholy is free. The jukebox only plays one song, but it's the right one.
textes.Bienvenue au Grand Concours de Grimaces: Welcome to the Great Grimace Contest! Watch closely, here we go: one, two, three… GRIMACE! … (All three pull… exactly the same face. The same one as always.) So? Who won?
textes.Bienvenue au Grand Hôtel des Embruns. Un: Welcome to the Grand Hotel des Embruns. A room with a sea view? They all have a sea view. That's the whole idea.
textes.Bienvenue au Perroquet Bleu ! Ici, la bo: Welcome to the Perroquet Bleu! Here the drinks are cool, the music is hot and the parrot is made of wood. What can I get you?
textes.Bienvenue au chantier, capitaine ! Ici,: Welcome to the shipyard, captain! Here we plane, nail, and tar… and dream of the open sea.
textes.Bienvenue au musée ! Enfin… chez moi. Ma: Welcome to the museum! Well… my home. But it's a museum. Have you seen my collection?
textes.Bienvenue chez le Disquaire ! Ici, il y: Welcome to the Record Shop! Here you'll find every record on the island. Vinyle lets me mind the shop when he goes out for some fresh air. Take your time.
textes.Bienvenue chez moi ! C'est petit, mais c: Welcome to my home! It's small, but it's warm and smells good.
textes.Bienvenue chez moi ! C'est tout rond, c': Welcome to my home! It's all round, it's all warm, and it smells lovely.
textes.Bienvenue chez moi ! Va dire bonjour à t: Welcome to my home! Go say hello to everyone. Even Grommelot. Especially Grommelot: he loves being ignored.
textes.Bienvenue chez un chevalier de Montjoie: Welcome to the home of a knight of Montjoie! I'm polishing my armor for the tournament. Want to help?
textes.Bienvenue dans la Guilde ! Le tableau de: Welcome to the Guild! The quest board is right behind you: four new contracts every day. Bring them back to me, I stamp them, and you go up in rank. And now that you're registered, the adventurers in the tavern might want to team up with you. Talk to Sister Pétronille, Violette and Sir Tancrède. All three of them have… a little problem.
textes.Bienvenue dans ma collection ! Deux mill: Welcome to my collection! Two thousand records. Pick one, I'll put it on the turntable.
textes.Bienvenue dans mon atelier ! Attention a: Welcome to my workshop! Watch out for the wires. And the sparks. And the cat. Want to help me test my machine?
textes.Bienvenue sur l'Île Al Dente !\nAu nord:
Welcome to Al Dente Island!
To the north: Mount Bolognese (it spits sauce).
To the west: the Colander Temple.
Please do not eat the signs.
textes.Bienvenue sur l'Île de Larsen !\nÀ l'oue:
Welcome to Larsen Island!
West: the Flower Camp.
East: Rainville (take an umbrella).
In the middle: the Main Stage.
textes.Bienvenue à La Forge du Canon ! Jos. Mon: Welcome to La Forge du Canon! Jos. My hearth is the old port-side cannon: I opened it up, filled it with bricks, and it heats better than a volcano. Need a blade?
textes.Bienvenue à l'auberge de La Dernière Bor: Welcome to the inn of La Dernière Bordée! Pierrick, innkeeper, at your service. A table? A hammock for the night? The hammocks are new. Well, they're less than fifty years old.
textes.Bienvenue à la Chope Ardente ! La seule: Welcome to the Blazing Mug! The only tavern under a volcano. Ulfa Chope-Pleine. A fizz? Two fizzes? The whole barrel?
textes.Bienvenue, bienvenue ! Souvenirs d'Azur: Welcome, welcome! Souvenirs d'Azur: postcards, painted shells, kites, and the finest snow globe collection in the archipelago. It never snows here, that's the funny part!
textes.Bienvenue, bienvenue au Marché de la Cal: Welcome, welcome to the Hold Market! Salomé, the best trader on the island. And the only one in Carène, but that changes nothing. Everything that floats, everything that shines, everything that sells!
textes.Bienvenue, bienvenue à Port-Azur, la per: Welcome, welcome to Port-Azur, the pearl of the archipelago! Aristide Bellanger, mayor for eighteen years, re-elected unanimously minus one vote. Colette's.
textes.Bienvenue, jeune ! Moi, je dansais déjà: Welcome, youngster! I was dancing on beaches back when your grandad was learning to walk.
textes.Bienvenue… Respire. Il reste un tapis, l: Welcome… Breathe. There's one mat left, the yellow one, by the door. Sit down, close your eyes, and listen to the wind on the canvas. Want to try?
textes.Bip ! Je fais comme Zéro. Bip !: Beep! I'm doing like Zéro. Beep!
textes.Bip, bip… clonk ! Synthé-Soda goût fruit: Beep, beep… clonk! Moon-fruit flavor Synth-Soda. Nobody knows what Moon fruits taste like.
textes.Bip-bip ! Le lecteur passe au vert : « B: Beep-beep! The reader turns green: “WELCOME, ROBOT NO. … ERROR … WELCOME ANYWAY.” The door sinks into the floor. Below, something very big breathes like an engine.
Beep. This furniture no longer belongs to you. Beep.
textes.Biscotte ! (Le petit rat saute de ton ép: Biscotte! (The little rat hops from your shoulder to his, nibbles his ear, then goes back to yours.) See? He chose you. He always goes back to your shoulder. (Petit-Pierre sniffles.) It's okay. He'll be better off with you, travelling, than here with Mange-Clous and his ladle. He's very clever, you know: when he disappears down a hole, he always comes back with something. A coin, a button, a pearl… Rats know where the treasures are. Here, my cabin boy's coins. And if you don't have a whistle yet to call your animals, take this one: Gwen carved it for me from a bone, with a dog, a cat, a rat and a pig carved around it. Whistle, and Biscotte will come back. And you'll come see me again, right? With him?
textes.Biscotte arrive en trottinant et te tire: Biscotte trots over and tugs your shoelace: “Shall we go?”
textes.Biscotte grimpe le long de ton bras et s: Biscotte climbs up your arm and settles on your shoulder, tail around your neck. He's at home.
textes.Biscotte saute de ton épaule et file ver: Biscotte hops off your shoulder and scurries home, zigzagging.
textes.Biscotte se dresse sur ton épaule, renif: Biscotte rears up on your shoulder, sniffing the salty air: “Ah, the smell of the hold!”
textes.Biscotte, un petit rat blanc et brun, vi: Biscotte, a little white and brown rat, lives in the hold of the Requin Borgne. He's the secret friend of Petit-Pierre, the cabin boy. But Mange-Clous, the cook, has sworn to throw him overboard: his cheeses keep disappearing. Petit-Pierre would like Biscotte to go off with someone kind before it's too late. To lure him out of the hold, you need aged cheese.
textes.Bizarre ? Hé ! Je t'interdis. … Bon. Un: Weird? Hey! How dare you. … Well. A little, maybe. But that's part of the charm.
Weird? Hey! How dare you. … Well. A little, maybe. But that's part of the charm.
textes.Bizarre, oui. C'est le mot. Je n'aurais: Weird, yes. That's the word. I couldn't have put it better.
textes.Bizarre, {nom} ? Tu ne {le} connais pas: Weird, {nom}? You don't know {le} like I do.
textes.Bizarre, {nom} ? Vous ne {le} connaissez: Weird, {nom}? You don't know {le} like I do.
textes.Bizarre… oui, peut-être. Mais qui ne l'e: Weird… yes, maybe. But who isn't, around here?
textes.Bière de Forgefer, ragoût de Dagna, from: Forgefer fizz, Dagna's stew, Hilda's cheese! And I buy honey and fruit. You have {pieces} coins.
Blue, Ori. All blue. Nothing to report.
textes.Bleu… oui. Je l'aurais deviné. Un bleu d: Blue… yes. I'd have guessed. A deep-bay blue: calm on top, deep underneath. I'll paint you into a corner of the sea, very small.
textes.Blorp ! Pour maman ! Elle est restée sur: Blorp! For Mama! She stayed on Gloop, she's too squishy to travel, so I send her photos of everything. But I'm missing the most important part: the people down below! The real Heavyfeet, on their islands! I don't dare go down. I'm green, I wobble, and the last time I said hello to a fisherman, he yelled “A GIANT JELLY!” and jumped into the water. Could you do it? Take my holo-camera. Photograph the mayor of Port-Azur, the lady from the pirate tavern, the Baron of Montjoie and the crested granny of Boucan. Four corners of the archipelago! Mama will bounce for joy!
textes.Bof. Gaston boude, la mer est grise dans: Meh. Gaston is sulking, the sea is grey inside my head, and I've lost my favourite spoon.
textes.Bois de l'eau ! Danser au soleil, ça ass: Drink some water! Dancing in the sun dries you out. Water from the village spring is the best.
textes.Bon bois. Droit, sec, solide. Voilà ving: Good wood. Straight, dry, solid. Here's twenty coins. And… thank you, {surnom}.
textes.Bon vent, va. Assieds-toi, j'en ai une n: Fair winds, you old so-and-so. Sit down, I've got a new one.
textes.Bon vent, {surnom} ! Et méfie-toi des li: Fair winds, {surnom}! And watch out for the vines on the right.
textes.Bon vent. Et si tu vois Barnabé… ne lui: Fair winds. And if you see Barnabé… don't tell him anything.
textes.Bon, d'accord : qu'est-ce qui est gris,: All right, fine: what's grey, very tall, and doesn't move? … Me when I'm asleep. And me when I'm awake. Hee hee!
textes.Bon, par où on va maintenant ?: So, which way do we go now?
textes.Bon, pour la traversée, je prendrai peut: Well, for the crossing, maybe I'll take a rowing boat. I'll row fast. That counts, right?
textes.Bon, pour {objet}, ça fera {prix}. Clou,: Right, for {objet}, that'll be {prix}. Clou, put that away. No, don't eat it.
textes.Bon. BON ! Prends-le. Gratuitement. Tu m: Fine. FINE! Take it. For free. You wore me down. But don't tell anyone: I have a reputation as a businesswoman. Well, businessman. Anyway.
Fine. Ten arches. Long ones, then.
textes.Bon. Et cette anisette, dimanche ?: Fine. And that lemonade, on Sunday?
textes.Bon. Il était une fois un hibou qui avai: All right. Once upon a time there was an owl who had lost his night…
textes.Bon. Je te le dis à toi, {surnom}. Chaqu: All right. I'm telling you, {surnom}. Every week, I write Lucas a letter. I don't sign it Lola. I sign it “The Seagull”. Sometimes I wonder if he thinks a real seagull is writing to him. That would be just like him. I don't dare talk to him, because if he said no… As long as I don't ask anything, he can't say no.
textes.Bon. Puisque c'est vous, {surnom}. Chaqu: Well. Since it's you, {surnom}. Every Friday, for two years, Hector has come to dinner at my place. In a clean shirt. The second sea bream is for him. I don't tell anyone, because here a story once told no longer belongs to those who live it: it belongs to Rosalie. This one, I'm keeping. It's the only true stone I've found here.
textes.Bon. Tiens, une brioche. Et pas de greno: All right. Here, a brioche. And no frogs in the dough trough.
textes.Bon. Une. Petite. Et tu ne le dis à pers: Fine. One. Small. And you don't tell anyone.
textes.Bondi ? Un lapin qui court vite et qui l: Bondi? A rabbit who runs fast and says so even faster. Three carrots, not one more, but a head as big as a pumpkin. He's cute, in his vanity. Shh.
textes.Bondi est mon voisin, dans l'arbre du su: Bondi is my neighbour, in the south tree. The night before his first cup, he knocked on my door at midnight: “Pépin, your drum is making my carrots shake.” So I moved my practice behind the bakery. He won the next day. He says it was thanks to the quiet. I say it was thanks to me.
textes.Bondi mange trois carottes avant chaque: Bondi eats three carrots before every race. He says it makes you run faster. I think it just makes… three fewer carrots.
textes.Bondi, c'est le champion. Il est rapide,: Bondi's the champion. He's fast, he's nice, he's annoying. Three times I've seen his back, and it's a very fine back, I admit. This time I'll see his snout.
textes.Bondi, mon petit frère, le champion. Je: Bondi, my little brother, the champion. I'm so proud of him my apron strings could burst. But oh, is he vain! Three carrots, not one more… but four slices of toast, if you please.
textes.Bonjour ! Au Pain Doré, tout sort du fou: Good morning! At the Pain Doré, everything's fresh from the oven. Just smell that!
textes.Bonjour ! Café de la Place, installez-vo: Hello! The Square Café, make yourself comfortable. A coffee? This is the best seat for watching the town go by.
textes.Bonjour ! Des fleurs ? Pour quelqu'un de: Hello! Flowers? For someone special? Everyone's special, so take two.
textes.Bonjour ! Du courrier pour vous ? Non. M: Hello! Any mail for you? No. But I check every morning anyway.
textes.Bonjour ! Excuse le désordre. Enfin, l'o: Hello! Excuse the mess. Well, the order. Well… everything's on the ceiling, you know.
Hello! Dr Roux's herbal shop. A graze, a sunburn, a broken heart? I have a tea for everything.
textes.Bonjour ! Je suis Grigri, le virus le mo: Hello! I'm Grigri, the cheapest virus in the world!
textes.Bonjour ! Je suis Pimprenelle, la plus g: Hello! I'm Pimprenelle, the greatest magician in the village! Well… when I have my wand.
textes.Bonjour ! La Poste de Port-Azur, lettres: Hello! The Port-Azur Post Office: letters, parcels and telegrams. Writing to someone?
textes.Bonjour ! Pas trop de bobos aujourd'hui: Hello! Not too many bumps and scrapes today?
textes.Bonjour ! Pivoine, herboriste. Tu as l'a: Hello! Pivoine, herbalist. You look tired… No? Then you soon will be, and you'll come back to see me. Mist tea for sleeping, moon tea for dreaming.
textes.Bonjour ! Tu as un bout de fromage ? Mêm: Hello! Do you have a bit of cheese? Even a small one?
textes.Bonjour ! Tu tombes bien, c'est l'heure: Hello! You've come at just the right time, it's breakfast. Are you hungry?
textes.Bonjour ! Une table ? Je vous apporte la: Hello! A table? I'll bring you the menu. There's only one menu, it's written on the blackboard.
textes.Bonjour ! Venez voir, j'ai presque fini: Hello! Come and see, I've almost finished the lighthouse.
textes.Bonjour ! Vous voulez des potins ? J'ai: Hello! Want some gossip? I've got gossip.
textes.Bonjour bonjour ! Dis, toi, tu te lèves: Morning, morning! Say, are you an early riser?
textes.Bonjour bonjour ! Gaston et moi discutio: Hello, hello! Gaston and I were just talking about you. Well, mostly Gaston.
textes.Bonjour bonjour ! Gérard Dupuis, en vaca: Hello hello! Gérard Dupuis, on holiday with my wife and the little one. May I take a photo? Ah, no, I've lost my camera. What a nuisance.
textes.Bonjour bonjour ! Levée à cinq heures, f: Morning, morning! Up at five, oven lit, dough kneaded. Mochi steals the cakes… Mochi! Put that down! Pépin practises his drum behind the bakery, and the dough rises in time. And Caramel… ever since the Great Swap chain broke between us, we greet each other with the tips of our whiskers. We have to: our girls are inseparable.
textes.Bonjour bonjour ! Trèfle, boulangère. Pa: Hello hello! Trèfle, baker. Carrot bread, mooncake… Everything's fresh from the oven, everything's warm. Mochi! Put that cake down! … Sorry. That's my daughter.
textes.Bonjour bonjour, Pépin. Le pain est chau: Morning, morning, Pépin. The bread's hot.
Good morning first. Then three coffees.
textes.Bonjour docteur ! Mes temps sont en bais: Morning, Doctor! My times are going down!
textes.Bonjour quand même, Grommelot ! Six pièc: Good morning anyway, Grommelot! Six coins a shard?
textes.Bonjour, Amirale ! J'ai sonné neuf heure: Morning, Admiral! I rang nine o'clock on the dot!
textes.Bonjour, Bramm. Tu as une chèvre sur l'é: Morning, Bramm. You've got a goat on your shoulder.
textes.Bonjour, Brume ! Tu sais déjà ce que j'a: Hello, Brume! Do you already know what I did this morning?
textes.Bonjour, Caelan. Tu as bien dormi ? Ah n: Morning, Caelan. Sleep well? Oh no, that's right, you were playing.
textes.Bonjour, Doyenne. Halo m'envoie vous sal: Hello, Elder. Halo sent me to greet you.
Good morning, Faelar. Three rays this morning.
textes.Bonjour, Grommelot ! Un petit nectar pou: Morning, Grommelot! A little nectar to sweeten your mood?
textes.Bonjour, Grommelot… Merci pour la coquil: Morning, Grommelot… Thank you for the nutshell.
Good morning, Your Majesty. Your flower has had its drink.
textes.Bonjour, Marée. Les laminaires sont bell: Good morning, Marée. Is the kelp nice today?
Hello, Moustache. I read the mud.
textes.Bonjour, Mélisse… J'ai un peu de rosée d: Morning, Mélisse… I've got a little moon dew.
Good morning, Octave. Your kapok tree says hello.
Good morning, Orophin. I'm heading north.
textes.Bonjour, Perlée. Ma fleur a bu ?: Good morning, Perlée. Has my flower had its drink?
textes.Bonjour, Pimprenelle. Tu allumes toujour: Hello, Pimprenelle. Do you still light the lanterns with a snap of your fingers?
textes.Bonjour, Pélagos ! Une sur trois, promis: Morning, Pélagos! One in three, promise!
textes.Bonjour, Rita. Toujours dans vos cartes: Good morning, Rita. Still in your cards?
textes.Bonjour, Rita. Vous n'avez rien vu, j'es: Good morning, Rita. You haven't seen anything, I hope?
textes.Bonjour, Thalion. Non, je ne te dirai pa: Good morning, Thalion. No, I won't tell you.
textes.Bonjour, jeune homme. Une demi-taille, t: Good morning, young man. Still half a size?
textes.Bonjour, jeune personne. Quelle heure es: Good day, young person. What time is it? Oh, forgive me. Nobody knows any more, around here.
textes.Bonjour, les abeilles ! … Elles m'ont en: Hello, bees! … Did they hear me?
textes.Bonjour, madame Colette ! Et ce pot, auj: Good day, Madame Colette! And that jar, today?
textes.Bonjour, maître. Le corail mord toujours: Good morning, master. Does the coral still bite?
textes.Bonjour, maître. Vous avez l'air en form: Good day, master. You look well.
textes.Bonjour, mon petit ! Attention où tu met: Hello, dear! Watch where you step: there's a cat everywhere.
textes.Bonjour, mon petit. Je tricote des pulls: Hello, dear. I knit plaid sweaters for the whole street. When it rains, you need to be warm. And when it doesn't rain… it rains anyway, here. Want a pair of socks? I have too many.
textes.Bonjour, petite étoile. Combien de quest: Good morning, little star. How many questions today?
textes.Bonjour, s'il te plaît, merci : trois mo: Hello, please, thank you: three more words, Ursule.
textes.Bonjour, {surnom}. La table du coin est: Hello, {surnom}. The corner table is free.
textes.Bonjour, {surnom}. Tu viendras danser, c: Hello, {surnom}. Will you come and dance tonight?
textes.Bonjour. Anouk, la guérisseuse. Mon infi: Hello. Anouk, the healer. My infirmary is on the lower deck, between the hammocks. Seaweed, honey, and plenty of patience. Are you hurt?
textes.Bonjour. Nolwenn, voilière. Tu vois les: Hello. Nolwenn, sailmaker. See the red and blue awnings all over Carène? Those are my old sails. I re-sew them, re-cut them, give them a second life.
textes.Bonjour. Perles, pierres, or ancien. J'a: Hello. Pearls, gems, antique gold. I buy too, if you have any treasures.
textes.Bonjour. Toujours une demi-taille de tro: Good morning. Still half a size too big?
Good morning. Three coffees. Thank you.
textes.Bonjour. Épicerie fine. On touche avec l: Good day. Fine groceries. Look with your eyes, not your hands.
textes.Bonjour. … Bonjour ! Bonjour, bonjour, b: Hello. … Hello! Hello, hello, hello! Sorry. It's been so long. (His voice is a little deep, a little crackly, like an old radio.) Thank you, my friend. Mio will be so happy. And Cargo… he kept it for me, didn't he? He keeps everything, that big softie. Here: these are the two sodas I had in my treasure hatch. For twenty years. They still sparkle.
textes.Bonjour… Attention où tu marches, chaque: Hello… Watch where you step, every dewdrop has a name.
textes.Bonjour… Pardon, je ne suis pas de très: Hello… Sorry, I'm not very good company. Hugo. I'm… on my honeymoon. Well, I was.
textes.Bonne garde, Thalion ! Je te joue quelqu: Good watch, Thalion! Shall I play you something?
Have a nice day! Enjoy the sunshine.
textes.Bonne nouvelle : mer d'huile aujourd'hui: Good news: sea like glass today, just how you like it. Even the goat would have held on.
textes.Bonne nuit. Le Léviathan craque, mais il: Good night. The Léviathan creaks, but it holds.
textes.Bonne nuit. Écoute bien : ce sont les ta: Good night. Listen closely: those are the moon drums. They'll rock you till morning.
textes.Bonne route ! Et si tu te perds dans la: Safe travels! And if you get lost in the mist, follow the lanterns.
textes.Bonne réponse. On alerte d'abord, on dis: Right answer. Alarm first, talk after. Even if it's Hulotte. Especially if it's Hulotte.
textes.Bonne réponse. Tiens : un accord de ré,: Right answer. Here: a D chord, just for you. Tonight, at the Perroquet, I'll play you three more.
textes.Bonsoir ! Il me reste deux croissants, j: Good evening! I've got two croissants left, you can have them half price.
textes.Bonsoir, Amélie. Toujours pas de corail: Good evening, Amélie. Still no coral?
textes.Bonsoir, Lilas ! Prête pour la lune ?: Evening, Lilas! Ready for the moon?
textes.Bonsoir, Lulu. Nos champignons brillent: Good evening, Lulu. Are our mushrooms glowing nicely?
textes.Bonsoir, Mère-Lune ! Votre cape va bien: Good evening, Mère-Lune! How's your cloak?
textes.Bonsoir, Mère-Lune. Vous m'avez regardée: Good evening, Mother Moon. Did you watch me?
textes.Bonsoir, Nausicaa. La marée est haute ?: Good evening, Nausicaa. Is the tide high?
textes.Bonsoir, Triton. Je chante la haute ?: Good evening, Triton. Shall I sing the high tide?
textes.Bonsoir, Ursule ! Juste des fers un tout: Evening, Ursule! Just horseshoes a teeny bit lighter?
textes.Bonsoir, la patronne ! Le poêle tient le: Evening, boss! Is the stove holding up?
Good evening, my girl. It smells good tonight.
