textes.Chaque samedi, je pose un régime devant: Every Saturday, I leave a bunch outside Barnabé's hut. Gaston counts it out loud: “One! Two! Three! Shipwreck!” He can only count to three; after that, he says “Shipwreck”. Barnabé says “Gaston, write that down!” and Gaston eats a banana. Rent paid.
textes.Chaque semaine, Bastien me monte son pan: Every week, Bastien brings his basket of fish up to me. We argue over the price of every sardine. He says “Peuchère”, I say “Cash”, and we always end up at last week's price. That's our way of saying hello.
textes.Chaque semaine, Fernand m'invite à l'ani: Every week, Fernand invites me for a glass of his famous lemonade, and every week I refuse. On Sundays, I come. He takes out two glasses and the bottle he hides in a lobster pot. We don't talk much. One Sunday, he made me laugh. He was so surprised he knocked the bottle over.
textes.Chaque semaine, Nadine me tend une envel: Every week, Nadine hands me an envelope, smiling. Too much. A big smile, with all her teeth. As if she knew something I don't. Or that I do. I take the envelope, I say thanks, I go home. She's still smiling behind me. I can feel it on my back.
textes.Chaque semaine, dans la boîte jaune, je: Every week, in the yellow postbox, I find an envelope addressed “To L., the tall one on the quay”. No name, no street. The tall one on the quay! There's only one in Port-Azur. I slip it into Lucas's letterbox, High Street, whistling, as if nothing were going on. I'm a postwoman, not a gossip. Well, not about that.
textes.Chaque semaine, je demande à Tchoum le p: Every week, I ask Tchoum the name of the twenty-fourth speaker. He says “Later”. I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}: I couldn't care less about speakers. It's to hear him talk. He has a lovely voice, Tchoum, when he lets it out. Two words a week. That's my treasure. Whatever you do, don't tell him.
textes.Chaque semaine, je demande à Zéphyr de q: Every week, I ask Zéphyr which island my hazelnut came from. He thinks, he scratches his head, and he says: “An island with trees.” THEY ALL HAVE TREES! Once, he said: “An island with trees and wind.” I thought we were getting somewhere. Nope.
textes.Chaque semaine, je lui échange une lampe: Every week I trade her a mother-of-pearl lamp for a bag of crackers. I eat the crackers, she resells the lamps, supposedly. Ondine, who counts everything, told me there are thirty-seven at her place. Lit. I said nothing. I made the next one a little prettier.
textes.Chaque semaine, je monte mon panier de p: Every week I carry my basket of fish up to Octave's cheese shop. We haggle over the price of every sardine. I say “Well I never”, he says “Cash”, and we always end up at last week's price. Once, I offered a lower price, just to see. He refused. He said it was fishy.
textes.Chaque semaine, je passe chez sa mère, a: Every week, I call on her mother, in the village, with a letter from Lola, and I come back with news: the roof, the cat, the neighbours. Her mother always gives me a jar of jam “for the little one”. Every time, she asks me if Lola looks happy. I say yes. It's true.
textes.Chaque soir au Cercle, on compare nos do: Every evening at the Circle, we compare our aching paws. She wins, I cheat. And every evening, when I get near the end of my story, she closes her eyes. Just before. Always just before. I wonder if she's really asleep.
textes.Chaque soir depuis trente ans, je souffl: Every evening for thirty years, I've blown a little mother-of-pearl lantern and set it on the canal, just in front of the bridge where Ianthé dances. She thinks they come from the current. I've never dared tell her. I blow mother-of-pearl very well, {surnom}. Words, much less so. They come out too soon, or not at all.
textes.Chaque soir, Ewen me raconte ce qu'il vo: Every evening, Ewen tells me what he sees on the horizon. Yesterday, he described a cloud shaped like a sock, three seagulls, and a dolphin doing somersaults. I don't know if the dolphin was real. I wrote it down anyway. He wanted it so much.
textes.Chaque soir, Pivoine me frotte les patte: Every evening Pivoine rubs my paws with her balm. The first evening it smelled so strong that, way up on the Lookout watch post, Croc-Gris sneezed. Three times. Pivoine said that proved it worked. My paws were better, it's true. Croc-Gris, less so.
textes.Chaque soir, Ulfa crie pour toute la tav: Every evening, Ulfa shouts for the whole tavern to hear: “And a glass of WATER for Nori!” I pour it into my flask when her back is turned. What I drink is dew gathered on the summit on full-moon nights, in an obsidian bowl. She wouldn't know the difference.
textes.Chaque soir, après le rapport à mon oncl: Every evening, after reporting to my uncle, I dictate to Ori what I've seen. “Three golems, black slope.” He writes. Then he asks: “And the sky?” The night of the lightning, I said: “Nothing.” He looked up from his page and stared at me for a long time. He didn't write anything. He knows, I think.
textes.Chaque soir, au Cercle, on compare nos d: Every evening, at the Circle, we compare our aches. “My left paw,” he says. “Both,” I say. He invents a third to win. And I know the end of “the moon that wouldn't go to bed”: his mother told it at the Circle when we were young. I don't tell it back to him. He'll find it again.
textes.Chaque soir, au crépuscule, on boit une: Every evening at dusk, we have a cup of tea together, at the Post Office. I come home, he goes up. I say “Good night, Papa”, he says “Good morning, sweetheart”. It's been eight years. Once, he got mixed up, and said “Good night” too. I was happy all evening. I don't know why.
textes.Chaque soir, au crépuscule, on compare n: Every evening, at dusk, we compare notes. One day, I brought him a map of the round tracks, drawn in charcoal: every step, every distance. He kept it one night. The next day, it was covered in numbers, arrows and stars. I couldn't make head or tail of my own map any more. He said that was progress.
textes.Chaque soir, au rapport, je lui donne un: Every evening, at report time, I give him a pretty stone I picked up on the heights. He takes it without a word and slips it into his pocket. One day I went into his lodge while he was at Ulfa's. There was a shelf, with all my stones, sorted by colour. Every single one. I backed out of the room.
textes.Chaque soir, elle vient au rapport : « T: Every evening, she comes to report: “Three golems on the black slope. One of Hilda's goats too high. Nothing else.” Then she gives me a stone picked up up there, always a pretty one. I've got a whole shelf of them in my guardhouse. Nobody knows.
textes.Chaque soir, il agite son chapeau vers l: Every evening, he waves his hat at the mist. Where I come from, nobody answers. One evening, I did: three flashes of a lantern, from the highest platform. He danced on his beach until midnight. He doesn't know it was me.
textes.Chaque soir, il arrive au pied du Chêne-: Every evening, he arrives at the foot of the Mother Oak. I say: “Basket?” He says: “Thank you, Bourru. I fly.” He takes the stairs. Very slowly. I watch him climb. All the way up. Just in case. It takes an hour. Hrmm. My basket: three minutes.
textes.Chaque soir, j'allume les lanternes du s: Every evening, I light the lanterns along the path, from the jetty to the square, then the ones on the walkways. Two hundred and forty lanterns. Rúmil brings me the light he fishes at dawn, and I pour it in. Then I keep watch until morning. I know every night in the Bois-Doré. No two are alike.
textes.Chaque soir, j'invente une histoire à Th: Every night, I make up a story for Théo to help him sleep. A bear called Captain, a kite that flies around the world, a sandcastle that never falls down. He says they're the best stories in the world. He doesn't know his mother has had practice. A lot of practice.
textes.Chaque soir, je dessine un truc dans le: Every evening, I draw something in the sky for the queen. Once, I did a crown. She said: “Oh, a mushroom!” It was NOT a mushroom. Since then, she says “mushroom” every time I draw a crown, and she laughs. So do I, honestly.
textes.Chaque soir, je garde un punch de côté,: Every evening, I keep a punch aside, behind the till, nice and cool. For Lucas, when he comes in. Toni sees it. He sees it every evening. He acts like nothing's going on and serves the others, whistling. Once, without even turning around, he just said: “Your secret punch would be better with a straw.”
textes.Chaque soir, je passe à La Rose des Vent: Every evening, I stop by La Rose des Vents to tell Félix what the passengers say about the other islands. He writes it all down, even the nonsense. One day, I told him about the seasick goat on the spring crossing. He wrote it down. On his map, in the middle of the channel, there's a tiny little goat. He says it's a landmark.
textes.Chaque soir, je pose un panier à l'entré: Every evening, I leave a basket at the mouth of his tunnel: bread, Hilda's cheese and a little note. In the morning, the basket's empty and the note's gone. One day I found all my notes in his jacket pocket, neatly folded. Hundreds of them. He doesn't throw them away. He rereads them, so he won't forget.
textes.Chaque soir, le port devient rose. Pas u: Every evening, the port turns pink. Not a pink from a tube: a pink that breathes. And I can't paint it. My mainland colours are sad, they've never seen the sea. So I started looking for true colours: coral, honey from the hills, the brown of a coconut. The herbalist refused me the coral. I understand. I'm sulking anyway.
textes.Chaque soir, quand L'Hirondelle accoste,: Every evening, when the Swallow comes alongside, Hortense is there on the promenade, watching the passengers come down. One by one. I come down last and give her a little nod. She does the same. One rainy evening, she wasn't there. I nodded to the empty bench. You never know.
textes.Chaque soir, quand j'ai allumé la lanter: Every evening, when I've lit the lantern, I come back down and my grandad asks: “Is it straight?” I say yes. He says: “Then the boats will come home.” Once I said no, just to see. He climbed up to the bow on his creaky knees. I never said no again.
textes.Chaque soir, quand je passe devant la na: Every evening, when I pass the basket lift on my way up to the treetop, Bourru says: “Hrmm. The lift?” And every evening I answer: “Thank you, Bourru. I'll fly.” Then I take the stairs, very slowly. I know he watches me climb all the way to the top, just in case. It does me good and hurts at the same time.
textes.Chaque vendredi, Rosalie me tend mes deu: Every Friday, Rosalie hands me my two sea bream with a trick question. “The lifeguard likes sea bream, you know?” The lifeguard is her son. “And the bookseller?” I answer: “I'm very hungry on Fridays.” She gives me my change with narrowed eyes. I never blush. Stones taught me to stay cool as marble.
textes.Chaque été, je range mes colonnes de chi: Every summer, I put away my columns of figures and come here to count sunsets. On the first day, I hired a pedalo to photograph the lighthouse. I went round in circles for an hour. The lighthouse looked superb from every angle. Kevin had to come and fetch me. In the evening, Paulo's bouillabaisse. My trousers no longer agree with me.
textes.Charge plus longtemps (la lueur devient: Charge longer (the glow turns blue): when you release, you spin and strike all around you, twice. In VR: click the right stick.
textes.Charger remplace la partie en cours : pe: Loading replaces the current game: remember to save first.
textes.Charmant aujourd'hui, enrhumée demain. P: Charming today, sniffles tomorrow. Come by the shop.
textes.Charming little town ! Le thé est épouva: Charming little town! The tea is dreadful, but the Perroquet's punch is divine.
textes.Charon grogne : « Déjà payé. Monte. » Et: Charon grunts: “Already paid. Get in.” And the boat glides over the black water.
textes.Charon, le passeur, te regarde de ses ye: Charon, the ferryman, looks at you with his golden eyes: “An obol to cross. No obol, no boat. And don't tell me you forgot it, they all say that.” (There was a bowl of obols in the Vestibule…)
textes.Chasser cinq slimes dans les prés: Hunt five slimes in the meadows
textes.Chasser deux grenouilles géantes au lac: Hunt two giant frogs at the lake
textes.Chasser deux mimiques (les vrais coffres: Hunt two mimics (the real chests thank you)
textes.Chasser dix gobelins (la Guilde a besoin: Hunt ten goblins (the Guild needs socks)
textes.Chasser huit grenouilles géantes (le lac: Hunt eight giant frogs (the lake is overflowing with croaks)
textes.Chasser la Duchesse, la Grenouille Reine: Hunt the Duchess, the Frog Queen of the lake (she ate a rowing boat)
textes.Chasser le virus de ton carnet : casser: Chase the virus out of your journal: break its three locks on the screen (if you take a break, Glitch helps you pick up again: near the Arcade Station in the morning and evening, in the arcade in the afternoon)
textes.Chasser les chiens d'enfer sauvages du c: Drive the wild hellhounds out of the lava field (east of the Great Blaze)
textes.Chasser les gargouilles des Ruines de l': Drive the gargoyles out of the Ruins of the Old Pandemonium (on the north-western cliffs of the island)
textes.Chasser les grenouilles géantes du Lac d: Hunt the giant frogs of the Frog Lake (east of Montjoie, through the East Gate; watch out for their tongues, they swallow you up)

Hunt the giant frogs of the Frog Lake (east of town, through the East Gate): the biggest one, the Duchess, will give back the sun rosary; then bring it back to Sister Pétronille (at the Temple of Dawn, in the Upper Town, or at the Guild in the afternoon)
textes.Chasser quatre gobelins au Bois des Luti: Hunt four goblins in the Goblin Wood (they steal socks)
textes.Chasser quatre squelettes dans le donjon: Hunt four skeletons in the dungeon (they frighten the mimics)
textes.Chasser trois loups au Bois des Lutins (: Hunt three wolves in the Goblin Wood (at night)
textes.Chasser trois slimes bleus (ils tachent: Hunt three blue slimes (they stain the washhouse laundry)
textes.Cherche les petites lumières qui dansent: Look for the little lights dancing under the big trees, far from the square. By day they shine too, if you know how to look.
textes.Chercher Miou sur le plateau de Rê, près: Look for Miou on the plateau of Ra, near the mastabas (the square tombs), and pick him up in your arms (E)
textes.Chercher Pépin dans le Bois de Cendre (a: Look for Pépin in the Ash Wood (south-east of the city, under the ember trees) and call him (E)
textes.Chez Ba Sidi, à la fin, on donne ce qu'o: At Ba Sidi's, at the end, you give what you like. The fishermen gave a sardine, the merchants a coin. All I had was a pot of Ramure honey, saved for the road. I set it in his dish. He tasted it with the tip of his finger, closed his eyes and said: “That one, I'll tell.” I wonder if he did.
textes.Chez Rose, pour choisir ma rose d'excuse: At Rose's, choosing my apology rose, I asked for ranunculus, then an old rose, a “Belle de Crécy”. She stared at me, wide-eyed. Léa taught me all those names, one a day, the year of the bouquets. Rose said: “You married a florist.” Then she sold me a perfectly plain rose: “To say sorry, the simplest one.”
textes.Chez nous, on dirait : « que tes racines: Where I come from, we'd say: “may your roots run deep”.
textes.Chez nous, on tient un carnet noir depui: In our family, we've kept a black book for two hundred years. Every hole in the Léviathan has its number in it, its date and the name of whoever plugged it. The first is my ancestor, the day after the wreck. I'm up to four thousand three hundred and twelve. I know them all. Some are like old neighbours: unpleasant, but loyal.
With a crow, it's the same thing.
textes.Choisis un talent pour le lire. Les tale: Pick a talent to read it. The talents of a branch are learned in order, from top to bottom.
textes.Chut ! J'ai gardé ton secret de la queue: Shh! I kept your tail secret! I didn't tell anyone! Except Myrtille, but she doesn't count.
textes.Chut ! Je fais entrer un trois-mâts dans: Shh! I'm getting a three-master into a bottle. All that's left is to pull the thread to raise the masts. Want to do it?
textes.Chut ! Je suis à deux doigts d'une décou: Shh! I'm on the verge of a discovery. Or an explosion. Do you want to press the button?
textes.Chut ! Ma tante est juste derrière !: Shh! My aunt's right behind me!
textes.Chut ! On joue à cache-cache ! Trois pet: Shh! We're playing hide-and-seek! Three little Moai have hidden under the rocks. Find them! … And don't lift the real rocks too hard, they're touchy.
textes.Chut ! Parle moins fort ! (Il regarde pa: Shh! Not so loud! (He looks all around.) It's about Biscotte. He's a rat. My rat. Well, the ship's rat, but he's my friend. He's tiny, white with brown spots, and he sleeps in my hammock when the captain isn't looking. Only, Mange-Clous lost three cheeses, and he swore on his ladle that he'd throw “that filthy rat” overboard! Biscotte isn't filthy! He washes three times a day! I'm just a cabin boy, I can't have a rat of my own, the captain says a cabin boy owns nothing. But you… could you take him? He likes shoulders and cheese. Mostly cheese. Go see Mange-Clous: if he knows Biscotte is leaving, he might give you something to lure him. He's grumpy, but he's not bad at heart. Just a bad cheese.
textes.Chut ! Tu es devant Nefer-Miou, la chatt: Shh! You are before Nefer-Miou, the sacred cat of the house. She descends from great Bastet herself. We owe her respect!
textes.Chut ! Tu vas faire peur aux chèvres. …: Shh! You'll frighten the goats. … Well, they're not afraid of anything. Hilda Plume-de-Suie. I keep the ash goats and I talk to the ravens.
textes.Chut, c'est un secret, {surnom}. Je sais: Shh, it's a secret, {surnom}. I know where my hazelnuts are. All of them. All two hundred and ninety-nine. I pretend I've lost them so people help me look. That way they stay with me a bit. Pomme-de-Pin works all the time, and Mum and Dad are far away. You'll still help me look, won't you?
textes.Chut, {surnom}, c'est un vrai secret. Ch: Shh, {surnom}, it's a real secret. Every evening I tell the mist about my day. Everything: the cakes, the races, the dragons. That way the mist tells my papa. I've never told Mummy. Because when Mummy cries, the bread's too salty. And her eyes would go all red. You won't tell anyone, will you?
textes.Chut. Approche. … Il y a dix ans, je l'a: Shh. Come closer. … Ten years ago, I had him. The Pond King, on the end of my line. Golden, laughing, with a sort of crown on his head. He weighed in my paw like a little sun. And I opened my paw. Because if I caught him, what would I wait for afterwards? … Nobody knows. Myrtille drew the crown all on her own.
textes.Chut. Il est là. Je le sens dans mes mou: Shh. He's here. I can feel it in my whiskers.
textes.Chut. Je chuchote. Je chuchote toujours,: Shh. I'm whispering. I always whisper with crates.
textes.Chut. Je prie. Enfin, je pense aux pâtes: Shh. I'm praying. Well, I'm thinking about pasta. Same thing.
textes.Chut. Je suis né à la pêcherie des chats: Shh. I was born at the cats' fishery, by the big pond. My father taught me only one thing: “Watch the float.” The rest I learned by watching the float. My rod, young Bedaine swapped it to me, at the end of his very first chain. It's patient, this rod. Gets it from me.
textes.Chut. Personne ne sait, au début. Regard: Shh. Nobody knows how, at first. Watch the float. Count to a hundred. Start again. In forty years, you'll know. Me, I'm starting to know.
textes.Chut. Plus gros chaque fois que tu deman: Shh. Bigger every time you ask.
Shh. You're scaring the light away.
Shh. You'll scare off the King.
textes.Chut. Tu vas faire fuir le Roi des mares: Shh. You'll scare off the King of the Pools. … Moustache. Fisherman. Sit down, don't move, and watch the float. That's all there is to do, and that's already a lot.
Shh. Come and sit down, little one.
textes.Chut. … Bien. Assieds-toi là, alors. Ne: Shh. … Good. Sit there, then. Don't move. Watch the float. … See? You know how.
textes.Chut. … Dis-moi. Tu sais attendre, toi ?: Shh. … Tell me. Do you know how to wait?
textes.Chut… Quelqu'un dort. Et il ronfle comme: Shh… Someone's sleeping. And snoring like a forge bellows.
textes.Chut… Trois enfants dorment sur des futo: Shh… Three children sleep on futons of every color. All you hear is the wind on the canvas, and a mother knitting.
textes.Chut… ah, c'est toi. Tu tombes bien : j': Shh… ah, it's you. Just in time: I need an opinion. Want to listen?
textes.Chut… ne bougez pas. Je vous regarde. Si: Shh… don't move. I'm looking at you. If you were a colour, which one would you be?
textes.Chut… ne bougez pas. La lumière est parf: Shh… don't move. The light is perfect. … There. Hello. Clémence, painter. Well, I try.
textes.Chut… ça mord peut-être. Non. Bon. Je pê: Shh… maybe something's biting. No. Oh well. I'm fishing.
textes.Chuuut. Quelqu'un chantonne tout bas : «: Shhh. Someone is humming very softly: “Sleep, little hammer…”
textes.Chère Hortense ! Toujours fidèle au post: Dear Hortense! Ever faithful at your post!
textes.Cinq ! Cinq beaux dorés ! (Il les caress: Five! Five beautiful golden ones! (He strokes them one by one, like little kittens.) You caught them gently, I can see. Not a single bump. They just look a bit offended. They'll get over it. They always do.
textes.Cinq ! Et une paille pour le drapeau. La: Five! And a straw for the flag. The pink one!
Five! I'll need five half coconuts, then.
textes.Cinq beaux champignons ! Ils sentent la: Five lovely mushrooms! They smell of rain. Here, two sap potions, with my thanks. Don't drink them all at once.
textes.Cinq blagues des petits Moaïs: Five jokes from the little Moai
textes.Cinq cents mètres de corde de chanvre, e: Five hundred metres of hemp rope, tightly coiled. Each end is closed with a funny knot: the friendship knot, says Galet. The harder you pull, the tighter it holds.
Five hundred push-ups and scared of a sardine. My son, ladies!
textes.Cinq coquillages nacrés ! Ma collection: Five pearly shells! My collection is complete! Here, take my old compass, and a few coins. You've earned them, {surnom}!
textes.Cinq esprits, cinq cercles de champignon: Five spirits, five rings of white mushrooms, in the forest around the village. Only the lantern can catch them. The lantern, and patience.
textes.Cinq heures. Et le vent sera de suroît,: Five o'clock. And the wind'll be south-westerly, my lovely.
textes.Cinq pièces, mon chou. Même les hamacs,: Five coins, dear. Even hammocks cost money here. Especially the hammocks: they've seen things.
textes.Cinq… et tous intacts. Regarde comme ils: Five… and all intact. Look how they shine, even in broad daylight. Tonight, the bridges of Ramure will be blue like they used to be. You have a gentle heart, little one, and gentle hands too. Here: fox ears, sewn by Pivoine. Put them on, and all of Ramure will know you're one of us.
textes.Cipactli balaie tout de sa queue !: Cipactli sweeps everything away with its tail!
textes.Cipactli plonge… et resurgit ailleurs !: Cipactli dives… and resurfaces somewhere else!
textes.Cipactli s'effondre dans un grondement d: Cipactli collapses with a mountain's rumble. His body turns to stone, earth, roots… as on the first day, when the gods made the world from his body. On the altar at the back, a green feather begins to glow.
textes.Cirque des Os, au nord. Suivre le chemin: Bone Hollow, north. Follow path of stones.
textes.Citoyen d'honneur, ça se mérite ! Rendez: Honorary citizen, that has to be earned! Do favours for our residents: ten favours, and I'll hand you the key to the town in front of everyone, with a fanfare. Well, with Django.
textes.Clac ! Le bras du tourniquet tombe, la l: Clack! The turnstile arm drops, the lamp turns green, and the iron shutter sinks into the floor. “STAFF EXIT AUTHORISED. HAVE A GOOD DESCENT.” The service stairs lead to the Assembly Line.
textes.Clac ! Un grondement, et les deux poids: Clack! A rumble, and the two weights slide back to their starting places.
textes.Clac ! Une lampe s'allume au-dessus de l: Clack! A lamp lights up above the door… and above your head, something very heavy goes “crrrr”. RUN! (The alcoves are free.)
textes.Clac-clac-FLOP ! L'Alouette se déplie au: Clack-clack-FLOP! The Alouette unfolds above you in mid-fall… and the canvas billows out. You're gliding!
textes.Clairement ! Tu entends, le poisson ? Qu: Clearly! Hear that, fish? Somebody recognises you! … He's touched. So am I. A bit.
textes.Classe conseillée : aventurier. (La boul: Recommended class: adventurer. (The ball recommends that to everyone.)
textes.Clic : choisir • double-clic : utilise: Click: select  •  double-click: use  •  I / Tab / Esc: close
textes.Clic, clac, cliquetis ! L'hélice tourne,: Click, clack, cliquetis! The propeller turns, the chain sings. Pedal, and up she goes! A little. It's not a rocket, it's an Alouette.
textes.Clic, clic, clic… Une grand-mère tricote: Click, click, click… A grandmother knits in a red armchair, surrounded by balls of yarn. Plaid sweaters dry on a line.
textes.Clic. La bibliothèque pivote… un passage: Click. The bookcase swivels… a secret passage!
textes.Clic… FIOU ! Une fléchette jaillit du mu: Click… WHIZZ! A dart shoots out of the east wall! The dark, cracked tiles are trapped: step on the light ones.
textes.Clique sur les tuiles pour les tourner :: Click the tiles to rotate them: connect the battery ⚡ to the antivirus ✚.
textes.Cliquetis, la cité des ingénieurs fous —: Cliquetis, the city of mad engineers — the Inventions Fair, the Zephyr, the cable car
textes.Cliquetis, la ville des inventeurs, en d: Cliquetis, the city of inventors, is overflowing with them
textes.Clonk ! Les trois lampes du synoptique p: Clonk! The three lamps on the diagram turn green: ALL BELTS GO TOWARD THE EXIT. (The intern would be proud. Well, if he understood.)
textes.Clonk ! Une canette de Synthé-Soda tombe: Clonk! A can of Synth-Soda drops into the tray. It's ice cold, and it glows a little in the dark.
textes.Clou (en fouillant ta poche) : « Hiii hi: Clou (rummaging in your pocket): “Heeee hee hee!”
textes.Clou ? Il est arrivé un matin, il a volé: Clou? He showed up one morning, stole my last coin, and stayed. We get along fine: we both love money.
textes.Clou a du rythme. Amène-le à la teuf, pe: Clou's got rhythm. Bring him to the party, peuchère!
textes.Clou fait tinter une pièce qu'il vient d: Clou jingles a coin he just took from you… and Octave takes it back.
textes.Clou fouille, trouve une miette, la mang: Clou rummages, finds a crumb, eats it, and falls asleep on your shoulder. He's adopted you. So have I, a little.
textes.Clou s'est caché derrière le comptoir. O: Clou is hiding behind the counter. You can only see his tail.
Clou tugs at your sleeve and holds out his hand.
textes.Clou veut savoir s'il peut fouiller tes: Clou wants to know if he can go through your pockets. He's asking, that's new.
textes.Clou, cache la caisse, voilà du monde !: Clou, hide the cash box, we've got company!
textes.Clou, tu as vu ? Il frappe le marchand !: Clou, did you see that? Hitting the shopkeeper! I'll remember this.
textes.Clémence peint la lumière comme je dessi: Clémence paints light the way I draw coastlines: getting it wrong a lot and starting again. I love watching her hunt for her pink.
textes.Clémence veut peindre avec des couleurs: Clémence wants to paint with natural colours: a red coral from the bottom of the bay, some honey and a coconut.
textes.Clémence veut peindre la musique. On ne: Clémence wants to paint music. You can't paint what you can't hold in your hands. And she drew me like a man with toothache.
textes.Clémence, c'est ma copine peintre. Elle: Clémence is my painter friend. She paints the lighthouse, the harbour, the sea, everything. She let me paint a sky! But she doesn't paint fast. Like, not fast at all.
textes.Clémence, elle m'a donné une petite toil: Clémence gave me a little canvas and a brush, and she said: “You do the sky.” So I made the sky all blue, and in the middle I put my kite, with all its colours. That way, it's still flying, on the canvas. Clémence kept it. She says it's the most beautiful sky at the lookout.
textes.Coco ! La recette de ma grand-mère ! Bon: Coconut! My grandmother's recipe! All right, Kiki sells it too now. But the real one's here. Don't repeat that to him. Actually, yes, do.
textes.Colette est la seule à voter contre moi,: Colette is the only one who's voted against me for eighteen years. An apple! Over an apple! I admire her consistency. I'll never admit it in public.
textes.Colette lit des romans d'amour. Ne lui d: Colette reads romance novels. Don't tell her I told you.
textes.Colette, c'est ma plus fidèle cliente :: Colette is my most loyal client: once a year, without fail, for the great love. She haggles over everything in life, except that. For that alone, I'm fond of her.
textes.Colette, c'est ma plus vieille amie et m: Colette is my oldest friend and my stingiest customer. A herbal tea, a novel, and a newspaper to hide the novel. Don't tell her I told you.
textes.Colette, l'épicière. Sévère, regardante,: Colette, the grocer. Stern, tight-fisted, she counts the change twice. And she has exquisite taste in literature. Exquisite. I can't say more.
textes.Colette. Elle compte tout : le papier, l: Colette. She counts everything: the paper, the string, the hello. Her prices are scary. My blades, at least, you know what they're for.
textes.Colline du Feedback\nQuand le vent souff:
Feedback Hill
When the wind blows hard, the hill whistles,
like a guitar too close to its amp.
textes.Combien ? Où ? Quelle taille ? Attendez,: How many? Where? How big? Wait, my notebook!
textes.Combien de cercles compte ce royaume ?: How many circles does this realm have?
textes.Combien de nains faut-il pour changer un: How many dwarves does it take to change a torch? None: we dig down to the lava, it's brighter.
textes.Comblé. Vous avez fait de ma vie de cher: Fulfilled. You've made my life as a researcher a successful one.
textes.Commander un navire qui flotte. Un seul,: To command a ship that floats. Just one, just once. To feel the helm turn under my hands, like Katell. Don't repeat that to Corentin.
textes.Comme Margaux ! Les gens du matin, je le: Like Margaux! Morning people — I admire them and I don't understand them. The best bread is at four in the morning, fine. But the best music is at midnight.
textes.Comme SECOND ?! Par la quille ! Je vais: As FIRST MATE?! By the keel! I'm telling everyone! No, wait, I'm not telling the Admiral. But everyone except her!
textes.Comme Titou ! Ceux qui bougent sont les: Like Titou! People who move look the best in long exposures: they become ghosts of light. Jump, spin… There, you've vanished. Gorgeous.
textes.Comme chaque matin depuis mille ans. Et: Like every morning for a thousand years. And I never tire of it.
textes.Comme disait ma grand-mère : jamais de c: As my grandmother used to say: never wear socks on the sand.
As the elders of Ramure say.
textes.Comme la mer : calme dessus, ça remue de: Like the sea: calm on top, churning underneath.
Like the crystal, when it's well.
textes.Comme le disait si bien un jeune voyageu: As a young traveller friend of mine put it so well: “Port-Azur, a gem!” That's you. I quote you everywhere.
textes.Comme le roc, Octave ! Ton fer chante so: Solid as a rock, Octave! Your iron sings under the bass.
textes.Comme moi ! On est pareils ! Tu sais quo: Just like me! We're the same! You know what? We'll look together. You for your island, me for my tree. I'll start with you, you look easier.
textes.Comme moi ? Alors bon courage, et dors d: Like me? Then good luck, and sleep on the boat. It's the only quiet moment of the day. Captain Léon toots the horn ever so softly when I'm asleep.
textes.Comme moi avec Gwenola. Euh, avec les po: Like me with Gwenola. Er, with the fish! With the fish, I meant. Ma doue, it's hot today.
textes.Comme moi, chaque nuit ! Hou ! Enfin que: Like me, every night! Hoo! At last someone who understands. You lose count, and you start again. That's the job.
textes.Comme mon enclume : solide, et un peu so: Like my anvil: solid, and a bit deaf.
As cabin boy, to start with.
textes.Comme quelqu'un qui écope avec une cuill: Like someone bailing with a spoon.
textes.Comme toujours, Majesté ! Ce sera six pi: As always, Majesty! That'll be six coins. Just kidding. Five.
textes.Comme tous les jours, Fundin. Pourquoi ?: Same as every day, Fundin. Why?
textes.Comme tout Carène. Ici, on préfère boite: Like all of Carène. Around here, people would rather limp than look like they're limping. I'll catch you out eventually, you know. I always do.
textes.Comme tu veux. Je suis de garde. Mais la: As you like. I'm on watch. But the high tide, yes.
textes.Comme un capitaine qui a trente ans de m: Like a captain with thirty years at sea and not a single breakdown. Touch wood.
textes.Comme un loir ! Je sens que c'est vrai :: Like a log! I can smell it's true: you look nice and fresh. Prescription: a moon tea, so you dream as well. Sleeping is good; dreaming is better.
textes.Comme un percepteur, milord. Il a fallu: Like a tax collector, milord. Had to hold it by the tail.
Like I've got two left feet.
textes.Comme un poisson ! Respect. Alors tu n'a: Like a fish! Respect. Then you've got no excuse for my starfish challenge. If you beat me, I'll do five hundred push-ups in front of the whole beach. I do them anyway, but still.
Like an admiral without a fleet: busy. A town of two hundred souls inside a leaking hull doesn't govern itself.
Like a song, very far away.
textes.Comme une pierre… Zéphyr serait vexé, il: Like a log… Zéphyr would be offended, he's forever bumping into logs. No matter: forgotten dreams fall into the clouds. Perhaps we keep a few of them for you.
textes.Comme une souche ! Par les racines de l': Like a log! By the roots of the Mother Tree, I envy you. I sleep like a brew on the stove: one eye open, watching in case I boil over.
textes.Comme une vieille coque : ça grince, mai: Like an old hull: it creaks, but it floats.
textes.Comme une épicière dont le fournisseur d: Like a grocer whose honey supplier is running late. Not good.
textes.Comme ça, Nono ? Le phoque élégant, vers: Like this, Nono? The elegant seal, version two?
textes.Comment appelle-t-on un Moaï qui danse ?: What do you call a dancing Moai?
textes.Comment appelle-t-on un chat tombé dans: What do you call a cat that fell into a pot of paint on Christmas Day? A Christmas paw-trait! … Hey, that's one of Paulo's jokes, not mine.
textes.Comment appelle-t-on un chien qui n'a pa: What do you call a dog with no legs?
textes.Comment attirer le perroquet de la capit: How do I lure the captain's parrot?
textes.Comment devenir citoyen de Port-Azur ?: How do I become a citizen of Port-Azur?
textes.Comment rejoindre ton île ?: How do I get to your island?
textes.Comment ta vie a commencé, ici ?: How did your life here begin?
textes.Comment un Moaï dit-il bonjour ?: How does a Moai say hello?
textes.Comment va ta barque ? Je lui dis bonjou: How's your rowboat? I say hello to her every morning at the jetty. She doesn't answer, but she floats.
textes.Comment va votre lame, my dear ? Si un j: How is your blade, my dear? If one day it retires, my display case awaits. With a golden label.
textes.Comment ça va ? Ça va qu'il y a un rival: How am I? I'm a man with a rival on the other side of the island telling tall tales about him, that's how.
textes.Comète repasse l'anneau d'or la première: Comète flies through the golden ring first: “VZIIIOU! I win!” She does a happy loop-the-loop. “Come on, rematch! Fly through the golden ring whenever you like!”
textes.Comète t'attend près de l'anneau d'or, a: Comète is waiting near the golden ring, above the Spaceport. Fly through it to start the race!
textes.Comète, depuis sa soucoupe : « Vziiiou !: Comète, from her saucer: “Vziiiou! No walking! Hop into your Star Glider (N key) and fly through the golden ring!”
textes.Comète, la pilote de soucoupe, s'ennuie: Comète, the saucer pilot, is bored: nobody wants to race her. Now that you have the Star Glider, she challenges you: first a practice run on the ring course of the Zero-Gravity Garden, then the great ring race in the sky, around Astralys.
textes.Comète, tu cherches un adversaire ?: Comète, are you looking for an opponent?
textes.Confiance ? Peuchère. Vous êtes un agnea: Trust? Good heavens. You're a little lamb. Here, you can. Elsewhere, count. Especially at the souvenir shop.
textes.Construire une passerelle si douce que S: To build a walkway so gentle that Sylwen climbs up it one day, with a tray. I've already drawn it: wide handrail, new planks, not a single crack. It'll be called “Just-Once”.
textes.Content ! J'ai retrouvé ma casquette, el: Happy! I found my cap, it was on Momo's head.
textes.Contrarié. Mon appareil photo ! J'ai dû: Annoyed. My camera! I must have put it down somewhere up there, at the lookout, while photographing the sunset.
textes.Contre qui ? Contre Bondi, alors. Deuxiè: Against who? Against Bondi, then. Second behind Bondi is… wait, I'm thinking… it's very good! Isn't it? Yes. Well, I think. You make me think, you do, it's tiring.
textes.Contre une lampe, comme d'habitude. Elle: For a lamp, as usual. This one's smaller than the last.
textes.Cool ! Alors je te lance un défi : le to: Cool! Then I challenge you: once round the harbour wall on “Wave 3”, against the clock. Kevin holds the record. OK, Kevin was swimming, but still.
textes.Cool. Le vent est parfait. Enfin, il est: Cool. The wind's perfect. Well, it's always perfect, I decide that.
textes.Coralin ! C'est un poisson ou un oursin,: Coralin! Is it a fish or a sea urchin today?
textes.Coralin ! Ta lampe de la semaine est un: Coralin! This week's lamp is a bit small.
textes.Coralin ? Mon sujet d'étude préféré. Per: Coralin? My favourite subject of study. Nobody gets things wrong with so much energy, or so much talent. His scrolls are the thickest in the library.
textes.Coralin ? Un génie du corail, un radin d: Coralin? A coral genius, a first-class penny-pincher and my almost-fiancé for four hundred years. He says my crackers are filling. He buys a bag a week.
textes.Coralin a des mains d'or et un caractère: Coralin has hands of gold and the temper of a sea urchin. He claims I still owe him for the mother-of-pearl throne. It may be true. I have no intention of checking.
textes.Coralin est le premier enfant né sous le: Coralin is the first child born under the dome. He cried so loud the crystal flickered, and the whole city laughed, for the first time since the wave. I've never told him, he'd become unbearable: that was the day I believed we could live here.
textes.Coralin fait semblant d'être grognon, ma: Coralin pretends to be grumpy, but he keeps his mother-of-pearl offcuts in a box marked “NOT FOR ONDINE”. So they must be for me, otherwise why would he write my name?
textes.Coralin m'a dit qu'une pomme, c'est un o: Coralin told me an apple is a red sea urchin that grows on trees. I did a drawing: a tree full of sea urchins. Abyssos filed it in the scroll of Coralin's mistakes. Coralin was furious. I was proud: it's my first drawing in the archives!
textes.Coralin m'a taillé ce trident en une heu: Coralin carved me this trident in an hour, on the night of the sharks. It bites a little. So does Coralin. But they're both good tools.
textes.Coralin parle à ses sculptures. Je l'ai: Coralin talks to his sculptures. I heard him. He tells them “good night”.
textes.Coralin se plaint des requins. Il a rais: Coralin complains about the sharks. He's right: they steal his shark teeth. … Well, the other way round.
textes.Coralin, c'est le meilleur tailleur de l: Coralin is the best carver in the city. He hasn't really spoken to me for a hundred years, but he does greet me. With his chin. That's something.
textes.Coralin, ton requin t'a rendu ton ciseau: Coralin, has your shark given you back your chisel?
textes.Coralin. Rien de cassé, aujourd'hui ? Mo: Coralin. Nothing broken today? My scroll is hungry.
textes.Corentin ! J'ai trouvé une deuxième bott: Corentin! I found a second boot in the basin!
textes.Corentin ! Par la lune, tu tangues encor: Corentin! By the moon, still rolling?
textes.Corentin ? Le petit-fils de Yann-le-Borg: Corentin? Yann-le-Borgne's grandson? Ha! Yes, I have the logbook. Here it is… But look: the pages that talk about the seal are blank. Moon ink, the sailors called it: it can only be read by the light of a moon you carry with you. I never understood it. Keep it, it may speak to you one day. And since you're chasing after the seals: ours, the desert one, sleeps beneath the walking dune. Rachid, the carpet merchant, has an old carpet that shows the way. He'll tell you… if he stops going on about his prices.
textes.Corentin a le cœur d'un phoque et l'idée: Corentin has the heart of a seal and the fixed idea that my seaweed store is the best hiding place for his hot honey drink. He's not wrong: nobody touches it. Except me.
textes.Corentin dit qu'il y a un monstre dans l: Corentin says there's a monster in the basin. I looked for it a whole afternoon. I found a boot.
textes.Corentin dit que la coque chante, les nu: Corentin says the hull sings on calm nights. He's right. But I've never told anyone, {surnom}: underwater, I hear it better than he does. And it doesn't come from the wood. It comes from below, from the stones. My grandmother heard it too. One day, she went down to see. She never dived again. She never said why.
textes.Corentin m'a dit qu'il y avait un monstr: Corentin told me there was a monster in the harbour basin. I searched for it a whole afternoon with a shrimping net. I found a boot. The week after, I found a second one! Corentin says the monster has two feet. I think it's a monster that keeps losing its boots.
textes.Corentin me cache ses grogs dans ma rése: Corentin hides his mugs of hot honey in my seaweed store. He thinks I don't know.
textes.Corentin raconte au coin de mon poêle de: Corentin has been telling stories by my stove for over fifty years. His stories change a little every night. His hot honeys, though, I count, and the numbers don't change.
textes.Corentin rit de mon titre depuis trente: Corentin has been laughing at my title for thirty years. He tells my ancestor's story better than I do, and it annoys me. He's right about a lot of things. That annoys me too.
textes.Corentin, de Carène ! Un conteur qui tan: Corentin, from Carène! A storyteller who rolls with the waves. He knows the end of every one of his stories, that one. I'm a bit jealous. Very, in fact. Don't tell him.
textes.Corentin, de Carène, cherche le journal: Corentin, from Carène, is looking for the Leviathan's logbook.
textes.Corentin, hier, ta baleine avait cinq ar: Corentin, yesterday your whale had five trees.
textes.Corentin, ta bolée est vide et ta bouche: Corentin, your mug is empty and your mouth is full of stories.
textes.Corentin, tu n'aurais pas oublié quelque: Corentin, you didn't forget something in my seaweed, did you?
textes.Corentin. Encore une histoire sur moi, c: Corentin. Another story about me tonight?
textes.Corne-Sur-Nez : gros, grincheux. Il grat: Horn-On-Nose: big, grumpy. He scrape ground with foot, then he CHARGE. You not stay in front! If he charge into rock: bong! He see stars. Hit!
textes.Correcte. Merci de demander, personne ne: Fair. Thank you for asking, nobody ever asks.
textes.Coucou ! Dis, t'as un frère ou une sœur,: Hiya! Say, have you got a brother or a sister? I've got Pomme-de-Pin! She makes bridges!
textes.Coucou ! Dis-moi, toi : un pont qui boug: Yoo-hoo! Tell me: a wobbly bridge, how do you cross it?
textes.Coucou ! Du courrier pour la lune ?: Yoo-hoo! Any post for the moon?
textes.Coucou ! Il chante juste ?: Hiya! Does it sing in tune?
textes.Coucou ! Il va bien, ton frère ou ta sœu: Hiya! How's your brother or sister? Did you teach them to hide hazelnuts?
textes.Coucou ! J'ai pas oublié : je te prête P: Hiya! I haven't forgotten: I'm lending you Pomme-de-Pin. One day. Not today, she's working.
textes.Coucou ! J'ai retrouvé une noisette ! Il: Cuckoo! I found a hazelnut! Only two hundred and ninety-nine to go!
textes.Coucou ! J'ai sept ans et j'habite dans: Hiya! I'm seven and I live in the west tree with my big sister Pomme-de-Pin and Granny Faîne. Dad's called Noyer and Mum's called Châtaigne! In the fine season they gather fallen wood in the deep forest, really far away, and they come home in winter with pockets full of stories. Winter's my favourite season. Guess why!
textes.Coucou ! Ma grand-mère, Mamie Faîne, a c: Yoo-hoo! My grandma, Granny Faîne, built almost every bridge in Ramure. Me, I tied my first knot at four, round her tail! She taught me the two squirrel rules: a bridge must dance with the wind, and you never cut down a living tree. Never! Only the fallen wood that Mum and Dad bring back from the deep forest.
textes.Coucou ! T'as des noisettes ? Non ? Domm: Cuckoo! Got any hazelnuts? No? Shame. I'm Gland. I hid three hundred. Can't remember where. Will you help me look?
textes.Coucou ! Tes clous sont trop gros !: Yoo-hoo! Your nails are too big!
textes.Coucou ! Ton miel, tout frais d'en haut: Yoo-hoo! Your honey, fresh from up top!
textes.Coucou ! Tu as traversé le pont de l'oue: Cuckoo! Did you cross the west bridge? It sings when the wind blows. I did that on purpose.
textes.Coucou ! Tu brilles pas du tout, toi. C': Hiya! You don't glow at all, you. Is that normal for a human? Welcome!
textes.Coucou, Bedaine ! T'as quelque chose pou: Yoo-hoo, Bedaine! Got anything for me?
textes.Coucou, Grommelot ! Mes graines ont fait: Hiya, Grommelot! Did my seeds go pop?
textes.Coucou, Grommelot ! Tu as reçu mes grain: Hello, Grommelot! Did you get my corn kernels?
textes.Coucou, coucou ! Pomme-de-Pin ! Charpent: Cuckoo, cuckoo! Pomme-de-Pin! Carpenter! Every bridge in Ramure is me! Well, me and my family. And my grandma. Mostly my grandma. They sway a bit? That's normal! That's the point!
textes.Coucou, la flèche ! Tu cours toujours su: Yoo-hoo, speedy! Still running across my bridges? Slow down in the middle, just once: listen.
textes.Coucou, toi qui as plein de frères et sœ: Hiya, you with all the brothers and sisters! Will you introduce me? Do they like hazelnuts?
textes.Coucou… Ils font boum-boum, comme moi. C: Hiya… They go boom-boom, like me. It's magic.
textes.Coucou… Tu sens la vibration dans le sab: Hiya… Can you feel the vibration in the sand? Close your eyes, it's magical.
textes.Couic ! Biscotte surgit de nulle part et: Squeak! Biscotte appears out of nowhere and climbs onto your shoulder.
textes.Couleurs de Gaston, en poisson. On ne le: Gaston's colours, as a fish. Found only in the jungle bay. Restores two hearts.
textes.Coups de marteau, copeaux qui volent, un: Hammer blows, flying wood shavings, a night of work… and here is the Sloop! Its cabin still smells of varnish. It's waiting for you at the pleasure-boat jetty.
textes.Courir coûte deux fois moins d'endurance: Running costs half the stamina, and you run 10% faster.
textes.Courir de la fontaine de la place à la p: Run from the fountain on the square to the lighthouse door in under 60 seconds
textes.Course abandonnée. Retourne à la fontain: Race abandoned. Go back to the fountain to try again.
textes.Coyotl demande si c'est vous qui m'envoy: Coyotl asks if you're the one who sent me.
textes.Coyotl et ses manières ! Oui. Dis-lui qu: Coyotl and his manners! Yes. Tell him that Cuauhtli the Eagle sends you, and that Tlaloc is thirsty.
textes.Coyotl, le potier d'Aztlán, façonne les: Coyotl, the potter of Aztlán, shapes Tlaloc's rain jars; but he only gives one away if the high priest sends you to ask.
textes.Creuser (pelle en main) là où l'ombre du: Dig (shovel in hand) where the shadow of the Houseboat's mast touches the sea at noon: on the sand, between the mast and the water
textes.Creuser le sable près de la paillote, au: Dig in the sand near the beach hut, at the water's edge (shovel in hand)
textes.Croc-Gris veille en haut, je piste en ba: Croc-Gris keeps watch up top, I track down below. He's gruff, he says “Halt” to the squirrels. I like him. Every morning, I give him my report. He says “Hm”. That means thank you.
textes.Croc-Gris veille sur nous depuis trente: Croc-Gris has watched over us for thirty years, and he hasn't smiled for twenty-nine. A good wolf. Too serious. I'm working on it.
Croc-Gris has watched over us for thirty years. He's never quite forgiven me for the monster. I like him. He's gentler than he'd like to believe.
textes.Croc-Gris, c'est le garde. Il dit « Halt: Croc-Gris is the guard. He says “Halt!” to everyone, even the leaves. He's got the best house in the village, right at the top, with the zip line! He growls, but he's nice. Shh.
textes.Croc-Gris, il dira « Halte ! », et moi j: Croc-Gris will say “Halt!”, and I'll say “Hot bread!”, and he'll smile. Even him. Nobody can resist hot bread.
textes.Croc-de-Sel se dit « pirate moderne ». I: Croc-de-Sel calls himself a “modern pirate”. He has a silver tooth and a tin mouth. An honest adversary, in his way: he always lies the same way.
textes.Croc-de-Sel. Toujours à chercher ce qui: Croc-de-Sel. Still looking for what isn't yours?
textes.Croissant ! Le choix des gens simples et: Croissant! The choice of simple, happy people. And of the sergeant. Well, simple, happy people all the same.
textes.Croissant de contrôle, madame. Tout est: Inspection croissant, madam. Is everything in order?
textes.Croquant ! Comme un coquillage ? Il faut: Crunchy! Like a shell? I have to taste one. Will you bring me some?
textes.Croquer un piment infernal devant le Pro: Bite into an infernal chili in front of Professor Malachar (Zébuline sells them at the Great Market)
textes.Croâ ! Tu as entendu ? Il a entendu. Le: Croâ! Did you hear that? He heard. Look at him puffing up his feathers. Thanks, {surnom}: now he'll think he's an eagle AND a king.
textes.Croâ dit qu'il a vu une porte de pierre,: Croâ says he saw a stone door, right at the top, on the edge of the crater. Croâ also says he's an eagle. So…
textes.Croâ n'a pas oublié que tu préfères les: Croâ hasn't forgotten that you prefer crows. He's saving you a feather. An old one. He's a bit stingy.
textes.Croâ porte son nouveau manteau de plumes: Croâ is wearing his new feather coat. He's unbearably proud.
textes.Croâ refuse. Il dit que vous savez march: Croâ refuses. He says you know how to walk.
Cuauhtli sent me: Tlaloc is thirsty.
textes.Cuauhtli, le grand prêtre d'Aztlán, cher: Cuauhtli, the high priest of Aztlán, is looking for someone to offer rain to Tlaloc and fire to Huitzilopochtli at the top of the Great Temple, and to go down beneath the temple, into the hall of the Five Suns.
textes.Cueillies sous la lune, comptées, parfai: Picked under the moon, counted, perfect. The usual price?
textes.Cueillir cinq bouquets de cempasúchil su: Pick five bouquets of cempasúchil on the chinampas, south and west of the lake of Aztlán
textes.Cueillir cinq fleurs de braise sur les p: Pick five ember flowers on the slopes of the Great Blaze (away from the lava flows)
textes.Cueillir les cinq champignons de lune, a: Pick the five moon mushrooms at the edge of the forest ponds around Ramure (the big pond west of the Circle, the pond in the Games Clearing, and the ones to the west, south and north)
textes.Cueillir trois champignons des bois dans: Pick three wild mushrooms in the Twisted Wood (south-west of the island)
textes.Cueillir trois touffes d'herbe à fièvre: Pick three tufts of feverweed at the water's edge in the Drowned Marsh (west of the island)
textes.Cueillir un Arc-en-ciel, aux lamelles de: Pick a Rainbow, with gills of every colour (in the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Cueillir un Babillard, qui fait de petit: Pick a Chatterbox, which makes little noises when you come near (in the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Cueillir un Bolet-Ressort, au chapeau or: Pick a Spring-Bolete, with its bouncy orange cap (in the Spore Cathedral, the old gasholder south of the town)
textes.Cueillir un Petit-Géant, minuscule mais: Pick a Little-Giant, tiny but very proud (in the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Cueillir un bouquet de tournesols dans l: Pick a bunch of sunflowers in Granny Sunflower's garden (in the Flower Camp, south-west of the campfire)
textes.Cueillir une Lunaire, pâle et argentée (: Pick a Moonling, pale and silvery (in the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Curieuse, comme toujours. J'ai goûté une: Curious, as always. I tasted a jungle berry this morning. I'll tell you tomorrow whether it was a good idea.
textes.Curieuse. Toujours curieuse. C'est mon h: Curious. Always curious. It's my favourite mood.
textes.Côté est, la mer est plus profonde. Les: On the east side, the sea is deeper. The big groupers hang around there. Bring me one, I'll pay you well.
All right, I'll take care of it.
textes.D'accord, je rentre au Temple. Que l'Aub: All right, I'll go back to the Temple. May the Dawn watch over you… and over your socks.
textes.D'accord, mais elle a déjà mangé tout le: Okay, but she's already eaten all the honey!
textes.D'accord, mon frère. Juste une banane à: Deal, my brother. Just one banana for the little one there.
textes.D'accord. Je respecte. Je te photographi: OK. I respect that. I'll photograph you in my head, then. It's blurry, but it doesn't fade.
textes.D'accord. Je retourne à mes livres. Merc: All right. I'll go back to my books. Thank you for taking me along…
All right. But I'll dance slowly.
textes.D'accord. Île grande. Mais pas trop atte: All right. Island big. But not wait too long: Grosse-Dent very hungry.
textes.D'au-dessus des nuages, Bastien. Comme h: From above the clouds, Bastien. Like yesterday.
textes.D'en haut, à la cime, on voit la mer à l: From up top, at the crown, you see the sea to the east and the mountain to the west. Go up at sunset. Don't tell anyone: it gets too crowded after.
textes.D'ici, le belvédère, on voit tout le por: From here, the lookout, you can see the whole harbour. In the morning it's blue, in the evening it's pink. I can never manage to paint the pink.
textes.D'ici, on voit tout : la baie, les deux: From here you can see everything: the bay, the two points, the meadows, and Stoneheart in the distance, with the highland snow behind it. On a clear day you can even see the caravans' smoke, to the south.
textes.D'ici, on voit toute la place. Et tout l: From here, you can see the whole square. And everyone. I know everything that happens in the village. Everything.
textes.D'un jardin où les vieux elfes boivent l: From a garden where old elves drink their tea while it's hot.
From an island far from here.
textes.DING DING DING ! Mélusine hurle depuis l: DING DING DING! Mélusine shouts from the Town Square: “ALERT! ALERT! All adventurers to the Southern Fields: THE TURNIPS HAVE WOKEN UP! Catch them before they replant themselves!”
textes.DONG… DONG… La cloche du Léviathan réson: DONG… DONG… The Léviathan's bell echoes through the whole hull. Somewhere, Ewen shouts: “It wasn't me!”
textes.Dagna ! Ton ragoût s'est vendu en une he: Dagna! Your stew sold out in an hour!
textes.Dagna ! Un tonneau de blonde pour ton ra: Dagna! A barrel of golden fizz to go with your stew.
textes.Dagna croit que mes corbeaux me réponden: Dagna thinks my crows answer me. She's right, but I won't tell her: she'd repeat it to a hundred dwarves before the stew.
textes.Dagna dit que c'est son ragoût qui fait: Dagna says it's her stew that sells my fizz. It's my fizz that washes down her stew! But I resell it at twice the price, so I don't say anything. Hardly anything.
textes.Dagna est persuadée que mon fromage boug: Dagna is convinced my cheese moves on its own. One evening, for a laugh, I slipped Croâ under the cloth. The cheese crossed the table cawing. Dagna dropped her spoon. Ever since, she puts my cheese in the stew as fast as she can. She says it's to calm it down.
textes.Dagna m'a donné un toit, un four et un b: Dagna gave me a roof, an oven and a bowl of stew the day I had nothing left. She sells my fizz on the terrace. I owe her everything. She says all I owe her is barrels.
textes.Dagna me nourrit à midi, que j'aie faim: Dagna feeds me at noon, hungry or not. She counts my smiles. She counts too much. But her stew keeps me warm all through the night watch.
textes.Dagna met trop de champignons dans son r: Dagna puts too many mushrooms in her stew, too much salt in her tempers and too much heart in everything else. The terrace would stand without its gates. Not without her.
Dagna puts too many mushrooms in her stew. I say so, and then I have three helpings.
textes.Dagna, ton ragoût fait chanter mes corbe: Dagna, your stew makes my crows sing.
textes.Dans Yggdrasil, des plantes se sont réve: Inside Yggdrasil, plants have awoken, nasty and hungry. Mother Bramble guards the Tree's crown.
In this one, you've got a hat.
textes.Dans chaque lettre, Perlée me demande co: In every letter Perlée asks me how many drops I've lost this week. I always answer “none”. But my letters arrive wet, so she knows. She doesn't say anything. In the next letter, she asks again. It's her way of loving me.
textes.Dans l'affaire des croissants, il est ve: In the croissant affair, he came to question me. Officially: notebook, pencil, cap. Except he had a vanilla cone in his other hand. “Where were you… mmh… last night?” The ice cream dripped onto his notebook. By the end, his notes were unreadable and sticky. He still “kept an eye on the ice-cream man” all week.
textes.Dans la Bergerie du Vent, j'ai vu une lu: In the Wind Sheepfold, I saw a moon above a pond and a sluice gate.
textes.Dans la baie de la jungle, il y a des po: In the jungle bay there are parrotfish. They're every colour under the sun and they bite like lawyers.
textes.Dans la cité, va à la Chope Ardente. Dis: In the city, go to the Blazing Mug. Tell Ulfa I sent you. She doesn't know me, but say it anyway.
textes.Dans la forêt des brumes, je me suis per: In the misty forest, I was lost for four days. The compass spun on its own, the moss wiped out my footprints. On the fifth morning, I found a line of shells laid on the moss, one every ten paces. I followed it to the edge of the woods. Nobody. Just shells, like the ones on Fañch's boat. They're drawn in notebook four.
textes.Dans la longue-vue, toute l'île, en noir: In the spyglass, the whole island, in black and white…
textes.Dans la poche d'un vieux manteau :: In the pocket of an old coat:
textes.Dans la première salle de l'Arbre, les l: In the Tree's first hall, the fireflies sing a tune in light. Listen with your eyes, and step on the stones in the same order!
textes.Dans la salle de la Sève, la lumière ne: In the Hall of Sap, light only goes straight… unless a mirror-flower turns it. Turn them until the light touches the heartwood.
textes.Dans le Glisseur stellaire ! La coque vi: In the Star Glider! The hull hums softly, the lights come on one by one.
textes.Dans le berceau : « Rrr… pfff… rrr… » Le: In the cradle: “Zzz… pfff… zzz…” The baby dwarf is already snoring like a forge.
textes.Dans le coffre : des jouets, une épée en: In the chest: toys, a wooden sword, a one-eyed teddy bear. Nobody.
textes.Dans le coffre : quarante pièces… et le: In the chest: forty coins… and the Crystal of the Dawn, warm as a rising sun. It will fit into the Seal of Winds, in front of the keep.
textes.Dans le coffre de la salle d'armes : qua: In the armoury chest: forty coins, a gold coin… and the Crystal of the Dusk, cold and blue as the evening. The Seal of Winds is waiting for it.
textes.Dans le coffret, au pied du sarcophage :: In the casket, at the foot of the sarcophagus: the last piece of Osiris.
textes.Dans le dôme, on respire. Dehors, il fau: Inside the dome, you can breathe. Outside, you need a mask, or to hold your breath. You have the mask of the Sky Kings. You're lucky.
textes.Dans le grand registre d'Orsik, il y a u: In Orsik's big ledger there's an empty line, on the eve of the king's coronation, ninety years ago. I asked him what went there. He said: “A smudge.” There was no smudge. He went all pale. I never asked again. But I never filled in the line either.
textes.Dans le sable, deux bouteilles de limona: In the sand, two bottles of lemonade buried to keep cool, with a label: “To share.”
textes.Dans le tombeau du désert, une fresque m: In the desert tomb, a fresco shows a sheepfold beneath the mountain.
textes.Dans les livres de quart rangés à la mai: In the logbooks kept at the town hall, I found the same sentence, in the same hand, night after night, for years: “Blue glow, to the west.” Never any comment. I copied it a hundred and twelve times into my journal. When I told Anselme, he went quite pale, then quite red, and shut his door on me. Rightly so, perhaps.
textes.Dans les vieux textes, on parle d'un gra: The old texts speak of a great crystal that gave air and light to a whole city. And of a queen with hair of sea foam.
textes.Dans mon vieux livre de remèdes, il y a: In my old book of remedies, there's a drawing of the elves' moonflower, in faded ink. Rose copied it out big and pinned it above her sink. I have it above my counter. We promised each other that the day we see a real one, we won't pick it. Just look at it.
textes.Dans son cercle, sur la place, on servai: In his circle, on the square, they served tea before every story. “Tea first,” Ba Sidi would say. I drank eleven glasses. Eleven! By the tenth story, I was telling it standing on a stool. Ba Sidi said it was the first time a bear had danced in his halqa. It wasn't a dance. It was the tea.
textes.Dans son histoire, je combats une pieuvr: In his story, I fight a thirty-armed octopus for three days and three nights. The children come and ask to see my scar. I do have one, but it was a shark, the first year. Just one, very ordinary. They're disappointed. I hate disappointing children. Thanks, Protée.
textes.Dans ton sac, le journal de bord se met: In your bag, the logbook starts to glow! In the Moonglow, silver lines appear on the blank pages: “I entrusted the Seal of Sea Spray to our Figurehead Lady. She will only give it back to whoever shows her her three sisters: the sands, the bronze and the mists. — Yves Kerhervé, last captain of the Léviathan.”
textes.Dans un cliquetis, les trois armures de: With a clatter, the three suits of armour in the armoury turn their heads toward you… and draw their swords.
textes.Dans un coin, un berceau. Dedans, un tou: In a corner, a cradle. Inside, a tiny dwarf sleeping, fists clenched like two little hammers.
textes.Dans un tombeau qui ne crache plus de fl: In a tomb that no longer spits flames: a vial of sap and a handful of coins. (The owner has gone on vacation.)
textes.Danser au mariage de Lulu, un jour. Être: To dance at Lulu's wedding one day. To be invited, show up on time, and dance with my daughter without looking anywhere else. Just one waltz. Even at a hundred and forty-five.
textes.Danser le pogo à un concert de la Halle: Join the mosh pit at a Howling Hall concert
textes.Danser un jour sur une vraie plage, là-h: To dance one day on a real beach, up there, on warm sand, with no ledge and no canal to fall into. And see if you can splash the sun.
textes.Danser une dernière fois au Cercle, peti: To dance one last time at the Circle, little one. For real, not just in my head. With Tilleul, who walks as badly as I do: between the two of us, we'll make a lovely crooked step.
To dance one night in the square at Tazira. To see if the moon over there, the one that grows thin, watches me too.
textes.Danser à la Nuit des Lanternes: Dance at the Night of Lanterns
textes.Danser à la prochaine fête de l'Aube jus: To dance at the next Dawn festival until sunrise, with Ilyria's longest ribbon. And at dawn, for someone to finally hand me a letter, instead of running off again.
textes.De belles plumes noires ! Croâ va être j: Lovely black feathers! Croâ will be jealous. Here: three cheeses and twenty coins. Eat the cheese quickly. It's… alive.
textes.De face ! Franc, direct, j'aime ça. Rega: Front view! Frank, direct, I like that. Look at the lens, smile… there. I can picture you already. Nicely centred, for once.
textes.De l'autre côté de l'île, à l'est, un vi: On the other side of the island, to the east, an old grump lives perched in a tree. Octave Taillefer. He sells shovels that bend and swords that rust. Don't tell him you know me.
textes.De l'eau ? Au Coco Loco ? … Bon. D'accor: Water? At the Coco Loco? … Fine. All right. I'll still give you a slice of lemon and a little umbrella. Got to keep up the style.
textes.De l'eau avec la lune dedans. Ça reste d: Water with the moon in it. Still water!
textes.De l'eau, c'est de l'eau. Même avec la l: Water is water. Even with the moon in it.
textes.De l'herbe, de la terre, et pas le moind: Grass, earth, and not the slightest eye. This one is looking at its feet… which it doesn't have.
textes.De l'obsidienne pure ! Regarde comme ell: Pure obsidian! See how it drinks the light. Here, two gold coins from my chest. And a rune carved into your memory: “Fire guards fire.” You'll understand one day.
textes.De la brume du matin, cueillie sur la gr: Morning mist, gathered over the big pond and bottled by Pivoine. It swirls gently behind the glass.
textes.De la graisse de chèvre du désert ! Ça n: Desert goat fat! That's completely different!
textes.De la mer ! Quelle réponse ! Comme dans: From the sea! What an answer! Like in the legends. I'll draw you a little wave in the corner of my map. With a question mark. Does that suit you?
textes.De la mer ?! Il y a des graines dans la: From the sea?! Are there seeds in the sea? Seaweed seeds? Oh, I need a seaweed seed. I absolutely need one.
textes.De la mer vers les nuages. Elles t'enten: From the sea towards the clouds. They can hear you.
textes.De la tisane. C'est tout ce qu'il en res: Herbal tea. That's all that's left of it.
textes.De ma terrasse, je vois tout : la fontai: From my terrace I see everything: the fountain, the clock, the sweethearts, the pickpockets. There aren't any pickpockets. But I'd see them.
textes.De midi à quatre heures, je remplace mon: From noon to four, I stand in for my uncle on watch. I keep an eye on the forest. Well, mostly on the Games Clearing, to watch Bondi train. Two years ago Éclair fell at the root bend; I shouted “you OK?” as I went by, without stopping, it was the race. Since then she looks at me like a skewer. She's cross with me, I think. I get it, mind you.
textes.De mon kiosque je vois la plage, la prom: From my kiosk I can see the beach, the promenade and the beach hut. I know everything that happens here. Well, everything that happens between ten in the morning and eight at night.
textes.De mon temps, les voitures roulaient par: In my day, cars drove on the ground. They did, really.
textes.De neuf heures à dix-neuf heures, je sui: From nine in the morning to seven at night, I'm on my chair. Five hundred push-ups between whistles. I fish out Yannick's customers, I keep an eye on my starfish challenge, my mum shouts for me to come and help her. In the evening, punch at Kiki's beach hut with Yannick. Then I go home to Lighthouse Street, where my neighbour the sergeant greets me very politely. Too politely.
textes.De onze à seize heures, ses cartes des f: From eleven till four, his charts of the seabed cover the drawing-room carpet. I walk around them. The guests walk around them. One day, a little boy stepped on an ocean trench, and the professor let out a cry. Since then, when he goes up to the lookout, I tidy them by order of depth. He's never noticed a thing. Or he pretends not to.
textes.De passage. Comme les voiliers. Ils dise: Passing through. Like the sailboats. They all say that, and half of them come back the next year. I'll put you down in pencil.
textes.De plus en plus souvent, les robots démé: More and more often, Mr Lisse's mover robots land on the quays to clear out the squats. Mamie Barricade would like you to help the Boucan fight off the next Movers' Raid.
textes.De profil ! Ah, vous avez un bon profil,: Profile! Ah, you do have a good profile, it's true. The left? The right? I'll let you know. I need golden light and a bit of luck.
textes.De quoi tu parles ? Je ne t'ai rien dema: What are you on about? I didn't ask you for anything.
textes.De quoi veux-tu parler ?: What do you want to talk about?
textes.De quoi voulez-vous parler ?: What would you like to talk about?
textes.De retour au sommet du Grand Temple, ent: Back at the top of the Great Temple, between Tlaloc and Huitzilopochtli.
textes.De retour au sommet du Temple de Kukulka: Back at the top of the Temple of Kukulkan. The sun, at last.
textes.De retour dans la nef de la Cathédrale-F: Back in the nave of the Forge Cathedral. It's nice and warm here.
textes.De retour sur le plateau de Rê, devant l: Back on the plateau of Ra, in front of the pyramid door.
textes.De retour à la lumière, devant la Porte: Back in the light, in front of the Gate of the Four Seals.
textes.De rien, Bramm. Mange tant que c'est cha: You're welcome, Bramm. Eat it while it's hot.
You're welcome. And smile, it costs nothing.
textes.De rien. Hm. Menteur. Ou nain. Les nains: Nothing. Hm. Liar. Or dwarf. Dwarves say that too.
textes.De temps en temps, Victor entre chez moi: Now and then, Victor comes into my shop with a real rare shell, found on the beach, to change my mind. A tiger cone, once, magnificent. I looked at it through the loupe, weighed it and paid the fair price. Not a penny more, not a smile. He left happy anyway. He's always happy. That's his flaw.
textes.Debout, matelot ! Le soleil se lève sur: Rise and shine, sailor! The sun is rising over the sea.
textes.Dehors ! Comme la dernière fois. Mais pl: Out! Like last time. But faster.
textes.Demain, alors ! Et un fromage, en attend: Tomorrow, then! And a cheese, in the meantime.
textes.Demain, cinq heures ? Le vent sera de su: Tomorrow, five o'clock? The wind'll be south-westerly.
textes.Demain, du soleil. Les cartes sont forme: Tomorrow, sunshine. The cards are adamant.
textes.Demain, on essaie au milieu ?: Tomorrow, shall we try somewhere in the middle?
textes.Demain, pêche à cinq heures. Qui vient ?: Tomorrow, fishing at five. Who's coming?
textes.Demain, pêche à cinq heures. Tu viens ?: Tomorrow, fishing at five. Coming? I ask everybody, nobody ever comes.
textes.Demande-moi de lire ton avenir. Je te di: Ask me to read your future. I'll tell you what the people here are hoping you'll do.
textes.Demander conseil à Perroquet-Joe (son ét: Ask Perroquet-Joe for advice (his stall is on the square of Port-Coutelas, near the well)
textes.Demander des pâtes fraîches à Mamma Lasa: Ask Mamma Lasagna for fresh pasta (at the Pasta Drying Shed in the daytime, at the oven on the Borgo's little piazza at noon and in the evening)
textes.Demander la Clé du Brasier à Frère Cendr: Ask Brother Cendrin for the Brasier key (in the Forge Cathedral, near the Ember Heart)
textes.Demander un grimoire à Théophraste Filan: Ask Théophraste Filandre for a spellbook, at the library (the big slate building, on the way up to the Academy)
textes.Demander une carte stellaire à Sextant (: Ask Sextant for a star chart (in the morning on the Gate lookout, around noon at the Museum, in the afternoon on the Observatory bridge, in the Gardens or at the Spaceport)
textes.Demander à Cargo, le grand androïde dock: Ask Cargo, the big docker android on the Drone Quay (north of the city), if he has a Z-Series voice chip
textes.Demander à Cuauhtli, le grand prêtre (au: Ask Cuauhtli, the high priest (at the foot of the Great Temple), to send you to Coyotl
textes.Demander à Lucas, le docker, le nom de s: Ask Lucas the docker the name of his boat
textes.Demander à Pépé Fernand le nom de sa bar: Ask Grandpa Fernand the name of his boat (on the quay, to the east)
textes.Demander à Sextant s'il a vu Plume-de-Nu: Ask Sextant if he has seen Plume-de-Nuage (he sketches on the Gate lookout in the morning, at the Museum around noon, then on the Observatory bridge, in the Gardens or at the Spaceport)
textes.Demander à Yannick le nom de ses bateaux: Ask Yannick the names of his boats (boat hire, on the quay)
textes.Depuis cent ans, c'est notre façon de no: For a hundred years, that's been our way of saying good morning.
textes.Depuis cet hiver, Bernard fait un détour: Since this winter, Bernard has been taking a detour through the fishermen's alley so as not to pass my window. I can hear him: “hop hop hop” fading away, then coming back on the other side. He adds three hundred metres to his lap to avoid me. Not exactly what I prescribed.
textes.Depuis ma prédiction, Hortense regarde c: Ever since my prediction, Hortense watches every stranger who steps off L'Hirondelle. An umbrella seller, two tourists, a gentleman with a goat. She looks them up and down, then sighs. She says she's keeping an eye on the time. I say she's keeping an eye on the quay.
textes.Depuis mes cinq ans, je cherche le Roi d: Since I was five, I've been looking for the Pond King with Grandpa. He's golden, big as a rabbit, and he laughs. One day I drew him. With a crown, because a king has a crown, that's normal. Grandpa looked at the drawing for a super long time, without saying anything. Even his whiskers stopped moving. Then he pinned it above his bed.
textes.Depuis minuit, Taeron. Je t'ai laissé un: Since midnight, Taeron. I left you a lantern next to it.
textes.Depuis que Barnabé passe à la teuf avec: Ever since Barnabé started coming to the party with Gaston on his shoulder, the parrot imitates the kick drum. One night, walking home through the jungle, I heard “Boom. Boom.” in the dark, right on a hundred and forty-five. I thought Mistral had put a speaker in the trees. It was Gaston, all alone, on a branch. I ran all the way home.
textes.Depuis que l'horloge s'est arrêtée, c'es: Since the clock stopped, I'm the one who tells Django the time. Fifty years of clockwork, it stays in your bones. Before going home for lunch, I tell him: “One o'clock, young man. Nap time.” He packs away his guitar, and the whole square looks as if it's off for a nap with him.
textes.Depuis que la montagne gronde, il descen: Ever since the mountain started rumbling, he comes down every night to ask me: “Well?” I answer: “Not today.” He nods and goes back up. One night, he didn't ask anything. He sat down beside me, and we listened to the mountain together until dawn.
textes.Depuis que la montagne gronde, je descen: Ever since the mountain started rumbling, I go down to his alcove every night. I ask: “Well?” He answers: “Not today.” I go back up. One night, I didn't ask anything. I sat down. He passed me his cup of moon water. It was revolting. We listened to the mountain until morning.
textes.Depuis que le Zéphyr passe, Tilleul et m: Since the Zéphyr started sailing, Tilleul and I have been writing to each other. Well, Ewen writes for me, and a little owl over there writes for him. His letters always stop in the middle of a story. I reply: “And then?” He replies with another story. I've been waiting three years for the end of the first one.
textes.Depuis que le Zéphyr se pose sur l'aire: Since the Zéphyr started landing on the pad north of the village, Ramure's post flies all the way to Cliquetis! In every bag, I slip a little note for Commander Zélie Hélice. She writes back. We've never met. Thanks to her, I bring Ardoise's letters to Caramel, postcards from Port-Azur… and a letter that went tick-tock, for Pépin.
textes.Depuis que le cristal pâlit, je tisse la: Since the crystal began to fade, I weave at night, {surnom}. A cape so tight it holds air, like a little dome. If the big one ever goes out, I want my daughter to be able to swim up to the sun without running out of breath. Ondine knows nothing about it. Pélagos pretends not to see it, under the bed.
textes.Depuis que tu as vu Triton dans ma sculp: Ever since you saw Triton in my sculpture, he's all I can see. I've turned it to face the wall.
textes.Depuis que tu passes me voir, ça va nett: Since you started visiting, I've been much better. Don't tell Gaston, he's jealous.
textes.Depuis quelque temps, Ori me lit les run: For a while now, Ori has been reading me the runes out loud, every evening, “for practice”. He reads slowly, and he gets the easiest ones wrong on purpose, so I'll correct him and feel useful. He's a terrible liar. He gets that from me.
textes.Depuis quelque temps, mes chaussures son: For a while now my shoes have been lighter. I swear! I run and it feels like I've got feathers on my heels. It's the training, obviously. I told Ursule, all proud. She said “Hm. Good.” and turned her back on me really fast. She was moved, I think. By my progress.
textes.Depuis quelque temps, ses énigmes sont t: Lately, her riddles are all easy when she's asking me. The other day: “I'm blue, I'm up high, and there are clouds in me.” I answered “the sky”, of course. She clapped much too loudly.
textes.Depuis quelques nuits, Thalassa tisse qu: For a few nights now, Thalassa has been weaving something very big, very tight, that she hides under the bed. She thinks I haven't noticed. I haven't said anything. In the mornings, I leave the longest kelp I can find beside her loom. She doesn't ask where it comes from.
textes.Depuis ses dix ans, je lui offre une per: Since she was ten, I've given her a pearl every birthday. She sews them onto a blue ribbon, one by one. There are fourteen. She wears it on feast days. Ewen asked if it was a captain's necklace. She answered: “No, it's a necklace of years.” He didn't understand. I did.
textes.Depuis une semaine, le Grand Spaghetti V: For a week now, the Great Flying Spaghetti has been sulking: its noodles droop, its eyes stay half-shut, and the volcano rumbles more than usual. The Reverend Father Farfalle has found the recipe that will make it friends again with its followers: the Great Reconciliation dish. It needs Mamma Lasagna's pasta, a ladleful of sauce from the Cooking Pot and parmesan grated with Captain Rigatoni's Golden Grater (which he buried somewhere thirty years ago).
textes.Depuis, elle m'envoie des graines. Pour: Since then she sends me seeds. To say sorry. Zéphyr drops them outside my door. I put them in the fire. They go “pop”. … It's quite nice, “pop”. Don't tell her. She'd send more.
textes.Depuis, je cache le dessin dans une chau: Since then, I've hidden the drawing in a sock. A clean sock, rolled up, at the bottom of my suitcase. On Tuesday, when I came back, I found the sock on my bed, neatly folded, with a little note: “Pretty crystal!” I no longer know where to put it. I'm thinking of carrying it on me, in my hat.
textes.Depuis, je joue toutes les nuits sous Fi: Since then, I play every night beneath Fil-d'Aube, Ilyria's tree-house. Thalion grumbles, Aëlwen sighs, Lirael lowers her lantern so it looks prettier. Haldir carries my letters, and I always run to take them back before he knocks. Forty-one verses, and still not the courage. Life is beautiful, and terribly slow.
textes.Depuis, je lui envoie des graines par Zé: Ever since, I've been sending him seeds via Zéphyr, to say sorry. Zéphyr says Grommelot throws them in his fire and they go “pop”. At least he keeps them warm! Last time, I sent him corn kernels, on purpose. They make much prettier pops.
textes.Depuis, je porte tout : les invitations: Since then, I carry everything: invitations to festivals, Taeron's complaints, Aëlwen's herbal teas, and Caelan's letters, which he takes back before I knock. When your boat came through the mist, I was the one who ran to tell Thalion. I'd never carried such big news.
