textes.Depuis, le professeur cache son dessin d: Since then, the professor hides his drawing in his sock. The left one. I found it anyway, putting away the laundry. I put it back in the sock, neatly folded, with a little note: “Very pretty crystal.” He didn't speak to me for two days. Then he asked me if I really thought it was pretty, that crystal.
textes.Depuis, les nuits de teuf, le kick trave: Since then, on party nights, the kick drum carries across the island all the way to my kapok tree. Clou dances on the roof. One night, he danced with the cash box in his arms. I was picking my coins out of the ferns until dawn. In time with the beat, too.
textes.Dernier verrou ! Le virus a débranché l': Last lock! The virus unplugged the antivirus. Click the tiles to rotate them, and rebuild the path between the battery ⚡ and the antivirus ✚.
textes.Dernière question. Mon frère jaloux m'a: Last question. My jealous brother shut me in a chest and threw me in the river; then he cut my body into pieces. My wife searched for every piece and gave me back life. Since then, I rule the kingdom of the dead. Who am I?
textes.Dernière énigme ! « Plus on m'enlève, pl: Last riddle! “The more you take away from me, the bigger I get.”
textes.Derrière le balancier de la grande horlo: Behind the pendulum of the grand clock, hanging from a nail: a little key!
textes.Derrière le balancier, il n'y a plus rie: There's nothing behind the pendulum anymore. Just the ticking.
textes.Derrière le mur fissuré, une petite nich: Behind the cracked wall, a little niche… with an urn.
textes.Derrière le tonneau : une araignée qui t: Behind the barrel: a spider staring at you. It hasn't seen anybody either.
textes.Derrière mon comptoir, je garde une chop: Behind my counter, I keep a dented mug. It was his father's. Bramm is the only one who drinks from it. One evening, a passing dwarf grabbed it. I snatched it back before he touched the foam. Bramm said nothing. He paid for the dwarf's round. That's his way of saying thank you.
textes.Derrière son comptoir, Ulfa garde une ch: Behind her counter, Ulfa keeps a dented mug. Mine. It was my father's. Nobody else drinks from it. Once, a passing dwarf picked it up. Ulfa took it back out of his hands before the first sip. I said nothing. I paid for his round. His.
textes.Derrière toutes les portes, on rit. Les: Behind every door, there's laughter. The little Moai seem very mischievous… and very curious about you.
textes.Derrière un hublot qui brille : un patch: Behind a shining porthole: a Bilge Rats patch, brand new, forgotten by a very old fan.
textes.Des blocs et des gravats jusqu'au plafon: Blocks and rubble up to the ceiling. Impossible with bare hands… With a shovel, perhaps.
textes.Des bouteilles partout, et dans chacune,: Bottles everywhere, and in each one, a tiny ship. Leaning over his workbench, an old sailor holds his breath.
textes.Des boutons ! Boutons de chemise, de man: Buttons! Shirt buttons, coat buttons, trouser buttons… One day, I'll sew myself a coat out of nothing but them.
textes.Des bâtons bien droits : de futurs manch: Nice straight sticks: future handles. You've got a good eye.
textes.Des cailloux ! Gratuits, ramassés soi-mê: Pebbles! Free, picked up yourself… You're my worst nightmare. But I respect it. I could paint them for you, your pebbles. Cheap. Authentically.
textes.Des cartes postales ! Court, joli, avec: Postcards! Short, pretty, with a picture. That's very good. But don't buy them from Victor, eh! … Well, yes. A few. He needs it.
textes.Des cercles de bois tressés de fil tourn: Wooden hoops woven with thread turn gently at the ends of their strings, with beads and feathers. A craftswoman knots a net by the light of the crown.
textes.Des champignons de braise ! Ils brillent: Ember mushrooms! They're still glowing! Here: three bowls of stew, piping hot. Four hearts each. Blow on it.
textes.Des chats. Partout. Sur le fauteuil, sou: Cats. Everywhere. On the armchair, under the table, on top of the wardrobe…
textes.Des chaussettes chauffées par une mini-c: Socks warmed by a mini-boiler at the ankle. Ideal for the highlands.
textes.Des chauves-souris ! Elles volent à haut: Bats! They fly at head height and swoop at you: strike them when they dive.
textes.Des chiens d'enfer ! Quand la gueule s'o: Hellhounds! When the jaws open and glow red, they're about to spit fire and pounce: step aside, then strike.
textes.Des chiens d'enfer sauvages ont pris le: Wild hellhounds have taken over the lava field, east of the Great Blaze, and growl at travellers. Captain Pyrus would like someone to drive them away.
textes.Des clients veulent les acheter. Le Lord: Guests want to buy them. The Lord offered an indecent sum for the little view of the port, the one with a black seagull on the jetty. I replied: “They are not for sale, milord. They belong to the house.” That seagull looks a great deal like a moustache. I didn't go looking for it. I spotted it straight away.
textes.Des coquillages de la VRAIE mer ! Ils so: Shells from the REAL sea! They're so pretty! Here, this is for you: a pearl I found in the fountain. Shh!
textes.Des coucous, des pendules, des horloges: Cuckoo clocks, mantel clocks, grandfather clocks… Here, there's no shortage of time.
textes.Des crabes de roche ! Gaston en a fait d: Rock crabs! Gaston had nightmares about them for ten years. Look after yourself, {surnom}, and eat before you go down.
textes.Des crabes de roche, là-dessous ? Gros c: Rock crabs, down there? Big as barrels? Watch their claws: when they go up, back off. When they come down, strike.
textes.Des crabes sortent du puits !: Crabs crawl out of the well!
textes.Des cœurs de magma ! Ils sont encore cha: Magma hearts! They're still warm! Here: sixty coins, and a ruby I found… I can't remember where. Thank you, {surnom}!
textes.Des dards jaillissent des murs ! Ces dal: Darts shoot out of the walls! Those darker flagstones are trapped.
textes.Des dattes de l'oasis, apportées par la: Dates from the oasis, brought by Mbarek's caravan: brown, glossy, sweet as honey. Restores one heart.
Drawings of waves on every wall. In the middle, a tiny little Moai stares at the wall, very serious.
textes.Des deux malades de cet hiver-là, l'une: Of the two patients that winter, one was Soazig, Gwenola's sister. Pierrick's mother. I tried the whole journal, page after page, until morning. As she left, Gwenola shook my hand and said thank you. Thank you, {surnom}. I hadn't managed to do anything. If I want so badly to go into the mists, it's because of that night.
textes.Des diablotins ! Ils ricanent, voltigent: Imps! They snicker, flutter about… and dive at you, pitchforks first. Step aside when they crouch, then strike.
textes.Des disques partout, dans des bacs le lo: Records everywhere, in crates along the wall. On a small cabinet, a turntable waits for someone to choose.
textes.Des djembés, une flûte, des voix qui cha: Djembes, a flute, voices singing in chorus. You want to get up and dance around a fire.
textes.Des dragons ! J'en ai connu un. Enfin, m: Dragons! I knew one. Well, my grandfather knew a dwarf who'd seen one. At my age, it's almost the same thing.
textes.Des fleurs d'œillet d'Inde, orange comme: Marigold flowers, orange like the setting sun, picked on the chinampas. Their scent, they say, guides souls. Xóchitl needs them.
textes.Des fois, Odette passe pendant que je pa: Sometimes Odette walks by while I'm talking to a crate. I pretend to cough: “Easy there, my… ahem, ahem.” She says nothing. She carries on with her register. I think she didn't notice. She looks like someone who notices nothing, sometimes. It's handy.
textes.Des fois, quand je fais ma longueur dans: Sometimes, when I do my lap of the bay, I see the sergeant on the promenade. He doesn't move, hands behind his back, as if on parade. He watches my arms, very closely. When I come out of the water, he pretends to be keeping an eye on a bicycle. There's never a bicycle.
textes.Des gargouilles fondent du haut des nuag: Gargoyles swoop down from the clouds!
textes.Des gargouilles se sont réveillées dans: Gargoyles have woken up in the Ruins of the Old Pandemonium, on the north-western cliffs. They swoop down on passing ships. Captain Charbonnel, the harbour master, would like someone to drive them away.
textes.Des gargouilles, mille sabords ! Des sta: Gargoyles, shiver me timbers! Statues that fly away, can you believe it? They nest in the Ruins of the Old Pandemonium, on the north-west cliffs, and they dive onto my sails. Go and drive them out. They're made of stone: hit hard.
textes.Des gobelins ! Petits, rapides, une lanc: Goblins! Small, quick, with a flint spear. When one pulls its spear back, parry (F) or roll (Ctrl). Don't worry: at the first scratch, it runs off.
textes.Des gobelins ? Qu'ils viennent ! Je les: Goblins? Let them come! I'm waiting for them! Preferably one at a time.
textes.Des graines de tournesol grillées au sel: Salted roasted sunflower seeds, in a little cloth bag. Perroquet-Joe swears no parrot can resist them.
textes.Des gâteaux sur la table, des gâteaux su: Cakes on the table, cakes on the sideboard, cakes cooling on the windowsill.
textes.Des haltères partout, un tapis, et quelq: Dumbbells everywhere, a mat, and someone puffing like a steam engine.
textes.Des lanternes de lune, petit. Dedans, il: Moon lanterns, little one. Inside is a pond mushroom that glows at night, soft and blue, like a piece of moon. Every spring, I replace them. This year, my paws no longer reach down to the water… Five of them grow, at the edge of the five ponds in the forest, around the village. Would you bring them to me? Pick them gently: they're shy.
textes.Des livres du sol au plafond. Ça sent le: Books from floor to ceiling. It smells of old paper… and mystery.
textes.Des lumières dansent dans la forêt. Des: Lights are dancing in the forest. Spirits, Faelar says. I don't shoot at spirits.
textes.Des lunettes dont les verres sont des ka: Glasses whose lenses are kaleidoscopes. The whole world becomes a rose window.
textes.Des légendes, m'as-tu dit. J'en ai rédig: Legends, you told me. I've drafted an accurate version of one, in case anyone up there wants to make corrections.
textes.Des légendes… Nous sommes devenus des lé: Legends… We've become legends. It's flattering, and it's sad. A legend is an archive somebody left out in the rain.
textes.Des mains d'ombre sortent des dalles noi: Shadow hands rise from the black flagstones and grab you! They surely fear light… moonlight, perhaps?
textes.Des marches mouillées : on entend l'eau,: Wet steps: you can hear the water below.
textes.Des marches tièdes : en bas, ça chauffe…: Lukewarm steps: down below it's hot… no, it's COLD. No, it's tidy. Anyway, we're going down.
textes.Des marches, des marches, encore des mar: Steps, steps, more steps… They call them the Thousand Steps. Odon counted 999: he's still looking for the last one.
textes.Des noix ? Grosses comme une tête ? Avec: Nuts? As big as a head? With water inside? You're pulling my leg. … No? By the hammer of Ancestor-Stone, your island is mad.
textes.Des noix de coco… Il faudra que j'essaie: Coconuts… I'll have to try that. For science.
textes.Des ombres… Elles glissent sans bruit da: Shades… They glide silently through the gloom of Limbo. They're not very sturdy: strike them when they reach out their arms.
textes.Des oursins qui brillent, Anselme ! Un c: Glowing sea urchins, Anselme! A crystal!
Sea urchins. And your coffee's cold.
textes.Des partitions partout, un pupitre, et u: Sheet music everywhere, a music stand, and an artist playing with his eyes closed. Lucky for him.
textes.Des pas métalliques résonnent dans la sa: Metallic footsteps echo through the hall… The guardians won't let you go up.
Round footprints, the pond. Nothing else.
textes.Des perches des mares grillées sur une b: Pond perch grilled on a bamboo stick by Caramel, the fishmonger. Crispy. Restores two hearts.
textes.Des perles ! Sous la mer ! Combien ? Gro: Pearls! Under the sea! How many? How big? Don't answer. Bring them. I pay well. Well… I pay.
textes.Des pirates ! Des humains qui volent l'o: Pirates! Humans who steal other people's gold on the sea… Here, what we mostly steal is the last slice of Sylwen's bread. It's less glorious, but it ends better.
textes.Des pièces ! Gratuites ! Tu es fou… mais: Coins! For free! You're crazy… but I'm keeping them.
textes.Des plans au mur, des outils partout. Un: Plans on the wall, tools everywhere. An inventor, bent over a workbench, didn't hear you come in.
textes.Des plumes de toutes les couleurs, parto: Feathers of every color, everywhere! On a mannequin, a magnificent headdress awaits its last feather.
textes.Des poissons de toutes les couleurs nage: Fish of every color swim… in the living-room air! Bubbles rise gently from the floor.
textes.Des pommes, des baies, du miel de la for: Apples, berries, forest honey! Grelot. Yes, it means little bell. There's one at the end of my tail, listen… No, that was my aunt. She left and took it with her.
textes.Des racines ferment l'escalier. La salle: Roots block the staircase. The hall is waiting for something: the light of the sap, perhaps, on that big knot of wood…
Thick roots block the staircase. Perhaps they'll open if the song of the fireflies is played again…
textes.Des raptors ! Ils tournent autour de toi: Raptors! They circle around you… When one crouches, hissing, it's about to LEAP: step aside! After its jump, it's dazed for a moment: strike.
textes.Des rochers partout. L'un d'eux vient de: Rocks everywhere. One of them just giggled. Rocks don't usually giggle.
textes.Des ronces noires, épaisses comme le poi: Black brambles, thick as a wrist, covered in glistening thorns. They block the whole cave entrance. The knife slides off them as if off glass.
textes.Des ronces surgissent d'entre les branch: Brambles burst from between the branches and march toward you! Carnivorous plants open their jaws…
textes.Des rumeurs ? Je n'en vends pas. Ça ne r: Rumours? I don't sell those. There's no money in it.
textes.Des rumeurs ? Je ne parle pas aux inconn: Rumours? I don't talk to strangers about important things. Come back when we're friends.
textes.Des sables mouvants ! Tu t'enfonces… Sor: Quicksand! You are sinking… Get out quickly, and stay on the flagstones.
textes.Des scorpions des sables ! Quand la queu: Sand scorpions! When the tail rises above the head, the sting is coming: back off, roll (Ctrl) or parry (F), then strike.
textes.Des seaux ? J'en ai plein ! Des tout neu: Seals? I've got loads! Brand-new ones, still flapping!
textes.Des spectres ! Les coups les traversent…: Specters! Blows pass right through them… Moonlight (key 4 then X; in VR, B) makes them visible, and vulnerable.
textes.Des spectres de givre ! Leur souffle gèl: Frost specters! Their breath freezes: when they lean toward you, step aside, then strike.
textes.Des statues qui tournent à deux ? C'est: Statues that turn in pairs? It's a combination lock, nothing more. Turn, count, think. Or whack it: that never works, but it feels good.
textes.Des tasses de tous les pays ! Il ne m'en: Cups from every country! I'm only missing one: the perfect cup. I've been looking for it for forty years.
textes.Des touristes trouvent mon perroquet eff: Some tourists find my parrot frightening. Too many claws. One evening, a lady asked Toni to take it down. Toni put down his tea towel and said: “Madam, that parrot is the house.” I was drinking at the bar. I said nothing. I drank slower, to stay longer.
textes.Des vipères noires, au fond du puits ? E: Black vipers, at the bottom of the well? They coil up before they strike, dead straight, like an arrow. Don't stand in front: one step to the side, and you take its head off on the way back.
textes.Des voix de pierre, graves et rondes, qu: Voices of stone, deep and round, making the walls vibrate. It's beautiful. Almost.
textes.Des vraies couleurs ! Le rouge d'un cora: Real colours! The red of a coral, at the bottom of the bay, west of the beach. The golden yellow of a honey pot. And the brown of a coconut. With those, I'll paint the finest canvas of my life.
textes.Des vêtements, une chaussette orpheline…: Clothes, an orphan sock… and a smell of mothballs. Nobody.
textes.Des éclats… de beaux éclats. Hmpf. Tiens: Shards… fine shards. Hmph. Here: thirty coins and a pinch of dust. And don't smile like that.
textes.Descendre au cinquième étage du Donjon d: Go down to the fifth floor of the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps
textes.Descendre au port de Cliquetis (téléphér: Go down to the harbour of Cliquetis (cable car or winding road) and find the golden gear, near the crane
textes.Descendre dans Xibalba, déjouer les Seig: Go down into Xibalba, outwit the Lords of Death and bring back the Jade Mask
textes.Descendre dans la Pyramide de Rê, traver: Go down into the Pyramid of Ra, cross the journey of the night and defeat Apophis at the bottom of the Duat
textes.Descendre dans les Neuf Cercles (la port: Go down into the Nine Circles (the iron door at the back of the Forge Cathedral), defeat the Frost Titan at the bottom of the Cocytus and bring back the Eternal Flame
textes.Descendre jusqu'au 2e étage du Donjon de: Go down to the 2nd floor of the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps
textes.Descendre jusqu'au 4e étage du Donjon de: Go down to the 4th floor of the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps
textes.Descendre les cinq étages du Donjon des: Go down the five floors of the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps (the entrance is under the ruined tower, at the foot of the Fangs, in the south-west of the island; Odon keeps the gate) and defeat the Jelly King in the Jelly Throne Room
textes.Descendre les marches de pierre jusqu'au: To go down the stone steps all the way to the bottom. It's pitch black past ten fathoms, I know. But a step always leads somewhere. I'd like to know where.
textes.Descendre sous le Cœur-de-Pierre, dans l: Go down beneath Stoneheart, into the Rose of Seals
textes.Descendre sous le Grand Temple, rallumer: Go down beneath the Great Temple, rekindle the Sun Stone, set the Fifth Sun in motion, defeat Cipactli
textes.Deux ! Une pour moi et une pour… euh… po: Two! One for me and one for… um… for me too.
Two? Now there's a husband who doesn't give up.
Two skewers, and one for the road.
textes.Deux cent quatre-vingt-dix-neuf de reste: Two hundred and ninety-nine to go!
textes.Deux cents ? Ils vont vouloir du miel, h: Two hundred? They'll want some honey, you know.
textes.Deux cœurs rendus ; le sort soigne aussi: Two hearts restored; the spell also heals wounded creatures.
textes.Deux daurades, comme d'habitude ? Et pou: Two sea bream, as usual? And who's the second one for?
textes.Deux fois ? Seulement ? C'est un très bo: Twice? Only? That's a very good score! The engineer from Cliquetis did three. One day, there'll be beds. Promise.
textes.Deux fois par jour, Hortense monte huile: Twice a day, Hortense goes up to oil her clock. I pass her with her oilcan and her key, straight as a ramrod. Whether it rings or not, she's never missed a single day. Me, who forgets to water my geraniums… I made her a bouquet once, for no reason. She asked me what I wanted. Nothing, that was the point.
textes.Deux fois, c'est pour ceux qui n'ont pas: Twice is for those who weren't listening the first time.
textes.Deux fragments sur trois ! Le troisième: Two fragments out of three! The third eye on my map is under the jungle, near the stone head. I drew four serpents in a circle… and an arrow going round. Or a snail.
textes.Deux golems, une chèvre, et un oncle qui: Two golems, one goat, and an uncle who looks tired.
textes.Deux gros os, rongés et luisants. Les ja: Two big bones, gnawed and shiny. The jaguars of the hills fight over them; throw them to a jaguar, and it will forget to bite you.
textes.Deux mains. Hm. Il te faut une poignée p: Two hands. Hm. You'll need a longer grip. And shoulders. You've got shoulders. More or less.
textes.Deux mois, trois cafés par jour : près d: Two months, three coffees a day: nearly two hundred coffees. A single “thank you”. On a Tuesday, at a quarter past ten, without looking up from his book. I nearly dropped the tray. I chalked it up on the slate behind the counter: “Professor's thank-you: Tuesday, 10:15.” He's never seen it. The slate's still there.
textes.Deux mâts, des voiles neuves, une roue d: Two masts, new sails, a gleaming steering wheel: the Schooner is in the water! I think I'm going to cry. (I'm crying.) She's waiting for you at the jetty.
textes.Deux nains se tiennent devant un grand m: Two dwarves stand before a big bronze mirror. They comb their beards while glaring at each other.
textes.Deux offrandes. À Tlaloc, une jarre d'ea: Two offerings. To Tlaloc, a jar of rainwater: Coyotl, the potter, makes them. To Huitzilopochtli, burning copal: Tochtli sells it at the market. Then the round slab will open between the two shrines, and you will go down to the Five Suns. In the deepest depths sleeps the Feather of the Feathered Serpent… and Cipactli, who guards it.
textes.Deux pains ce matin, Sylwen. Tu parles c: Two loaves this morning, Sylwen. You sound like my mother.
textes.Deux personnes se disputent au milieu du: Two people are arguing in the middle of the living room. The topic:
textes.Deux personnes sont agenouillées devant…: Two people kneel before… a cat. Stretched out on a cushion between two oil lamps, it pretends to sleep.
textes.Deux petites pièces, voyageur. Le destin: Two little coins, traveller. Destiny isn't read for free.
Two coins. I gave you a good price.
textes.Deux punchs et une bière naine, table tr: Two punches and a dwarven root beer, table three!
textes.Deux runes de golem. Bien. TRÈS bien. …: Two golem runes. Good. VERY good. … OPEN THE GREAT GATE! The tall one is one of us! Here, thirty coins. And don't say I'm nice.
textes.Deux siècles après, Faelar a enfin fini: Two centuries later, Faelar finally finished the story of the humans' tree. The ending was: “And a little elf went to see.” Then he looked at me and smiled. He hadn't fallen asleep by chance that night.
textes.Deux vrais jaguars rôdent sur les pentes: Two real jaguars are prowling the slopes of the Smoking Mountain, to the west. They killed one of Xóchitl's turkeys. Mixtli, the jaguar warrior, wants someone to face them.
textes.Deux yeux d'argent dans la brume… LE GRA: Two silver eyes in the mist… THE GREAT MIST WOLF! You can't see it, you can't touch it. Except, perhaps, by the light of the moon.
textes.Deux, cette fois ! Une pour Léa, et une: Two, this time! One for Léa, and one to apologise in advance.
Two. And not in front of everyone. Hmph.
Two. One for me, one for the gull.
textes.Deuxième verrou : sa combinaison de coul: Second lock: its colour combination. Watch the order in which the squares light up, then click them in the same order.
textes.Deuxième énigme ! « Je cours sans jambes: Second riddle! “I run without legs, I sing without a mouth, and I have a bed but never lie down in it.”
textes.Devant trois vrais crabes. Ils ont appla: In front of three real crabs. They clapped. Well, I think so.
textes.Devenir archère ! Ou herboriste. Ou expl: Become an archer! Or a herbalist. Or an explorer! No, all three! And go and see the real sea, the one with the singing shells. With you!
textes.Devenir la plus grande magicienne des de: Become the greatest magician of both kingdoms, up top AND down below! And one day light up all the stars with a snap of my fingers. Well, the ones that are willing.
On Sunday, yes it is. And Clara's coming too.
textes.Ding ! Rez-de-chaussée. Les néons du bou: Ding! Ground floor. The boulevard's neon lights, the noise of the cars… back on the street.
textes.Ding ! Une voix polie : « L'ascenseur de: Ding! A polite voice: “The service elevator only serves floors already visited. You have visited nothing. How sad.” The doors stay closed.
textes.Ding, dong, dilin… Les tubes du carillon: Ding, dong, dilin… The chime tubes sing, and the wind joins in. Far below, you can see the yurts, the red fields, the stage, and the sea.
textes.Dire à Mégaphone que c'est le moment (à: Tell Mégaphone it's time (at the sound desk, in the middle of the meadow)
textes.Dis bonjour à mes filles, cette fois. Ge: Say hello to my girls this time. Nicely.
textes.Dis donc, toi qui voyages : pièces ou tr: Say, you're a traveller: coins or swaps, which do you prefer?
textes.Dis donc, toi. Ta lame, tu lui as donné: Say, you. Your blade, have you given it a name?
textes.Dis donc, {surnom}, toi qui as des jambe: Say, {surnom}, you've got legs: have you ever won anything? A race, a contest, a bet?
textes.Dis maintenant ta confession devant les: Now speak your confession before the forty-two judges.
textes.Dis, dis, c'est vrai que là d'où tu vien: Say, say, is it true that where you come from, people don't have tails?
textes.Dis, l'étranger… tu as déjà dit une chos: Say, stranger… have you ever said something true while pretending to joke?
textes.Dis, le terrestre ! Toi, tu arrives plut: Hey, landlubber! Do you tend to arrive early, right on time, or late?
textes.Dis, quand tu étais petit… enfin, plus p: Hey, when you were little… well, littler… did you get up to mischief?
textes.Dis, si tu avais une baguette magique, t: Hey, if you had a magic wand, what would you do first? Quick, quick, answer!
textes.Dis, t'as déjà vu un dauphin, toi ? Un v: Hey, have you ever seen a dolphin? A real one, that jumps?
textes.Dis, toi qui brilles pas du tout : tu as: Hey, you who don't glow at all: are you scared of the dark sometimes? You can tell me, okay!
textes.Dis, toi, tu es plutôt du matin ou du so: Hey, you — are you more of a morning person or a night person?
Tell them thank you. From a distance, mind.
textes.Dis-moi franchement, champion : tu sais: Tell me straight, champ: can you swim? Really?
textes.Dis-moi franchement, je le sentirai si t: Tell me honestly, I'll smell it if you lie: do you sleep well at night?
textes.Dis-moi franchement, {surnom}. Si la mer: Tell me truly, {surnom}. If the sea gave us back our island tomorrow, would the people above welcome us?
textes.Dis-moi tout : sur ta plage, qu'est-ce q: Tell me everything: on your beach, what do you eat in the morning?
textes.Dis-moi un truc, {surnom} : toi, tu dans: Tell me something, {surnom}: what do you dance with? Your feet, your arms… or in your head?
textes.Dis-moi, comment soignent-ils les blessu: Tell me, how do they heal wounds where you come from?
textes.Dis-moi, d'où viens-tu, comme ça ?: Tell me, where do you come from, then?
textes.Dis-moi, grand client : toi, tu marchand: Tell me, big customer: do you haggle, or do you pay the price you're asked?
textes.Dis-moi, jeune : ta toute première fête,: Tell me, kid: your very first party, where was it?
textes.Dis-moi, jeune humain : chez toi, quelle: Tell me, young human: back home, what story did they tell you to help you sleep?
textes.Dis-moi, le grand… qu'est-ce qui fait un: Tell me, big one… what makes a good warrior?
textes.Dis-moi, matelot : tu sais barrer un bat: Tell me, sailor: can you steer a boat?
textes.Dis-moi, mon ami : qu'est-ce que tu ne t: Tell me, my friend: what would you never swap?
textes.Dis-moi, petit, toi qui as vu du pays :: Tell me, youngster, you who've seen the world: do you prefer a true story, or a beautiful one?
textes.Dis-moi, petit… As-tu une maison où l'on: Tell me, little one… Do you have a home where someone is waiting for you?
textes.Dis-moi, quand tu te fais mal, tu le mon: Tell me, when you hurt yourself, do you show it straight away, or hide it until it turns green?
textes.Dis-moi, toi : tu aimes la cuisine relev: Tell me, you: do you like spicy food? So it sings in your mouth?
textes.Dis-moi, toi : tu es plutôt du soir ou d: Tell me: are you more of an evening person or a morning person?
textes.Dis-moi, toi : tu oses dire les choses e: Tell me: do you dare say things to people's faces?
textes.Dis-moi, toi : tu parles à tes affaires: Tell me, you: do you talk to your things? To your sword, your bag, your boat?
textes.Dis-moi, toi qui as l'air d'avoir réfléc: Tell me, you look like you've thought about things: can you win by coming second? I say yes. Well, I think.
textes.Dis-moi, toi qui viens de dehors… tu l'a: Tell me, you who come from outside… have you ever seen the whale?
textes.Dis-moi, toi qui viens de la mer… le bat: Tell me, you who come from the sea… what's a boat like? Is it scary?
textes.Dis-moi, toi qui viens de loin : tu préf: Tell me, you who come from far away: do you prefer true stories, or made-up ones?
textes.Dis-moi, toi qui vis ici… Tu aimes la fo: Tell me, you who live here… Do you love the forest?
textes.Dis-moi, toi, franchement : tu tires ou: Tell me, honestly: are you a shooter or a pointer?
textes.Dis-moi, toi, quand tu voyages : tu rapp: Tell me, when you travel: do you bring back souvenirs?
textes.Dis-moi, toi, tu sais reconnaître un poi: Tell me, you: can you tell a fresh fish?
textes.Dis-moi, toi. Une vieille dette, ça s'ef: Tell me, you. An old debt: does time wipe it out, or does it get paid?
textes.Dis-moi, tu as rencontré {qn}. Comment t: Tell me, you've met {qn}. What do you make of {le}?
textes.Dis-moi, voyageur : tu veux connaître to: Tell me, traveller: do you want to know your future, or would you rather be surprised?
textes.Dis-moi, {surnom} : est-ce que quelqu'un: Tell me, {surnom}: is someone waiting for you somewhere, with a hot bowl of soup?
textes.Dis-moi, {surnom} : quand tu rêves, la n: Tell me, {surnom}: when you dream at night, do you remember it when you wake up?
textes.Dis-moi, {surnom}, toi qui cours d'île e: Tell me, {surnom}, you who run from island to island: do you sleep well at night?
textes.Dis-moi, {surnom}, toi qui voyages : tu: Tell me, {surnom}, you who travel: do you prefer a sea like glass or a good swell?
textes.Dis-moi, {surnom}. Tu préfères quoi : le: Tell me, {surnom}. What do you prefer: silence, music, or the sound of the waves?
textes.Dis-moi, {surnom}… qu'est-ce qu'on mange: Tell me, {surnom}… what do you eat back home, on your island?
textes.Dis-moi, {surnom}… si tu étais roi, quel: Tell me, {surnom}… if you were king, what would your first law be?
textes.Dis-moi, {surnom}… tu préfères les chèvr: Tell me, {surnom}… do you prefer goats or crows?
textes.Dis-moi, {surnom}… une lame, tu l'aimes: Tell me, {surnom}… how do you like a blade? Light, heavy, or something else?
textes.Dis-moi… le soleil, là-haut, est-il touj: Tell me… the sun, up there, is it still as warm as ever?
textes.Dis-moi… tu as peur de l'eau profonde, t: Tell me… are you scared of deep water? Where you can't see the bottom any more?
textes.Dis-moi… tu connais ce vieux fou de Barn: Tell me… do you know that old loon Barnabé, on the other side?
textes.Dis… quand je monterai voir le soleil, t: Hey… when I go up to see the sun, do you think I'll be scared?
textes.Dis… tu donnes des noms aux choses, toi: Say… do you give things names?
textes.Dites-moi franchement, entre nous : vous: Tell me honestly, between us: do you make your bed in the morning?
textes.Dites-moi, entre nous… vous lisez des ro: Tell me, just between us… do you read romance novels? Go on, admit it.
textes.Dites-moi, et soyez honnête, hein : vous: Tell me, and be honest, eh: do you like my crackers?
textes.Dites-moi, jeune personne : vous êtes en: Tell me, young person: are you usually early, on time or late?
textes.Dites-moi, my dear : quel est l'objet le: Tell me, my dear: what is the most precious object you own?
textes.Dites-moi, vous : vous écrivez encore de: Tell me, you: do you still write letters?
textes.Dites-moi, vous avez rencontré {qn}. Com: Tell me, you've met {qn}. What do you make of {le}?
textes.Dites-moi. Quand on vous rend la monnaie: Tell me. When you're given change, do you count it, or do you trust?
textes.Dix Grandes Courses, {surnom}. Dix ! Deu: Ten Great Races, {surnom}. Ten! Fourth twice, ninth once, and the rest we don't count. So I picked up the brushes and painted the record board. Then I ordered a stopwatch from Cliquetis: the letter arrived going tick-tock, and Plumette listened to it before I did. Since then, I time everything. Even the bread. Especially the bread.
textes.Dix minutes ! Tu me les as volées, ces d: Ten minutes! You stole those ten minutes from me!
textes.Dix pièces, la bague, et on n'en parle p: Ten coins for the ring, and we'll say no more.
textes.Dix poissons, du safran et le secret de: Ten fish, saffron and the secret of Paulo's nonna. Restores all hearts.
textes.Dix-sept ans. Je pars pour l'arbre du Gu: Seventeen. I'm leaving for the Lookout tree. Dad says nothing. He stares at his float. Very hard. … Caramel puts down her fish knife. She says: “She runs. Let her run, Dad.” … He nodded. Once. … I never said thank you to Caramel.
textes.Django ! Tu joues à quelle heure, ce soi: Django! What time are you playing tonight?
textes.Django a perdu sa partition, ce matin, s: Django lost his sheet music this morning, on the quay. The wind scattered it. Now he only plays three songs, and he hates them.
textes.Django a trois chansons qu'il déteste et: Django has three songs he hates and that people request every night. I keep count. On Monday he played “The Sad Fisherman” eleven times. In between, I bring him his glass of water with a little note: “Three more?” He answers with a wrong note, on purpose, right as I walk past the stage.
textes.Django est le plus beau modèle de l'île,: Django is the handsomest model on the island, and the touchiest. He says you can't paint music. I'm going to prove him wrong.
textes.Django est un grand artiste et un petit: Django is a great artist and a petty critic. He says I have the voice of a seal with a cold. I call on him for every ceremony anyway: we've only got one guitarist.
textes.Django, c'est l'âme du Perroquet. Il jou: Django is the soul of the Perroquet. He plays like no one else, grumbles like everyone else, and he's as proud as his grandfather. The day the wind took his sheet music, it broke my heart.
textes.Django, notre musicien, mon voisin de la: Django, our musician, my neighbour on High Street. He plays like an angel and pokes his nose into everything like a cat. He slows the music down when Lucas walks in. On purpose.
textes.Dong… La vieille cloche sonne sur toute: Dong… The old bell rings out over the whole island.
textes.Donner les baguettes de batterie à Gédéo: Give the drumsticks to Gédéon (at the Lisse & Fils sales office in the daytime, on the quays in the late afternoon, at the entrance to the Howling Hall in the evening)
textes.Donner un coup de pinceau (le Pinceau de: Make a brushstroke (the island's Brush, dipped in the Palette)
textes.Donner votre avis à Héloïse Manivelle, d: Give your opinion to Héloïse Manivelle, in front of the Academy
textes.Dormir jusqu'à midi. Une seule fois. Et: To sleep until noon. Just once. And in the evening, to still see Lirael's lanterns lit, because the forest's little lights had come back and filled them all on their own.
textes.Doucement quand même. Elles ont de toute: Gently, though. They have tiny little ears.
textes.Doucement, Lumi… Les fleurs dorment enco: Gently, Lumi… The flowers are still asleep.
textes.Doucement, Majesté… Une fée de la rosée: Gently, Your Majesty… A dew fairy doesn't drink. She gives.
textes.Doucement, ma feuille. Le sentier ne va: Gently, my little leaf. The path isn't going to fly away.
textes.Doucement, moussaillon ! Une question à: Easy there, cabin girl! One question at a time, and the bell on the hour.
textes.Doux… Mamma mia. Bon. Je comprends. Les: Mild… Mamma mia. Fine. I understand. The world needs delicate stomachs too. I'll make you a little convalescent's bouillabaisse. My pot's going to cry.
textes.Douze ans. Un héron a volé la pêche de p: Twelve. A heron stole Dad's catch. From the basket. It flew off. I ran. All the way round the big pond. Faster than it. It dropped the fish. … Dad scolded: “A cat waits.” … I chose to run. At seventeen, I left the fishery. For the Lookout tree. Near the last bend.
textes.Douze tasses, Aristide. Je compte toujou: Twelve cups, Aristide. I'm still counting.
textes.Douze tasses, Aristide. Ne touche à rien: Twelve cups, Aristide. Don't touch anything.
textes.Douze, Barnabé ! Et un collier pour Gast: Twelve, Barnabé! And a necklace for Gaston, bro!
Twelve. And we'll say no more.
Elder, the Heart is beating again.
textes.Doyenne, pourquoi les ponts de lumière c: Elder, why are the bridges of light flickering?
textes.Du Guet, par temps clair, on voit le dir: From the Watchtower, on a clear day, you can see the Cliquetis airship coming in from the north. It buzzes like a bumblebee. The rabbits hide every time.
textes.Du beau minerai rouge ! Attends… (DING !: Fine red ore! Wait… (CLANG! CLANG! CLANG! PSSSHHH!) There. A dwarven sword. Broad blade, golden guard, a ruby on the pommel. It cuts iron like butter. Don't break it.
textes.Du bois ! Mon charbon te remercie. {prix: Wood! My charcoal thanks you. {prix} coins a log.
textes.Du bois coupé… Tu sais, chez nous, c'est: Cut wood… You know, where I come from, that's a bit like offering… an arm. No. Thank you.
textes.Du bon bois, coupé à la hache. Octave en: Good wood, cut with the axe. Octave buys it for his forge.
textes.Du bord de l'île, on voit tout l'archipe: From the edge of the island you can see the whole archipelago, tiny, in the middle of the sea. Don't lean too far: clouds don't hold you up.
textes.Du cacao battu jusqu'à mousser, avec un: Cocoa whisked until frothy, with a little chilli and vanilla: the drink of the Maya kings, bitter and invigorating. Restores one heart.
textes.Du haut des plates-formes, on voit ton î: From the top of the platforms, you can see your island and the jungle. And sometimes Barnabé waving his arms. We don't wave back.
textes.Du jus de coco, moussaillon ! C'est de l: Coconut juice, cabin boy! It's water with ambition.
textes.Du matin ? Comme Margaux et Rosalie, alo: Morning? Like Margaux and Rosalie, then. Brave people. Me, at six, I sleep like a log. Come by at ten, I'll treat you to a coffee. Mornings are quiet here.
textes.Du miel ! Du VRAI miel ! Tiens : trois b: Honey! REAL honey! Here: three fizzes, twenty-five coins, and when the honey drink is ready, your first tankard is on the house.
textes.Du miel sauvage ! Gaston, pas touche. …: Wild honey! Gaston, paws off. … Fine, one drop.
textes.Du miel sauvage ! Il sent la fleur et la: Wild honey! It smells of flowers and sap. Here: three piping-hot honey breads. Well, lukewarm. The oven, you know.
textes.Du poisson ! Ici, on n'en voit presque j: Fish! We almost never see any here, the sea's too far from the pot. Grilled, you say? With what? No mushrooms? You poor little thing.
textes.Du poisson ? Le matin ? … Les humains so: Fish? In the morning? … Humans are brave. Well, I don't judge. But have some bread with it. On the side. To make me happy.
textes.Du poisson, des patates douces, des bana: Fish, sweet potatoes, bananas… and my grandfather's favorite stone. For the flavor. He says that's the secret. He's made of stone, so naturally he thinks stone tastes good.
textes.Du safran ! Tu as dit safran ! Toi, tu a: Saffron! You said saffron! You've got the soul of a cook. Nonna would have adopted you. She'd have put you under the table with me.
textes.Du slime remonte dans les puits de la Ba: Slime is rising in the wells of the Lower Town and in the fountain on the Great Square. Master Hugues knows where it comes from: from the bottom of the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps, at the foot of the Fangs, where the Jelly King reigns. I have to go down the five floors, defeat the King and bring back his Royal jelly heart.
textes.Du verre de volcan, noir et tranchant, q: Volcanic glass, black and sharp, found near the crater. Nori the runesmith carves his runes into it.
From the village, on the other island.
From the village, on the island across the way.
textes.Duel à la loyale ! Aux poings, et person: A fair duel! Fists only, and nobody interferes. (F: guard · Ctrl: roll)
Dwalin! Put that sack down and come and eat.
textes.Dwalin ! Ton charbon fume avant de brûle: Dwalin! Your coal smokes before it burns.
textes.Dwalin a porté tout le charbon de la mon: Dwalin carried all the coal in the mountain, and me along with it. His back hurts, and I think that's partly my fault. The least I owe him is a shiny shield.
textes.Dwalin apporte le charbon tous les matin: Dwalin brings the coal every morning. Wet, one time in three. He swears it isn't. The fire says it is. I believe the fire.
textes.Dwalin porte le charbon de toute la terr: Dwalin carries coal for the whole terrace on his back and he never complains. Well, he complains about his back. But never about anything else.
As soon as… as soon as the wind turns.
textes.Débordée mais contente. J'ai trouvé une: Run off my feet but happy. I found a pearl under a bed this morning. Well, a button.
textes.Débordée, oui. Le registre des bateaux d: Overwhelmed, yes. The boat register must be up to date for the season, and nobody comes by to declare their boat. Old Fernand, Yannick who hires out boats, and Lucas who has a rowing boat even though he says he doesn't. Ask them the name of their boat. I'll pay you.
textes.Débordée. Nimiel s'est encore écorché le: Swamped. Nimiel skinned her knees again climbing the walkways.
textes.Débordée. Trois voiliers à l'heure, deux: Swamped. Three sailboats an hour, two fishermen fighting over the same berth, and the register doesn't fill itself in.
textes.Décoiffé ! C'est le mot ! Mon chapeau à: Windswept! That's the word! My feathered hat! The finest! The one for grand occasions, small occasions, and days without any occasion! The wind carried it off from the rampart. It hopped from roof to roof, above the Middle Town, then flew off to the south. Aurore says it will come back on its own. It never comes back on its own. Would you be so kind as to look for it, young person? It has a green feather. It's very distinguished. You'll recognise it.
textes.Dégager l'éboulement de la galerie sous: Clear the rockfall in the tunnel under the sea
textes.Déjà ? Bon. Gaston va encore bouder. Rev: Already? Fine. Gaston's going to sulk again. Come back soon.
textes.Déjà ? Le temps file quand on mixe !: Already? Time flies when you're mixing!
textes.Déjà de retour ? Tu ne peux plus te pass: Back already? You can't do without my conversation any more, admit it.
textes.Déjà {nb_poissons} prises ! Et ton plus: {nb_poissons} catches already! And your best: {record}. Not bad for a beginner.
textes.Délicieuses ! Oh, vous êtes un amour. Ou: Delicious! Oh, you're a sweetheart. Or a fibber. Both make very good customers. Here, I'll give you the polite-people price: same as everyone else's.
textes.Démasqué ! Ha ha ! Personne ne m'avait j: Caught! Ha ha! Nobody ever found me so fast. Well… except my grandmother. And the cat.
textes.Désaccordé. Le vent a emporté ma partiti: Out of tune. The wind took my sheet music, my most beautiful song, the one I wrote for the sea. Three pages, gone.
textes.Désespéré. J'ai perdu mon alliance en jo: Desperate. I lost my wedding ring playing in the waves. Léa won't look at me any more.
textes.Désormais, quand tu te promèneras en vil: From now on, when you stroll around town, you'll hear me in every loudspeaker: the news, the classifieds, the weather... and you, now and then. You're a radio star now. Here, your fee. And stay tuned!
textes.Détendue. Je n'ai rien fait depuis trois: Relaxed. I haven't done a thing for three days, and I intend to keep it that way.

textes.ENCORE ?! Mais tu es grand ! Alors on a: STILL?! But you're all grown up! So you're allowed, even when you're big? I have to tell Thalion. No. I definitely have to NOT tell Thalion.
textes.EURÊKA ! … Non. Raté. Mais quel joli ver: EUREKA! … No. Failed. But what a lovely green!
textes.Edmond ! J'ai votre tableau de la semain: Edmond! I've got your painting for the week.
textes.Edmond est l'homme le plus digne et le p: Edmond is the most dignified and generous man in Port-Azur. He calls it “the management”. I know perfectly well it's him.
textes.Edmond me remet le courrier de l'univers: Edmond hands me the university's mail on a silver tray, with Nadine's caramel beside it. He sets it on the lounge table, steps back two paces and waits. One day, I asked him to put it further away. He put the tray on the piano, at the far end of the lounge, then came back to tell me: “It is far away, professor.” He never smiles. Almost.
textes.Edmond, le réceptionniste. Un homme d'un: Edmond, the receptionist. A man of archaeological discretion. He's been stepping around my charts without a word for two months. It's a form of respect.
textes.Elandor ! Tu as encore marché sur mes vi: Elandor! You've trodden on my violets again.
textes.Elandor est le plus doux des maris et le: Elandor is the gentlest of husbands and the slowest of walkers. He keeps me waiting everywhere. But when he arrives, he always has something to show me.
Elandor never gets lost, according to him. According to me, he got lost for nine days, and I searched for him without sleeping. He was watching a snail. I'm fond of him. From a distance. With a rope.
textes.Elle a encore bougé, Le Goff ?: Has it moved again, Le Goff?
textes.Elle a l'œil triste parce qu'elle sait q: It has a sad eye because it knows it's ending up at your place.
She's allowed. She's two hundred years old.
textes.Elle a le temps, elle est pleine tout le: She's got time, she's full all the time!
textes.Elle a planté un caillou rond dans son c: She planted a round pebble in her corner of the garden, saying it was a seed from a surface tree. I water it every morning. She asks me if it's growing. I say it's thinking. That's true of a lot of things down here.
textes.Elle a raccourci ma tournée de dix minut: She cut ten minutes off my round: she takes the olive-tree alley instead of going round by the fountain. Thirty years I went round by the fountain! In the morning, from the pitch, I watch her go by and I check my watch. She's always on time. That's the worst part.
textes.Elle a refusé de me la faire. Elle a dit: She refused to make it. She said a new ring doesn't tell the same story, and you don't fool a woman with a ring. Then she took a big jeweller's magnifying glass out of her drawer and lent it to me: “Keep looking. The sand gives back what it takes, if you insist.”
It's thirsty. Like you. Here, drink.
textes.Elle a voulu accrocher une clochette « a: She wanted to hang an “anti-ghost” bell outside the linen room on the fourth floor. I refused, very quickly. Perhaps a little too quickly. She gave me a funny look. I invoked the regulations: no bells in the corridors. There were no regulations about bells. I drafted them that very evening.
textes.Elle a vu mon appareil sur le banc du be: She saw my camera on the bench at the lookout. She didn't touch it: “Someone might be looking for it.” The someone was me! I searched the hotel, the beds, Théo's pockets… and there it was waiting for me up there, sitting quietly on its bench, with a painter beside it gazing at it like a landscape.
It loves the sea, that whistle. Like me.
textes.Elle attend depuis mille ans, elle n'est: It's been waiting a thousand years, one more week won't hurt.
So will it, milord. In the same place.
She moves a little. She dances slowly.
textes.Elle chantait ma ballade du roi Atlas su: She was singing my ballad of King Atlas in the square, and at the third verse I had an idea: a queen, and an octopus. I stood up to tell her. She didn't miss a note. She put the octopus in. The whole city applauded the octopus. I've never been so proud of a singer.
textes.Elle chante en pesant mes poissons. Moi,: She sings while she weighs my fish. And while she sings, I discreetly put my thumb on the pan of the scales. She keeps singing, doesn't look at me, and takes five hundred grams off the price. Exactly the weight of my thumb. We've been doing it for years. We've never once argued.
textes.Elle compte triple, Momo. J'avais mes lu: It counts triple, Momo. I had my sunglasses on.
textes.Elle dessine des poissons au bas de mes: She draws fish at the bottom of my letters to her dad. Little ones, big ones, striped ones, and always one with a crown. Ardoise writes back that he's hung them all on his boat's mast. Mrrr. I don't know if it's true. I prefer to believe it.
textes.Elle dit ça pour que je saute encore. Et: She says that so I'll jump again. And it works!
textes.Elle déteste mes haches. « On ne coupe p: She hates my axes. “You don't cut down a living tree!” A forge needs wood. One day, an axe disappeared. I found it in a wasps' nest. I took it back. They stung me. Eleven times. I said nothing. Neither did she. Next day, she bought nails from me. Hm. A draw.
textes.Elle est entrée avec son béret et un sou: She came in with her beret and an enormous smile: “Some red coral, please, for my red.” I explained that you don't rip up coral, it takes a hundred years to grow. She said: “Just a little piece.” I replied: “Just a little century.” She walked out in a huff.
textes.Elle est heureuse. C'est pareil, pour un: She's happy. For a speaker, that's the same thing.
textes.Elle est intacte ! Ce soir, mon phare br: It's intact! Tonight my lighthouse will shine all the way to the village again. Here… when you keep watch over a lighthouse, you learn to breathe slowly. I'll teach you: you'll last longer underwater.
textes.Elle est là ! Elle flotte au-dessus du b: She's here! She's floating above the pool, with her guilty little look! (Nova wipes away a blue tear.) Thank you, thank you! Do you know what she's singing right now? The gurgles translate to: “I went to see the world. It's big. I prefer it here.” Here: two cosmic jellies from Gloubi, it's all I have that's precious. And you can come see Plume-de-Nuage whenever you like. She'll remember you. Jellyfish never forget those who bring them home.
textes.Elle est venue à Forgefer quand elle éta: She came to Forgefer when she was young, with a sack of badly forged nails and not a word. She stayed a season at the terrace forge. In the evenings, sitting by the fire, her fur would smoke. Bramm complained about finding hairs in his mug. I talked enough for two. She listened. We got on very well.
textes.Elle existe… Elle existe ! Une reine, un: It exists… It exists! A queen, a dome, a crystal that sings… Forty years of mockery, and I was right! Take this, it's all my holiday money. And remember this: the Atlanteans breathed slowly. Do as they did.
textes.Elle fait trente centimètres, Félix. Ell: It's one foot high, Félix. It's almost flat.
textes.Elle finit en chef-d'œuvre ! Et dimanche: It's ending up a masterpiece! And on Sunday, what will be missing this time?
textes.Elle les envoie danser ailleurs. C'est p: It sends them off to dance somewhere else. That's not the same.
textes.Elle lit derrière le journal de la veill: She reads behind yesterday's paper, always folded the same way. One evening, the novel was so good she held the paper upside down for an hour. I turned it round as I went past, without stopping. The next day, she left me a tip. A tip, from Colette! I thought she was ill.
textes.Elle m'a compté le papier d'emballage. P: She charged me for the wrapping paper. For three apples. One penny. I paid. A week later, she brings me her cheese knife, chipped. I sharpen it. Properly. I charge her for the sharpening. To the penny. She paid. We said nothing. We respect each other.
textes.Elle m'a confié sa graine de cactus des: She trusted me with her dwarf cactus seed, begging me to water it. A cactus hardly wants any water. So I give it one drop a month. Not one more. In spring, it grew a yellow flower. Noisette cried for joy. I watched her cry.
She asked me what an apple was. I've never seen one either! So I said: “a red sea urchin that grows on trees”. She repeated it to the whole city. Now if anyone proves me wrong, my honour sinks. Don't bring an apple down here, all right?
textes.Elle m'a demandé ce que la baleine dit a: She asked me what the whale says to the crystal. I searched ten thousand scrolls for three days. Nothing. I had to admit I didn't know. The next day, I found a pebble on my desk, with writing on it: “Abyssos doesn't know everything.” I archived it, of course.
textes.Elle m'a demandé de planter un arbre pou: She asked me to plant a tree for every tree I cut down. I said no. Three times. Now I have a nursery behind the forge: twenty-six little kapok trees. Don't tell anyone. Especially not Barnabé.
textes.Elle m'a demandé si quelqu'un était déjà: She asked me if anyone had ever left the dome without going through the Gate. I said: “Never, not on my watch.” She looked at me for a long time, with her big eyes, as if she knew something. Then she said: “OK.” I don't like it when she says “OK” like that.
textes.Elle m'a demandé une aiguille spéciale :: She asked me for a special needle: as long as my hand, curved, sturdy, for thick canvas. I asked what canvas. She said: “A canvas.” I forged the needle without asking anything else. I'm not nosy. Well, I am. But I know how to keep quiet.
textes.Elle m'a donné de l'hibiscus séché pour: She gave me dried hibiscus to replace the coral. In the bowl, a sublime red, deep, almost wine-dark. I put it on the canvas that evening, very proud. The next morning, it was brown. Dead-leaf brown. Amélie said it was “very autumnal”. I laughed. Later. Much later.
textes.Elle m'a offert du nectar pour mon anniv: She gave me nectar for my birthday. I poured the bottle on my roots. In front of her. In spring the root grew a flower. A nectar flower. Even the roots betray me. Hmph.
textes.Elle m'a offert un dessin : moi, sur mon: She gave me a drawing: me, on my throne, with hair reaching the ceiling. “That's because you're a thousand years old,” she explained. I asked who had told her that. She clapped both hands over her mouth. I didn't have to look far: there's only one guard, at the Gate.
textes.Elle m'a posé cent dix-sept questions su: She asked me a hundred and seventeen questions about humans in a single evening. I answered by describing Barnabé. Ever since, she's convinced that all humans talk to a parrot. I didn't have the heart to tell her otherwise.
textes.Elle m'a posé une devinette. « Je grogne: She set me a riddle. “I grumble in the morning, I grumble at night…” I thought about it. I said: “A bear.” She laughed for three days. Three. And I was right. Bears grumble. Hmph.
textes.Elle m'a promis de me prévenir quand la: She promised to let me know when the whale came by. One night she ran up to me: “Triton! It's above the palace!” I took one step. Then I remembered I was on guard, and I stayed. She sang me the whale for an hour. It was almost better. Almost.
textes.Elle m'a prédit que je traverserais la m: She predicted I'd cross the sea before I turned sixty. I'm fifty-eight, and I get seasick. I have two years left to prove her wrong. I fully intend to. Well… I fully intend not to. I'm not quite sure which side I'm on any more.
textes.Elle m'a vendu une potion de sève, une f: She sold me a sap potion, a green phial that smells of the forest. “One spoonful in the morning.” I take two, so I go faster. She doesn't agree. I tried to explain that it's mathematical. She gave me the look I used to give pupils who dawdled.
She's eating the chimney, more like.
textes.Elle me garde un tabouret près de l'encl: She keeps a stool for me by the anvil. I tell stories to the customers while she hammers, and the customers stay for both. One morning, she leaned a walking stick against my door with a moon on the handle. Without a word. A walking stick, from Ursule, is a whole sentence. That one meant: “Don't fall, Father.”
textes.Elle me regarde. Au départ, au marché, a: She looks at me. At the start line, at the market, at the Circle. Staring, without blinking, with the tip of her tail twitching just a teeny bit. Like a cat in front of a skewer, {surnom}. One day I tested it: I hid behind a barrel. She looked at the barrel. I'm not reassured at all.
textes.Elle me réclame depuis des années la rec: For years she's been asking me for the recipe for the caravan traders' cream. I asked Aïcha, who asked a caravan trader, who laughed: goat fat and cinnamon. That's exactly what I brought Anouk, in a pretty pot. She didn't believe me. Nobody ever believes me when I tell the truth.
textes.Elle monte, Triton. Tu veux que je la ch: It's rising, Triton. Do you want me to sing it more quietly?
textes.Elle ne grince pas, elle chante. C'est t: It doesn't creak, it sings. It's your thread rubbing.
textes.Elle penche un peu. C'est le style, Octa: It leans a little. That's the style, Octave.
She loses her drops in my roots. Makes them wet. Makes them go mouldy. So I pick them up and put them back outside her door, in a nutshell. For my roots, not for her. Once she was watching for me behind her window. I pretended I was just passing. Hmph.
textes.Elle pose ses énigmes devant MA boutique: She sets her riddles in front of MY shop. Customers stop, think, scratch their heads… and leave without buying anything, their heads full. Once a bumblebee spent a whole day trying to work one out. He didn't buy anything either.
textes.Elle pousse vers le haut, Borin. Vers la: It's growing upwards, Borin. Towards glory.
textes.Elle prétend que mes énigmes font fuir s: She claims my riddles scare off her customers. Nonsense: they stay in front of her shop for hours on end, thinking. Once a bumblebee stayed a whole day. He didn't buy anything, fine. But he left cleverer.
She was looking at the moon, behind you.
It stays where it is, milord.
textes.Elle revient toujours avec des pétales d: She always comes back with petals in her hair and golden pollen on her cheeks. I say they're real.
textes.Elle ronronne ! Nefer-Miou t'a accepté !: She's purring! Nefer-Miou has accepted you! It's a great honor. Take this honey cake: it's what she would have wanted.
She purrs, Tchoum. She likes me.
It came unplugged. It likes you.
textes.Elle s'est envolée ? Oh, mon petit… Tu a: She flew away? Oh, my dear… You have gentle hands, and a gentle heart too. Here, some coins, and a feather she left on my roof this morning: she came to thank you, I think.
textes.Elle se pose… mais le bouclier d'épines: She lands… but the thorn shield protects her. The roses of light!
textes.Elle se souvient de toi ! Elle ronronne: She remembers you! She's purring even louder than last time.
It smells of punch, this week.
textes.Elle sort à peine du four !: It's barely out of the oven!
She likes you, Bramm. You're steady.
It's waiting for you. So is the thyme, it's sulking.
textes.Elle t'embrasse. Toujours pas de retour: She sends her love. Still not going back?
textes.Elle te suit ! Brioche te suit ! Regarde: She's following you! Brioche is following you! Look at her, sitting at your feet, tail neatly curled, like a queen who has chosen her carriage. (Rosalie wipes her eyes with her apron.) It's the smell of the fish, it stings. Listen to me: she eats one sardine a day, not two, she has her dignity. She chases butterflies, she never catches them. And she has a gift: she can sense hidden treasures. I once saw her meow for an hour in front of a paving stone in the square; underneath, there was an old gold coin. Listen to her when she meows. Here, a few coins. And if you don't have anything yet to call your animals, take this bone whistle: my grandfather, the fisherman, carved it with a dog, a cat, a rat and a pig. He said that one day, someone would have all four. Whistle, and those who love you will come running.
textes.Elle te tend une paire de chaussettes à: She hands you a pair of plaid socks, all warm… and a few coins hidden inside. “For coffee.”
She'll hold a hundred years, Admiral.
It's holding. Not a word, Jos.
It's been waiting for you for ten minutes.
textes.Elle était authentique ! Authentiquement: It was authentic! An authentic tablecloth.
textes.Elle était jolie, non ?: It was a nice one, though, wasn't it?
It was full of my drops.
textes.Elle était si belle, je voulais la regar: It was so pretty, I wanted to look at it from far away!
textes.Elles ont chanté pour toi. Je les ai ent: They sang for you. I heard them all the way here. So it's settled: you are a wizard of Arcanelle. Here, your staff: wood from the Twisted Wood and a crystal from the Circle. In your hand, it makes your spells lighter. And your magic is greater from now on. Go, wizard. The world needs light, fire, ice, wind, patience and healing. Healing most of all.
textes.Elles s'inquiètent. (Une grande fleur cl: They're worried. (A big flower blinks three times, very fast.) See? Three quick blinks means “where are the little ones?” The little ones are my glowing seeds. I was drying them in the sun, at the end of the bridge of light... and a gust of wind pushed them into the Zero-Gravity Garden. Over there, nothing falls back down. They float, way up high, between the leaves that fall upward. Me, with my eight-hundred-year-old knees, I jump like an old squash. You're young. Jump! Catch them! Three seeds, round and warm, glowing like night-lights.
textes.Elles se sont toutes arrêtées à une heur: They all stopped at a different time. That way, one of them is always right. Twice a day.
textes.Elles sont en fer, maintenant, Brunna. G: They're iron now, Brunna. Thanks to you!
textes.Elles t'aiment bien ! Et elles avaient p: They like you! And they were scared you'd get lost!
textes.Elles t'ont entendue. Elles bourdonnent: They heard you. They're buzzing with delight.
textes.Elles étaient derrière le comptoir, tes: Were your cards behind the counter, then?
textes.Embêtée ? Je suis CLOUÉE AU SOL ! (Elle: Upset? I'm GROUNDED! (She shows her wing in a sling.) I sprained it on a chimney. I still have three letters: one for Grumbald, at the Diable Repu; one for Ombreline, at the Library of Souls; one for Gorgoth, at the arena. Would you? I'll pay you in stamps. No, in coins.
textes.En avance ! Fffiou ! Enfin quelqu'un de: Early! Fffwoosh! Finally, someone serious. You walk slowly, but you set off early. That's a technique. Respect.
textes.En bateau ? Peuchère ! Assis, les bras c: By boat? Good grief! Sitting there, arms folded, looking at the sea? Well, the sea is pretty. But at least run up the steps of the quay.
textes.En cachette ! Comme moi, petite, dans le: In secret! Like me, as a girl, in the broom cupboard. Welcome to the club. There are far more of us than people think, you know. Even behind shop counters.
textes.En cachette ! Oh, tout le monde commence: In secret! Oh, everyone starts in secret. For me it was on my mother's hooves, in the kitchen. For Grelot, behind her stall, between customers.
textes.En ce moment, je ne passe plus devant l': These days, I don't go past the herbalist's any more. I take the fishermen's alley: three hundred metres extra, good for training! Nothing to do with the doctor. Nothing at all. And when I bump into her, I tell her my times. Going down! She doesn't believe me. She's wrong. Well… she's right.
textes.En choisissant sa rose, Hugo m'a récité: While choosing his rose, Hugo recited the name of every flower in my shop. The real names, the scientific ones! I was floored. He blushed: “Léa taught me them. Over a year.” A year of buying bouquets to learn the names of flowers! That boy, I'd have married him myself.
textes.En dansant ! Coucou, coucou ! C'est exac: Dancing! Yoo-hoo, yoo-hoo! That's exactly it! A bridge dances, so you dance with it! That settles it: my next bridge, you'll open it.
textes.En entrant, il ôte son chapeau. Pas pour: When he comes in, he takes off his hat. Not for me: for the jar. He looks up at the top shelf and says: “Good morning.” To the jar of figs. Then to me. In that order. I find it ridiculous. I don't find it all that ridiculous. I don't know any more.
textes.En faisant son lit, j'ai trouvé sous l'o: Making his bed, I found a magnificent drawing under the professor's pillow: a city under the sea, with a great crystal in the middle, all blue. I told Gisèle. And Rosalie. And Madame Rita, and… well, everyone. He went as red as a lobster. I feel bad about it. A little.
textes.En garde, créature ! Tu ne sais pas à qu: On guard, creature! You don't know who you're dealing with!
textes.En grenouille, une fois, j'ai attrapé un: As a frog, once, I caught a moth. With my tongue. First go. … Not a bad feeling. Don't tell Pimprenelle. She'd change me every day. And I'd say no. Probably.
textes.En harmonie. Rien ne remplace une chanso: In harmony. Nothing beats a song you've found again.
textes.En marchant vite, alors ! Les clients ar: A brisk walk, then! The customers are coming!
textes.En partant, elle a laissé sur mon enclum: When she left, she left a little silver bell on my anvil. Not a word, of course. I hung it above the forge door. When Fundin comes running in, it rings, and he stops dead. It's the only thing in the world that stops Fundin.
textes.En plein morceau, je lui ai demandé de r: In the middle of a song, I asked him to play the low note again. For its colour. He sighed, he played it again. I closed my eyes: dark violet, almost plum. He played it ten times, grumbling that I was mad. I don't know why he did as I said. But I've got my violet.
textes.En pleine forme ! J'ai fait trois fois l: Feeling great! I flew three times round the Tree before breakfast.
textes.En pleine forme ! J'ai vendu tout le mér: On top form! I sold all the grouper before nine o'clock.
textes.En pleine forme ! Je cours tous les mati: Fighting fit! I run every morning. To the bakery.
textes.En remontant vers sa cité, je l'ai vu gl: On the way back up to his city, I saw him slip one of my axes into his belt instead of tossing it on the pile. Just one, the best. He probably says it's for showing apprentices what not to do. Me, I know a customer with taste when I see one.
textes.En rentrant de ma traversée, j'ai couru: When I got back from my crossing, I ran to see Corentin even before my mother. I told him: “There's a gate at the foot of Stoneheart. Your story is true.” He looked offended: “Of course it's true, lad. What did you think?” Then he downed his hot honey in one go. I think he was moved.
Late… Ah. A delay is nothing. Usually. Just watch out for the delays that matter, okay? Fffwoosh. Right, I'm off.
textes.En revenant de Tazira, j'ai montré à Lil: Coming back from Tazira, I showed Lilas the steps they dance on their square. She said: “A goat dance!” She learned it anyway, laughing. That very evening, the whole Circle tried it. Bedaine rolled onto Pépin, Gland thought he was a billy goat, and Mother Moon danced it with one paw, without leaving her moss.
In circles, I know. On purpose.
textes.En selle ! Stick gauche : vers l'avant p: Saddle up! Left stick: forward to climb, back to descend, left or right to turn. Right trigger: faster, left trigger: brake. A: land.
textes.En selle ! Z / S : plus vite / freiner,: Saddle up! W / S: faster / brake, A / D: turn, Space: climb, Ctrl: descend, E: land.
textes.Enchanting ! Je note, je note !: Enchanting! I'm writing it down, writing it down!
textes.Encore ! Dehors ! La boutique est fermée: Again! Out! The shop is closed!
textes.Encore ? Bon. Elle est très grande, et e: Again? All right. It's very big, and it never stops talking.
Again? That's the third this month.
Again? At least she has taste.
Again? That one loves the smoke.
Again? Your runes are repeating themselves.
textes.Encore ? J'en ai trente sous mon lit, Ma: Again? I've got thirty under my bed, Marée.
textes.Encore ? Je l'ai appris hier, Protée !: Again? I only learned it yesterday, Protée!
textes.Encore ? Je l'ai bouchée la semaine dern: Again? I plugged it last week.
textes.Encore ? Mais à qui écrivez-vous, Victor: Again? But who are you writing to, Victor?
textes.Encore ? Tu as déjà la bouche toute roug: Again? Your mouth is already all red. Wait until the ladle cools down.
Again? You know it better than I do.
textes.Encore ? Tu vas me courir après, comme d: Again? Are you going to chase after me, as usual?
textes.Encore ? Tu vas réveiller les nains, Tch: Again? You'll wake the dwarves, Tchoum!
textes.Encore ?! Je m'en souviendrai, crois-moi: Again?! I'll remember this, believe me.
Again?! You like explosions, you do. So do I.
textes.Encore ?! Tu as un estomac de Moaï, toi: Again?! You have a Moai's stomach! … Come back tomorrow, it needs to cook some more.
textes.Encore des marches. Tes mollets proteste: More steps. Your calves protest politely.
textes.Encore des marches. Ça sent l'huile de m: More steps. It smells of machine oil and steam.
textes.Encore faim ? Mamie a encore une galette: Still hungry? Granny have one more flatbread.
textes.Encore gagné ! Tu regardais où, Lucas ?: Won again! Where were you looking, Lucas? Oh, I know where.
textes.Encore le virus de Fil ? Donne-moi ton c: Fil's virus again? Give me your journal. (She plugs a pink cable into your journal and types at lightning speed.) There: I'm opening up the system for you. Pick up where you left off.
textes.Encore lui ? Je finirai par croire que t: Him again? I'm starting to think you do it on purpose.
textes.Encore toi ! Tu vas finir par voler, à f: You again! Keep this up and you'll end up flying.
textes.Encore toi, {surnom}. Tu as des pièces,: You again, {surnom}. You've got coins, I hope.
textes.Encore toi. Hmpf. Tu tiens debout, c'est: You again. Hmph. You're still standing, that's something.
textes.Encore toi. Tu ne tiens pas en place, he: You again. Can't sit still, can you?
Three more rows, and then I'll have lunch.
textes.Encore trouvé ! La prochaine fois, je me: Found again! Next time, I'm hiding in the fireplace. No, just kidding. Or maybe not.
textes.Encore un ? Tu as bon appétit, ça fait p: Another one? You've got a good appetite, it's a joy to see!
textes.Encore un tour ! Les rubans s'emmêlent u: One more lap! The ribbons get a bit tangled, but nobody will mind.
textes.Encore une réussite ! Tu devrais ouvrir: Another success! You should open your own shop.
textes.Encore {dernier_cadeau} ? Tu me gâtes !: {dernier_cadeau} again? You spoil me! That's {nb_cadeaux} gifts, I'm counting, you know.
textes.Encore {manque} coquillages ! Sur la pla: {manque} more shells! There are loads on your island's beach, Lyra said!
textes.Encore {manque} cœurs de magma, {surnom}: {manque} more magma hearts, {surnom}. My lanterns are flickering.
textes.Encore {manque} perles. Rondes et blanch: {manque} more pearls. Round and white, like dew.
textes.Encore {manque} rayons de miel, {surnom}: {manque} more honeycombs, {surnom}. My barrel is waiting.
textes.Encore {manque}… Elles sont peut-être da: {manque} more… Maybe they're in corners nobody ever goes to. Or right at the top.
Child of the surface… come closer.
textes.Enfant, sur le continent, j'ai ramassé u: As a child, on the mainland, I picked up a large shell on the edge of a grey beach. I held it to my ear, and I heard a city. Voices, bells, a crowd under the water. That evening, my grandfather read me a very old text about a sunken city and a queen with hair of sea foam. I never quite came back from it.
textes.Enfin ! Mes clients réclamaient leurs ta: At last! My customers were demanding their toast. Thank you, and tell Margaux she's an angel.
textes.Enfin quelqu'un de sérieux. Comptant, to: Finally, someone serious. Cash, always cash. Debts are like iron: they don't disappear just because you look the other way.
textes.Enfin quelqu'un qui reconnaît le génie !: At last, someone who recognises genius! I'm coming. Stay behind me when I cast a lightning bolt. Or in front. Well, not too close.
Well… it's not my best day.
textes.Ensommeillé, mais heureux. Les vieux our: Sleepy, but happy. Old bears doze.
textes.Entendre les clochettes des fées du Bois: To hear the little bells of the Bois-Doré fairies, the ones that play in rhythm. Keep them in my head, and hum them to Mistral so he can make a track out of them.
textes.Entendre une baleine me répondre. Une se: To hear a whale answer me. Just once. My great-grandfather spoke to them as to old friends; all I've ever had from them is their backs.
textes.Entendu ! … Une toute petite, alors ?: Understood! … Just a teeny one, then?
Heard it… Me too, I think, one night. Or it was Nausicaa. Or my stomach. The job makes you suspicious.
textes.Entre deux pots de tomates : une tirelir: Between two tomato pots: a piggy bank shaped like a radish. Radis had forgotten it. He'll say it's for you.
textes.Entre nous, depuis que Nimiel est née, j: Between you and me, since Nimiel was born, I only pick with one hand: the other catches her. I know she climbs with no hands, that she's hiding a frog, and that she sneaks out at night with something long under her arm. I pretend I know nothing. Mothers do a lot of pretending.
textes.Entre nous, j'ai toujours rêvé d'être ch: Between you and me, I always dreamt of being an opera singer. Django says I have the voice of a seal with a cold.
textes.Entre nous, j'aurais voulu être maître-n: Between us, I'd have liked to be a lifeguard. But I can't swim. So I keep watch over the town. It's a big swimming pool, without the water.
textes.Entre nous, petit : c'est qui, le champi: Between you and me, kid: who's the champion of Port-Azur?
textes.Entre nous… ce n'était peut-être pas que: Between you and me… maybe it wasn't just the map. Maybe I'd dozed off a bit at the helm. Don't EVER tell Barnabé.
textes.Entre nous… j'ai vu des lumières au somm: Between you and me… I saw lights at the top of the tallest rock spire one night. Gaston says it was the moon. Gaston says a lot of things.
textes.Entre, entre ! Et ferme la porte, sinon: Come in, come in! And shut the door, or Filou will slip off again.
textes.Entre, entre ! Ici, la porte est toujour: Come in, come in! Here the door is always open and the teapot always warm. Want some herbal tea? Mint from Lavande's garden, chamomile, and a poppy petal for the color.
textes.Entre, entre, ne reste pas dans le coura: Come in, come in, don't stand in the draft!
Come in, come in, don't stand in the draught! Welcome to La Dernière Bordée. Here we eat, we drink, we sing off-key and we sleep dry. I'm Gwenola. Everyone says “Mother Gwenola”. So will you.
Come in, come in, traveller… I was expecting you. Well, I expect everyone, it's my job. Madame Rita sees the past, the present and what is left to do.
textes.Entrer dans Pandémonia, la cité aux mill: Enter Pandémonia, the city of a thousand lanterns
textes.Entrer dans Yggdrasil par la porte aux r: Enter Yggdrasil through the rune door
Enter Yggdrasil through the rune door, cross its three halls to the Crown and receive the seed
textes.Entrer dans l'Usine Grise (au sud-est de: Enter the Grey Factory (in the south-east of the island, behind the Spore Wood), go down the five floors and defeat the Great Digger in the President's Pit
textes.Entrer dans la cité de cristal et de lum: Enter the city of crystal and light
textes.Entrer dans la cité sous la montagne: Enter the city under the mountain
textes.Entrer dans le Rocher du Crâne par sa bo: Enter Skull Rock through its mouth and open Barbe-Sanglante's chest (E)
Come in! … Oh no, it's locked.
Staircase B: reserved for polite robots.
textes.Espace : pédaler E : replier l'Alouett: Space: pedal   E: fold the Alouette
textes.Essaie, grand frère. J'ai encore mal aux: Go ahead, big brother. My arms still ache from last time.
textes.Essayer le Glisseur stellaire : l'appele: Try out the Star Glider: call it, climb aboard and fly off above Astralys
textes.Essayez la betterave. Ça tache, au moins: Try beetroot. At least it stains.
textes.Essoufflé mais vivant ! C'est ça, le sec: Out of breath but alive! That's the secret.
textes.Est-ce que… tu pleures, toi, quelquefois: Do you… do you ever cry? Humans, I mean. Does it happen to you?
textes.Et Mistral vous passe le bonjour. Enfin,: And Mistral says hello. Well, the kick does.
textes.Et Octave, il en dit quoi, de ta cabane: And Octave, what does he say about your shack?
textes.Et aller un jour à Forgefer, frapper à l: And go to Forgefer one day, knock on Master Hrolf's door, and tell him I held on. He'll say I hit too hard. Where he's from, that means hello.
textes.Et apprendre à Ewen à plonger pour de vr: And teach Ewen to dive for real. Without counting. Underwater, you don't count. You listen.
textes.Et apprendre à nager correctement. Pour: And learn to swim properly. For Lucie's stones. For science, obviously. Mostly for science.
textes.Et après, je montrerai le Roi à papy. Po: And then I'll show the King to Grandpa. So he can see him for real, up close. He deserves it, he's been waiting super long.
textes.Et après, tu m'aides à faire le phare ?: And after, will you help me make the lighthouse?
textes.Et au milieu du pont, je mettrai une noi: And in the middle of the bridge, I'll put a hazelnut. A real one, not hidden. For the moon. I bet it's never tasted one.
textes.Et aujourd'hui, six. Tu notes ?: And today, six. Are you writing this down?
textes.Et avoir un perroquet. Les vrais capitai: And have a parrot. Real captains have a parrot. Or a seagull, at a push. A polite seagull.
textes.Et battre Bernard. Une fois. Officiellem: And beat Bernard. Once. Officially, with a judge, a stopwatch and no red flag. Afterwards, I'll buy him a punch. Fruit only, at his age.
textes.Et c'est presque vrai. Tiens, fais-moi u: And it's almost true. Here, make me a cloud.
textes.Et ce quelqu'un qui marche beaucoup ? Il: And that someone who walks a lot? He'll turn up eventually.
textes.Et celui-là, milord ? Je lui invente que: And this one, milord? What story shall I make up for it?
textes.Et chaque année, vous payez. Les cartes: And every year, you pay. The cards have a long memory.
textes.Et chez toi, on t'attend toujours avec l: And at home, are they still waiting for you with soup? Eat mine anyway. It doesn't count as betrayal.
textes.Et compter les pas du dôme deux fois de: And to count the paces of the dome twice in a row, and get the same number twice. A person can dream small.
textes.Et de deux ! Plus qu'un, et on le met à: And that's two! Just one more, and into the trash it goes.
textes.Et derrière la porte ? Ah… ceux qui sava: And behind the gate? Ah… those who knew died long ago. A treasure, some say. A monster, say others. Me, I say: both. It's always both.
textes.Et deux fois la boulangerie. Farine sur: And the bakery twice. Flour on your belly.
And say good night to the banana trees for me.
textes.Et dérouler la carte. Un jour. Avec Barn: And unroll the map. One day. With Barnabé beside me. We'd finally know. Or we'd argue for another twenty-two years. That'd be something, at least.
And then? Tell me what happened next.
textes.Et entendre la lune me dire quelque chos: And hear the moon tell me something. Anything. Even “go home”. I'm already home. I'd go anyway.
textes.Et exposer une toile dans une vraie gale: And to show a canvas in a real gallery. With my parents standing in front of it, saying nothing, for a long time. And then my father saying: “The seagulls are very good.”
textes.Et faire monter mon cerf-volant plus hau: And make my kite go higher than the lighthouse. Higher than the seagulls. That way, Daddy will see it without looking in his machine.
textes.Et faire un collier pour chaque personne: And make a necklace for every single person on the island. Even Barnabé. Even Gaston.
textes.Et finir la carte complète de l'archipel: And to finish the complete map of the archipelago. All of it! With the Citadel in the clouds and the sunken city to the south-west. The professor will hold the ruler for me.
textes.Et finir la fresque du mur. Un jour où j: And finish the mural on the wall. One day when I'm brave enough for it to be less beautiful than in my dreams.
