textes.Et finir mes jours sous ma barque, avec: And end my days under my boat, with a fire in front and a mug in my hand. Like now, in fact. I think I'm already living my dream.
textes.Et goûter la cuisine des grands, une foi: And taste the big folk's cooking, once. To know. And to tell them it needs more mushrooms.
textes.Et grâce à toi, ma collection est complè: And thanks to you, my collection is complete.
textes.Et il y a la galette. Elle refroidit plu: And there's the crêpe. It cools down faster than the hull.
textes.Et je le bats. D'un centimètre. Et cette: And I beat him. By one centimetre. And this time, Nina does the measuring.
textes.Et je sais que tu as fait un cadeau à %s: And I know you gave a present to %s.
textes.Et je sais que vous avez fait un cadeau: And I know you gave a present to %s.
textes.Et l'exposer à la mairie de ma ville, av: And to exhibit it at my town hall back home, with my best sunsets. Twelve. Well: the two sharp ones, and ten artistic ones.
textes.Et la caisse douze, elle va bien ?: And crate twelve, is she OK?
textes.Et la chèvre, elle voit la différence ?: And can the goat tell the difference?
textes.Et la clé, c'est un caillou. Comme tous: And the key is a pebble. Like all the pebbles on the island. Good luck! Hee hee!
textes.Et la lune, alors, ne voulait plus se co: And so the moon would not go to bed…
textes.Et la nuit, faire un signal avec la poin: And at night, signal with the tip of the obelisk to the other lighthouse, the one up there. Just to see if it answers.
textes.Et la première, je la donnerais à Horten: And the first one, I'd give to Hortense. She's waited enough in her life: a flower that waits for the moon, she'd understand it better than anyone.
textes.Et la troisième louche, elle vérifie quo: And the third ladleful, what's that checking?
textes.Et le crabe de mardi, il compte ?: And Tuesday's crab, does that count?
textes.Et le dauphin, il est revenu ?: And the dolphin, did he come back?
textes.Et le disque rare, celui des deux villag: And the rare record, the one about the two villages?
textes.Et le griller sur le quai, pour tout le: And grill it on the quay, for everyone. Even for Anselme. Especially for Anselme. He loves grouper, I know he does: I've seen him eat it with his brother.
textes.Et le professeur qui parle. À tout le mo: And the professor talking. To everyone. For an hour. That evening, I'll gladly close the terrace late.
textes.Et le punch secret, il est servi ?: And the secret punch, has it been served?
textes.Et le signer de mon vrai nom. Une seule: And to sign it with my real name. Just once. Sylvie Dupuis, schoolteacher. To see the look on Gérard's face. He'd take a photo of it, I imagine. Blurry.
textes.Et le tempo, Gaston, tu le notes aussi ?: And the tempo, Gaston, are you writing that down too?
textes.Et le troisième est suave comme la mort: And the third is smooth as death! … No, I'm joking, mostly it's very sweet. Here, keep the mint for the road.
textes.Et maintenant, il y a toi ! J'ai rempli: And now there's you! I've filled a whole scroll with your stories from up there. Abyssos says my tree looks like an angry octopus, but he's never seen one either, so there. And Triton is teaching me to hold my breath, so I can go out one day. I can last till forty. He says three hundred. I think he cheats.
textes.Et mange-la, cette fois. Ne bouche pas u: And eat it this time. Don't plug a hole with it.
textes.Et moi des bananes. On fait des croissan: And I brought bananas. Shall we make banana croissants?
textes.Et moi je saute un doigt plus haut, frér: And I'll jump a finger higher, bro! Like yesterday!
textes.Et monter un jour sur une passerelle ave: And one day to go up on a footbridge with a tray. Just one. Without dropping anything. Maybe.
textes.Et monter une fois à bord du Zéphyr, pou: And to go aboard the Zéphyr once, to see the rooftops all those letters come from. And finally meet Zélie. I'll find out if she really has aviator goggles.
textes.Et ne viens pas te plaindre si tu casses: And don't come complaining if you break a jaw. Or two. Jaws mend. The Doc is there for that.
textes.Et ouvrir un deuxième kiosque, au pied d: And open a second kiosk, at the foot of the lighthouse. Nina will run it when she's grown up. With a captain's cap, if she likes.
textes.Et ouvrir une petite terrasse au village: And open a little terrace café in the village, with three tables and a chalkboard, facing the sea. For my mother to sit there and see that I was right to leave. And that I came back. A little.
textes.Et peut-être, au bout de la chaîne, mon: And maybe, at the end of the chain, my friend… my sister. That, I wouldn't swap for anything.
textes.Et plus une seule dans ma couronne, ente: And not a single one more in my crown, understood?
textes.Et porter une dernière lettre à Hortense: And deliver one last letter to Hortense. Good news, for once. I'd put my postman's cap back on, knock, and say: “Something today, Hortense.”
textes.Et puis aujourd'hui, je suis de bonne hu: And besides, today I'm in a good mood.
textes.Et puis fermer la boutique une semaine e: And then to close the shop for a whole week, and have someone make a cup of tea for me, for once. Just one. Nice and hot.
textes.Et puis rentrer, monter à la tribune du: And then go home, step up to the podium of the great lecture hall and read, before the whole university, a lecture entitled: “Moreau Was Right”. One hour. No notes. With a shell on the lectern.
textes.Et puis revenir. Oh, oui, revenir. Parce: And then come back. Oh, yes, come back. Because ours is always round, and someone has to rock it.
textes.Et puis un jeudi, la petite femme de cha: And then one Thursday, the little chambermaid from the hotel sat down at my table, for a laugh. Pauline. She talked for an hour; I drew three cards. She's come back every Thursday since. And it's curious, traveller: since that Thursday, my predictions have become… astonishing. The cards had found themselves a friend, no doubt.
textes.Et puis un jour, peut-être… Tazira. Mrrr: And then one day, maybe… Tazira. Mrrr. Maybe. Don't repeat it, it tires me out just thinking about it.
And then an infirmary with a window. A real one, round, looking out over the bay. Patients heal faster when they can see the sea. It's not in any journal, but it's true.
textes.Et puis, un jour, laisser la barre de L': And then, one day, hand the Swallow's helm over to Nina. When she's grown up, and has stopped ringing the bell too early. That gives me a bit of time.
textes.Et puis, un matin, ouvrir ma boîte à moi: And then, one morning, open my own letterbox and find a letter in it. A real one, not from me. I'd look at it three times before opening it.
textes.Et puis… un soir, monter à l'échelle d'O: And then… one evening, climbing up Octave's ladder with two coconuts and a pack of cards. Like on the Seagull. He'd cheat, I'd pretend not to see a thing. Don't tell Gaston.
textes.Et qu'ont-elles dit ? Avec un sujet et u: And what did they say? With a subject and a verb, if possible.
textes.Et qu'un jour, mon oncle Bedaine y achèt: And one day, my uncle Bedaine buys something there. Once. With a coin. Even a teeny one. I'll frame that coin.
textes.Et qu'Éclair vienne s'asseoir sur le pon: And that Éclair comes and sits on the jetty. A whole morning. Without running. I wouldn't say anything. Shh. Just the two of us and the float.
textes.Et quand je serai grande, un bateau qui: And when I grow up, a boat that sells ice cream, and I'm the captain! Strawberry-dolphin for everyone. Léon rides for free. Bruno too. You'll pay, but not much.
textes.Et quand la grande voile du Léviathan to: And when the Léviathan's great sail finally falls, on a fine day, to be there to fold it. Nobody is allowed to touch it. But someone will have to pick it up.
textes.Et que Borin vienne l'écouter. Qu'il gro: And for Borin to come and listen to it. For him to grumble: “Not bad… for a hairy one.” Hm. That would do me.
textes.Et que Colette trouve enfin son grand am: And for Colette to finally find her great love. Fifteen years I've been predicting it! After that, I can predict something else for her. A good honey harvest, for instance. She'll pay less, but I'll sleep better.
textes.Et que Mochi apprenne à pétrir avant de: And for Mochi to learn to knead before delivering bread at a run. In that order. Knead, then run. Not the other way round, Mochi!
And for Nadine to agree to have dinner with me. At Paulo's, at a table in the sun. I'd pay for everything. Even the bread. You see how serious it is.
textes.Et que Pierrick ouvre son auberge sur la: And for Pierrick to open his inn on dry land, with real beds. He thinks I'm making fun of him. I've already sewn him the sheets. They're in the chest, under the tablecloths.
textes.Et que Sigrun dise oui. À quoi ? Je ne l: And for Sigrun to say yes. To what? I haven't asked her yet.
textes.Et que Thalion me dise « bravo ». Une se: And for Thalion to say “well done” to me. Just once. Even really quietly.
textes.Et que l'horloge sonne pendant mon disco: And for the clock to strike during my speech. Right at the conclusion. Bong! What an effect, good heavens. They'd talk about it across the whole archipelago.
textes.Et que mon fournisseur de miel arrive à: And for my honey supplier to arrive on time. Once. Just once. I'm not asking for the moon.
textes.Et que mon peuple dorme une nuit entière: And for my people to sleep one whole night without hearing the mountain rumble. Just one. I'd spend it awake, just to listen to them sleep.
textes.Et que pour une fois, quelqu'un entende: And for once, for somebody to hear the ending. Any ending. Even me. Especially me.
textes.Et quoi d'autre, dedans ?: And what else is in it?
textes.Et raconter une dernière histoire, très: And to tell one last story, a very long one, without falling asleep before the end.
textes.Et rapporter une fleur de lune vivante,: And bring back a living moonflower, in a pot, to grow at Rose's. We'd watch it open together at night, the two of us, with a cup of herbal tea.
textes.Et reparler à Fernand. Sans avoir à le d: And speak to Fernand again. Without having to say it. Just end up at the same table one lunchtime, and have him pass me the salt.
textes.Et retrouver ma première pioche. Elle do: And find my first pickaxe. It must be somewhere. Everything is somewhere.
textes.Et revenir chaque année, chambre sept, r: And come back every year, room seven, to look at the sea from the balcony. Without crying, this time. Or else from laughing.
textes.Et revoir la lumière bleue, une fois. Av: And to see the blue light again, once. With someone beside me who sees it too.
textes.Et revoir une dernière fois ma baleine a: And to see my whale with trees on its back one last time. The youngsters say it was an island. An island that winked at me, then.
textes.Et résoudre une vraie affaire. Avec un v: And solve a real case. With a real culprit, a confession and a signature at the bottom of the report. A culprit who isn't a chicken. I've had enough of chickens.
textes.Et salée ! Comme les larmes. Mais en plu: And salty! Like tears. But bigger.
textes.Et sans chêne, la coque tiendra combien: And without oak, how long will the hull hold?
textes.Et sculpter un visage. Un seul, qui ress: And to carve a face. Just one, that looks like somebody. After that, I'll make fish for the rest of my life. On purpose, this time.
textes.Et si Cerbère n'en veut pas… mange-les !: And if Cerberus doesn't want them… eat them! They're very good for humans too.
textes.Et si on retrouvait les quatre sceaux ?: What if we found the four seals?
textes.Et ta bière, c'est de l'eau avec du brui: And your fizz is water with noise in it.
textes.Et ta lame, elle porte toujours bien son: And your blade, is it still living up to its name? Bring it to me, I'll give it a makeover.
textes.Et ta potion avait un goût d'écorce brûl: And your potion tasted of burnt bark.
textes.Et tes voisins, ils sont comment ?: And your neighbours, what are they like?
textes.Et tisser un jour une passerelle si long: And one day to weave a footbridge so long it reaches all the way to your island. Taeron says it's impossible. All the more reason.
textes.Et toi, Nori, toujours à l'eau ? Tu vas: And you, Nori, still on water? You'll rust!
textes.Et toi, de quoi tu rêves ?: And you, what do you dream of?
textes.Et toi, dis-moi franchement, les yeux da: And you, tell me honestly, look me in the eye: do you run, or do you walk?
And you, have you eaten? No? Sit down.
textes.Et toi, tu as pointé comme une baguette: And you pointed like a soggy baguette.
textes.Et toi, tu mesures comme un facteur !: And you measure like a postman!
And you lose like a baker.
textes.Et toi, tu rentres trop tard. Je vois ta: And you come home too late. I can see your lantern at the basin.
textes.Et toi, tu rigoles ?!: And you, you think it's funny?!
And you're still full of hot air.
textes.Et ton trente-troisième ingrédient, c'es: And your thirty-third ingredient, is it cinnamon?
textes.Et trois cents ans que tu écoutes. Elle: And you've been listening for three hundred years. My riddle works rather well.
And three slices of bread, I know.
textes.Et trouver le trente-troisième ingrédien: And find Aïcha's thirty-third ingredient. Not to sell it! Just to see her face.
textes.Et trouver un mot, en haut. Un seul. Un: And find a word, up there. Just one. One would be enough. Hrmm. Still looking.
textes.Et tu as encore fait boum-boum à mes ban: And have you been going boom-boom at my banana trees again?
textes.Et tu as rendu la vie à l'Arbre sacré. L: And you gave life back to the sacred Tree. Bois-Doré will never forget it.
textes.Et tu l'as mangé, au moins ? Tu es toute: And did you at least eat it? You're all skin and bones!
textes.Et tu m'as frappé %d fois. Je n'oublie p: And you hit me %d times. I don't forget.
textes.Et tu m'as frappé une fois. Je n'oublie: And you hit me once. I don't forget.
textes.Et tu m'as rapporté de quoi faire six ma: And you brought me enough to make six shovel handles. That, I don't forget.
textes.Et tu me laisses le premier rayon ?: And you'll leave me the first ray?
textes.Et tu n'as pas dit un mot, cette fois ?: And you didn't say a word, this time?
textes.Et un fantôme, s'il en reste un de libre: And a ghost, if there's a spare one left. But a polite one, who doesn't snore. The one on the fourth floor I'll leave to Monsieur Edmond.
textes.Et un jour, battre le fer à côté de ce p: And one day, hammer iron side by side with that little smith Octave. To show him. Kindly. With a big hammer.
textes.Et un jour, dire un truc à quelqu'un. Un: And one day, say something to someone. Something real. Longer than three words. … One day.
textes.Et un jour, par hasard, en goûtant une c: And one day, by chance, tasting a spoonful, to stumble upon nonna's real flavour. I'd recognise it straight away. I'd cry into the soup, and it would be even better.
textes.Et un jour, planter une graine de l'Arbr: And one day, plant a seed of the Mother Tree on every island of the archipelago, so that human children can climb in it. Trees quickly learn to love those who climb them.
textes.Et un jour, rentrer dans la jungle, ouvr: And one day, go back to the jungle, open a nut with one stroke in front of my grandfather and serve him a punch. He'll say: “One stroke? Fine.” Where I come from, that means bravo.
textes.Et un jour, un vrai lord anglais est ent: And one day, a real English lord walked into my shop. He picked up a snow globe, a little lighthouse in the snow, shook it, and cried “Splendid!”. He declared it the favourite piece of his four thousand objects. Four thousand! Since then, I'm supplier to a lord. It's written on my shop window. And I tell everyone. Right now, for instance, I'm telling you.
textes.Et un soir, jouer avec Django, le guitar: And one night, play with Django, the guitarist at the Perroquet Bleu. A techno-waltz. Port-Azur would never get over it.
textes.Et un soir, oser dire une phrase à quelq: And one evening, to dare say a sentence to someone… without a basket of croissants in my arms to hide behind.
textes.Et un soir, un perroquet bleu qui entrer: And one evening, a blue parrot flying in through the window and landing on the counter, all by itself, like a regular. I'd serve it a glass of water. It would pay in feathers.
textes.Et un soir, une anisette sur le quai. Fe: And one evening, a glass of lemonade on the quay. Fernand on one side, Anselme on the other. On the same bench. I wouldn't say anything. Neither would they, probably. That would already be a lot.
textes.Et un tiramisu, deux cuillères. Cette fo: And a tiramisu, two spoons. This time, you eat it!
textes.Et un verre d'EAU pour Nori !: And a glass of WATER for Nori!
textes.Et une chambre pour ma tante, avec un po: And a room for my aunt, with a stove. She'll say no. I'll build it anyway.
textes.Et une fois… rire. Fort. Sans que person: And once… laugh. Loudly. With nobody watching. Hmph. Forget that.
textes.Et une petite horloge. À moi. Pour la bo: And a little clock. Mine. For the jeweller's shop: she hasn't got one. A shop with no time in it, that won't do. Hm.
textes.Et une petite maison, avec un ponton. Po: And a little house, with a jetty. For Gertrude. The boat, I mean. She deserves a jetty of her own.
textes.Et une photo de toute l'île vue d'en hau: And a photo of the whole island from above, at night, with the wall of sound blinking. I'd need a giant bird. Apparently they exist.
textes.Et une source d'eau fraîche juste à côté: And a spring of fresh water right next to the dance floor. That way, nobody would have an excuse any more.
textes.Et voilà ! L'Alouette. Toile tendue, hau: There! The Alouette. Canvas stretched, stays adjusted, spring harness. I've invented something! Well, the hang glider may already have existed elsewhere… but not in Cliquetis! Go to the end of the runway, and take flight!
textes.Et voilà, tout est par terre. Je la réét: And there you go, everything's on the floor. I'll turn it off again tonight, it's more restful for sleeping.
textes.Et voilà. Attention, c'est chaud. Avec u: There you go. Careful, it's hot. With a cloud of cream. A real cloud, from Rainville.
And there we go. Another ghost.
textes.Et voilà. Prends le temps de le savourer: There you are. Take your time and enjoy it.
textes.Et voilà. Prenez le temps de le savourer: There you are. Take your time and enjoy it.
textes.Et voir Bondi courir derrière quelqu'un,: And to see Bondi run behind someone, just once. He runs better when he's chasing. Everyone runs better when they're chasing. I should know.
textes.Et voir Carène tenir debout sans moi, un: And to see Carène stand on its own without me, one day. That's an admiral's real job: to no longer be needed. I'm not there yet.
textes.Et voir Nina capitaine. Ou glacière. Ou: And to see Nina become a captain. Or an ice-cream maker. Or both, on a boat that sells ice cream. Even if it's far away. Especially if it's far away: I'll bake her croissants for the journey.
And to see Nori finish a mug. A real one. I'd keel over, but I'd keel over happy.
textes.Et voir la vieille barque du bassin pass: And see the old boat from the basin round the point one day, under a hand-sewn sail. From afar. If I cry, I'll say it's the tar.
textes.Et voir le lever du soleil depuis l'eau,: And watch the sunrise from the water, with Sofia. Mistral says his track sounds even better from out there.
textes.Et voir, un printemps, les lanternes ble: And to see, one spring, the blue lanterns on every bridge without having had to hang them myself. That day, I'll know Ramure no longer needs my old paws.
textes.Et vous m'avez frappé %d fois. Je n'oubl: And you hit me %d times. I don't forget.
textes.Et vous m'avez frappé une fois. Je n'oub: And you hit me once. I don't forget.
textes.Et vous, pas de lunettes d'aviatrice. Je: And you've got no aviator goggles. I'm a little disappointed.
textes.Et zéro lit. Moi non plus, remarque. On: And zero beds. Same as me, mind you. We're even.
textes.Et être là, juste à côté, le jour où Ond: And to be there, right beside her, the day Ondine sees the sun. I'd like to see her face. I think I'd find my own in it, at her age.
textes.Euh… La table, les chaises, le lit, l'ar: Uh… The table, the chairs, the bed, the wardrobe… everything is on the CEILING.
textes.Euh… garde-le, va. Ça me ferait de la pe: Er… you keep it, go on. I'd feel bad throwing it away.
textes.Euphorique ! Le dernier morceau, j'ai cr: Ecstatic! On that last track, I thought I was going to take off.
textes.Ewen ! Tu l'as trouvé, mon monstre, aujo: Ewen! Did you find my monster today?
textes.Ewen ? Je connais ses genoux mieux que l: Ewen? I know his knees better than he does. Without him, I'd have half my bandages left, and I'd be very bored.
textes.Ewen a encore grimpé à la grande hune sa: Ewen climbed up to the main top again without permission. The Admiral had him scrubbing the deck for three days.
textes.Ewen compte combien de temps je reste so: Ewen counts how long I stay underwater, and he always gets it wrong. He talks more than a seagull. But he's always waiting for me at the edge. That's rare.
textes.Ewen est arrivé un matin avec une échard: Ewen turned up one morning with a splinter as big as a nail in his thumb: he'd wanted to see if he could climb up to the crow's nest without using his hands. Answer: no. I pulled it out, he didn't cry. He just asked if he could keep it to show Lucie.
textes.Ewen est bavard, maladroit, il sonne la: Ewen's a chatterbox, clumsy, he rings the bell at the drop of a hat. He's the best cabin boy Carène has had in fifty years. Don't you repeat that to him.
textes.Ewen fait des nœuds dans mes hamacs, son: Ewen ties knots in my hammocks, rings the bell under my windows and climbs everything. Somebody has to tell the Admiral. Usually it's me. He never stays cross with me for long, which is annoying.
textes.Ewen m'a demandé combien de trous il fal: Ewen asked me how many holes you'd have to plug to make the Léviathan float. I opened the black book: four thousand three hundred and twelve, plus tomorrow's. He said: “Oh, that's not that many.” I sighed. That evening, I did the sums for real. Two of us, working hard, sixty years. He's twelve. It could be done.
textes.Ewen sonne la cloche à contretemps, grim: Ewen rings the bell at the wrong moment, climbs where it's forbidden, and asks more questions than there are answers. He's got the makings of a captain. That's exactly what worries me.
textes.Ewen veut devenir capitaine. Il a douze: Ewen wants to be a captain. He's twelve and he's already got the hat.
textes.Ewen veut remettre le Léviathan à l'eau: Ewen wants to put the Léviathan back in the water and sail off with everyone. Everyone laughs. Me, I sigh. Because I know how many holes there are. And because some people really do leave.
textes.Ewen écrit mes lettres et corrige mes hi: Ewen writes my letters and corrects my stories. He adds dragons. The worst of it is, they're better with his dragons.
textes.Ewen. Combien de coups pour neuf heures: Ewen. How many strokes for nine o'clock?
textes.Ewen. Je descends longtemps. Tu comptes: Ewen. I'm going down for a long time. Will you count?
Ewen. Don't touch the tar without me.
textes.Ewen. Pas un nœud aujourd'hui. Pas un se: Ewen. Not one knot today. Not a single one.
textes.Ewen. Si je trouve un seul nœud de chais: Ewen. If I find a single bowline, I'm telling the Admiral.
textes.Exact. L'affaire des croissants. Chaque: Exactly. The croissant affair. Every night, half a dozen go missing from the bakery. I have three witnesses: Margaux, her daughter Nina and Bruno the ice-cream seller. Question them. Me, I'm keeping an eye on… the ice-cream seller.
textes.Exactement. Tu me dois toujours trois la: Exactly. You still owe me three lamps.
textes.Excellent ! Le corail se laisse tailler: Excellent! The coral is carving like butter today.
textes.Excellent ! Un rubis gros comme un œuf d: Excellent! A ruby as big as a raven's egg arrived this morning.
textes.Excellent choix ! Ma grand-mère disait t: Excellent choice! My grandmother always used to say… um… I forget. But it was about that, I'm sure.
textes.Excellent. J'ai encore battu Marcel. Il: Excellent. I beat Marcel again. He'll tell you otherwise.
textes.Excellente ! J'ai reçu un vieil atlas de: Excellent! I've received an old atlas of the Sky Kings. Apparently there was once an island that flew.
textes.Excellente ! J'ai une carte à moitié bla: Excellent! I've got a half-blank map in front of me. There's nothing more exciting in the world.
textes.Excellente ! J'ai vendu trois cordes, de: Excellent! I sold three ropes, two lanterns and a crab that didn't want to be sold.
textes.Excellente ! La saison est bonne, les hô: Excellent! The season's good, the hotels are full, and it hasn't rained for forty days.
textes.Excellente version. Je n'y avais pas pen: Excellent version. I hadn't thought of that.
textes.Extraordinary ! Elle sera la reine de ma: Extraordinary! She will be the queen of my collection. Here are two gold coins, minted by my great-grandfather. Cheers!
textes.FAUSSE ?! Ma carte était un chef-d'œuvre: WRONG?! My map was a masterpiece! Gaston, remind me never to speak of that fellow again.
textes.Faelar ! Cette fois, tu me donnes la rép: Faelar! This time, will you give me the answer?
textes.Faelar ! Raconte celle du hibou !: Faelar! Tell the one about the owl!
textes.Faelar ! Une histoire pour mon four, ce: Faelar! A story for my oven this morning?
textes.Faelar ? Le plus bavard des elfes, et le: Faelar? The chattiest of elves, and the only one who's ever beaten me. He left me a riddle three hundred years ago, and he had the nerve to grow old with the answer.
textes.Faelar ? Le plus vieil elfe du monde, et: Faelar? The oldest elf in the world, and he knows my song by heart! He thinks the hero is shorter than in the verses. That's poetry, come now!
textes.Faelar a neuf cent quatre-vingt-sept ans: Faelar is nine hundred and eighty-seven, and he refuses to drink a tea unless it has a story. So I make them up for him. He knows. He drinks them anyway.
textes.Faelar a toussé pendant trois siècles. I: Faelar coughed for three centuries. He said it was “an old friend who punctuates my stories”. I made him a hundred herbal teas. He'd pour half of each into his fern's pot. The fern never coughed, mind you. It's now two metres tall.
textes.Faelar a vu pousser presque tous les arb: Faelar has watched almost every tree in Bois-Doré grow. Nobody tells stories better than he does. When he doesn't fall asleep halfway through.
textes.Faelar connaît trois mille histoires ! I: Faelar knows three thousand stories! He falls asleep in the middle, but that doesn't matter: I know the ending. Well, I make one up. He says mine are better.
textes.Faelar m'a appris qu'une histoire ne rem: Faelar taught me that a story doesn't fill your belly. He didn't mean to. That's why I became a baker. I save him the first crust of every batch.
textes.Faelar m'a appris à pêcher la lumière en: Faelar taught me to fish for light while talking non-stop beside me. I think he did it on purpose: if you can fish next to Faelar, you can fish anywhere.
textes.Faelar m'a dit que les esprits-lucioles: Faelar told me the firefly spirits dance above the rings of white mushrooms. I saw one! I wanted to follow it, but Faelar hooked my sleeve with his walking stick. He said: “Not you. Not yet.” I sulked at him for two days. Then he told me a story and I forgot.
textes.Faelar m'a parlé d'un cercle de champign: Faelar told me about a ring of white mushrooms where spirits dance. I laughed. Then I went there seven nights in a row. On the eighth, there was a little light. I ran home and shook him: he'd been asleep for two days. He opened one eye, said “I know”, and went back to sleep.
textes.Faelar raconte des choses que personne n: Faelar tells of things nobody has seen. I go and look. Most of the time there's nothing. But sometimes there's something, and that's why I keep going back.
textes.Faelar raconte qu'un humain a vaincu le: Faelar says a human defeated the great serpent under the sea. Was it you?! Have a loaf. Have two!
textes.Faelar s'est endormi au milieu d'une his: Faelar fell asleep in the middle of a story. Again. We put a flower on his nose.
textes.Faelar vient raconter une histoire à mon: Faelar comes to tell my oven a story every morning while the bread bakes. I swear the oven rises better. Faelar swears he doesn't come for the crust. One of us is lying, and it isn't the oven.
textes.Faelar, tu t'étais endormi exprès, ce so: Faelar, you fell asleep on purpose that night. Admit it.
textes.Faelar. Ton hibou d'argent, au nord. Rie: Faelar. Your silver owl, up north. Nothing.
textes.Faire la connaissance de Pip, le plus je: Meet Pip, the youngest of the apprentices (in the Academy courtyard in the morning, on the village square in the evening)
textes.Faire le tour complet de l'île avec Nimi: To walk all the way around the island with Nimiel one day, taking our time. She'll run ahead, I'll walk behind, and we'll meet up at the same spot. That's how a family travels.
textes.Faire le tour de la ville en monorail (l: Ride the monorail around the city (all four stations)
textes.Faire le tour de toute la grande île en: Run all the way round the big island! Cliquetis, Tazira, Carène, and back to Ramure. And get there before the Zéphyr!
textes.Faire les offrandes du Grand Temple d'Az: Make the offerings at the Great Temple of Aztlán
textes.Faire redescendre les quatre livres envo: Bring the four runaway books back down with telekinesis (key 9 then V, aiming at the book; in VR, left trigger): on the library roof, on the highest Moonstone of the Circle, at a window of the Leaning Tower and in a big oak in the Twisted Wood
textes.Faire siffler l'ampli (l'effet Larsen): Make the amp squeal (the Larsen effect)
textes.Faire tourner la vieille vanne de la gra: Turn the old sluice valve of Ramure's big pond with the Cog (key 3 then X; in VR, B), then, at night, take the Seal of Mists from the round stone at the bottom of the pond
Make a map of all my tunnels. All of them! Even the ones I've forgotten. Especially those. And hang it above the bed, for Brunna.
textes.Faire venir mon bateau au ponton de Port: Bring my boat to the Port-Azur jetty
textes.Fais voir tes mains. Et tes coudes. Et d: Show me your hands. And your elbows. And behind your ears.
textes.Faites glisser pour déplacer, molette po: Drag to move, mouse wheel to zoom.
Drag to move, scroll wheel to zoom.  ▲ you  ★ objective  ⚓ liner
textes.Fanny ? Elle déborde, elle rit, elle ren: Fanny? She overflows, she laughs, she knocks everything over. A whirlwind that smells of croissants. She's a good friend. A very good friend. Yep.
textes.Fanny pétrit en dansant. Une fois, elle: Fanny kneads while dancing. Once, she shaped a whole batch of croissants “in rhythm”, to the music still in her head. They came out of the oven all twisted, all in the same direction, as if they were dancing. I sold them as “party croissants”. They went before all the others.
textes.Fanny, c'est la famille qui arrive par l: Fanny is the family that arrives by boat every evening. She smells of warm croissants. One day she'll say yes to banana croissants. I can feel it. Good, good.
textes.Fanny, c'est un feu d'artifice avec un t: Fanny is a firework in an apron. I found her dancing behind her counter and brought her back here. My best idea. After the crab step.
textes.Fanny, mon apprentie. Elle danse toute l: Fanny, my apprentice. She dances all night at the beach party and kneads all morning. I don't know when she sleeps. Neither does she. I adore her.
textes.Farineuse ! Je suis farineuse jusqu'au b: Floury! I'm floury right up to the tips of my ears.
textes.Fatigué, mais content. La caisse numéro: Tired, but happy. Crate number twelve arrived in one piece. Her name's Gertrude.
textes.Fatigué. J'ai battu le fer toute la nuit: Tired. I was hammering iron all night. A sword doesn't make itself while you sing.
textes.Fatigué. J'ai compté les dunes du sud to: Tired. I spent all day counting the southern dunes. They won't stay put.
textes.Fatigué. Mais la coque n'a pas pris une: Tired. But the hull didn't take a drop today. Well, hardly a drop.
Tired. Forty feet of tunnel yesterday. And it caved in. Well, thirty-nine.
textes.Fatigué. À mon âge, les filets pèsent pl: Tired. At my age, the nets weigh more than the fish.
textes.Fatiguée. Garder un arbre, c'est garder: Tired. Guarding a tree is like guarding a dream: you must never quite close your eyes.
textes.Fatiguée. J'ai veillé toute la nuit sur: Tired. I sat up all night over a brew. It went sour. Like my mood.
textes.Fatiguée. Le marteau pèse plus lourd le: Tired. The hammer weighs more in the evening. The honey, less.
textes.Fatiguée. Le roi a chanté jusqu'à l'aube: Tired. The king sang until dawn. Have you ever heard a dwarf king sing? Don't.
textes.Fañch a encore parlé à son poisson. Il d: Fañch has been talking to his fish again. He says it answers him.
textes.Fañch a laissé tomber le couteau de son: Fañch dropped his grandfather's knife in ten fathoms of water. I dived three times. At the bottom, a crab the size of a plate had settled on it and didn't want to give it back. We had a discussion. I won. Fañch cried when he got it back, and he said it was the salt. In Carène, everybody says that.
textes.Fañch connaissait ma mère. Il m'a appris: Fañch knew my mother. He taught me to read the currents before I could read at all. He drops everything in the water, I fish it out. That's our arrangement.
textes.Fañch m'apprend à barrer, à l'aube, en s: Fañch is teaching me to steer, at dawn, in secret. He makes terrible jokes and smells of mackerel. He's the only one who's never asked me why I want to leave.
textes.Fañch parle à ses poissons. Je sais pour: Fañch talks to his fish. I know why he talks to them: it's my fault, and I'll never apologise for it. He's stubborn. So am I.
textes.Fañch se moque de mes comptes. Il dit qu: Fañch makes fun of my counting. He says no ships ever pass. That's not true: every evening, one passes. His. Late.
textes.Fañch vit sous une barque retournée et m: Fañch lives under an upturned boat and gets me up on it every autumn to plug his roof. He pays me in mackerel. I say there's no need, I take them anyway. He laughs at everything. It's restful.
textes.Fañch. Ton toit tiendra jusqu'au printem: Fañch. Your roof will hold till spring.
textes.Fañch. Tu es encore rentré après la lant: Fañch. You came in after the lantern again.
textes.Fenêtre fermée, c'est noté. La chambre n: Window closed, duly noted. Room nine double-locks. I'm keeping it in mind, for you.
textes.Fenêtre ouverte, je l'ai noté. Si vous p: Window open, I've made a note. If you take a room, I'll put you on the open-sea side. With the seagulls.
textes.Fer forgé par Octave. En main, clic (gâc: Iron forged by Octave. In hand, click (trigger in VR) to dig in sand or earth: shells, coins… and sometimes a treasure.
textes.Ferme, Aëlwen. Ce soir, mon cœur va bien: Close up, Aëlwen. Tonight my heart is fine. She looked at me.
Locked. A sign: “FOR SALE. Wisteria Cottage, unbeatable view, wisteria included, frogs optional. Inquire with Monsieur Prosper, Upper Town.”
textes.Fermé à clé. Une petite clé l'ouvrirait…: Locked. A small key would open it… You can find them in other chests, and sometimes in crates and jars.
textes.Fermée. Très sage. Les embruns sont traî: Closed. Very wise. Sea spray is treacherous, and mosquitoes have no manners. I would recommend room nine: its window double-locks.
textes.Fernand ! A splendid fellow. Un vieux lo: Fernand! A splendid fellow. An old sea dog who knows every monster in the ocean, and who let me have a dragon tooth for next to nothing. His eye twinkles when he sees me. Emotion, no doubt.
textes.Fernand ! Mon premier patron, mon sauveu: Fernand! My first boss, my saviour, the best fisherman in the archipelago. He tells the story of my shipwreck badly, but I forgive him: he was there.
textes.Fernand ! Ta daurade, elle a l'œil trist: Fernand! Your sea bream has a sad eye. I'll take it off you cheaper.
textes.Fernand ? Un menteur de première classe: Fernand? A first-class liar about the size of fish. And the man who held the other end of the net, the morning of Marius. He has the best spot on the quay. I won't take it back from him.
textes.Fernand pêchait avec mon frère, autrefoi: Fernand used to fish with my brother. We don't speak any more. Something about a net.
textes.Fernand racontait à tout le quai son mér: Fernand was telling the whole quay about his forty-kilo grouper. I had it carried onto the harbour office scales, in front of him and in front of witnesses. Twenty-five. He said the fish had lost weight from emotion. Since then, when he starts the story, I just say “Twenty-five”. He corrects himself. Every other time.
textes.Fernand, c'est mon vieux pêcheur, mon fo: Fernand is my old fisherman, my supplier and my worst critic. His sea bream are the finest in the archipelago. His compliments, he keeps to himself.
textes.Fernand. Il pêchait avec mon frère. Il a: Fernand. He fished with my brother. He kept what wasn't his to keep. We don't speak any more. That's all.
Hooked! Keep the tension in the green.
textes.Festival du Larsen\nChaque soir à 20 h 3:
Larsen Festival
Every evening at 8:30 PM: “The Sun and the Rain”,
the two villages on the Main Stage!
Fireworks at 11 PM.
textes.Festival du Larsen\nLa Grande Scène se p:
Larsen Festival
The Main Stage is getting ready…
Come back soon: it's going to be loud!
Fire good. Fire warm. Ougha like fire.
textes.Fffiou ! Je repasse demain, promis !: Whoosh! I'll be back tomorrow, promise!
textes.Fidèle, oui. Et je compte toujours le ce: Faithful, yes. And I'm still counting that centimetre.
Off you go, off you go! The forest is waiting.
Off you go. And don't knock anybody over tonight.
textes.Fin de l'alerte : les navets se sont tou: End of the alert: the turnips have all replanted themselves, looking innocent. Father Gaubert sighs: “They'll do it again. They always do.”
textes.Firmin Cogne a perdu l'engrenage d'or de: Firmin Cogne lost the golden gear of his perpetual-motion engine during a demonstration. It rolled all the way down the cliffs, towards the harbour.
Flatterer. You won't get off that easily.
textes.Fondant ! Comme mes glaces. Il fait si c: Melting! Like my ice creams. It's so hot.
textes.Forgefer, la cité des nains: Forgefer, the city of the dwarves
textes.Forgefer, la cité sous la montagne: Forgefer, the city under the mountain
textes.Forgefer. Une halle immense taillée dans: Forgefer. An immense hall carved into the mountain: pillars engraved with runes, channels of lava lighting everything orange, the smell of coal and hot iron… At the far end, on his throne, King Thorgal.
textes.Forger une lame que Borin regarde sans d: To forge a blade Borin looks at without saying “Hmpf”. Even just a little “Hm”. A “Hm” would already be glory.
textes.Forger une lame si parfaite que Nori n'y: Forge a blade so perfect that Nori can't find a thing to fault. Nothing. Not a rune, not a hair. He'll open his mouth, and shut it again. That day, the rounds are on me. Every round.
textes.Forger une pièce si belle que Borin la p: Forge a piece so beautiful that Borin sets it down on a Forgefer anvil. Without a word. Not even “not bad”. Just sets it down.
textes.Forger une épée si belle que même Borin: Forge a sword so beautiful that even Borin Barbe-de-Fer would look at it without a word. Just once. I'd settle for his silence. That, at least, costs nothing.
textes.Forgé par Brutus, trois dents de crocodi: Forged by Brutus, with three crocodile teeth set in the iron. As long as it's in your bag, your punches hit harder in brawls (+1). Fists only.
textes.Forgé par Hector à l'Enclume Bleue : lam: Forged by Hector at L'Enclume Bleue: a curved blade of blued steel, with a brass shell guard. Damage: 10, and the third hit of a combo strikes half again as hard.
textes.Forgée par Borin Barbe-de-Fer dans l'aci: Forged by Borin Barbe-de-Fer from volcano steel: a short, broad blade, a golden guard, a ruby on the pommel. Damage: 9, and the third hit of a combo strikes half again as hard.
textes.Formidable ! La taverne est pleine, les: Fantastic! The tavern's full, the songs are out of tune, all is well.
textes.Forêt calme. Brume calme. Tout est calme: Forest calm. Mist calm. Everything's calm, Thalion.
textes.Fouiller les caisses au bout du quai, cô: Search the crates at the end of the quay, on the lighthouse side
textes.Fraise ! Peuchère, tu as du goût. Tu con: Strawberry! My oh my, you've got taste. Do you know the strawberry-dolphin? Nina invented it. With a pinch of sea salt. You'll weep.
textes.Frappe le tronc avec le fer de la hache: Strike the trunk with the iron of the axe!
textes.Frapper à la porte des quatre maisons: Knock on the doors of the four houses
textes.Fromage de chèvre des cendres, le meille: Ash goat cheese, the best in the world. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Frustrée. Il me manque les vraies couleu: Frustrated. I'm missing the true colours of the sea: the red of coral, the yellow of hill honey, the brown of coconut. Mainland paint tubes are so dull.
textes.Frérot, sois honnête : tu crois que j'ai: Bro, be honest: do you think I danced with a dolphin?
textes.Fuiii ! Brioche apparaît sur un muret, s: Weee! Brioche appears on a low wall, stretches for a long time, and joins you without hurrying.
textes.Fuiii-iii ! Sardine arrive au grand galo: Weee-eee! Sardine comes at a full gallop, ears flying (well, one of them).
textes.Fundin ! Le soufflet, pas ma barbe !: Fundin! The bellows, not my beard!
textes.Fundin a des bras de nain, un cœur de na: Fundin has a dwarf's arms, a dwarf's heart and a head full of air. He botches everything, but he botches it with gusto. Hmph. I was the same. Don't tell him.
textes.Fundin a deux mains gauches et un cœur t: Fundin has two left hands and a heart too big for his chest. His eyes follow me when I walk by. He thinks I don't see him. I see everything: it's my job.
textes.Fundin est un bon gamin avec deux mains: Fundin is a good lad with two left hands. Borin shouts, he apologises, he tries again. I feed him on the sly, or he'd forget to eat.
textes.Fundin, tes bottes ! Recule de l'enclume: Fundin, your boots! Step back from the anvil.
textes.Fundin. Tu as encore de la suie sur le n: Fundin. You've got soot on your nose again.
textes.Furieux. Le cochonnet a disparu ! Et Mar: Furious. The jack has vanished! And Marcel says it's my fault. I say he threw it too hard.
textes.Fâchée ! Quelqu'un me vole des croissant: Cross! Someone steals my croissants every night. The constable can't find a thing.
textes.Fébrile. Toutes les légendes situent la: Feverish. Every legend places the sunken city south-west of the village. But I can't swim.
textes.Félix ! Votre carte est sèche, je vous l: Félix! Your map is dry, here it is.
textes.Félix connaît l'archipel par cœur sans l: Félix knows the archipelago by heart without ever having seen it. He describes islands to me, and I want to paint them. He's a poet who makes maps.
textes.Félix m'a dessiné la route du tour de l': Félix drew me the route round the archipelago, island by island, with the currents, the winds, and a little star wherever there's a good place to eat. I pinned it on the wall of the rental shop. Customers look at it. I say it's my next trip. They ask me when. I answer: “Soon.”
textes.Félix note toutes mes prédictions dans u: Félix writes down all my predictions in a little black notebook, with the date, to catch me out. He's found three that came true. Three! He came to tell me, furious, as if I'd done it on purpose. I asked him which ones. He refused to tell me. I think one of the three is about him.
textes.Félix, c'est mon navigateur. Il connaît: Félix is my navigator. He knows every island, every coast, every current. He's never seen them, but that's a detail. He draws the way people dream.
textes.Félix, le cartographe. Un homme qui conn: Félix, the map-maker. A man who knows every island and has never seen a single one. He says I'm his eyes at sea. I say he has good eyes on land.
textes.Félix, le libraire. Il dit que je ne voi: Félix, the bookseller. He says I don't see the future, I just know the gossip. He may be right. But he comes to check every week. You don't keep an eye on something you don't believe in.
textes.Félix, mon libraire. Le seul homme de ce: Félix, my bookseller. The only man on this island who understands my charts as well as I do. “The two greatest explorers who never left,” he says. It's true. It's sad. It's very true.
textes.GERMAINE ! L'AMPLI ! (Elle court cherche: GERMAINE! THE AMP! (She runs to fetch Clou. Clou arrives, takes Germaine, hugs her to his chest and says nothing for a whole minute. Then he nods at you. Just once. Rouille cries.) He nodded at you! Do you know how many people have gotten a nod from Clou? Four! And the drumsticks... you keep them. We don't have a real drummer yet. They're waiting for someone. Maybe you'll find out who.
textes.GORGOTH LE CORNU, le champion de l'arène: GORGOTH THE HORNED, champion of the arena! He charges with lowered horns: step aside at the last moment, strike him in the back. The crowd roars!
textes.GROSSE-DENT ! Le roi du Cirque des Os. S: GROSSE-DENT! The king of the Bone Hollow. His skin is thick… When he ROARS, he's going to charge: dodge at the last moment and let him smash into the rock of the hollow. Stunned, he takes double damage! Don't stay behind him: his tail sweeps everything.
textes.Gagner la Grande Course : prendre le dép: Win the Great Race: start under the arch of the Games Clearing (E), pass under the ten arches in order and come back first
textes.Gagner le troisième morceau contre Sylva: Win the third piece from Sylvain (three wins in a row at the big table of the Shark's Tooth), then take the three pieces to Philémon Lunette, the mapmaker (in front of his tower)
textes.Gagner les quatre manches du Tournoi des: Win the four rounds of the Tournament of Horns (strike the gong, at the edge of the arena sand)
textes.Galettes d'algues (deux cœurs !). Et je: Seaweed cakes (two hearts!). And I buy fish, shells, pearls, shark teeth. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Garde le Bail, mon grand. Non, ne discut: Keep the Lease, kiddo. No, don't argue: the assembly voted. It'll be better with you than in a drawer: that way, it'll travel. The Boucan is ours, forever, and thanks to you. Here, the whole common fund. And a title. We don't like titles here. But this one, we voted for laughing: Hero of Port-Boucan. Tonight, concert. You go to the front of the line.
textes.Garde ça, {surnom}. Tu en auras plus bes: Keep it, {surnom}. You'll need it more than I do. Me, I fight with metaphors.
Keep it well, then. It's beautiful.
Keep it a while longer, captain.
textes.Garde-le, voyons : on dirait que tu en a: Keep it, come now: looks like you need it.
Keep it. It smells of… dry land.
textes.Garder la Grande Porte un jour. Une seul: To guard the Great Gate for one day. Just one day, while Bramm has a fizz at Ulfa's. Just to see his face when he gets back.
textes.Garder le silence ! Vous connaissez la p: Remain silent! You know the procedure, I see. That's very suspicious. Or very polite. I'll keep watch on you during my rounds. Discreetly.
textes.Gaspard ! Kick et Basse te disent bonjou: Gaspard! Kick and Bass say hello!
textes.Gaspard ! Tu as commencé par le plancher: Gaspard! Did you start with the floor this time?
textes.Gaspard ? Mon meilleur élève. Mon seul é: Gaspard? My best pupil. My only pupil, all right, but the best. He nods when I talk: either he's listening, or it's the music.
textes.Gaspard Fusain, le guetteur du Belvédère: Gaspard Fusain, the lookout of the Belvedere, saw a little glint shining at the top of Mount Charcoal through his telescope. He thinks it's the pot of purple (no. 6). He'd like you to look for yourself, then go and fetch it.
textes.Gaspard boit de l'eau toutes les cinq mi: Gaspard drinks water every five minutes. He's right to, but he tells everyone about it.
Gaspard says a hut is meant to be shut. I leave the door open for the breeze, and I've got three crabs living in my hammock: Kick, Bass and Mistral. Gaspard sighs very loudly when he sees them. But the other day I caught him giving a bit of banana to Bass. He said he was just passing by.
textes.Gaspard est monté à mon échelle demander: Gaspard climbed my ladder to ask for nails. He saw my joints, mortise and tenon, not a single nail, as it happens. He stood there with his mouth open for an hour. He even stopped nodding. Now that's a compliment.
textes.Gaspard est un bon garçon qui boit de l': Gaspard is a good lad who drinks water and tells everyone about it. He's right: I carried him to the spring the day he wasn't drinking any. He owes me a song.
textes.Gaspard m'a construit l'estrade, là, sou: Gaspard built me the stage, right here under my feet. He nods his head, he drinks water, he tells you to drink water. The calmest guy on the beach, and the most stubborn.
textes.Gaspard m'a construit une cabane au-dess: Gaspard built me a hut above my banana grove, eighty-three planks. I paid him in bunches, one per plank. He said thank you for every bunch. Afterwards, for three months, he made a funny face every time he saw a banana. I think he really loved them.
textes.Gaspard m'a prêté sa cabane d'essai pour: Gaspard lent me his test hut for two nights, and it's been three weeks. He knocks before going into his own place. He's the nicest boy on the island, and the most obsessed with water.
textes.Gaspard, c'est mon voisin de jungle et m: Gaspard is my jungle neighbour and my brother at heart. He built my hut, he stood my banana trees back up, and he tells me to drink water. Good, good. I drink coconut.
textes.Gaspard, je t'ai raconté la fois où…: Gaspard, did I tell you about the time…
textes.Gaspard, l'estrade a grincé deux fois de: Gaspard, the stage creaked twice in a row.
textes.Gaspard, vous ne rêviez pas : voici le v: Gaspard, you weren't dreaming: here's the purple!
textes.Gaspard. On hoche ensemble. Il ne parle: Gaspard. We nod together. He doesn't talk much, neither do I. We understand each other. … And he brings me water. I only drink his.
textes.Gaston : « Barnabé est un génie ! Un gén: Gaston: “Barnabé is a genius! A genius!”
textes.Gaston : « RRRAAAH ! » Il ne te parlera: Gaston: “RRRAAAH!” He won't speak to you for a week. Neither will I, maybe.
textes.Gaston : « Rrrah ! Il a bon goût ! » Il: Gaston: “Rrrah! Good taste!” He adores you now. That's rare.
Gaston has learned his kick drum. “Boom. Boom. Boom.” At five in the morning, right above my pillow. Mistral says it's a remix. I say it's a curse. But I tap my foot all the same.
textes.Gaston dit que c'était une luciole. Gast: Gaston says it was a firefly. Gaston is jealous.
textes.Gaston dit que je suis le meilleur serve: Gaston says I'm the best waiter on the island. I'm the only waiter robot on the island.
textes.Gaston m'a fait un smiley qui tire la la: Gaston made me a smiley sticking out its tongue!
textes.Gaston m'a trouvé, pas l'inverse. Il est: Gaston found me, not the other way round. He came down from a tree and said “Shipwreck”. He was the first to speak to me here.
textes.Gaston ne porte pas de bijoux. … Il est: Gaston doesn't wear jewellery. … What colour is it?
textes.Gaston veut savoir : tu le trouves beau: Gaston wants to know: do you think he's handsome?
textes.Gaston, cache les coquillages, il revien: Gaston, hide the seashells, here comes trouble again!
textes.Gaston, note : Octave m'a parlé. Huit mo: Gaston, write this down: Octave spoke to me. Eight words more than last year.
textes.Gaston, on m'offre {dernier_cadeau}. Oui: Gaston, someone's giving me {dernier_cadeau}. Yes. Don't laugh.
textes.Gaston, tu as vu ? Il m'a frappé ! Note-: Gaston, did you see that? I've been hit! Write it down!
textes.Gaston, tu entends ? Une elfe qui se sou: Gaston, did you hear that? An elf who remembers me!
textes.Germaine, Père Gaubert m'envoie, pour le: Germaine, Père Gaubert sent me, about the little pig.
textes.Gertrude va très bien. Elle te dit bonjo: Gertrude is very well. She says hello.
textes.Gilwen ! Ton miel de ce mois-ci, il est: Gilwen! This month's honey is a bit pale, isn't it?
textes.Gilwen ! Ton miel de tilleul arrive à po: Gilwen! Your lime-blossom honey's arrived just in time.
textes.Gilwen dit que je vole les fleurs de ses: Gilwen says I steal her bees' flowers. Flowers belong to no one. Her bees, on the other hand, follow me everywhere to take back their loot.
textes.Gilwen dit que je vole ses abeilles. Les: Gilwen says I steal her bees. The bees up top belong to nobody. She says I don't greet them with a song. I don't sing. Everyone knows why.
textes.Gilwen m'a appris que les abeilles n'aim: Gilwen taught me that bees don't like people in a hurry. One morning I ran over to her hives to ask for honey urgently, and three bees stung me on the nose. Gilwen said: “They could tell you hadn't said hello.” Ever since, I say hello to them. Even from a distance.
textes.Gilwen m'a dit : « Si tu leur chantais q: Gilwen told me: “If you sang them something before taking the honey, they wouldn't sting you.” I tried. Once. They stung me twice as much. Gilwen said it wasn't about singing, it was about singing in tune. I don't talk to her about songs any more.
textes.Gilwen m'apporte son miel tous les matin: Gilwen brings me her honey every morning, humming. Her bees adore her, and so do I. Without her, my bread would just be bread. With her, it's sunshine.
textes.Gilwen me fournit le miel des potions. E: Gilwen supplies the honey for my potions. She talks to her bees more than to elves, and they answer her better. She thinks I haggle too much. It's true.
Gilwen. I'm going up for the honey.
textes.Gilwen. Tes abeilles sont encore sur mes: Gilwen. Your bees are on my roses again.
textes.Gisèle avait dix ans quand elle m'a appr: Gisèle was ten when she taught me to carry a tray. She still talks to me like an apprentice. She's the best boss on the island.
textes.Gisèle me garde les nouvelles du matin c: Gisèle saves me the morning news the way others save a croissant. Who argued, who arrived on the Swallow, who lost their jack. She serves it to me with the dish of the day. I pretend not to listen. She pretends not to notice.
textes.Gisèle me garde ma table depuis des anné: Gisèle has kept my table for me for years, the only one with a view of the whole harbour. She serves me without my ordering. She's the most efficient person in Port-Azur, after me.
textes.Gisèle sait tout sur tout le monde et ne: Gisèle knows everything about everyone and says almost nothing. Almost. She's the only one I'd trust with my till.
textes.Gisèle, je l'ai connue en socquettes, so: I knew Gisèle when she was in ankle socks, under her mother's table. Now she runs the café, and she knows everything about me just from the way I sit down. It's annoying, a woman who guesses.
textes.Gland ! Le seul petit qui ne s'endort ja: Gland! The only little one who never falls asleep before the end. It's a tragedy. A wonderful little tragedy, with a bushy tail.
textes.Gland a perdu trois cents noisettes. Enf: Gland lost three hundred hazelnuts. Well, two hundred and ninety-nine. I help him look. One day I found one! It was in one of Mummy's mooncakes. Inside! How it got there, nobody knows. I ate it with the cake. Gland shouted. Mummy shouted. I said it was a new cake, hazelnut flavour.
textes.Gland dit qu'il y a un dragon sous la gr: Gland says there's a dragon under the big pond. Myrtille says it's the Pond King, with a crown. I say a dragon-fish, because it's both, it's logical. Hulotte can see in the dark: he saw cake on my snout! And Roux's phoenix feather, I bought it, for a mooncake. I wear it in my hair. Look!
Gland says there's a dragon under the great pool. Myrtille says it's a big fish. I say it's a dragon-fish.
textes.Gland fait une alerte tous les jours ave: Gland does an alert every day with Croc-Gris's zip line. “Alert! Alert!” So I tell Pomme-de-Pin, and she tells him off. He says I'm a telltale. I say I'm a guard, like Croc-Gris. He says guards don't have floppy ears. That's surely not true.
textes.Gland m'a appris à grimper, au pied du C: Gland taught me to climb, at the foot of the Mother Oak. He said: “Easy! One paw, then the other paw!” I got up onto the first branch. And I stayed sitting on it. All afternoon. Gland went up and down to the top to show me. I watched. Rabbits don't climb. They run.
textes.Gland, c'est un frimeur. Il grimpe vite,: Gland is a show-off. He climbs fast, fine, but he's a squirrel, that's cheating! And he keeps telling me I'm amazing. That's fishy.
textes.Gland, il parle trop et il dit n'importe: Gland talks too much and says silly things: he says it's a dragon. It's a dragon-fish! But he's funny. And I help him look for his hazelnuts. A bit.
textes.Gland, mon petit frère, a caché trois ce: Gland, my little brother, hid three hundred hazelnuts somewhere in the Mother Oak. He doesn't remember where. Neither do I. The tree might.
textes.Gland. Il saute sur le ponton, il parle: Gland. He jumps on the jetty, he talks about dragons, he scares off everything that swims. … But he comes back every day. That's patience too.
textes.Gland. Une alerte par jour. Fausse, chaq: Gland. One alarm a day. False, every time. Noisy. Cheeky. He says I've got the best house in the village. … He's not wrong.
textes.Glaucos ! Encore une lanterne sur le can: Glaucos! Another lantern on the canal tonight.
textes.Glaucos ! Tu as vu ? Encore une lanterne: Glaucos! Did you see? Another lantern on the canal!
textes.Glaucos souffle la nacre comme personne: Glaucos blows mother-of-pearl like nobody else and talks like an oyster: mouth shut. He crosses my bridge every evening. For the light, he says.
Glaucos was my apprentice, the best one. Then he started blowing mother-of-pearl like a soap bubble. Puffed-up mother-of-pearl! He calls it art. I call it hot air.
textes.Glaucos. Il souffle les vasques de nacre: Glaucos. He blows the mother-of-pearl basins my corals live in. He speaks softly. I like that.
Glitch says it's a bad idea. But it's almost free…
textes.Glitch, c'était toi, dans l'écran ?: Glitch, was that you, in the screen?
textes.Glorb ! Voici tes holo-photos des quatre: Glorb! Here are your holo-photos from the four corners of the archipelago.
textes.Glorb, le touriste de la planète Gloop,: Glorb, the tourist from the planet Gloop, would like to send his mum photos from the four corners of the archipelago. But he's green and wobbly, and he's afraid of scaring the people down below. He gives you his holo-photo: you need to photograph the mayor of Port-Azur, Mama Grog in Balafre, the Baron of Montjoie and Mamie Barricade in the Boucan, then bring the camera back to him.
textes.Glorb, pourquoi tu photographies tout ?: Glorb, why do you photograph everything?
textes.Glou, glou. L'eau a un goût de… rien du: Glug, glug. The water tastes of… absolutely nothing. Optimised. It still feels good (one more heart).
textes.Gné ?… Si c'est le facteur, posez ça sur: Hmm?… If it's the mailman, put it on the table… zzz…
textes.Gontran Lestrange, dit Jambe-de-Bois, le: Gontran Lestrange, known as Jambe-de-Bois, captain of the Veuve Écarlate, has owed Mama Grog forty coins for three moons. She wants his purse.
textes.Good morning, madame Margaux ! Six, comm: Good morning, Madame Margaux! Six, as always.
textes.Gorgoth baisse les cornes… et charge !: Gorgoth lowers his horns… and charges!
textes.Gorgée d'eau, avec une algue en prime. Q: Soaked through, with a bonus piece of seaweed. Somebody, somewhere, has a cold foot.
textes.Goûter la sauce du volcan avec la louche: Taste the volcano's sauce with the giant ladle
textes.Goûter le néo-ramen du robot du Marché d: Taste the robot's neo-ramen at the Night Market
textes.Goûter le thé stellaire de Gloubi (au Ca: Taste Gloubi's star tea (at the Nebula Café, west of the Agora of Stars)
textes.Goûter un maquereau grillé, là-haut, sur: To taste a grilled mackerel, up there, on a beach, with the sun on my back. Grandmother talked about it like a treasure. And never see another cracker again. Well, sell a few more, all the same.
textes.Grand-Bec : il vole. Il tourne, il tourn: Big-Beak: he fly. He circle, circle, then dive at you. You duck… no, you roll! When he go back up, he slow: hit!
textes.Grand-Mère Aquarelle est devant la Palet: Grandma Watercolour is in front of the Palette, Gaspard at the Lookout.
textes.Grand-Mère Aquarelle, l'île a retrouvé t: Grandmother Watercolour, the island has all its colours back!
textes.Grand-Mère Aquarelle, le brun est revenu: Grandmother Watercolour, the brown has returned to the clearing!
textes.Grand-Mère Aquarelle, pourquoi l'île est: Grand-Mère Aquarelle, why is the island all grey?
textes.Grand-oncle, je vous lis la rune du nord: Great-uncle, shall I read you the north rune?
textes.Grand-père Tilleul raconte les meilleure: Grandpa Tilleul tells the best stories in the world. The others fall asleep before the end. Not me! But he never finishes. Weird, huh?
textes.Grand-père Ébène raconte que Cerbère, le: Grandpa Ébène says that Cerberus, the three-headed dog of the Nine Circles, can't resist honey cakes: one per head. Bobor, the baker, is happy to bake three… if he has honey.
Scratch behind the ear. No, the other one. THERE.
textes.Gravé sur une poutre : « Le trésor de Pa: Carved on a beam: “Grandpa's treasure: to share with whoever finds it. Except the chocolate coins: those are for me.”
textes.Grelot reçoit des cartes de sa tante Sés: Grelot gets postcards from her aunt Sésame, from impossible places. I bring them to her at the market. She reads them laughing. She laughs a lot. Sometimes a little too loudly.
textes.Grelot se moque de mes carottes. Tous le: Grelot makes fun of my carrots. Every day. I say her apples weigh you down. We don't get on. And I never eat her pies any more. Never.
textes.Grelot vend ses pommes contre des pièces: Grelot sells her apples for coins. Coins! A tanuki! My niece is an embarrassment. But her apples are good.
textes.Grelot, c'est la marchande de fruits. Je: Grelot is the fruit seller. I bring her wild honey from up top, she pays me in coins. I don't know what to do with coins, so I worked it out: I hang them under my bridges!
textes.Grelot, c'est ma meilleure amie. Elle pa: Grelot is my best friend. She talks for two, laughs for three, and saves me the best apples. She teases me far too much. I adore her anyway.
textes.Grelot, dépêche-toi, les tambours commen: Grelot, hurry up, the drums are starting!
textes.Grimli ! Tu as encore dormi dans la mine: Grimli! Did you sleep in the mine again?
textes.Grimli a encore perdu une galerie. Perdu: Grimli has lost a tunnel again. Lost. A tunnel. That takes some doing.
textes.Grimli dort dans sa mine. Il dit que c'e: Grimli sleeps in his mine. He says it's quieter. Mostly it's because his wife snores.
textes.Grimli est le seul nain qui soit jamais: Grimli is the only dwarf who has ever got into my place without using the door. Through the floor. That doesn't count. But I don't forget.
textes.Grimli est venu me dire qu'il avait ente: Grimli came to tell me he'd heard a heart beating deep in a tunnel. He drew the way on a slate. I recognised the old signs of the descent to the Heart of the Mountain. I asked him to forget that path. Then I wiped the slate. He didn't notice. He'd already forgotten.
textes.Grimli oublie ses galeries, mais la mont: Grimli forgets his tunnels, but the mountain remembers him. He hears things I can only read. It's a gift. He thinks it's absent-mindedness.
textes.Grimli perd ses galeries, ses pioches et: Grimli loses his tunnels, his pickaxes and his socks, but never his good mood. He's got a fine beard. Not the finest. The finest is mine.
textes.Grimli perd tout, sauf son sourire. Il d: Grimli loses everything except his smile. He sleeps in his mine and says it's because of my snoring. I snore, fine. But not THAT much.
textes.Grimli trouve des rubis superbes et ne s: Grimli finds superb rubies and never knows where. A miner who doesn't know where he's digging is a thief who doesn't know it. Or a genius. I haven't decided yet.
textes.Grimli trouve du minerai partout et ses: Grimli finds ore everywhere and his tunnels nowhere. His beard got singed a hundred years ago, and he claims it grew back finer than mine. Ha.
textes.Grimli. Tu as perdu quoi, aujourd'hui ?: Grimli. What have you lost today?
textes.Grimli. Tu as retrouvé ta galerie ?: Grimli. Did you find your tunnel?
textes.Grimper au Belvédère des Couleurs, en ha: Climb to the Lookout of Colours, at the top of the Great Oak
textes.Grimper au sommet des Crocs (les colline: Climb to the top of the Fangs (the rocky hills in the south-west, above the dungeon entrance) and pick up three storm crystals
textes.Grisou dit qu'il va battre Bondi cette f: Grisou says he'll beat Bondi this time. He says it every time. Éclair says nothing. She's the one to watch.
textes.Grisou dit qu'il va battre Bondi. Il le: Grisou says he's going to beat Bondi. He says it every time! I love it. A fellow who's never won and still believes, that reminds me of someone.
textes.Grisou m'a demandé une Grande Course qui: Grisou asked me for a Great Race that goes all the way round the island, because a wolf is all about stamina. I got out the stopwatch, I counted the arches it would take, the nights, the snack breaks… Three weeks, {surnom}. Three weeks of racing! He said: “Perfect.” I put the stopwatch away very quickly.
Grisou talks a lot. He runs less.
textes.Grisou, c'est mon rival. Trois fois deux: Grisou is my rival. Three times second behind me. Nice, chatty, not really dangerous. Well… a wolf never gives up. I keep an eye on him. He keeps one on me too, from the lookout post.
textes.Grisou. Il vient chaque soir à l'heure d: Grisou. Comes every evening at closing time. He talks. He talks. He talks some more. Exhausting. Hm. He carries the coal, at least.
textes.Grmbl… Bon. Pour toi. Mais tu ne le dis: Grmbl… Fine. For you. But you tell nobody.
textes.Grognon. Un requin m'a volé mon outil pr: Grumpy. A shark stole my favourite tool. It's been taunting me from the reef.
textes.Grok chasse. Grok rate. Grok chasse enco: Grok hunt. Grok miss. Grok hunt again.
textes.Grok chasseur. Grok connaît toutes les b: Grok hunter. Grok know every beast on island. You want know?
textes.Grommelot ! Tu veux être une grenouille,: Grommelot! Do you want to be a frog this morning?
textes.Grommelot ! Une énigme : qu'est-ce qui g: Grommelot! A riddle: what grumbles in the morning and…
textes.Grommelot ? Le lutin qui garde les racin: Grommelot? The goblin who guards the roots, down below. He chased me off with a broom and he still hasn't forgiven me for my hole. I like him anyway: he grumbles like a seed sprouting.
textes.Grommelot ? Mon cobaye préféré ! Il dit: Grommelot? My favourite guinea pig! He says he hates being a frog. I say he's never looked as happy as he does on a lily pad.
textes.Grommelot ? Un nœud de racine avec une b: Grommelot? A knot of root with a beard. He calls me a glitter-gnat and snatches my crystal shards from under my nose.
textes.Grommelot ? Une énigme que je n'ai pas f: Grommelot? A riddle I haven't finished solving. He grumbles, fine. But he sees far, further than any of us. I learnt that too late.
textes.Grommelot collectionne les éclats de cri: Grommelot collects crystal shards. He says they're for his fireplace. I think he finds them pretty.
textes.Grommelot dit qu'il collectionne les écl: Grommelot says he collects crystal shards for his fireplace. One evening I went past his window: he was sitting on the floor in front of the fire, watching the colours dance in his shards. He was smiling. Grommelot. Smiling. I told everyone, and he's never forgiven me.
Grommelot pretends to be mean. He growls, he grumbles… but he's the kindest in the whole kingdom. You mustn't tell him. He'd be offended.
Grommelot pretends to be mean. He gave me a blanket last winter. Grumbling.
textes.Grosse-Dent dort maintenant. Grosse-Dent: Grosse-Dent sleep now. Grosse-Dent snore. Grosse-Dent nice when sleep.
textes.Grosse-Dent est furieux : il va plus vit: Grosse-Dent is furious: he's faster now… and he's calling his raptor pals!
textes.Grosse-Dent s'est cogné la tête contre l: Grosse-Dent bumped his head on the rock! He's seeing stars: STRIKE HIM NOW!
textes.Grosse-Dent s'écroule… et se met à RONFL: Grosse-Dent collapses… and starts SNORING. He sleeps like a baby (an eight-ton baby). The Clan will talk about it for generations! Go back and see Ougha at the Camp.
textes.Grosse-Dent toujours là. Ougha entend so: Grosse-Dent still there. Ougha hear roar at night.
textes.Grouik ! Truffe a déterré une truffe ! I: Oink! Truffle dug up a truffle! He sets it at your feet, snout full of dirt.
textes.Grouik ! Ça veut dire « je suis content: Oink! That means “I'm happy”. Oink oink means “very”.
textes.Grouik grouik ! Truffe arrive au petit t: Oink oink! Truffle arrives at a little trot, ears flopping.
textes.Grrrrinc… Deuxième vanne. Les jets de ce: Grrrrinc… Second valve. The jets in this corridor switch off; the gauge reads “MEDIUM”. One more!
textes.Grrrrinc… PFFFFSSSHHH ! Toute la chauffe: Grrrrinc… PFFFFSSSHHH! The whole boiler room lets out a long sigh of relief. The gauge falls to “SLIPPERS” (that's the minimum).
textes.Grrrrinc… Tu tournes le gros volant roug: Grrrrinc… You turn the big red wheel. The pipes sigh, and the jets in this corridor fall silent. The pressure gauge, near the door, drops a notch: “HIGH”.
textes.Grrr… Les loups du Guet vont entendre pa: Grrr… The wolves of the Watchtower will hear about you.
Grrr… It smells of bolts around here.
textes.Grâce à ma bière, qui fait passer ta cui: Thanks to my fizz, which washes your cooking down!
textes.Grâce à ma cuisine, Ulfa. Pas à ta bière: Thanks to my cooking, Ulfa. Not your fizz.
textes.Grâce à tes bâtons, j'ai de quoi travail: Thanks to your sticks, I've got enough work for the whole winter. Well, there's no winter here. The whole year, then.
textes.Grâce à tes champignons, j'ai soigné la: Thanks to your mushrooms, I cured half the village's cough. Faelar included. He says it's the first time in three centuries.
textes.Grâce à tes champignons, même Bramm a so: Thanks to your mushrooms, even Bramm smiled. For half a second. I counted.
textes.Grâce à tes cœurs de magma, ma galerie e: Thanks to your magma hearts, my tunnel is lit up like a party hall. I found my silver vein again. And two pickaxes. And a dwarf.
textes.Grâce à toi, Orsik ! Un roi n'oublie pas: Thanks to you, Orsik! A king never forgets.
textes.Grâce à toi, j'ai changé Grommelot en gr: Thanks to you, I turned Grommelot into a frog this morning. Five minutes. He loved it. He says he didn't.
textes.Grâce à toi, le Grand Cristal brille de: Thanks to you, the Great Crystal shines over Atlantis once again.
Thanks to you, my collection is complete. Well, until I find a bigger one to complete.
textes.Grégoire a les meilleurs yeux de Carène: Grégoire has the best eyes in Carène and the worst temper. He holds a grudge over one tiny question mark. But when he says he's seen something, I write it down. Almost in ink.
textes.Grégoire a servi ma mère, puis moi. Il n: Grégoire served my mother, then me. He never says anything he hasn't seen. So when he says he saw a light in Stoneheart, I don't sleep all night.
Grégoire counts the passing ships. None ever pass. But his lantern, at night, is what brings me home. I tease him, he sulks. That's how we like each other.
textes.Grégoire jure qu'il a vu de la lumière d: Grégoire swears he's seen light in Stoneheart at night. Grégoire has good eyes. That's exactly what worries me.
textes.Grégoire m'a prêté son carnet de guetteu: Grégoire lent me his lookout's journal: forty years of notes, winds, whales, storms, ships. I found a line in it from twenty years ago: “Light on Stoneheart, one second. Probably nothing.” His first light. He'd forgotten it. I haven't told him yet.
textes.Grégoire, là-haut dans sa hune, compte l: Grégoire, up in his crow's nest, counts the ships going by. None ever go by. He counts anyway.
textes.Grésille ? Elle ne grésille même plus !: Crackling? It doesn't even crackle anymore! It does... nothing! Pschhh... nothing at all! The storm ripped my antenna off the Rusty Whale's mast. I saw it fly off like a scrap-metal seagull, over the town, and land at the very top of the painted water tower, in the east. Twenty-eight metres! Fusible gets dizzy on the second rung, Boulon is too heavy for the ladder, and me... I'm a radio host, not a mountaineer. Would you go fetch it? I'll do a special show for you. Four hours long. All about you.
textes.Gunnar ! Ton bouclier brille trop. Je va: Gunnar! Your shield's too shiny. I'm going to blacken it.
textes.Gunnar garde ma halle, mon trône et ma d: Gunnar guards my hall, my throne and my dignity. He's the one who tells me, very quietly, that my crown is on my head. Nobody does it with such tact.
textes.Gunnar garde un tapis rouge, un trône et: Gunnar guards a red carpet, a throne and a king who loses his crown while it's on his head. He calls that a job. He smiles too much for a guard.
textes.Gunnar monte de la halle tous les soirs: Gunnar comes up from the hall every evening to drink a mug. The same mug, for three years now. He thinks I don't see him topping it up with water. He's sweet. He's a goof. He's sweet.
textes.Gwenola ! Un maquereau pour toi, le plus: Gwenola! A mackerel for you, the finest one.
textes.Gwenola ? La meilleure galette de la côt: Gwenola? The best crêpes on the coast and the hardest head in Carène. She teases me because I talk to fish. She knows full well why I talk to them.
textes.Gwenola compte mes grogs avec des harico: Gwenola counts my hot honeys with dried beans: one bean in her left pocket per mug served. After the third, it's herbal tea. One evening, while she was laughing, I slipped some beans into her right pocket. She checked the wrong pocket and served me five. The next day she'd sewn the right pocket shut.
textes.Gwenola m'a fait venir une nuit pour rép: Gwenola called me in one night to fix her stove hinge without letting the fire drop. “Not by one degree, Jos.” I worked till dawn, my beard sizzling. In the morning, she laid her hand on the door, said “good”, and served me the biggest breakfast of my life: four crêpes, two mugs and a smile.
textes.Gwenola me met une galette dans la poche: Gwenola has slipped a pancake into my pocket every morning for thirty years. I never asked her for anything. I've never really said thank you. She knows. At the Bordée, they know everything.
textes.Gwenola, c'est le poêle qui ne s'éteint: Gwenola is the stove that never goes out and the hand that never serves me more than three hot honeys. Without her, my stories wouldn't have a chair.
textes.Gwenola, il y a la capitainerie, les com: Gwenola, there's the harbour office, the accounts, the hull…
textes.Gwenola, je n'ai vraiment pas le temps a: Gwenola, I really don't have time today.
textes.Gwenola, ma belle, un petit grog pour la: Gwenola, my lovely, a little hot honey for the throat?
textes.Gâchette : boire un verre d'eau: Trigger: drink a glass of water
textes.Gâchette : consulter le Tableau des Quêt: Trigger: look at the Quest Board
textes.Gâchette : danser autour de l'arbre à ru: Trigger: dance around the ribbon tree
textes.Gâchette : descendre dans le Donjon des: Trigger: go down into the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps
textes.Gâchette : descendre dans les Neuf Cercl: Trigger: descend into the Nine Circles
textes.Gâchette : déplier l'Alouette et s'élanc: Trigger: unfold the Alouette and take off
textes.Gâchette : les lucioles du bassin: Trigger: the fireflies in the pool
textes.Gâchette : ouvrir avec une petite clé: Trigger: open with a small key
textes.Gâchette : plonger la main dans l'eau: Trigger: dip your hand in the water
textes.Gâchette : poser la main sur l'autel: Trigger: lay your hand on the altar
textes.Gâchette : poser le Plat sur l'autel: Trigger: place the Dish on the altar
textes.Gâchette : redescendre à la bouée: Trigger: go back down to the buoy
textes.Gâchette : regarder la Palette de pierre: Trigger: look at the Stone Palette
textes.Gâchette : remonter à la surface: Trigger: go back up to the surface
textes.Gâchette : rendre ses yeux au Grand Moaï: Trigger: give the Great Moai his eyes back
textes.Gâchette : rentrer sur la plage: Trigger: go back to the beach
textes.Gâchette : renvoyer votre compagnon se r: Trigger: send your companion to rest
textes.Gâchette : s'accrocher à la tyrolienne: Trigger: hang on to the zip line
textes.Gâchette : verser les pots dans la Palet: Trigger: pour the pots into the Palette
textes.Gâchette droite : descendre l'échelle: Right trigger: climb down the ladder
textes.Gédéon joue ! Et il joue JUSTE !: Gédéon plays! And he plays IN TUNE!
textes.Gédéon respire un grand coup, traverse l: Gédéon takes a deep breath, crosses the pit (the crowd parts, intrigued), climbs onto the stage, takes the stand-in's place, and twirls his drumsticks. A drumroll. The Howling Hall falls silent. Then it HOWLS.
textes.Gédéon, le fils de Monsieur Lisse, tapot: Gédéon, Mr Lisse's son, taps out rhythms on everything he touches. Every evening, he listens to the Bilge Rats from behind the door of the Howling Hall. He's a brilliant drummer, but he has neither drumsticks nor courage. As for the drumsticks, you've kept them since the Great Boucan

Gédéon, Mr Lisse's son, taps out rhythms on everything he touches. Every evening, he listens to the Bilge Rats from behind the door of the Howling Hall. He's a brilliant drummer, but he has neither drumsticks nor courage. As for the drumsticks, you've kept them since the Great Boucan…
textes.Gédéon, pourquoi vous tapotez toujours ?: Gédéon, why are you always tapping?
textes.Génial ! Tiens, trois noix de coco. Non,: Brilliant! Here, three coconuts. No, two. We start with two. If you drop one, you take a bow: that's the clown's rule.
textes.Génial… Bien, bien. Tu as du courage, to: Brilliant… Good, good. You're brave, you are. Me, just looking at the Swallow makes my knees go all wavy.
textes.Gérard ! Ta table t'attend. Bouillabaiss: Gérard! Your table is waiting. Bouillabaisse?
textes.Gérard Dupuis a oublié son appareil phot: Gérard Dupuis left his camera at the lookout, at the top of the hill.
textes.Gérard photographie plus qu'il ne regard: Gérard photographs more than he looks. But when he really looks, he's the gentlest man in the world. He just ought to lose his camera more often.
textes.Gérard photographie tout et ne regarde r: Gérard photographs everything and looks at nothing. He's nice, he's funny, and he gets on my nerves. A photo steals a landscape; I keep telling him so.
Gérard wanted to photograph my pot. Never! Because of the secret. I hid it under a tea towel and stood in front of it, arms spread wide. He photographed the tea towel. He says it's his best photo. It's blurry.
textes.Gérard, c'est mon client de midi. Bouill: Gérard is my lunchtime regular. Bouillabaisse every day, twice if he dares. A man who eats like that, I'd adopt him if he didn't already have a family.
textes.Gérard, chéri. Tu regardes le coucher de: Gérard, darling. Are you watching the sunset, or looking for it in your pocket?
textes.Gérard, mon touriste préféré. Toujours d: Gérard, my favourite tourist. Always in a good mood, always a camera round his neck — when he hasn't left it somewhere. He did an hour of pedalo in circles. A champion, in his own way.
