textes.HA ! Tu as l'œil, le grand ! Tiens : le: HA! You've got a good eye, big fella! Here: my mother's stew. We only give it to beard connoisseurs.
textes.HA HA ! C'est mon chef-d'œuvre ! Je l'ap: HA HA! It's my masterpiece! I'll call it “The Visitor Who Ate a Lemon.”
textes.HA HA HA ! Tu as remarqué ! On fait ce c: HA HA HA! You noticed! We've been holding this contest for a thousand years, and it's a tie every time. Here, you have a good eye: a seashell medal!
textes.HALTE ! Qui va l… Un humain ?! Un vrai ?: HALT! Who goes th… A human?! A real one?! Three hundred years I've guarded this gate, and nobody has ever come! Welcome to Atlantis! Er… I mean: welcome. Please remain calm.
textes.HO HO ! Par le marteau d'Ancêtre-Pierre: HO HO! By the hammer of Ancestor-Stone! I tried that in my second year. Ulfa shut the Mug for three days. Three days without fizz in the whole kingdom. But the intention was royal.
textes.HO HO ! Par le marteau d'Ancêtre-Pierre,: HO HO! By the hammer of Ancestor-Stone, there's a big'un who talks sense! A blade should weigh like an oath. Otherwise, it's a spoon.
textes.Ha ! Alors je préfère notre cristal. Il: Ha! Then I prefer our crystal. It burns nobody.
textes.Ha ! Alors, on part quand ?: Ha! So, when do we leave?
textes.Ha ! Amirale ! Toujours à commander un b: Ha! Admiral! Still commanding a ship that doesn't move?
textes.Ha ! Apporte-la, je la redresse. Sans qu: Ha! Bring it over, I'll straighten it. No questions.
textes.Ha ! Assieds-toi plus près, toi. Une bel: Ha! Sit closer, you. A beautiful story is a truth that dressed up nicely to go out. As we say on board.
textes.Ha ! Celle-là, je la mets dans mon spect: Ha! That one's going in my show. The kids won't get it, but the parents will. The best audience is when everyone laughs for different reasons.
textes.Ha ! Comme Grisou ! Bon, ça marche, mais: Ha! Like Grisou! Well, it works, but you miss the music. The stones sing for those who take their time!
textes.Ha ! De la fontaine de la place jusqu'à: Ha! From the fountain in the square to the lighthouse door, in under sixty seconds. The clock starts when you pass near the fountain. Ready?
textes.Ha ! Enfin quelqu'un de raisonnable ! To: Ha! Finally someone sensible! High five. But don't say it too loud near the Swap Market: my uncle has sharp ears. And a fragile heart.
textes.Ha ! Enfin quelqu'un qui a des yeux ! Ré: Ha! Finally someone with eyes! Say it louder, Raymond is deaf in his left ear. The one that hears the truth.
textes.Ha ! Enfin quelqu'un qui le voit ! Je co: Ha! Finally someone who sees it! I was starting to wonder.
textes.Ha ! Faux, j'espère ? Ici on chante faux: Ha! Off-key, I hope? Here we sing off-key, or the king takes offence. He sings so off-key the barrels crack. You'll fit right in!
textes.Ha ! Je tape moins fort. Pour toi. Un pe: Ha! I'll bang softer. For you. A bit.
textes.Ha ! La meilleure réponse que j'aie ente: Ha! Best answer I've heard in twenty years. Welcome.
textes.Ha ! Le plus honnête de tous. Tout le mo: Ha! The most honest of all. Everyone's like that, you know. Even Professor Moreau makes his bed when he knows I'm coming. To hide his drawings in it.
textes.Ha ! Le revoilà ! Approche, approche, le: Ha! Here he is again! Come closer, come closer, the iron's hot.
textes.Ha ! Non, elle repousse. C'était un trou: Ha! No, that grows back. It was a hole. Ask me for your prize, you made me laugh.
textes.Ha ! Non. Et la prochaine fois que tu ma: Ha! No. And next time you haggle, it costs more.
textes.Ha ! Toi aussi ? Bienvenue au club de Br: Ha! You too? Welcome to Bramm's club. That makes two of you. He never smiles; you, at least, try.
textes.Ha ! Toi aussi ? … Ha. … Moi aussi. Chut: Ha! You too? … Ha. … Me too. Shh. We won't talk about it any more, OK? We'll pretend we're joking.
textes.Ha ! Toi, au moins, tu as des yeux. Quar: Ha! At least you've got eyes. Forty-one verses, and not a single word face to face. I could wait a thousand years. … I may have to help him along a little.
textes.Ha ! Tu me rendras la moitié, comme d'ha: Ha! You'll give me half back, as usual.
textes.Ha ! Un frère de bord ! Et elles te répo: Ha! A shipmate! And do they answer you? No? Mine neither. Hardly ever. Keep at it, it's a matter of patience.
textes.Ha ! Un vrai ! Enfin un adversaire ! Les: Ha! A real one! An opponent at last! Folks in Carène pay the marked price, it's so boring… Come to the stall, we'll have some fun.
textes.Ha ! Une personne raisonnable ! J'en voi: Ha! A reasonable person! I see so few. If one of my maps ever sends you into a swamp, come back and tell me. It happens. Rarely. Twice.
textes.Ha ! Voilà quelqu'un de bien. Une lame q: Ha! Now there's a decent sort. A blade with a name gets looked after, sharpened, talked to. My ancestor talked to his cannons. Me, to my anvil.
Ha! Now that's a dwarf's answer.
Ha ha! Well played, you too.
textes.Ha ha ! Bonne journée !: Ha ha! Have a nice day!
textes.Ha ha ! Elle est bonne !: Ha ha! That's a good one!
textes.Ha ha ! Il ne connaît qu'une danse : la: Ha ha! He knows only one dance: the screwdriver waltz. But he dances it with heart. Well, with a piston.
textes.Ha ha ! La machine a parlé ! Elle a dit: Ha ha! The machine has spoken! It said “BOOM,” but it spoke! Keep this little souvenir.
textes.Ha ha ! Tu parles comme Faelar. Il a déj: Ha ha! You sound like Faelar. He once slept three years straight, you know. He says it's the best way not to age too fast.
textes.Ha ha ! Tu vois, mon trésor, les humains: Ha ha! See, my treasure, humans make faces too! They're just like us… only paler.
textes.Ha ha ! Un Pied-Lourd qui aime flotter !: Ha ha! A Heavyfoot who likes floating! You're almost a Lumen. Come back anytime, gravity is overrated.
textes.Ha ha ! À la prochaine !: Ha ha! See you next time!
textes.Ha ha ha ! Grommelot ne chante JAMAIS. M: Ha ha ha! Grommelot NEVER sings. But I like the idea. It was the river.
textes.Ha. Celle-là, je l'entends chaque semain: Ha. I hear that one every week, usually just before someone gets carried in to me on a plank. Keep a jar of seaweed salve in your bag anyway.
textes.Haches, pelles, clous pour les ponts de: Axes, shovels, nails for Pomme-de-Pin's bridges. Bells for the lanterns. Myrtille's, Mochi's and Gland's little bells hang on the Mother Oak: on Mochi's, I engraved a little moon. My father sits on his stool and tells the customers stories. I hammer. In the evening, Grisou comes to talk. A lot. I close anyway.
textes.Haldir ! Tu as un message pour moi ?: Haldir! Have you got a message for me?
textes.Haldir ! Une lettre pour Fil-d'Aube. Cou: Haldir! A letter for Fil-d'Aube. Run!
textes.Haldir court plus vite que tout le Bois-: Haldir runs faster than the whole Bois-Doré, except when he's coming towards me. He trod on my feet seventeen times at the last festival. I counted. I always count.
textes.Haldir est le meilleur messager du Bois-: Haldir is the best messenger in the Bois-Doré, and the most patient. He carries my letters to Ilyria. And he brings them back to me, when I catch up with him. I always catch up with him.
textes.Haldir passe devant ma tour dix fois par: Haldir runs past my tower ten times a day and never says where he's going. I ask. That's my job. He doesn't answer. That's his, apparently.
textes.Halo dit qu'il faut goûter votre thé ste: Halo says I should taste your stellar tea.
textes.Halo m'envoie m'inscrire au registre des: Halo sent me to sign the visitors' register.
textes.Halo, comment devient-on visiteur d'Astr: Halo, how does one become a visitor to Astralys?
textes.Halo, le gardien du Portail d'accueil, v: Halo, the keeper of the Welcome Gate, wants you to become an official visitor of Astralys, as tradition demands: get yourself entered in the register by Écliptique, taste the star tea at Gloubi's, then go and greet Elder Astrée.
textes.Halte ! Qui va là ? … Ah, ma recrue. Rep: Halt! Who goes there? … Ah, my recruit. At ease.
textes.Halte ! Qui va là ? … Oh, un visiteur. P: Halt! Who goes there? … Oh, a visitor. Sorry, force of habit. Want to see my armor?
textes.Halte ! Un grand. Sur NOTRE plage. Bramm: Halt! A tall one. On OUR beach. Bramm Poing-de-Roc, guard of the Great Gate. Nobody enters Forgefer uninvited.
Halt! … Ah, it's you. Go on through.
textes.Halte ! … Ah, c'est toi. Trois, quatre…: Halt! … Oh, it's you. Three, four…
textes.Halte. Tu es sur le pont du Léviathan, e: Halt. You're standing on the deck of the Léviathan, and this deck is our home. I am Morgane Kerhervé, admiral of Carène. Who sent you, and across which sea?
textes.Halte. Un humain… avec la boussole de Ly: Halt. A human… with Lyra's compass. Fine. Thalion Ventvif, guard of Bois-Doré. I've got my eye on you.
textes.Halte. Une question. Si tu voyais quelqu: Halt. A question. If you saw something strange in the forest, what would you do?
textes.Halte. … Bon, tu as l'air inoffensif. Cr: Halt. … All right, you look harmless. Croc-Gris, guard of the Watchtower. From up there, I can see the whole forest, and the whole forest knows I can see it. Welcome to Ramure. No mischief.
textes.Head: Head
textes.Hector ? Un grand qui a porté mon charbo: Hector? A big'un who carried my coal for three years without complaining. Well, complaining, but carrying it. He forges decently. For a big'un. Hmph.
textes.Hector est un bon artisan, je ne dis pas: Hector is a good craftsman, I won't say otherwise. But a blacksmith who “never has the time” for a clock is like a baker who's never hungry.
textes.Hector fabrique des choses qui font peur: Hector makes frightening things and sells them at frightening prices. I prefer jams. And my prices are fair.
textes.Hector me forge mes griffes de sertissag: Hector forges my setting prongs: tiny little steel claws, to hold a stone without hurting it. The first time, I looked at them through the loupe and asked him where he'd learned to work so fine. He grunted: “With the dwarves.” Then, lower: “For once, it wasn't for an axe.”
textes.Hector, c'est l'homme qui a forgé mon en: Hector is the man who forged my sign and has been drinking it for twenty years. He talks little, grunts well, and sings out of tune while hammering. A true friend. He'll never say so.
textes.Hector, l'armurier, fabrique des choses: Hector, the armourer, makes frightening things. I prefer jam.
textes.Hector. Vous avez levé les yeux, ce mati: Hector. Did you look up, this morning?
textes.Hein ? Quelle heure est-il ? … Zzz…: Huh? What time is it? … Zzz…
textes.Hein ? Quoi ? Un grand ! Pardon, je croy: Eh? What? A tall one! Sorry, I thought it was a rockfall. Grimli Pic-Rouillé, miner. The oldest miner in the oldest mine.
textes.Hein ? Tu l'entends aussi ? Boum… boum…: Eh? You hear it too? Boom… boom… Oh, no, you mean cave-ins. Yes. Me too. Especially the ones I cause myself.
textes.Hein ?! Quoi ? … Ah, c'est un rêve. Bonn: Huh?! What? … Ah, it's a dream. Good night, dream.
textes.Heureuse comme une jeune fille. Toutes l: Happy as a young girl. Every hour, the bell sings.
textes.Heureuse. La graine dort dans la terre d: Happy. The seed sleeps in the soil of the clearing. In a thousand years, a new Yggdrasil will watch over you.
textes.Heureuse. La lumière est revenue, les en: Happy. The light is back, the children play on the canal bridges. A queen asks for nothing more.
textes.Heyyy ! Bienvenue, frérot ! Ici, une seu: Heyyy! Welcome, bro! Only one rule here: we dance and we smile!
textes.Hi hi ! Tu veux que je me retransforme ?: Hee hee! Want me to turn back? No? Shame, I was a very beautiful teapot.
textes.Hi hi ! Ça, c'était la chanson du crapau: Hee hee! That was the song of the toad with a cold!
Yesterday! It hasn't moved an inch.
textes.Hier, c'était une sardine. Les sardines,: Yesterday it was a sardine. Sardines are dim.
textes.Hier, j'ai dit à Gunnar : « Ça fait troi: Yesterday, I said to Gunnar: “You've been drinking the same mug for three years.” He went red right up to his ears and talked to me about his shield for an hour. He has a very fine shield. I know: he's described it to me forty times. One day, I'll ask him why he comes. Not just yet.
textes.Hier, une araignée de cristal m'a fait p: Yesterday a crystal spider gave me a fright. I dropped everything! My drops rolled everywhere: into the Hall of Prisms, the garden, the cave… Would you bring me back {manque}? They shine, you'll see them.
textes.Hilda ! Cette année, c'est ma barbe qui: Hilda! This year, my beard wins.
textes.Hilda ! Ta chèvre noire est sur le toit: Hilda! Your black goat's on Borin's roof.
textes.Hilda ! Ton fromage a encore bougé cette: Hilda! Your cheese moved again last night!
textes.Hilda ! Un corbeau, vite. Un message urg: Hilda! A raven, quick. An urgent message.
textes.Hilda connaît chaque chèvre par son nom: Hilda knows every goat by name and every raven by its mood. We cross paths on the slopes every day. We tell each other everything. Well, almost everything.
textes.Hilda dit que c'est elle qui a la plus b: Hilda says she has the finest beard on the mountain. I can't argue: she's right, and her crows agree with her.
textes.Hilda fait le meilleur fromage du monde: Hilda makes the best cheese in the world and she talks to crows. The crows answer. I heard it. She says they don't, but I heard it.
textes.Hilda garde mes corbeaux messagers. Elle: Hilda keeps my messenger ravens. She says I make them fly too much. A king needs news. And cheese. Especially at night.
textes.Hilda laisse ses chèvres me grimper dess: Hilda lets her goats climb on me. She says they like rocks. I'm not a rock. Well… not only.
textes.Hilda parle à ses corbeaux. Et ses corbe: Hilda talks to her ravens. And her ravens answer her. I heard them!
textes.Hisser le panier de la poulie du Grand-C: Hoist the basket on the Great Oak's pulley
textes.Hisser le panier de la poulie, sur la pl: Hoist the pulley basket, on the Great Oak platform, next to the Council House (or look inside it, down at the foot of the tree)
textes.Historique ? Je l'ai fini mardi !: Historic? I finished it on Tuesday!
textes.Hi… hi hi… rrrrr… (Il rit en dormant. Pu: Hee… hee hee… rrrrr… (He laughs in his sleep. Then he snores even louder.)
textes.Hm ? Ah, c'est toi qu'on appelle le voya: Hm? Ah, so you're the one they call the traveler?
textes.Hm ? Ah, c'est toi, le voyageur ? Assied: Hm? Ah, it's you, the traveller? Sit down. Here, silence tastes of basil.
Hm? Ah. Sorry, I was watching the horizon. Grégoire, lookout. I watch the sea for Carène. And the land too, now. You never know where trouble will come from.
textes.Hm ? Oh, pardon. Lucien Moreau, archéolo: Hm? Oh, sorry. Lucien Moreau, archaeologist. Professor. On holiday, officially. Unofficially, I'm looking for Atlantis.
textes.Hm ? Oh, un visiteur. Hulotte, astronome: Hm? Oh, a visitor. Hulotte, astronomer. Every night I climb to the treetop and count the stars. I'm up to four thousand two hundred and twelve. Or thirteen. You've made me lose count.
textes.Hm hm. Tu es plus malin que mes petits-e: Hm hm. You're smarter than my grandchildren. … Look: they're all asleep. As usual. Go, traveler. And if you find the eyes… the Great Moai is waiting for you.
textes.Hm. Alors tu sais ce que c'est. On la re: Hm. Then you know what it's like. You look at it, you turn round to point it out, and it's gone. Don't let anyone tell you that you dreamed it.
Hm. In pencil, that's a start.
textes.Hm. Au moins vous l'avouez. Mon fiancé é: Hm. At least you admit it. My fiancé was always late too. He said the sea doesn't wear a watch. … Don't pull that face, I'm not scolding you. Not much.
textes.Hm. Bonne réponse. Le Roi, je l'attends: Hm. Good answer. The King, I've waited thirty years for. Dinner, not one minute. Shh, don't tell Caramel.
textes.Hm. Comme Ewen. Ça fait de bons capitain: Hm. Like Ewen. That makes good captains and bad cabin boys. In Carène, as long as you respect the ship, I ask nothing more of you.
Hm. Tomorrow, the part without arches.
textes.Hm. Elle est en fer. Sinon, elle rouille: Hm. It's iron. Otherwise it rusts.
textes.Hm. Hm, hm. (Il prend le pot, le regarde: Hm. Hm, hm. (He takes the pot and examines it through the spyglass, from very close up, which is no use at all.) I wasn't dreaming. Well. In spring, the mountain heather will be purple again. I'll be able to draw it in charcoal. It'll be grey on the paper, but I'll know. Here: my old compass. It points north. Almost.
Hm. Next time, I'll put it out.
textes.Hm. Note-la quand même. On ne sait jamai: Hm. Write it down anyway. You never know.
textes.Hm. On verra. Tes bottes disent que tu a: Hm. We'll see. Your boots say you went round the market twice this morning. But I believe you. Half.
textes.Hm. Pas glorieux. Mais vivant. Mieux vau: Hm. Not glorious. But alive. Better a live guard than a brave one. Don't tell Grisou.
textes.Hm. Peut-être. Ce matin, tout là-haut, a: Hm. Maybe. This morning, way up high, at the top of Mount Charcoal: a glint. Not a stone, not water. A pot. The purple one, I bet: number six, the heather's. But my legs don't climb the mountain anymore. First look through my spyglass, there, at the edge of the Lookout. If you see it too, then I'm not dreaming.
Hm. You get home before dark.
textes.Hm. Toi, {surnom}, tu peux savoir. J'ai: Hm. You, {surnom}, you can know. I'm scared of heights. Never crossed a rope bridge. Never. I forge all their nails, and I take the stairs. Half an hour. At dawn, Bourru takes me up in the basket. Without a word. I close my eyes. Pomme-de-Pin thinks I look down on her bridges. It's not that. It's not that at all.
textes.Hm. Toi. Tu as peur de quoi ?: Hm. You. What are you scared of?
textes.Hm. Ton épée. Tu la tiens à une main ou: Hm. Your sword. One hand or two?
textes.Hmm ? J'ai perdu le fil. Ça m'arrive. So: Hmm? I lost my train of thought. It happens. Often.
textes.Hmm ? Un visiteur… de la surface ? Atten: Hmm? A visitor… from the surface? Wait, let me find a quill. I must write this down. “Day 365,214: a human.”
Hmm. This one tastes like spring water.
textes.Hmm. La suite, il faut la mériter. Repas: Hmm. The rest has to be earned. Drop by again, we'll see.
Hmm. The rest has to be earned. Drop by again, we'll see.
textes.Hmm. Les coraux ont pâli. Pas les vasque: Hmm. The corals have paled. Not the basins.
Hmm. My grandmother used to say the same. Then she'd carve the path before anyone took it. Perhaps you're right. The stones hesitate when you walk by.
textes.Hmm. Tu comptes comment, cette fois ?: Hmm. And how are you counting this time?
textes.Hmm. Tu es bien indulgent. Attends un pe: Hmm. You're very forgiving. Just wait, you'll see.
textes.Hmm. Tu es de ceux qui vérifient. Comme: Hmm. You're one of those who check. Like Matthias: he writes my stories down in a journal and counts the whales. I like you anyway. A bit less, but I do.
textes.Hmm. Une loi de grand cœur. Sous la mont: Hmm. A law with a big heart. Under the mountain, everyone has a roof, but not always a place by the fire. I'll think about it. Royally. Ori, write that down.
textes.Hmm. Vous êtes bien indulgent. Attendez: Hmm. You're very forgiving. Just wait, you'll see.
textes.Hmm. Ça ne se forge pas, ça ne se boit p: Hmm. Can't forge it, can't drink it… but thanks.
Hmpf. And thank you. Write that down.
textes.Hmpf. Le grand. Toujours à taper fort et: Hmph. The big one. Still hitting hard and wrong?
textes.Hmpf. Toi. Tu marches sur des racines to: Hmph. You. You walk on roots all day long. Ever said thank you to them?
textes.Hmpf. Un humain. Trop grand, trop bruyan: Hmph. A human. Too tall, too loud, too… human. Grommelot, keeper of the roots. What do you want?
textes.Hmpf. Un rêve. … Que les racines tiennen: Hmph. A dream. … That the roots hold for another four hundred years. And that one day somebody says thank you. Not to me. To the roots. Fine. To me too, a bit.
textes.Hmpf. Une lame d'elfe, quoi. Bon. Léger,: Hmph. An elf blade, then. Fine. I can do light too. I don't like it, but I can do it. Don't tell Fundin, he'd want to try.
textes.Hmpf. Ça ne se pèse pas, ça. … Mais c'es: Hmpf. You can't weigh that. … But it's pretty. Don't repeat it, people will think I'm sentimental. I'm not. Not in public.
textes.Hmpf. … Bon. D'accord. Le tressage est r: Hmpf. … Fine. All right. The braiding is a success. A LITTLE.
textes.Hmpf. … C'était pourtant ma plus belle g: Hmph. … And that was my best grimace.
textes.Hnnnngh… La caisse ne bouge pas : quelqu: Hnnnngh… The crate won't budge: something is blocking it on the other side (or it's the edge of the storage area).
textes.Ho ! Un visiteur dans mon atelier ! Cora: Ho! A visitor in my workshop! Coralin, coral craftsman. I carve, I polish, I sculpt. Don't touch the red coral: it bites.
textes.Ho ho ! Le Grand Troc, c'est une chaîne,: Ho ho! The Great Swap is a chain, my friend. I give you this singing pebble: listen, when the wind passes through it, it whistles. You'll swap it for something better, then that something for something better still… Pomme-de-Pin, the carpenter, loves singing pebbles. Start with her. And at the end, come back and see me: I want to know what my pebble became!
textes.Ho ho ! Un vrai mineur ! Le noir, c'est: Ho ho! A real miner! The dark is just light that's sleeping. Come digging one day. You won't get lost. Well… less than me.
textes.Ho ho ! {dernier_cadeau} ! Tu as l'œil,: Ho ho! {dernier_cadeau}! You've got a good eye, for a tall one.
textes.Honnête. C'est ce que tout Carène fait,: Honest. That's what all of Carène does, with me. I don't mind. Bring me wood, that's all I ask.
textes.Honorine est seule au four ce matin. Il: Honorine is alone at the oven this morning. There are three loaves left to deliver: one to Mamie Rissole, at the Guild tavern; one to Aurore, at the castle; one to Gilles, at the North Gate. If she leaves the oven, everything burns.
textes.Hop ! Bondi. Champion de la Grande Cours: Hop! Bondi. Great Race champion, three years running. Want some advice? Don't follow me: all you'll see is my heels.
textes.Hop ! Dernier-né de la famille, quatorze: Hop! Youngest of the family, fourteen years after Trèfle. I grew up in the smell of bread, running round the oven. Still today, every morning, I help Mum and Dad in the rabbit vegetable garden, and I pick my three carrots. Not the biggest: the straightest. A straight carrot makes you run straight. It's science.
textes.Hop ! Dis-moi, toi : tu cours vite ?: Hop! Tell me, you: are you a fast runner?
textes.Hop ! Jusqu'à la boulangerie. Tu pars av: Hop! To the bakery. You start first.
textes.Hop ! Qu'il s'ennuie. Il est bien, là-ha: Hop! Let it be bored. It's happy up there.
textes.Hop ! Salut, Grisou. Deuxième, aujourd'h: Hop! Hi, Grisou. Second place today?
textes.Hop ! Trois. Mon record tient toujours,: Hop! Three. Does my record still stand, Pépin?
textes.Hop hop ! Encore toi ? Tu t'entraînes ?: Hop hop! You again? Training? Me too. All the time.
textes.Hop hop hop ! Bernard, soixante-sept ans: Hup hup hup! Bernard, sixty-seven years old, three laps of the island a day! What about you, do you run?
Hop hop hop! Sorry! Hop… hop.
textes.Hop hop hop ! Un coureur ! Demain, sept: Hop hop hop! A runner! Tomorrow, seven o'clock, at the fountain. I'll give you a ten-metre head start. Oh, all right, five.
textes.Hop hop hop… tout doucement. Bonne nuit: Hop hop hop… nice and quiet. Good night!
textes.Hortense ? La femme la plus fidèle de Po: Hortense? The most faithful woman in Port-Azur. I nod to her every evening from the quay. That's all I dare. I would so have liked to bring her something other than bad news.
textes.Hortense bat la mesure du pied, juste à: Hortense taps the beat with her foot, right to the second. She's my metronome, my first listener, and the only one who dares tell me I play too fast.
textes.Hortense dit que l'horloge de la mairie: Hortense says the town hall clock stopped the day her fiancé went to sea. It's sad and a little bit beautiful.
textes.Hortense est la femme la plus fidèle que: Hortense is the most faithful woman I know. She's been waiting for fifty years, and she oils her clock twice a day, whether it rings or not. I admire her. I don't know how she does it.
Hortense is the memory of our square. She also counts my promises, which is far less pleasant.
textes.Hortense est sûre que c'est moi qui pose: Hortense is sure I'm the one leaving a sprig of lavender on her bench every morning. I've sworn on my satchel, on Raymond's head, on my boules. She doesn't believe me. Now she “gives back” the lavender: every morning I find it in the middle of my pitch, right where I point. Raymond finds it hilarious. Me, I keep it.
textes.Hortense voudrait que je répare son horl: Hortense wants me to fix her clock. She needs a new cogwheel. If someone brought me something to heat the forge… logs, and a few stones for the mould.
textes.Hortense, la gardienne de l'horloge, est: Hortense, the clock keeper, is in despair: nobody on the square knows what time it is any more.
textes.Hortense, ma vieille amie. Trente ans, j: Hortense, my old friend. Thirty years I knocked on her door. She thinks I'm the one leaving her lavender. It isn't me. I wish it were.
textes.Hortense, ma voisine de palier. Elle ne: Hortense, my next-door neighbour. She doesn't believe in my nonsense and she tells everyone so. But she looks at every stranger who crosses the square. The cards and I are waiting with her.
textes.Hou ! Bonjour ! Plumette, postière de Ra: Hoo! Hello! Plumette, postmistress of Ramure. Mail for the trees, mail for the ponds, mail for the other towns. It all leaves from the top of the Mother Oak. Got a letter? No? Well, write one, then!
textes.Hou ! Dis-moi, toi : tu as quelqu'un à q: Hoo! Tell me: do you have someone to write to?
textes.Hou ! Enfin la nuit ! Je me sens toute n: Hoo! Night at last! I feel brand new.
textes.Hou ! J'attends toujours ta lettre, tu s: Hoo! I'm still waiting for your letter, you know. I've already written the reply. Just in case.
textes.Hou ! Je suis la fille de Hulotte. Mon p: Hoo! I'm Hulotte's daughter. My father carried Ramure's post for thirty years. When I was tiny, I travelled in his satchel, among the letters, with just my head poking out. I knew every door before I could read. People gave me a hazelnut when they took their post. I was a bit like the stamp.
textes.Hou ! Je t'entends arriver, Pomme-de-Pin: Hoo! I can hear you coming, Pomme-de-Pin.
Hoo! Not yet. She's slow to reply.
textes.Hou ! Rien pour toi aujourd'hui. Mais de: Hoo! Nothing for you today. But tomorrow, maybe.
textes.Hou ! Toi qui écris à plein de monde : t: Hoo! You who write to loads of people: not forgetting anyone? I never forget an address.
textes.Hou ! Tu as écrit à la personne qui te m: Hoo! Did you write to the person you miss? My satchel always has room.
textes.Hou ! Un gland d'or ! Je le mettrai sur: Hoo! A golden acorn! I'll put it on my counter, it'll bring luck to the post. Here's a moon feather: it falls from our wings on full-moon nights. Which is to say every night, here. Pivoine is looking for some for her vials.
textes.Hou… Alors écris-lui ! Je m'occupe du re: Hoo… Then write to them! I'll take care of the rest. I won't read a thing, promise. I'll just listen a little, if it goes tick-tock.
textes.Hou… Bonsoir, petite. On monte ?: Hoo… Good evening, little one. Shall we climb?
textes.Hou… Dis-moi : tu as déjà compté les éto: Hoo… Tell me: have you ever counted the stars?
Hoo… And every evening, that's true.
textes.Hou… Je suis né à la Poste, tout en haut: Hoo… I was born at the Post Office, right at the top of the Mother Oak. As a child, I didn't sleep: I counted the lanterns on the bridges. A hundred and seventeen, the evening I turned six. A hundred and eighteen the next day: Mother Moon had put up a new one. Then one evening I looked up a little higher. The stars. There were far more of them. I never looked down again.
textes.Hou… Regarde ma longue lunette, {surnom}: Hoo… Look at my long telescope, {surnom}. Come closer. Look into it. … See? Nothing. It's a tube of rolled bark. There's no glass. I've never looked through a real lens. Céleste sends me calculations, whole pages of them. I answer with poems, because I don't know how to do anything else. I'm a little ashamed of it. Very.
textes.Hou… Tu sais pourquoi je travaille le jo: Hoo… Do you know why I work by day, {surnom}? Not just for the post. When I was little, I'd wait for night at the treetop, so my father would look at me. But he looked at the sky. Always the sky. So now I leave the night to him, with his stars. I don't share. I've never told him. A postmistress says nothing. Nor does a daughter, sometimes.
textes.Hou… Tu viens regarder le ciel ? Il est: Hoo… Have you come to look at the sky? It's very beautiful tonight. It's very beautiful every night.
textes.Hrmm ! La nacelle t'attend. Monte, monte: Hrmm! The basket's waiting for you. Climb in, climb in.
textes.Hrmm. Bien. Alors regarde en bas. C'est: Hrmm. Good. Then look down. It's pretty down there too.
textes.Hrmm. Bourru. Je garde la nacelle d'osie: Hrmm. Bourru. I keep the wicker basket lift: it goes up to the top of the Mother Oak, and comes back down. Climb in, wait a bit, and up you go. I pull the rope. Well, the pulley does. But I keep an eye on it.
textes.Hrmm. Grand-père Frêne a tressé la nacel: Hrmm. Grandpa Frêne wove the basket. Wicker and rope. After him, Father kept it. He talked to the passengers. A long time. They took the stairs. Me, a cub, I slept in it. At the treetop. In the sun. The wind rocked it. Best nap in the world. Hrmm. Still today.
textes.Hrmm. Monter Lilas à la cime. Au coucher: Hrmm. Take Lilas up to the treetop. At sunset. In the basket. Nobody else.
textes.Hrmm. Pas grave. Je tire doucement. Très: Hrmm. No matter. I pull gently. Very gently. Close your eyes.
textes.Hrmm. Toi, {surnom}. Tu gardes ça. Je ta: Hrmm. You, {surnom}. Keep this to yourself. I drum slowly on purpose. So the dance lasts. Lilas's dance. The slower it is, the longer she dances. I love her. For years. Never told her anything. Nothing. Just “Hrmm”. She must think I'm a drum.
textes.Hugo ? Mon mari. Le plus timide, le plus: Hugo? My husband. The shyest, most stubborn and kindest of men. He lost his wedding ring after ten days. I love him anyway. Even more, actually.
textes.Hugo a perdu son alliance dans le sable,: Hugo has lost his wedding ring in the sand, near the Coco Loco beach hut, where the waves come in.
textes.Hugo m'a acheté une rose rouge, la plus: Hugo bought a red rose from me, the most beautiful one, to apologise to Léa. An hour later, he brought it back: she hadn't taken it. He didn't know what to do with it. I put it in a vase on my counter, “for the time being”. For the time being until what, I have no idea. But I changed its water every morning.
textes.Hugo, c'est mon petit marié. Timide comm: Hugo is my little groom. Shy as a shrimp, but with a heart as big as my pot. He looks at his finger with every bite. There's a story behind it, and my soup is mixed up in it, I can feel it.
textes.Hugo, le jeune marié, m'a acheté une ros: Hugo, the young groom, bought a rose from me to apologise to Léa. She didn't take it. It must be serious.
textes.Hugo, le jeune marié. Un garçon timide c: Hugo, the young groom. A boy as shy as a rosebud, who had the misfortune to lose the one thing he mustn't. He came to me to make amends. Flowers don't fix everything. But they help.
textes.Huit pièces la chambre, thé du matin com: Eight coins a room, morning tea included. Caravaneers pay in dates; you don't even have dates.
textes.Hulotte compte les étoiles toute la nuit: Hulotte counts the stars all night. I look at them. We don't have the same method. He thinks I'm not serious enough. He's right, but that's no reason.
textes.Hulotte dit qu'il a vu une étoile tomber: Hulotte says he saw a star fall into the big pond. I tell everyone it was a firefly that had drunk too much moon tea. The whole market laughed. Hulotte didn't. He looked at me with his big round eyes, without a word, for a whole minute. I've never seen an owl so unamused. I'd sort of earned it.
textes.Hulotte monte à la cime toutes les nuits: Hulotte goes up to the crown every night to look at the stars. He never takes the basket. He flies. Well, he says he flies.
textes.Hulotte regarde le ciel, je regarde le s: Hulotte looks at the sky, I look at the ground. He calculates, I sniff. He says a star fell into the big pond. Me, I believe in tracks. Not in the sky.
textes.Hulotte voit dans le noir ! Il m'a dit q: Hulotte can see in the dark! He told me I had cake on my snout. In the dark!
textes.Hulotte. Il compte les étoiles. Il ne pr: Hulotte. He counts the stars. He won't take my basket. Never. Not for ten years. Hrmm. It's safe now. Very safe.
textes.Hulotte. Il monte la nuit avec une lante: Hulotte. He climbs at night with a lantern and a tube. From afar, he looks like a monster. He knows it. And he pokes his beak into things that are none of his business.
Hmm. We'll need a new roof. Again.
Hmm… I don't see a boat.
textes.Hé ! Bienvenue au local de répète ! Il n: Hey! Welcome to the rehearsal room! We need a voice. Want to try the mic?
textes.Hé ! Ho ! On frappe, avant d'entrer chez: Hey! Ho! You knock before you enter people's homes!
textes.Hé ! Hé ! Toi, d'en haut !: Hey! Hey! You, from up there!
textes.Hé ! Hé, toi ! Tu n'aurais pas vu une ba: Hey! Hey, you! You haven't seen a wand, have you?
textes.Hé ! Je suis de ton côté, imbécile ! … P: Hey! I'm on your side, you fool! … Not anymore!
textes.Hé ! Regarde mes pieds, c'est le pas du: Hey! Look at my feet, it's the crab step! Try it!
textes.Hé ! Rends-moi mes fenêtres !: Hey! Give me back my windows!
textes.Hé ! Toi ! Tu as des jambes ? Deux ? Par: Hey! You! Got legs? Two? Perfect! Pépin, organiser of the Great Race of Ramure: ten lantern arches, a loop around the village, and Bondi to beat. Nobody beats Bondi. Want to try?
textes.Hé ! Toi ! Viens voir mon atelier !: Hey! You! Come and see my workshop!
textes.Hé ! Toi ! Ça sent bon, hein ? Viens goû: Hey! You! Smells good, doesn't it? Come and have a taste!
textes.Hé ! Toi aussi ? Bon, demande à Zoé. Et: Hey! You too? OK, ask Zoé. And if she says “almost”, that's a yes. Round here, almost means yes.
textes.Hé ! Tout le monde parle de toi, tu sais: Hey! Everyone's talking about you, you know?
textes.Hé ! Tout le monde parle de vous, vous s: Hey! Everyone's talking about you, you know?
textes.Hé ! Tu as l'air d'avoir voyagé. Tu as d: Hey! You look well-travelled. Got any maps?
textes.Hé ! Tu as vu ma dernière course ? Deuxi: Hey! Did you see my last race? Second! Nearly first! Well… second.
textes.Hé ! Tu sais danser, toi ? Sois honnête,: Hey! Can you dance? Be honest, I'm a teacher, I see everything.
textes.Hé ! Tu tombes bien. On répète pour… pou: Hey! Perfect timing. We're rehearsing for… for nothing, actually. There's no festival anymore. But we rehearse anyway. Want to turn up the amp? The knob goes up to eleven.
textes.Hé ! Tu veux finir par-dessus bord ?: Hey! Want to end up overboard?
textes.Hé ! Un tour en mer ?: Hey! A trip out to sea?
textes.Hé ! Viens. Je te présente Bérénice. Ell: Hey! Come here. Meet Bérénice. She arrived this morning. You understand.
textes.Hé hé ! Je ne faisais que demander !: Heh heh! I was only asking!
textes.Hé hé ! La deuxième fois, c'était pour t: Heh heh! The second time was for swapping.
textes.Hé hé ! Mes voiles vous disent merci. Pr: Ha ha! My sails say thank you. Take this: the harbour bounty.
textes.Hé hé ! Mon grand-père a troqué une feui: Heh heh! My grandfather traded a “magic” leaf for a house: the house in the pond tree, where I still live! There was nothing magic about the leaf, my friend, but the deal, now that was magic. I grew up there, among the piles of swaps, and I learned to count before I could walk: a pebble, a feather, a vial. As we tanukis say: everything's worth something, especially the rest.
textes.Hé hé ! Trois théières, comme la premièr: Heh heh! Three teapots, like the first time?
textes.Hé hé ! Un caillou-qui-chante pour ma ch: Heh heh! A singing-stone for my carpenter!
textes.Hé hé ! Un vrai tanuki ! Viens dans mes: Heh heh! A true tanuki! Come here and give me a hug, my friend! … But not everything. Not everything, my friend. Not everything.
textes.Hé hé ! Une chaîne de troc qui ferait le: Heh heh! A swap chain that would go round the whole big island: Ramure, Cliquetis, Tazira, Carène, and back! And at the end, something so beautiful nobody could ever swap it again.
textes.Hé hé ! Voilà le renard du marché !: Heh heh! Here comes the market fox!
textes.Hé hé hé ! Un nouveau visage ! Bedaine,: Heh heh heh! A new face! Bedaine, master of the Great Swap. No coins here, my friend: we swap! One thing for another, and everyone leaves richer. It's magic. Well, it's business.
textes.Hé hé, il te manque quelque chose ! Revi: Heh heh, you're missing something! Come back when you have everything.
textes.Hé oui, comme tout le monde. Tu dors pen: Yep, like everybody. You sleep while the fish get up. That's life, I don't hold it against you. Well, a little.
Oh yes. Lime blossom, lemon balm, lavender.
textes.Hé, c'est toi ! Tu veux voir la grande h: Hey, it's you! Want to see the main top? Don't tell the Admiral.
textes.Hé, champion ! Trois carottes, ce matin: Hey, champ! Three carrots this morning?
textes.Hé, dis : si t'avais un bateau, un vrai,: Hey, say: if you had a ship, a real one, would you take me on board? As cabin boy? Or even as first mate?
textes.Hé, l'amateur de punch ! Ton verre t'att: Hey, punch lover! Your glass is waiting for you. Well, in my head. The straw is striped, as promised.
textes.Hé, la personne du soir ! Tu as les cern: Hey, night person! You've got party eye-bags, I can tell. They suit you.
textes.Hé, le barreur ! Le défi de la jetée tie: Hey, helmsman! The harbour-wall challenge still stands. “Wave 3” is waiting for you. She can't wait either.
textes.Hé, le grand ! Tu as besoin d'une lame ?: Hey, big one! Need a blade?
textes.Hé, le poisson ! Il y a des étoiles de m: Hey, fish! There are starfish waiting for you down there. They're getting impatient.
textes.Hé, les bras en l'air ! Le prochain morc: Hey, arms-in-the-air! The next track that builds up is for you. Get your shoulders ready.
textes.Hé, là-dessous ! Monte par l'échelle si: Hey, down there! Climb the ladder if you want to do business!
textes.Hé, petit ! Assieds-toi pas sur mon file: Hey, youngster! Don't sit on my net, it took me three hours to mend.
textes.Hé, renard déguisé ! Tu plaisantes encor: Hey, fox in disguise! Still joking for real? Me too. We should stop. You first.
textes.Hé, t'as pas oublié ? Je suis ton second: Hey, you didn't forget, right? I'm your first mate! I've already practised the orders: “Heave to!”, “Cast off!”, “A pancake!”
textes.Hé, te revoilà ! Le son t'a manqué, avou: Hey, you're back! You missed the beat, admit it.
textes.Hé, toi ! Il paraît qu'on t'a parlé de m: Hey, you! I hear someone's been telling you about me…
textes.Hé, toi ! Il paraît que tu as un avis su: Hey, you! I hear you have an opinion about me?
textes.Hé, toi qui danses sur les ponts ! Mon p: Hey, bridge dancer! My next bridge is still yours to open. Dancing, obviously.
textes.Hé, toi qui jongles ! J'ai gardé les deu: Hey, juggler! I kept the two coconuts for you. We'll move up to three whenever you like.
textes.Hé, toi qui ne t'arrêtes jamais ! Tu rep: Hey, you who never stop! You still keep coming back. That's how it starts, I'm warning you.
textes.Hé, vous ! Il paraît qu'on vous a parlé: Hey, you! I hear someone's been telling you about me…
textes.Hé, vous ! Il paraît que vous avez un av: Hey, you! I hear you have an opinion about me?
textes.Hé, {surnom} ! J'ai trouvé un truc ce ma: Hey, {surnom}! I found a thing this morning. No idea what it is. Want to buy it?
textes.Hé. Tu as bu de l'eau, aujourd'hui ? Vra: Hey. Have you drunk water today? Really drunk, mind. Not one sip.
textes.Héloïse Manivelle, ingénieure-en-chef, p: Héloïse Manivelle, chief engineer, chairs the jury of the Inventions Fair. She needs the opinion of an unbiased visitor.

textes.Ianthé ! Tu danses sur ma marée, ce soir: Ianthé! Are you dancing to my tide tonight?
textes.Ianthé ! Une petite danse ? Je te paie e: Ianthé! A little dance? I'll pay you in crackers!
textes.Ianthé danse comme je chante, en plus vi: Ianthé dances the way I sing, only faster and wetter. She says she's the one people watch. I'm the one people listen to.
textes.Ianthé danse devant mon étal et le clien: Ianthé dances in front of my stall and the customers come all by themselves. I pay her in crackers. She says she'd prefer coins. Everyone says that.
textes.Ianthé danse sur le pont sud tous les so: Ianthé dances on the south bridge every evening. I… I happen to pass that way. For the mother-of-pearl. The light's better there. That's all.
textes.Ianthé m'a demandé un jour pourquoi je n: Ianthé once asked me why I never taste my own crackers. I said I wasn't hungry. She smiled, as if she knew. Since then, when she dances in front of the stall, she pretends to bite into one and pulls a face, a tiny one, just for me. We laugh, the two of us, without a word.
textes.Ici ? Ta première ? Alors souviens-toi b: Here? Your first? Then remember this night well, kid. You tell the story of your firsts your whole life. And you polish it a little each time.
textes.Ici c'est la teuf, là-bas c'est la valse: Here it's the party, over there it's the waltz. The two islands are made for each other.
textes.Ici, je loge chambre douze, au Grand Hôt: Here, I stay in room twelve at the Grand Hotel. Six croissants from Madame Margaux every morning. A snow globe from Victor every week. Fernand's sea dragon tooth, under a glass dome. Toni's divine punch, paid in gold. Madame Colette's jar of figs, which she refuses to sell me. And Edmond's moustache, which I covet in silence. Well, almost in silence.
textes.Ici, je ne fais rien. Rien du tout. Depu: Here, I do nothing. Nothing at all. For three days, I've been sunbathing, reading, watching my two children from my towel, and in the evening we dine at Paulo's. The grocer recommended her favourite novel, the fortune-teller made me a prediction, and one evening I passed some chocolate to the young bride next door, who was crying. For someone who does nothing, I'm very busy.
textes.Ici, sous terre, impossible de voler : t: Here, underground, you can't fly: you land.
textes.Ici, tout se règle à la pétanque. Les ma: Here, everything gets settled with pétanque. Weddings, inheritances, elections. The mayor won at pétanque.
textes.Il a aimé ton histoire d'hier, Faelar. C: It liked your story yesterday, Faelar. The one about the hedgehog.
textes.Il a apporté son chronomètre de Cliqueti: He brought his Cliquetis stopwatch to the bakery. Now he times the baking: “Twenty-two minutes, Trèfle! Record broken!” It's not a race, Pépin, it's bread! But I have to admit: since then, I haven't burnt a thing. Cerfeuil would have laughed. He burnt every loaf, and without a stopwatch.
textes.Il a baptisé sa glace coco « Bruno-Loco: He named his coconut ice cream “Bruno-Loco”, in my honour, he says. The day I went to taste it at the beach hut, he didn't make me pay: “It's your recipe, brother.” Then he made me pay for the glass of water. He's sharp, that boy.
textes.Il a construit un château à quatre tours: He built a castle with four towers and a moat. I photographed it from every angle: front, back, from above, lying in the sand. Sixty-two photos. When I looked up, the sea had carried off a tower. Théo said: “You didn't even look at it, Dad.” But I've got sixty-two photos of it.
textes.Il a dit « peut-être ». C'est mieux qu'h: It said “maybe”. That's better than yesterday.
textes.Il a encore oublié de remonter la nacell: He forgot to bring the basket back down again. Three rabbits waited at the bottom a whole morning. I found him asleep at the treetop, nose in the sun. I growled. He said: “Hrmm. They took the stairs? Serves them right.” He was right. I didn't tell him.
textes.Il a entendu parler des chaussures à res: He heard about the spring shoes in Cliquetis. He begged me. Three evenings. “Just two springs, Ursule!” No. I told Pépin. Pépin said: “Cheating.” Grisou sulked for a week. The forge was quiet. Lovely week. Since then, he asks for lighter shoes. “Just in case.”
textes.Il a goûté une de mes galettes par jour: He tasted one of my crackers a day for forty days, taking notes, to find the recipe. On the forty-first, he came to read me his scroll, all proud. I said: “Wrong. All wrong.” He was so disappointed I gave him a cracker. Free! He wrote that down too, of course.
He seems to regret your quarrel.
textes.Il a mes pattes, ton crabe sentimental !: Your sentimental crab has my legs!
textes.Il a posé une pièce d'or sur mon comptoi: He put a gold coin on my counter, a big one, with his great-grandfather's head on it. “For the oldest jar in the shop, madam.” I pushed it back with my fingertip. He took a goat's cheese instead, and paid for it with the same coin. I didn't have change. I gave it to him in honey. Six jars.
textes.Il a un chronomètre de Cliquetis, et il: He has a stopwatch from Cliquetis, and he times everything: the race, the warm-up, the nap, even my carrots. “Forty-three seconds for three carrots, Bondi, a record!” I hear the tick-tock even in my dreams.
textes.Il a écrit dans ses rouleaux que la prem: He wrote in his scrolls that grandmother's first cracker was “dreadful”. Dreadful! I went to the archives to scratch the word out myself. He sat on the scroll. We stayed like that for an hour. In the end he added “eaten while weeping for joy”. I accepted the deal.
textes.Il avait dix ans, des genoux écorchés et: He was ten, with scraped knees and the nerve of a government minister. He took the finest apple off my stall, bit into it in front of me, and said: “I'll pay you when I'm mayor.” I wrote it in my notebook. Page one. He's been mayor for eighteen years. The page hasn't changed.
textes.Il avait six ans, il courait sur la plag: He was six, running along the beach knocking over the parasols, and banging on two coconuts and a conch. I taught him to count with his feet. I named him Mistral, because he blew through like the wind. Now he gets the whole village dancing. I tell people he learned on seashells. It's true. More or less.
textes.Il balaie ! Colle-toi à ses chenilles, o: It sweeps! Stick close to its tracks, or back away out of reach.
It's sulking, Thalion. It has its moods.
textes.Il brille au soleil. Un marchand en voud: It shines in the sun. A merchant might want it.
It shines, Coralin. Just like yours.
It sings too loud. Clou can't sleep any more.
textes.Il chante « Marée Basse » ! Il chante «: It's singing “Low Tide”! It's singing “Low Tide”!
textes.Il cherchait la chaleur, Dagna. Comme to: It was looking for warmth, Dagna. Like everyone.
textes.Il croit que je ne l'ai pas vu, la nuit,: He thinks I didn't see him, at night, behind the lanterns, watching me run. … I saw him. So one morning I left my tracks on purpose. On his training path. Nice and clear. Fourteen laps. So he'd count. … He counted.
textes.Il croit que je ne le vois pas, la nuit,: He thinks I don't see him at night, under my windows, with his mother-of-pearl lamp and an empty scroll. He's waiting for my lamp to go out so he can finally write something cheerful. Some nights I blow it out on purpose, even if I'm not sleeping. He goes home delighted.
textes.Il croit que je ne vois pas les haricots: He thinks I don't see the beans he slips into my right pocket to cheat on his hot honeys. I see them. Once, I let him: I served him his five hot honeys, and made him pay for all five. He paid in stories, five stories. Good deal. But I sewed my pocket shut all the same.
textes.Il croit que je triche aux osselets. Je: He thinks I cheat at jacks. I don't cheat: I just blow on the shells a tiny bit, to make them spin. Blowing is my job. He says it's cheating. Coralin used to say the same. I'm starting to think it's a city-wide affliction.
He dances better than Haldir now.
textes.Il dit que je chante faux. J'ai chanté u: He says I sing off-key. I sang once, at the Dawn Festival, a hundred years ago, because I'd been asked to. Nobody has asked me again. That's perfectly fine. But I don't see why he has to remind everyone of it at every festival.
He says your map was wrong.
textes.Il dit toujours : « C'est la mer. » Quan: He always says: “It's the sea.” When it crackles. Once it was a crab, inside Raoul. … Fine. Most of the time, it's true, it's the sea. But I check. He never checks. He trusts me. Trust is heavy. It's good.
textes.Il déteste ma tisane de lune. Alors, les: He hates my moon tea. So on nights when he can't sleep, I serve it to him in an old sailor's mug with a spoonful of honey at the bottom, and say it's the captains' hot honey. He downs it in one, goes “aaah” like Corentin, and sleeps like a rock.
textes.Il en manque {manque}. Les araignées de: {manque} still missing. The spiders in the western cave. Go.
textes.Il est 23 heures… Les projecteurs s'étei: It's 11 PM… The spotlights go out for a moment. At the side of the stage, Clapotis holds Bouton-d'Or's hand, and doesn't take his eyes off the sky. FFFIIIIIIUUU… BOOM!
He went to ask Octave for nails. He came back saying Octave's shacks are better. I sulked for three days. On the fourth, I taught him the clove hitch, which Octave doesn't know. We have our weapons too.
textes.Il est arrivé à Forgefer avec des bras d: He turned up in Forgefer with big'un arms and a mule's head. I gave him sacks of coal. Three years of sacks. He came back every morning. On the first day of the fourth year, I handed him a hammer. He looked at it like the king's crown. I went to fetch a mug of fizz, so I wouldn't have to see his face.
textes.Il est au crayon. Je l'effacerai le jour: It's in pencil. I'll rub it out the day I see it.
textes.Il est en bois. Et il ne sert pas les pu: It's made of wood. And it doesn't serve punch.
textes.Il est entré et il a posé sa main sur mo: He came in and laid his hand on my counter like a piece of evidence. “Exactly the same,” he said. Then, very quietly: “Half a size smaller, without it showing.” A ring too big that slips off in the waves… I didn't need my loupe to understand.
textes.Il est frais, il est beau mon poisson !: Fresh and lovely, my fish! Come closer, come closer! I'm Rosalie, and here we only sell this morning's catch.
textes.Il est gros comment ? Il est gros commen: How big is it? How big is it?
textes.Il est monté un soir, sans prévenir, ave: He came up one evening, unannounced, with two cups of coffee. At the two hundredth step, I heard him puffing like a whale. He got to the top with one empty cup and one half-full. He handed me the half. I drank it. I didn't say thank you. He came back anyway.
textes.Il est parfait. Mes filles ont butiné le: It's perfect. My girls have been foraging the lime trees.
textes.Il est parfait… Attendez… Écoutez ! Tic,: It's perfect… Wait… Listen! Tick, tock… and… DONG! It chimes! After so many years! Thank you, thank you… You've given the square its heart back.
textes.Il est parti par là-bas, vers la colline: It went over there, towards the hill, above the houses in the west! It got stuck in a tree, I'm sure of it!
It's been down for an hour.
textes.Il est revenu de Cliquetis, autrefois, a: Long ago, he came back from Cliquetis with a compass that points south. South! For a tracker, that's a treasure: you always know where you're not going. By the time I went to ask him for it, he'd swapped it in Carène, for a telescope. I haven't quite forgiven him.
textes.Il est tard, oui. Mais la nuit a ses sec: It's late, yes. But the night has its secrets.
textes.Il est tout petit, Grégoire ! C'est de l: It's tiny, Grégoire! It's called rigour!
textes.Il est venu me demander de garder la Gra: He came and asked to guard the Great Gate with me. I looked at him for an hour without saying a thing. He talked the whole hour. I said: “No. You smile too much.” He went off to guard the hall. He still smiles. He even smiles on duty. Hmph.
textes.Il est venu me saluer dans la clairière,: He came to greet me in the clearing, Gaston on his shoulder and only one boot on. He asked me if elves ate shells. I said we mostly ate flowers. The next day, he brought me a bouquet. Of shells. I kept it.
textes.Il existera quand tu m'auras donné la cr: He will exist once you've given me the crust.
textes.Il fait bon. Les heures passent tranquil: It's pleasant out. The hours drift by.
textes.Il fait noir… Tu entends ce bruit ? C'ét: It's dark… Do you hear that noise? That was my tummy. I think.
textes.Il fait nuit. Je reste tout près de toi,: It's night. I'll stay right next to you, if you don't mind.
Everyone has to be kept covered.
textes.Il faut posséder au moins un des quatre: You must own at least one of the four seals.
I need to tighten his bolts.
textes.Il grandit tous les soirs, ton doigt, je: That finger of yours grows every night, if you ask me.
textes.Il hoche la tête. Ça prend trois semaine: He nods his head. It takes three weeks.
It found it. In my cauldron.
He has it… under his arm. It's a start.
textes.Il laisse des miettes de gomme partout s: He leaves eraser crumbs all over my table. He draws, he rubs out, he draws again: a city, a crystal, columns. The day he finally spoke, it was to explain the crystal to me. A whole hour. I closed the terrace late. I didn't understand a thing. It was very beautiful, all the same.
textes.Il laisse toujours un pourboire « munici: He always leaves a “municipal” tip. One coin, set down nice and straight on the saucer, with a little speech: “For the staff of the Square, on behalf of the town.” The staff is me. One day, I gave him the coin back: “For the broken cups, on behalf of the café.” He laughed about it for a week.
textes.Il m'a acheté trois pommes. Je les ai em: He bought three apples from me. I wrapped them in paper, as I do for everyone, and I charged him for the paper. One penny. He looked at the paper, he paid. The next week, I took him my cheese knife to sharpen. He charged me for the sharpening. To the penny. I said nothing. Hm.
textes.Il m'a arrêté sur le quai, carnet à la m: He stopped me on the quay, notebook in hand: “Running on a public thoroughfare.” I asked him to read me the regulations. He read them: “No bicycles on the quay.” I looked at my legs, I looked at the sergeant. No wheels. The next day, there was a slate: “Runners: walking pace.” I overtake it with a salute.
textes.Il m'a demandé de lui rapporter quelque: He asked me to bring him something “really from the bottom”. I brought him up an old copper button from the Léviathan, with an anchor on it. He sewed it onto his hat, crooked, with fishing line. He says it's his captain's medal. He shows it to everyone.
textes.Il m'a demandé de mettre en couleur sa c: He asked me to colour his map of Port-Azur, the one the mayor gives to visitors. I painted the sea in six blues: the port blue, the bay blue, the open-sea blue… He held the map at arm's length, eyes shining: “It's the first map that looks wet.” I nearly cried.
textes.Il m'a demandé les plans de son auberge,: He asked me for plans of his inn, with real beds and a sign. I drew twelve rooms. He added in pencil, in a corner: “My aunt's room, with a stove.” He thinks I didn't see. I went over it in ink.
textes.Il m'a demandé pourquoi je n'arrive pas: He asked me why I can't paint the pink. I explained the light, the sad tubes, the evening that keeps moving. He thought about it, then said: “Pink is when blue and red give each other a kiss.” I tried it. It didn't work. But I've never heard a better theory.
textes.Il m'a demandé un jour : « Amirale, si j: He once asked me: “Admiral, if I repair the Léviathan, can I be captain?” I answered: “If you repair it, you'll be admiral.” He thought about it, and said: “No. Captain's better: you're on the ship.” He's right. I didn't tell him.
textes.Il m'a dessiné une carte du Bois-Doré sa: He drew me a map of Bois-Doré without ever having been there. Everything's wrong: the trees, the walkways, the number of moons. Except the Mother Tree, exactly in its place. I hung it at home, above my bed.
textes.Il m'a dicté la ballade du roi Atlas. Le: He dictated the ballad of King Atlas to me. The next day, I was singing it in the square, and in the third verse, Protée stood up in the front row: “No, no, now it's a queen, and she has an octopus!” Everyone laughed. I carried on with the octopus. I'm a professional.
textes.Il m'a dicté un jour : « Par ordre du ro: One day he dictated: “By order of the king, fizz is a royal treasure.” I wrote: “Fizz is a treasure.” He shouted: “Where did royal go?” I said: “Ulfa would never have put it up.” He thought about it, he laughed, he signed. The decree still hangs above the counter at the Mug.
textes.Il m'a donné un crayon enduit de cire et: He gave me a wax-coated pencil and a little board, to draw underwater. I tried. My drawing looked like a poorly octopus. He framed it. It hangs in the harbour master's office, next to the big map. When people ask him what it is, he says: “A discovery.”
textes.Il m'a emmené en pédalo, « pour voir la: He took me out in a pedalo, “to see the coast from below”. He pedalled, I looked. After three metres, I felt the sea rising in my throat. After four, I was leaning over the side. He turned round, singing. I've never been so far from home.
textes.Il m'a frappé ! Vous avez vu ?!: He hit me! Did you see?!
textes.Il m'a rapporté de sa grande traversée u: He brought me back a black pebble from the highlands after his great crossing, telling me it was ore. It was coal. I said nothing: I put it in the forge, and on its fire I forged him a pair of compasses for his maps. He still doesn't know his ore was coal.
textes.Il m'a taillé un peigne dans une branche: He carved me a comb from a branch that fell from his kapok tree. He repeated three times: “Fallen. Not cut.” I wear it every day. In Bois-Doré, people ask me which elf carved it. I answer: a bear.
textes.Il m'apporte le minerai des pentes rouge: He brings me ore from the red slopes, and every time he forgets a sack somewhere on the mountain. Once, he forgot Fundin. Fundin came back the next day, black as soot, with the sack and a bat in his hood. I paid Grimli anyway. The ore was good.
I still need {manque}, {surnom}. My cauldron is waiting.
textes.Il m'en manque {manque}. Elles brillent: I'm still missing {manque}. They shine like tiny little moons lying on the ground.
textes.Il m'envoie des corbeaux à minuit avec d: He sends me crows at midnight with very important messages. “The king is hungry.” “The king requests cheese.” “The king asks whether the cheese is asleep.” One night, I sent Croâ back with a cheese tied to his leg. Croâ ate it on the way. The king thanked me for the crow.
textes.Il m'échange une lampe de nacre chaque s: Every week he trades me a mother-of-pearl lamp for my crackers. He thinks I resell them. I've kept them all. Thirty-seven lamps, lit, in my house. At night it looks like a little crystal. If you tell him, I'll charge you double for life.
textes.Il m'écoute moi, ou il t'écoute toi ?: Is he listening to me, or is he listening to you?
textes.Il manque encore {manque_liste}. Ne te p: We're still missing {manque_liste}. Don't hurry: the Tree is patient, even when it's ill.
textes.Il manque encore {manque} Perles de Lumi: {manque} Pearls of Light are still missing. The crystal is waiting patiently. So am I.
textes.Il manque la mer. Elle ne rentre pas dan: The sea is missing. It doesn't fit in your speakers.
textes.Il manque un pêcheur, Fernand !: What's missing is a fisherman, Fernand!
There's a ruby missing tonight, Ulfa.
textes.Il manque un truc. Je te dirai quand je: Something's missing. I'll tell you when I know.
textes.Il me faut du bois droit pour mes flèche: I need straight wood for my arrows. Bring me {manque} good straight sticks and I'll pay you. Honestly.
textes.Il me faut du bois, oui. Une voie d'eau: I need wood, yes. A leak has opened under the forge, on the port side: nothing serious, but if I don't plug it, Jos will end the week with his feet in the water. Four logs. Good wood, not driftwood. An axe, a tree, and back you come.
textes.Il me faut encore {manque_liste}. Courag: I still need {manque_liste}. Courage: the Tree is waiting for you. It never complains, but I can hear it sigh.
textes.Il me faut encore {manque} dents de requ: I still need {manque} shark teeth. Keep going!
textes.Il me faut {manque} runes. Pas une de mo: I need {manque} runes. Not one less. A gate doesn't open halfway.
I'm out of wild honey, {surnom}. Could you find me {manque} combs? In the hollow trees on your island, when you chop wood. I'll bake you bread in return!
textes.Il me manque encore {manque_liste}. La f: I'm still missing {manque_liste}. The moonflower only grows at the top of the little jungle peak, the one that looks over the bay. The water: draw it with the vial from the pool of the big waterfall, in the north-east of this island. And the golden seed… the waves carried it off long ago. Perhaps a collector picked it up?
textes.Il me manque encore {manque} champignons: I still need {manque} mushrooms. Patience: the forest is full of them.
textes.Il me manque encore {manque} minerais. P: I still need {manque} ores. No iron, no sword. That's the law of the anvil.
textes.Il me manque encore {manque} rayons de m: I still need {manque} honeycombs. Keep going, my oven is waiting for you!
textes.Il me manque {manque} éclats d'obsidienn: I still need {manque} obsidian shards. The runes are waiting.
textes.Il me raconte tout ce qu'il entend sur l: He tells me everything he hears on deck: the islands, the winds, the rumours. Even the seasick goat: “She saw the elves' island, and she threw up.” I wrote it all down. In the margin of my map, near the Bois-Doré, there's a tiny little goat. She's my most reliable source.
textes.Il me reproche d'écrire des histoires mo: He accuses me of writing dead stories. “A true story is a story that has lived.” I asked him for proof. He held a shell to my ear and said: “Listen.” All I heard was the sea. He said: “There. It's all in there.” For once, I didn't write anything down.
textes.Il me reste un pain au chocolat à deux b: I've got one two-bar pain au chocolat left. Quick, before Nina gets back from the fountain!
textes.Il ment. Comme tous les arbres. Et tous: It's lying. Like all trees. And all customers.
It's not for sale. Same as yesterday.
textes.Il n'y a eu qu'une autre exception, il y: There's only been one other exception, a hundred and twenty years ago: “The Pearl of the avenue has vanished. Black ship sunk to the west.” The handwriting shook that evening too. I asked him how it had happened. He said: “I didn't see anything.” Then he looked at his feet for a very long time. I didn't write that down. That's rare.
textes.Il n'y a jamais de détails dans « rien »: There are never any details in “nothing”. That's what saddens me.
textes.Il n'y a jamais eu de dragon, petit. Il: There never was a dragon, lad. There was a very big dwarf.
textes.Il n'y a personne. Le parquet craque sou: There's nobody. The floorboards creak under your steps. Especially near the rug.
textes.Il n'y a personne. Une maison bien rangé: There's nobody here. A tidy house that smells of wax and bread.
textes.Il n'y a personne… juste une théière sur: There's nobody here… just a teapot on the low table. A teapot with… a bushy tail?
textes.Il n'y a plus rien sous le coussin. Just: There's nothing left under the cushion. Just a bit of cat fur.
textes.Il n'y a rien dans mes poches ! … Enfin,: There's nothing in my pockets! … Well, nothing that goes croak.
textes.Il n'y avait pas de loup dans cette hist: There was no wolf in that story.
There aren't any under my windows.
textes.Il nageait près de la paillote du Coco L: He was swimming near the Coco Loco beach hut, where the waves meet the sand. It must be buried there. But you can't get it out with your hands.
textes.Il naît : tout s'éveille.\nIl règne : to:
It is born: everything awakens.
It reigns: everything blazes.
It dies: everything sheds its leaves.
Where it never goes, everything sleeps.
It doesn't move. Its cannons do.
textes.Il ouvre une noix de coco d'un seul coup: He opens a coconut with a single stroke of the machete, like his grandfather. The first day, he did it in front of my kiosk, to impress me. Whack! Two perfect halves. The juice squirted over my window, my cones and the sergeant. Lefort wanted to fine him for “splashing”. He got an ice cream instead.
textes.Il paie chaque histoire d'une noisette,: He pays for each story with a hazelnut, set nice and straight on my knee, and takes it back when he leaves, “for next time”. One evening, I was the one who fell asleep before him. When I woke up, he'd finished the story by himself, for the other little ones. With a dragon. There's always a dragon, with Gland.
textes.Il paraît qu'il y a cent ans, un tonneau: They say that a hundred years ago, a barrel rolled off a cart onto an elf who'd come to sell wood, and Bramm smiled. I was in the kitchen. I didn't see a thing. I've been watching out ever since. With every bowl, I look at his beard. It twitches, sometimes. I note it all down on my kitchen wall, in chalk.
textes.Il paraît qu'il y a des ruines sous les: They say there are ruins under the roots of the great kapok trees. Stairs that lead nowhere. Or else very far away.
textes.Il paraît qu'il y aura de la daurade, ve: I hear there'll be sea bream on Friday.
textes.Il paraît qu'on peut voir le Grand Spagh: They say you can see the Great Spaghetti through the holes in the ceiling. I'm looking for the right hole.
textes.Il paraît qu'on trouve des petites croix: They say you can find little wooden crosses on the beaches. Castaways more far-sighted than me buried their savings there.
textes.Il paraît qu'à Cliquetis, ils ont des ch: Apparently in Cliquetis they have spring-loaded shoes. If I had some… No. Pépin would say it's cheating. Pépin's right. But still.
textes.Il paraît qu'à Port-Azur, Django joue de: Word is that in Port-Azur, Django plays waltzes at the Perroquet Bleu. One day we'll do a track together: waltz-techno!
textes.Il paraît qu'à Port-Azur, ils font des c: Apparently in Port-Azur they make croissants. That means “crescent” — bread shaped like a crescent moon! Like ours! But only half.
textes.Il paraît que Faelar a raconté l'histoir: I hear Faelar told the story of the first seed. Again.
textes.Il paraît que Hulotte a vu une étoile to: Apparently Hulotte saw a star fall into the great pool. Me, I think it was a firefly that had drunk too much moon tea.
textes.Il paraît que Mistral prépare un morceau: Word is Mistral's working on a track with whale songs. It's going to be huge.
textes.Il paraît que de l'autre côté de l'île v: They say on the other side of the island lives an old loon who talks to seashells. Barnabé, his name is. Don't believe a word he says about me.
textes.Il paraît que je suis « un peu bizarre »: Apparently I'm “a bit weird”, according to you. It was {qn} who told me. I'll think about it. Or not.
Apparently I'm “a bit weird”, according to you. It was {qn} who told me. I'll think about it. Or not.
textes.Il paraît que la Porte aux Quatre Sceaux: Apparently the Gate of the Four Seals is made of stone, but its hinges are metal. A metal nobody knows. I'd love to see a bit of it.
textes.Il paraît que tu as aidé {qn}. {Il} aura: I hear you helped {qn}. {Il} could have managed on {son} own, but there you go.
textes.Il paraît que tu as frappé {qn}. Je ne d: I hear you hit {qn}. I shouldn't laugh. I laughed anyway.
textes.Il paraît que tu as offert {objet} à {qn: I hear you gave {objet} to {qn}. {Il} talked my ear off about it all day. Thank you on behalf of {lui}.
I hear you gave {objet} to {qn}… {Il} hates that! Don't worry, I said it's the thought that counts.
textes.Il paraît que tu as soigné l'Arbre sacré: They say you healed the sacred Tree on your island. Thank you, human.
textes.Il paraît que tu fais des cadeaux à {qn}: I hear you've been giving presents to {qn}. That's nice of you.
textes.Il paraît que tu me trouves sympathique: I hear you think I'm nice? It was {qn} who told me. Well, that warms my heart.

textes.Il paraît que {qn} t'a parlé de moi. Je: I hear {qn} told you about me. I didn't know {il} knew me so well.
textes.Il paraît que {qn} t'a parlé de moi. Ne: I hear {qn} told you about me. Don't believe everything {il} says.
textes.Il paraît que {qn} t'a parlé de moi. Tou: I hear {qn} told you about me. All good things, I hope.
textes.Il paraît que {qn} t'a raconté toute sa: I hear {qn} told you {son} whole life story. You must be a good listener, you.

textes.Il passe parfois une barque, loin, à l'o: Now and then a boat goes by, far off, to the west. It comes from the village islands and the elves. I count them. This year: three. Including you.
textes.Il passe à chaque ronde, les mains dans: He comes by on every patrol, hands behind his back, all casual. He looks at the beach, he looks at the sea, he looks at the vanilla. I hold out a cone. He takes it without a word, like a piece of evidence. Three times a day. Rosalie shouts it all over the port. He says he's “keeping an eye on the kiosk”. Of course he is.
It's crying, more like. It's wet.
It rains inside, it's the atmosphere.
textes.Il pousse à l'ombre des grands arbres. R: It grows in the shade of the tall trees. Restores half a heart.
textes.Il pétille sur la langue comme une poign: It fizzes on the tongue like a handful of stars.
textes.Il pêche au pied du phare, maintenant, a: He fishes at the foot of the lighthouse now, at the end of the jetty, just when I go up for my watch. He says it's the best spot. It's true. That annoys me all the more. He whistles. Out of tune. To needle me. One evening I threw a handful of coarse salt at him through the skylight. He said thank you, and salted his sardine.
textes.Il racontait le naufrage du Léviathan de: He told the wreck of the Léviathan standing up, rolling like a ship: left for the wave, right for the wind, and the whole circle rolled with him. When the ship hit land, he dropped down onto the sand. Three old folk of Tazira got seasick. I applauded. I've never dared tell a story lying down.
textes.Il raconte partout que l'idée de faire f: He tells everyone the idea of making the gunports smoke, against the Murène Noire, was his. It's possible: he whispered it to me at the rail, between two hot honeys. But I was the one who got into the boat. An idea, Corentin, doesn't go and parley with a pirate.
textes.Il refuse d'enlever son képi pendant les: He refuses to take off his cap during massages. “A sergeant does not uncover on duty.” We're alone, in the back room, door shut. He keeps the cap on. He walks out stiff as a post, and gives me a regulation salute on the threshold of the back door.
He regrets your quarrel, I think.
textes.Il reste Pixel, quelque part dans la cit: Pixel is still out there, somewhere in the city…
textes.Il reste Quark… écoute bien : il fredonn: Quark is still out there… listen carefully: he hums when he hides.
textes.Il reste une chose que je n'ai jamais di: There's one thing I've never told anyone. Someday, maybe. When I trust you.
There's one thing I've never told anyone. Someday, maybe. When I trust you.
textes.Il revient tous les ans. J'écris « sorti: It comes back every year. I'm writing “out”.
textes.Il s'appelle Moustache ! Regarde ses mou: His name is Moustache! Look at his whiskers!
textes.Il s'est arrêté net au bord de la plate-: He stopped dead at the edge of the platform! Strike!
textes.Il s'est assis devant ma forge pendant t: He sat in front of my forge for thirty days so I'd take him on as an apprentice. Ash was raining down, he stayed. On the thirtieth day, I handed him a broom. He took it as if it were the king's axe. Twelve years later, he's still sweeping. Not as well, but with pride.
textes.Il s'est assommé contre la paroi ! C'est: He knocked himself out against the wall! Now's the moment!
textes.Il sait sourire, c'est déjà ça. Yo, capi: He knows how to smile, that's something. Yo, captain!
textes.Il sort une lame ! Le lâche !: He's drawing a blade! The coward!
textes.Il sort, tout au fond, un disque dans un: From the very back, he pulls out a record in a handmade sleeve: a sun and a cloud holding hands. “Vinyle kept this one for the day the two villages made peace. That day has come.” The music starts: djembes, a fuzzy guitar, and two girls' voices… those of Granny Sunflower and Mother Downpour, fifty years ago.
textes.Il t'a dit quelque chose, celui-là ?: Did that one say anything to you?
textes.Il t'a touché ? Avec son Appendice Nouil: He touched you? With his Noodly Appendage? (The Reverend takes off his golden colander, presses it to his heart, and puts it back on crooked.) My child… In forty years, he has touched only three people. A fisherman, a baker, and Nonno Tortellini, in 1987 — he says it was a wink, but it was a noodle. You are the fourth. Here: two plates of Mamma's spaghetti, two focaccias fresh from the oven, and a title, which I'll write myself in the great book. Ramen, my child. Ramen!
textes.Il te manque des pièces… Bon. Je te l'of: You're short of coins… Fine. It's on me. But don't tell Spleen, he'd say I'm too nice. He'd be right.
textes.Il te manque quelques pièces. Reviens qu: You're a few coins short. Come back when you've got enough to pay.
textes.Il te réveille d'un coup : endurance au: It wakes you up in one go: stamina at maximum.
textes.Il te suit ! Regarde-le, le groin collé: He's following you! Look at him, snout glued to your shoes! (Père Gaubert laughs, then blows his nose loudly.) It's the pollen. Listen carefully, lad: he eats anything, but not the golden turnips, no, those are my little ones. In the woods and meadows, let him sniff around: he'll find you truffles, and sometimes some old buried thing, a coin, a ring… He has a golden snout, I'm telling you. Here, two truffles he found for me yesterday, and a few coins. And if you don't already have a whistle to call your animals, take my father's, carved from bone: a dog, a cat, a rat and a pig all around it. Whistle, and your pig will come back. Gently with my little one, all right!
textes.Il tient depuis deux cents ans, Jos. Et: It's held for two hundred years, Jos. And so has your hinge.
It flows the other way, the current.
textes.Il tourne tous les jours, le vent, Matth: The wind turns every day, Matthias.
He'll come round to my side one day.
textes.Il va battre son record… Non… Si… NON !: He's going to beat his record… No… Yes… NO!
textes.Il va très bien ! Enfin, il tourne un pe: It's very well! Well, it spins a little when I think about it.
It's waiting for you. It lives up to its name.
textes.Il vous manque quelques pièces. Revenez: You're a few coins short. Come back when you can pay.
textes.Il y a cent ans, Glaucos a ramolli des c: A hundred years ago, Glaucos softened some shells in the crystal's heat and blew into them through a reed. A round lamp, in three minutes. It takes me three weeks to carve one. I said: “That's cheating.” He packed up his tools, very politely, and left that same evening. He kept the apron.
A hundred years ago, Orsik never laughed. He counted. So one evening, I took a ruby from him. Just one. Then another the next day. At the Forge Festival, I gave him back a full mug: three hundred and sixty-five rubies. The face he made… I thought he was going to cry. He laughed. For the first time.
textes.Il y a cent ans, Yggdrasil a cessé de do: A hundred years ago, Yggdrasil stopped giving its seeds. That same winter, Églantine, queen of the root fairies and my friend, wrote to me: “Something is growing under my throne. Come.” When I went down, the brambles were already closing off the north. I called to her for three nights. The brambles answered. She didn't.
textes.Il y a cent ans, le grand tremblement a: A hundred years ago, the great quake split the old gates of Forgefer. The old king told me: “Forty days.” I took thirty-nine. Grimli hauled the ore up for me on his back. On the last evening, a spark singed off half his beard. He says it grew back finer. He's lying. The gates, though, haven't budged. Now that's solid.
textes.Il y a cent ans, les ronces ont poussé a: A hundred years ago the brambles grew in the north, and they took our Queen Églantine. I cried for a whole month. And one morning I saw that my tears weren't drying: they shone, perfectly round, like moon dew. Since then, when I lose my drops… I make more. It's not very practical.
textes.Il y a cent ans, un automne, j'ai trouvé: A hundred years ago, one autumn, I found a black shoot up north, in the old root. It smelled of iron. I warned Queen Églantine. I warned everyone. They said: “You're always grumbling, Grommelot.” Yes. That time I had good reason to grumble. When winter came, the brambles were everywhere. And the queen, inside them.
textes.Il y a cent ans, à la fête de l'Aube, en: A hundred years ago, at the Dawn festival, in the middle of a ballad, my G string snapped. A blue-eyed elf climbed onto the stage and replaced it with a golden thread, without a word. Then she stepped down again. I forgot the rest of the ballad. I forgot Celebrë singing. I forgot my own name, I think.
textes.Il y a cent ans, à la fête de l'Aube, je: A hundred years ago, at the Dawn festival, I was singing the “Ballad” with Caelan. A string broke, Ilyria came up to replace it, and Caelan ran off after her. Mid-verse! I sang alone for a whole hour, making up the words. They say it was my finest hour. Mostly it was my longest.
textes.Il y a cent ans, à la fête de l'Aube, un: A hundred years ago, at the Dawn festival, a string on Caelan's harp snapped in the middle of the ballad. I had a golden thread in my pocket, I can't remember why. I went up, tied it, came back down. He looked at me as if I'd brought him the moon. He's played under my window every night since. I should have kept my thread.
textes.Il y a cent cinquante ans, le volcan a t: A hundred and fifty years ago, the volcano coughed all winter long. The ash fell like grey snow, and the terrace forges mustn't go out. So we brought the big cauldron out of the city, Bramm carried it on his back, and I fed a hundred dwarves with a cracked ladle. Borin forged me a spoon. I still have it.
textes.Il y a cent quatre-vingts ans, les genou: A hundred and eighty years ago, my father's knees gave out. He handed me the spear without a word. The first visitor that day was a goat. I made it wait three hours, on principle. It ate the hem of my cloak. I didn't move. You don't move.
textes.Il y a cent vingt ans, j'ai chanté la ma: A hundred and twenty years ago, on the steps of the Gate, I sang the high tide so softly that Triton fell asleep. I saw him. He looked so peaceful that I didn't want to wake him. The next day, the Pearl of the avenue had vanished. I've never said a word, {surnom}. Least of all to him.
textes.Il y a cent vingt ans, je suivais une ve: A hundred and twenty years ago, I was following a vein of iron, happy as can be, and I came up a little too far. My head popped out through the floor of the guardhouse, between Bramm's boots. I asked him if he'd moved house. He's never forgiven me. Me, I've forgotten why he's cross. Almost.
textes.Il y a cent vingt ans, le sol de ma loge: A hundred and twenty years ago, the floor of my guardhouse cracked open. A head popped out, between my boots. A helmet, a grey beard: Grimli. “Sorry, I was looking for my tunnel.” The gate was never forced. The floor was. That doesn't count. I filled the hole myself. With a gate stone, and my fist.
