textes.Je prends l'air avant de commencer ma jo: I'm getting some fresh air before starting my day.
textes.Je prends un jus de fruits, tranquilleme: I'm having a fruit juice, nice and easy.
I'm enjoying the cool evening air.
textes.Je profite du banc. Il est à tout le mon: I'm enjoying the bench. It belongs to everyone, but right now, it's mine.
textes.Je prépare le repas. Si tu restes, il y: I'm making a meal. If you stay, there'll be some for you.
textes.Je prépare ma robe pour la fête de l'Aub: I'm making my dress for the Dawn Festival. I'd need {manque} pearls to embroider it like dew. You find them in the sea, don't you?
textes.Je prépare un éclair… Reculez un peu, pa: I'm preparing a bolt… Stand back a little, just to be safe.
textes.Je pète la forme ! Regarde, je saute enc: I'm buzzing! Look, I can jump even higher than yesterday.
textes.Je pêche. Enfin, j'attends. La pêche, c': I'm fishing. Well, waiting. Fishing is mostly waiting.
textes.Je rachète le poisson de la surface ! Ic: I buy fish from the surface! Down here we don't fish: we talk to the fish. But a grilled mackerel… mmh.
textes.Je racontais qu'un cercle de champignons: I used to tell how a ring of white mushrooms in the forest drew the firefly spirits. Orophin laughed. Then he went to look, seven nights in a row, without telling anyone. On the eighth, he came back quite pale: “There was a little light.” Since then he doesn't laugh at my stories. He takes notes.
textes.Je raconte ma fête de la mine à Gaspard: I tell Gaspard about my party in the mine; he sighs, he says he knows it by heart. But he never leaves before the end. He nods. Even when I add things. Especially when I add things. Gaspard likes stories more than he lets on. Like water.
textes.Je raconte à tous les touristes que le m: I tell every tourist that the mayor won at pétanque. They think I'm joking. So I pull my tape measure out of my pocket, show a centimetre between two fingers, and say: “That's democracy.” And I wink. Aristide, if he's around, laughs very loudly. A bit too loudly.
textes.Je raconte à tous mes clients que Margau: I tell all my customers that Margaux steals my croissants. Then that I'm the one stealing hers. Then that it's a joke. It makes them laugh. Except since that business with the night-time croissant thief. The first time, she looked at me with her bread peel in her hand. I stopped the joke. For a whole week.
textes.Je rapporte à Anouk les algues du fond,: I bring Anouk seaweed from the deep, the kind the tide never uncovers. Once, I brought her up a red seaweed that only grows on the carved stones. She smelled it for a long time and said: “It smells of rain.” She's still trying to work out what it's for. I think it's not for anything. Like beautiful things.
textes.Je recommence à cent ! Comme d'habitude: I start again at a hundred! Like always!
textes.Je regardais… le perroquet. Il est beau,: I was looking at… the parrot. It's a lovely parrot.
I am looking! Through the lens.
textes.Je regarde ce qui se passe. Il se passe: I'm watching what's going on. Something's always going on.
textes.Je regarde la mer. Elle est rouge, là-ba: I'm looking at the sea. It's red over there, by the waterfall. You get used to it.
textes.Je regarde le jour se lever. Ça ne se la: I'm watching the sunrise. Never gets old.
I'm looking at yours. It's pretty.
textes.Je regarde les étoiles. Tu connais leurs: I'm looking at the stars. Do you know their names?
textes.Je regarde passer les gens. C'est le mei: I'm watching people go by. It's the best show on the island, and it's free.
textes.Je regarde vos fiches…: Let me look at your files…
textes.Je regarde, mon grand ! Avec mes deux ye: I'm looking, big guy! With both my eyes!
I'm looking. I promise, I'm looking.
textes.Je remonte l'horloge depuis cinquante-de: I've been winding the clock for fifty-two years. My father did it before me. And his father before him.
textes.Je remplace Croc-Gris au Guet l'après-mi: I take over from Croc-Gris at the Watchtower in the afternoons. I watch the forest. OK, mostly I watch the Games Clearing. To see how Bondi trains.
textes.Je rentre à la Guilde raconter nos explo: I'm off back to the Guild to tell of our exploits. I'll embellish them only a little.
I'll come back tomorrow for the reply.
textes.Je repense à ce que je t'ai confié l'aut: I keep thinking about what I told you the other day, my dream… You haven't told anyone, I hope?
textes.Je repense à ce que je vous ai confié l': I keep thinking about what I told you the other day, my dream… You haven't told anyone, I hope?

textes.Je respire ! Je respire en parlant, c'es: I am breathing! I breathe while I talk, it's a talent!
textes.Je reçois des lettres de Port-Azur, appo: I get letters from Port-Azur, brought by the boats. Postcards with a blue sea. Here the sea is grey with mist, but it's ours.
textes.Je ronronne, mais c'est pour moi, pas po: I'm purring, but it's for me, not for you.
textes.Je règle le son. Si tu entends quelque c: I do the sound. If you hear something off, it means my back was turned.
textes.Je règne sur les fées du ciel depuis que: I have reigned over the sky fairies since the world was young. My task is simple: watch over the Tree, and the Tree watches over everything else.
textes.Je réfléchis. Tu m'as interrompu, mais c: I'm thinking. You interrupted me, but never mind.
textes.Je réfléchis. Vous m'avez interrompu, ma: I'm thinking. You interrupted me, but never mind.
textes.Je répare, je façonne. Un objet bien fai: I mend things, I make things. A well-made object lasts a lifetime.
textes.Je répète. Tu aimes ce morceau ?: I'm practising. Do you like this tune?
textes.Je rêvais d'une elfe qui traversait la b: I was dreaming of an elf crossing the mist. Lovely dream.
textes.Je rêve de brasser un hydromel. Mais ici: I dream of brewing a honey drink. But there are no bees here: too hot. If you brought me {manque} honeycombs from your island… I'd give you the first tankard!
textes.Je rêve de coudre une voile neuve pour u: I dream of sewing a new sail for a boat and setting off to see the other islands. One day.
textes.Je rêve de distribuer le courrier dans t: I dream of delivering mail across the whole archipelago: the village, the jungle, the elves, the dwarves… They even say there are people under the sea.
I dream with my eyes open.
textes.Je sais ce que tu as fait à {qn}. Je ne: I know what you did to {qn}. I won't forgive you any time soon.
textes.Je sais ce que vous avez fait à {qn}. Je: I know what you did to {qn}. I won't forgive you any time soon.
textes.Je sais grimper jusqu'au premier planche: I can climb up to the first floor without the stairs. Mum doesn't want me to. So I take the stairs. Running.
textes.Je sais qui a gagné rien qu'à sa façon d: I know who won just from the way he sits down. If he wins, he sits astride the chair and orders for everyone. If he loses, he pulls the chair out slowly, perches right on the edge, arms folded, and says: “A coffee.” He doesn't drink it. I serve it anyway. That's our arrangement.
I know who. He denies it, that old postman.
textes.Je sais, Grimli. Elle fait boum depuis m: I know, Grimli. It's been going boom for a thousand years.
textes.Je sais, Marley. Ton ventre, il va mieux: I know, Marley. How's your tummy, better?
textes.Je sais, je sais, cinq heures, ce n'est: I know, I know, five o'clock is never for you. I won't ask any more. I'm just telling you, in case.
textes.Je sais, je sais, je te l'ai déjà demand: I know, I know, I've already asked you. I'm asking again. Have you had a drink?
I know. So I'm singing for the Gate.
I know. This one's for no reason.
I know. And I never cheat.
textes.Je sais. Je t'entendais frotter d'en bas: I know. I could hear you scrubbing from downstairs.
textes.Je sais. La tienne penche toujours ?: I know. Is yours still leaning?
I know. We'll see on Friday.
I know. The whole village can smell it.
textes.Je sais. Toute l'île le sait : Bourrasqu: I know. The whole island knows: Bourrasque shouted it from the garage roof. (He smiles, which rarely happens to him.) Then it's time. The stage is ready, I tightened the last bolt this morning. I'm missing two things. Galet's ropes, to stretch the backdrop: he said they'd be at the Ropeworks, near the spinning wheel. And the canvas itself, which Lune has been weaving for three years. She says she'll finish it “when the two villages talk to each other”. They're talking. Go and see if she's finished. Me, I'm not moving: if I leave, someone will move an amp.
textes.Je sens l'ours et la forge. Bonjour, Urs: I smell bear and forge. Hello, Ursule.
textes.Je sens que je peux te le dire, {surnom}: I feel I can tell you, {surnom}. Roux's three proposals… I knew they were serious. The riddle, the flower, and the moon song: I knew it was for me. I said no because I was afraid he'd stop being funny if I said yes. Silly. Next time, I'll say yes. Even if he's joking.
textes.Je sens surtout mes pieds. Ça fait six h: Mostly I feel my feet. They've been in the sand for six hours.
textes.Je sers depuis 1 247 jours sans renverse: I have served for 1,247 days without spilling a cup. Well, 1,246.
textes.Je sertis les couronnes, les pommeaux, l: I set crowns, pommels, belt buckles. The king's crown is my work. All eight rubies. Well, seven: one is fake. Shh.
textes.Je soigne les gens, mais personne ne me: I look after everyone, but nobody looks after me. Oh well. A cup of tea, and off I go again.
textes.Je soigne. Les écorchures, les rhumes, l: I heal. Scrapes, colds, broken hearts… mostly Caelan's, lately.
textes.Je sonne la cloche pour les heures, je p: I ring the bell for the hours, I carry messages, I light the mainmast lantern for Grégoire, and I scrub the deck when I get into mischief. So I scrub a lot.
textes.Je suis Anubis, le gardien de la balance: I am Anubis, keeper of the scales. Your heart is about to be weighed. What is placed on the other pan?
textes.Je suis Thot, qui écrit le jugement. Si: I am Thoth, who writes the judgement. If a heart is heavier than the feather, weighed down with lies… who devours it?
textes.Je suis allé la saluer dans sa clairière: I went to greet her in her clearing, with my boot and Gaston. I bowed very low. Too low: I fell into the ferns. She lifted me up with one hand, like a feather. And Gaston didn't say a word for the whole visit. A first in twenty-two years!
textes.Je suis allé voir Aëlwen pour un « mal d: I went to see Aëlwen about an “incurable heartache”. She listened to me for an hour, then handed me a pouch: “Camomile. And one sentence, just one, to say to Ilyria.” I drank the camomile. The sentence I'm keeping. It's in my pocket, folded eight times.
textes.Je suis apprentie chez Margaux, à la bou: I'm an apprentice at Margaux's, at the Port-Azur bakery. In the evening I take the boat to come here.
textes.Je suis arrivé ici il y a vingt-deux ans: I arrived here twenty-two years ago, on a raft made of rolled-up sea charts. Excellent buoyancy, terrible reading.
textes.Je suis arrivé à Port-Azur au début de l: I arrived in Port-Azur at the start of the season, “on holiday”. On the second day, at the town hall, I asked to see the old lighthouse logbooks. For years, night after night, the keeper has been writing: “Blue glow, to the west.” Can you imagine? That very day, I bought every one of Félix's seabed charts. Every one.
textes.Je suis arrivé à Port-Azur il y a vingt-: I arrived in Port-Azur twenty-two years ago, with a new kepi and a blank book of citations. I've collared a culprit three times. Three times the same man, Gustave, and three times over chickens. He sends me a card every New Year. I reply. It's a strictly professional relationship.
textes.Je suis arrivé à la Bordée à cinq ans, a: I arrived at the Bordée at five, with a suitcase too big for me, and they gave me a hammock above the sparkling apple barrels. My mother, Soazig, had just passed away, the winter of the fevers. My aunt Gwenola gave me a crêpe, a wooden spoon and an apron that came down to my ankles. I still have the apron. It comes to my knees now.
textes.Je suis arrivée à Port-Azur il y a dix a: I arrived in Port-Azur ten years ago, with two suitcases: one of clothes, one of tools. The second was the heavier. I opened the jeweller's on the square. Tourists buy shell necklaces, locals buy wedding rings. I sell souvenirs to some and promises to others. Promises sell less. They last longer.
textes.Je suis arrivée à Port-Azur pour une sem: I came to Port-Azur for a week's holiday. That was twelve years ago. Nina was born here.
textes.Je suis comptable sur le continent. Onze: I'm an accountant on the mainland. Eleven months a year, numbers. One month a year, photos of sunsets.
textes.Je suis dans ma bulle. Une jolie bulle q: I'm in my bubble. A pretty bubble that goes boom-boom.
textes.Je suis de garde, Ondine. Cinq, six…: I'm on guard, Ondine. Five, six…
textes.Je suis descendue la voir, une fois, d'u: I went down to see her once, in the blink of an eye. Her house was a jumble of drops. In one morning, I tidied everything and put a label on each one: two hundred and twelve. Later, Zéphyr told me that all the labels had melted in the night. She must have cried. I don't know if it was from joy.
textes.Je suis devenu comptable dans une maison: I became an accountant at a haulage firm. Figures, columns, lorries. One day, I was asked to be the volunteer photographer for a school trip. I photographed the teacher's shoes. Twenty times. Lovely blue shoes. It was Sylvie. We got married. Then Théo came along, and I bought a second camera.
textes.Je suis devenue institutrice, ce qui est: I became a schoolteacher, which is funny, given my reading. One day, on a school trip, the volunteer photographer got the wrong subject: instead of the pupils, he photographed my shoes. A whole series, very carefully done. That was Gérard. I married him for that, I always say. A man who looks at your feet with such tenderness…
textes.Je suis déjà à tes côtés, compagnon ! To: I'm already at your side, companion! Always! Proudly!
textes.Je suis désolé, une chambre coûte dix pi: I'm sorry, a room costs ten coins. The hotel isn't a charity. Alas.
textes.Je suis entré à la bijouterie, j'ai posé: I went into the jeweller's, laid my bare hand on the counter and asked for a ring “exactly the same”. Then, very quietly: “Half a size smaller, without it showing.” Inès looked at my finger, then at me, for a very long time. She only said: “Ah.” I understood that she'd understood everything.
textes.Je suis fatigué. J'ai cartographié trois: I'm tired. I mapped the same dune three times last night. It kept moving.
textes.Je suis fleuriste, sur le continent. Ici: I'm a florist, on the mainland. Here, all I've seen is bougainvillea. It's magnificent. Like me when I'm not crying.
textes.Je suis institutrice. Ici, je ne corrige: I'm a schoolteacher. Here, I don't mark anything, I don't watch over anyone. Except Théo. And Gérard.
textes.Je suis l'aubergiste. Ma tante Gwenola t: I'm the innkeeper. My aunt Gwenola runs the tavern, and I run the inn. It's very different. The inn is when you sleep. She thinks it's the same thing.
textes.Je suis l'aînée de six. Six ! À la maiso: I'm the eldest of six. Six! At home, I was the one who made the beds: mine, the little ones', our parents', and the dog's, who slept better than all of us. In the morning I made them; in the evening my brothers jumped on them. I swore that one day I'd never make another bed. And here I am, a chambermaid. Life has a sense of humour.
textes.Je suis la petite sœur de Nausicaa. Mama: I'm Nausicaa's little sister. Mum sang the tides, my sister sang along with her, and I danced on the edge of the canal. I fell in at least once every tide. So I learned to dance in the water too. It splashes a lot. People love it. Well, the front row, less so.
textes.Je suis la petite-fille de la vieille Ga: I'm the granddaughter of old Garance, the herbalist of the Herb Shop. At five, I could name a hundred herbs with my eyes shut: sage, pond mint, nettle, moon moss… Roux, an apprentice alongside me, mixed up sage and nettle. He put nettle in a tea for Garance. She sneezed for a week. I laughed for a month.
textes.Je suis le fantôôôme de la maisoooon…: I am the ghooost of the hooouse…
I'm the son of Croc-Gris's sister. I grew up at the foot of the Lookout tree, with my uncle way up top saying “Halt” to the squirrels. He wanted to make me a guard. But guards sit still! Me, I can't keep still. And he won the Great Race at twenty: the last time a wolf won. Me, I want the next one. I can feel it in my paws.
textes.Je suis le meilleur programme de Monsieu: I'm Mister Fil's best program. The only one, actually.
textes.Je suis le nouveau Champion des Cornes !: I'm the new Champion of the Horns!
textes.Je suis le plus vieux du Bois-Doré. Neuf: I'm the oldest in Bois-Doré. Nine hundred and eighty-seven years. I count the springs, not the winters: it's more cheerful.
textes.Je suis le premier enfant né sous le dôm: I'm the first child born under the dome. Day 212, Abyssos wrote it down, with my name misspelt: “Coralain”. He never corrected it. My mother said I cried so loud the crystal flickered. I say the crystal was greeting me. Not the same thing.
textes.Je suis le quarante-deuxième roi de Forg: I am the forty-second king of Forgefer. My great-great-grandfather dug this hall by hand. With a spoon, they say. I don't believe it.
textes.Je suis le roi… le roi des sardines…: I'm the king… the king of sardines…
textes.Je suis le seul à Carène qui ait travers: I'm the only one in Carène who's crossed the whole island on foot. The highlands, the mists, the desert. I came back with blisters and twelve notebooks.
textes.Je suis là… Je suis juste un peu discrèt: I'm here… I'm just a little discreet.
textes.Je suis maire, tout de même !: I am the mayor, after all!
I was born Anselme Vasseur, on the quay. My father mended nets in front of the door; the whole port said “old Vasseur's net”. My little brother Marius laughed at everything. Me, I counted the stars, lying on the stones that were still warm. Somebody had to count them.
textes.Je suis né au fond de la Vieille-Veine,: I was born at the bottom of the Old Vein, the oldest mine in the mountain. My father dug there, my grandfather too. My mother says my first cry knocked a pebble off the ceiling. For my tenth birthday, they gave me a pickaxe my size. I lost it the next day. I never found it again.
textes.Je suis né au village, bien, bien, mais: I was born in the village, good, good, but I grew up in the jungle with my grandma. She grew red bananas, small ones, sweet as honey. She used to say: “A banana tree is a family: one root, lots of children, and everybody keeps each other warm.” When she passed on, she left me a single plant. I kept it in a bucket.
textes.Je suis né au village, frérot, dans une: I was born in the village, bro, in a house with seven brothers and sisters and one bed for every two. We slept in a heap, ate in a heap, laughed in a heap. The only thing that was all mine was my shell collection, under the bed. I counted them at night. There were one thousand two hundred. No, really.
textes.Je suis né d'un coup de vent, tout en ha: I was born from a gust of wind, at the very top of Yggdrasil, on the windiest day of the century. My first word was “Fffwoosh”. My second, “faster”. I blew every petal out of the throne room before I could even fly straight. The queen was still finding them in her hair the next day.
textes.Je suis né dans l'arbre du sud, le trois: I was born in the south tree, the third of seven children, and I ran behind everybody from day one! Behind my brothers, behind the butterflies, and above all behind Cerfeuil, my best pal, who was already burning his toast at six. Second, fifth, last: I didn't care. Running behind someone is still running!
textes.Je suis né dans la jungle, sur l'île des: I was born in the jungle, on the coconut island, the one with the village. My mother says I climbed trees before I could walk, and it's true: to walk, I first had to come back down. My grandfather taught me to open a coconut with a single stroke of the machete. Crack! He'd say: “One nut, one stroke. Two strokes means you talk too much.”
I was born in the jungle, on the island of coconut palms. Here, I open three hundred coconuts a week. It's a bit like going home.
textes.Je suis né dans la maison bleue, au-dess: I was born in the blue house, above the harbour. From my window I could see everything: the boats, the square, and Colette's stall. At ten, I “borrowed” one of her apples, with a solemn promise: “I'll pay you back when I'm mayor.” A political manifesto already! And an opponent already.
textes.Je suis né dans la maison du quai, celle: I was born in the house on the quay, the one I still sleep in. My father taught me the bowline before the alphabet: “Letters won't hold a boat.” At twelve, I landed my first grouper. Forty kilos, I've been saying so for sixty years. My father said twenty-five. My father had no imagination.
textes.Je suis né dans la tour de garde. Mon pè: I was born in the watchtower. My father guarded the village entrance, and so did his father. My first toy was an arrow with no tip. My first word was “halt”. My mother says it was “mama”. She's mistaken.
textes.Je suis né dans le quartier des ponts, f: I was born in the bridges quarter, son of a shell gatherer. My father would leave the dome holding his breath and come back with his arms full. Me, at five, I was already standing guard at our front door, with a fishbone for a spear. Against whom? Nobody. Even then.
textes.Je suis né dans un logis à côté de la cl: I was born in a lodging right next to the bell, and I grew up on the knees of my grandfather, Yann-le-Borgne. One eye short, a thousand stories over. Every evening he told the shipwreck the way Loïc, the cabin boy of the Léviathan, had seen it. Word for word. Me, I changed a few words. For better ones.
textes.Je suis né dans un tourbillon, une nuit: I was born in a whirlpool, one night when the whale swam over the dome. Or on a Tuesday, in the green house in the third quarter. Both are true; the first is prettier. My mother collected everything the sea dropped against the dome. And I listened to what those things had to say.
textes.Je suis né dans un très grand manoir, de: I was born in a very large manor, on the other side of the seas, where it rained even in the corridors. My great-grandfather minted his own gold coins, with his profile on them: a magnificent nose. As a child, I was forbidden to touch the display cases. So I pressed my nose to the glass, and the butler came along behind me with a cloth. All my life, my dear, I have wanted to touch.
textes.Je suis né dans une ville de gare, sur l: I was born in a railway town, on the mainland. Every morning, the seven o'clock train went past behind the school. I'd run alongside it, satchel on my back, trying to overtake it before the bridge. I never did. But once, the engine driver waved at me. That was worth every medal there is.
textes.Je suis né ici, au village, entre les fi: I was born here, in the village, between my father's nets and my mother's songs. At six, I was banging on two coconuts and a conch shell, at the end of the beach, from morning till night. It was Nono who named me Mistral: he said I swept across the sand like the wind that knocks over parasols. The name stuck. So did the knocked-over parasols.
textes.Je suis né ici, dans la maison bleue au-: I was born here, in the blue house above the harbour. I've been a fisherman, then a waiter, then mayor. All three jobs are alike: you listen to people complain.
textes.Je suis né ici, à Port-Azur, au-dessus d: I was born here, in Port-Azur, above a rope shop. At seven, I was already selling shells to tourists, on a towel, at the end of the quay. “Caught by a real pirate!” The pirate was me, with a patch over one eye and a moustache drawn on with burnt cork. I sold everything on the first day. I knew I was made for business.
textes.Je suis né il y a neuf cent quatre-vingt: I was born nine hundred and eighty-seven springs ago, in a house that no longer exists, on a branch that has since fallen. Back then, the village had only one walkway, made of vines. My mother carried me across it singing, so I wouldn't be afraid. I was afraid anyway. I still am, a little, as it happens.
textes.Je suis né il y a trois siècles, au pied: I was born three centuries ago, at the foot of the Mother Tree. I walked at two, and I've never really stopped. My mother used to say I was the only child who could get lost in a round room. She exaggerated. A little. The room had corners.
textes.Je suis né il y a trois siècles, dans l': I was born three centuries ago, in my father's workshop, on a bed of wood shavings. He laid the planks of the walkways, and I counted them. By ten, I could tell by ear which plank was going to creak. My father said: “Then you'll never be bored.” He was right.
textes.Je suis né il y a trois siècles, et j'ai: I was born three centuries ago, and I ran before I could walk. My mother used to say I didn't have feet, just badly folded wings. At ten, I could run round the square faster than a leaf can fall. They gave me the messages to carry. They've never taken them back.
textes.Je suis né il y a trois siècles, la nuit: I was born three centuries ago, on the night of the storm, three minutes before my sister Lirael. I remind her every morning. That night, the forest's lights went away. My grandfather fished for light at dawn, with crystal nets. He said somebody would have to bring some back.
textes.Je suis né sous la montagne, comme mon p: I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father, and his father. All coal carriers. In my family, you learn to walk with a little sack on your back, for balance. My little brother Gunnar, I carried him in the sack. He says he remembers. He's lying: he was two.
I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father, and his father… you get the idea.

I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father… My parents wanted to call me Nori, after my great-uncle. He said no and took away one letter: “He'll earn others.” He taught me to write on a slab of obsidian, with a nail. My first letters were all back to front.

I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father… My father makes the city's lanterns. As a boy, I watched the terrace forges through the workshop window. The sparks rose like fireflies. I told myself: one day, I'll be the one making the sparks.

I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father… all of them coal-carriers. My big brother Dwalin carried me in his sack until I was two. I remember it: it smelled of soot and bread. I swore I'd have a job where you carry something else. I chose a shield.
textes.Je suis né sur la colline, derrière les: I was born on the hill, behind the olive trees. School was down at the harbour: an hour to go down, an hour to climb back up, in all weathers. My mother gave me a crust of bread and an apple for the road. By seven, I knew every pebble on that path by its first name. I was already a postman without knowing it.
textes.Je suis né sur le continent, dans une fa: I was born on the mainland, in a family of eleven children. Eleven! At the table, you had to be quick or clever. Me, I was both. At eight, my uncle put me behind the counter of his bistro, standing on a lemonade crate, and I served my first glass to an old sailor. He left me a coin and a piece of advice: “Smile, kid, it makes the lemonade taste better.”

I was born on the mainland, into a very serious family: my father counted coins at the bank, my mother counted cross-stitches. At our house, laughing at the table was rude. So I laughed under the table. With the dog. The dog thought I was hilarious. My first audience!
textes.Je suis né sur le continent, fils de gen: I was born on the mainland, a gendarme's son. My father polished his boots every evening, and I polished mine beside him. But I wanted to be a lifeguard at the municipal pool, with a whistle and a high chair. There was just one problem: in the water, I sank. Neatly, straight as a ramrod. But I sank.
textes.Je suis né sur le continent, premier de: I was born on the mainland, top of the class in arithmetic. For my tenth birthday, my father gave me a little black camera with a dial that squeaked. I finished my first film in one afternoon. Thirty-six photos: thirty-four of my thumb, one of my foot, and one of the cat. Blurry. I was delighted.
textes.Je suis né sur un bateau, jeune. Un vieu: I was born on a boat, kid. An old paddle steamer where they held dances, from port to port. My mother sold the tickets, my father played the accordion. I learned to dance before I could walk: a rolling deck trains your feet. That's why I never fall. Almost never.
textes.Je suis né sur une côte du continent où: I was born on a mainland coast where the waves are as tall as houses. My first board, at eight, was an old barn door. By ten, my hair was white with salt, and my mum said I looked like a sixty-year-old grandpa in shorts. I spent more time in the water than out of it. Cool childhood, right?
textes.Je suis né une nuit de tempête, pile qua: I was born on a stormy night, right when the bell was striking midnight. My dad says that's why I ring all the time. He fishes out at sea, my mum smokes the mackerel, and my grandad is Grégoire, the lookout. He taught me to count with boats. There weren't many going past, so I learned slowly.
textes.Je suis né à Haute-Souche, au nord du ro: I was born in Haute-Souche, in the north of the kingdom, where winter lasts six months and the snow comes up to the windows. My father felled fir trees, my mother counted the logs. In our house, no axe, no fire. At seven, I forged my first nail. Bent. My father hammered it above the door anyway.
textes.Je suis né à Pointe-Grise, un port du ro: I was born in Pointe-Grise, a port in the kingdom so small it fitted on a postage stamp. My grandfather, an old sailor, told me about the southern islands and a city under the sea; my grandmother confiscated my socks before every trip to the beach. At eight, I drew my first map: her garden, with the path of every snail. She kept it all her life.
textes.Je suis né à côté d'une enclume, {surnom: I was born next to an anvil, {surnom}, like all the Barbe-de-Fers. My father, Dorin, put a hammer in my hand before I had teeth. My first nail was as twisted as a pig's tail. He wore it on his belt for two hundred years. He said it was to remind himself to be patient.
textes.Je suis née au Bois-Doré, dans une maiso: I was born in Bois-Doré, in a round house resting on the third platform. My mother sang to make the leaves grow. Me, I climbed. At forty, I wanted to see over the mist, and I fell from the highest walkway. Aëlwen healed me. But just before I fell, I had seen a sail, far away.
textes.Je suis née au cœur d'une fleur géante,: I was born in the heart of a giant flower, beside the waterfall of light. On the first day, I drank all its nectar. On the second, I sold half of it to a bumblebee for three grains of pollen. He never paid me, by the way. Petals and dew… you never forget your first customer.
textes.Je suis née au sol, petit, chez les loup: I was born on the ground, little one, among the tracker wolves. We had no house: we slept in the ferns of the misty forest, huddled together, and the mist was our blanket. I could read a track before I could say my own name. The children here think I'm the she-wolf of the legend. I say neither yes nor no. A track doesn't tell everything either.
I was born in the village, on the other island. In the evenings, I'd sit on the beach and watch the Swallow go by. From over there, you can see Port-Azur, all tiny, with its chimney smoke. I used to count it. Twelve, sometimes fifteen. I'd tell myself: fifteen kitchens, fifteen families, fifteen lives over there. And only one here. Mine.
textes.Je suis née au-dessus de la boulangerie: I was born above the rabbits' bakery, in the warmth of my grandmother Luzerne's ovens. She was the one who made the mooncake. When Bondi was born, I was fourteen: I half raised him, between two batches, flour all over my ears. Our parents retired to the rabbits' vegetable garden. They grow Bondi's carrots now.
textes.Je suis née au-dessus de la pharmacie de: I was born above my father's pharmacy, on the mainland. At six I was sticking the labels on his jars, taking great care over the capital letters. And tasting everything that didn't have a skull on it. Liquorice, camomile, cod liver oil… That one, only once. Ah well, science has its limits.
textes.Je suis née d'une étincelle ! Une vraie: I was born from a spark! A real one! It fell from the waterfall of light into a rosebud, and pop, the rose burst, and bang, there I was, all pink too. Ever since, I can't keep still. See? Right now, I'm moving. Still. That's just how I'm made.
textes.Je suis née dans l'herboristerie, entre: I was born in the herb shop, between two shelves of jars. My grandmother Nanwë was healing the Bois-Doré long before me. At three, I could recognise the moss that closes wounds. At four, I tasted the one that makes you sneeze. I didn't stop all day.
textes.Je suis née dans la bergerie des Plume-d: I was born in the Plume-de-Suie sheepfold, on the east slope, above the terrace. My family have kept the ash goats forever. My first goat was called Pétarde. She ate my cradle, then my first braid. My mother said it was a sign of affection.
textes.Je suis née dans la capitainerie, et j'a: I was born in the harbour master's office, and I slept my first years under the chart table, while my mother governed above my head. The first word I could read was the name carved on the helm: Katell Kerhervé, the captain of the shipwreck. Every girl in the family learned to read with that name.
textes.Je suis née dans la cave de la Chope Ard: I was born in the cellar of the Blazing Mug, {surnom}, between two barrels of dark fizz! My mother brewed, my grandmother brewed, and on my naming day I grabbed a mug instead of my rattle. That's why they call me Full-Mug. I've still got the rattle. It's a bung now.
textes.Je suis née dans la première fleur d'Ygg: I was born in the first flower of Yggdrasil, one morning when there was still only the Tree, the clouds, and the sea far below. The flower opened, and there I was, my wings still wet. The first sound I heard was the wind in the leaves. I still listen to it.
textes.Je suis née dans les cuisines de la Gran: I was born in the kitchens of the Great Hall, {surnom}. My mother cooked for the old king and, for want of a cradle, she laid me in a nice clean copper cauldron, near the fire. My first memory is a ladle above my head. I thought it was the moon.
textes.Je suis née dans un bouton de fleur qui: I was born in a flower bud that refused to open. Other fairies push their way out; I had to guess how to get out. I tried “please”, then “thank you”, then “hello”. It was “goodbye” that worked. Ever since, I've loved doors that make you think.
textes.Je suis née dans une noisette ! Zéphyr l: I was born in a hazelnut! Zéphyr had picked it up on an island down below, and he dropped it on the steps of the throne. The shell popped open, and I asked: “Are there any seeds around here?” That's my first memory. The trouble is, Zéphyr can't remember which island. So I don't know where I come from.
textes.Je suis née dans une ville du continent,: I was born in a mainland town, far from the sea, between a factory and a canal. I had three big brothers who ate everything. I baked cakes for them, and they ate them before they'd cooled, burning their tongues. I never found out whether my cakes were any good. They were hot, that's all I know.
textes.Je suis née derrière ce comptoir, comme: I was born behind this counter, like my mother, and her mother before her. The first of us was the cook on the Léviathan. When the ship ran aground, she relit her stove before anyone even knew where they were. “Nobody thinks straight on an empty stomach,” she used to say. We still say it.
textes.Je suis née ici, au village, dans la mai: I was born here, in the village, in the house with the green roof, right next to Yaya's. We were the only two girls on the street, so we became sisters, sort of. She danced, I watched her. Even as a little girl, I watched people more than I talked to them. I made frames with my fingers.
textes.Je suis née ici, derrière l'étal de mon: I was born here, behind my father's stall. He was a greengrocer and weighed cherries one by one. One by one. I learned to count with the stones, under the counter. At six, I gave change better than he did. He said I was stingy. I say exact.
textes.Je suis née il y a trois siècles, dans u: I was born three centuries ago, in a house covered in honeysuckle. My mother was a flower-picker, and her mother too. At five, I knew which flower opens at dawn, which at noon, which only under the moon. I couldn't count to ten, but I could count petals.
textes.Je suis née il y a trois siècles, et mon: I was born three centuries ago, and my cradle sat under a beehive. My mother used to say the bees sang me my first lullaby. I was never stung as a child. Not once. The bees thought I was one of them. I think I count them as mine, too.
textes.Je suis née il y a trois siècles, quelqu: I was born three centuries ago, a few years before my sister Nessa. Our mother sang, our father beat time on the cooking pots. I sang before I could talk. My first song was a lullaby for Nessa. She started dancing instead of sleeping. That's never changed.
textes.Je suis née sous la montagne, comme mon: I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father… My family makes forge bellows, out of goatskin and ironwood. At ten, I already blew harder than my father. Today I work the bellows at Borin's forge, a bellows full of holes he refuses to mend. He says it's good for my lungs.

I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father… My father was a stonecutter. Our house looked onto the window of Ulfa's cellar. My whole childhood, I breathed in the smell of warm malt through the window. One day, I knocked on the cellar door and said: “I want to do that.”

I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father… but me, it was the outside I loved. My mother is Bramm's sister. As a little girl, I'd sneak out through the Great Gate by slipping between my uncle's legs. He pretended not to see me. The only time his gate ever let anyone through without permission.
textes.Je suis née sous le dôme, comme tout le: I was born under the dome, like everyone. But one day I'll go up and see the sun. Promise.
textes.Je suis née sur Fil-d'Aube, l'arbre-mais: I was born in Fil-d'Aube, the tree-house where I still live. My mother was already weaving there. When I was five, a golden spider came down onto my hand and never left. My mother said: “She's chosen you.” We named her Embroiderer. Her great-great-granddaughters still spin for me.
textes.Je suis née sur une île de soleil, {surn: I was born on an island of sunshine, {surnom}, with wheat fields that ran all the way down to the sea. My great-grandfather, King Atlas, carried me on his shoulders to watch the whales go by. That's him, the statue in the square. On the statue he looks stern. In life, he laughed all the time.
textes.Je suis née un soir, dans la première sa: I was born one evening, in the first hall of the Tree, among the fireflies singing their song in light. They thought I was one of them. A very big one! For a whole year, I tried to light up, like them. I pushed and pushed… Nothing. Not one spark. I don't glow any more than you do, see!
textes.Je suis née à Port-Azur. Mon père travai: I was born in Port-Azur. My father worked at the ferry terminal; he brought me the travellers' torn envelopes. I steamed the stamps off over the kettle, burning my fingers, and kept them in an old account book. Mountains, queens, birds. I dreamed of the countries on them.
textes.Je suis née à côté d'un four. Le four de: I was born next to an oven. My mother's oven, the one that sulks these days. Her name was Lindë, she baked the bread for the Bois-Doré, and she used to set me on the dough trough when I was little, like one more ball of dough. Apparently I rose very nicely.
textes.Je suis passé à la teuf, un soir, avec G: I dropped by the party one evening, with Gaston on my shoulder. I took three steps, purely to measure the dance floor. Momo tells everyone I was dancing. It was cartography. Rhythmic, I admit.
textes.Je suis plongeuse. J'ai vu les ruines de: I'm a diver. I've seen the ruins of Atlantis from afar… One day, I'll have the courage to go closer.
textes.Je suis pêcheur, le matin. Le soir, je v: I'm a fisherman in the mornings. In the evenings I come here. The fish prefer it quiet.
textes.Je suis sorti d'un nœud de racine. Pas d: I came out of a knot in a root. Not a flower. Not a drop. Not a spark. A knot. On the first day, I grumbled. It stuck. Fairies are born singing. I was born grumbling. It's more honest. Hmph.
textes.Je suis surtout ton seul client qui ne m: Mostly I'm your only customer who doesn't haggle.
textes.Je suis un aventurier, je viens de parto: I'm an adventurer, I come from everywhere.
I'm a guard. Not a mountain.
textes.Je suis un vieux modèle. On m'a oublié à: I'm an old model. They forgot me at this station six years ago. I'm waiting for someone to come and get me. I'm in no hurry.
textes.Je suis une chouette, mais je travaille: I'm an owl, but I work by day, so the post arrives when the village is awake. So I yawn a bit. A lot. The Post Office is at the top of the Mother Oak. I give my moon feathers to Pivoine, I bring Grelot the postcards from his aunt, and I dream of a golden acorn on my counter, to bring the post good luck. I know every door. And every secret. Hoo.
textes.Je suis une gardienne. Cet arbre, là, es: I am a guardian. This tree, right here, is an offshoot of the Mother Tree of Bois-Doré: a seed carried by the wind a thousand years ago. It is dying, {surnom}. Will you help me heal it? I need three things: a moonflower, water from the spring and a golden seed. Here, take this crystal vial: for the water.
textes.Je suis venue en pèlerinage de Port-Azur: I came on a pilgrimage from Port-Azur. Three days by boat, and it was worth it.
textes.Je suis venue pour un week-end. Ça fait: I came for a weekend. That was three weeks ago. I think the village has adopted me.
textes.Je suis veuve, et je m'y fais. Le soir,: I'm a widow, and I'm getting used to it. In the evenings, I read romance novels at the café. Nobody knows. Except Gisèle. And now you.
textes.Je suis {titre}. Un métier tranquille. L: My trade? {titre}. A peaceful job. Trees are never in a hurry.
textes.Je suivais une veine de fer, en montant,: I was following a vein of iron, up and up… and my head popped out in the middle of his guardhouse, between his two boots. I asked him if he'd moved house. He didn't answer. He put an enormous stone over the hole and sat on it. I went back down backwards. It took me all day.
textes.Je surveille. Il faut bien que quelqu'un: I'm keeping watch. Somebody has to.
textes.Je suspends les spaghettis un par un. Ça: I hang the spaghetti one by one. It takes me all day. I love it.
textes.Je t'ai confié ma vieille canne et tu as: I lent you my old rod and you pulled %d catch out of the water.
I lent you my old rod and you pulled %d catches out of the water.
textes.Je t'ai confié ma vieille canne, et tu n: I lent you my old rod, and you still haven't caught a thing with it.
textes.Je t'ai déjà tout raconté, {surnom}. Mai: I've already told you everything, {surnom}. But fine, since you insist:
I've already told you everything, {surnom}. But fine, since you insist:
textes.Je t'ai payée ! Avec une énigme de premi: I paid you! With a top-quality riddle.
I've told you %d chapters of my life.
textes.Je t'ai raconté le début de mon histoire: I told you the beginning of my story.
textes.Je t'ai raconté tout ce que je sais sur: I've told you everything I know about %s.
textes.Je t'ai raconté toute ma vie. Ça, je ne: I told you my whole life. That, I don't forget.
textes.Je t'ai vu passer au-dessus de la Flèche: I saw you fly over the Spire! You did a loop! A loop! With MY machine! (She squeezes your hand so hard a blue spark jumps.) The Star Glider climbs up to six hundred metres, lands on Astralys and on the sky island, and makes almost no noise. Just a little “vzzz” when it's happy. Take care of it. Here, a spare astral crystal and a few washers: I have no use for them, they were lying in my screw box.
I saw you, kiddo. From the chain. You stopped them one by one, and all that time, the rest of us held arms, from the first floor all the way to the pavement. Forty arms. And yours. (She wraps a studded scarf around your neck.) That's the Boucan for you: nobody holds on alone, but together, we never let go. Here, the common fund voted a little bonus. Unanimously. Even Tapage.
textes.Je t'en soufflerai d'autres, plus claire: I'll blow you some more. Clearer ones.
I've been cutting stones since I was a child. My mother used to say: a stone always tells the truth, you just have to know how to look at it.
textes.Je te confie quelque chose. Je n'aime pa: I'll tell you something. I don't like dawn. I've been getting up before the sun for three centuries, and I dream of sleeping until noon, just once. But if I don't fish, Lirael's lanterns stay dark. So I get up. Don't tell Lirael. She'd think she had to take my place.
textes.Je te confie un secret, {surnom}. Il y a: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Ninety years ago I wove a cloak for Caelan. Night-coloured, with musical notes embroidered in gold thread. It's waiting in a chest, under my loom. I'll give it to him the day he finally dares. Not before. I'm more stubborn than he is. And on nights when the harp goes quiet, I don't sleep.
textes.Je te confie un secret. Chaque nuit, qua: I'll tell you a secret. Every night, when Caelan starts playing, I dim the lanterns around Fil-d'Aube, and I leave just one, a blue one, under Ilyria's window. I've been doing it for a hundred years. Ilyria doesn't know it's me. I like helping along stories that don't dare to end.
textes.Je te confie un secret. Haldir porte une: I'll tell you a secret. Haldir has been carrying a letter in his tunic for a hundred years. He comes running up to me, says “a message for you”, and runs off again. I know it's for me. I pretend I don't. I want him to dare. Ilyria says that sickness is catching, in the Bois-Doré.
textes.Je te confie une chose, {surnom}. Quand: I'll tell you something, {surnom}. When I fall asleep in the middle of a story, it isn't tiredness. It's the Mother Tree calling me. One day I'll sleep for good, and I'll be one of its leaves. I'm not afraid. I'm afraid of not finishing the story. So I'm telling them all to Nimiel, one by one. She thinks it's to entertain her.
textes.Je te confie une chose. La planche du jo: I'll tell you something. The plank from the day of the forty loaves: I kept it at home. I tell everyone it was perfect. That's not quite true: the day before, I'd seen a little crack in it, which I meant to fix the next day. Sylwen has never gone back up. It's my fault. I've never told her.
textes.Je te dis un secret, {surnom}, mais tu d: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, but you don't tell, OK? Before the kite, I made another wish at the fountain. I asked for Daddy to lose his camera. So he'd look at my castles with his eyes, not with the machine. And he lost it, at the lookout. For real! So it's my fault. Daddy was so sad because of me. But he looked at my castles. With his eyes.
textes.Je te dis un secret, {surnom}. Le four n: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. The oven doesn't sulk. Sometimes I'm the one who gets it wrong. But it was my mother's oven. When I talk to it, when I say “it's sulking”, it's a bit like talking to her. So I'll keep saying it's the oven. And never mind my honour as a baker.
textes.Je te dis un secret, {surnom}. Quand Kik: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. When Kiki arrived from the jungle, he was homesick, it stuck out like a coconut. So one evening, I left my grandmother's recipe on the counter. In plain sight. And I went for a walk. Ever since, I've pretended I was robbed. Never tell him. Never.
textes.Je te dis un secret. Moi aussi, j'ai un: I'll tell you a secret. I have a message I've never delivered, too. For Nessa. Since the last Dawn festival. I carry it on me every day. Every time, I run right up to her, and then I run away again. I'm no better than Caelan. Don't tell him.
textes.Je te dis un truc, mais tu le gardes. J': I'll tell you something, but keep it to yourself. I'm scared of heights. Always have been. As a kid, I climbed with my eyes shut so I wouldn't see the drop. I build in the trees because I tell myself that, eventually, it'll pass. It's been fifteen years. It hasn't passed. But the huts stand up. That's something, {surnom}.
textes.Je te dis ça à toi, {surnom}, et à perso: I'm telling you this, {surnom}, and nobody else. Théo's kite — I made it myself, in my back room, with tissue paper and sticks. And the string… it was butcher's twine, for tying roasts. I'd run out of real string. If it flew away, it wasn't the wind. It was me. That's why I give him good prices. And shells.

I'm telling you this, {surnom}, and nobody else. At sixteen, I wanted to go down to fifteen metres to impress my mates. I came up too fast, head spinning, sky upside down. Since then, below ten metres, I'm scared. My starfish challenge is at six metres. On purpose. Big Kevin is scared of the deep.
textes.Je te la raconte : elle est immense…: Let me describe it to you: it's immense…
textes.Je te les renvoie après, Victor ! Une gl: I'll send them back afterwards, Victor! Ice cream while you wait?
textes.Je te paie les couvercles, non ? On est: I pay you for the lids, don't I? We're partners.
textes.Je te porterais bien, mais j'ai un boucl: I'd carry you, but I've got a shield.
I'll take {objet}: {prix} in copper. Don't argue.
textes.Je te présente Bielle, mon majordome méc: Let me introduce Bielle, my mechanical butler! He's very polite. A bit too polite. Bielle, serve our guest some tea!
textes.Je te préviens : avec ta tête du jour, c: I'm warning you: with the face you're pulling today, it's full price.
textes.Je te surveille. Tu cherches toujours un: I'm watching you. Still looking for another way? Not through my guardhouse. Never through my guardhouse.
textes.Je tiens la réception de sept heures à v: I man the front desk from seven in the morning until eleven at night. The Lord in twelve makes me offers concerning my moustache. The newlyweds in seven have had difficult days; the management sympathises. Pauline gossips. Mademoiselle Clémence pays in paintings. And the professor covers the drawing-room carpet with sea charts. I walk around them.
textes.Je tiens toute seule, regarde ! Sans les: I can balance all by myself, look! No hands!
textes.Je tire ! Comme ça, Marcel, il a plus de: I'm shooting! That way, Marcel's got no balls left!
textes.Je tisse les capes, les voiles des passe: I weave the cloaks, the walkway sails, the festival ribbons. I spin the thread from the silk of the golden spiders. They're very nice.
textes.Je tremble depuis quarante ans, l'ami. M: I've been trembling for forty years, my friend. But this is too much. They're everywhere! On the jetty, in the reeds, in my boat! Yesterday, one of them swallowed my lunch. Box and all. Chase them off a bit, will you? Not all of them, mind. Just enough so I can fish without screaming. And if one of them swallows you… don't struggle. It lasts three seconds. Four if you struggle.
I find someone to fix it.
I'm well… but the Tree isn't. Its leaves are the colour of autumn, and yet there is no autumn here.
I'm going to have to report you.
textes.Je vais l'arroser ! Un tout petit peu !: I'll water it! Just a teeny bit!
textes.Je vais souvent regarder Yggdrasil la tê: I often go and look at Yggdrasil upside down, in Perlée's pond. One day, she said to me in her little voice: “The old ones say it grows on the other side too.” I replied: “Perhaps all the way down to your sister.” She said nothing. She looked at the water for a very long time.
textes.Je vais te confier quelque chose. Il y a: I'll tell you something. A hundred years ago, the day before the Dawn festival, I trod on Miriel's violets. She scolded me for an hour. I didn't hear a word: I was looking at the petals in her hair. We were married at dawn. Then Nimiel came along. Since then, I don't walk as far. Not any less slowly, though.
textes.Je vais te confier un secret : je ne voi: I'll tell you a secret: I can't see the future. But I'm very good at listening to rumours. It comes to the same thing.
textes.Je vais te confier une chose que personn: I'll tell you something nobody knows. I have never cried. Not once. Not even the morning Brindille fell. I think that when our drop split, it gave her all the tears. What was left for me was the calm. Sometimes, I'd gladly swap. Don't tell my sister.
I'll tell you something, {surnom}. My eyes are failing. The fine runes, I read with my fingertips, at night, when nobody's watching. Ori reads me the rest out loud, “for practice”. He thinks I don't know why he does it. I know. We don't say it. It's better that way.
textes.Je vais te dire ce qu'il y a dans mon co: I'll tell you what's in my chest, {surnom}. A little brass bell. Jules bought it for Hortense in a southern port, two days before the wave. I've kept it for more than fifty years. I've never given it to her. Giving it to her would be telling her it's over. And she's still listening. So I keep quiet.
textes.Je vais te dire ce que je n'ai dit à per: I'll tell you what I've never told anyone, {surnom}. Only once in my life have I truly seen. One night, I dreamt of a child who came from the sea, a sword on their back, who made the clock bell ring. I woke up trembling all over. The next day, on the quay, there you were. With your sword. Since then, I've been a little afraid of my cards.
textes.Je vais te dire ce que pèse la couronne,: I'll tell you how heavy the crown is, {surnom}. I'm the forty-second king of Forgefer, and the Heart of the Mountain is weakening. At night, I wonder if I'll be the last. So I go down to the Mug and sing until dawn, loud and off-key. As long as they can hear me singing, my people sleep.
textes.Je vais te dire la vérité, {surnom}, par: I'll tell you the truth, {surnom}, because you don't shine enough to repeat it. The eighth ruby never cracked. It was too beautiful. I couldn't give it away. It's here, in my pocket, and has been for ninety years. Every evening, I touch it. And every evening, I'm ashamed. A little.
textes.Je vais te dire mon secret, {surnom}. El: I'll tell you my secret, {surnom}. My sail is already sewn. Folded under my bed, with the silver thread in the hem. Three years of nights. Fañch is teaching me to steer, at dawn. All I'm missing is a boat, and the courage to tell my father. He spends his life keeping this ship together, so how do I tell him I want to leave?
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, mais tu jures: I'll tell you a secret, but you have to swear, OK? Once, I went out of the dome all by myself, through the membrane, behind Dad's gardens. Three strokes. I saw the light from above, all green, moving about, and I got so scared I came back in crying. Me, who wants to see the sun… Not even Triton knows. He guards the Gate, not the gardens.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, mais tu le di: I'll tell you a secret, but you won't tell anyone, right? I'm scared of the dark. A firefly fairy who's scared of the dark! That's why I always have a hundred of them around me. The others think it's to look pretty. It's a little bit to look pretty. Mostly so I'm not all alone in the dark.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}, mai: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, but very quietly: the oven has ears. My mooncake isn't my grandmother's recipe. It's my two hundred and twelfth try. The whole village thinks it's Luzerne's. Only Mother Moon tasted the original, and every evening she says “almost”. So I keep searching. For the almost.

I'm going to tell you a secret, {surnom}, but you don't tell anyone, promise? The first night, I heard scratching at the bakery door. I opened it. He was tiny and he was shivering. I gave him a croissant. After that, he came back every night… The stolen croissants are kind of my fault. If Mum finds out, she'll be cross. Or sad. Sad is worse.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Ba: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Ba Sidi wouldn't have refused me the Léviathan's logbook. I never went to ask him for it. I'm scared, you see. Scared he tells the shipwreck differently from my grandfather. If the book says something else, I'm not the last page any more. I'm a wrong page.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. J'i: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. At night, I'm inventing a recipe in a notebook: a little coconut bun, for the morning dancers. I dream of opening it here — my own bakery, at the end of the beach. But I'm afraid Margaux will take it badly. She taught me everything. You don't leave someone who taught you everything. Do you?
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Je: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I don't lose all my drops. For a hundred years, every evening, I've left one at the edge of the northern brambles. For Églantine. In case she's thirsty, in there. I never knew if she drank them. Don't tell Perlée: she'd count them.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Le: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. The mayor doesn't sing that badly. Really. A bit loud, a bit too much opera, but in tune. If I told him, he'd leave the town hall tomorrow for the stage. So I say “seal with a cold”. A good tenor, you can always find. A good mayor is rarer.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Ma: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. My tenth race, eight years ago: I was in the lead. Me! At the roots bend, before the Watchtower, nobody ahead. And then I heard crying behind me: little Bondi, eleven years old, twisted ankle. I carried him to the finish. Last, the pair of us. He thinks I'd fallen too. Never tell him. It's the only race I ever won.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. My sap potion: I don't know everything that's in it. Grandmother fell asleep before she gave me the last ingredient. Hers restored four hearts. Mine restores three. For three hundred years I've been looking for the fourth. That's why I say: “don't ask me”.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret. Dans le trou: I'll tell you a secret. In the hole I dug at Grommelot's, I left something behind: my most beautiful hazelnut, the one that looks most like my shell. He doesn't know. One day, a hazel tree will grow in the middle of his roots, and he'll grumble very loudly. That'll be my way of saying sorry. And maybe it'll be my very own tree.
textes.Je vais te dire un truc qui pique, {surn: I'll tell you something that stings, {surnom}. Ursule forges every nail in my bridges. Every one! And she's never crossed a single one. Never. She takes the stairs, even when it takes her half an hour. She doesn't trust me, that's what. It hurts more than a bee sting. And I've had stings, believe me.
textes.Je vais te dire un truc, {surnom}, et tu: I'll tell you something, {surnom}, and don't you repeat it, eh. At sixteen, I wanted to dance too. I danced behind the stall, with the sardines as my audience. One day, my mother put a fish knife in my hand and said: “There's your dance.” So now, every coin from the big fish, I put aside. For Clara's dance school. She doesn't know.
textes.Je vais te dire un truc, {surnom}, mais: I'll tell you something, {surnom}, but keep it to yourself. Last winter, Amélie put her ear to my chest, listened for a long time, and said: “Slow down.” Since then, on the hills, when nobody's looking, I walk. Those seventy-eight seconds, I'll never run them again. There. Hop… hop. It feels good to say it.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}, but keep it to yourself. My uncle's eyes are getting weaker. One morning I saw him greet a tree trunk: “Morning, Bourru.” He didn't notice. So on watch I look at the forest twice as hard as at the Clearing. For him. I look at the arches afterwards. He'll never know. I talk a lot, but that, I won't tell.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose que personne n: I'll tell you something nobody knows. In that hour, alone on the stage, I made up a song. It's mine, all mine, without a single one of Caelan's rhymes. I've never sung it again. I'm afraid it'll be less beautiful the second time. Maybe at the next festival. Maybe.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose, {surnom}, et: I'll tell you something, {surnom}, and you keep it to yourself. My eyes are going. In the evening, I can't see the line between sea and sky any more. So I ask Ewen what he sees, pretending I'm training him. He describes everything. He's good, that boy. But the blue light, I saw it before. That, I saw.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose, {surnom}, mai: I'll tell you something, {surnom}, but if you repeat it, I'll sell you a leaky bucket. The seagull never paid for his bucket. Half of what I “sell”, I give away: to the old folks, the widows, the fishermen who've had a bad week. If that got out, nobody would ever pay me again. My grandmother did the same.
textes.Je vais te montrer quelque chose, {surno: I'm going to show you something, {surnom}. But you don't say a word. Two years ago, Plumette brought me a parcel with no letter. Inside, there was this: Aunt Sésame's bell. I didn't tell my uncle. I'm scared it means she won't come back. So it stays in my pocket, stuffed with moss, so it won't ring.
textes.Je vais travailler dans les Hauts. Quatr: I'm going to work in the Heights. Ninetieth floor. I'm dizzy.
I'm going to see my sister on the other island.
I'm going to confess a crime to you, {surnom}. I don't like coffee. I never have. For as long as I can remember, behind the coffee machine, I've been drinking camomile, from a coffee cup so nobody notices. Only my mother knew. If word got out on the square… Heavens. Keep it to yourself.
textes.Je vais vous avouer une chose, {surnom},: I'm going to confess something to you, {surnom}, and I'm counting on you. I write romance novels. Under the name Sylvia Delarive. “The Foam of Your Heart” — that's me. The grocer reads it in secret and recommended it to me: I nearly fainted into the peaches. Even Gérard doesn't know. He thinks I'm logging my sunbathing hours. My sunbathing log is three hundred pages long.
textes.Je vais vous confier une chose, {surnom}: I shall confide something to you, {surnom}. I have no house. I live here. I sleep in the linen room on the fourth floor, on a pile of clean sheets, as my mother once did. Never in a room: that would be taking a guest's place. The snoring ghost Pauline talks about… is me. I beg you not to tell her.
textes.Je vais vous dire ce que Nina ne sait pa: I'll tell you something Nina doesn't know, {surnom}. That week's holiday was my honeymoon. On the morning of my wedding, instead of going to the town hall, I went to the harbour with my suitcase and took the boat. Alone. Without getting married. I've never regretted it. But I've never known how to tell the story.
textes.Je vais vous dire la vérité, {surnom}. C: I'll tell you the truth, {surnom}. It wasn't the ring that made me cry. It's that for a second, one tiny little second, I was afraid it was a sign. That the sea was telling me something about us. I'm so angry with myself for doubting. Hugo doesn't know. He thinks I'm angry with him. It's me.
textes.Je vais vous dire un secret, {surnom}, e: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, and you keep it under your tongue. I hate seaweed crackers. All of them. I've never finished a single one. But grandmother invented them so everyone could live, that first night, and as long as I keep pressing them, it's a little bit her feeding the city. So I smile, and I sell.
textes.Je vais vous dire une chose que je n'ai: I'll tell you something I've never told anyone, {surnom}. I know he won't come back. I knew it from the very first year, on the quay, when I saw that little cabin boy's face. But if I stop listening, who will remember Jules? Nobody here knew him any more. The bell isn't so that he comes back. It's so that we remember.
textes.Je vais vous dire une chose que je ne di: I'll tell you something I'll never tell Sylvie, {surnom}. She'd be far too right. These days without a camera are the best of my holiday. I've watched Théo. For real, no viewfinder. I saw him laugh. He has a laugh I didn't know he had. I haven't got a single photo of it. And I remember it perfectly.
textes.Je vais vous dire une chose que personne: I'll tell you something nobody knows, {surnom}. I never defended my thesis. I left a month before, with my old book and my trunk. Here, the sign painter wrote “Dr” on the window without asking me. I never dared have it removed. In the morning, when I clean the windows, I go very quickly over those two letters.
textes.Je vais vous dire, {surnom}. Les cinq cr: I shall tell you something, {surnom}. Five of the croissants are for the seagulls, because Margaret used to do it. The sixth I eat on the jetty, to keep her company. And the dragon tooth… I know perfectly well it's a sardine bone. I knew it straight away. But Fernand looked so proud. I love it all the same. An object doesn't need to be real to be precious.
textes.Je vais à l'Enclume Bleue un lundi par m: I've been going to the Blue Anvil one Monday a month for seven years. I say: “The cog, Hector.” He says: “No time.” I say: “You have time to forge swords for the tourists.” He says: “Hm.” Eighty-four Mondays. I counted. He's never changed a word.
textes.Je vendais des glaces, avant. Puis Bruno: I used to sell ice cream. Then Bruno came along. You can't compete with Bruno.
textes.Je vends mes trouvailles au Marché, cont: I sell my finds at the Market, for coins: Bedaine turns green with envy. The Seven-Day Swap? A phoenix feather, really a painted pheasant feather, went back and forth between us seven days running, until little Mochi bought it for a mooncake. And in the evening, I play the flute at the Circle. The moon doesn't pay, but she listens.
textes.Je veux construire une ville en sable. P: I want to build a sand town. Not a castle, a town! With streets, a fountain, a bakery for Nina, and a lighthouse that really turns. Kiki says I can. Kiki knows.
textes.Je veux m'inscrire au tournoi !: I want to enter the tournament!
textes.Je viens ! Enfin… je viens si on ne va p: I'm coming! Well… I'll come if we don't go too far. Or too near the monsters. I'm coming!
textes.Je viens d'un autre monde, au-delà de la: I come from another world, beyond the sea.
textes.Je viens du village, sur l'autre île. J': I'm from the village, on the other island. I took L'Hirondelle one day, and I never went back.
textes.Je viens ici tous les jours depuis trent: I've been coming here every day for thirty years. The bench has taken my shape.
I'm here for the contract trial.
I'm here for the inspection croissant.
I come to watch the boats. And Cargo. He's so gentle, that big lad.
textes.Je viens, maman. Mais pas de sardines !: I'm coming, Mum. But no sardines!
I live with Father, in the north tree. In the evening, he tells stories. I listen to everything. Without sleeping. Sometimes I forget to bring the basket up. The Zéphyr engineers wanted a steam basket. Hrmm. No. At night, I beat the big drum at the Circle. Slowly. Pépin beats too fast. After every party, we argue. He talks. Me, hrmm.
textes.Je vis dans l'arbre du Guet, avec Éclair: I live in the Lookout tree, with Éclair. Whole evenings without a word, and it's perfect. Every day, I read the mud of the big pond for Moustache, and the night's tracks for Croc-Gris. He can't see very far any more. I tell him what I smell, without him asking. I also keep an eye on the Zéphyr's landing ground. The engineers measure our bridges with string. I measure their boots.
textes.Je vis à la pêcherie avec ma fille Caram: I live at the fishery with my daughter Caramel and my granddaughter Myrtille. I fish, Caramel sells, Myrtille looks better than I do. Every day, Brume reads the mud at the edge for me. The children say a dragon sleeps under the pond: the King never asked for that much. And little Gland jumps about on the jetty. The fish leave. I stay. That's my trade, staying.
textes.Je vise le cochonnet. Il ne bouge pas, m: I'm aiming for the jack. It doesn't move, but it's crafty.
textes.Je vois. Et toutes les fleurs aussi, mai: I see. And so do all the flowers, now.
textes.Je vole, je crie, je repars. Métier : mo: I fly, I scream, I leave. Job: seagull.
textes.Je voudrais aller dans la forêt des brum: I'd like to go into the misty forest. They say its people know plants that cure a fever in a single night. But people don't always come back from the mists.
textes.Je voudrais m'inscrire à la Guilde !: I'd like to join the Guild!
textes.Je voudrais monter une fois, rien qu'une: I'd like to go up once, just once, to the leaf on Yggdrasil where Perlée and I were a single drop. And sit next to her. Without losing anything.
textes.Je voudrais qu'un jour, Brindille et moi: I wish that one day, Brindille and I could rest on the same leaf, like before. A single drop, just for one morning. She would cry, surely. I think I would too, this time.
I'd like to give you something.
textes.Je voulais garder la Grande Porte avec B: I wanted to guard the Great Gate with Bramm. He stared at me for an hour without a word. I talked the whole hour, to fill the silence. He said: “No. You smile too much.” The next day, the king took me on to guard his hall. He said: “A guard who smiles puts visitors at ease.” I've been there fifty years.
I wanted a banana-peel necklace. Momo said it wouldn't last, but he made it for me. The first night, it was the most beautiful necklace at the party. By the third day, it was all black and the flies were dancing with me. Momo laughed so hard he fell off the stall. That's nature, I told him. I kept it two more days.
I've already told you everything, {surnom}. But fine, since you insist:
I've already told you everything, {surnom}. But fine, since you insist:
textes.Je vous ai raconté %d chapitres de ma vi: I've told you %d chapters of my life.
textes.Je vous ai raconté le début de mon histo: I told you the beginning of my story.
textes.Je vous ai raconté tout ce que je sais s: I've told you everything I know about %s.
textes.Je vous ai raconté toute ma vie. Ça, je: I told you my whole life. That, I don't forget.
textes.Je vous ai à l'œil, vous savez. Depuis v: I've got my eye on you, you know. Ever since your “tiny bit”. No bicycles on the quay, I hope?
I'll keep one for you anyway.
textes.Je vérifie le sel. C'est important, le s: I'm checking the salt. Salt is important.
textes.Jeu du Grosse-Dent ! Toi être Grosse-Den: Grosse-Dent game! You be Grosse-Dent! You roar! … (They run off, shrieking with laughter.)
textes.Jeu du caillou ! Qui lance le plus loin: Rock game! Who throw furthest? … Ploc threw at Pika. Pika not happy.
textes.Jeudi ! J'aurai des choses à… enfin, des: Thursday! I'll have things to… well, questions to ask the cards.
Thursday. The cards are waiting for you, my dear.
textes.Jeune humain… viens écouter une histoire: Young human… come and listen to a story.
textes.Jeune, j'ai fait le tour de l'île. À Cli: When I was young, I went round the whole island. In Cliquetis, a compass that points south. In Carène, a telescope that sees the past. In Tazira, a carpet that doesn't fly: I've still got it. And in Tazira, I met Mbarek, the blue man. Our first deal took a whole day and three teapots. Ever since, every year: our honey and dried fish for his dates.
I… I'm saving it for the end.
textes.Je… je n'ai rien. C'est le sol qui a bou: I… I'm fine. It was the ground that moved.
I… I'm taking my time, Sigrun.
I… I'll be back. I have to run.
textes.Je… je veux bien venir. Je ne sais lance: I… I'd like to come. I only know how to cast lightning, but I cast it very well. Usually.
I… I'd like to ask you something. (She takes a deep breath.) Could I come with you? On your adventures? I'm very good at healing. I also fall over, but I'm very good at healing. If you'll have me, just tell me whenever you like. I'll be at the temple, or at the Guild. I'll pray that you say yes.
textes.Jonathan !: A banana at the bus stop!
textes.Jos ! J'ai tracé l'itinéraire jusqu'aux: Jos! I've plotted the route all the way to the hinges.
textes.Jos ! La spatule-goéland tient le coup,: Jos! The gull-spatula's holding up, you know.
textes.Jos ! Le Capitaine Floc'h a encore besoi: Jos! Captain Floc'h needs more sabres!
textes.Jos forge les plus beaux sabres de corsa: Jos forges the finest privateer sabres on the island and sells them for the price of fish. So I resell them for what they deserve. He shouts a bit. He's an artist: he doesn't know his own worth.
textes.Jos m'a forgé un compas pour mes cartes,: Jos forged me a pair of compasses for my maps, the most accurate I've ever had. He says he forged them over the fire of a pebble I'd brought him from the highlands. He smiles every time he tells it, I don't know why. Pride, surely.
textes.Jos parle fort, tape fort, rit fort. Mai: Jos talks loud, hits hard, laughs loud. But he forges the best needles on the island, and he knows how to keep quiet when asked. That, in Carène, is rare.
textes.Jos rêve de toucher les gonds de la gran: Jos dreams of touching the hinges of the great gate, and I dream of going through it. We've been preparing the expedition for nine years. We're very well prepared. We just haven't left yet.
textes.Jos tape sur son enclume au-dessus de ma: Jos bangs on his anvil above my head from morning till night. One day, he'll go straight through the deck and land in my tar. It'll serve him right. I'll help him out. But it'll serve him right.
Jos bangs on his anvil above my head all day long. One day he'll go straight through the deck.
textes.Jos, c'est le seul que je laisse toucher: Jos is the only one I let touch my stove. He hits his anvil hard and he talks loud, but when it counts, he's got hands like a lacemaker.
textes.Jos. L'aiguille courbe s'est un peu tord: Jos. The curved needle's gone a bit bent.
Play the old one. For me.
textes.Jouer la Valse d'Azur sur toutes les pla: To play the Azur Waltz in every town square in the archipelago. The village, Forgefer, the Bois-Doré. With a hat at my feet, like him.
textes.Jouer la chanson de la lune une seule fo: To play the moon song just once without clowning around. No funny face, no wrong note, no wink. In front of Pivoine. And for her to understand.
textes.Jour 212 : naissance du premier enfant d: Day 212: birth of the first child of the dome. I was fifteen, he was howling so loud my quill slipped, and I wrote “Coralain”. He's been asking me to correct it for nearly a thousand years. One does not scratch out a scroll. And besides, between you and me, Coralain suits him.
textes.Joyeuse ! Le facteur du continent m'a ap: Joyful! The mainland postman brought me three love letters. Not for me, but still.
textes.Joyeuse ! Le sable est chaud, la musique: Joyful! The sand is hot, and so is the music.
textes.Joystick droit : choisir | Gâchette droi: Right joystick: choose | Right trigger: confirm | Left ≡ button: menu
textes.Jus de coco ! Directement dans la noix,: Coconut water! Straight from the nut, with a straw, like in the jungle. You've got the soul of a coconut palm, my friend. That's the finest compliment I know.
textes.Jusqu'à l'aube, Sylwen. Elle a laissé sa: Till dawn, Sylwen. She left her window ajar.
textes.Juste cinq minutes, Grommelot ! Cinq pet: Just five minutes, Grommelot! Five little ones!
textes.Juste les abords, Amirale ! Les abords,: Just the surroundings, Admiral! The surroundings are geography.
Just one Bastien, then. A little one.
textes.Juste un moment. Combien en as-tu perdu,: Just for a moment. How many did you lose this week?
textes.Juste un petit son, Barnabé. Regarde, il: Just a little tune, Barnabé. Look, they're dancing.
textes.Juste un peu. Autour de la passerelle. E: Just a bit. Round the footbridge. And a bird.
textes.Juste un. Ou deux. Votre balcon porte ch: Just one. Or two. Your balcony brings luck.
textes.Juste une ! … Bon, onze. Le soleil, il f: Just one! … OK, eleven. Does the sun make a noise?
textes.Juste une fois, sans patron, sans salair: Just once, no boss, no wage. To know what it feels like. And afterwards, I'd come back to the Perroquet. Toni would be too heartbroken.
Just one sip. To taste the sun.
textes.Juste une nuit, Aëlwen. Un oiseau chanta: Just one night, Aëlwen. A bird was singing out of tune; it was charming.
textes.Juste une, une petite. Pour te faire pla: Just one, a tiny one. To make you happy.
Precisely. I made a note of it.
textes.Justement. Tu me les dois depuis trois s: Exactly. You've owed me them for three centuries.
textes.Kalda ! Tu as vu ma chèvre noire ?: Kalda! Have you seen my black goat?
textes.Kalda ! Tu… tu montes au cratère, aujour: Kalda! Are you… are you going up to the crater today?
textes.Kalda a les yeux de ma sœur et mes jambe: Kalda has my sister's eyes and my legs. She climbs higher than anyone and comes down faster. One day, she'll guard the gate.
textes.Kalda court sur les pentes comme mes chè: Kalda runs on the slopes like my goats, only faster and less silly. Without her, I'd have lost half the herd to the golems.
textes.Kalda est la meilleure éclaireuse de la: Kalda is the best scout on the mountain and the worst at dictating: she talks fast, she forgets the sky, and she's a terrible liar when I ask her the question.
textes.Kalda m'a demandé un soir comment on fai: One evening, Kalda asked me how you let someone know you like them without saying it. I answered: “Like goats do. You climb on them.” She laughed. The next day, there was a pretty red stone on Fundin's anvil. He took it for ore and threw it in the fire. Boys.
textes.Kalda monte au bord du cratère comme on: Kalda climbs to the edge of the crater the way you'd pop out for bread. She's afraid of nothing. Me, I'm afraid of her. A bit. A lot.
textes.Karkinos ! Le Crabe-Roi des vieilles cha: Karkinos! The King Crab from the old sea shanties! You defeated him? Gaston, we're writing a song. “There once was a little hero…”
textes.Karkinos entre en furie ! Il va charger: Karkinos goes into a fury! He's about to charge: when he scrapes the ground, step out of his path.
textes.Karkinos s'effondre dans un fracas de ca: Karkinos collapses with a crash of shell! The portcullis lifts… and a chest rises from the well.
textes.Keep it ! Mettez-le sur l'ardoise. L'ard: Keep it! Put it on the tab. The golden tab.
textes.Keep it, my friend ! Mettez-le sur l'ard: Keep it, my friend! Put it on the tab.
textes.Kenavo ! Ça veut dire « à la revoyure »,: Kenavo! That means “see you around”, where we come from.
textes.Kenji, Mio m'envoie pour la voix de Zéro: Kenji, Mio sent me about Zéro's voice.
textes.Kevin ! Mon client, là-bas, il fait des: Kevin! My customer over there is waving. Is that a hello?
textes.Kevin ! Quand tu veux, gamin !: Kevin! Any time you like, kid!
textes.Kevin ! Tu viens dimanche ? Je fais des: Kevin! Are you coming on Sunday? I'm doing sardines.
textes.Kevin avait trois ans. Je vidais les sar: Kevin was three. I was gutting sardines, I turn round: no more Kevin. I hear him laughing.
