He was in the sardine tub, up to his neck, and swimming in it! Breaststroke, already. The customers were clapping. I pulled him out by his braces. He smelled of sardines for a week. Today he hates the smell of fish. I wonder why.
textes.Kevin dit qu'il nage plus vite que je ne: Kevin says he swims faster than I run. That's not true. We've never settled it, but it's not true.
textes.Kevin met au défi de remonter trois étoi: Kevin challenges you to bring up three starfish from the bottom of the bay.
textes.Kevin, c'est mon pote. Le meilleur maîtr: Kevin's my buddy. Best lifeguard in the archipelago, shoulders as wide as a pedalo. He fishes my customers out with a smile. Well, nearly always with a smile.
textes.Kevin, le maître-nageur, a des muscles m: Kevin, the lifeguard, has muscles but also a heart. He saved three tourists this week. Two of whom weren't drowning.
textes.Kevin, le maître-nageur, lance un défi à: Kevin, the lifeguard, challenges anyone who thinks they're a good diver. Nobody's managed it yet.
textes.Kevin, le maître-nageur, mon voisin de l: Kevin, the lifeguard, my neighbour on Lighthouse Street. A brave lad. He has the job I'd have liked. I don't hold it against him. Not much.
textes.Kevin, le maître-nageur, prétend qu'il n: Kevin, the lifeguard, claims he swims faster than I run. We've never settled it.
textes.Kevin, mon voisin de plage. Des muscles: Kevin, my beach neighbour. Muscles everywhere and a heart in the middle. He rescues people all day long, even the ones who don't need it. Especially those.
textes.Kiki ! Kiki ! J'ai besoin d'une tour en: Kiki! Kiki! I need a coconut tower!
textes.Kiki et moi, on parle depuis des années: Kiki and I have been talking for years about a punch contest: the Perroquet against the Coco Loco, in front of the whole town. We've set the date three times. Three times, we've found an excuse. The truth is, we're both scared. If I lose, I close. If he loses, he cries. So we drink each other's punch and say “not bad”.
textes.Kiki fait du punch coco, comme moi, mais: Kiki makes coconut punch, like me, but on the beach, in a flowery shirt. A good lad. He drinks at my place every evening. And the jungle boat doesn't deliver to me anymore. I'm not saying anything. I'm just noting it.
textes.Kiki m'a piqué ma recette coco. Je l'ava: Kiki pinched my coconut recipe. I'd pinched it from my grandmother. We're even, and he's my best friend on the beach.
Kiki pinched my coconut ice-cream recipe. I pinched it from my grandmother, so we're even.
textes.Kiki m'a prêté sa louche, sa lanterne et: Kiki lent me his ladle, his lantern and his shoulder, all on the same evening. I owe him at least a thousand punches. He won't let me pay for them.
textes.Kiki, c'est mon copain. Il est grand et: Kiki's my friend. He's tall and he laughs all the time, and he opens coconuts in one go! He says one day I'll make a town. He's right.
textes.Kiki, c'est mon voisin de plage et mon b: Kiki is my beach neighbour and my barman. He counts my rescues better than I do. He embellishes them, too. But he always has ice.
textes.Kiki, il a juré qu'il marcherait jamais: Kiki swore he'd never step on my castle. He swore on his machete! Once, he was carrying three coconuts and couldn't see his feet. He jumped over the moat at the last second, and fell in the sand. The coconuts too. But the castle, nothing at all. Kiki keeps his promises.
textes.Kiki, il me donne des pailles pour faire: Kiki gives me straws to make flags for my towers. Once, he gave me a pink straw, with a little paper umbrella. I put the umbrella on the biggest tower. Everyone said it was the best castle on the beach. Even a lady with a hat.
textes.Kiki, mon ami. Tu n'aurais pas vu mes no: Kiki, my friend. You haven't seen my coconuts, have you?
textes.Kiki, mon voisin de la gare maritime. Un: Kiki, my neighbour from the ferry terminal. An adorable boy who plays the ukulele under my window at midnight. Bad music, freely given, as he says. Given, yes. Not asked for.
Kiki. Midnight on the dot, last night. Again.
textes.Kinich, le garçon au moustique, veut bie: Kinich, the boy with the mosquito, is willing to lend Xan, his mosquito, to whoever goes down into Xibalba. But he's hungry.
textes.Kira ! Kira ! Encore le tour qui brille: Kira! Kira! Do the shiny trick again!
textes.L'Accueillotron : « Monsieur Lisse n'est: The Welcomatron: “Mister Lisse is not available. Mister Lisse is never available. That is his charm.”
textes.L'Accueillotron : « Pour descendre, adre: The Welcomatron: “To go down, go to the Offices. To go up, go to the terminals. To complain, go to the wall.”
textes.L'Accueillotron : « Puis-je vous propose: The Welcomatron: “May I offer you a glass of water? No? Perfect: it is more optimal.”
textes.L'Accueillotron baisse la voix : « Entre: The Welcomatron lowers its voice: “Between us… the punks upstairs make very good soup. Don't repeat that. Beep.”
textes.L'Accueillotron tourne la tête (vrrr) :: The Welcomatron turns its head (vrrr): “Hello. Your visit is important to us. That is why it will be processed in order of arrival, in 2087.”
textes.L'Achéron, une rivière d'eau noire et fr: The Acheron, a river of cold black water. On the bank, a boat, and in it, a tall hooded figure with golden eyes: Charon, the ferryman.
textes.L'Ahu du Couchant — ils regardent le sol: The Sunset Ahu — they watch the sun rise over the island, every morning, since forever
textes.L'Ahu du Levant — sept Moaïs alignés, le: The Sunrise Ahu — seven Moai in a row, backs to the sea, watching over the island
textes.L'Aile de la Lune. Un gouffre sans fond,: The Moon Wing. A bottomless chasm, a stone island in the middle, and two lovely slate bridges leading to it… Too lovely, perhaps. At the far end, on the ledge, a door and four dials.
textes.L'Aile des Marées. Un grand bassin, des: The Tide Wing. A great basin, rafts floating far below, and at the far end, a door on a ledge, out of reach. Beside you, a big bronze wheel: the tide wheel. Above the far ledge, the motionless sails of a mill…
textes.L'Aile des Rouages. Un gouffre noir, des: The Cog Wing. A black chasm, cast-iron platforms standing still on their rails, and on the ledge, against the wall, a big geared engine, stopped. Jammed, perhaps?
textes.L'Aile des Sables. Au milieu, un sable q: The Sand Wing. In the middle, shifting sand… quicksand! Paths of flagstones cross it. Four unlit braziers at the four points of the compass, and a stele in the centre.
textes.L'Alouette, le deltaplane de Philibert (: The Alouette, Philibert's hang glider (at the Wing Workshop, west of Cliquetis)
textes.L'Amirale fait peur à tout le monde. À m: The Admiral scares everyone. Me too, a bit. But she gave me her hat, and you don't give your hat to someone you don't like. I think.
textes.L'Amirale m'écoute. C'est rare, quelqu'u: The Admiral listens to me. That's rare, someone who listens to a lookout. Her mother listened to me too. The Kerhervés have bad tempers and good ears.
textes.L'Amirale me demande chaque printemps co: Every spring, the Admiral asks me how long the hull will hold, and every time I ask for wood, she says “budget”. You can't plug holes with budgets.
textes.L'Amirale me laisse travailler sur la gr: The Admiral lets me work on the big table in her harbour office. She wants maps of the coast, I want the centre. We argue politely. She always has the last word. That's her job.
textes.L'Amulette du Serpent ! Reconstituée ! E: The Serpent Amulet! Put back together! Is it glowing green? On my map, under the big serpent, it says “Abyss”. And a little drawing of me running away.
textes.L'Amulette du Serpent s'illumine. Les ch: The Serpent Amulet lights up. The chains snap clean…
textes.L'Arbre ? Laisse-moi d'abord te parler d: The Tree? Let me tell you about it first. Ask me who I am.
textes.L'Arbre sacré respire à nouveau. Chaque: The sacred Tree breathes again. Every time I look at it, I think of you.
textes.L'Arbre-Mère a semé des graines sur tout: The Mother Tree sowed seeds on every island. The one Lyra guarded was the last to be dying. You saved it. The Wood will remember.
textes.L'Archiduchesse m'envoie : je descends c: The Archduchess sent me: I'm going down to fetch the Eternal Flame.
textes.L'Atlantide ! Une cité entière, sous une: Atlantis! An entire city, under an immense bubble of air, thirty meters beneath the sea… You can breathe. In the center, atop its tower, a great crystal slowly dims.
textes.L'Atlantide ! Vous l'avez vue ! Racontez: Atlantis! You've seen it! Tell me everything, I beg you!
textes.L'Enclume Bleue. Des lames qui coupent,: The Enclume Bleue. Blades that cut, axes that split. Looking or buying?
textes.L'Entrepôt Automatique. Des rayonnages j: The Automated Warehouse. Shelves up to the ceiling, robot forklifts honking, and an area of crates to push in the west. Way at the back, on a mezzanine, something is shining.
textes.L'Hirondelle a quarante ans. Je l'ai rep: The Swallow is forty years old. I've repainted her six times. She's carried kings, newlyweds and a goat. The goat was seasick.
textes.L'Hirondelle arrive ! Patientez sur le q: L'Hirondelle is arriving! Please wait on the dock.
textes.L'Hirondelle est à quai : parlez au capi: L'Hirondelle is at the dock: speak to Captain Léon.
textes.L'Oliveraie — de vieux oliviers tordus,: The Olive Grove — old twisted olive trees, and singing cicadas
textes.L'Usine Grise. L'Accueillotron te fait u: The Grey Factory. The Welcomatron waves a claw at you.
textes.L'acier rebondit sur la roche ! Ses quat: The steel bounces off the rock! His four runes protect him: each one fears the power of its seal.
textes.L'aider à sortir de la boîte: Help him out of the box
textes.L'aiguille tremble, hésite, puis indique: The needle trembles, hesitates, then points south. Both ends of the needle. Now you can relax.
textes.L'aile de la chouette se redresse… Elle: The owl's wing straightens up… It hoots, flaps its wings and flies off toward the moon. Mère Sauge will be pleased.
textes.L'an dernier, Glaucos a soufflé douze va: Last year, Glaucos blew twelve new basins for my corals. Light, clear: the crystal's light shines right through them. He wouldn't take anything in return. So every evening, we play shell jacks on the rim of a basin. He cheats. I let him win. We don't talk about it. It's good.
textes.L'an dernier, Mochi s'est glissée au dép: Last year, Mochi slipped onto the start line of the Great Race, between the grown-ups' legs. She got through the first arch before I caught her by the dungarees. She was wriggling and shouting “I won the arch!”. Her dad would have laughed so hard the forest would have shaken. So I laughed for him.
textes.L'an dernier, j'étais en plein sauvetage: Last year, I was in the middle of a rescue, a tourist in my arms and water up to my neck, when I heard from the stall: “KEVIN! Are you coming for lunch on Sunday?” The whole beach heard. The tourist asked me if that was my mum. I said no. He didn't believe me.
textes.L'an dernier, je me suis glissée au dépa: Last year I sneaked onto the start line of the Great Race, between the big ones! I ran and ran, and I got through the first arch! Then Godfather Pépin caught me. Uncle Bondi turned round to wave at me, and he nearly lost! He won anyway. I won too. Getting through the first arch is already winning.
textes.L'an dernier, pendant la Grande Course,: Last year, during the Great Race, I hear little footsteps behind me. I turn round: Mochi! She'd just gone through the first arch, in among the big ones. I waved at her, while running, with both paws. Grisou used it to catch up on me. I still won. Just. I tell everyone I did it on purpose.
textes.L'année de mes dix-neuf ans, ma mère est: The year I turned nineteen, my mum fell ill. Not serious, but for a long time. The remedies from the herbalist in Port-Azur were expensive. I made necklaces day and night, I took the boat every morning to sell them at the harbour. She got better in the spring. That day, I decided to smile for the whole family. All the time.
textes.L'année de mes quarante ans, une tempête: The year I turned forty, a storm threw my boat, the Rozenn, onto the rocks at the point. I swam, and so did she, in her own way. We both washed up on the beach, broken. No money for another one. So I flipped her over and moved in underneath. She was shipwrecked before me, that kind of thing brings you close.
textes.L'année dernière, c'était au deuxième. O: Last year, it was on the second. We're making progress.
textes.L'année dernière, elle a vendu à un cara: Last year, she sold a caravanner “a bit of Carène wind”: an empty jar, sealed with a circle of my canvas. He paid for it. He came back the next day to buy a second one, for his sister. Since then, I'm the one who sews the lids on Salomé's jars. She pays me well. I'm not proud of it.
textes.L'année dernière, j'ai emprunté le vieil: Last year I borrowed Thalion's old bow. Just to see! I aimed at an apple on the bench. I hit Sylwen's door. Three times. The door fell down. Thalion said “never again”. Sylwen said “it's only a door”. Mummy didn't say anything at all, and that was the worst.
textes.L'année suivante, la Belle-Étoile est re: The following year, the Fair Star came back into port. I'd put on my blue dress. The sailors came down one by one, and not him. It was the little cabin boy who came to me, Léon, fourteen, in tears: “Swept away by a wave, miss.” Nothing was ever found. Not a button, not a letter. So I kept on listening.
textes.L'après-midi est long et doux. Parfait p: The afternoon is long and gentle. Perfect for a nap.
textes.L'après-midi, je vais lézarder sur la pl: In the afternoon, I go and laze on the beach. If you see a red towel, that's me.
In the afternoon, the island gets lazy. So do I.
textes.L'après-midi, quand je passe sur le quai: In the afternoon, when I cross the quay on my way to the beach, Lucas is lifting crates. One at a time, usually. When I walk past: three. Three crates stacked up, face all red, arms trembling. Once the top one slipped. He caught it with his knee and said “hello” to me at the same time. That's our longest conversation.
textes.L'après-midi, à la vigie du Guet, Grisou: In the afternoon, up in the Lookout's watchtower, Grisou is supposed to be keeping watch over the forest. He watches the Games Clearing: I can see his snout poking over the railing. So I do my fastest starts right underneath, on purpose. Hop! He sighs so loudly you can hear it from down below.
textes.L'archimage Séraphine Astrelune veut bie: Archmage Séraphine Astrelune is willing to take me on as an apprentice. I need a spellbook, and to get to know the other apprentices.
textes.L'archimage m'envoie chercher un grimoir: The archmage sent me to fetch a spellbook.
textes.L'ardoise est pleine. Je vais devoir en: The tab's full. I'll have to buy a second one.
textes.L'armoire à fournitures ! Dedans : des t: The supply cupboard! Inside: paper clips, a sad stapler, a few coins… and a vial forgotten by an intern.
textes.L'armurier ? Un homme qui parle peu et f: The armourer? A man who speaks little and forges true. Between people of metal and stone, we understand each other. I'll say no more: there's nothing to say.
textes.L'arrière du Léviathan est sous l'eau :: The stern of the Léviathan is underwater: the sea came in through the great southern breach, and the hold filled up. We turned it into a basin for the rowing boats. What's already sunk can't sink. That's my philosophy.
The inn? You mean the hammocks.
The inn gets thirsty too. The jugs.
textes.L'autre jour, Gérard était sur le ponton: The other day, Gérard was on the jetty while I was renting the “Gérard” pedalo to a family. I shouted: “The Gérard's free!” He turned round, all pleased: “Yes?” I said: “No, nothing, Gérard. I meant the pedalo.” He laughed, didn't get it, and did the camera gesture with his fingers: click. A true professional.
textes.L'autre jour, Léa m'a demandé une boutur: The other day, Léa asked me for a bougainvillea cutting, for her shop on the mainland, when she goes home. I promised her the most vigorous one. I'm nursing it in one of Kiki's coconut pots. It's already growing crooked, like all the others. I don't dare warn Léa: in ten years, it'll eat her shop.
textes.L'autre jour, Nina a défié Marcel. Une s: The other day, Nina challenged Marcel. Just one ball. He laughed. She pointed, he pointed, and I took out my tape measure. She was closer by one centimetre! One centimetre, {surnom}. Marcel asked to measure again. I said: “A centimetre is a centimetre.” The face he pulled… It was worth eighteen years of waiting.
textes.L'autre jour, il a loué mon pédalo à un: The other day, he hired out my pedalo to a couple, right in front of me. He told them: “Take the Gérard, it goes round beautifully.” How kind, he gave them my name as a reference! I gave them a little wave: “That's me, Gérard!” They burst out laughing. They must have found me very likeable.
textes.L'autre jour, je l'ai attrapé au vol dev: The other day I caught him in passing by the fountain, two fingers on his wrist, while he jogged on the spot. “My times are going down, doctor, down!” His pulse wasn't going down. I sold him a sap potion and he left at a walk. For ten metres.
textes.L'autre matin, il a joué une valse beauc: The other morning, he played a waltz far too fast. I rapped three sharp knocks on the cobbles with my heel. He started again, slower. At the end, two tourists clapped. He bowed to me, guitar on his heart. I didn't smile. Well, not much.
textes.L'autre soir, Barnabé est descendu jusqu: The other night, Barnabé came down to the dance floor with Gaston on his shoulder. He did three dance steps, right on the kick, and left without a word. Since then, Gaston goes “Boom. Boom.” all over the jungle, at a hundred and forty-five. I've got a feathered fan, and he's got rhythm.
textes.L'autre soir, Kiki est arrivé au Perroqu: The other evening, Kiki came into the Perroquet with a coconut under his arm. “A present, Toni!” A coconut. One! The jungle boat hasn't delivered a single one to me in weeks, and he gives me one, with a bow on it. I thanked him. I looked him in the eye. He looked at his feet.
textes.L'autre soir, Lucas jouait contre Victor: The other night, Lucas was playing against Victor. I walked behind him with my tray and saw his hand: three aces. Three! He looked up at me, put his cards down any old how, and lost. Victor scooped up the coins, laughing. Lucas didn't even look at what he'd lost. He was still looking at me.
textes.L'eau de la vasque s'allume, de bleu, de: The water in the basin lights up, blue, green, turquoise. At the back of the room, the five great stones begin to glow… and something rises from the water.
textes.L'eau du bassin de la grande chute, dans: Water from the pool of the great waterfall, in the crystal vial. It sparkles a little, as if it were holding stars.
textes.L'eau du cratère regarde le ciel, immobi: The crater water looks at the sky, motionless… Very close to the edge, beneath the Lake Guardian, something shines under the surface.
textes.L'eau est glacée et a un goût de pierre…: The water is icy and tastes of stone… Your strength returns all at once. All your hearts are full.
textes.L'eau et la foudre… Je vais faire très a: Water and lightning… I'll be very careful.
textes.L'eau noire est glaciale… Tu te hisses s: The black water is freezing… You haul yourself onto the edge of the platform.
textes.L'eau verte du Cénote est aux dieux : on: The green water of the Cenote belongs to the gods: climb back up by the steps.
textes.L'elfe ? Elle parle aux arbres et elle n: The elf? She talks to trees and doesn't like axes. But she climbs my ladder without making the third rung creak. That, I respect.
textes.L'elfe. Je n'ai pas de hache sur moi, re: Elf. I've got no axe on me, look.
textes.L'encre de seiche sèche mal, sous le dôm: Squid ink dries badly under the dome. But I'm not complaining. Well, I am. A bit.
textes.L'enfant du quai, l'été dernier. Je l'ai: The child on the quay, last summer. I saw him fall, I ran to the edge, and I whistled fit to burst my cheeks. Kevin arrived like an arrow, dived in without even taking off his vest, and brought the little one out in ten seconds. He handed him to me. I carried the child to his mother. In my report, I wrote: “Joint intervention.”
textes.L'enseigne, je l'ai forgée en trois jour: The sign, I forged it in three days. An iron parrot, wings spread. Singing off-key, as always. The beak's a bit crooked: I fluffed the last note. Toni hung it up himself, the first night. Crooked. He said: “He looks alive.” I left it crooked. Twenty years.
textes.L'entraînement : faire le parcours d'ann: Training: complete the glowing ring course in the Zero-Gravity Garden (to the west, at the end of the bridge of light) and set a record
textes.L'esprit de l'Arbre ne parle qu'à ceux q: The spirit of the Tree speaks only to those who have crossed its four halls. It has always been so.
textes.L'examen du gâteau caché, à dix ans. Je: The hidden-cake exam, at ten. I came back furious, with half the cake and Bedaine's tracks drawn on a piece of bark. Mère-Lune looked at the drawing for a long time. She said: “You found the cake and the thief. Two answers.” Then she gave me half marks. The other half was for the cake.
textes.L'herboriste. Elle parle trop. Moi, pas: The herbalist. She talks too much. Me, not enough. Her vials are good. Her teas… hm. Hot water. She hasn't forgotten.
textes.L'histoire de la lune toujours pleine ?: The story of the always-full moon? Long, long ago, a she-wolf rescued the moon when it fell into the great pool. To thank her, the moon promised to shine round and full above Ramure, every night. And she keeps her word. Look.
textes.L'hiver de Cerfeuil, je ne dormais plus: The winter of Cerfeuil, I didn't sleep at all any more. I kneaded at night, I cried into the flour. One morning, Pivoine turned up with a little vial full of mist, stoppered with a moon feather. “Open it in bed, not before.” I opened it. I slept twelve hours. The first vial of mist in Ramure was for me.
textes.L'hiver de la cendre, Dagna nourrissait: In the winter of ash, Dagna fed a hundred dwarves with a cracked ladle. I forged her a spoon. Three weeks, {surnom}. Three weeks for a spoon, ten days for the king's axe. She says it's my masterpiece, and I say “Hmph”. Because if I say anything else, I'll end up saying all the rest.
textes.L'hiver de la cendre, il fallait monter: In the winter of ash, my big cauldron had to be carried up from the city to the terrace. Nobody could manage it. Bramm left his gate, for the only time in his life. He lifted it all by himself and climbed the steps without a word. At the top, he said: “It's too hot.” And he went back to guarding.
textes.L'hiver de la cendre, j'ai quitté mon po: In the winter of ash, I left my post only once: to help Dagna carry her big cauldron from the city to the terrace, under the falling ash. It weighed more than the gate. She never forgot it. Neither did I. It was the only time.
textes.L'hiver de la cendre, ma louche s'est fe: In the winter of ash, my ladle split in two. Three weeks later, Borin turned up with a big iron spoon, smooth as a pebble, a little flame engraved on the handle. He said “Hmph” and left. Three weeks: I know, I counted the days he missed his stew.
textes.L'hiver dernier, Corentin toussait à fen: Last winter, Corentin had a cough fit to split the ship's rail. He refused my honey syrup until I told him a story at the same time: one spoonful, one story. He got better in nine stories. He says the sixth was so bad he coughed on purpose to get another one.
textes.L'hiver dernier, Dwalin s'est bloqué le: Last winter, Dwalin put his back out with one sack too many. I laid him down by the cauldron under three blankets and spoon-fed him for three days. On the fourth, he said he was feeling better. On the fifth, he admitted he'd been feeling better since the second.
Last winter, Marcel had the flu. I went to the pitch anyway and played on my own, against a pebble. The pebble won. In the evening, I took some soup round to Marcel's, on the other side of the hedge. He asked me who'd won. I said: “Me.” He said: “Liar.” He was already feeling better.
textes.L'hiver dernier, elle grelottait. Ses de: Last winter she was shivering. Her teeth were chattering. You could hear it from my place. I couldn't sleep. So I threw her a blanket. A spare one. … It was mine. Atchoo. Don't repeat it.
textes.L'hiver dernier, en pleine tempête, la l: Last winter, in the middle of a storm, the lantern on the mainmast went out, and three boats were still out there. I rang the bell, and then I climbed. Right to the top. Without permission. The wind was pulling my hair. I lit it again, and the boats came home. Afterwards I scrubbed the deck for three days. And the Admiral gave me her hat.
textes.L'hiver dernier, j'avais si froid que me: Last winter I was so cold my drops froze. Grommelot threw a blanket in front of my door, growling: “Too many blankets at my place. Clutter.” It was his. He didn't have another one. All winter, I heard him sneezing behind his door.
textes.L'hiver dernier, je me suis bloqué le do: Last winter, I put my back out with one sack too many. Godmother laid me down by the cauldron under three blankets and spoon-fed me. After two days, I felt better. I waited until the fifth to say so. She knew, I think. All she said was: “Stew cures everything. Even liars.”
textes.L'hiver dernier, mon étau s'est fendu. J: Last winter, my vice split. I didn't tell anyone. The next morning, it was on my counter, repaired, greased, with a new screw. No note, no bill. Hector, who charges for coal by weight! When I thanked him on the square, he said: “For what?” And he left.
textes.L'hiver dernier, six de ses hamacs ont l: Last winter, six of his hammocks gave way the same night. He came to the stall, all pale, not daring to ask. I found him the best hemp rope from the highlands, at cost. He asked why. I said: “Without you, who would I fight with?” It was true.
textes.L'hiver des fièvres, ma petite sœur Soaz: The winter of the fevers, my little sister Soazig passed away. She left behind a five-year-old boy, with carrot-coloured hair and a suitcase too big for him. Pierrick. I put him to bed in a hammock above the sparkling apple barrels. He never really came down. Well, he did: to grow up, and to get it into his head that he runs the inn.
textes.L'hiver du grand froid, elle m'a prêté s: In the winter of the great cold, she lent me her old tracker's cloak. In spring, I swapped it for three pots of honey. I'd forgotten it wasn't mine! It took me a year and eleven swaps to get it back. The worst: a drum for a goat. The goat ate two of my hats and a corner of the market. Heh heh… I had it coming.
textes.L'hiver du grand froid, il y a quinze an: In the winter of the great frost, fifteen years ago, Bedaine was shivering at his market. I lent him my old tracker's cape, the one that had seen the edge of the world. By spring he'd swapped it for three jars of honey. Three! It took him a year and eleven swaps to get it back. I think he was colder that year than the winter before.
textes.L'hiver où Cerfeuil est parti, Trèfle ne: The winter Cerfeuil left, Trèfle couldn't sleep, and her bread burned, which never happened to her. I gathered the morning mist off the big pond, asked Plumette for a moon feather to hold it in, and put the vial by her bed. She slept till noon. The village bread was late. Nobody complained.
textes.L'hiver où elle était chez les nains, à: The winter she was with the dwarves, in Forgefer, I wrote to her every week. Six pages, with stories inside. She wrote back once: “Cold. Good. Ursule.” I keep the letter in my pocket, look, here it is, all worn. It's the shortest story I know, and it has a happy ending.
textes.L'hiver où il a perdu sa barque, Fañch d: The winter he lost his boat, Fañch slept under it, on the beach, in the open wind. I brought him soup every evening for two months, saying it was leftovers. There were never any leftovers. I made it specially for him. He knew. We've never talked about it.
textes.L'hiver où le fer a manqué, j'ai fait ve: The winter iron ran short, I had three sacks of ore brought down from the highlands by a shepherd who owed me a favour, and I sold them to Jos at the old price. He was suspicious, he looked for the catch. There wasn't one. A blacksmith who isn't forging starts talking. And when Jos talks, the whole hold hears it.
textes.L'horloge de la place est arrêtée : il l: The clock on the square has stopped: it needs a new cogwheel, which only Hector can forge.
textes.L'huile est au coin du poêle. Comme d'ha: The oil's by the stove. As usual.
textes.L'humain est encore là. Il a l'air genti: The human is still here. They look kind.
textes.L'hydromel de Berthe, au Chaudron Fumant: Berthe's honey drink, at Le Chaudron Fumant: made with honey from Mother Sauge's hives, sweet and golden. Restores one heart.
textes.L'hôtel a été construit par un armateur: The hotel was built by a mad shipowner who wanted to see the sea from his bed. He had forty-two windows put in. Then he got seasick.
The hotel is a town within the town. There's even a ghost, on the fourth floor. It snores.
textes.L'ibis, l'œil d'Horus, le soleil : le no: The ibis, the eye of Horus, the sun: the king's name is written! A deep click… the stone door sinks into the floor.
textes.L'intérieur d'Yggdrasil ! Le tronc est c: Inside Yggdrasil! The trunk is hollow like a tower. The walls glow with mushrooms and moss, roots hang from the ceiling. In the middle, a pool where fireflies dance; around it, five stones carved with runes. At the far end, a staircase of roots… blocked by a tangle of roots.
textes.L'objet que tu vises, même hors de porté: The item you aim at, even out of reach, flies into your hand.
textes.L'obélisque, derrière moi, monte jusqu'à: The obelisk behind me reaches all the way to the surface. Its tip lights up at night: it's our lighthouse.
textes.L'orange ! « Ô cascade orangée, au solei: The orange! “O orange waterfall, in rediscovered sun, you tumble down laughing…” (He searches.) “…into the pond that awaited you.” It doesn't rhyme. It's marvellous. Go pour it in, paint cup number seven, and tonight at sunset I'll write you an ode. Here, in the meantime: my finest feather. It smudges a little.
textes.L'orange de la Cascade d'Encre: The orange of the Ink Waterfall
One doesn't rule out the other.
textes.L'Étang Gommé\n(ne pas effacer les canar:
The Rubbed-Out Pond
(please don't erase the ducks)
textes.L'Étang Gommé — une eau calme, des nénup: The Rubbed-Out Pond — calm water, water lilies drawn in pencil
textes.L'Île Al Dente — l'île de la secte du Sp: Al Dente Island — the island of the Flying Spaghetti sect: a volcano spitting tomato sauce, a temple shaped like a colander… and something floating above
textes.L'Île Al Dente, au sud-ouest de l'archip: Al Dente Island, in the south-west of the archipelago
textes.L'Île Al Dente, l'île du Spaghetti Volan: Al Dente Island, the island of the Flying Spaghetti
textes.L'Île Al Dente, le Temple-Passoire: Al Dente Island, the Colander Temple
textes.L'Île Crayonnée\nIci, tout attend ses co:
Sketched Island
Here, everything awaits its colours.
textes.L'Île Crayonnée — ici, tout est en noir: Sketched Island — here, everything is black and white, like a forgotten colouring page… Who took the island's colours?
textes.L'Île Crayonnée, au sud-est de l'archipe: Sketched Island, in the south-east of the archipelago
textes.L'Île Crayonnée, l'île sans couleurs: Sketched Island, the island without colours
textes.L'Île Crayonnée, le Belvédère des Couleu: Sketched Island, the Lookout of Colours
textes.L'Île Pixelithique — ici, tout est en pe: Pixelithic Island — here, everything is made of little squares… except you
textes.L'Île aux Moaïs — des géants de pierre q: Moai Island — stone giants who watch over the island… and who, they say, laugh when your back is turned
textes.L'Île aux Moaïs, l'escalier du Grand Moa: Moai Island, the stairway of the Great Moai
textes.L'Île aux Moaïs, la Salle du Chant: Moai Island, the Hall of Song
textes.L'Île aux Moaïs, le Cœur du Chant: Moai Island, the Heart of the Song
textes.L'Île de Braise — Pandémonia, la cité de: Ember Island — Pandémonia, the city of demons (they're very nice)
textes.L'Île de Larsen — une grande ville de yo: Larsen Island — a big town of yurts: the hippies of the Flower Camp, the grunge kids of Rainville… and, in between, the Main Stage
textes.L'Île de Larsen, chez le Disquaire: Larsen Island, at the Record Shop
textes.L'Île de Montjoie — la ville des aventur: Montjoie Island — the adventurers' town (they recruit there; there's a lot of laughing)
textes.L'Île de la Balafre — Port-Coutelas, le: Balafre Island — Port-Coutelas, the pirates' lair
textes.L'Île des Trois Soleils: The Island of the Three Suns
textes.L'Île des Trois Soleils — Per-Hâpy, Yaxc: The Island of the Three Suns — Per-Hâpy, Yaxché and Aztlán
textes.L'Île du Boucan — Port-Boucan, la ville: Boucan Island — Port-Boucan, the free town (here, everything is shared, even the noise)
The echo isn't on the crew list. Nine.
textes.L'écorce est tiède, et vibre doucement,: The bark is warm, and hums softly, like a very slow heartbeat. No door… for now. The fairy queen surely knows more.
textes.L'épée des Rois-Ciel, trouvée dans le tr: The sword of the Sky Kings, found in the treasure of the Storm Tower. Its blade crackles with little blue sparks. Damage: 12, and the third hit of a combo strikes half again as hard.
textes.L'établi de Philibert : des croquis d'ai: Philibert's workbench: sketches of wings everywhere, scraps of canvas, an oil can, a cup of cold coffee. A note: “IDEA! Make people fly. Ask for help (canvas, logs, bolts).” Philibert must be hanging around town: talk to him.
textes.L'établi de Philibert. Sur le mur, une p: Philibert's workbench. On the wall, a framed photo of the Albatros. Below it, a note: “What next? The Lumens of Astralys, they say, build machines that fly all the way to the stars…”
textes.L'étang reflète Yggdrasil la tête en bas: The pond reflects Yggdrasil upside down. The old ones say the Tree also grows the other way, beneath the clouds.
textes.L'étoile, au sommet, brille d'une lumièr: The star at the top glows with a soft light, as if someone had lit it.
textes.L'étoile, la dune, le soleil… Les trois: The star, the dune, the sun… The three rings line up! A low rumble rises from the dune, the sand begins to flow… and the slab slowly sinks into the ground.
textes.L'été dernier, Caelan a chanté quarante: Last summer Caelan sang forty verses for Ilyria, in the square. She fell asleep at the twelfth. Well, she closed her eyes. I listened to the whole thing while kneading, and my dough rose twice as high as usual. I've asked him to come back and sing on Saturdays.
textes.L'été dernier, un enfant est tombé du qu: Last summer, a child fell off the quay, between two boats. I was three metres away. Three metres, and I couldn't jump. I whistled, I shouted, I called Kevin. He came running, he dived in, he pulled the little one out. Everyone applauded the lifeguard. Me, I went home, put my kepi on the table, and didn't sleep all night.
textes.L'été dernier, un gamin est tombé du qua: Last summer, a kid fell off the quay, between two boats. The sergeant got there first. He stopped at the edge, white as a sheet, and blew his whistle with all his might. I ran, dived, got the kid out. The sergeant shook my hand very hard, without a word. His eyes were wet. Mine too. Harbour water, surely.
textes.L'été des méduses, il est entré en boita: The summer of the jellyfish, he limped in, his calf as red as a lobster, and said: “Nothing serious, doctor. Assault on duty.” He refused to sit down until I'd entered it in a register. I don't have a register. I wrote it on a bag of lime-blossom tea. He signed it.
textes.L'été des méduses, il y a huit ans, j'ai: The summer of the jellyfish, eight years ago, I was stung on the calf on duty, watching the beach. A jellyfish the size of a plate. I finished my rounds limping, on principle. Doctor Roux put a vinegar and aloe balm on it, and I smelled of gherkins for three days. Since then, she's the only one I trust.
textes.L'été sans pluie, Amélie a monté les sea: The summer without rain, Amélie carried the buckets up with me every evening, in a dress and sandals, without ever complaining. Well, once: she slipped, the bucket tipped over her feet, and she said a word I didn't know they taught you in medical school. We laughed so hard we had to sit down in the dust.
textes.L'été sans pluie, je l'ai croisée sur le: The summer without rain, I came across her on the hill path, a bucket of water in each hand, dripping with sweat, trying to save her lavender. I took two buckets as well. Two months, morning and evening. We barely spoke, we counted our steps. When the rain finally fell, we danced in the rows of thyme like two little girls.
textes.L'île ? Du bois partout, du bon. Ce from: The island? Wood everywhere, good wood. This kapok tree here, under your feet: it's held up my hut for twenty years without a creak.
textes.L'île est grande, et chaque côte a son c: The island is big, and every coast has its own sky. Ours is the west: the sea, the meadows and the wind. To the north, the highlands and their snow; to the east, the misty forest; to the south, the desert. And in the middle, Stoneheart.
textes.L'île flottante. Le vent siffle, les nua: The floating island. The wind whistles, clouds drift beneath your feet, and far away the ocean glitters, a hundred and fifty metres below… To the north rises the Citadel of the Clouds.
textes.L'Œil d'Horus ! L'œil que Thot a guéri,: The Eye of Horus! The eye Thoth healed, the sign of returning light. 150 coins, one more heart, and a title: “Eye of Ra”. Ra's barque will carry you back to the light. In the highlands, a niche in the Altar of the Three Suns awaits this eye.
textes.L'Œil reste éteint… Il faudrait l'Amulet: The Eye stays dark… You would need the Serpent Amulet.
textes.L'œil du serpent passe du rouge au vert…: The serpent's eye turns from red to green…
textes.LA CHAUMIÈRE DES GLYCINES ! Un palais !: THE WISTERIA COTTAGE! A palace! A dream! A bed so soft that you wake up rested, whatever kind of night you've had! A shelf where your trophies from the other islands will shine like stars! A fireplace! A roof! Almost whole! And if you faint on the island, they'll bring you home, not lay you between two temple benches! Three hundred coins. Not one less. Believe me: it's an exceptional bargain. And what's more… it's true.
textes.LA GRANDE PELLETEUSE ! Neuf mètres d'aci: THE GREAT DIGGER! Nine meters of steel, piloted by OPTIMUS-LISSE. Your sword bounces off its armor… Avoid the bucket (the red circle), then strike the HOSES, which glow when it's stuck in the ground!
textes.LA GRENOUILLE REINE, la plus grosse du l: THE FROG QUEEN, the biggest one in the lake! Her tongue reaches very far, and she has a mighty appetite. Don't stand in front of her mouth!
textes.LE CAPITAINE SANS-CHAIR ! L'ancien secon: CAPTAIN FLESHLESS! Bloodbeard's old first mate still guards the treasure. Back off when he whirls his sabre, and beware: he calls his men from beyond the grave.
textes.LE CHEF GOBELIN ! Un casque d'os, et sa: THE GOBLIN CHIEF! A bone helmet, and his banner as a club. He charges, bellowing, and calls his gang. Step aside from his charges, then strike.
textes.LE COLOSSE À VAPEUR ! Un automate haut c: THE STEAM COLOSSUS! An automaton as tall as a house, with a boiler rumbling on its back. You'd need to jam its gears…
textes.LE COULOIR DU ROCHER\nPrière de courir.\:
THE BOULDER CORRIDOR
Please run.
(The alcoves are free.)
textes.LE FESTIVAL DU LARSEN ! Sur la Grande Sc: THE LARSEN FESTIVAL! On the Main Stage, the Gouttières and the drums of the Flower Camp play together. In the front row, Granny Sunflower and Mother Downpour hold hands and sing off-key, very loudly.
textes.LE GARDE-MARÉE ! Un crabe grand comme un: THE TIDE GUARD! A crab as big as a rowboat, its shell covered in coral. Nothing pierces it… but a strong enough wind might knock it over.
textes.LE GARDIEN DU CŒUR ! Un colosse de roche: THE HEART GUARDIAN! A colossus of rock, veined with fire, four runes glowing on his body… Each one answers to the power of a seal. Shatter them!
textes.LE GRAND LIVRE DES COFFRES (tome 7 : « C: THE GREAT BOOK OF CHESTS (volume 7: “The Ones That Bite”). “Six chests sleep here, and three have teeth. The skull smiles too much: beware of smiles. The crown thinks it's a king: it bites like a king. The hourglass counts the seconds until its dinner (you). The candle and the books are honest, but poor. The true treasure sleeps beside the one who keeps watch at night and answers only 'hoo'.” In the margin, in pencil: “I tried the skull. I don't recommend it.”
textes.LE JAUNE ! Tu l'as trouvé ! T'es le meil: THE YELLOW! You found it! You're the best finder on the whole island! (She jumps, she dances, she falls in the sand, she gets back up.) Quick, quick, to the Palette, paint cup number four! I want my socks to have stripes again. Here: my most beautiful seashell. It sings, if you believe really hard.
textes.LE NOUVEAU CHAMPION ! (Elle te soulève d: THE NEW CHAMPION! (She lifts you with one arm.) Even Gorgoth is happy: he says you fight the way one writes a poem. Here, your share of the takings, and two iced lavas, on the house.
textes.LE ROI CHAMPIGNARD ! Une couronne de cha: THE MUSHLING KING! A crown of mushrooms, and a spore cloud as big as a house. He isn't mean… but you're going to sneeze! Keep your distance when his cap swells up.
textes.LE ROI GÉLATINEUX ! Quatre mètres de gel: THE JELLY KING! Four meters of jelly… and a tiny crown. When he leaps, get away: he lands with all his weight. And beware, he splits!
textes.LE SCORPION-ROI ! Cuirassé d'or, une que: THE SCORPION KING! Armored in gold, with a tail as long as a mast. Its armor stops steel… but its eyes fear flame.
textes.LE TITAN DE GIVRE ! Il garde la Flamme É: THE FROST TITAN! He guards the Eternal Flame at the bottom of the Cocytus. Beware of his club and his icy breath; strike him when he gets back up.
textes.LES MONDES DE TRAVERS PC | MANETTE : s:
LES MONDES DE TRAVERS PC  |  CONTROLLER: left stick: walk  •  right stick: camera  •  A: jump  •  B: roll  •  X: strike  •  Y: talk / open
LB: parry  •  RB: run  •  LT: power  •  RT: spell  •  d-pad: eagle, teleport, power, spell  •  Start: menu  •  Select: journal
textes.LES TROIS ! Bravo ! Maintenant, tu as go: ALL THREE! Bravo! Now you've tasted the soup, heard Rustine whistle and drunk Sirène's lemonade: you're officially from Boucan. Well, there's no official paper. We voted against papers in assembly. Here, a few coins from the common fund, for your first days. And come to the concert tonight: we'll be waiting for you in the pit!
textes.LISSE & FILS\nHaut (ou bas):
LISSE & SONS
This side up (or down)
textes.LISSE & FILS\nPLAN DES ÉTAGES\n\n-1 Les:
LISSE & SONS
FLOOR PLAN

-1  The Offices
-2  The Assembly Line
-3  The Boiler Room
-4  The Automated Warehouse
-5  The President's Pit
(no entry, especially for you)
textes.La Barque-Maison — une vieille barque re: The Houseboat — an old boat turned upside down on the sand, a mast, a flag… it's Captain Rigatoni's home
textes.La Bergerie du Vent. Une grande grotte,: The Wind Sheepfold. A big cave, a wooden pen, dry straw, a cold hearth. At the very back, a bronze wall and a round door like a gear, guarded by two metal statues.
textes.La Bibliothèque des Mimiques. Des livres: The Mimic Library. Books up to the ceiling, six chests on six platforms, each guarded by a little statue… and, in the middle, a great open book on a lectern.
textes.La Bourrasque prend dans les ailes du mo: The Gust catches in the mill's sails! They begin to turn, a chain creaks… and a drawbridge falls from the far ledge down to the last raft. The far door rises.
textes.La Butte de la Carrière — des têtes de p: The Quarry Mound — stone heads poking out of the grass, as if to watch the clouds go by
textes.La Cantine à prix libre. Une grande marm: The Pay-What-You-Can Canteen. A big pot steams, a slate reads: “SOUP OF THE DAY: EVERYBODY'S SOUP. Price: whatever you like. Even nothing. Especially if you're hungry.” A tin box waits for coins.
textes.La Cascade Arrabbiata — la sauce tombe d: The Arrabbiata Falls — the sauce pours off the cliff into the sea, which turns all red
textes.La Cascade d'Encre — le ruisseau tombe d: The Ink Waterfall — the stream tumbles from the cliff into the pond in long pen strokes
textes.La Chaufferie. Il fait chaud, ça siffle,: The Boiler Room. It's hot, it hisses, it rumbles: steam jets blow in rhythm across the corridor. The pressure gauge on the door, at the far end, is in the red: you need to find the three valves.
textes.La Chaîne de Montage ! Des bras robots s: The Assembly Line! Robot arms welding mover robots, a pit full of bolts, and three conveyor belts running toward the exit… or not. The switching console is right there.
textes.La Chope Ardente, c'est le cœur de Forge: The Blazing Mug is the heart of Forgefer. The king has his throne, I have my counter. We know who people come to see.
textes.La Chorale des Pierres Chantantes ! Nous: The Choir of the Singing Stones! We're rehearsing for the full moon festival. Want to conduct? Take the baton!
textes.La Clairière des Géants — un grand cercl: The Giants' Clearing — a great circle of short grass, old oaks all around, and in the middle… a painter's palette made of stone
textes.La Clé du Brasier tourne dans la serrure: The Brasier key turns in the lock. The iron door opens onto a staircase going down… and an icy air rises from the depths.
textes.La Colline du Feedback — d'ici, on voit: Feedback Hill — from here, you can see the whole island… and hear the wind whistle
textes.La Corderie\nIci, le chanvre devient cor:
The Ropeworks
Here, hemp becomes rope, canvas and twine.
(Nothing else. We just braid.)
textes.La Corderie — ici, le chanvre devient co: The Ropeworks — here, hemp becomes rope
textes.La Couronne d'Yggdrasil ! À ciel ouvert,: The Crown of Yggdrasil! Open to the sky, among immense branches, the top of the trunk makes a great square of living wood. But something is creeping between the branches…
textes.La Douat, le monde de la nuit. Un ciel d: The Duat, the world of night. A starry sky beneath the stone, a black river on each side, and at the far end Ra's barque, unlit. The silence… too much silence.
textes.La Doyenne m'envoie. Que se passe-t-il a: The Elder sent me. What's going on with the Heart?
textes.La Fausse Alerte. Pleine nuit. Une forme: The False Alarm. Dead of night. A shape climbs the Mother Oak. A long neck. A fiery eye at the end. I sounded it. Any guard would have. It was Hulotte with his lantern and his long telescope. He still laughs when he passes me. Me, I don't laugh. It was a drill. I wrote it in the log: “drill”.
textes.La Flamme brûle plus fort, la Bourrasque: The Flame burns hotter, the Gust blows wider, the Moonglow lasts longer, the Cog turns longer.
textes.La Flamme l'aveugle ! Le Scorpion-Roi es: The Flame blinds it! The Scorpion King is stunned: strike!
textes.La Flamme prend dans les ronces noires !: The Flame catches in the black brambles! They twist, crackle, hiss… and fall to ashes.
textes.La Flamme Éternelle ! Elle ne brûle pas: The Eternal Flame! It doesn't burn your fingers: it warms them. 150 coins, an extra heart, and a title: “Conqueror of the Frost Titan”. Bring it back to the Ember Heart, in the Forge Cathedral!
textes.La Flamme Éternelle bondit dans le Cœur-: The Eternal Flame leaps into the Ember Heart! A great golden flame rises to the vaults, and the whole city warms up at once. Go and tell the Archduchess!
The Door Flower only opens to the sun. She's very vain.
textes.La Fleur-Porte s'est ouverte ! Le Jardin: The Door Flower has opened! The Fairy Garden is right behind it.
textes.La Fleur-Porte s'est ouverte pour toi !: The Flower-Gate opened for you! Further on, they say, lives the Bramble Queen. She likes neither humans, nor elves, nor anyone. Be careful.
textes.La Fosse du Président. Une arène de béto: The President's Pit. A concrete arena beneath a glass office all in gold. On the wall, a giant screen lights up: two red eyes, a bar for a mouth… OPTIMUS-LISSE is watching you.
textes.La Goélette : huit mètres et demi, deux: The Schooner: eight and a half metres, two masts, gaff sails and a real steering wheel, like the great captains. The most elegant, the fastest under sail (12 m/s).
textes.La Grande Course ! Passe sous les dix ar: The Great Race! Pass under the ten lantern arches, in order, and come back here. Ready?
textes.La Grande Galerie. Un rayon de soleil —: The Great Gallery. A ray of sunlight — so deep down here! — enters through a narrow shaft and strikes a bronze mirror. There are others, on stands. At the far end, on the door, a dull gold disc.
textes.La Grande Grotte du Clan — ça sent la fu: The Great Clan Cave — it smells of smoke, fur and fern flatbread
textes.La Grande Pelleteuse siffle… un jet de v: The Great Digger hisses… a jet of steam! Get away from its tracks!
textes.La Grande Porte mène à la cité. Bramm ne: The Great Gate leads to the city. Bramm lets nobody in. Nobody.
textes.La Grande Porte ne bouge pas. Bramm, le: The Great Gate doesn't budge. Bramm, the guard, eyes you suspiciously. He's the one you have to convince.
textes.La Grande Tablée, c'est la meilleure inv: The Great Table is the best invention since the fork.
textes.La Gratuiterie : une longue table couver: The Free Shop: a long table covered in objects, and a hand-painted sign: “NOTHING IS THROWN AWAY, EVERYTHING IS GIVEN. One item per day per person, thank you! — Trocante”.
textes.La Grotte aux Peintures — des bêtes roug: The Painting Cave — red and ochre beasts run across the walls
textes.La Jungle des Fougères — des fougères gr: The Fern Jungle — ferns as tall as trees, and hissing among the leaves
textes.La Lueur de lune révèle une quatrième ru: The Moonlight reveals a fourth rune, on his forehead! Strike it!
textes.La Maison Obscure. Le noir complet. Une: The Dark House. Complete blackness. A voice: “Here are our torches. Keep them lit all night, and give them back to us WHOLE tomorrow.” Three empty torch holders, on the walls.
textes.La Maison des Chauves-souris. Des millie: The House of Bats. Thousands of tiny cries, up there, in the dark. And a silence, lower down, much heavier.
textes.La Maison des Jaguars est calme. La port: The House of Jaguars is calm. The door at the back sinks into the floor: behind it, a ball court.
textes.La Maison des Jaguars. Des yeux jaunes d: The House of Jaguars. Yellow eyes in the shadows, growls, gnawed bones all over the floor…
textes.La Maison des Lames. Quatre lames d'obsi: The House of Blades. Four obsidian blades, tall as a man, sweep the room from wall to wall. Near the entrance, an empty altar.
textes.La Mare aux Mantras — une eau calme, des: The Mantra Pond — calm water, water lilies, frogs meditating
textes.La Marmite\nNe pas se pencher. Ne pas tr:
The Cooking Pot
Do not lean over. Do not dip your fingers.
That's what the ladle is for.
textes.La Marmite — le cratère est plein de sau: The Cooking Pot — the crater is full of simmering tomato sauce: it smells of garlic, basil and warm tomato
textes.La Montagne de Feu. Le sable est noir, l: Fire Mountain. The sand is black, the air smells of sulfur and coal… Above the beach, braziers and forge smoke: Forgefer, the city of the dwarves.
textes.La Montagne de Feu. Mille ans que nous c: The Fire Mountain. A thousand years we've been digging beneath it. It rumbles, it smokes, it keeps us warm. It's our mother.
textes.La Mère-Ronce se fane, se recroqueville…: Mother Bramble withers, curls up… and falls as golden dust. The branches of Yggdrasil shiver with relief.
textes.La Mère-Ronce, la reine des plantes d'Yg: Mother Bramble, queen of the plants of Yggdrasil! Her bite reaches very far. Wait until she strikes at nothing, then run and hit her before she straightens up.
textes.La Mère-Ronce, reine des plantes d'Yggdr: Mother Bramble, queen of the plants of Yggdrasil
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, Brume m'a r: On the Night of the False Alarm, Brume recognised me by smell, three bridges away, while the alarm was still ringing. She said I smelled of moon tea. I'd had two cups. Three. Since then, when I climb to the treetop, I wonder if she's following me by nose. Hoo. Probably.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, Brume était: On the Night of the False Alarm, Brume was down by the ponds. She sniffed the air and ran to the Lookout to tell me: “It's Hulotte.” Too late. I'd sounded it. She never blamed me. She just said, the next day: “Good drill.” A good girl.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, Croc-Gris h: On the Night of the False Alarm, Croc-Gris was howling, all of Ramure was running about in their nightshirts, my son was carrying me down the stairs. And Mother Moon, sitting on her moss, simply said: “It's only Hulotte.” It was Hulotte. She didn't even spill her tea. I lost a slipper.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, il a vu un: On the Night of the False Alarm, he saw a long-necked monster climbing the Mother Oak and sounded the alarm. All of Ramure came tumbling down in their nightshirts. Me, I stayed sitting and said: “It's only Hulotte.” It was Hulotte, with his lantern and his long telescope. Croc-Gris says it was a drill. He didn't speak to me for three days.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, il avait ci: On the Night of the False Alarm, he was five. He came down the zip line in his pyjamas, all alone, shouting “Wheee”. Everyone was scared. Not him. The next day, he came back to ask me what time the next alarm was. Since then, he does it himself. Every day. At snack time.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, j'ai su ava: On the Night of the False Alarm, I knew before anyone that the monster was him. The smell: lantern tallow, feathers, moon tea. He drinks too much of it. I recognised him three bridges away. When I told him, he sighed that I had a nose without poetry. I took it as a compliment.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, j'avais cin: On the Night of the False Alarm, I was five. Croc-Gris shouted “ALERT!” and I ran to the Lookout in my pyjamas. I took the zip line all by myself, wheeeee, all the way down! Everyone was scared. Me, I was laughing. At the bottom, Granny Faîne caught me by the tail. The next day I asked Croc-Gris when the next alert was.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, j'étais en: On the Night of the False Alarm, I was down by the ponds. I sniffed the wind: it was Hulotte, not a monster. I ran towards the Lookout to say so. The alarm was already ringing, and all of Ramure was tumbling down the stairs in their nightshirts. The next day, I told him: “Good drill.” He looked at me. He said: “Yes.”
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, je montais: On the Night of the False Alarm, I was climbing the Mother Oak's stairs with my lantern and my long telescope on my shoulder. The monster's long neck was the telescope; its fiery eye, my lantern. All of Ramure came down in their nightshirts. Me, I reached the treetop, and there was no one left up there. Hoo. I still laugh about it. He doesn't.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, mes vieille: On the Night of the False Alarm, my old paws wouldn't go down. Bourru picked me up like a cub and carried me all the way down the stairs. At the bottom, he said: “Hrmm. Light.” I was still telling a story, apparently. I don't remember. I remember “light”. Nobody had said that to me in sixty years.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, tout Ramure: On the Night of the False Alarm, all of Ramure was running about in nightshirts. The little ones were crying, Bourru was carrying Tilleul down in his arms. Only one stayed sitting: Mère-Lune. She said: “It's only Hulotte.” Calmly. Before anyone. Without even looking up. I've never got over it.

On the Night of the False Alarm, all of Ramure came tumbling down in their nightshirts. Bourru came down the stairs carrying his old father in his arms like a cub, and Tilleul was still telling a story over his shoulder. Me, I stayed sitting on my moss. He waved to me as he passed, very dignified. He'd lost a slipper.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte. Tout le mon: The Night of the False Alarm. Everyone was going down. Father, his paws wouldn't. I carried him in my arms. The whole staircase. He was still telling stories. At the bottom, I put him down. I said: “Hrmm. Light.” He went quiet. One minute. First time in his life. Hrmm. He doesn't eat enough.
textes.La Palette de pierre : les neuf godets s: The Stone Palette: all nine paint wells are full, each in its own colour, from blue to pink. It shines in the sun like a rainbow laid in the grass.
textes.La Palette de pierre : neuf godets numér: The Stone Palette: nine numbered paint wells, from 1 to 9, all empty and dry. At the bottom of the first, a tiny trace of blue… Who took the island's colours?
textes.La Perle de l'Épave est dans le coffre d: The Wreck Pearl is in the chest of “The Black Mermaid”, the ship that sank west of the Gate. Surface sailors had stolen it…
textes.La Perle de la Fosse repose sur l'autel,: The Trench Pearl rests on the altar at the bottom of the Jellyfish Trench, to the north, beyond the kelp forest. Jellyfish sting: don't brush against them.
textes.La Perle du Jardin dort dans le grand bé: The Garden Pearl sleeps in the giant clam, in the heart of the coral reef, north-east of the city. The sharks circle it. Be quick.
textes.La Pierre du Soleil gronde… et rejette l: The Sun Stone rumbles… and spits out the four glyphs, which fall back into your hands. That isn't the order of the suns. (The codex, at the entrance, shows that order.)
textes.La Place des Hologrammes — trois carpes: Hologram Square — three light carp swim above the passersby
textes.La Plage des Œufs — des nids, des œufs…: Egg Beach — nests, eggs… don't disturb them
textes.La Plaine des Cornes — attention aux Cor: The Plain of Horns — beware of the Nose-Horns, they're grumpy
textes.La Plume de Quetzalcóatl ! Le Serpent à: Quetzalcóatl's Feather! The Feathered Serpent, god of wind and knowledge. 150 coins, an extra heart, and a title: “Bearer of the Fifth Sun”. A staircase of light leads back up to the top of the Great Temple.
textes.La Porte aux Quatre Sceaux: The Gate of the Four Seals
textes.La Porte aux Quatre Sceaux est ouverte !: The Gate of the Four Seals is open!
textes.La Porte aux Quatre Sceaux ouverte: The Gate of the Four Seals opened
textes.La Porte aux Quatre Sceaux. Les quatre c: The Gate of the Four Seals. The four hollows are still empty. Behind the stone, very far away, it sounds as if a heart is beating.
textes.La Porte de l'Abîme, en pierre noire. Un: The Abyss Gate, in black stone. A green glow protects it. Behind it, something immense is breathing… The Eye Stone, right there, may be waiting for the amulet.
textes.La Porte du Serpent s'ouvre ! Les trois: The Serpent Gate opens! The three fragments have fused: the SERPENT AMULET. Its green eye lights up the darkness.
textes.La Prairie du Festival — la Grande Scène: The Festival Meadow — the Main Stage awaits its festival
textes.La Reine des Ronces pousse un cri… Les é: The Bramble Queen cries out… The thorns fall from her gown like dead leaves. A pink light wraps around her…
The Bramble Queen flies out of reach. When she lands, exhausted, that's the time to strike!
textes.La Reine des Ronces… c'était Églantine ?: The Bramble Queen… was Églantine? The Fairy Queen herself, prisoner of her own thorns for a hundred years! And it was a little human who set her free. I'll have to write a new song. A long one.
textes.La Reine des Ronces… on n'en parle pas t: The Bramble Queen… we don't speak of her too loudly here. Her brambles have eaten half our kingdom.
textes.La Reine hurle : « Mes enfants, à moi !: The Queen howls: “My children, to me!” Crystal spiders burst from the brambles!
textes.La Reine se relève, et son bouclier d'ép: The Queen gets back up, and her thorn shield grows back! The roses of light close again…
textes.La Rose des Sceaux. Une salle ronde comm: The Rose of Seals. A hall as round as a square, four columns, four doors. On the floor, an engraved compass rose, and at the centre a round seal beneath four dark crystals. Under the vault, a red crystal hangs and beats like a heart.
textes.La Râpe d'Or… Arrr. Bon. Je vais te dire: The Golden Grater… Arrr. Well. I'll tell you the truth, matey. I buried it thirty years ago, so nobody would steal it from me. And then I forgot where. (Pesto shouts: “RAMEN!”) … No, wait. I remember the phrase: “where the mast's shadow touches the sea at noon”. My mast is the Houseboat's. Take a shovel, and dig on the sand, between the mast and the water. You don't have a shovel? I sell one. Cheap. I'm a pirate, not a thief.
textes.La Salle de la Sève. À l'ouest, une sour: The Sap Hall. To the west, an amber spring from which golden light flows. Three flowers with polished silver hearts, like mirrors. To the east, a big knot of dark wood: the heart of the tree?
textes.La Salle des Deux Vérités. Anubis, le di: The Hall of the Two Truths. Anubis, the jackal god, and Thoth, the ibis god, before a great golden scale. Along the walls, the forty-two judges.
textes.La Salle des Pièges. À l'est, un champ d: The Trap Room. To the east, a field of tiles (some are dark and cracked…); to the west, a campfire and goblins; to the south, a closed door, and three unlit lamps above it. Three levers to find!
textes.La Salle des Prismes est au bout du coul: The Prism Hall is at the end of the corridor. The sun comes down through a crack… but it no longer reaches the Door Flower.
textes.La Salle des Saisons. Quatre fleurs de p: The Hall of Seasons. Four stone flowers, one at each cardinal point, and a carved stele right next to you… And leaves that move all by themselves!
textes.La Salle du Cœur. Le grand cristal bat d: The Heart Chamber. The great crystal beats gently, with a golden light. All is calm.
textes.La Salle du Cœur. Une caverne immense, r: The Heart Chamber. An immense, round cavern, veins of fire in the floor. In the middle, hanging from chains, a red crystal larger than a house… that beats. And beneath it, something is rising.
textes.La Salle du Trône Gélatineux. Le sol col: The Jelly Throne Room. The floor sticks to your soles, a jelly throne wobbles at the far end… and a smell of green apple hangs everywhere.
textes.La Terrasse du Ciel — à 150 mètres au-de: The Sky Terrace — 150 meters above the streets: the whole city, the sea, and the archipelago in the distance
textes.La Tomateraie — des tomates grosses comm: The Tomato Grove — tomatoes as big as fists, red, warm from the sun
textes.La Tour Axiome — 265 mètres de verre ; s: The Axiom Tower — 265 meters of glass; its elevator goes up to the Sky Terrace
textes.La Tourmente : un couloir au bord d'un g: The Tempest: a corridor on the edge of a fiery chasm, and a wind that never stops blowing, in gusts. The pillars against the wall make good shelters.
The Waltz plays when it wants to. Serve first.
textes.La bague en corail rose, il me l'a laiss: The pink coral ring, he offered it at twelve coins, friend's price. I offered nine, fiancée's price. A week of haggling! In the end he said “eleven”, I said “ten”, and we looked at each other. Neither of us gave in. The ring's still in his drawer. I know: I check when his back is turned.
textes.La bague est dans ma poche depuis des jo: The ring has been in my pocket for days. I'm waiting for the right moment. The right century, maybe.
textes.La baguette de Pimprenelle ! Son étoile: Pimprenelle's wand! Its crystal star crackles between your fingers. She'll be delighted to have it back, in the Fairy Village.
textes.La bague… Tu en as trouvé une ? Avec une: The ring… Have you found one? With a blue stone, mind. Not red. Red is for declarations of war.
textes.La baie devant la plage descend doucemen: The bay in front of the beach slopes gently. At the bottom there are orange starfish. Bringing them up to the surface is my challenge for the tough ones.
textes.La baie est poissonneuse, abritée par le: The bay is full of fish, sheltered by the two points. Further out, there are the big ones. And to the north, under the highland cliffs, lobsters the size of dogs.
textes.La balance penche lourdement : ton cœur: The scale tips heavily: your heart weighs more than the feather! In the shadows behind the judges, something growls… AMMIT THE DEVOURER bursts out!
textes.La balance s'équilibre : ton cœur est au: The scale balances: your heart is as light as Ma'at's feather! Thoth writes on his tablet: “True of voice.” Your heart returns to your chest… and at the far end of the hall, the door to the Duat opens.
textes.La balle roule, rebondit sur le talus… e: The ball rolls, bounces off the slope… and falls back into the alley. The Lords snigger. Aim for the stone ring, on the wall.
textes.La bannière ! LA BANNIÈRE ! (Il la brand: The banner! THE BANNER! (He waves it, trips on his cape, falls, and is still waving it, lying down.) A real feat! With a witness! With sunshine! Bertrand! BERTRAND! We need a song! And not a single cloud in it!
textes.La barque de Rê glisse sur le fleuve de: The barque of Ra glides over the river of night… and drops you off in the sunlight, in front of the pyramid door.
textes.La betterave. Ma vie d'artiste est un dr: Beetroot. My artistic life is a tragedy.
The Montjoie library is that way. Just for your information.
textes.La bijouterie le matin, le déjeuner chez: The jeweller's in the morning, lunch at Paulo's, the shop, a stroll in the evening. Victor drops by to offer me “authentic” shells that smell of paint. A young newlywed asked me for a ring “exactly the same”. And Rosalie counts my Friday sea bream with saucer eyes. A quiet life, as you can see. In Port-Azur, nothing stays quiet for long.
textes.La bière épaisse et douce de Mérit, fait: Mérit's thick, sweet barley drink, made with barley bread and dates. The Egyptians drank it like liquid bread. Restores one heart.
textes.La boisson du Diable Repu, sans alcool :: The house drink of Au Diable Repu, alcohol-free: honey, fire cinnamon, a pinch of sulphur from the springs (for the colour). It smells of eggs, and it warms you right through. Restores one heart.
textes.La botte de Barnabé ! Je vais la clouer: Barnabé's boot! I'll nail it above my door. Like a trophy.
textes.La boule ajoute : « Évitez les grenouill: The ball adds: “Avoid the frogs.” Nobody knows why. Everybody listens.
textes.La boule devient rose une seconde. D'apr: The ball turns pink for a second. According to Églantine, that means “hidden talent”. Very hidden.
textes.La boule embue sa propre vitre. Elle a b: The ball fogs up its own glass. It needs a moment.
The ball makes a little satisfied noise. Églantine notes: “The ball is happy.”
textes.La boule ne ment jamais. Elle exagère, p: The ball never lies. It exaggerates, sometimes.
textes.La boussole que je t'ai donnée ne montre: The compass I gave you doesn't point north. It points to what you're really looking for. Usually, that's north.
textes.La boutique est FERMÉE. Pour toi. Revien: The shop is CLOSED. To you. Come back when I've got over your punches.
textes.La boîte aux lettres jaune devant la pos: The yellow postbox outside the post office? If you slip a wish into it, I won't read it. Promise.
textes.La brioche du Four Éternel de Bobor, dor: The brioche from Bobor's Eternal Oven, golden, split on top, baked over the embers that never go out. Still warm, at any hour. Restores two hearts.
textes.La brume ? C'est le souffle de l'Arbre-M: The mist? It's the Mother Tree's breath. It opens for those it loves. It seems to like you. It has strange tastes.
textes.La brume est calme… Tu as fait tout ce q: The mist is calm… You've done everything there was to do. The stars salute you. So do I.
textes.La cachette est vide : tu as déjà pris l: The hiding place is empty: you've already taken the treasure. The parrot gives you a knowing look.
textes.La caisse vient se caler contre le quai: The crate slides up against the loading dock: a nice step! Jump on it, then onto the dock… then onto the mezzanine.
textes.La caisse à outils du chauffagiste ! Une: The boiler technician's toolbox! A wrench, some patches… and coins. On the lid: “Do not open during steam bursts.”
textes.La capitaine. Elle voit tout, elle note: The captain. She sees everything, she writes everything down. She scares me a bit. But she's fair. I respect her.
textes.La carte d'Églantine montre la passe ent: Églantine's map shows the pass between the Fire Reefs, to the west. The dwarves of Fire Mountain live over there.
textes.La carte des Récifs de Feu ! Les nains d: The map of the Fire Reefs! The dwarves of the Fire Mountain… They forged the finest blades in the world. My grandfather sold them moonwood, eight centuries ago. He came back with an axe and without his beard. Head towards the sunset, beyond the jungle. And knock hard: dwarves are a little deaf, from all that hammering on anvils.
textes.La carte frémit dans ton sac. Le sable d: The map quivers in your bag. The sand of the Circus rises… bones come up and fit together: CAPTAIN SANS-CHAIR!
textes.La cascade de lumière descend des racine: The waterfall of light flows down from the Mother Tree's roots. It's its sap. Don't drink it: you'd glow for a week.
textes.La casquette de Bastien, je l'ai repêché: I fished Bastien's cap out of the water the night Fanny sent him flying into the sea. I put it on so it could dry. It dried on my head for three days. He found it and gave me an hour-long lecture. I listened with the cap on my head. He didn't dare take it back during the lecture.
textes.La chambre de la terrasse. Laisse la fen: The terrace room. Leave the window open: you'll fall asleep to the party, and wake up to the seagulls.
textes.La chambre du dessus. Le lit est à resso: The room upstairs. The bed has springs: if you bounce off the ceiling, that's normal. The alarm clock rings at seven; it plays the trumpet.
textes.La chambre du haut, celle avec la lucarn: The top room, the one with the skylight. If the cauldron sings tonight, that's normal: it's dreaming.
textes.La chapelle d'Isis. Deux gros blocs de g: The chapel of Isis. Two big granite blocks, and two bronze slabs engraved with an ankh. Near the entrance, a bronze ring on the wall.
textes.La chapelle de Khépri, le scarabée. Un s: The chapel of Khepri, the scarab. A floor of slabs above a pit of sand. Some are engraved with a tiny scarab.
textes.La chapelle de Serket, la déesse au scor: The chapel of Serket, the scorpion goddess. Something is scratching in the corners…
textes.La chapelle obscure. Pas une torche. Jus: The dark chapel. Not a single torch. Just a green glow at the very back… and shuffling footsteps.
textes.La charpentière. Trop bruyante. Ses pont: The carpenter. Too noisy. Her bridges dance too much. But they hold. I respect that. I don't say so.
textes.La chaudière ronronne, la cheminée fume,: The boiler purrs, the chimney smokes, the propeller churns: your boat has a steam engine! Careful, it starts with a jolt.
textes.La chaîne d'os ne bouge pas. Dehors, que: The chain of bones won't budge. Outside, something still guards the treasure… (Captain Sans-Chair, in the Circus)
textes.La chaîne d'os tombe en poussière. Le co: The chain of bones crumbles to dust. The lid creaks… BARBE-SANGLANTE'S TREASURE! (
textes.La chaîne tombe ! Ventaile pousse un cri: The chain falls! Ventaile lets out an immense cry that echoes through the crater… but she is too weak to fly. She is hungry: bring her fish (three).
textes.La chorale te remercie avec ce qu'elle a: The choir thanks you with what it has.
textes.La chèvre qui est montée trop haut, vers: The goat that climbed too high, towards the golems? Kalda saw her come back down. She told me: “She was running so fast her horns arrived before she did.” Then, more quietly: “The golems didn't follow her. They didn't even turn their heads.” That scared me.
textes.La cime du Chêne-Mère : la Poste des cho: The top of the Mother Oak: the Owl Post Office.
textes.La cinquième corde a cassé. Hulotte deda: The fifth rope snapped. Hulotte inside, the mail bag clutched to him. He was counting the wickers. Out loud. Me, I held on. He counted up to a hundred and twelve. Then the pulley locked. He got out. He said thank you. He never got back in. Hrmm.
textes.La cité s'étend sous toute la montagne :: The city stretches under the whole mountain: the great hall, the Royal Forge, the mines, the dormitories… and my cellar. The biggest room of all.
textes.La cloche de la Cathédrale sonne douze c: The Cathedral bell strikes twelve… THE NIGHT OF LANTERNS BEGINS! From every street, the demons pour into the Great Square, laughing and singing. Calcine strikes up a wild jig.
textes.La cloche de la Tour Penchée: The bell of the Leaning Tower
textes.La cloche de la Tour Penchée a sonné !: The bell of the Leaning Tower has rung!
textes.La cloche de la Tour Penchée sonne sur t: The bell of the Leaning Tower rings out over the whole island! Zéphyrine must have heard it.
textes.La clé d'argent tourne. Les hiboux cisel: The silver key turns. The engraved owls all open an eye (“hoo”) and the silver door sinks into the floor. Further down, it smells of green apple… and jelly.
textes.La clé d'or de la ville, remise par le m: The golden key to the town, given by the mayor to the honorary citizen. It opens no doors, but every heart.
textes.La clé de cuivre entre dans la bouche de: The copper key slides into the mouth of the frog lock, which goes “ribbit” (yes, really). The copper door sinks into the floor.
textes.La commandante Zélie Hélice, à Cliquetis: Commander Zélie Hélice, in Cliquetis! We write each other a little note in every bag. I've never seen her. But I recognise her handwriting: it leans forward, like an airship.
The rope snapped. I held the basket. Bare hands. It slipped. It burned. And Ursule arrived. An iron bar. In the pulley. Clack. Done. We never talked about it. Never. Ten years. Hrmm. No need. That evening, she gave me her honey pot. Her own. Whole.
textes.La couchette, c'est pour la nuit (à part: The bunk is for the night (from 7 p.m.)… For now, the sun is winking at you!
textes.La cour des Seigneurs de Xibalba. Douze: The court of the Lords of Xibalba. Twelve thrones, twelve motionless figures. A dry voice: “Greet the Lords then, traveller… the greatest first.”
textes.La couronne des Rois-Ciel : or blanc, sa: The crown of the Sky Kings: white gold, sapphires and cloud pearls. Proof that you defeated Lord Storm. It's worth a fortune… but who would dare sell it?
The crown is heavy. Especially in the morning.
textes.La course passe sous les dix arches : la: The race goes under the ten arches: the Games Clearing, the north, the western pools, the Circle, the south, the forge, the Watchtower… and back. Don't cut through the trees: the arches count.
textes.La cuisine des petits Moaïs : un four cr: The little Moai's kitchen: an oven dug into the ground, gourds, and a lot of patience.
textes.La dalle glisse dans un raclement. Une é: The slab slides away with a scrape. A ladder descends into the dark… and a cool breath rises up.
textes.La dalle ne bouge pas d'un cheveu. Il ma: The slab doesn't budge an inch. Something is missing to open it. The little Moai might know…
textes.La dalle s'enfonce sous ton poids !: The slab sinks under your weight!
textes.La danse de la lune raconte l'histoire d: The moon dance tells the story of the she-wolf who saved the moon when it fell into the pond. The moment she lifts it out of the water… that's when everyone raises their arms. You'll see.
textes.La date de la création du monde: The date of the creation of the world
textes.La dernière Furie s'enfuit en hurlant («: The last Fury flees, screaming (“We'll be back! We never come back.”). The great iron gate of Dité creaks, glows red… and opens.
textes.La dernière fois, cela ressemblait à un: Last time, it looked like a mushroom.
textes.La dernière fois, il est venu payer. Une: Last time, he came to pay. One coin, with great ceremony, in front of witnesses. I got out my notebook and calculated the interest since the day of the apple: four hundred and twelve coins and change. He went pale. I refused his coin. A debt doesn't get paid back at a discount.
Last time, I told you about %s.
Last time, I told you about %s.
textes.La dernière fois, tu n'avais pas assez b: Last time, you hadn't drunk enough. So, today? Show me your water bottle.
textes.La dernière pluie d'étoiles filantes a f: The last shower of shooting stars cracked three lenses of Zénith's great telescope. To cast new ones, he needs three meteorite fragments that fell on the island that night. After that, he'd like to show you the Night of the Auroras through the repaired telescope.
textes.La dernière vanne ! L'eau monte jusqu'au: The last sluice! The water rises to the brim, and the chinampas form a floating path to the opposite shore. Just like in the time of the Sun of Water, when men became fish…
textes.La dernière, la plus belle !: The last one, the most beautiful!
textes.La deuxième borne. Des chameaux sont gra: The second marker. Camels are engraved on its sides, in a line. The arrow still points northeast.
textes.La deuxième fois que je suis montée là-h: The second time I went up there, Queen Oriane told me the tree was sick. She asked me if I'd have the courage to go inside it, into the great trunk. I said no. I was so scared, {surnom}. Since then, I give my mushrooms to people who look braver than me. I watch them go. I'm a bit ashamed.
textes.La deuxième, la Perle de l'Épave, est l': The second, the Wreck Pearl, is the age of humans: sailors stole it, and their ship, “The Black Mermaid”, sank to the west. It stayed in the captain's chest.
The management approves of the cloud.
textes.La direction ne fait pas de commentaire,: The management has no comment, madame.
textes.La direction vous remercie. Le sujet ?: The management thanks you. The subject?
textes.La fameuse tourte de Mamie Rissole, la c: Mamie Rissole's famous pie (she's the Guild's cook): a golden crust, vegetables, mushrooms, melted cheese, and a secret she has never told anyone. Master Hugues eats three a day. Restores three hearts.
textes.La femme de chambre. Une personne très…: The chambermaid. A very… observant person. Too much so. She has turned my work into a topic of conversation. I remain polite. It is difficult.
textes.La fierté de Gustave Fiole, à L'Alambic: The pride of Gustave Fiole, at L'Alambic: moon dew, three drops of honey and a kind thought. It restores six points of magic.
textes.La fièvre des marais a couché la moitié: Marsh fever has laid up half the crew of the Veuve Écarlate. The Doc needs three tufts of feverweed, which grow at the water's edge in the Drowned Marsh.
textes.La flamme prend. Rien d'autre ne se pass: The flame catches. Nothing else happens… for now.
textes.La flamme prend… puis toutes les flammes: The flame catches… then all the flames snuff out at once, in a puff of sand. That was not the course of the sun.
textes.La fleur de cristal frémit… et les cloch: The crystal flower trembles… and the bells start singing on their own. Listen closely, and watch which ones light up.
textes.La fleur de lune ! Ses pétales brillent: The moonflower! Its petals glow softly between your fingers, like a piece of night.
textes.La fleur de lune… l'eau de la source… la:
