textes.Le beffroi. Quatre cloches de bronze pen: The belfry. Four bronze bells hang beneath the spire, each marked with a sign: the Wave, the Sun, the Moon, the Wind. They wait to be rung… in the right order.
textes.Le bleu ! Et il n'a même pas pris l'eau: The blue! And it didn't even get wet! (He turns the pot every which way and sniffs it.) It smells like the sky. Quick, go pour it into the Palette: paint cup number one, the very first. I want to see the pond turn blue from here. Here, for your trouble: two apples from my apple tree. They're still white, but they taste very good.
textes.Le bleu de l'Étang Gommé: The blue of the Rubbed-Out Pond
textes.Le bleu. Là-bas, tu vois ? Sur le grand: The blue. Over there, see? On the big water lily, in the middle. Pot number one, the island's blue. It floated out there the day after the Downpour, and it hasn't budged since. Me, I swim like a pebble. A painted pebble, but a pebble. Would you fetch it for me? With the blue, the pond will find its sky again, and the stream its water. And I'll get my trade back.
textes.Le bloc ne bouge plus : le mur, ou l'aut: The block won't budge: the wall, or the other block, is holding it.
textes.Le blé est bien haut cette année. Nonno: The wheat is really tall this year. Nonno says it's thanks to the volcano.
textes.Le bois de l'île est bon. Le chêne des h: The island's wood is good. Highland oak especially. But the northern shepherds sell it for its weight in gold.
textes.Le bois, c'est surtout utile pour se cha: Wood is mostly good for keeping warm.
textes.Le bol fumant du robot des nouilles du M: The steaming bowl from the noodle robot at the Night Market: noodles, a golden broth, an egg, vegetables, and a smiley face drawn in sauce. Restores two and a half hearts.
textes.Le bout seulement. Le reste fond très bi: Just the toe. The rest melts very nicely.
textes.Le bras du robot plonge dans la marmite,: The robot's arm dives into the pot, stirs, drains, pours… “A NEO-RAMEN! CAREFUL, IT'S HOT!” It even takes a little bow.
textes.Le brasero de l'est flambe : le soleil s: The east brazier blazes: the sun rises.
textes.Le brasero de l'ouest flambe : le soleil: The west brazier blazes: the sun sets.
textes.Le brasero du nord s'allume : le soleil: The north brazier lights: the sun sleeps. All four flames roar together… and the great slab at the back slides upward.
textes.Le brasero du sud flambe : le soleil brû: The south brazier blazes: the sun burns at noon.
textes.Le brigadier ? Il a enquêté sur mes croi: The sergeant? He investigated my croissants like a crime against the state. And he comes to eat one every morning, “for inspection”. Annoying. But he says thank you.
textes.Le brigadier ? Le patient le plus fidèle: The sergeant? The most loyal and most discreet patient on the island. He patrols with his back in pieces and his cap perfectly straight. I admire him, and I scold him.
textes.Le brigadier Lefort est un homme d'ordre: Sergeant Lefort is a man of order and a very bad runner. I'm very fond of him. He'd happily give me a ticket.
textes.Le brigadier Lefort fait des rondes, mai: Sergeant Lefort does his rounds, but he always stops in front of the ice-cream shop. Always.
textes.Le brigadier Lefort vient me voir pour s: Constable Lefort comes to see me about his bad back. He doesn't want anyone to know, he still goes on patrol.
textes.Le brigadier Lefort, c'est un brave homm: Sergeant Lefort is a good man, stiff as a fish board. He does his rounds very seriously. And he always stops at the ice-cream stand. Always.
textes.Le brigadier achète quand même ses sardi: The sergeant still buys his sardines from me, every Tuesday. He asks for “six sardines, no comment”. I always put the nicest one on top, laughing. He pretends not to see it. But he tips his cap to me as he leaves. That's his way of saying thank you.
textes.Le brigadier, c'est mon voisin de la rue: The sergeant is my neighbour on Lighthouse Street. An upright man, stiff as a parasol pole. He says he'd have liked to be a lifeguard. I believe him.
textes.Le brigadier, c'est mon voisin et mon me: The sergeant is my neighbour and my best customer. Three ice creams a day, state secret. An upright man, with a soft spot for vanilla.
textes.Le bâton des sorciers d'Arcanelle, remis: The staff of the wizards of Arcanelle, presented at the Circle of Moonstones: wood from the Twisted Wood and a purple crystal. In hand, each spell costs one less point of magic. Damage: 6.
textes.Le bénitier géant s'entrouvre lentement…: The giant clam slowly opens a crack… In the hollow of its blue mantle shines the Pearl of the Garden, the age of life.
textes.Le cacao, c'est la boisson des dieux !: Cacao is the drink of the gods!
textes.Le cadeau de Lyra : son aiguille de cris: Lyra's gift: its crystal needle points towards the Mother Tree, to the east. With it, the boat can cross the mist of Bois-Doré.
textes.Le café du Café de la Bielle, passé sous: Coffee from the Crankshaft Café, pressure-brewed in a copper boiler. It would wake the dead, and it restores one heart.
textes.Le capitaine est toujours à l'heure. Enf: The captain is always on time. Well, almost.
textes.Le carnet sept dit : « Pied du Cœur-de-P: Notebook seven says: “Foot of Stoneheart. Fog. Saw nothing.” That's not true, {surnom}. It was clear. I saw the gate, from afar, at sunset. And I heard the mountain breathing, slowly, deeply. I ran for two days without stopping, all the way to Carène. I've never been back. Everyone thinks I just never had the time.
textes.Le carrefour. Quatre chemins partent ver: The crossroads. Four paths lead south: a red one, a black one, a white one, a yellow one. Which one leads to the Lords?
textes.Le cercle de champignons, au bord de la: The mushroom ring at the edge of the clearing will take you back to your beach whenever you wish.
textes.Le cercle de lumière te dépose dans la c: The circle of light sets you down in the fairy glade. Queen Oriane is waiting for you: the seed of Yggdrasil glows at the bottom of your bag.
textes.Le cerf-volant de Théo s'est envolé vers: Théo's kite has flown off towards the western hills.
textes.Le chant du berger, peint à la chaux sur: The shepherd's song, whitewashed on a board: “Three sheep on the ridge, in the morning sun; one in the valley, sulking in the thyme; two in the sheepfold, asleep by the fire. Count them in order, and the wind will open for you.”
textes.Le chantier naval de Port-Azur : ça sent: The Port-Azur shipyard: it smells of sawdust and tar. On the slipway, a schooner is taking shape, rib after rib…
textes.Le chapeau que je porte, c'était celui d: The hat I'm wearing was the Admiral's when she was little. She gave it to me after the night of the lantern, without a word, left on my scrubbing bucket. It's too big, I stuff paper in it. Nolwenn says it'll fit me in two years. I can't wait.
textes.Le chat a quatre genoux, Yaya, c'est de: The cat has four knees, Yaya, that's cheating!
The cat is looking at me. I'm looking away. It started it.
textes.Le chat ouvre un œil, te juge, et se ren: The cat opens one eye, judges you, and goes back to sleep. You're accepted.
textes.Le chat ronronne. Puis il te mord gentim: The cat purrs. Then it bites you gently, just for show. Then it purrs again.
textes.Le chef gobelin agite sa bannière en hur: The goblin chief waves his banner, yelling: “To me, gang!” Two goblins burst out of the bushes!
textes.Le chef gobelin baisse sa hampe… et char: The goblin chief lowers his pole… and charges, bellowing!
textes.Le chef-d'œuvre d'Octave : acier trempé,: Octave's masterpiece: tempered steel, brass guard. Damage: 6, and the third hit of a combo strikes half again as hard. Ready for the battles to come.
textes.Le chemin de Xibalba… on peut y descendr: The road to Xibalba… can we go down there?
textes.Le chemin tourne, tourne… et te ramène a: The path turns, and turns… and brings you back to the crossroads. Somewhere, dry laughter echoes. That wasn't the right path.
textes.Le chocolat chaud du Café Feedback, avec: Hot chocolate from the Feedback Café, with a cloud of cream. It warms your hands, your tummy and your heart. Restores one and a half hearts.
textes.Le cidre doux du verger de Père Gaubert,: Père Gaubert's sweet sparkling apple drink from his orchard, alcohol-free and fizzy, served nice and cold at "La Grenouille Repue". The bubbles tickle your nose. Restores one heart.
textes.Le ciel s'allume : des rideaux de lumièr: The sky lights up: curtains of green, pink and blue light ripple above Astralys. The Night of the Auroras begins!
textes.Le ciel s'assombrit d'un coup. Un éclair: The sky suddenly darkens. A bolt of lightning strikes the centre of the platform… An immense suit of armour steps out of it: LORD STORM, THE KNIGHT OF STORMS!
textes.Le cinquième soleil brille au-dessus du: The fifth sun shines above the fire… but it doesn't move. The gods had the same trouble: a motionless sun burns everything. It would need a great breath, that of Ehécatl, the wind.
textes.Le cinquième étage de l'Usine Grise: The fifth floor of the Grey Factory
textes.Le cinquième étage des Mille Marches: The fifth floor of the Thousand Steps
textes.Le cochonnet ? Moi je l'ai vu filer sous: The jack? I saw it shoot under a bench, near the fountain. But I'm too old to get down on all fours.
textes.Le cochonnet a roulé vers la fontaine, ç: The jack rolled towards the fountain, that I'm sure of. After that… a mystery.
textes.Le cochonnet, c'est Marcel qui l'a lancé: The jack — Marcel threw it too hard. It rolled towards the fountain, and after that, a mystery. We played with a pebble, a disgrace. Then we sulked, each at one end of the pitch. Three days. The three longest days of my life. His too: he came and sulked right next to me.
textes.Le codex des soleils, sur une peau de ce: The codex of the suns, painted on deerskin: in the middle, our sun, the fifth. Around it, the four suns before, each with its number in red dots, and arrows turning: 1, 2, 3, 4… then 5, at the centre.
textes.Le coffre bâille. Très grand. Avec une l: The chest yawns. Very wide. With a tongue. It wasn't a chest!
textes.Le coffre de la Mouette ! Tu l'as trouvé: The Seagull's chest! You found it right where I said? MY MAP WAS RIGHT! Gaston, write down the date!
textes.Le coffre de la chandelle s'ouvre… sur u: The candle's chest opens… to an old boot, and a note: “Missed! But at least this one doesn't bite.”
textes.Le coffre des livres est honnête, et pau: The books' chest is honest, and poor: a few coins, a vial of sap, and a bookmark.
textes.Le coffre du capitaine grince… Entre les: The captain's chest creaks… Among the moldy coins gleams the Pearl of the Wreck, the age of men.
textes.Le coffre du hibou ne mord pas : il grin: The owl's chest doesn't bite: it only creaks. Inside, on a velvet cushion, a silver key engraved with little owls.
textes.Le coffret qui est monté du sol contient: The casket that rose from the floor holds a piece of Osiris!
textes.Le copal crépite sur les braises, et une: The copal crackles on the embers, and a white, fragrant smoke rises toward the sun. Huitzilopochtli is pleased.
textes.Le corail ! Le miel ! La noix de coco !: The coral! The honey! The coconut! I'll grind, mix, and… look at that red! Here, it's all I have, but I'm also giving you my eternal admiration.
textes.Le corail rouge pousse lentement : un do: Red coral grows slowly: a finger's width per century. My sculptures are all over a thousand years old. So am I, almost.
textes.Le couloir des lames : quatre grandes la: The corridor of blades: four great blades swinging from wall to wall, some flagstones darker than the others… and sand at the end. Watch closely, and go at the right moment.
textes.Le crabe amoureux. Je l'ai inventé ce ma: The Crab in Love. I invented it this morning.
textes.Le crabe sentimental, Titou. Rien à voir: The sentimental crab, Titou. Totally different, it has more heart.
textes.Le cristal a brillé. Je l'ai vu d'ici. I: The crystal shone. I saw it from here. It doesn't shine for everyone. Here. Some coins. And when you feel hot, in summer, think of the lake. It will think of you.
textes.Le cristal bleu s'illumine, et le hall s: The blue crystal lights up, and the hall dissolves with a chime… You're back in the sun, in front of the ruined tower. (Odon, without looking up: “Floor 1. Noted.”)
textes.Le cristal est glacé. Il ne se passe rie: The crystal is icy. Nothing happens… for now.
textes.Le cristal pâlit, et les coraux pâlissen: The crystal is fading, and the corals are fading with it. In the evening, I sit among the basins and sing them the only song I know, my father's. I sing off-key. Ondine heard me, I think. She didn't say anything. If the corals go out, {surnom}, I won't know who to talk to any more.
textes.Le cœur de bois est tiède. La lumière l': The wooden heart is warm. The light reaches it, but too weakly: it must first pass through the three mirror-flowers.
textes.Le cœur du Roi Gélatineux : une grosse g: The heart of the Jelly King: a big green jelly that glows softly, with a tiny gold crown stuck on top. It still beats a little, like a happy pudding. Master Hugues has dreamed of it for twenty years.
textes.Le cœur lourd et les cordes légères. Ily: Heavy heart, light strings. Ilyria smiled at me this morning. Or perhaps she was smiling at the light.
textes.Le dauphin, j'y étais. Momo dansait dans: The dolphin, I was there. Momo was dancing waist-deep in the water, arms in the air, and a dolphin swam by ten metres away. It jumped once and left. Momo turned round shouting: “Did you see? It's dancing with me!” I gave him two thumbs up. The dolphin made no comment.
The last one had a rubber ring too.
textes.Le dernier bouquet retombe en pluie d'or: The last bouquet falls back in a golden rain. The whole meadow applauds. Clapotis shouts: “I SAW SOME! REAL ONES!” And Bouton-d'Or places a crown of daisies on his head.
textes.Le dernier coup d'un enchaînement frappe: The last blow of a combo hits twice as hard, and every blow has a one-in-eight chance to be critical.
textes.Le dernier couplet ! Il n'existe pas enc: The last verse! It doesn't exist yet: first you need a King. The Brawl King is the one who puts the three champions of the harbor on the mat. Gros-Louis, of the Requin Borgne. Le Muet, of the Veuve Écarlate. Belle-Humeur, of the Morue Enragée. With fists, no blades: otherwise it doesn't count. A fair duel, or a good brawl, as you like. And after that… I sing!
textes.Le dernier cristal s'illumine ! Très loi: The last crystal lights up! Far away, in the Rose of Seals, a long rumble… The circle of light beside the dais will take you there.
textes.Le dernier jaguar tombe. Dans le silence: The last jaguar falls. In the silence, the jaguar head on the altar opens its mouth: a small casket has appeared in it.
textes.Le dernier. Le héros ne fait pas trois m: The last one. The hero isn't ten feet tall.
textes.Le deuxième jour sans appareil, une vagu: On the second day without a camera, a wave filled his moat and he fell into it bottom first. He laughed. Head thrown back, sand right into his ears. I reached for my camera, out of habit. It wasn't there. So I laughed too. We laughed like two seals. Nobody took our picture.
textes.Le deuxième jour, Kiki a accroché une pa: On the second day, Kiki hung a sign on the beach hut: “Wedding ring lost. Reward: one punch.” All afternoon, tourists searched the sand in front of the bar. They found a bottle cap, a sandal and a very offended crab. Kiki gave them the punch anyway. He said it was for the effort.
textes.Le deuxième jour, il me racontait une hi: On the second day, he was telling me a story about a giant octopus, standing at the bow, arms spread wide: “And then it opened its tentacles, like this!” Splash. The sea was flat as a millpond, not a ripple. I fished him out with the boathook, by his belt, like a sack of potatoes. He finished his story dripping wet.
textes.Le deuxième soir où elle pleurait sur le: The second evening she was crying on the balcony of room seven, I had a tray sent up: tea, two biscuits, and a card with the hotel letterhead. On it I wrote, in my finest hand: “The management sympathises.” Nothing more. The management, in this case, was me. But the phrase carries more authority.
textes.Le deuxième soir, on a frappé à la porte: On the second evening, there was a knock at the door of room seven. A tray, a teapot, two cups (two!) and a little handwritten card, in very upright writing: “The management sympathises.” No signature. I didn't drink the second cup. But I left it on the table, just in case.
textes.Le deuxième verre est fort comme l'amour: The second glass is strong as love… Here.
textes.Le diamant se pose, ça crépite… « Flaque: The needle drops, it crackles… “Puddles in Minor,” by the Gutters. A guitar creaking softly, a voice whispering. Outside, the rain keeps the beat.
textes.Le dimanche matin, Mistral a passé un mo: On the Sunday morning, Mistral played a really soft track, and everyone turned towards the sea. The sun came up out of the water, pink, enormous. I cried without knowing why. My boat home went by at eight, right in front of me. I waved at it. So good. That was three weeks ago.
textes.Le dimanche soir, je monte la soupe au p: On Sunday evenings, I carry the soup up to the lighthouse in a pot wrapped in three tea towels. Three hundred and twenty steps. If I dawdle, it arrives lukewarm, and Anselme eats it lukewarm without a word. If I hurry, it arrives hot, and he eats it hot without a word. I hurry anyway.
textes.Le dimanche, elle frappe trois coups, el: On Sundays, she knocks three times, comes up, sets down the soup. We eat without talking, facing the sea. When I leave some bread, she says: “Anselme Vasseur, finish your plate.” Like to a little boy. I'm past sixty. I finish my plate.
textes.Le dire au capitaine Charbonnel (à la ca: Tell Captain Charbonnel (at the port's harbour master's office)
textes.Le dire au capitaine Pyrus (à la porte d: Tell Captain Pyrus (at the palace gate, or at the barracks)
textes.Le dire à Crochet (sur le quai le matin,: Tell Crochet (on the quay in the morning, at the forge in the afternoon, at the Shark's Tooth in the evening)
textes.Le dire à Cuauhtli, le grand prêtre (au: Tell Cuauhtli, the high priest (at the foot of the Great Temple)
textes.Le dire à Ix Kanul, la grande prêtresse: Tell Ix Kanul, the high priestess (at the temple, or at the Cenote in the morning)
textes.Le dire à Madame Hurla (au guichet de l': Tell Madame Hurla (at the arena ticket booth, or on the square)
textes.Le dire à Mixtli, le guerrier-jaguar (su: Tell Mixtli, the jaguar warrior (on the square of Aztlán)
textes.Le dire à Néferet, la prêtresse de Rê (a: Tell Néferet, the priestess of Ra (at the temple of Per-Hâpy)
textes.Le dire à Pigment (au Mur d'Expression l: Tell Pigment (at the Expression Wall in the morning, near the water tower or the skatepark in the afternoon, at the print shop in the evening)
textes.Le dire à Tom le Violoneux (au Crâne Fen: Tell Tom the Fiddler (at the Crâne Fendu, in the evening)
textes.Le dire à Yvon (sur son ponton de pêche,: Tell Yvon (on his fishing jetty, by the lake)
textes.Le dire à Zébuline (à son étal d'épices: Tell Zébuline (at her spice stall in the Great Market)
textes.Le dire à l'Archiduchesse Ignatia (au pa: Tell Archduchess Ignatia (at the palace, on the Citadel)
textes.Le dirigeable de Cliquetis se pose maint: The airship from Cliquetis lands north of the village now, on the landing field. The engineers get off, look at our bridges, take notes. They think our bridges sway too much. That's the point.
textes.Le disque des deux villages: The disc of the two villages
textes.Le disque tourne, le diamant crépite…: The record spins, the needle crackles…
textes.Le distributeur affiche : « Merci ! Bonn: The machine displays: “Thank you! Have a nice evening, human!” Clonk! A Synth-Soda.
textes.Le distributeur hésite, réfléchit, puis: The machine hesitates, thinks, then: clonk! “On the house.” It's nice, this machine.
textes.Le dixième jour, on jouait dans les vagu: On the tenth day, we were playing in the waves. He raised his hand to splash me, he was laughing, and I saw it: his finger was bare. He looked at his hand as if it belonged to someone else. I said nothing. I got out of the water, went up to the balcony, and didn't say another word to him. I watched the sea. At least it knew where the ring was.
The tenth was for the echo.
textes.Le docteur Amélie est la femme la plus g: Doctor Amélie is the kindest woman on the island. I'm avoiding her a bit at the moment. Nothing serious. Hop hop hop!
textes.Le docteur Roux soigne tout avec des tis: Doctor Roux treats everything with herbal teas. Hers didn't cure a thing, but it smelled so good that I stopped crying to breathe it in.
textes.Le dragon… il a mangé mes chaussettes…: The dragon… he ate my socks…
textes.Le drap tombe : c'est un enfant du quart: The sheet falls: it's a kid from the neighborhood, delighted. “Really? Great! Here, my treasure, for your courage!”
textes.Le dôme fait quatre-vingt-douze pas de l: The dome is ninety-two paces wide. I counted them. Twice. The second time I got ninety-three.
textes.Le fanzine de Port-Boucan, imprimé par A: Port-Boucan's fanzine, printed by Agrafe at the Spinning Mill print shop: drawings by Pigment, Lentille's soup recipe, gossip from Radio Boucan, and a whole page about this week's stand-in drummer.
textes.Le fer, on le trouve au nord, dans les h: Iron is found in the north, in the highlands. The shepherds dig it out of the rocks and sell it to the caravanners, who sell it on to us for twice the price.
textes.Le fer, ça ne ment pas. Et le tien, il c: Iron doesn't lie. And yours, how much does it cost?
textes.Le feu ! Enfin quelqu'un qui demande le: Fire! At last, someone who asks for fire and not light! Fine. Rule number one: fire must be fed. Go and fetch me three logs of twisted wood from the Twisted Wood, to the southwest. Twisted wood burns long and without smoke. Bring them back, and I'll teach you.
textes.Le feu de Teotihuacan, où les dieux atte: The fire of Teotihuacan, where the gods waited for one of their own to throw himself in and become the sun. On one altar, the rich offerings of Tecciztécatl; on the other, the humble offerings of Nanahuatzin. What will you throw into the fire?
textes.Le feu de la forge est bon. Donc moi aus: The forge fire is good. So I'm good too.
textes.Le fil d'or autour, c'est le vent qui l': Then it was the wind that tied the golden thread round them.
textes.Le filet, je m'en moque, {surnom}. Je pe: I don't care about the net, {surnom}. I can tell you that, you of all people. That morning, it was Fernand who was beside Marius. Not me. I was watching from above. I hold it against him that he was in my place. It isn't fair, I know. It changes nothing.
textes.Le flacon brun du Doc Saignée : rhum, mi: Doc Saignée's brown flask: molasses, honey, feverweed and a secret. One sip, and you get back up from almost any brawl. Restores four hearts.
textes.Le fleuve de la nuit se met à bouillonne: The river of night begins to boil. An enormous head rises from the black water, eyes red as embers: APOPHIS, the serpent of chaos, who wants to swallow the sun!
textes.Le flotteur est à l'eau. Patience…: The float is in the water. Patience…
textes.Le fond du puits. Au nord, une caverne s: The bottom of the well. To the north, a cavern opens onto still, black water. (The chain lets you climb back up in one go.)
textes.Le four de terre ! On creuse, on chauffe: The earth oven! We dig, we heat the stones, we bury, we wait, we dig it up. It's ready in three hours. Or three hundred years. I never remember.
textes.Le fromage des chèvres des cendres de Hi: Cheese from Hilda's ash goats. It smells strong. Restores two hearts.
textes.Le gardien du phare. Un homme taciturne: The lighthouse keeper. A taciturn man who holds, without knowing it, the greatest discovery of the century in a logbook. He won't talk about it. He lets me climb up. It's a start.
textes.Le gel. Hm. Il faut de la patience. Vous: Frost. Hm. It takes patience. Do you have any? We'll see. On the northern cliffs, where the wind never stops, fall flakes that never melt: the eternal frost. Bring me three. Without running. Frost doesn't like it when you run.
textes.Le gobelet en plastique dit : « Un seul: The plastic cup says: “One glass per visit. Hydration is a cost.”
textes.Le gobelin lâche un cri aigu… et détale: The goblin lets out a shrill cry… and scurries off squealing! How brave.
textes.Le godet est planté dans le sol ! Les du: The bucket is stuck in the ground! The hoses are exposed: STRIKE THEM!
textes.Le godet se lève… Un cercle rouge au sol: The bucket rises… A red circle on the ground: get out of it!
textes.Le gong ne veut rien dire tant qu'on n'e: The gong means nothing until you're signed up. Madame Hurla runs the arena's ticket window: she registers the contestants (and she shouts very loudly).
textes.Le goudron non plus. Et pourtant, il se: Neither does tar. And yet it keeps quiet.
textes.Le grand air, enfin… s'il sentait autre: The open air, at last… if only it smelled of something other than sulphur.
textes.Le grand serpent des abysses… Faelar dit: The great serpent of the deep… Faelar says you defeated it. If that's true, I take back what I said about you. Some of it.
textes.Le grand serpent s'est réveillé ? Alors: The great serpent has woken up? Then you'll need a good blade and lots of coconuts. I'll give you a discount. No, I'm joking, I never give discounts.
The big shipyard register is open. Yannick wrote in it: “Orders to be noted here, payment in the box, I build at night (and I sing).”
textes.Le gâteau de lune, c'est la recette de m: Mooncake is my grandmother's recipe: chestnut flour, honey, and a round of bean paste drawn like the moon. We eat it on festival night. So, every night.
textes.Le hall du Donjon des Mille Marches: The hall of the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps
textes.Le hamac du fond t'attend, toi qui dors: The hammock at the back is waiting for you, you who sleep like a baby. I shook it out this morning. Gently.
textes.Le hamac du fond, à bâbord. Le Léviathan: The hammock at the back, on the port side. The Léviathan will rock you to sleep. Good night!
textes.Le hamac du fond, à côté des tonneaux. S: The hammock at the back, next to the barrels. If Tonneau snores, give him a thump, he's used to it.
textes.Le hibou, parce que sa femme est chouett: The owl, because his wife is a hoot!
textes.Le héron. Elle avait douze ans. Il m'a p: The heron. She was twelve. It took a perch from my basket. She shot off like an arrow, all the way round the big pond, faster than the bird. She came back with the perch in her arms, eyes shining. And I said: “A cat waits.” … What an old stick-in-the-mud I am.
textes.Le héros du cochonnet ! Assieds-toi, on: The hero of the jack! Sit down, we'll teach you.
textes.Le jaune ! Le bleu, on dirait la mer un: The yellow one! The blue one looks like the sea on a rainy day!
textes.Le jaune de la Grève Blanche: The yellow of the White Strand
textes.Le jeu de balle des Seigneurs. Une allée: The Lords' ball court. An alley, two slopes, two stone rings high up on the walls. The rubber ball, in the middle. “Play against us, traveller. Three times through the ring, and you pass.”
textes.Le jeune couple de l'hôtel dîne ici tous: The young couple from the hotel dine here every evening. He stares at his finger, she stares at the sea. There's a mystery there.
textes.Le jeune marié ! Il a retourné tout mon: The newlywed! He turned over my whole stretch of beach with my punch ladle. A nice boy. Very bad with a ladle.
textes.Le jeune marié de l'hôtel est venu me de: The young groom from the hotel came to ask if I could make a wedding ring “exactly the same”. I think he's done something silly.
textes.Le jeune marié de l'hôtel. Un gentil gar: The young newlywed from the hotel. A nice boy, a bad liar, like all nice boys. He did something silly: it's up to him to fix it, not me.
textes.Le jour de l'élection, la dernière boule: On election day, Aristide's last ball rolled, and rolled, and stopped “one centimetre away”. He raised his arms as if he'd won a war. He even cried a bit. I shouted “Thief!” I've been shouting it for eighteen years. He keeps the ball on his desk, on a red cushion, like a holy relic.
textes.Le jour de l'élection, la place entière: On election day, the whole square held its breath. Marcel lay down on the ground, tape measure between his teeth, and measured three times. He got up, dusted off his trousers and announced: “One centimetre.” Then he winked at me. For eighteen years I've wondered what that wink meant.
textes.Le jour de la chèvre, mon oncle a ri pen: The day of the goat, my uncle laughed for an hour. Then he saw me counting coins, and he stopped laughing. “A tanuki who sells!” He announced it to the whole market, like a disaster. But that evening he gave me my first purse. An old leather purse, empty. “So you can be ashamed properly,” he said.
textes.Le jour de la corde, les pattes de Bourr: The day of the rope, Bourru's paws were burnt. Pivoine treated them for a month. Every day. I forged her a balm spatula. Left it on her counter. Said nothing. She still uses it. I've seen.
textes.Le jour de la course, toute la plage éta: On race day, the whole beach was there. Bernard was warming up swinging his arms, I was doing push-ups. And the wind picked up. Red flag. The rules, I'm the one who enforces them: I had to raise the flag myself that cancelled my own race. Bernard shouted that I was scared. I shouted that it was the law. Seven years we've been shouting.
textes.Le jour de la fête du port, le maire fai: On the day of the harbour festival, the mayor gives his speech on the platform, right under the stopped clock face. He talks about the future, the season, progress. For half an hour, he doesn't look up once. Me, I look at the clock face, then at him, then at the clock face. He sweats. It isn't just the sun.
textes.Le jour de ma naissance, il a écrit mon: The day I was born, he wrote my name “Coralain”. I've asked him a hundred times to fix it. He says you don't scratch out a scroll: “The mistake is part of history.” So officially, the dome's first child is called Coralain. And I'm still the one who ends up in the scroll of mistakes.
textes.Le jour de ma naissance, j'ai soufflé to: On the day I was born, I blew every petal out of the throne room. The queen's hair was full of them. She didn't shout. She handed me a letter and said: “Since you can't stay still, go and be somewhere else.” I've never come back on time since. But I've always come back.
textes.Le jour de ma retraite, je lui ai donné: The day I retired, I gave her my satchel. The old leather one, with the buckle that sticks. I told her: “It knows the way, just let it carry you.” She still has it. She only re-stitched the strap. With yellow thread. Yellow! My satchel…
textes.Le jour de notre rencontre, Gérard a pho: The day we met, Gérard photographed my shoes, blue ones with little bows, instead of the pupils. He showed them to me afterwards, very proud: “Look at the light on the bow.” I still have those photos. They're sharp. The only ones of his life, perhaps. Which goes to show: you have to know what you're looking at.
textes.Le jour de sa naissance, Zéphyr a souffl: On the day he was born, Zéphyr blew every petal out of the throne room. I still had some in my hair the next day. I understood that a wind like that needed keeping busy. I gave him a letter. He has never stopped since.
textes.Le jour de son couronnement, Thorgal est: On the day of his coronation, Thorgal came to my alcove, alone, before the celebrations. He asked me: “Will I be a good king?” The runes said: “He will lose his crown a thousand times and find it a thousand and one.” I read them to him. He laughed. He loses it every day. He always finds it.
textes.Le jour des daurades, quand Paulo a crié: The day of the sea bream, when Paulo shouted “Day-old!”, I looked at Fernand. He was looking at his boots. I understood. I swore to Paulo they were caught that morning, and I paid Fernand the morning price, without a word. He never said thank you. But since then, on Mondays, he saves me his best sea bream.
textes.Le jour des quarante pains, je suis arri: On the day of the forty loaves, I came running into the square. It was raining honey loaves. The children were dancing, Faelar had one in each hand. And Sylwen, white as a sheet, was clinging to the railing. I helped her down, plank by plank. She didn't say a word. At the bottom, she gave me a loaf.
textes.Le jour du cochonnet, Raymond a lancé de: The day of the jack, Raymond threw crooked and the jack rolled off towards the fountain. I say under a bench. He says I shot like a klutz. Me! We sulked for three days, each on his own pitch, playing with a pebble. After three days, he came to ask me if my pebble rolled better than his.
textes.Le jour du record, j'ai dansé sur le pon: On record day, I danced on the south bridge with my ribbons, and Marée sold eighty crackers. She gave me ten. So I danced the saddest dance of my life in front of her stall. Nobody dared buy a thing. The next day, she paid me in coins. Three. It's a start.
textes.Le jour du « vol », j'étais au kiosque d: On the day of the “theft”, I was at Bruno's kiosk, sad as a coconut palm with no coconuts. He went to fetch milk from the back, and left a little notebook open on the counter: “Granny's Coconut Ice Cream”. I copied it all onto my arm, in pencil. I left proud as a pirate. For a week, I didn't wash that arm.
textes.Le jour où Fundin a trempé une lame roug: The day Fundin quenched a red-hot blade in my cauldron, I ran to the forge, spoon raised. Borin planted himself in front of his apprentice, arms wide: “It was for the salt.” The stew tasted of iron, and everyone thought it was better. Since then, I slip an old nail in, on the sly.
textes.Le jour où Ianthé a dansé sur le pont su: The day Ianthé danced on the south bridge with her seaweed ribbons, I sold eighty crackers. A record! To thank her, I gave her ten. She looked at me, then danced a very slow, very sad dance in front of the stall. I didn't sell another thing all day. The next day, I paid her in coins. Three.
textes.Le jour où elle est partie vivre à l'arb: The day she went to live in the Lookout tree, Dad stared at his float as if he wanted to drown it. Not a word. So I put down my fish knife and said: “She runs, Dad. Let her run.” He nodded. Éclair never said thank you. She looks at me, sometimes. Same thing.
textes.Le jour où elle est venue, elle s'est in: The day she came, she settled right at the front, at the bow, hair in the wind, and sang the whole crossing. Off-key, but loud. The passengers clapped when we arrived. And I knew right then that she wouldn't go back. People who sing at the bow never go back.
textes.Le jour où il est devenu garde, à vingt-: The day he became a guard, at twenty-five, I knitted him a red scarf, so he could be seen from afar in the mist. He found it too flashy. Thirty years later, he still wears it. He says it's for the cold. A stitch ran last winter: he darned it himself, all crooked. I said nothing.
textes.Le jour où il est reparti, son tablier é: The day he left, his apron was burnt all over, like a colander. I told him: “Not bad… for a big'un.” He grinned from ear to ear. He didn't know it's my highest compliment. Don't tell him. I say it to Octave too, but quieter.
textes.Le jour où j'ai inauguré le pont de l'ou: The day I opened the west bridge, Bedaine wanted to cross first, belly out, very proud. The wind got up. The bridge danced. The stones sang. And Bedaine turned all green! Seasick, on a bridge! Since then, he crosses it with his eyes shut, humming to drown out the stones.
textes.Le jour où j'ai parlé des signes sous la: The day I talked about the signs under the keel, Matthias ran to the pontoon with a notebook, no shoes on, and asked me forty questions. I said: “Come and see.” He swims badly. He came anyway, with a rope round his waist. He saw. He came up crying. He says it was the salt water.
textes.Le jour où j'ai perdu ma baguette, j'ai: The day I lost my wand, I had only one idea: hide my hands behind my back every time Zéphyr flew by. He carries everything to the queen, that chatterbox. Even secrets. Especially secrets. My arms ached for weeks.
textes.Le jour où j'ai quitté la cave d'Ulfa, j: The day I left Ulfa's cellar, I came up to the terrace with a sack of barley and red eyes. Dagna looked at me, said “You're hungry”, and opened up her old bread oven for me. It only heats on one side. Hot side, I make fizz. Cold side, I sleep. It suits us fine.
textes.Le jour où j'ai trempé une lame rouge da: The day I quenched a red-hot blade in Dagna's cauldron, I thought I was done for. Dagna was coming, ladle raised. Borin stepped in front of me, arms spread wide, and said: “It was for the salt.” Nobody had ever stood up for me like that. That evening, he made me sweep twice. Fair's fair.
textes.Le jour où j'étais coincée au deuxième p: The day I was stuck on the second floor, everyone was at the market. Nobody could hear me. And then Auntie came. Three leaps. She tucked me under her arm like a skewer, and hop, down. She just said: “… Shh.” Mummy doesn't know anything. Auntie and me have a secret.
textes.Le jour où je suis devenu garde, j'avais: The day I became a guard, I was twenty-five, with ears too stiff. Mère-Lune climbed up to the Lookout. She still climbed, back then. She tied this red scarf round my neck: “So they can see you from afar, little one. A guard should be seen.” Thirty years I've worn it. The moths tried. They lost.
textes.Le jour où je suis tombée dans le canal: The day I fell into the canal right at high tide, I kept dancing in the water, and Mum kept singing. Nausicaa laughed so hard she missed her verse. The only time in her life she's ever missed a verse. I remind her often. Very often.
textes.Le jour où la corde a cassé, elle avait: The day the rope snapped, she was sixteen. She braided the sixth rope all night, with Granny Faîne. Me, next to them, forging the hooks. All night. Not a word. Her neither, not a word. The only time. In the morning, the rope held. The hooks too. Hm. Good night, that one.
textes.Le jour où la corde a cassé, il y a dix: The day the rope snapped, ten years ago, the basket dropped all at once. Hulotte inside. Bourru caught the rope with his bare hands. I grabbed an iron bar and jammed the pulley. We said nothing to each other. Not that day, not after. But I know. And he knows.
textes.Le jour où la corde de la nacelle a cass: The day the basket rope snapped, I treated Bourru's paws, burnt by the rope. Ursule stood behind me, without a word, holding the pot of balm. When I'd finished, I saw her eyes. She'd been crying. She doesn't know I saw. She never will. That's why I forgive her for the hot water. Almost.
textes.Le jour où les abeilles d'en haut ont es: The day the bees up top swarmed, Gilwen couldn't climb: she's afraid of heights. I went up with her basket. I brought the swarm back. Forty stings. She said thank you, then she said I'd shaken them about. She's right. But I brought them back.
textes.Le jour où ma chèvre a dormi sur son trô: The day my goat slept on his throne, he summoned me to the Great Hall. I was trembling. He said: “A shepherdess whose goat finds the way to the throne all by herself knows how to lead.” And he put me in charge of his messenger crows. I never admitted the goat had simply got lost.
textes.Le jour où mon grand-père lui a vendu le: The day my grandfather sold him the logbook, I was fourteen and crying in the square. Ba Sidi, young and skinny back then, gave me a date and said: “Paper can be sold, little one. The story stays with you.” I ate the date. I hated him for twenty years. Then I understood.
textes.Le jour où on a inauguré son pont de l'o: The day we opened her west bridge, the whole village crossed it singing. The bridge swayed, the stones whistled… and me, in the middle, I got seasick. Seasick, my friend, over a pond! Since then, I cross it with my eyes shut. Pomme-de-Pin still laughs about it. My stomach's still up in my whiskers.
textes.Le jour où on lui a donné son nom, Dwali: On his naming day, Dwalin grabbed my ladle from his cradle and wouldn't let go. His father said: “He'll be a cook.” He carries coal. But every day, he stops by my kitchen and holds the ladle for a minute. He says it rests his back.
textes.Le jour où papa a perdu son appareil, il: The day Daddy lost his camera, he sat down next to my castle and looked at it. With his eyes. He said: “The left tower's leaning a bit.” He'd noticed! He even helped dig the moat. He's got big hands, it goes faster. He laughed when the wave came. Me too.
textes.Le jour où quarante pains de miel sont t: The day forty honey loaves fell off the footbridge, Taeron came running, looked at the plank and said: “Nothing wrong with it.” Then he took it out, carried it home, and never put it back. I say that's proof. He says it's a keepsake.
textes.Le jour où sa mère lui a passé la bousso: The day her mother handed her the Kerhervé compass, Morgane came to the tavern alone, in the evening, in a uniform too big for her. She asked for a sparkling apple and didn't say a word. I sat beside her until closing time. We said nothing. The next day, she was the Admiral.
textes.Le jour où son masque de plongée s'est f: The day her diving mask cracked, I gave her the best one on the stall, saying she'd pay me in pearls. She never did, and I never asked for anything. A diver without a mask is a merchant without pearls. It's business. There. Business.
textes.Le jour où tu es arrivé avec son épée, j: The day you showed up with his sword, I took it, weighed it, rang it on the anvil. A good sound. I said “not bad, for a big'un”, and I spent the night forging a better one. Fundin was asleep standing up against the bellows. Me, I was smiling. It was a good night.
textes.Le jour où tu es arrivé, Triton a couru: The day you arrived, Triton ran all the way to my workshop shouting: “A human! A real one!” Then he realised he'd left the Gate. First time in three hundred years. He dashed off so fast he knocked over three of my lamps. I billed him for them. Friend's price: double.
textes.Le jour où tu es arrivé, j'ai couru l'an: The day you arrived, I ran to tell Coralin. The square, two bridges, his workshop… and then it hit me: I'd left the Gate. First time in three hundred years. I dashed back so fast I knocked over three of his lamps. He billed me for them. Friend's price: double.
textes.Le jour tombe. Vous qui avez un peu peur: Day is falling. You who are a little afraid of the dark: look up. It's turning. I'm up there.
textes.Le jour, j'aime m'allonger contre les en: In the daytime, I like lying up against the speakers. It's a back massage.
In the daytime I sleep standing up. Forgive me.
textes.Le jour, je vérifie. Les câbles, le sabl: By day, I check. The cables, the sand in the knobs, the crabs in Raoul. By night, I nod my head next to Gaspard. When Mistral sleeps, I mind the desk. I don't change anything. A good sound, you don't change it. You keep it. Like a friend. … That was long, what I just said.
textes.Le jour, l'épicerie. Le soir, une tisane: By day, the shop. In the evening, a herbal tea at the café and a novel hidden behind the newspaper. I vote against the mayor. Rita foretells a great love for me, I pay. An English lord wants my jar of figs, I refuse. And a tourist blushed when I recommended my favourite novel to her. People are odd. Me, I'm normal.
textes.Le jour, la librairie. À l'heure dorée,: By day, the bookshop. At the golden hour, the lookout, where Clémence paints while I watch. I sold all my charts of the seabed to Professor Moreau, one by one. Madame Rita makes predictions for me, which I note down in a notebook. And I've received an old atlas of the Sky Kings: apparently there was once an island that flew! Can you imagine?
textes.Le journal du dernier capitaine du Lévia: The journal of the last captain of the Léviathan, bound in leather that still smells of salt. Whole pages are blank… Moon ink, Ba Sidi used to say: it can only be read by the light of a moon you carry with you.
textes.Le jury ? Oh ! Écoutez… (Le piano joue u: The jury? Oh! Listen… (The piano plays a waltz. The keys press themselves down. At the end, the piano takes a bow.) It plays better in the morning. It's a bit under the weather in the evening.
The jury sent me to see your automaton.
The jury sent me to see your machine.
The jury sent me to see your piano.
textes.Le lendemain de la grande tempête, la ba: The day after the big storm, Marley's banana grove was flattened. He was sitting in front of it, smiling anyway, which was worse than if he'd cried. I came with ropes. We stood every plant back up, one by one, for two days. He talked to every banana tree like a cousin.
textes.Le lendemain de la plage, en faisant la: The day after the beach, doing room seven, I found Léa's pillow soaking wet. Not seawater, mind: tears. I turned it to the dry side before she came back. That's what a chambermaid is for, too. And for keeping quiet, normally. Normally.
textes.Le lendemain de la tempête, j'étais assi: The day after the storm, I was sitting in front of my flattened banana trees, smiling, because that's what I do. Gaspard turned up with ropes. He said: “You're smiling too much, it worries me.” We stood everyone back up in two days. At the end, I cried a little. He handed me his water bottle, of course.
textes.Le lendemain de notre rencontre, je lui: The day after we met, I brought him a scarf woven from the seaweed he'd told me off for cutting. He was speechless for so long I thought I'd upset him. Then he asked: “How many did you cut?” I said: “One in three.” He married me the following year.
textes.Le lendemain, Pauline a plié les serviet: The next day, Pauline folded the towels in number seven into hearts. And the day after. A whole week of terry-cloth hearts: on the bed, on the washbasin, on the balcony railing. I said nothing. I'm still cross with her. A little less with every heart.
textes.Le lendemain, elle est descendue à la ré: The next day, she came down to reception, her eyes still red, and said to me: “Thank the management for me.” I replied: “I shall not fail to, madam.” I felt my ears go hot. Apparently she calls me “the gentleman with the moustache who sympathises”. I'm flattered. Discreetly.
textes.Le lendemain, il m'a offert un seau. Un: The next day, he gave me a bucket. A lovely blue bucket, with a ribbon: “For the great voyage, navigator.” I put it in the bookshop window, under the globe. Customers ask what it's doing there. I reply: “It's my equipment.”
textes.Le lendemain, je suis descendue à la réc: The next day, I went down to reception to thank “the management”. The gentleman with the moustache straightened up, went red to the ears and said: “The management takes note, madame.” Then he tidied the same pen three times. I think the management was him.
textes.Le maire ? Hm. Il envoie tout le monde m: The mayor? Hm. He sends everyone to say hello to me. Fine. Hello. The port is yours, don't get up to any mischief.
textes.Le maire chante sous la douche. On l'ent: The mayor sings in the shower. You can hear him from the harbour.
textes.Le maire chante sous sa douche ; on l'en: The mayor sings in the shower; you can hear him from the port. I told him he had the voice of a seal with a cold. I stand by it. Officially.
textes.Le maire cherche des gens serviables. Il: The mayor is looking for helpful people. He pays in smiles and coins, which is rare for a mayor.
textes.Le maire fera citoyen d'honneur celui qu: The mayor will make whoever helps out the whole town an honorary citizen.
The mayor sent me to say hello.
textes.Le maire me doit une pomme depuis quaran: The mayor has owed me an apple for forty years. I vote against him. It isn't a grudge, it's bookkeeping.
textes.Le maire parle très bien. Il promet très: The mayor speaks very well. He promises very well too. The clock was to be repaired “before the end of the year”: fourteen times. I have a notebook.
textes.Le maire veut que je fasse connaissance: The mayor wants me to get to know the town: the harbour master's office, the hotel and the tavern.
textes.Le maire, je l'ai connu serveur : douze: The mayor, I knew him as a waiter: twelve cups on the first day. He's become a good mayor. A bit long-winded in his speeches, but still.
textes.Le marché est dans la cale du Léviathan,: The market is in the Léviathan's hold, at the back. By day, you come in through the great breach on the beach side. Beyond the stalls, the hold is underwater: that's the basin, where the boats come in.
textes.Le masque des Rois-Ciel : tu respires so: The Sky Kings' mask: you can breathe underwater! Explore the depths… southwest of the village, a light shines at the bottom.
textes.Le masque des Rois-Ciel, trouvé dans le: The mask of the Sky Kings, found in Lord Storm's treasure: crystal lenses rimmed with brass. As long as it's in your bag, you can breathe underwater. The Sky Kings used it to visit… a sunken city?
textes.Le matin après le rocher, j'étais assis: The morning after the rock, I was sitting on the sand, soaked, my hammer on my knees. A raft of rolled-up maps drifted past offshore, Barnabé on top, shouting: “The map was right!” I shouted: “Row!” Those were the last kind words we said to each other.
textes.Le matin de la lumière bleue, toute la t: The morning of the blue light, the whole tavern was laughing at Grégoire. I had him come up to the harbour office, made him tell it all twice, and marked the spot with an ink cross on the big map. I didn't smile. I didn't feel like it at all. Since then, every evening, I look in that direction.
textes.Le matin de mon sacre, je suis allé voir: On the morning of my coronation, I went to see Nori, alone, to ask whether I'd be a good king. He read a rune and said: “You will lose your crown a thousand times and find it a thousand and one.” I thought it was a prophecy. It was an observation. I lose my crown every day.
textes.Le matin du dauphin, Lucas était au bout: The morning of the dolphin, Lucas was at the end of the quay with a crate on his shoulder. He put it down and said “dolphin”. All by himself, without me asking! Then he put me on his shoulders to see if the dolphin came back. It didn't. But from up there you can see all the boats, and even Léon's cap.
textes.Le matin et l'après-midi, je plonge au b: Mornings and afternoons, I dive off the end of the pontoon. At noon, I eat on the dock pontoon, feet in the water. Ewen counts my seconds and gets it wrong. Matthias wants me to draw the stones underwater. With a pencil. In the evening, at the beach fire, I stay quiet. It's my favourite moment.
textes.Le matin et le soir, je joue à la fontai: In the morning and the evening, I play at the fountain. In the afternoon, it's the beach. Sometimes there's Théo, the hotel baby, who cried for days over his kite. And there's Brioche! He's a little all-white dog, I'm the one who named him. He's not mine. Not yet. I threw a coin in the fountain to get a dog. That counts, right?
textes.Le matin où Celebrë avait perdu sa voix,: The morning Celebrë lost her voice, nothing came into my nets. I told her to whistle. She whistled, and three rays came. Ever since, I keep telling her the light prefers whistling, to tease her. It's not true. The light prefers her voice. So do I.
textes.Le matin où j'ai parlé de la lumière ble: The morning I told them about the blue light, the whole tavern was already laughing. The Admiral called me up to the harbour master's office, had me tell it all twice, and marked the spot on her chart with a cross. A cross in ink. She didn't smile once. I'm grateful to her for that.
textes.Le matin où la Murène Noire est entrée d: The morning the Murène Noire sailed into the bay, I went out to meet her in Fañch's boat, standing in the stern. Croc-de-Sel shouted from his deck: “Admiral of what?” I pointed to the smoking gunports: “Of that.” He looked for a long time. Then he came about. As he left, he saluted me with his tricorn. I didn't respond.
textes.Le matin, j'ai toujours plein d'idées. L: In the morning I'm full of ideas. By the afternoon, I've forgotten them.
textes.Le matin, je fais des châteaux devant la: In the morning, I make castles in front of the beach hut. Kiki gives me coconut halves for the towers. Sometimes I go and see Clémence at the lookout, she let me paint a sky. In the evening, at the fountain, there's Nina, she calls me baby. I'm not a baby. And Daddy takes pictures of everything. Well, when he's got his camera.
textes.Le matin, je joue sur les bancs de la pl: In the morning, I play on the benches in the square; Hortense taps out the beat, more accurate than a metronome. In the evening, the stage at the Perroquet. I live on the Rue Haute, between Lola and Lucas: I hear things, I don't repeat them. The mayor sings in the shower. And a painter drew me with my mouth open, like a grouper. I play in profile.
textes.Le matin, je m'assois près de la cloche: In the morning, I sit by the bell and tell stories to the seagulls. In the afternoon, at the rail, to the fishermen mending nets. In the evening, by the stove of the Bordée, to anyone who'll listen. Ewen writes my letters, because my hand shakes, and he corrects my stories while he's at it. That boy ruins everything. I adore him.
textes.Le matin, je prête dix lucioles à Perlée: In the morning, I lend ten fireflies to Perlée for her rounds. In the evening, three to Noisette to sort her seeds. At night, I feed them honey. Zéphyr says they only love me for the honey. He's jealous. Oh, and there's another Lumi, down below, in the elves' roots! We write to each other. Zéphyr mixes us up all the time.
textes.Le matin, je sonne les heures. Après, je: In the morning, I ring the hours. After that, I carry messages, I write Corentin's letters to the bear in Ramure, I count how long Lucie stays underwater, and in the evening I light the lantern for my grandad. And I ask Tobias how you put a ship back in the water. He sighs. But he answers a bit, now.
textes.Le matin, je suis un scarabée qui pousse: In the morning, I am a scarab pushing a ball of fire. At noon, a falcon shining above the world. In the evening, an old man with a ram's head who descends into the night. Who am I?
textes.Le matin, je vends le poisson de papa. L: In the morning, I sell Dad's fish. In the afternoon, grilled skewers, which I invented: perch, sardine, perch, a pinch of pond salt. Croc-Gris has one every day at noon, Grisou too, on the run, without stopping. I never taste the merchandise. I check it's cooked. That's not the same. Mrrr.
textes.Le matin, l'air sent bon. C'est le meill: The air smells lovely in the morning. It's the best time for thinking.
textes.Le matin, la boutique. L'après-midi, le: Mornings, the shop. Afternoons, the jetty. Evenings, the beach hut, a fruit punch with Kevin, who counts up the customers he's fished out for me. Odette threatening to tell the mayor — three seasons and counting. And Félix, the bookseller: I took him out on a pedalo, he went green three metres from the jetty. Now he draws me routes. From the quay.
textes.Le maître dit, le maître dit… Et toi, tu: Master says, master says… And you, have you eaten?
textes.Le maître est redevenu normal ! Enfin… i: The master is back to normal! Well… he still feels like eating flies sometimes. Thanks again!
textes.Le maître sorcier, redevenu humain, rega: The master wizard, human again, looks sternly at his apprentice. His skin is still a little green.
textes.Le meilleur coin de pêche ? Le bout de l: The best fishing spot? The end of the jetty, at nightfall. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Le meilleur moment à Port-Azur ? Six heu: The best time in Port-Azur? Six in the morning, when the boats come in and the sun rises behind the lighthouse.
textes.Le meilleur moment, c'est le lever du so: The best moment is sunrise. Mistral plays a really soft track and everyone watches the sea.
textes.Le meilleur parcours ? De la fontaine ju: The best route? From the fountain to the lighthouse: the high street, the quay, then the climb up the point. Nobody does it in under eighty seconds. Except me. Well, I used to.
textes.Le meilleur porteur. Hé oui. C'est déjà: The best carrier. Yep. That's something.
textes.Le meilleur, Salomé. Le meilleur. Et c'e: The best one, Salomé. The best one. And that's me.
textes.Le miel vient des abeilles des grands ar: The honey comes from the bees in the tall trees. Pomme-de-Pin climbs up to fetch it, right to the top. She always comes down with three stings and a smile.
textes.Le mieux, c'est quand la marée monte pen: The best bit is when the tide comes in while we're dancing. We end up with our feet in the water.
textes.Le milieu ! Regarde : tout autour, j'ai: The middle! Look: all around, I've drawn the coasts, the moors, the marshes, the dunes… and in the centre, a big blank. Stoneheart. At the foot of its west face there's a door, the Door of the Four Seals. I've never dared go up there alone: they say the mountain breathes. You, you don't look afraid. Go and see it, examine it closely, and come back and tell me.
textes.Le minerai de la montagne est le meilleu: The mountain's ore is the best in the world. Red as rust, heavy as an oath.
textes.Le mois dernier, Titou m'a emprunté mes: Last month, Titou borrowed my last six glow sticks to juggle. “Look, Lila, a rainbow!” The fourth went into the sea, the fifth into Nono's hair, the sixth I don't know where. Since then I haven't had any, and I tell newcomers to dance with their hands.
textes.Le mois dernier, un pêcheur s'est tartin: Last month, a fisherman smeared his back with Salomé's balm for a sunburn. He came to see me that evening, red as a lobster and smelling of cake. I treated the sunburn. The next day, Salomé had written on her stall: “Recommended by the infirmary”. I wiped off the chalk myself.
textes.Le mois dernier, une voie d'eau s'est ou: Last month, a leak opened right under my forge. Tobias sent someone for good timber, and in the meantime he plugged it with whatever was to hand. My feet were in the water, his nose was in the tar, and he said: “Don't move, or I'll caulk you in with it.” I didn't move.
textes.Le mois où Tilleul a reçu tous les compt: The month Tilleul got all of Bedaine's accounts, my father was sure he'd delivered right: “North tree, third door.” It was the pond tree. Bedaine was looking everywhere for his accounts, Tilleul was telling them to everyone like a story. That day, I took the satchel. My father said thank you. He looked relieved. So did I, a little.
textes.Le mois où j'ai livré les comptes de Bed: The month I delivered Bedaine's accounts to Tilleul's, I was sure of myself: third door, north tree. Tilleul read them with great interest, he thought it was a story. Bedaine thought it was a theft. Plumette took the mailbag the next day, without a word. She was right. Me, I had a shooting star to write down.
textes.Le moment ? LE moment ? (Elle pose sa ta: The time? THE time? (She puts down her cup.) One, two… (She looks at the stage, the canvas, you.) … THREE. (She puts her finger on the middle button, the one with no name, and pushes it all the way up. The speakers switch on with a great gust, all over the meadow.) Ten years I've been waiting. Tonight, at eight thirty, we play. Both villages. Come, and stand at the front: I want to see someone dancing in the first row.
The gentleman with the moustache who sympathises. He didn't tell anyone, at least. In this hotel, that's practically a miracle.
textes.Le monte-charge grince, cliquette et mon: The freight lift creaks, rattles and climbs… and climbs… (with a little elevator tune, very optimised)… then opens in the Grey Factory courtyard, in broad daylight. The Lisse-Center plans are in your bag. Port-Boucan is going to party!
textes.Le morceau du lever de soleil n'a pas de: The sunrise track has no name. So every morning I suggest one. “Hello Sea”. “Zoé Stays”. “Jelly Legs”. I'm up to twenty-one. He says “not bad” every time. I don't think he'll ever choose. And I think I'm fine with that.
textes.Le moteur s'essouffle… et s'arrête. Les: The engine wheezes… and stops. The platforms come to a halt.
textes.Le moteur à cristal des Lumens : silenci: The Lumens' crystal engine: silent as a dreaming fish, it leaves a trail of light behind it. Seventy percent faster than sail alone!
textes.Le moteur à cristal se monte à la place: The crystal engine goes in where the steam engine was. Steam first, stars after!
textes.Le moteur à vapeur, d'après les plans de: The steam engine, from Cliquetis's plans: a boiler, a smoking chimney, a propeller that churns the water. Thirty percent faster. Choo-choo… er, sorry: toot-toot!
The sound wall? Twenty-four speakers. I know them all by their first names.
textes.Le musée secret du canard en caoutchouc: The secret rubber duck museum! One hundred forty-four ducks, arranged by size. And a sign: “DO NOT SQUEAK THEM.”
textes.Le mystère ! Tu me plais, toi. Ceux qui: The mystery! I like you. People who love mysteries are the only ones who listen right to the end. The others skip to the last page.
textes.Le même prix que la semaine dernière, l': Same price as last week, my friend.
textes.Le même que la dernière fois !: The same one as last time!
textes.Le même que la dernière fois ! Il était: The same one as last time! It was very stable.
textes.Le nectar doré de Mélisse, cueilli au cœ: Mélisse's golden nectar, gathered from the heart of the giant flowers. Restores four hearts.
textes.Le neuvième jour, je l'ai trouvé assis s: On the ninth day, I found him sitting on a stone at the edge of the mist, watching a snail cross the path. He said: “Shh, he's nearly there.” I waited with him. The snail got there. Then we went home. I never admitted that I was glad to see it arrive, too.
textes.Le nez de la statue du roi Atlas, c'est: The nose on King Atlas's statue? That's me. The old one had been broken since the flood. I tried to redo the king's from the fresco, and… it came out my way. The queen looked at it for a long time, then said: “My great-grandfather would have laughed.” I take that as a compliment. Free, again.
textes.Le noir. Hm. Allume une forge, il s'en v: The dark. Hm. Light a forge, it goes away. Come at closing time, if you like.
textes.Le nord, jusqu'où ? Et jusqu'à quand ?: North, how far? And until when?
textes.Le noyau encore chaud d'un élémentaire d: The still-warm core of a magma elemental. Grimli the miner uses them to light his tunnels.
textes.Le pain ! (Elle soupire de soulagement.): The bread! (She sighs with relief.) The Baron had already taken out his mourning hat. I'll take it to him right away. Thank you. You've saved the castle's morning. That's no small thing: it's often in danger.
textes.Le pain de Trèfle, la boulangère de Ramu: Bread from Trèfle, the baker of Ramure: soft, golden, made with carrots from the rabbits' vegetable garden. Restores two hearts.
textes.Le pain doré de Sylwen, la boulangère du: The golden bread of Sylwen, the baker of Bois-Doré. It smells of honey and sunshine. Restores two hearts.
textes.Le pain, on le range dans le tiroir ou d: Do we keep bread in the drawer or in the bread box?
textes.Le panier de livraison de Margaux, rempl: Margaux's delivery basket, full of baguettes and croissants. No helping yourself.
textes.Le panier remonte en grinçant… Au fond,: The basket creaks up… At the bottom, a small, dented paint pot with a label: “5”. + Pot of brown (no. 5). To be poured into its well in the Stone Palette!
textes.Le papillon s'envole. Brioche le regarde: The butterfly flutters away. Brioche watches it go, very dignified: “I was letting it go.”
textes.Le papyrus de Thot, le dieu à tête d'ibi: The papyrus of Thoth, the ibis-headed god, scribe of the gods. Thoth points to a cartouche — the king's name, written from top to bottom: three signs, one beneath the other. Look at them carefully.
textes.Le parvis du Temple-Passoire — une fourc: The forecourt of the Colander Temple — a giant fork and spoon, a sauce fountain… and, up there, the Great Flying Spaghetti
textes.Le passage est libre ! La galerie sous l: The way is clear! The gallery under the sea now links the two islands.
textes.Le perroquet a vendu la mèche… Le trésor: The parrot spilled the beans… The captain's treasure is hidden somewhere around here!
textes.Le perroquet de Barnabé imite le kick. «: Barnabé's parrot imitates the kick. “Boom. Boom. Boom.” It's creepy.
textes.Le perroquet ne s'est pas envolé, {surno: The parrot didn't fly away, {surnom}. I let it go. It was sad in its cage, it looked at the window all day long. One morning, I opened the cage door and went to get the bread. “Flew away” makes a better story, that's all. And sometimes, in the evening, right at the top of the lighthouse, I think I see something blue. I raise my glass. Just in case.
textes.Le petit Aristide ! Mon mousse de deux j: Little Aristide! My two-day cabin boy. He became mayor, he talks well, he gave me a medal. But he never comes fishing.
textes.Le petit Gaspard construit des cabanes c: Young Gaspard builds huts the way Barnabé draws maps: with heart, and crooked. But he listens. That's rare.
textes.Le petit Théo a perdu le cerf-volant que: Little Théo lost the kite I sold him. It was half price. I should've charged full price.
textes.Le petit Théo construit des châteaux de: Little Théo builds huge sandcastles. One day he'll build a whole town.
Little Théo comes to watch me paint. He told me his kite fell into a pine tree, near here. Poor thing.
textes.Le petit Théo, mon plus jeune client. So: Little Théo, my youngest customer. His kite flew away — the one I sold him. At half price! I should have charged full price. Oh well. I give him shells instead, same thing.
textes.Le petit démon court vers toi : « C'est: The little demon runs toward you: “It's my friend the human!”
textes.Le petit est entré avec son père, il a v: The little one came in with his dad, saw the kite hanging from the ceiling — the rainbow one — and froze. He didn't ask for anything, he just looked. Me, I never give discounts. Never. I gave him half price. His dad thanked me three times. I don't know what came over me. The heat, probably.
textes.Le phare n'éclaire plus aussi loin, la n: The lighthouse doesn't shine as far at night anymore. Anselme says it's nothing.
textes.Le phare, cette fois ! Avec un nuage ros: The lighthouse, this time! With a pink cloud.
textes.Le phare, cette fois. Ne cherchez pas la: The lighthouse, this time. Don't go looking for the moustache.
The foot of the Mother Oak.
textes.Le pinceau des doyens du Village des Arb: The brush of the elders of the Treehouse Village, entrusted to you by Grandma Aquarelle. It only paints with the colours of the Stone Palette: dip it in the Palette (20 strokes), then, in hand, E (trigger in VR) to put a dab of colour in front of you, on Sketched Island.
textes.Le pinceau est sec. Trempe-le dans la Pa: The brush is dry. Dip it in the Stone Palette, in the middle of the clearing (a colour must have come back to it).
textes.Le plus agaçant, c'est qu'il regarde. To: The most annoying part is that he looks. Every day, crossing the square, Hector glances up at the clock face. Three seconds, no more. I can see him perfectly well from my bench. Once, I called out: “It hasn't moved!” He jumped like a boy caught with his hand in the sugar bowl.
textes.Le plus beau château de Théo avait quatr: Théo's finest castle had four towers made of half coconuts and a moat “dug by the sea”. Truth is, the sea had mostly nibbled at it. He asked me for straws for the flags, I gave him striped ones. He planted the last one on the keep and declared the beach hut a “friendly town”. I signed the treaty with an ice cube.
textes.Le poisson rouge fait des tours. Il a l': The goldfish does tricks. It looks like it's thinking. About what? A mystery.
textes.Le poisson rouge te regarde. Glouglou. T: The goldfish looks at you. Blub blub. You feel like it's judging you.
The fish came off the hook.
textes.Le pont aussi a besoin d'écho. Prends le: The deck needs an echo too. Get the bucket.
textes.Le port est abrité par la jetée. À l'est: The harbour is sheltered by the jetty. To the east, Anselme's lighthouse. To the west, the ferry terminal and the beach. Don't swim in the harbour, propellers are unforgiving.
textes.Le port, c'est mon royaume. Les poubelle: The harbour is my kingdom. The bins are my pantry.
textes.Le pot de figues, je ne l'ai jamais ouve: I've never opened that jar of figs, {surnom}. I told myself: the day someone deserves it. The other day, the Lord was there, with his ridiculous hat and his puppy-dog eyes. I put my hand on the ladder. I nearly brought it down. For him. It frightened me. I charged him for the wrapping paper, to calm myself down.
textes.Le premier jeudi, j'ai regardé Pauline l: The first Thursday, I looked at Pauline for a long time, and I predicted a house with three bedrooms, with beds she wouldn't have to make. She knocked over her cup. The whole promenade turned round. She still asks me how I knew. I tell her: “The cards, my dear.” And she nods, very serious.
textes.Le premier jour de tournée, Marcel m'a e: On my first day on the round, Marcel took me to the villa at the end, where a huge dog was barking like a foghorn. He took a sugar lump out of his pocket: “A sugar lump, and you say hello using his name. He's called Pompon.” Pompon ate the sugar and licked my hand. He's very old now. I always have a sugar lump in my satchel.
textes.Le premier jour du Zéphyr, j'ai senti l': On the Zéphyr's first day, I smelled hot oil and heard a droning, very far to the north. I climbed up to the Lookout: “It's coming. A bumblebee as big as the Mother Oak.” Croc-Gris stared north for a long time. An hour later, the airship came out of the clouds. He said: “I'd seen it.” Of course.
textes.Le premier jour où Borin lui a confié le: The first day Borin trusted him with the tongs, Fundin dropped a red-hot bar on his own foot. He didn't cry out. He said “Sorry, master” and carried on. That evening, I saw his boot, melted right through on top. I sewed him a new one, with an iron toecap. He still wears it.
textes.Le premier jour, Gérard a loué un pédalo: On the first day, Gérard rented a pedalo to “go round the harbour”. He went round the pedalo. For an hour, in circles, photographing the lighthouse every time he passed: click, one lap, click, one lap. I waved at him, he waved back. Kevin ended up going to fetch him. Gérard said: “What a lovely trip!”
textes.Le premier jour, Gérard a regardé son as: On the first day, Gérard looked at his plate, took out his camera, and photographed it from the front, from the side, and from above, standing on his chair. “Like a work of art,” he said. It went cold. I served him a second one, nice and hot. He photographed that too. An artist, I tell you.
textes.Le premier jour, il portait le plateau c: On the first day, he carried the tray the way you'd carry a dead fish: at arm's length, stiff as a board. Twelve cups on the floor before noon. My mother was holding her head. I was ten. I took the tray from him and put my open hand underneath: “Like this.” He looked at me as if I were the mayor. Life's funny.
textes.Le premier jour, j'ai demandé à madame C: On the first day, I asked Madame Colette for “the oldest jar in the shop”. She raised her eyes to the top shelf, to a dusty jar of figs, and said: “Not for sale.” I offered a gold coin. She said “Not for sale” in exactly the same tone. Remarkable. Since then, I come back every day, and I buy a cheese.
textes.Le premier jour, j'ai pris quarante phot: On the first day, I took forty photos of the lighthouse from the pedalo. A superb series: the lighthouse from the front, the lighthouse from the front, the lighthouse from the front… I felt like the lighthouse was following me. Actually, I was going round in circles. Yannick looked at the series and said: “That's captain's work.” He's a real connoisseur.
textes.Le premier jour, quand Léon a sonné le d: The first day, when Léon rang for departure, I walked down onto the quay with my bag. He shouted from the gangway: “We're leaving, kiddo!” I shouted: “I'm staying!” He looked at my return ticket, then at me, put the ticket in his pocket and cast off. Not another word. I cried, I laughed, and I went to the Perroquet.
textes.Le premier matin de Zoé, j'ai passé le m: Zoé's first morning, I played the gentle sunrise track. She sat down in the sand and cried, without a sound, smiling. I let the track run twice, which I never do. The Sunday boat went past at eight. She waved to it.
textes.Le premier matin où Fañch m'a emmenée da: The first morning Fañch took me out into the bay, he hoisted a little sail I'd sewn for him years before. When it filled, I cried. I told him it was the wind in my eyes. He said: “Of course.” And he looked the other way for the whole tack. I can never thank him enough.
textes.Le premier matin sous le dôme, je suis a: On the first morning under the dome, I went to ask her, quill in hand: “Majesty, what is this day called?” She looked at me as if I were mad. Then she smiled, for the first time since the wave, and said: “The first, I suppose.” It's the finest scroll I have.
textes.Le premier matin sous le dôme, tout le m: The first morning under the dome, everyone was weeping. Abyssos was fourteen and had a quill. He came and asked me, very seriously: “Majesty, what is this day called?” I had no idea. I said: “The first, I suppose.” He wrote “Day 1”. He hasn't skipped a single one since.
textes.Le premier matin à l'hôtel, je me suis r: The first morning at the hotel, I woke up alone. Léa was on the balcony of room seven, barefoot, both hands on the railing. She was looking at the sea the way you look at someone you've been waiting for a long time. I didn't disturb her. I watched her watching. That's my best holiday memory.
textes.Le premier ne compte pas, il était pour: The first doesn't count, it was for the story.
textes.Le premier plancher, je le fais sans l'e: The first floor, I do it without the stairs, easy. One day I wanted the second. I climbed and climbed… and then I couldn't move. Not up, not down. My ears were all flat. Auntie Éclair came in three leaps, hop hop hop, and brought me down. She didn't tell Mummy. You won't either, eh? Mrrrow.
textes.Le premier portrait. Elle me l'a montré,: The first portrait. She showed it to me, proud as anything. Me, mouth open, eyebrows up, looking like a man who's just bitten a pebble. “It's during the chorus,” she said. Since then, I play in profile, facing the sea. She says my profile is better. That offends me too.
textes.Le premier soir de leur voyage de noces,: On the first evening of their honeymoon, they came in holding hands, brand new. I grabbed my ladle like a microphone and sang my nonna's wedding song at their table. The whole restaurant clapped along. Hugo went bright red. Léa cried. The good kind of tears.
textes.Le premier soir où Fanny est venue, elle: The first night Fanny came, she was dancing right next to me. Her arm flew out, my cap flew into the sea, and me after it. I came out soaking wet. She laughed so hard that Mistral turned the music down to listen. My cap — Momo fished it out. He never really gave it back.
textes.Le premier soir où j'ai dormi dans sa ca: The first night I slept in his hut, Gaspard left a water flask on the doorstep, with a note: “Drink.” The second night, a flask and a note: “Drink more.” It's been three weeks. I have a whole collection of little notes. I've pinned them on the wall, between the shells.
textes.Le premier soir sans alliance, je me sui: The first evening without my ring, I sat at the end of the Coco Loco's counter. Kiki served me a glass and called it a “consolation punch”. The next day too. On the third evening, there was a little label on the glass, with my name. I never found out what he put in it. It consoled a little.
textes.Le premier soir, Hector est venu accroch: On the first evening, Hector came to hang the sign he'd forged for me: an iron parrot, wings spread. He hung it crooked. I told him so. He answered: “It's a parrot leaning over to look at the customers.” It's been leaning for twenty years. The tourists photograph it. I've never straightened it.
textes.Le premier soir, Zoé était au bord de la: The first night, Zoé was at the edge of the dance floor, all stiff, her weekend bag in her hand. I took the bag, put it down in the sand, and showed her the crab step. She did it all crooked, laughed, started again. She forgot her bag until morning. A real crab had moved in.
textes.Le premier soir, il y a cent ans, quand: The first evening, a hundred years ago, when I saw a ruby was missing, I closed the shop and searched the whole hall. Nothing. At the Forge Festival, Ulfa set a full mug down on my counter: three hundred and sixty-five rubies. She said: “You looked bored.” I haven't been bored since.
textes.Le premier soir, il était tout seul. Qua: The first night, he was all alone. Four speakers. One crackling. He was mixing anyway, with a big smile, for the sea. I thought: that one needs somebody. I took a fishbone out of my pocket. I fixed it. He said thank you forty times. Me, once.
textes.Le premier soir, j'étais au bord de la p: The first night, I was at the edge of the dance floor with my weekend bag, all stiff. Yaya took the bag, put it in the sand and said: “Watch my feet.” Crab step. I messed up, I laughed, I started again. By morning I'd totally forgotten the bag. There was a crab in it. A real one.
textes.Le premier soir, quand j'ai suivi ses tr: The first evening, when I followed her tracks to her door, I was soaked up to my ears. She didn't ask my name. She asked: “How many times did I stop, on the way?” I said: “Three. Once for a flower.” She smiled. She gave me a blanket, and a whole cake. That time, I got it whole.
textes.Le printemps dernier, j'ai sorti un méro: Last spring, I landed a grouper. Twenty-five kilos, weighed by Odette, nothing I can do about it. I carried it on my shoulder to Paulo's, right along the quay. When he saw it, he dropped his ladle and burst into song. Opera, in the middle of the kitchen. The customers applauded the grouper.
textes.Le printemps où Miriel a cueilli tout le: The spring Miriel picked the whole clover meadow for the festival crowns, my girls went round in circles for a whole day, lost. I went to see her with a hundred bees around my head. She put half the crowns back in the meadow. It's the only time bees have ever danced at the Dawn festival.
The fair price is mine, Miriel.
textes.Le prochain monorail arrive dans… mainte: The next monorail arrives in… now. No. Now.
textes.Le professeur Boum a encore perdu le toi: Professor Boum has lost the roof of his workshop again. For the fifteenth one, he needs iron ore.
textes.Le professeur Moreau cherche l'Atlantide: Professor Moreau is looking for Atlantis. I sold him all my charts of the seabed. He hasn't found anything… yet.
textes.Le professeur Moreau est gentil comme to: Professor Moreau is as sweet as can be, and as absent-minded as ten men. He's looking for a city under the sea. I'm looking for his socks. To each their own treasure.
textes.Le professeur Moreau est un client exige: Professor Moreau is a demanding, absent-minded and sincere guest. He is looking for a city under the sea. In the meantime, he mostly occupies my carpet.
