textes.Les trois runes ! « Fiat lux » : « que l: The three runes! “Fiat lux”: “let there be light.” It's the motto of the Academy, and from now on it's a little bit yours. Keep these coins. And come back and watch the stars with me one night: it's even more beautiful with someone who can make light.
textes.Les trois runes de la crypte brillent !: The three runes in the crypt are shining!
textes.Les trois runes de la crypte brillent d': The three runes of the crypt shine gold: “Fiat lux”. Aurélien Lumen will want to know.
textes.Les trois soleils se lèvent ensemble ! R: The three suns rise together! Ra, Kinich Ahau and Tonatiuh greet you: you are the Child of the Three Suns.
textes.Les tuyaux qui s'allument en bleu sont d: The pipes lit up in blue are already connected to the battery. Start from the battery, on the left, and go one tile at a time.
textes.Les témoins, dans l'affaire des croissan: The witnesses in the croissant case: the baker, her daughter Nina, and Bruno the ice-cream man, who closes late. Question them for me.
textes.Les têtes de la Carrière regardent l'hor: The Quarry heads look at the horizon, or at their feet… All of them? No: a little lower down, one of them has its nose in the air, watching the clouds go by.
The waves… They play better than I do. Always in rhythm, never tired. Wait: a minor chord, very soft. That's the sea.
textes.Les vieilles blagues, c'est comme le lev: Old jokes are like sourdough: they keep!
textes.Les vraies ! Bon choix. Mais attention :: True ones! Good choice. But careful: a true story is a story that happened once. The best ones happened twice.
textes.Les vrais Seigneurs ont crié, et les aut: The real Lords cried out, and the others called them by name! Two of them didn't flinch: wooden dummies.
textes.Les yeux de pierre brillent. « Tiens. Je: The stone eyes shine. “Here. I found it in my dream. It's for you.”
textes.Les yeux de tes amis, m'avais-tu dit. J': Your friends' eyes, you told me. I've thought about it. Ulfa's eyes shine when she's robbing me. It's a start.
textes.Les yeux fermés ? Montre ! … Hé ! Pas ma: With your eyes closed? Show me! … Hey! Not bad. The rabbit comes out of the hole, goes round the tree, goes back down the hole. My father would be pleased.
textes.Les éclats de cristal… Quand le feu pass: Crystal shards… When the fire shines through them, they make colours. Red, blue, gold. Like the northern gardens, before the brambles. In the evening I sit in front of them and watch. I've never said this. They're pretty. There. I've said it. If you repeat it, I'll say you're lying. Hmph.
textes.Les étoiles : on les compte ou on les re: The stars: do you count them or watch them?
textes.Lettres, colis, télégrammes, et beaucoup: Letters, parcels, telegrams, and a lot of chatter. Victor crying unfair competition while buying a stamp from me. Professor Moreau trembling in front of his university letters. Lola's letters “To L.”, which I slip into Lucas's letterbox, whistling. And my cards for Barnabé, Lyra, Ulfa and the queen under the sea. If she exists.
textes.Lever les yeux vers le Grand Spaghetti V: Look up at the Great Flying Spaghetti
textes.Levée à quatre heures, comme tous les jo: Up at four, same as every day. But when people smile biting into my bread, I go back to bed happy.
textes.Levée à quatre heures. Fanny, mon appren: Up at four. Fanny, my apprentice, comes straight from the beach party with sand in her hair and kneads while dancing. Raymond delivers the bread, at the moment with a sprained ankle. Paulo tells everyone I steal his croissants. The Lord takes six. Croissants went missing in the night, and the sergeant investigated, a croissant in his hand. And in the dough, a drop of elven honey. Shh.
textes.Le… le poisson-lune doré ? Pour moi ? Je: The… the golden sunfish? For me? I… I don't know what to say. Neither does Gaston. That's a first.
textes.Le… le poisson-lune doré. Ma parole. {pr: The… the golden sunfish. Well I never. {prix} coins, and that's a bargain for you. Clou, close your mouth.
textes.Lila ! Je t'ai rapporté un bâton lumineu: Lila! I brought you back a glow stick. Just the one.
textes.Lila a photographié ma danse, l'appareil: Lila photographed my dancing, with the shutter open for a whole track. In the photo, my orange beanie makes a big curve, like a rolling wave. I folded it in four and I keep it in my beanie. When some youngster tells me I dance like a seal, I take it out. He goes quiet.
textes.Lila attrape la lumière avec sa boîte ma: Lila catches light with her magic box. In her photos, you can see what you can't see with the naked eye. She photographed my fairy pollen. Bastien says it's a fault. Bastien says a lot of things.
textes.Lila est la seule à voir que je danse co: Lila's the only one who sees that I dance like a wave. The others see a seal. She has an artist's eyes and a grandmother's patience. At her age!
textes.Lila fait des photos magiques. Sur toute: Lila takes magical photos. In every one of mine, I'm a pink ghost with sunglasses. She says it's my fault. I say it's my style.
textes.Lila m'a demandé de rester immobile une: Lila asked me to stay still for just one second for a photo. I made an enormous effort, held my breath, closed my eyes behind my sunglasses… and sneezed. She sighed so hard the photo moved too. I had it framed. It's my favourite portrait.
textes.Lila m'a prêté toutes ses photos de la t: Lila lent me all her party photos for the mural. I spread them out on the sand for a whole night, by the light of a mushroom. There was Grandpa as a wave, Titou as a ghost, Yaya as a moon. It was so beautiful I was afraid of spoiling it by painting it. In the morning, I gave her photos back, neatly sorted.
textes.Lila, c'est ma sœur, ma voisine depuis t: Lila is my sister, my next-door neighbour forever and my only audience when I was ten. She even proved that the cat dances. She's always right, it's annoying.
textes.Lila, ma belle, tu veux ma vague, ce soi: Lila, my dear, want my wave tonight?
textes.Lila, ta photo du chat, je l'ai encore r: Lila, I looked at your photo of the cat again last night.
textes.Lila, tu as photographié la lune, ce soi: Lila, did you photograph the moon tonight?
textes.Lilas danse comme une feuille qui aurait: Lilas dances like a leaf that's decided never to fall. She comes to me for advice. I tell her nonsense, and then one real piece of advice, at the end. She always waits for the end.
textes.Lilas danse comme une plume qui tombe. E: Lilas dances like a falling feather. Every evening she asks me to play softer. I promise, and then the moon rises out of the pond, and… boom. She's very patient with me.
textes.Lilas danse la louve qui a sauvé la lune: Lilas dances the she-wolf who saved the moon better than the she-wolf herself, I'm sure of it. When she dances, I'm eighteen again. It doesn't last, but it's good.
textes.Lilas, c'est ma meilleure amie et la plu: Lilas is my best friend and the most beautiful dancer in the forest. She blushes at the slightest thing. Especially at a certain “hrmm”. Just saying.
textes.Lilas. Hrmm. Elle danse. Je tape. C'est: Lilas. Hrmm. She dances. I drum. That's all. … She dances well. Very well. Hrmm. That's all.
textes.Lili Pinceau, la fille de Basile (neuf a: Lili Pinceau, Basile's daughter (nine and a half), saw the pot of yellow (no. 4) roll along the beach to the big sandcastle at the far end of the shore, to the west. But the tide has covered everything, and she can't remember where the castle door is.
textes.Lili, j'ai trouvé le jaune ! Il était au: Lili, I found the yellow! It was at the foot of the tower.
textes.Lirael ! Une planche gémit, vers l'est ?: Lirael! Is a plank moaning, over to the east?
textes.Lirael veille la nuit, je pêche à l'aube: Lirael keeps watch at night, I fish at dawn. We pass each other at daybreak: she goes to bed, I go to work. Three centuries of saying good morning and good night at the same time.
textes.Lirael veille les lanternes pendant que: Lirael watches over the lanterns while I watch over a window. At that hour, we're the only two awake in the Bois-Doré. She dims the light when I play. She's a friend.
Lirael lives on the platform next door. She hangs her lanterns on my railings and warns me when a plank moans in the dark. The best neighbour in the sky.
textes.Lirael. Tu baisses la lanterne bleue, ce: Lirael. Will you dim the blue lantern tonight?
textes.Lire la dernière rune, tout au fond, prè: To read the last rune, at the very bottom, near the Heart of the Mountain. Nobody has read it for a thousand years. I'll have to go down there before my fingers forget.
textes.Lire les pages blanches du journal de bo: Read the blank pages of the logbook by Moonglow (key 4 then X; in VR, B), with the logbook in your bag
textes.Lire mes romans d'amour en terrasse, au: To read my romance novels on a café terrace, in the sun, with no newspaper in front. Let everyone see the cover. And let me finish the chapter.
textes.Lis-moi la rune du nord, Ori. Pour t'ent: Read me the north rune, Ori. For practice.
textes.Lisse & Fils vous remercie de votre coop: Lisse & Fils thanks you for your cooperation.
textes.Livraison pour… erreur. Livraison pour p: Delivery for… error. Delivery for nobody. Bzz.
textes.Livrer enfin ma lettre à Nessa. Peut-êtr: To finally deliver my letter to Nessa. Maybe at the next Dawn festival, between two dances. And not to tread on her feet this time. Or not more than ten times, anyway.
textes.Livrer le pain à Edmond (Grand Hôtel): Deliver the bread to Edmond (Grand Hotel)
textes.Livrer le pain à Gisèle (Café de la Plac: Deliver the bread to Gisèle (the Square Café)
textes.Livrer le pain à Paulo (Chez Paulo, sur: Deliver the bread to Paulo (Chez Paulo, on the quay)
textes.Loin, loin ? Plus loin que les nains ? I: Far far? Further than the dwarves? Are there seeds there? Will you bring me one next time? Just one! Two!
textes.Lola, c'est ma serveuse, et presque ma n: Lola is my waitress, and almost my niece. She carries four glasses in each hand and writes the chalkboard better than a poet. She has a soft spot for a docker. I'm not saying anything. Well, maybe a little.
textes.Lola, c'est ma voisine, ma serveuse préf: Lola is my neighbour, my favourite waitress and my glass of water between songs. She deserves to have waltzes played for her.
textes.Lola, du Perroquet, envoie une lettre ch: Lola, from the Perroquet, sends a letter every week to a certain “L.”. It's none of my business. But it's Lucas, isn't it?
textes.Lola, la serveuse du Perroquet. Elle pos: Lola, the Perroquet's waitress. She posts a letter every Friday, hiding behind the pillar. I know nothing. I'm a tomb. A smiling tomb.
textes.Lola, la serveuse du Perroquet… elle est: Lola, the waitress at the Perroquet… she's nice, isn't she? … Nothing. Forget it.
textes.Lola, la table du fond. Et le grand du q: Lola, the table at the back. And look, the big fellow from the quay just came in.
textes.Lola, ma petite passagère. Elle est mont: Lola, my little passenger. She came aboard for the day, five years ago. The day isn't over yet. I'm keeping her return ticket, just in case.
Lola… She writes the menu on the slate. She has lovely handwriting. She's nice, isn't she? … Nothing. I'm not saying anything.
textes.Long-Cou ? Long-Cou gentil ! Long-Cou ma: Long-Neck? Long-Neck nice! Long-Neck eat trees. Long-Neck never mean. But watch his feet: very big feet.
textes.Longue-vue : clic droit (ou stick droit): Spyglass: right click (or right stick) to look around; L to put it away.
textes.Longues comme le canal, Thalassa ! Et un: Long as the canal, Thalassa! And a cracker with it?
textes.Lord Pemberton paierait cher une vraie c: Lord Pemberton would pay a lot for a real curiosity: a feather from the giant eagle, a naga scale, or a shark tooth.
textes.Lord Pemberton, chambre douze. Le client: Lord Pemberton, room twelve. The nicest guest in the hotel, and the most cluttered. Before you can touch the bed, you have to dust a dragon's tooth, eleven snow globes and a porcelain egg.
textes.Lord Pemberton, mon client le plus fidèl: Lord Pemberton, my most faithful and most distinguished customer. He owns four thousand objects, and his favourite comes from my shop. From mine! I can't get over it. I don't want to get over it.
textes.Lourde et bien équilibrée. Elle abat les: Heavy and well balanced. It fells young trees (a pale notch on the trunk) and coconut palms: logs, coconuts, honey… Damage: 5.
textes.Lucas ! Chut, pour Brioche. Il dort dans: Lucas! Shh, for Brioche. He's sleeping in the crate.
textes.Lucas ? Un docker. Grand. Il joue aux ca: Lucas? A docker. Tall. He plays cards, he loses. That's it. That's all I have to say. … He's nice, isn't he?
textes.Lucas a encore perdu aux cartes. Il est: Lucas lost at cards again. He's cute when he loses.
textes.Lucas est le plus honnête docker que j'a: Lucas is the most honest docker I've ever seen. He steals nothing, he breaks almost nothing, and he talks to crates. I pretend not to know. It makes him happy.
textes.Lucas, c'est mon adversaire aux cartes,: Lucas is my card opponent, every evening. I always win. Not because I'm good: because he looks at the waitress instead of his cards. I'm not going to complain.
textes.Lucas, il est grand comme une porte et i: Lucas is as tall as a door and he talks to crates. He keeps all my secrets. And he's the only one who believes in my dolphin, because he saw it too.
textes.Lucas, le docker, parle aux caisses quan: Lucas, the docker, talks to the crates when he thinks nobody can hear.
textes.Lucas, le grand docker. Solide comme une: Lucas, the big tall docker. Solid as a crate, and red as a tomato the moment he sees my satchel. It's very sweet. I say nothing. Almost nothing.
textes.Lucie ! Aujourd'hui, je compte avec des: Lucie! Today I'm counting with pebbles, one at a time!
textes.Lucie ! J'ai fait tomber ma pipe au bout: Lucie! I dropped my tin whistle off the end of the pontoon.
textes.Lucie ! J'ai une théorie sur tes cercles: Lucie! I've got a theory about your circles, they could be…
textes.Lucie ! Une perle aujourd'hui ? Je te fa: Lucie! A pearl today? I'll give you a good price.
textes.Lucie a trouvé des pierres taillées au f: Lucie found carved stones at the bottom of the bay. Carved! Someone lived here before us.
textes.Lucie et moi, on se connaît depuis qu'on: Lucie and I have known each other since we could walk. Well, her, since she could swim. She doesn't talk much. With her, I don't need to talk either.
textes.Lucie fait le tour de la coque par en de: Lucie goes round the hull from underneath and tells me where it's seeping. She's never wrong, and she never talks for nothing. If all of Carène were like her, I'd have fewer headaches.
textes.Lucie m'a apporté une perle presque rose: Lucie brought me an almost pink pearl, with a little spot. I paid her the price of a spotted pearl. That evening I sold it for triple to a caravan trader, as a “pearl of the Figurehead Lady”. The next day, Lucie walked past the stall, read the label, and just said: “Have a nice day, Salomé.” I didn't sleep a wink.
textes.Lucie m'a appris à faire la planche dans: Lucie taught me to float on my back in the basin. She told me: “Look at the sky and forget you have a back.” I forgot my back, I floated, and then a seagull gave me a funny look. I burst out laughing and sank. Lucie laughed too. Lucie laughing is rare. It was worth the mouthful of salt water.
textes.Lucie me rapporte les meilleures algues: Lucie brings me the best seaweed in the bay, from the bottom, the kind you never find at low tide. She doesn't talk much and she listens well. Around here, both are rare.
textes.Lucie me rapporte les plus belles perles: Lucie brings me the finest pearls on the island and never haggles. She looks at me with her big calm eyes, and I get the feeling I'm the one being swindled. It's very unpleasant.
textes.Lucie peut rester sous l'eau plus longte: Lucie can stay underwater longer than a seal. I timed her. Well, I counted. Up to a hundred, then I got mixed up.
textes.Lucie plonge sous la coque. Elle dit qu': Lucie dives under the hull. She says there are things carved on the keel, underneath. Things nobody wrote.
textes.Lucie voit sous l'eau ce que personne ne: Lucie sees things underwater that nobody else sees: carved stones! She talks little, and when she does, I forget what I was going to say. For me, that's very rare.
textes.Lucie, c'est la meilleure plongeuse de l: Lucie is the best diver on the island. She stays underwater longer than a seal, I counted. She doesn't talk much, but when she does, it's to say incredible stuff.
textes.Lucie, je l'ai connue grosse comme une s: I've known Lucie since she was the size of a sardine, clinging to her mother's neck in the bay. She fishes out everything I drop. And I drop everything.
textes.Lucie. Alors, ça suinte où, aujourd'hui: Lucie. So, where's it seeping today?
textes.Lucie. Tu as cinq minutes ?: Lucie. Have you got five minutes?
textes.Lui, il a de l'humour !: Now he's got a sense of humor!
textes.Lulu ! Il souffle d'où, le vent, ce soir: Lulu! Where's the wind blowing from tonight?
textes.Lulu ? La seule humaine dont j'entende l: Lulu? The only human whose dreams I can hear from up here. They go boom-boom. I entrusted her with our glowing mushrooms: she knows who deserves to come up.
textes.Lulu a des champignons qui emmènent au p: Lulu has mushrooms that take you to fairyland. I ask her every day, nicely, very nicely. She always answers: “Soon.” Soon takes a long time.
textes.Lulu a promis de peindre le mur de son i: Lulu promised to paint the wall of sound two years ago. The wall is still white, and it's my favourite mural. She sees things I can't hear.
textes.Lulu dit que les enceintes ont des senti: Lulu says the speakers have feelings. Everyone laughs. Not me. One evening she pressed her ear against Jojo: “He's sad, he's all alone down there.” I moved him up next to Raoul. He sounds better. … Don't tell her it was for her.
Lulu sleeps against Germaine in the afternoons. Germaine doesn't like it. … Neither do I. But Lulu says Germaine purrs. It's true. She purrs.
textes.Lulu dort contre les enceintes, l'après-: Lulu sleeps against the speakers in the afternoon. She says it's like a massage.
textes.Lulu m'a fait asseoir sur la balançoire: Lulu sat me on Gaspard's swing, “just to see”. She said: “Up there, the world spins a bit, at first.” By the third swing, I was all green. She said softly: “We'll wait until your tummy is ready.” I think she's worried for me. That's kind. It's also a long wait.
textes.Lulu m'a tendu un de ses champignons qui: Lulu handed me one of her glowing mushrooms, in front of everyone. “One bite and you fly.” I put it in my pocket to be nice. The next day, it was still glowing in my hook box. I threw it into the sea. The fish came and swam round it, all lit up. I haven't told anyone.
textes.Lulu voit des couleurs qui n'existent pa: Lulu sees colours that don't exist yet. I catch them, she puts them on the sails. We're made to work together. If she ever decides to start the mural.
textes.Lulu voulait peindre les fées sur une vo: Lulu wanted to paint the fairies on a sail, but when she wakes up she always forgets our colours. So I have Zéphyr bring her a petal every month, one colour at a time. Her mural isn't finished. She says she has time. I think she's right.
textes.Lulu, avec ses champignons et ses fées…: Lulu, with her mushrooms and her fairies… Me, I believe what I see, and what I see is a purple octopus on my sail scaring off the fish. She's sweet. She talks nonsense.
textes.Lulu, c'est ma petite-fille, mon soleil: Lulu is my granddaughter, my sunshine and my second chance. She sees fairies. Me, I saw dwarves dance in a mine. In our family, we see things.
textes.Lulu, c'est vrai, ton histoire de royaum: Lulu, is it true, your story about the fairy kingdom?
textes.Lulu, ce soir tu brilles. Je peux ?: Lulu, you're glowing tonight. May I?
textes.Lulu, je te le demande très gentiment, a: Lulu, I'm asking you very nicely today.
textes.Lumi ! Tu me prêtes Cacahuète, ce soir ?: Lumi! Can I borrow Peanut tonight?
textes.Lumi croit que ses lucioles l'aiment. El: Lumi thinks her fireflies love her. Mostly they love the honey she gives them.
Lumi thinks her fireflies love her. Mostly they love the honey she gives them. She talks nonstop, she shows off with her drawings in the sky. Fine. She draws well.
textes.Lumi parle fort, rit fort, vole fort. Ma: Lumi talks loud, laughs loud, flies loud. But every morning, before dawn, her fireflies light up my flowers. Without her, I'd be setting down my drops by feel.
textes.Lumi t'a guidé jusqu'ici ? C'est la plus: Lumi guided you here? She's the youngest of us. And the bravest.
textes.Lumi voulait une goutte à son nom. Chaqu: Lumi wanted a drop with her name. Every drop already has its own. So I set one under a firefly, on a flower by the pond. It was glowing. I said: “This one is called Lumi.” She shrieked with joy so loudly that the drop fell off. I set down another one. Gently.
textes.Lumi, c'est le rire du royaume. Elle par: Lumi is the laughter of the kingdom. She talks more than all the others put together, she doesn't glow, and yet she's the one who lights up our evenings.
textes.Lumi, c'est ma meilleure amie ! Elle me: Lumi is my best friend! She lends me her fireflies in the evening, she laughs at all my jokes, and she still sort of believes fireflies grow in pots.
textes.Lumi, que dessines-tu dans le ciel, ce s: Lumi, what are you drawing in the sky tonight?
Lumi. Your fireflies followed me again.
textes.Lumina, la lanternière, prépare la Nuit: Lumina, the lantern-maker, is preparing the Night of Lanterns: the seven Great Lanterns of the city must be lit. When they're all shining, and Zigomar's rockets are ready, Pandémonia will dance all night long on the Great Square.
textes.Luzerne n'a jamais écrit la recette du g: Luzerne never wrote down the mooncake recipe. Never! “It's in the paws,” she'd say. When she left with the mist, I was eighteen, with paws that knew nothing. It took me two hundred and twelve tries to work out the chestnut flour, the honey and the round of bean paste. Two hundred and twelve! The village ate a lot of failed cakes.
textes.Lyra ! Raconte encore la mer ! S'il te p: Lyra! Tell me about the sea again! Pleeease!
textes.Lyra ! Tu as encore dormi dans les branc: Lyra! Did you sleep in the branches again? You've got moss in your hair.
textes.Lyra ! Tu as mangé ? Tu as encore l'air: Lyra! Have you eaten? You still look like a twig.
textes.Lyra ! Tu veux l'histoire de la première: Lyra! Would you like the story of the first seed?
textes.Lyra ? Je l'ai soignée de sa première fi: Lyra? I nursed her from her first fever to her first heartache. She went off to watch over a tree on the other side of the mist, and she came back talking about a “kind human”. I wonder who.
textes.Lyra dit qu'il a sauvé l'Arbre sacré. Al: Lyra says they saved the sacred Tree. So they're kind.
textes.Lyra est partie loin, de l'autre côté de: Lyra went far away, to the other side of the mist, and came back thin as a twig. I fattened her up in a week. She says she missed my bread more than anything. I believe her.
textes.Lyra est revenue grâce à toi. Elle n'arr: Lyra came back thanks to you. She won't stop talking about “the kind human”. It suits you.
textes.Lyra m'a appris à marcher sans faire cra: Lyra taught me to walk without crunching the leaves, like when she used to watch over her tree. You have to put your heel down really gently and think about something light. I think about feathers. It works! Except with Thalion. He always hears me. He says I think too loud.
textes.Lyra m'a demandé l'histoire des graines: Lyra asked me for the story of the Mother Tree's seeds more often than anyone. One day she went off to guard one. She's very single-minded, that little one.
textes.Lyra m'a rapporté un coquillage de la pl: Lyra brought me back a shell from the humans' beach. She said you could hear the sea in it. I slept with it against my ear for a month! It goes “whoooosh”. She told me about Barnabé too, so now I know: all humans talk to a parrot. Where do you hide yours?
textes.Lyra, c'est la plus courageuse du Bois-D: Lyra's the bravest in the whole Bois-Doré! She went to the other side of the mist, all by herself! She told me everything. Well, nearly. She's saving the rest for later.
textes.Là ? C'est ta poche, Pierrick. Il y a un: There? That's your pocket, Pierrick. There's a spoon in it.
textes.Là-bas, au-dessus de l'océan : l'île flo: Over there, above the ocean: the floating island! Waterfalls pour from it down to the sea, and on its summit, the Citadel of the Clouds. You can land on the esplanade, to the south.
textes.Là-haut, au-dessus de la passoire, flott: Up there, above the colander, floats the Great Flying Spaghetti: an enormous tangle of spaghetti, two meatballs, and two eyes on stalks… looking at you. It just blinked. It really did.

Up there, above the colander, floats the Great Flying Spaghetti: an enormous tangle of spaghetti, two meatballs, and two eyes on stalks… half closed. Its noodles hang limp. It looks like it's sulking.
textes.Là-haut, près du cratère, la lave crache: Up there, near the crater, the lava spits out magma elementals. Don't go near them without a weapon.
textes.Lâche mon compagnon, batracien ! Tu vas: Let go of my companion, you amphibian! You'll taste my sword!
textes.Lève ta garde (F, ou grip gauche en VR): Raise your guard (F, or left grip in VR) at the last moment, just before the blow: no damage, the enemy is stunned and your riposte hits double.
textes.Léa a pleuré dans mon thym pendant des j: Léa cried into my thyme for days. A florist crying in the middle of the herbs broke my heart. My herbal tea couldn't do much about it.
textes.Léa est fleuriste, comme moi, mais sur l: Léa is a florist, like me, but on the mainland. She knows the names of a hundred flowers, maybe more. A real colleague. And she likes my bougainvilleas. She's the only one.
textes.Léa est venue s'excuser pour la rose qu': Léa came to apologise for the rose she'd refused. She said three words of apology, then she saw my peonies, and we talked flowers for two hours. Cuttings, greenfly, the best water for tulips. I forgot to close at noon. A colleague, a real one, on my little island. I'd never had one.
textes.Léa sait où je l'ai perdue : dans le sab: Léa knows where I lost it: in the sand, near the beach hut, where the waves come in. With a shovel, maybe…
textes.Léa, c'est ma femme. Je le dis souvent,: Léa is my wife. I say it a lot, because I still can't believe it. She knows the names of a hundred flowers. I know hers. That's enough for me.
textes.Léa, la jeune mariée de la sept. Une fle: Léa, the young bride in room seven. A flower, that girl. I hurt her without meaning to, with my big mouth. She's still a bit cross with me, and she's right to be.
textes.Léa, notre voisine de balcon. Une jeune: Léa, our balcony neighbour. A very pretty young bride, who cried one evening on the balcony next door. I lent her some chocolate and my experience. The chocolate, mostly.
textes.Légendaire. Barnabé dit qu'il n'en exist: Legendary. Barnabé says there is only one. He was wrong.
textes.Léger comme une plume. Comme toutes mes: Light as a feather. Like all my feathers, come to think of it.
textes.Légère comme une graine au vent ! L'Arbr: Light as a seed on the wind! The Tree is singing again. Can you hear it?
textes.Légère comme une plume. Une plume qui sa: Light as a feather. A bouncing feather.
textes.Léon ! Des nouvelles des îles ?: Léon! Any news from the islands?
textes.Léon ? Un bon capitaine et un homme poli: Léon? A good captain and a polite man. He gives me a nod every evening as he comes alongside. To me, he'll always be fourteen with red eyes.
textes.Léon m'a appris le nœud de huit. C'est f: Léon taught me the figure-eight knot. It's easy: you make an eight and you pull. Then I taught it to Mum, to Grandpa Raymond, to Lucas, to the sergeant… and to Brioche! OK, Brioche ate the string. But he listened all the way to the end.
textes.Léon, c'est le meilleur capitaine du mon: Léon is the best captain in the world. He has an all-white beard, he knows every knot and he lets me ring the bell. When I'm older I'll be like him, but with a ponytail.
textes.Léon, c'est mon capitaine. Il m'a amenée: Léon is my captain. He brought me here and he never once tried to take me back. He carries my letters to my mother. He's sort of my grandpa of the sea.
textes.Léon, ce sont mes yeux en mer. Chaque so: Léon is my eyes at sea. Every evening, he brings me back what the passengers have seen. He's the most discreet man in the archipelago. I owe him more than he lets on.
textes.Léon. Cinquante ans qu'on se connaît. On: Léon. We've known each other fifty years. We've spoken ten times, maybe. The rest, we say with lights.
textes.M'aider ? Avec les crocodiles ? Ha ! … T: Help me? With the crocodiles? Ha! … You're serious. Well. At the river mouth, to the east, three big crocodiles lie on the sandbanks. They eat my fish out of my nets, and sometimes the nets along with them. Bring me two of their teeth: I'll hang them on my boat. The others will understand.
textes.MA BAGUETTE ! Pif ! Paf ! Ça marche ! Ti: MY WAND! Zip! Zap! It works! Here, two pinches of fairy dust. You're the best human in the world. The only one I know, but the best!
textes.MA BOTTE ! Ma botte gauche ! Vingt-deux: MY BOOT! My left boot! Twenty-two years I've been hopping on one foot! {surnom}, you're my hero!
textes.MA CARTE ! Un peu mâchonnée, un peu sent: MY MAP! A bit chewed, smelling a bit of sardine… but it's the one! Look: the cliff, the caves, the cross. Behind the Skala, I knew it! Here, your share, little sailor. And a bottle of Mama Lou's best tonic. If you ever want to sign on aboard the Murène, there's always a hammock for you.
textes.MIOU ! (Le chat saute de tes bras dans l: MIOU! (The cat leaps from your arms into hers and purrs like a mill.) You smell of the tomb, naughty cat! … Thank you, thank you! Here, it's my lucky scarab. Ptahmose made it for me. It'll bring you luck too, now.
textes.MON ANTENNE ! (Il la serre dans ses bras: MY ANTENNA! (He hugs it, climbs the mast, screws it back on, climbs down, throws himself at his mic.) Pschhh... Pschhh... THIS IS RADIO BOUCAN, 98.7, THE RADIO THAT NEVER GOES OFF... EXCEPT WHEN THE ANTENNA FALLS! AND IT'S BACK UP! Ladies and gentlemen, dear listeners, dear seagulls, the antenna was saved by a hero you all know! ... Well, that you're about to know. I'll be talking about it until tomorrow.
textes.MON CERF-VOLANT ! Merci merci merci ! Ti: MY KITE! Thank you thank you thank you! Here, my prettiest shells. And Dad said to give you this too.
textes.MON CHAPEAU ! (Il le pose sur sa tête, l: MY HAT! (He puts it on his head, takes it off, kisses it, puts it back.) On the windmill! It wanted to see the countryside, the rascal. It has a bit of flour on the feather. It makes it look wise. Thank you, thank you, thank you! Aurore! AURORE! My hat has come back! All on its own! … With some help.
textes.Ma Mochi. Six ans, des oreilles qui tomb: My Mochi. Six years old, ears that droop like mine, and a bottomless tummy for mooncakes. I pretend not to count them. I'm at four hundred and twelve this year.
textes.Ma Mélisse est partie avec la brume il y: My Mélisse left with the mist ten winters ago. That's how we say it, here. I live with my son Bourru in the north tree, and my daughter Ursule hammers away right next door. Every evening, at the Circle, the little ones snuggle up against my tummy for “the moon that wouldn't go to bed”. One by one, they nod off. All except Gland. That little squirrel gives me cold sweats.
textes.Ma Nimiel est la plus curieuse des elfes: My Nimiel is the most curious of elves and the most scraped. She takes after me, apparently. And yet I don't remember ever pulling on a door.
textes.Ma baguette ! Je l'ai perdue dans la Gro: My wand! I lost it in the Cave of Jumping Mushrooms, west of the garden. It's stuck RIGHT AT THE TOP, on the ledge. Jump on the mushrooms, they'll launch you up. Will you bring it back to me?
textes.Ma bande, c'est Mochi et Gland. Sous la: My gang is Mochi and Gland. Under the big pond, Gland says there's a dragon, Mochi says a dragon-fish, and I know it's the King, with his crown. Gland hid hazelnuts in Mummy's crates, she shouted really loud. And at night, our ears glow a little. We compare. Mine glow the most. Gland says no. Gland's wrong.
textes.Ma barbe a encore poussé, Borin. Tu as v: My beard's grown again, Borin. Did you see?
textes.Ma barque ? « La Marguerite ». Comme ma: My boat? “La Marguerite”. Like my wife. Tell Odette, and tell her she can come over for a cool drink too.
textes.Ma bouillabaisse sur toutes les îles ! C: My bouillabaisse on every island! With the elves, with the dwarves, and even under the sea, in the sunken city. Down there, at least, the fish would be fresh, eh! It would just have to swim into the pot.
textes.Ma boulangère préférée ! Il est encore t: My favourite baker! And it's still warm, too!
textes.Ma boule en bois, elle roule un peu de t: My wooden ball rolls a bit crooked, but it's the best one. Grandpa Raymond is teaching me to point near the fountain. You have to bend your knees and look at the jack like it's an ice cream. That's what he says. The other day, I beat Marcel by one centimetre! Grandpa got out his tape measure. He was so happy.
textes.Ma bourse ! Quarante pièces, le compte e: My purse! Forty coins, the count is right. (She bites a coin.) And they're real, too. You, dearie, are welcome at the Crâne Fendu. Here: your share, and two hot drinks from my personal stock. Don't tell anyone I have a personal stock.
textes.Ma cadette, Éclair. Le jour où elle a co: My youngest, Éclair. The day she ran after the heron, all the way round the pond, I understood she'd never be a fisher. I said: “A cat waits.” … I still regret it. She was waiting for something else from me that day. Since then, I watch every Great Race from the jetty. Once, I stood up. I lost a rod over it.
textes.Ma canne ? Rends-moi d'abord ce petit se: My rod? First do me that little favour: my pearly shells. Then we'll talk fish.
textes.Ma carte ! La carte de mon grand-père, l: My map! My grandfather's map, Captain Sel's! I'd put it down on a barrel, on the quay, while I tied my bootlaces. A ginger cat jumped on it, grabbed it in its mouth, and hop: one crate, another crate, a roof. I don't climb on roofs, I'm afraid of heights. Find it, and you'll get your share. A small share. But a share.
textes.Ma casquette rouge, je l'ai cherchée tro: My red cap — I looked for it for three days. It was on Momo's head, and he was dancing in it. He told me: “I found it in the water, bro, it's a gift from the sea.” It was in the water because Fanny sent it there. That doesn't make it a gift from the sea, Momo.
textes.Ma chanson sur le vainqueur de Nâga, je: My song about the conqueror of Nâga, I sang it to the mist every evening for a whole month. Forty verses, at the top of my lungs. How it got across is a mystery: the wind, or Gaston whistling it to every bird. The fact is that a nine-hundred-and-eighty-seven-year-old elf knows it. I'm published!
textes.Ma chaussette ! Vous avez encore… Ah, ma: My sock! You've gone and… Oh, mademoiselle!
textes.Ma chaussette n'est pas un sujet de conv: My sock is not a topic of conversation.
textes.Ma cheminée brille comme une étoile. Hmp: My fireplace shines like a star. Hmph. … Thank you.
textes.Ma chère Colette ! Toujours pas de pardo: My dear Colette! Still no forgiveness?
textes.Ma chère Pauline fait ma chambre, et ell: My dear Pauline does my room, and she gives a story to each of my objects. They're the finest in my catalogue. Far finer than the real ones, in fact.
textes.Ma collection a un trou, {surnom}. Un tr: My collection has a hole in it, {surnom}. A gaping hole! I'm missing {manque} pearly shells. There are some on your village beach. Would you bring me some?
Ma doue! Then it'll be a washtub.
textes.Ma doue ! Alors il a deux pieds, ton mon: Ma doue! Then your monster has two feet.
textes.Ma doue ! Alors il a deux pieds. C'est p: Ma doue! Then it has two feet. That's worse than I thought.
Ma doue… The job's getting tough.
textes.Ma défunte épouse collectionnait les coq: My late wife collected shells. I collect everything else, so as not to feel alone in that big manor.
textes.Ma femme me disait : « Fernand, un jour: My wife used to say: “Fernand, one day the sea will keep you.” She was wrong. It was her the sea kept from me… Well. We don't talk about that.
textes.Ma fille ! Je racontais justement qu'il: My daughter! I was just telling everyone that twice upon a time there was a…
textes.Ma fille aînée, la forgeronne. J'ai pris: My eldest daughter, the blacksmith. I took all the family's words, there were none left for her. She uses hammer blows instead, and you can hear them all the way to the Circle.
textes.Ma fille aînée. Je pêche, elle vend. Ell: My eldest daughter. I fish, she sells. She scolds me when I stay out in the damp. She's right. I stay anyway.
textes.Ma fille, Plumette. Elle a repris la sac: My daughter, Plumette. She took over the mailbag eight years ago, and the post has never been delivered so well. I'm very proud of her. I tell everyone. Except her. Hoo.
textes.Ma fille. Elle a les mains de sa mère et: My daughter. She has her mother's hands and her father's thick head. She sews sails for boats that never leave. I know what she's thinking when she looks at the sea. I pretend I don't.
textes.Ma fille. Grise comme son père, maligne: My daughter. Grey like her father, clever like no one else. I tell her to take the stairs. She takes the stairs. Running. She gets that from her aunt.
textes.Ma filleule, la fille de mon meilleur am: My goddaughter, the daughter of my best friend Cerfeuil. She's got his laugh, {surnom}. The very same: loud, all of a sudden, no warning. When she laughs, I can hear her from the starting arch.
textes.Ma fiole de brume, c'est de la brume du: My vial of mist is morning mist, gathered over the great pool before sunrise. We bottle it with a moon feather so it won't float away. It mends heavy hearts.
textes.Ma flûte est taillée dans un bambou du C: My flute is carved from a bamboo from the Circle. It has seven holes. The eighth was made by a squirrel. Since then, it plays one extra note.
textes.Ma grand-mère Enora plongeait, ma mère T: My grandmother Enora dived, my mother Tifenn too. Me, I learned to swim before I could walk, clinging to my mother's neck in the bay. In our family, they say we have gills behind our ears. I checked in a mirror, when I was little. Nothing. But I didn't look everywhere.
textes.Ma grand-mère Yvonne tenait déjà l'étal,: My grandmother Yvonne already ran the stall, at the back of the hold. She used to say: “An empty hold is an empty heart.” And yet, in the hungry winter, she emptied everything to feed Carène: the flour, the salt, the apples, even her mother-of-pearl buttons. She said it was the best deal of her life. It took me twenty years to understand the maths.
textes.Ma grand-mère disait : « Une cale vide,: My grandmother used to say: “An empty hold is an empty heart.” So I fill it. You come in through the breach on the beach, and you land right on my stall. That's on purpose.
textes.Ma grand-mère lisait dans le marc de caf: My grandmother read coffee grounds, my mother read palms. Me, I read people. It's more reliable.
textes.Ma grand-mère lisait l'avenir dans le ma: My grandmother read the future in coffee grounds, my mother in the lines of the hand. Me, as a little girl, sitting under the table, I didn't look at the cups or the hands. I looked at the clients: their shoes, their sighs, the wedding ring they kept twisting. At eight, I knew who was going to cry before my mother opened her mouth.
textes.Ma grand-mère m'a élevé, rue du Phare, t: My grandmother raised me, on the Rue du Phare, three doors down. She made apple tart by slapping the pastry hard on the table and singing off-key. The whole street could hear her. I forge the same way. Hard and off-key. Iron likes it. The neighbours, less so. Hm.
textes.Ma grand-mère plongeait pour les perles,: My grandmother dove for pearls, off the village, with a stone tied to her ankle to sink faster. She'd come up with her hands full of oysters, and she sang underwater, I swear. She taught me to hold my breath before she taught me to read. Three minutes, at ten years old.
textes.Ma grand-mère s'appelait Salicorne. C'es: My grandmother was called Salicorne. She pressed the very first seaweed cracker, the first night under the dome, when there was no wheat left. She'd describe the taste of bread and grilled mackerel with her eyes closed. I was born long after, in the smell of drying seaweed. Bread, I only know from her stories.
textes.Ma grand-mère tenait l'étal, ma mère ten: My grandmother ran the stall, my mother ran the stall, and me, at six, I stood on a crate next to them, gutting sardines and singing. I sang out of tune, but loud. The customers said my sardines were the cheeriest in the harbour. My grandmother used to say: “You've got to sing to fish, they've left their home.”
textes.Ma grande sœur, c'est la meilleure charp: My big sister is the best carpenter in the world. She builds all the bridges in Ramure, with Granny Faîne. When I'm older I'll build bridges with her, all the way to the moon. She works too much.
textes.Ma grande sœur, quatorze ans de plus que: My big sister, fourteen years older than me. She half raised me, between batches. She makes my carrot bread. She says I'm vain. Not true. I'm precise.
textes.Ma grenouille s'appelle Bouton ! Je l'ai: My frog's called Button! I found her under the fountain, in my secret hiding place. Oops. She was all alone and she was cold. I put her in my pocket, then in Sylwen's dough trough, because it was warm. Sylwen screamed. So did Button. Well, he went “croak”.
textes.Ma hache ! Tu en prends soin ? Pas sur l: My axe! Are you taking care of it? Not on the rocks, eh.
textes.Ma jarre ! Elle venait de ma grand-mère: My jar! It came from my grandmother!
textes.Ma journée ? Trois tours de l'île. Le pr: My day? Three laps of the island. The first ends at the lighthouse: two knocks on the door to confirm the time, Anselme grunts, that's a good sign. Pétanque in the afternoon with Marcel. The sergeant who wants to give me a ticket. And Amélie's sap potions, which I drink without quite knowing why. Well… I know. Hop hop hop!
textes.Ma journée commence au premier reflet du: My day begins with the crystal's first gleam. I polish the trident, count the sharks, salute the obelisk. In the evening I take my report to Abyssos, and Nausicaa comes to sing the high tide on the steps. Ondine counts with me, Coralin drops by to tell me his woes. And now there's you. My Gate is finally good for something.
textes.Ma journée. Le matin, Brume me fait son: My day. In the morning, Brume gives me her report: the night's tracks, the round footprints at the big pond. At noon, I go down for a bite. One of Caramel's skewers. In the afternoon, my nephew takes over, and watches the Clearing instead of the forest. In the evening, the drums at the Circle. I sit at the back. I don't listen. I keep an eye on the drums.
textes.Ma lumière n'a pas besoin de rigueur. El: My light doesn't need rigour. It needs to be believed.
textes.Ma maman réparait les voiles des bateaux: My mum mended boat sails, on the mainland, in a big shed that smelled of canvas and salt. I drew on the offcuts, with charcoal and blackberry juice. Flying fish, swimming moons. The sailors said: “She's got funny ideas, the little one.” That was kind, I think.
textes.Ma maman, c'est la meilleure boulangère: My mummy's the best baker in the world. She makes the mooncake. She says “Mochi! Put that cake down!” thirty times a day. She doesn't count the cakes. Well, she pretends not to.
textes.Ma maman, c'est la meilleure. Elle inven: My mummy's the best. She makes up stories every night and she can count everything. Except she puts on too much sun cream. Way too much.
textes.Ma maman, c'est la poissonnière. Elle fa: My mum is the fishmonger. She makes the best skewers and she stretches seven times. But when a letter from Dad arrives, she gets sad. I don't know why.
textes.Ma marraine me nourrit deux fois par jou: My godmother feeds me twice a day and scolds me three times. I don't know which I like best. Yes I do: the stew.
My whiskers tell me you're nice.
textes.Ma mère chantait les marées avant moi. C: My mother sang the tides before me. Every tide has its song: high tide is broad, low tide is gentle, slack water hardly sings at all. She also taught me the lullaby of the old island, which she had from the queen's mother. I still sing it, for one person only, on nights when the palace stays lit.
textes.Ma mère m'a appris à coudre avant de m'a: My mother taught me to sew before she taught me to read: the sailmaker's stitch, the boltrope stitch, the sailmaker's palm snug in my hand. The winter I turned fifteen, she sewed her last canvas, and left it for me to finish. I finished it. It's the blue awning on the square, in front of the tavern. I re-sew it every spring.
textes.Ma mère taillait les pierres. Elle disai: My mother cut stones. She'd say: “A stone always tells the truth, you just have to know how to look at it.” She made me look at pebbles for hours, in the sun, then by candlelight. At nine, I cut my first garnet. It was crooked. She wore it round her neck for the rest of her life.
textes.Ma mère tissait déjà au bord du canal, e: My mother already wove by the canal, and I played with her offcuts. At six, I braided my first seaweed belt. It came undone that very evening, right in the middle of a bridge, and the whole city laughed. My mother told me: “One more knot, next time.” Since then, I always tie one more knot.
textes.Ma mère vendait du poisson, sa mère vend: My mother sold fish, her mother sold fish… and my daughter wants to be a dancer. That's life, eh.
textes.Ma mère était lingère dans un grand hôte: My mother was a laundress in a grand hotel on the mainland. I grew up among piles of sheets, with the smell of hot irons. I could fold a towel into a swan before I could read. At seven, I was making peacocks. The manager gave me a coin. I still have it. I've never spent it: that would be inelegant.
textes.Ma mère, Bruyère, a dansé pour la lune a: My mother, Bruyère, danced for the moon at the Circle for thirty years. I learned the steps standing on her hooves when I was tiny: she danced, and I danced without touching the ground. Does are rare in Ramure, you know. There are never many of us. So we dance for everyone.
textes.Ma mère, Rosalie. La plus grande voix du: My mum, Rosalie. The loudest voice in the harbour. She's proud of me and tells everyone; she tells me off, and tells everyone that too. It evens out.
My mum is Rosalie, the fishmonger. I grew up between the sardine crates. I've been diving since I could walk: at five, I was bringing up sea urchins for the stall, one in each hand. My little sister Clara danced on the empty crates while Mum shouted the prices. We were the best show in the harbour, and it was free.
textes.Ma nièce Mochi veut être coureuse « comm: My niece Mochi wants to be a runner “like Uncle Bondi”. She's got talent: she always starts before the signal. That's cheating. But it's talent.
textes.Ma pension. Trois chambres, pas une de p: My own guesthouse. Three rooms, not one more, and a painted sign: “The Made Beds”. The rules will fit on one line: every guest makes their own bed. Me, I'll serve the coffee and listen to the stories.
textes.Ma petite Nimiel court partout, tombe pa: My little Nimiel runs everywhere, falls everywhere, laughs everywhere. She got my feet and her mother's voice. I'm the proudest and most out-of-breath father in the Bois-Doré.
textes.Ma petite dernière. Elle faisait fuir le: My youngest. She used to scare off the fish. Now she scares off the rabbits. … I'm proud of her. Don't tell her. I'll tell her. One day.
textes.Ma petite louve. Elle lit une trace mieu: My little she-wolf. She reads a track better than I ever did. She still has to learn to listen. It'll come. Or it won't, and I'll love her just the same.
My little sprout. Go and wash.
textes.Ma petite sœur. Quinze ans d'écart : je: My little sister. Fifteen years apart: I half raised her on the jetty. She doesn't talk, she runs. Me, I talk for two, and stretch for three.
textes.Ma petite-fille. Elle cherche le Roi ave: My granddaughter. She's been looking for the King with me since she was five. She looks better, she says. It's true. She has brand-new eyes.
textes.Ma pioche, Hilda. Et… je ne sais plus qu: My pickaxe, Hilda. And… I can't remember what else.
My whistle. Over by the pontoon. It must have rolled.
textes.Ma pièce préférée, sur quatre mille : un: My favourite piece, out of four thousand: a snow globe by Victor. A little lighthouse in the snow, in Port-Azur, where it never snows! That is genius. I shake it every night before sleeping. The flakes fall on the lighthouse, and for one minute, it's winter in Port-Azur, just for me.
textes.Ma porte a des sceaux, pas de serrure !: My gate has seals, not a lock!
textes.Ma potion de sève ? La recette de ma gra: My sap potion? My grandmother's recipe. It restores three hearts at once. Don't ask me what's in it.
textes.Ma première année d'amirale, une voie d': My first year as admiral, a leak opened under the stern, in the middle of the night. I was terrified. Tobias came up from the hold, black with tar, looked at me and said: “She'll hold a hundred years, Admiral.” I believed him. I know now he said it for my sake. So I pretend to believe it still. For his.
textes.Ma première gorgée de punch au Perroquet: My first sip of punch at the Perroquet! I put down my glass, closed my eyes and said “Divine!” so loudly that Django stopped playing. Toni thought I was choking. He slapped me on the back. Ever since, he serves me asking “Divine, milord?” and I answer “Divine!”. It's our little ritual.
textes.Ma première grande voile de passerelle,: My first great walkway sail I wove two centuries ago, between Fil-d'Aube and the Mother Tree. Taeron had just taken over his father's workshop: he laid the planks, I laid the threads. He said my sail would last a year. It hasn't budged since. He's redone his planks four times. I remind him often.
textes.Ma première lame entière, je l'ai forgée: My first whole blade, I forged it in ten days. I showed it to him, proud as anything. He took it, rang it on the anvil, looked at it. Then he put it back in the fire. Melted. Without a word. I cried behind the coal store. The next day, I forged a better one. He said: “Hmph.” That was a lot.
textes.Ma première nuit, à seize ans, au moment: My first night, at sixteen, just as I was lifting the moon out of the pond, I stumbled. The whole Circle held its breath. And Mother Moon's voice, so gentle, from her moss: “You don't lift it, little one. You rock it.” I rocked. Since then, every evening, at that moment, I still hear her, even when she says nothing.
textes.Ma première plongée avec Sofia, j'ai bu: My first dive with Sofia, I drank half the bay. I came up coughing and laughing: “It's like dancing, but you can't shout!” Sofia laughed too, a real laugh, not her quiet little smile. She said nobody had ever described diving so well.
textes.Ma proposition tient toujours : des leço: My offer still stands: lessons, early in the morning, no witnesses. I'm used to it. Well… I mean, I've got the time.
textes.Ma recette vient de ma nonna. Elle metta: My recipe comes from my nonna. She used ten fish, saffron, and a secret I'll never tell. Not even under torture. Especially not under torture.
textes.Ma robe brille comme un matin de rosée,: My dress shines like a dewy morning, thanks to you. Caelan saw it. He dropped his harp.
textes.Ma sœur Celebrë me chantait une berceuse: My sister Celebrë sang me a lullaby to put me to sleep. I danced. My mother tried every lullaby in the Bois-Doré: I danced to them all. In the end she said: “Fine. Dance, then.” I haven't stopped for three centuries. I sleep very well, by the way. Afterwards.
textes.Ma sœur. Forte. Plus forte que moi. Pres: My sister. Strong. Stronger than me. Almost. She growls when I forget the basket. Hrmm. She's right. Often. And for the rest… Hrmm. Nothing.
textes.Ma tante Gwenola tient la taverne, et mo: My aunt Gwenola runs the tavern, and I run the inn. She thinks it's the same thing. She lets me believe I'm the boss, I pretend to believe her. We're very happy like that.
textes.Ma tante, l'auberge a besoin de draps ne: Auntie, the inn needs new sheets.
Auntie, jugs are the tavern. I'm the inn.
textes.Ma tata Éclair, c'est la plus rapide de: My auntie Éclair is the fastest in all of Ramure! Well, apart from Bondi. For now. She doesn't talk much, but when she looks at me, it's like a hug.
textes.Ma terra incognita ! Toujours pas décidé: My terra incognita! Still not ready to tell me where you're from? My map is waiting. So is my curiosity.
textes.Ma tisane de lune, c'est sa rosée. Un jo: My moon tea is made with her dew. One day Brindille cried over my pot because she'd failed one of Cardamome's riddles. That batch was the best of my life. I called it “Tea of Tears” and sold it very dear. Brindille paid for hers with a sugared petal. That's the fair price of a tear.
My tea. And not a word.
textes.Ma toute première course, à onze ans. Au: My very first race, at eleven. At the root bend, I fall, twisted ankle. And there's Pépin, on the ground too: he'd fallen just before, poor thing. He took me on his back and we finished the race together, last. He said: “The last ones always arrive together, it's nicer.” Good old Pépin. No good at running, but strong.
textes.Ma toute première semaine, on m'avait mi: My very first week, they put me on nights, for the towels. Around two o'clock, near the fourth-floor linen room, I heard snoring. Real snoring, a big gentleman's snore. I ran to the stairs without looking back. The next day, I looked in the linen room: nobody. Just some slightly rumpled sheets. Since then, I know it: there's a ghost in the Grand Hôtel.
textes.Ma vague ? C'est un phoque élégant, ma b: My wave? It's an elegant seal, my dear. But all right.
textes.Ma version, la vraie : une vague de dix: My version, the true one: a ten-metre wave, out of nowhere, catches me at the bow while I'm holding the tiller with a firm hand. Fernand says the sea was flat as a millpond and I was telling an octopus story. He exaggerates. Let's say the wave was… five metres. Three. Well, a wave.
textes.Ma voisine de la rue Haute. Elle lit l'a: My neighbour on the High Street. She reads the future in cards, I read the time by the sun. One of us has a real job.
My golden voice! I've changed the chorus.
textes.Ma vraie harpe, je l'ai sculptée à cent: My real harp I carved at a hundred, from moonwood, the kind that only grows in the north of the island. It took me twenty years to find its voice. For three centuries I've played at festivals, at births, at farewells. Celebrë sang, I played, and the Bois-Doré danced. Listen to the wind: it remembers.
textes.Madame Colette est la femme la plus têtu: Madame Colette is the most stubborn woman in the archipelago, and she owns the most mysterious jar of jam in the world. She refuses to sell it to me. Every day. With admirable consistency.
textes.Madame Colette me fait payer le papier d: Madame Colette charges me for the wrapping paper. Me, who pays in gold! A little copper coin for my cheese paper. I found it splendid. I kept the paper: it's in my collection, folded in four, with a label. “Madame Colette's paper. Paid.”
textes.Madame Dupuis, ma voisine de balcon. Ell: Madame Dupuis, my balcony neighbour. She saved me with a square of chocolate and a story about a husband who was always late. I owe her a whole box.
textes.Madame Gisèle m'a appris, l'autre jour,: Madame Gisèle informed me the other day that in two months I had said “thank you” to her only once. She counted! I was mortified. Since then, I say thank you with every coffee. Three thank-yous a morning. She says it's too many, that it breaks her concentration. We are looking for a happy medium.
textes.Madame Gisèle tient le meilleur café de: Madame Gisèle makes the best coffee on the island. I've told her so, I believe. Once. I think a great deal, you see. I talk little, in the mornings.
textes.Madame Hortense ! L'horloge, avant la fi: Madame Hortense! The clock, before the end of the year!
textes.Madame Hortense. Cinquante ans qu'elle r: Madame Hortense. Fifty years she's been winding that clock. She asked me for a cog. She was right to ask. Hm.
textes.Madame Hurla : « ABANDON ! Il a quitté l: Madame Hurla: “FORFEIT! He has left the sand!” The crowd boos (kindly). We'll replay the round whenever you like.
textes.Madame Hurla : « DEUXIÈME MANCHE ! Ils o: Madame Hurla: “SECOND ROUND! They have fangs, they have flames, they have no manners: TWO HELLHOUNDS!”
textes.Madame Hurla : « K.O. ! On le ramasse !: Madame Hurla: “K.O.! Someone pick him up!” Two demons carry you to the arena door, and Bulle brings you a mug of hot sulphur tea. We'll replay the round whenever you like.
textes.Madame Hurla : « LA FINALE ! Sept ans in: Madame Hurla: “THE FINAL! Undefeated for seven years, two metres forty of horns, a heart of butter: GORGOTH THE HORNED!” The crowd leaps to its feet.
textes.Madame Hurla : « TROISIÈME MANCHE ! Du b: Madame Hurla: “THIRD ROUND! Walking bronze and sniggering imps: TWO AUTOMATONS AND TWO IMPS!”
textes.Madame Hurla, dans son porte-voix : « ME: Madame Hurla, through her megaphone: “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, DEMONS! First round of the Tournament of Horns: THREE IMPS, more annoying than nasty!”
textes.Madame Hurla, la maîtresse de l'Arène de: Madame Hurla, mistress of the Arena of Horns, is looking for a contender for the great tournament: four rounds, the last one against Gorgoth the Horned, the undefeated champion.
textes.Madame Léa ! Je n'ai rien dit à personne: Madame Léa! I haven't told anyone anything today.
textes.Madame Léa, de la sept. Une jeune person: Madame Léa, from room seven. A charming young person who has cried a great deal on our balconies. The management was very affected.
textes.Madame Margaux fait les croissants les p: Madame Margaux makes the goldenest croissants in the archipelago. She keeps them for me every morning, in a bag all my own. A woman who understands that a croissant is a collector's item.
textes.Madame Margaux, la boulangère. Une victi: Madame Margaux, the baker. A brave victim and a remarkable baker. She makes remarks to me. I note them down.
textes.Madame Olga a ouvert sa fenêtre pour fai: Madame Olga opened her window to let out a draught spell. The spell got out, along with three pages of her spellbook. They've been scattered all over town.
textes.Madame Olga, votre grimoire a l'air bien: Madame Olga, your spellbook looks rather thin
Madame Olga, your spellbook looks rather thin…
textes.Madame Rita lit l'avenir dans les cartes: Madame Rita reads the future in the cards. I think she mostly reads it in the promenade gossip. But she does it with such talent that I keep coming back.
textes.Madame Rita ne voit pas l'avenir. Elle c: Madame Rita doesn't see the future. She knows the rumours very well. The worst of it is, she's sometimes right. It annoys me.
textes.Madame Rita prétend voir l'avenir. Moi j: Madame Rita claims she can see the future. What I mostly see is that she knows the gossip very well.
textes.Madame Rita, c'est ma voisine et ma copi: Madame Rita is my neighbour and my friend. She reads the future in the cards and she always has an aniseed sweet in her pocket. Her predictions are incredible. Really. Incredible.
textes.Madame. La direction espère que tout va: Madam. The management hopes all is well.
textes.Mademoiselle Clémence a beaucoup de tale: Mademoiselle Clémence has a lot of talent and a funny idea of helping people out. She saw my camera, and she left it there. So as not to disturb it, I suppose.
textes.Mademoiselle Clémence règle sa chambre e: Mademoiselle Clémence pays for her room in paintings. It is a decision of the management. The management has excellent taste.
textes.Mademoiselle Lyra ! Je vous salue bien b: Miss Lyra! I bow most deeply to you!
textes.Mademoiselle Lyra ? Une vraie elfe, {sur: Miss Lyra? A real elf, {surnom}! Three hundred and twelve years old and not a single wrinkle. I get one per tide, and she finds me charming all the same.
textes.Mae govannen, voyageur. Chez nous, les p: Mae govannen, traveler. At our place, plants grow when you sing to them. Want to sing with me?
textes.Magnifique ! Du fer bien lourd. Avec ça,: Magnificent! Nice heavy iron. With that, my roof will last at least… a week!
textes.Magnifique ! Ils sentent encore la mer !: Magnificent! They still smell of the sea! Here, three bowls of my bouillabaisse, and for you, at Paulo's, it will always be a friend's price.
textes.Magnifique ! Tu as l'air de réfléchir à: Magnificent! You look like you're thinking about something very important. What were you thinking about? … Snack time? Perfect.
textes.Magnifique ! Tu as une voix de pierre !: Magnificent! You have a voice of stone!
textes.Magnifique, le plus beau perroquet du mo: Magnificent, the most beautiful parrot in the world.
textes.Magnifiques ! Jaunes comme des canaris !: Magnificent! Yellow as canaries! (He crushes them in a mortar, he mixes, he sneezes, he laughs.) The rockets are ready! Tell Lumina the Night of Lanterns will have its fireworks!
textes.Magnifiques ? Il leur manque le principa: Magnificent? They're missing the main thing: ember flowers! Flame petals, yellow in the middle, red at the tips. They only grow on the slopes of the Great Blaze, where the ground is warm. Bring me five. Don't step on the lava flows, mind you: I'm too old to be treating burns.
textes.Maintenant il vient me voir sur le quai,: Now he comes to see me on the quay, very serious, with his notebook: “My dear Fernand, would you also have mermaid scales?” I told him mermaids are seasonal. He wrote down “seasonal”. I was ashamed all evening. The next day, he brought me a croissant. I was even more ashamed.
textes.Maintenant, j'ai des genoux qui grincent: These days I have creaky knees and a blue house near the village spring. My granddaughter Lulu has lived with me for three years. In the evening we go down to the party together, she holds my arm all the way to the dance floor, and there I let go. The youngsters say I dance like a seal. Lila has the photo: it's a wave.
textes.Maintenant, je construis des cabanes pou: These days I build huts for whoever wants one. Marley's, above his banana trees. Mistral's stage. My little test hut near the beach, the one that leans, where Zoé is sleeping at the moment. In the evenings, I nod my head next to Tchoum. We don't talk. We're good. Right.
textes.Maintenant, je dors dans la cabane d'ess: Now I sleep in Gaspard's test hut, the leaning one, with three crabs. In the afternoons I go to Yaya's class. I swim with Sofia, I help Momo drill his shells. I dance till sunrise, and every morning I suggest a name for Mistral's track. The village has adopted me, I think. And I've adopted it too.
textes.Maintenant, je grimpe aux passerelles, j: Now I climb the footbridges, I listen to Faelar's stories, I eat Sylwen's bread and I ask loads of questions. Aëlwen patches up my knees. Lyra told me about the sea and the shells. And then you turned up with your round ears! It's the best year of my whole life. Well, of all forty-two.
textes.Maintenant, je me lève à quatre heures,: These days, I get up at four, knead till noon, sleep a little, and in the evening I take the boat with Margaux's leftovers. I dance, I catch the last Swallow back, I sleep three hours. I knead in rhythm, at a hundred and forty-five. Margaux says my croissants have swing. I think that's a compliment.
textes.Maintenant, je peins les voiles des pêch: Now I paint the fishermen's sails: an octopus for Bastien, stars for others. In the afternoon, I nap against Germaine, the speaker that purrs. At night, I pick the fairies' mushrooms in the ring, behind the dune. And the mural on the wall of sound… it's coming along. In my head. It's very beautiful, in my head.
textes.Maintenant, les mouettes connaissent l'h: Now the seagulls know the time. From half past six, there are a dozen of them lined up on the bakery roof. Waiting for the Lord. When he comes out with his bag, they all take off together behind him, like an escort. Nina says it's his royal guard.
textes.Maintenant, mes genoux ne veulent plus g: These days, my knees won't climb any more. I keep watch from the bow, with the spyglass, and it's my grandson Ewen who goes up to light the lantern. I still count the ships. This year: three. Including you. I wrote you in the journal. In ink, not pencil.
There is now. I added it.
textes.Maintiens pour mouliner, relâche si ça t: Hold to reel, release if it pulls too hard
textes.Mais Kick et Basse vont s'ennuyer, Gaspa: But Kick and Bass will get bored, Gaspard!
textes.Mais le Sceau d'Airain cliquette dans ta: But the Bronze Seal clicks in your pocket… The Cogwheel (key 3, then X)?
textes.Mais moi si, si on traîne !: But I will, if we dawdle!
textes.Mais à Ramure, il n'y a jamais de nuit s: But in Ramure, there's never a moonless night. Maybe that's why we're so rarely afraid here. I keep looking all the same. A nose never sleeps.
textes.Mais… QU'EST-CE QUE TU FICHES CHEZ MOI ?: But… WHAT ON EARTH ARE YOU DOING IN MY HOUSE?!
textes.Mais… comment ça tient ?: But… how does it stay up?
textes.Mais… je suis déjà là, juste derrière to: But… I'm already here, right behind you! I have been all along!
textes.Majesté ! C'est vous ! Vous êtes revenue: Majesty! It's you! You've come back!
textes.Majesté ! Ce soir, je te dessine une cou: Your Majesty! Tonight, I'm drawing you a crown!
textes.Majesté ! Je vous ai apporté des fleurs: Your Majesty! I've brought you moonflowers.
textes.Majesté ! Le brin de ta couronne a une t: Your Majesty! Has the sprout in your crown got a third leaf?
textes.Majesté ! Le soleil, il fait du bruit ?: Majesty! Does the sun make a noise?
textes.Majesté ! Toutes les lettres livrées ! U: Your Majesty! All letters delivered! A record!
textes.Majesté ! Vous avez vu le nez du roi Atl: Majesty! Have you seen King Atlas's nose? I polished it this morning.
textes.Majesté ! Vous êtes descendue ! Pif ! Pa: Your Majesty! You've come down! Pop! Bang! Welcome!
Majesty, your decree is four pages long.
textes.Majesté. Les runes ont parlé, cette nuit: Majesty. The runes spoke last night.
Your Majesty. Your crows are tired.
textes.Majesté. Votre couronne brille, aujourd': Majesty. Your crown is shining today.
textes.Mal. Clou a caché mon marteau. Et il ne: Bad. Clou hid my hammer. And he won't say where.
Badly. I think about too many things.
textes.Mal. Les golems des hauteurs se sont rév: Bad. The golems of the heights have woken up. They come down at night. The stones rumble.
textes.Mal. Très mal. Mais tu n'y es pour rien…: Bad. Very bad. But it's not your fault… well, hardly your fault.
textes.Malebolge, le Huitième Cercle : trois fo: Malebolge, the Eighth Circle: three ditches of fire, three turning iron bridges. And little imps, the Malebranches, sniggering as they wait for you.
textes.Malheureuse. Mon mari a perdu son allian: Miserable. My husband lost his wedding ring after ten days. Ten days!
textes.Malin. Les gens en savent plus que les c: Clever. People know more than maps. But watch out: in Carène, if you ask Corentin for directions, you end up in a story, not at your destination.
textes.Mal… Je m'en doutais : tu as les yeux ce: Badly… I thought so: you've got rings round your eyes like a tanuki. Prescription: a mist tea every evening, and no Trèfle tart after midnight.
Mama Grog is demanding her forty coins.
textes.Mama Grog, une holo-photo pour un touris: Mama Grog, a holo-photo for a space tourist?
textes.Maman ! J'ai vu une tortue ! La quarante: Mum! I saw a turtle! The forty-fourth!
textes.Maman ! J'ai été très sage, aujourd'hui: Mummy! I was really good today!
textes.Maman chante quand elle pétrit. Elle cha: Mum sings when she kneads. She sings out of tune, out of tune, out of tune! Even the dough pulls a face. I sing with her, and then we laugh so much she has to start the dough again. Fanny says we're the worst singers on the island. It's true. At least we're champions at something.
textes.Maman cueille les fleurs de tout le vill: Mummy picks the flowers for the whole village. She always smells of violets, and she always knows when I've been naughty. Even when I haven't done it yet.
textes.Maman dit qu'on n'a pas le droit d'y tre: Mum says we're not allowed to dip our bread in it. But she says nothing about fingers.
Mum says I ask too many questions. Why does she say that?
textes.Maman dit que je suis née un matin de pl: Mummy says I was born on a rainy morning, and that I yelled so loud the frogs in the fountain went quiet. Daddy says I opened my eyes and straight away looked up, at the footbridges. I don't remember, I was too little. But I believe Daddy.
textes.Maman dit que l'Arbre-Mère veille sur no: Mummy says the Mother Tree watches over us at night. Once I asked her: “And who watches over the Mother Tree?” She thought for a really long time. Then she said: “You will, when you're grown up.” Ever since, I say goodnight to the Tree every evening. And to Mummy too.
textes.Maman m'a interdit de grimper au premier: Mum told me I'm not allowed to climb to the first platform without the stairs. So I take the stairs! Running, four steps at a time, shouting “I'm obeying!”. Mum goes “Mrrr” with her eyes closed. That means she's got nothing to say back. I won.
textes.Maman m'a tissé une robe avec des algues: Mum wove me a dress out of seaweed in every colour of the canal. She put in a golden thread, a tiny one, hidden in the hem. She says it's a ray of sunshine, so I have one on me until I see the real thing. I check every night that it's still there.
textes.Maman tisse les algues : les robes, les: Mum weaves seaweed: dresses, curtains, blankets. She says I'm the only thread she can't keep straight. It's a compliment, I think.
textes.Maman, elle fait le meilleur pain et ell: Mum makes the best bread and she gets up while it's still dark. She says I ask too many questions. But she answers anyway. One time in three.
textes.Maman, elle me met de la crème solaire p: Mummy puts sun cream all over me. On my nose, on my ears, behind my knees. I'm all white, I look like a ghost. The ladies on the beach laugh. Even Kevin the lifeguard said “Hi, little ghost.” Mummy says it doesn't matter, ghosts don't get sunburnt.
textes.Maman, pourquoi le pain il gonfle ?: Mum, why does bread puff up?
textes.Maman, tu me racontes la fin de l'histoi: Mummy, will you tell me the end of the story?
textes.Mamie Barricade, une holo-photo pour un: Mamie Barricade, a holo-photo for a space tourist?
Mamie Kiku sent you a message! (No. But click anyway.)
textes.Mamie Tournesol et Mère Averse ont fait: Granny Sunflower and Mother Downpour have made peace: the Larsen Festival can come back! Jack, the head roadie, has been repairing the Main Stage for years. He's missing Galet's ropes, Lune's canvas… and someone to tell Mégaphone to finally press his third button.
textes.Mamie Tournesol, Mère Averse vous a fait: Granny Sunflower, Mother Downpour made you this umbrella.
textes.Mamie Tournesol, la doyenne du Camp des: Granny Sunflower, the eldest of the Flower Camp, and Mother Downpour, the eldest of Rainville, were the best friends in the world. Fifty years ago, they fell out over the weather (sun or rain for the festival?), and since then nobody has dared to step onto the Main Stage. Granny Sunflower would like to make peace… but she doesn't dare.
textes.Mamie Tournesol, pourquoi regardez-vous: Granny Sunflower, why are you looking at Rainville like that?
textes.Mamie, comment arrêter Lisse pour de bon: Mamie, how do we stop Lisse for good?
textes.Mamie, que se passe-t-il quand la sirène: Mamie, what happens when the siren wails?
textes.Mamma Lasagna a encore fait trop de pâte: Mamma Lasagna has made too much pasta again. Like every day. Luckily.
textes.Mamma Lasagna, le Révérend a besoin de v: Mamma Lasagna, the Reverend needs your pasta for the sacred Dish.
textes.Manette : croix ou stick pour viser: Controller: d-pad or stick to aim
textes.Mange d'abord, Odette. Il ne va pas s'en: Eat first, Odette. Your sailboat isn't going to fly away.
textes.Mange d'abord. Les voiliers ne partiront: Eat first. The boats won't sail off.
textes.Mange-Clous, je viens vous débarrasser d: Mange-Clous, I've come to rid you of the rat.
textes.Marcel ! Trois fois l'archipel, tu dis ?: Marcel! Three times round the archipelago, you say?
textes.Marcel ? Un bavard qui jure trop. Trente: Marcel? A chatterbox who swears too much. Thirty years he brought me my letters, and on days with no letters he came anyway. About the lavender, he denies it. He denies it very badly.
textes.Marcel ? Un tricheur, un menteur et un f: Marcel? A cheat, a liar and a postman. Forty years he's been measuring crooked. He's my best friend, but if he asks you, I never said so.
textes.Marcel a porté le courrier pendant trent: Marcel carried the post for thirty years, and he carried my one-centimetre victory. A precise man. Sometimes too precise.
textes.Marcel, c'est le facteur le plus marcheu: Marcel is the walkingest postman in history. He says his round is worth my marathons. We argued, we did the maths: he might be right.
textes.Marcel, mon ancien chef de tournée. Il m: Marcel, my old round boss. He taught me everything, and he still keeps an eye on me from his pétanque pitch. I pretend to be annoyed. I'm touched.
textes.Marchander ? Sur un bateau, les prix son: Haggle? On a ship, prices are nailed to the mast.
textes.Marchander ? Va voir Bedaine, au Grand T: Haggle? Go and see Bedaine, at the Great Swap. My prices are round as the moon.
Haggle with a dwarf? Ho ho! No.
textes.Marcher ?! Hop hop… Bon. Chacun son truc: Walk?! Hop hop… Fine. Each to their own. Walking is running with patience. Lots and lots of patience.
textes.Marcher jusqu'au bout de la brume, là où: To walk to the very end of the mist, where it stops, and see what lies beyond. Not to leave. Just so I can make my report: “Report: the world is big.”
textes.Marché conclu ! Tope là, de la patte. Qu: Deal! Shake on it, paw to hand. What shall we swap next?
textes.Marché conclu. {objet}, pour {prix} pièc: Deal. {objet}, for {prix} coins. You won't regret it.
textes.Margaux m'a appris le pain, la patience: Margaux taught me bread, patience and getting up at four. She grumbles when I dance in the bakehouse, but she's the first to start humming.
textes.Margaux me donne ses invendus du soir po: Margaux gives me her evening leftovers for the party, so they don't go to waste, she says. One evening there were twelve croissants in the basket, still piping hot, with a note: “Leftovers.” We never bake a batch in the evening. Margaux can't lie to save her life. I didn't say a thing. I just hugged her really tight.
textes.Margaux n'a personne pour livrer le pain: Margaux has no one to deliver the bread to Chez Paulo, the Square Café and the Grand Hotel.
textes.Margaux vole mes croissants à moi. Non,: Margaux steals my croissants. No, I'm joking, I'm the one who steals hers. No, I'm joking again.
textes.Margaux, c'est la meilleure boulangère d: Margaux is the best baker in Port-Azur. The only one, too, but that changes nothing. Her bread is my soup's best friend. She laughs at my jokes. Almost always.
textes.Margaux, c'est la petite qui a repris ma: Margaux is the girl who took over my bakery. She puts too much honey in her bread. I eat it twice a day, to check. Always too much honey.
textes.Margaux, ma belle ! Tes croissants, ils: Margaux, bella! Your croissants are at my place, I stole them!
textes.Marley ! Combien de régimes, cette semai: Marley! How many bunches this week?
textes.Marley ? Il cultive ses bananes dans mon: Marley? He grows his bananas in my corner and pays me in bunches. The best tenant in the world. He only makes noise for the banana trees.
textes.Marley fait écouter de la musique à mes: Marley plays music to my banana trees, on a little box that goes boom. I sing them sea shanties. We ended up making a deal: him on even days, me on odd days. The bunches have never been so big. Gaston leans towards the boom.
textes.Marley jure qu'il n'écoute jamais ce que: Marley swears he never listens to what I confide in my banana trees. But last week, he asked me, all casual: “And Mireille, is she any better?” By Neptune's beard! I've switched banana trees.
textes.Marley m'a demandé un collier en peau de: Marley asked me for a banana-peel necklace. I said it wouldn't hold. He insisted, so I made it. He wore it proudly a whole evening. Two days later it was all black and the flies followed him across the dance floor. He said: “That's nature, my brother.” I fell off the stall laughing.
textes.Marley n'a jamais pris le bateau. Jamais: Marley has never taken the boat. Never. So he gives me messages for Port-Azur: “Say hello to the harbour for me.” “Tell the lighthouse it blinks nicely.” I say them out loud, on deck. Captain Léon gives me funny looks. But I say them. That much I can't refuse him.
textes.Marley veut tellement aller chez les fée: Marley wants so badly to go to the fairies. He asks nicely, very nicely, every day. But his tummy already spins on a swing. I don't want him to be scared, up there.
textes.Marley, aujourd'hui, on vend. On ne donn: Marley, today we sell. We don't give anything away. Deal?
textes.Marley, c'est mon associé au stand du ma: Marley's my partner at the market stall. I sell the necklaces; he gives away the bananas. He says everyone is family. And family never pays.
textes.Marley, c'est mon voisin et mon meilleur: Marley's my neighbour and my best mate. He pays for my huts in bananas and says everyone is family. With him, it's true.
textes.Marley, j'ai vu une banane qui brillait,: Marley, I saw a glowing banana, in the ring.
textes.Marley, je l'aime bien, hein. Mais il ve: I like Marley, really. But he wants to put banana in everything I make. In croissants, in brioche, in baguettes. In baguettes, {surnom}!
Marley, no. I know what you're going to say. No.
textes.Marley, tu as bu de l'eau ?: Marley, have you drunk some water?
textes.Marée ? La meilleure commerçante du dôme: Marée? The best trader in the dome. We nearly got married, four hundred years ago. We got stuck on the price of the ring. Three coins apart.
textes.Marée coupe mes algues. Une sur trois, e: Marée cuts my seaweed. One in three, she says. She counts the way she talks: very fast, and not always right.
textes.Marée m'a proposé de vendre des « galett: Marée suggested selling “royal crackers”, with my portrait on them, at twice the price. I refused. The next day she was selling “almost royal crackers”, with a lady who looked a great deal like me, except for the nose. I walked by and bought one. I paid for it.
textes.Marée me paie en galettes. En galettes !: Marée pays me in crackers. In crackers! I've got thirty under my bed. But when I dance in front of her stall, she's the one who claps loudest. So, well.
textes.Marée me vend les plus longues laminaire: Marée sells me the longest kelp under the dome. She talks as much as she sells, which is to say a lot. She has a good heart, under all the coins.
