textes.Marée parle plus vite que le courant et: Marée talks faster than the current and counts faster still. Her crackers, I really do love them. I think I'm the only one.
Marée won't let me archive her recipes. “Secrets don't get written down.” Everything gets written down. Except, apparently, the seaweed cracker.
textes.Marée vend des galettes d'algues. Elles: Marée sells seaweed cakes. They're… nourishing. That's the kind word.
textes.Marée, la galette de ce matin était parf: Marée, this morning's cracker was perfect.
textes.Marée, si tu me paies en galettes, je da: Marée, if you pay me in crackers, I'll dance at a walk.
textes.Marée. Juste le sel. Dis-moi juste combi: Marée. Just the salt. Just tell me how much salt.
textes.Marée. Un sac de galettes, comme d'habit: Marée. A bag of crackers, as usual.
textes.Matthias ! Cette année, on y va, à la gr: Matthias! This year, are we going to the great gate?
textes.Matthias ! Note bien : ce soir, la balei: Matthias! Write this down: tonight, the whale has six trees.
textes.Matthias ! Toujours pas de clé ? Je t'ai: Matthias! Still no key? I'll give you a good price.
textes.Matthias ! Tu es repassé voir ma prairie: Matthias! Did you go and check on my meadow?
textes.Matthias a un carnet rien que pour mes h: Matthias has a journal just for my stories, his thirteenth. He notes the date, the place, and the number of hot honeys. One evening he told me: “Yesterday your whale had three trees on its back. Today it has five.” I answered: “It grew.” He wrote that down.
textes.Matthias est le seul à prendre mon auber: Matthias is the only one who takes my inn seriously. He drew me the plot, the plans, even the sign. He talks a lot, but it's always to say kind things.
textes.Matthias est venu à la proue avec un com: Matthias came to the bow with a compass and a protractor, to measure the angle of my blue light. I showed him the spot. He calculated all afternoon. That evening, on his map, there was a little blue dot, and next to it: “according to Grégoire (?)”. It took me three weeks to speak to him again.
textes.Matthias et moi, on doit aller voir ense: Matthias and I are supposed to go and see the hinges of the great gate together. We decide it every year, at the tavern, on the third round of sparkling apple. We've never gone.
textes.Matthias m'a dessiné les plans de mon au: Matthias drew the plans for my inn: twelve rooms. In one corner, I pencilled in a little room for my aunt, with a stove. A few days later, it had been gone over in ink, with an extra window. He didn't say anything. Neither did I. He's a true friend.
textes.Matthias m'envoie : que savez-vous des q: Matthias sent me: what do you know about the four seals?
textes.Matthias me pose cent questions et n'éco: Matthias asks me a hundred questions and doesn't listen to a single answer. He put my blue light on his map with a question mark. A question mark. Next to my name.
textes.Matthias parle trop. Il voudrait que je: Matthias talks too much. He wants me to draw underwater, with a pencil. But he's the only one who didn't think I was mad about my stones. That counts.
textes.Matthias raconte à qui veut l'entendre q: Matthias tells anyone who'll listen that he'll open the Gate of the Four Seals. I offered to sell him a key. He didn't laugh.
textes.Matthias rêve d'ouvrir la Porte aux Quat: Matthias dreams of opening the Gate of the Four Seals. The four seals must be found, one for each people of the great island: the sea spray of Carène, the sands of Tazira, the bronze of the northern shepherds, the mists of Ramure. Each seal leads to the next.
textes.Matthias veut ouvrir une porte que perso: Matthias wants to open a door nobody has opened in two hundred years. I offered him a key. He didn't laugh. Dreamers never laugh at their dreams. It's touching.
textes.Matthias écrit mes histoires dans un car: Matthias writes my stories down in a journal to check them. As if you could check a story! But he's the only one who listens to me with a pencil. It's flattering.
textes.Matthias, le cartographe de Carène, rêve: Matthias, the mapmaker of Carène, dreams of drawing the heart of the island. He'd like to know what the great sealed gate at the foot of Stoneheart looks like.
textes.Matthias. Tu as toujours ton point d'int: Matthias. Still got your question mark?
textes.Mauvaise réponse. Pour un garde. Pour un: Wrong answer. For a guard. For a tracker, right answer. Go and see Brume. She'll like you. Me, I'll keep an eye on you.
textes.Mauvaise. Comme d'habitude. Merci de dem: Bad. As usual. Thanks for asking. Hmph.
textes.Maître Faelar ! Vous connaissez vraiment: Master Faelar! Do you really know my song?
textes.Maître Hugues, la fontaine fait des bull: Master Hugues, the fountain is making green bubbles
Master Hugues, the fountain is making green bubbles…
textes.Mbarek ! Mon ami ! Du miel des brumes co: Mbarek! My friend! Mist honey for your dates?
textes.Mbarek, l'homme bleu de Tazira ! Il parl: Mbarek, the blue man of Tazira! He talks little and never laughs at my jokes. Never. I count that as friendship, my friend: you have to be very close to dare not to laugh.
textes.Me rendre ma canne ? Jamais de la vie !: Give me back my rod? Not on your life! It's yours now. Go fishing, {surnom}.
Giving me back my own work? Keep it. What's sold is sold.
textes.Me reposer ? À mon poste ? Majesté, quel: Rest? At my post? Majesty, what an idea!
textes.Meilleure fournisseuse de l'île : du mie: Best supplier on the island: treetop honey, and not one complaint, even with a stung nose. She can't count coins, but she knows how to make them sing.
textes.Mener la lumière de la sève jusqu'au cœu: Guide the light of the sap to the heartwood
textes.Merci ! Et un client content, un !: Thanks! And that's one happy customer!
textes.Merci ! Lune a tissé la toile, Galet a f: Thanks! Lune wove the canvas, Galet made the ropes, and I painted the door. Here, take this for the road.
textes.Merci ! Merci ! Deuxième, c'est battre t: Thanks! Thanks! Second means beating everyone but one. That's almost everyone, right! I'm going to tell Pépin. And Bondi. Especially Bondi.
textes.Merci ! Ne le dis pas trop fort : sinon: Thank you! Don't say it too loud, or we'll have to repaint the kitchen too.
textes.Merci ! Reviens quand tu veux, la porte: Thanks! Come back whenever you like, the door is always open.
textes.Merci ! Reviens quand tu veux. Même pour: Thanks! Come back whenever you like. Even for nothing. Especially for nothing: I'm a bit bored.
textes.Merci ! Tiens, prends donc ça pour la ro: Thank you! Here, take this for the road. Nobody leaves my house on an empty stomach!
textes.Merci ! Tu es mon plus grand fan. Mon se: Thank you! You're my biggest fan. My only fan, but the biggest.
Thanks! You hide well, you know.
textes.Merci bien. Ça trouvera sa place dans la: Thanks kindly. It'll find a place in the hold.
textes.Merci d'avoir ramené les esprits-luciole: Thank you for bringing the firefly spirits back. The Mother Tree has been singing ever since you came.
textes.Merci de ne pas me mentir. La peur, je l: Thank you for not lying to me. Fear I know well: you don't chase it away, you learn to walk beside it. So it will be up to us to be gentle, when the day comes.
textes.Merci de patienter : votre déménagement: Please wait: your move is in progress.
Thank you again, from the bottom of my heart.
textes.Merci encore, {surnom}. Grâce à toi, je: Thank you again, {surnom}. Thanks to you, I can go home. And you can come too: the compass knows the way.
Thank you for the lavender, Marcel.
textes.Merci, Bastien ! T'es le meilleur porteu: Thanks, Bastien! You're the best carrier on the island, you are.
Thank you, Gwenola. Sorry. I mean, thank you.
textes.Merci, Marée. Elle a le goût de ta grand: Thank you, Marée. It tastes of your grandmother.
textes.Merci, Perlée. Et toi, qui t'arrose ?: Thank you, Perlée. And you, who waters you?
textes.Merci, Triton. Repose-toi un peu, veux-t: Thank you, Triton. Do rest a little, won't you?
textes.Merci, merci ! Tenez, des croissants tou: Thank you, thank you! Here, some piping hot croissants. And from now on, at my place, you'll always get a little discount.
textes.Merci, mon gars. Tiens, quelques pièces,: Thank you, lad. Here, a few coins, and a bag of seeds. Plant them wherever you like. But if one day they run away… it won't be my fault. It'll be the soil of Montjoie.
textes.Merci, parrain ! Et mon île, tu t'en sou: Thanks, godfather! And my island, do you remember it?
textes.Merci, petite pousse. Tiens, une fleur d: Thank you, little sprout. Here, a nebula flower from my garden: it opens when you're happy. And two moon biscuits: Gloubi makes them with flour from my flowers. Don't tell him, he thinks it's a secret.
textes.Merci. C'est… curieux. Je lui trouverai: Thank you. It's… curious. I'll find a place for it.
Thank you. That one's very beautiful.
textes.Merci. Je me demande bien qui les a posé: Thank you. I do wonder who put them there.
textes.Merci. Je vais lui trouver une place dan: Thank you. I'll find a place for it among my things.
textes.Merci. Note-le aussi. Ça fait combien ?: Thank you. Write that down too. How many is that?
textes.Merci… Je ne sais pas à quoi ça sert, ma: Thank you… I don't know what it's for, but it's pretty when it floats.
textes.Merci… c'est gentil. Je vais bien lui tr: Thanks… that's kind. I'm sure I'll find a spot for it.
textes.Merveilleuse ! J'ai vendu une boule à ne: Marvellous! I sold a snow globe to a penguin. No, to a tourist. But he looked like a penguin.
textes.Merveilleusement ! Le cristal chante de: Wonderfully! The crystal is singing again!
textes.Merveilleusement bien ! Le pain a levé,: Wonderfully well! The bread has risen, the bees are singing, and nobody has spilled my flour today.
textes.Merveilleux. Tu viens goûter la tisane,: Wonderful. Coming to taste the tea this evening?
So were my bees. For a thousand years.
My friends are my other halves.
textes.Mes amoureux ! Une table pour deux ?: My lovebirds! A table for two?
textes.Mes bougainvilliers ont envahi le toit d: My bougainvilleas invaded Kiki's roof, then his chimney. He's never complained. He brings me empty coconuts, cut clean with a single stroke of the machete, and I turn them into pots. I've got thirty-two now. My customers love them. I've never thanked him. If I thank him, he'll play me one more song.
textes.Mes bâtons ? Je ne t'ai rien demandé. Pa: My sticks? I haven't asked you for anything. Not yet.
textes.Mes bâtons, tu y penses ? Il m'en faut {: My sticks, remember? I need {manque}. Without a handle, a shovel is just a flat rock.
textes.Mes chèvres grimpent partout : sur les r: My goats climb everywhere: on rocks, on roofs, on Bramm. Their milk makes the best cheese on the mountain.
textes.Mes coquillages ? Quels coquillages ? Ah: My shells? What shells? Ah… I haven't asked you for anything yet, I believe.
textes.Mes coquillages chantent ! Enfin, ils fo: My shells sing! Well, they go “whoooosh”. It's the sea singing, Faelar says.
textes.Mes coquillages nacrés, tu y penses ? Il: My pearly shells, have you remembered? I need {manque}. My collection is trembling with impatience.
textes.Mes coquillages « authentiques » ? Je le: My “authentic” shells? I pick them up myself, I paint them myself. They're authentically mine.
textes.Mes couleurs ! Tu as volé mes couleurs !: My colours! You stole my colours!
textes.Mes filles comptent leurs brassées, elle: My girls count their armfuls too.
textes.Mes filles ont travaillé toute la semain: My girls worked all week for you.
My girls can hear you, Aëlwen.
textes.Mes fils te rattraperont. Comme d'habitu: My threads will catch you. As usual.
textes.Mes fleurs n'ont jamais été aussi belles: My flowers have never been so beautiful. You're a very kind human.
textes.Mes flèches de ton bois volent droit. Je: My arrows made from your wood fly true. I don't forget.
textes.Mes fruits ! Tout par terre !: My fruit! All over the ground!
textes.Mes gouttes ! Toutes ! Tiens, de la pous: My drops! All of them! Here, fairy dust, two pinches. And twenty coins. And… thank you. Really.
textes.Mes journées ? J'aide Mélisse à remplir: My days? I help Mélisse fill her bottles, I tell Brindille stories so she doesn't cry, and I invent spells in a notebook. There are three hundred and four! Number one is the frog spell for Grommelot. It has forty-two variations. Grommelot has tried them all. Not willingly.
textes.Mes lanternes s'éteignent tout le temps,: My lanterns keep going out down there. I'd need {manque} magma hearts: they glow for a hundred years. The magma elementals near the crater have one in their bellies… You see what I mean.
textes.Mes livres… Quatre. Pendant la grande te: My books… Four of them. During the great storm, they flew out the window. One is on the library roof. Another on the tallest of the Moonstones. The third on the ledge of a window in the Leaning Tower. The last in a big twisted oak in the Twisted Wood. Nobody can climb up there. But we can call them. I'll teach you.
My fireflies saw you going round in circles.
textes.Mes moteurs ne sont pas faits pour ça. J: My motors aren't made for this. I keep going anyway.
textes.Mes os craquent comme du bois sec, mais: My bones creak like dry wood, but my heart is green. I'm fine.
textes.Mes pages ! (Elle les recoud dans le gri: My pages! (She sews them back into the grimoire with a needle that sews by itself… almost.) Let's see… “How to turn a bubble into a butterfly.” “How to find your glasses.” “Nettle soup.” Oh! The soup! I've been looking for it for years!
textes.Mes pages ! Les trois ! … Ce soir, au Pe: My pages! All three! … Tonight, at the Perroquet, I'll play “The Azure Waltz” for you. And that song… it will give you breath, you'll see.
textes.Mes palmes te vont ? Tu nages comme un v: Do my flippers fit? You swim like a real Atlantean now. Almost.
textes.Mes parents croient que je rentre la sem: My parents think I'm coming home next week, {surnom}. I've been writing that to them for eight weeks. “Next week.” Eight letters. I don't dare tell them I want to stay. To be a painter, not a notary. Every time I pick up my pen, I hear my father sigh from across the sea.
textes.Mes parents fabriquaient des violons. Su: My parents made violins. On the mainland. In the workshop, nobody talked: we listened to the wood. A violin that sounded off, my father heard it at the fifth plank. Me, at the first. He told me: “You've got the ear.” That's all he said to me. It was a lot.
textes.Mes parents voulaient que je sois notair: My parents wanted me to be a notary. I paint notaries, sometimes. They pose well, they don't move.
textes.Mes parents étaient maraîchers, sur le c: My parents were market gardeners, on the mainland, among the leeks and cabbages. I was such a shy child I blushed when people asked me the time. So I never wore a watch. That way, I could say “I don't know” without lying. And blush anyway.
textes.Mes plus beaux champs de fleurs étaient: My finest flower fields were in the north, all the way to the sea. The winter the brambles came, a hundred years ago, I lost them in a single night. By morning there was nothing left but black thorns and a smell of burnt sugar. Since then my flowers grow in three pots outside my door. So yes, my nectar is expensive. So are flowers.
textes.Mes premiers flacons étaient tout tordus: My first bottles were all crooked: I melted the crystal shards too close to the waterfall, and they ran like honey. At the Cousins' Festival, when the sky fairies came down to visit us, I sold the lot anyway. My first buyer was Zéphyr. He drank the bottle in one gulp and said “more”.
My prices are as steady as the dome.
textes.Mes prix sont justes. Les elfes ne mente: My prices are fair. Elves never lie about prices.
textes.Mes sujets m'ont tout dit : tu as aidé m: My subjects told me everything: you helped my guard, my forge, my kitchens, my mines. A king rewards. Here: three gold coins from the Royal Forge. And the title of friend of Forgefer. The title is free. The gold isn't.
textes.Mes tuyaux ! Ne touche pas à mes tuyaux: My pipes! Don't touch my pipes!
textes.Mes {manque} bâtons ? Une flèche tordue,: My {manque} sticks? A crooked arrow is a lost arrow.
textes.Mes {manque} champignons de braise, {sur: My {manque} ember mushrooms, {surnom}! Look for the little red glows in the ash, near the fumaroles.
textes.Mes {manque} minerais, {surnom} ? Les pi: My {manque} ores, {surnom}? The rust-veined stones, on the mountainside.
textes.Mes {manque} perles… La fête approche. E: My {manque} pearls… The festival is getting close. Well, in ten years. But still.
textes.Mes {manque} plumes, {surnom} ? Regarde: My {manque} feathers, {surnom}? Look under the rocks where the ravens land.
textes.Mes {manque} rayons de miel, tu y penses: My {manque} honeycombs, have you thought about them? My oven brings it up every day.
textes.Mes {manque} rayons de miel, {surnom} ?: My {manque} honeycombs, {surnom}? On your island, in the hollow trees.
textes.Mes {manque} éclats. J'attends. J'ai l'h: My {manque} shards. I'm waiting. I'm used to waiting.
textes.Mes éclats de cristal ? Je les fais fond: My crystal shards? I melt them in the waterfall light to make bottles. I'll buy them from you if you find any.
textes.Mesdames et messieurs ! Port-Azur reconn: Ladies and gentlemen! Port-Azur today honours one of its own! Here is the key to the town. From now on, all our shopkeepers will give you a discount, and you'll always have a seat on our terraces. And in our hearts. Django, music!
textes.Messager du Soleil et de la Pluie: Messenger of the Sun and the Rain
textes.Mets-le au frais. Et toi, assieds-toi et: Put it somewhere cool. And you, sit down and eat.
textes.Mets-toi bien en face du bloc pour le po: Stand squarely in front of the block to push it.
textes.Mettre au tapis les trois champions du p: Knock down the three harbour champions, with fists and no blades: Gros-Louis (Requin Borgne), the Silent One (Veuve Écarlate), Belle-Humeur (Morue Enragée) — you can offer them a fair duel
textes.Miaou. Miaou ? Miaaaou. Cette maison app: Meow. Meow? Meeeow. This house obviously belongs to the cats.
textes.Midi ! Le soleil est tout en haut. L'omb: Noon! The sun is right at the top. The shadows are tiny.
textes.Mieux. Encore un « hop » de moins, et je: Better. One less “hop” and I'll give you a hug.
textes.Mieux. Mais ton pain, toujours trop de m: Better. But your bread, still too much honey.
textes.Mille ans que je n'avais pas parlé !: A thousand years since I last spoke!
One thousand two hundred and twelve teaspoons. This one tasted the king's soup. This one stirred a dragon's tea. Well, that's what I was told.
textes.Mille sabords… Un jour, je viendrai véri: Blistering barnacles… One day, I'll come and check.
textes.Milord ! J'aurai peut-être une plume de: Milord! I might have a flying-fish feather for you.
Milord, I still don't have change.
Milord. My moustache stays where it is.
textes.Mince ! Il est maigre comme un balai, mo: Drat! He's thin as a rake, my poor grimoire! I opened the window to let out a little draught spell, and it left with three pages! The most important ones! Well, I think so: I can't remember what was on them. That's why they're important. They flew off over the town. Find them for me, dearie. They glow a little. They're surely magic.
textes.Minos enroule sa queue autour de lui, un: Minos coils his tail around himself, once, twice, three times… “WRONG! Go back to the start of the hall, and think.” (Ombreline, the librarian, knows all the answers.)
textes.Mio, pourquoi Zéro ne fait-il que « bip: Mio, why does Zéro only ever say "beep"?
textes.Miou ronronne dans tes bras. Ramène-le à: Miou purrs in your arms. Take him back to Nebet, in Per-Hâpy!
textes.Miou, le chat roux à l'oreille tordue de: Miou, little Nebet's ginger cat with the crooked ear, has been missing for three days. Khéty says cats love the coolness of the tombs, up on the plateau of Ra.
textes.Miriel cueille les fleurs de mes abeille: Miriel picks my bees' flowers before they've finished foraging them. She says flowers belong to no one. They belong to whoever feeds on them.
textes.Miriel m'a apporté un jour une fleur de: Once, Miriel brought me a moonflower picked at high noon. “It was open, I swear!” A moonflower picked in the sun cures nothing. We argued about the price for an hour. Then we put it in a glass of water and had tea beside it.
textes.Miriel me cueille les fleurs de lune. El: Miriel picks moonflowers for me. She sells them dear, I pay a fair price. We never agree on the difference. She's a good mother, and a tough trader.
textes.Miriel sait où pousse chaque fleur de l': Miriel knows where every flower on the island grows. I know where every path goes. Between the two of us, we never get lost. Well, I do. But she always finds me.
Miriel, I'm going for a little stroll.
textes.Miriel. Tu as cueilli le pré de lavande: Miriel. Did you pick the lavender meadow?
textes.Mistral ! Ma barque te salue. Elle a enc: Mistral! My boat says hello. Her back still aches.
textes.Mistral ? Le seul client de l'île qui pa: Mistral? The only customer on the island who pays cash without haggling. Shame he makes so much noise with what he buys from me.
textes.Mistral ? Le seul homme de l'île qui fas: Mistral? The only man on the island who makes more noise than I do. I admire him, and I sleep with cotton wool in my ears.
textes.Mistral a promis une teuf sous l'eau, à: Mistral promised an underwater party, in Atlantis. I don't know how he's going to manage the speakers.
textes.Mistral est merveilleux, mais il parle d: Mistral is wonderful, but he talks about Atlantis like it's the next beach over. “Going this week?” He doesn't know what's down there. I know a little.
textes.Mistral fait trembler la baie toutes les: Mistral makes the bay shake every night. I ought to complain. But his beats sound like those of the Mother Tree, when you press your ear to the bark.
textes.Mistral joue pour nous, pour la mer et p: Mistral plays for us, for the sea and for the fairies, even if he didn't know it at first. He's been waiting for my mural for two years without ever rushing me. He's the most patient of winds.
textes.Mistral mixait sur la pointe des pieds,: Mistral used to mix on tiptoe — his decks were too high for him. My calves hurt just watching him. I took a rope, measured his arms while he played, and the next day he had a stage. It creaks a bit on the offbeat. I tell him it's on purpose. It almost is.
textes.Mistral, c'est la raison pour laquelle j: Mistral is the reason I'm still here. One single track, at sunrise, and I missed my boat. I'll never forgive him. I adore him.
textes.Mistral, c'est le cœur de la teuf. Il ou: Mistral is the heart of the party. He forgets to drink, he forgets to sleep, he even forgot his decks were too high. Me, I don't forget. That's why I'm here.
textes.Mistral, comme le vent. J'ai monté ce mu: Mistral, like the wind. I built this sound wall piece by piece, with Barnabé lending me his rowing boat to carry it all.
textes.Mistral, le vent tourne vers les nuages,: Mistral, the wind's turning towards the clouds tonight.
textes.Mistral, ton chant de baleine… c'est pre: Mistral, your whale song… it's almost right.
textes.Mistral. … Le meilleur. Il compose, je r: Mistral. … The best. He composes, I tune. He talks, I nod. It's worked like that for six years. It'll keep working.
textes.Mistral… Ce soir, tu pourrais jouer un p: Mistral… Tonight, could you play a little less loudly?
textes.Misère. Elle a appris ça où, cette petit: Good grief. Where did she learn that, this girl?
textes.Misère… Elle était bonne, au moins ?: Oh, misery… Was it good, at least?
textes.Mmh ? Pardon, je bronzais. Sylvie, la fe: Mmh? Sorry, I was sunbathing. Sylvie, Gérard's wife. Are you local?
textes.Mmh… pas maintenant… je suis occupé… à d: Mmh… not now… I'm busy… sleeping…
textes.Mmmh… une tarte… grande comme la maison…: Mmmh… a pie… as big as the house…
textes.Moaïs : la doyenne et la légende: Moai: the elder and the legend
textes.Moaïs : le petit qui n'a jamais vu la me: Moai: the little one who has never seen the sea
textes.Mochi ! Tu as de la farine jusqu'aux ore: Mochi! You've got flour up to your ears.
textes.Mochi dit que c'est un dragon-poisson, s: Mochi says it's a dragon-fish under the pool. Gland says it's a dragon. I say it's the King of the Pools, and he's got a crown.
textes.Mochi m'a demandé si son papa était dans: Mochi asked me if her papa was among the stars. I said I hadn't finished counting. That same evening, she wanted to name star four thousand two hundred and thirteen. She called it “Cerfeuil”. I wrote it down like that in my journal, in ink, not pencil. Since then, when I reach thirteen, I say good evening.
textes.Mochi monte l'escalier avec moi au crépu: Mochi climbs the stairs with me at dusk, very slowly, asking a thousand questions. A thousand and twenty-three, yesterday. She always has cake somewhere on her.
textes.Mochi, c'est ma copine, même si nos mama: Mochi's my friend, even though our mums are cross with each other over some sardine-and-carrot business. She talks nonsense about the dragon-fish. But she gives me her sardines.
textes.Mochi, c'est une pipelette. Elle parle p: Mochi's a chatterbox. She talks almost as much as me, it's very annoying. She says “dragon-fish”. She tells on me. But she helps me look for my hazelnuts. And she eats them.

textes.Mode testeur : ce lieu n'existe pas dans: Tester mode: this place doesn't exist in this version.
textes.Mode testeur : l'Île Pixelithique n'est: Tester mode: Pixelithic Island isn't here.
textes.Mode testeur : l'Île aux Moaïs n'est pas: Tester mode: Moai Island isn't here.
textes.Mode testeur : pas de maison à visiter i: Tester mode: no house to visit here.
textes.Moi ? Charpentier et forgeron de la Moue: Me? Carpenter and blacksmith of the Stubborn Seagull, the finest three-master in the kingdom. Until the rock.
textes.Moi ? Comme un coquillage à marée haute: Me? Like a shell at high tide: full of water and delighted about it!
textes.Moi ? Euh… Un verre pour un collègue, al: Me? Er… A drink for a colleague, then?
textes.Moi ? J'ai trois cent douze ans. C'est j: Me? I'm three hundred and twelve years old. That's young, where I come from. My mother says I'm “still very green”.
textes.Moi ? Jamais de la vie. Qu'est-ce que tu: Me? Never in my life. What did you find?
Me? I haven't the faintest idea.
textes.Moi ? Je ne tapote pas. (Tap-tap-tap, bo: Me? I don't tap. (Tap-tap-tap, boom-tchak.) ... Well. All right. I tap. I always have. On everything. You know, every evening, I listen to the Bilge Rats from behind the Hall's door. I know all the songs. All the drum parts. And every night, the stand-in drummer gets it wrong, and in my head, I play it right. But I don't have any sticks. Dad would never have allowed it. And besides... I'm a Lisse. They'll never want a Lisse on their stage. (He looks at your hands.) You... you have drumsticks, don't you? The ones from the Great Boucan?
textes.Moi ? Je ne vois rien d'ici. À peine tou: Me? I can't see a thing from up here. Barely the whole square.
textes.Moi ? Je suis {titre}. Un métier honnête: Me? I'm the local {titre}. An honest trade. Like all dwarf trades.
textes.Moi ? Je suis {titre}. Un métier tranqui: Me? I'm the local {titre}. A peaceful job, under the sea. Everything is peaceful, under the sea.
textes.Moi ? Rien de bien extraordinaire. Je vi: Me? Nothing very extraordinary. I've lived here forever. Well, for three centuries.
textes.Moi ? Trop sucré ? Je n'ai jamais dit ça: Me? Too sweet? I never said that! Never!
textes.Moi ? À mon âge, on s'endort quand on pe: Me? At my age, you sleep when you can, little leaf.
textes.Moi ? … Tu es malin, {surnom}. Trop mali: Me? … You're clever, {surnom}. Too clever for a human. I didn't hear the question. Look at this thread, it's fascinating.
textes.Moi Pika ! Toi viens d'où ? Pays des Lis: Me Pika! Where you from? Land of Smooth Ones? There, children smooth too? They roll to go faster? Hee hee hee!
textes.Moi aussi ! Bon, ça fait trois semaines,: Me too! Okay, it's only been three weeks, but I can feel it. Come on, there's room in Gaspard's hut. Well, ask the crabs.
textes.Moi aussi ! Mais de loin !: I saw you too! But from a distance!
I'm scared of demons too, you know.
textes.Moi aussi, j'essaie. Mais mes larmes bri: I try to as well. But my tears shine, so everyone sees them. At least yours are discreet tears. That's lucky.
textes.Moi aussi, je suis lent. On va bien s'en: I'm slow too. We'll get along just fine.
textes.Moi aussi, longtemps. Ici, c'est facile: Me too, for a long time. Here it's easy: at night, nobody watches anybody, everybody watches the sea. Come and dance at the back, near Tchoum. He keeps his eyes closed.
textes.Moi aussi. C'est bien le problème. Quand: Me too. That's exactly the problem. When the ring slipped off, I thought it was one, and a bad one. I'm trying to believe it wasn't. You see, believing is tiring.
textes.Moi aussi. Un peu, beaucoup. Ce n'est pa: Me too. A little, a lot. Fear's no big deal. You just have to breathe slower than it does. It gets tired before you do.
textes.Moi je sais qui vole les croissants. C'e: I know who steals the croissants. It's a little white dog! He hides them by the crates, at the end of the quay. But I like him, so shh.
Three times, me. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Moi, Majesté ? J'archivais… les étoiles: Me, Majesty? I was archiving… starfish.
textes.Moi, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, je t'a: I, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, shall go with you! Adventure awaits us, and so does dinner!
textes.Moi, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, je te: I, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, challenge you! Chaaarge!
textes.Moi, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, je vou: I, Sir Tancrède de Tournevent, follow you! No, I lead you! No, I walk beside you! Onward!
I was scared of the sea.
Me, I forget everything. Very handy.
textes.Moi, je n'ai que des papillons. … Des pa: Me, I only have butterflies. … Stone butterflies. They don't fly very well.
textes.Moi, je t'ai porté avec un sac de charbo: I carried you with a sack of coal on top.
textes.Moi, plus tard, je serai archère ! Ou he: When I grow up, I'll be an archer! Or an herbalist. Or an explorer! Like you!
textes.Moins d'une minute ! Tu as des ailes aux: Under a minute! You've got wings on your feet. Here, I'll teach you my secret: breathe well, and never look back.
Not so loud! My father's coming this way.
textes.Moins fort ? Peuchère, les nains vont en: Less loud? Peuchère, the dwarves will complain again!
Less than the last one. Again.
textes.Moins vite, petit. Mes genoux ont soixan: Slower, lad. My knees are seventy-five years old.
textes.Momo ! Ce soir, je fais deux pirouettes: Momo! Tonight I'm doing two pirouettes!
textes.Momo ? Un garçon adorable qui perce des: Momo? A lovely boy who drills holes in shells. HOLES, {surnom}. I'm fond of him, but I recount my collection after every one of his visits.
Momo says he danced with a dolphin. Well, he danced in the water, and a dolphin swam by. That's pretty much the same.
textes.Momo est gentil comme tout, mais tout ce: Momo's as sweet as can be, but anything left lying around ends up on him: my cap, my bucket, my boat. He doesn't steal, he says. He borrows forever.
textes.Momo et moi, on fait un concours de saut: Momo and I have a jumping contest every night, in front of the wall of sound. We mark the height on a palm tree, with a shell. The palm tree is covered in them. One night, Momo jumped so high he grabbed a coconut. It fell back on his head. He said: “Legend.” I said it didn't count. But it was a legend.
Momo swears he danced with a dolphin. So I did the dolphin in my show: I jump, I go “kik-kik”, I land in a bucket of water. Momo came to watch, ready to grumble. He laughed so hard he gave every kid a necklace. Fifteen necklaces. It's my best fee ever, and he's the one who paid it.
textes.Momo m'a fait un collier avec un coquill: Momo made me a necklace with a heart-shaped shell. He gave it to me without a word, which is very rare for Momo. I said “Oh, a crab!” as a joke. He said: “Yes, that's it, a crab.” He went bright red under his bandana. I wear it every day. It's a very pretty crab.
textes.Momo saute plus haut que moi. D'un doigt: Momo jumps higher than me. By a finger. He tells everyone. But I do a pirouette in the air, and a pirouette counts double.
textes.Momo saute plus haut que tout le monde,: Momo jumps higher than everyone, smiles bigger than everyone, and says he danced with a dolphin. It's almost true. I was there.
textes.Momo transforme mes coquillages en colli: Momo turns my shells into necklaces and my days into bursts of laughter. He jumps too high, he talks too loud, and he asks me only one question a day. For Momo, that's very polite.
textes.Momo, c'est mon associé au marché et mon: Momo is my partner at the market and my cousin at heart. He counts the coins, I count the smiles. At the end of the day, I've always earned more than him.
textes.Momo, mon frère ! On a vendu combien, au: Momo, my brother! How much did we sell today?
textes.Momo, tiens, pour tes colliers. Il vient: Momo, here, for your necklaces. It came from very far away.
textes.Momo, tu n'aurais pas vu mon seau ?: Momo, you haven't seen my bucket, have you?
textes.Mon Kevin ! Maître-nageur, le plus beau: My Kevin! A lifeguard, the handsomest on the beach, and the strongest. He saves everyone, except his mother at six in the morning when the ice needs carrying. Five hundred push-ups, but not one crate.
textes.Mon Pépin ! Mon petit Pépin ! Il n'est p: My Pépin! My little Pépin! He hasn't come home from the Academy, and Ortie says he wanted to see the glowing mushrooms in the Ash Wood… The wood, at night, is full of wild imps! Would you go and find him? He has a little lantern, and horns as big as hazelnuts.
textes.Mon acier ne fond pas. Il se laisse fair: My steel doesn't melt. It just goes along with it, out of politeness.
textes.Mon amateur de fraise ! Tu as goûté le f: My strawberry fan! Have you tried Nina's strawberry-dolphin? She's going to ask you, get your answer ready.
textes.Mon amateur de musique ! Passe ce soir a: My music lover! Come by the Perroquet tonight, I've saved you a D chord. The best one.
textes.Mon ami ! Regardez-le tourner, mon phare: My friend! Look at it turning, my lighthouse. Thanks to you.
textes.Mon ami du piment ! Ta bouillabaisse, je: My chilli friend! I made your bouillabaisse volcano-style. Cry away.
textes.Mon ami du « presque » ! Je te dirai qua: My “almost” buddy! I'll tell you when the dolphin swings by again. And this time, it'll be “absolutely”.
textes.Mon ancêtre, Alan Le Goff, était le pilo: My ancestor, Alan Le Goff, was the Léviathan's pilot. He was the one who plotted the course, that night. Right onto the rocks. Ever since, the Le Goffs draw maps to make up for it. My father drew the bay, my grandfather the stars. Me, as a boy, I drew the ship's frames in chalk on the floor of the harbour master's office.
textes.Mon appareil ! Et… vous avez pris une ph: My camera! And… did you take a photo with it? Oh no. Just as well. Here, for the climb.
textes.Mon appareil photo ! Je l'ai posé au bel: My camera! I left it at the lookout, at the top of the hill, to photograph the sunset, and I came back down without it. My legs won't climb back up. Would you mind?
textes.Mon apprenti grenouilleur ! Grommelot te: My apprentice frog-maker! Grommelot says hello. Well, he grunts in your direction.
My apprenticeship lasted two hundred years. One day, to prove to Grandmother that the blue berries were harmless, I ate a handful. I spent two days chatting with fireflies. They had a lot of opinions. Grandmother wrote it all down in her journal, under “Aëlwen, case number one”.
textes.Mon arc est taillé dans une branche tomb: My bow is carved from a branch that fell from the Mother Tree. We never cut the Tree. Never.
textes.Mon arrière-arrière-grand-père était à b: My great-great-grandfather was aboard on the night of the wreck. He told the story to his son, who told it to his… all the way down to me. I'm the last page of the book.
textes.Mon associé du « ça dépend » ! Alors, au: My “it depends” partner! So, what does it depend on today? Apples, I hope.
textes.Mon aïeul, Hervé Le Floc'h, était maître: My ancestor, Hervé Le Floc'h, was master gunner on the Léviathan. Forty cannons, and he called every one of them by a first name. Me, I grew up on the lower deck, playing hide-and-seek in their cold mouths. My mother would shout: “Jos, get out of that cannon!” It's the sentence I heard most in my whole childhood.
textes.Mon aïeule commandait le Léviathan quand: My ancestor commanded the Léviathan when it ran aground. Two hundred years later, it's still a Kerhervé at the helm. A helm that doesn't turn any more, but still.
textes.Mon bleu ! Je vous ai mis dans ma derniè: My blue! I put you in my latest canvas. There, under the jetty. You can't see yourself? I can.
textes.Mon catalogue de Port-Azur fait trois ca: My Port-Azur catalogue fills three notebooks. Half of it is Pauline's stories: the button of the elegant pirate, the spoon of the cross-eyed queen, the tooth of the dragon who swallowed a lighthouse. I write them down word for word. The day she opens her guesthouse, I'll give her the notebooks. She'll have plenty to tell.
textes.Mon cerf-volant, je l'ai acheté chez le: I bought my kite from the souvenir man, Victor. Half price! It had all the colours, red, yellow, blue, green, and a big tail with knots. It flew really well. And then the wind went “whoooosh”, the string went “snap”, and it went off towards the hill, over the houses. I watched it till it was teeny tiny.
textes.Mon cerf-volant… Le vent l'a emporté ver: My kite… The wind carried it off towards the hill, over there, above the houses. It's stuck somewhere, I'm sure of it. Can you find it? Please?
textes.Mon cerf-volant… il s'est envolé… Il éta: My kite… it flew away… It was red, yellow, blue and green, and it had a tail with bows on…
textes.Mon chapelet ! (Elle le serre contre ell: My rosary! (She hugs it to herself, then pulls away.) It's… a little sticky. It's nothing! It's nothing at all! Oh Dawn, thank you. And thank you. You went looking for something inside a frog, for me. Nobody had ever done that.
textes.Mon cher Marcel ! Toujours votre mètre ?: My dear Marcel! Still got your tape measure?
textes.Mon cher Raymond ! Toujours fidèle au po: My dear Raymond! Faithful as ever!
textes.Mon cher Raymond ! Une revanche, demain: My dear Raymond! A rematch, tomorrow?
textes.Mon cher citoyen d'honneur ! Port-Azur v: My dear honorary citizen! Port-Azur owes you so much.
textes.Mon client de profil ! J'ai repéré la lu: My profile client! I've found the ideal light for your good side: seven in the evening, in front of the lighthouse.
My favourite customer! Well, my customer. Come and see what's new!
textes.Mon collectionneur ! J'ai reçu des boule: My collector! Snow globes came in this morning. There's one waiting for you, I can feel it.
textes.Mon complice des lectures cachées ! Vous: My partner in secret reading! Do you have a book under your pillow right now? Don't answer. I know.
textes.Mon danseur en cachette ! Tu as dansé, d: My secret dancer! Have you danced since? In your room? I won't tell anyone.
textes.Mon dernier jour de glacier, il faisait: My last day as an ice-cream seller, it was hot enough to melt the seagulls. I opened my cool box at ten o'clock: everything had melted. Vanilla, strawberry, lemon — one lukewarm soup. Across the way, at Bruno's, the queue went all the way to the fountain. I sold my soup to the seagulls, at a knock-down price. They didn't pay. The next day, I was selling postcards.
textes.Mon dessin du Roi, avec la couronne, pap: My drawing of the King, with the crown, Grandpa pinned it above his bed. Every time he walks past, he looks at it. Once, I saw him touch the crown with the tip of his finger. Really gently. As if he recognised it. Grandpas are weird.
My back won't let me sit.
textes.Mon défunt mari était pêcheur. Fernand l: My late husband was a fisherman. Fernand knew him. That's why I give him the best spot on the quay.
textes.Mon engrenage ! Pas une dent de cassée !: My gear! Not a single tooth broken! Look… I put it back… I turn the crank… IT TURNS! It turns! For ever! Or at least until the end of the Fair. Here, take this, and this hat: it has a fan. I don't know why I had it, but it's yours.
textes.Mon entorse ? Un faux pas en pointant. À: My sprain? A misstep while pointing. To Margaux, I said it was while shooting. To Gisèle, dodging one of Marcel's balls. To Paulo, saving a baguette. Well. All three are a little bit true. What's certain is that with this ankle, I curse the morning deliveries step by step.
textes.Mon explorateur préféré ! Racontez-moi t: My favourite explorer! Tell me everything.
textes.Mon fantôme préféré ! Ta photo floue est: My favourite ghost! Your blurry photo is hanging next to Titou's. You make a fine pair.
textes.Mon fiancé est parti en mer quand j'avai: My fiancé went to sea when I was twenty. I promised him I'd hear the bell ring for his return. He never came back, but I never stopped listening.
textes.Mon fils ! Tu tombes bien, je racontais: My son! Perfect timing, I was just telling everyone…
textes.Mon fils dit trois mots par jour, et moi: My son says three words a day, and I say three thousand: between the two of us, it averages out. He listens to all my stories without a word. Best audience in the world.
textes.Mon four boude. Je lui parle gentiment,: My oven is sulking. I talk to it nicely, but it sulks.
textes.Mon fromager ne parle pas. … Il a dit qu: My kapok tree doesn't talk. … What did it say?
textes.Mon frère Rúmil et moi, nous sommes nés: My brother Rúmil and I were born three centuries ago, on the night of the storm, the night the firefly spirits flew away. Our mother used to say the Wood had lost its lights and gained two children. Maybe that's why we've always chased after light, he and I.
textes.Mon frère de cordes ! Tu avais dit : ave: My brother of the strings! You said: with a song. I've written the forty-second verse. For the two of us.
textes.Mon grand regret : ne jamais avoir quitt: My great regret: never having left Port-Azur. I get seasick. A seasick cartographer… that's my tragedy.
textes.Mon grand-oncle sait tout, et il le dit: My great-uncle knows everything, and says it softly. He's four hundred and twelve. I still have a lot to learn, and I fully expect him to give me the time.
My grandfather came with the clan. Behind Mère-Lune, on foot, through the mist. The wolves followed her here. At twenty, I won the Great Race. Last wolf to have won it. At twenty-five, I became a guard. Mère-Lune knitted me this red scarf. I still wear it. Nothing else to say.
textes.Mon grand-père jouait sur les places, de: My grandfather played in town squares, from town to town, with a hat at his feet. As a little boy, I sat beside him and counted the coins. One coin, one note. He said it was the only useful arithmetic. He gave me my first guitar when I was six. It was bigger than me. I slept with it.
textes.Mon grand-père s'est endormi sous l'Arbr: My grandfather fell asleep beneath the Mother Tree before he could teach me. It was Faelar who showed me the old way: stretch the net above the fountain, wait for the first ray, and above all, don't talk. Not talking, with Faelar beside you, was the hardest part. It took me a hundred years. Lirael put that ray in her first lantern.
textes.Mon grand-père, c'est le meilleur guette: My grandad is the best lookout in the world. Forty years in the crow's nest! He's seen a white whale, a ghost ship and a blue light. I believe him about everything.
textes.Mon groin a un super-pouvoir : il trouve: My snout has a superpower: it finds food.
textes.Mon histoire ? Il n'y a pas grand-chose: My story? There's not much to tell.
textes.Mon hydromel est un triomphe ! Le roi en: My honey drink is a triumph! The king drank a whole barrel. He danced on the table. The table remembers.
textes.Mon loir ! Tu as rêvé de quoi, cette nui: My little sleepyhead! What did you dream about last night? Don't lie, I can smell dreams. A bit.
textes.Mon lève-tôt ! Je t'ai gardé un pain cha: My early bird! I've saved you a warm loaf. The first of the batch, the one that sings when you break it.
My manor holds four thousand objects. A roc's egg, an admiral's moustache, a snow globe from Victor… my favourite.
textes.Mon mari, Cerfeuil, était boulanger. Il: My husband, Cerfeuil, was a baker. He burnt every loaf, but he had the best palate of anyone. He left with the mist when Mochi was one, five years ago. I couldn't sleep any more. Pivoine made me the first vial of mist, and I slept. And Pépin, his best friend, has come every morning since to carry the flour sacks. He'd promised him.
textes.Mon meilleur client ! Clou, sors le tabo: My best customer! Clou, bring out the stool.
My best customer! Well, my customer.
textes.Mon morceau du lever de soleil n'a pas d: My sunrise track has no name. Every morning, Zoé suggests one: “Hello Sea”, “Jelly Legs”, “Zoé Stays”. She's up to twenty-one. I haven't picked any of them. I think I like her searching too much.
textes.Mon neveu. Le fils de ma sœur. Je voulai: My nephew. My sister's son. I wanted a guard. I got a runner. He talks too much, he watches the Clearing instead of the forest. But he comes up on time. That counts.
textes.Mon oiseau de nuit ! Ce soir, Django jou: My night owl! Django's playing tonight. I'll save you the stool at the end, the one that doesn't creak.
My uncle Bedaine swaps. I sell. He says it's a disgrace for a tanuki. I say coins fit in a pocket, and a goat doesn't.
textes.Mon oncle est un mur. Un bon mur, solide: My uncle is a wall. A good wall, solid, protective. But just try making a wall laugh. I've been trying for eighty years.
textes.Mon oncle m'a élevée au milieu des trocs: My uncle raised me surrounded by swaps. He's impossible, stubborn as a carpet that doesn't fly, and I adore him. He says I shame him. He still takes my apples. Well, he swaps for them.
textes.Mon oncle, le garde. Il voulait un neveu: My uncle, the guard. He wanted a guard nephew, he got a runner nephew. He pretends to be disappointed. But I've seen him leaning out of the watch post during my races. I have, I have.
textes.Mon or ! L'heure dorée vient de passer,: My gold! The golden hour just went by, and I thought of you. Don't laugh, it's my job.
My trousers say no! … A small one.
textes.Mon papa, il est gentil et il fait des b: My daddy's nice and he makes daddy jokes. He takes pictures of everything, all the time. But sometimes he puts the machine away and looks with his eyes. Those are the best times.
textes.Mon papa, il s'appelait Cerfeuil. Je m'e: My papa was called Cerfeuil. I don't remember him, I was too little. But I know he burned the bread and laughed really loud, Godfather Pépin told me. I've got his wooden spoon, it's all black at the end. He went away with the mist. So in the evening, I say hello to the mist. That way, it's polite.
textes.Mon papy, c'est le meilleur pêcheur du m: My grandpa is the best fisherman in the world. He's never caught the King, but that's because he's waiting for the right moment. I look harder. But he waits harder.
textes.Mon pas-trop ! Tu as mangé tes trois car: My not-very! Have you eaten your three carrots? Not four, eh. Four weighs you down.
textes.Mon patient raisonnable ! Vous voyez, je: My sensible patient! You see, I remember you. So, no new scrapes?
textes.Mon petit cocotier ! J'ai une noix bien: My little coconut palm! I've got a nice fresh nut for you. I'll open it in one go. Crack!
textes.Mon petit frère garde la halle du roi av: My little brother guards the king's hall with a shiny shield. Me, I carry coal. He's got the fine job. I've got the good back. Well, I had.
textes.Mon petit frère, Gland ! Il parle plus v: My little brother, Gland! He talks faster than the wind and loses his hazelnuts faster than he hides them. He wants to build bridges all the way to the moon. He'll get there, I think.
textes.Mon petit frère. Il oublie la nacelle. I: My little brother. He forgets the basket. He forgets the time. But he never forgets anything important. Hm. Solid.
textes.Mon petit tanuki ! Tout se troque, hein: My little tanuki! Everything can be swapped, eh? … Almost everything. You'll see.
textes.Mon peuple forge depuis mille ans. Nos l: My people have been forging for a thousand years. Our blades have slain dragons. Well, one dragon. A small one. It had a cold.
textes.Mon peuple vivait sur une île, autrefois: My people once lived on an island, like yours. One night the sea rose and swallowed it. The Great Crystal wrapped us in a bubble of air, and we stayed. A thousand years, under the sea.
textes.Mon plus grand exploit ? (Il bombe le to: My greatest feat? (He puffs out his chest, then deflates it.) Friend… I'll confess something. They're all lost in the fog. All of them. I need a REAL feat. With a witness. And sunshine. Deep in the Goblin Wood, the goblins have a camp, and a chief, and a banner decorated with the feathers from the guards' helmets. Defeat him with me, or in front of me, or even a little in my place, and bring back the banner. I, SIR TANCRÈDE DE TOURNEVENT, swear to follow you afterwards to the ends of the earth!
textes.Mon pointeur ! Tu fais équipe avec moi,: My pointer! You're on my team next time. Marcel's already shaking.
textes.Mon pote ! Tu tombes bien, Mistral va lâ: My mate! Perfect timing, Mistral's about to drop a big one.
textes.Mon premier examen, à dix ans : le gâtea: My first exam, at ten: the mooncake hidden by Mère-Lune. I followed the trail all morning. Under the stump, there was half the cake left, and tanuki tracks all around, wide, happy ones. Bedaine told me later he was “checking the hiding place”. With his teeth, apparently.
textes.Mon premier jour de serveur : douze tass: My first day as a waiter: twelve cups, one by one, on the tiled floor, right in front of the owner. At the thirteenth, a little girl planted herself in front of me: “You hold the tray with your hand open. Not like a fish.” It was Gisèle, aged ten. She was right. I never broke another thing. Almost.
textes.Mon premier jour de vigie tout seul, j'a: My first day on watch alone, I saw a white shape zip between the trees, faster than the wind. I shouted “Alert! Alert!” with all my might. My uncle came back up, grumbling, eighty steps. It was Bondi training. He said: “A fast rabbit is not an alert.” For a runner it is!
textes.Mon premier matin ici, Mistral a passé l: My first morning here, Mistral played the really soft track, the sunrise one. I sat down in the sand and cried like a little kid. He looked at me from behind his decks and let the track play through twice. He never does that. He said afterwards it was an accident.
textes.Mon premier pont à moi, c'est celui de l: My very own first bridge is the west one. I hung singing-stones underneath. On opening day, the wind got up, the bridge danced, sang… and Bedaine got seasick! Later, the Zéphyr's engineers wanted metal bridges. I asked if metal knows how to dance. They went off to take notes somewhere else. Yoo-hoo, bye-bye!
textes.Mon premier pont, je l'ai fait tout seul: My first bridge, I built it all by myself when I was five: two twigs over a puddle, with a hazelnut in the middle for weight. Pomme-de-Pin looked at it very seriously. She blew on it. It danced! She said it was a real bridge. I ate the hazelnut. The bridge sort of collapsed. I kept it anyway.
textes.Mon premier portrait de lui, je l'ai fai: My first portrait of him, I did during a chorus: mouth wide open, eyebrows up. He looked at the drawing and said: “I look like I've got toothache.” It's true, a little. Since then, he plays in profile, facing the sea. He thinks it's punishing me. His profile is magnificent.
textes.Mon premier soir au Perroquet, avec mon: My first evening at the Perroquet, with my first tray, I spilled a whole punch over a big docker. On his shirt, down his neck, everywhere. He didn't even get up. He just said: “It's nothing, it smells nice.” His name was Lucas. I've never got over it. Him, I think he washed his shirt.
textes.Mon premier soir, j'ai fait un grand ges: My first night, I made a big gesture and Bastien ended up sitting in the sea, his cap drifting out to sea. I apologised ten times, laughing. He kept saying “It's nothing, it's nothing”, with water up to his waist. He didn't move for a long while. I think he was stunned.
textes.Mon premier soir, j'ai marché dans la me: My first night, I walked into the sea and my feet lit up blue. I screamed. Mistral came down from his decks to explain: “It's plankton.” I said: “Yes, and it's dancing.” He laughed and said: “Exactly.” Since then, plankton officially dances. Mistral said so.
textes.Mon premier soufflet, je l'avais cousu m: My first bellows I sewed myself: it wheezed like a seal with a cold. Today's was made by Nolwenn from an old sail, at fifteen, her first job all on her own. The stitches are a bit crooked. She's offered a hundred times to redo it. I refuse. It blows very well, crooked.
textes.Mon premier vrai voyageur, c'était un in: My first real traveller was an engineer from Cliquetis, off the Zéphyr. He fell out of his hammock three times in the night. In the morning, he'd written in chalk on the bulkhead: “Charming. But is a bed too much to ask?” I kept the chalk. That was the day I knew: one day, I'll have beds. Real ones. With legs.
textes.Mon punch, c'est ma fierté. Mais il me m: My punch is my pride and joy. But I'm short of coconuts: the boat from the jungle hasn't come.
textes.Mon père a porté le courrier trente ans,: My father carried the post for thirty years, nose in the air. Now he counts the stars. I work by day, him by night. We cross paths at dusk. That's something.
textes.Mon père a sculpté la statue du roi Atla: My father carved the statue of King Atlas, up there, back when there was marble and sunshine. Under the sea, no more quarries: he switched to coral, grumbling. On my eighth birthday he gave me his silver chisel. “Red coral bites. Bite harder.” That's all I know about the trade. The rest, I made up.
textes.Mon père bouche les trous de ce bateau,: My father plugs the holes in this ship, like his father before him. He sighs, he grumbles, he never says “I love you”. He says it with the crêpes he saves for me. I love him. That's exactly the problem.
My father is a notary, on the mainland. As a little girl, I drew in the margins of his deeds while he saw his clients. One day, I illustrated a house sale with seagulls everywhere. Very good seagulls, they were. The client went to another notary. My father banned me from his office. I drew under the door.
textes.Mon père gardait la Grande Porte avant m: My father guarded the Great Gate before me. I grew up in the guardhouse, between his spear and his mug. My first word was “Halt”. My mother wanted “mama”. She waited. The second was “Who goes there”. Hmph.
textes.Mon père pêchait, ma mère ramendait les: My father fished, my mother mended the nets, and I followed old Mother Tréphine, the healer, at every low tide. She had me taste the seaweeds one by one: “This one heals, that one makes you sick, remember which.” I remembered. Especially that one.
textes.Mon père pêchait, son père aussi, et com: My father fished, and his father too, and so on all the way back to the shipwreck. Before that they probably fished as well, just somewhere else. At five, I held the line while my father slept in the bottom of the boat. One day, I hauled up a conger eel bigger than me. I think it was the one that brought me back to shore.
textes.Mon père tenait La Rose des Vents avant: My father ran La Rose des Vents before me. I lived under the counter, among the atlases. In the afternoons, I'd take a piece of chalk and redraw his maps on the cobbles of the quay: the coasts, the capes, the bays. The fishermen walked over them laughing. In the evening, the port's brooms wiped everything away. The next day, I started again.
textes.Mon père tressait les cordes des arcs, m: My father braided bowstrings, my mother sang so they would hold. When I was three, I plucked a bowstring and cried, because it played a very sad “A”. My father understood before I did: he carved me a little harp from a fallen branch. Five strings, and a lot of ambition.
textes.Mon père était calfat, mon grand-père au: My father was a caulker, so was my grandfather, and his before him, ever since the wreck. At seven, I was given my first job: holding the tar pot. I burnt three fingers on the first day. My father said: “Good. Now you know what's hot.” That was his whole lesson. It was a good lesson.
My father was a caulker, my grandfather too. My whole family has spent their lives keeping this ship from drowning. It's run aground, but it could still drown. It's a talent.
textes.Mon père était changeur à la Grande Hall: My father was a money-changer in the Great Hall. He weighed gold, I weighed my marbles. At four, I swallowed a ruby that was lying on his counter. The whole family waited three days. We got it back. Don't ask how. My father set it in my first belt buckle. I still wear it.
textes.Mon père était charpentier de marine. J': My father was a ship's carpenter. I grew up among hulls under repair, and I'd climb the masts the moment his back was turned. At six, I could tie a bowline, a clove hitch and a half hitch. Write my name, no. My mother used to say I had tar instead of blood. She wasn't wrong.
textes.Mon père était docker, comme moi. Petit,: My father was a docker, like me. When I was little, I slept on the flour sacks while he unloaded the boats. It was soft, it smelled nice. When I wasn't sleeping, I counted seagulls. Once I counted forty-three. My father said: “Good. Now count the sacks.”
textes.Mon père était gardien de l'horloge de l: My father was keeper of the square's clock, and his father before him. As a little girl, I'd go up the tower with them and nap on the floor, my cheek against the frame of the mechanism. Tick, tock. I've never slept so well since. My mother said I had a pendulum instead of a heart. She wasn't entirely wrong.
textes.Mon père était guetteur avant moi, et so: My father was a lookout before me, and his father too. In our family, you're born with one eye on the horizon. At eight, my father hoisted me up to the main top and said: “Look. And say nothing until you're sure.” I looked. I've never talked much since.
textes.Mon père était le boulanger d'Au Pain Do: My father was the baker at Au Pain Doré, and his father before him. I grew up in the bakehouse, up to my knees in flour. My father gave me the rolls that went wrong, and I practised pointing in the yard, with a loaf for the jack. At ten, I could land a stale roll a finger's width from the loaf. The neighbourhood dogs adored me.
textes.Mon père était pêcheur, mon grand-père a: My father was a fisherman, so was my grandfather, and his father before him, on this very beach. At four, I slept at the bottom of the boat, between the lobster pots. I knew the names of the fish before I knew my letters. Even today, I read the sea better than a book. Yep.
textes.Mon père, Thrain le Lent, quarante et un: My father, Thrain the Slow, forty-first king, wanted to teach me to rule. Me, I wanted to hide in the cellar of the Blazing Mug, behind the biggest barrel. A young innkeeper found me there one evening. Ulfa. She didn't give me away. She taught me to pull a fizz. A king never forgets.
textes.Mon père, Tobias, bouche les trous du ba: My father, Tobias, plugs the holes in the ship. My mother, Annaig, used to sew its sails. I grew up between the two, with tar on one cheek and thread on the other. My mother said I was a well-caulked sail. I never knew if it was a compliment. I think it was.
textes.Mon père, c'est Tilleul. Il a pris tous: My father is Tilleul. He took all the family's words. I took the hammer. As a cub, during his stories, I banged on pots. Bing. Bang. It helped him, he said. At ten, old Charbon, the bears' blacksmith, took me on as an apprentice. He didn't talk much. We got on well.
My father. He talks for two. For ten. You want to talk, talk to Tilleul. Me, I listen. I love him. Don't repeat that to him.
textes.Mon père. Il pêche, je vends. Il jure qu: My father. He fishes, I sell. He swears he's seen the Pond King. I think he dreamt it. And it worries me, watching him spend his life on that jetty.
textes.Mon péché mignon ? %s. Rien qu'en y pens: My guilty pleasure? %s. Just thinking about it makes me smile.
textes.Mon record tient toujours, Pépin ?: Is my record still standing, Pépin?
textes.Mon rouge ! J'ai pensé à vous en broyant: My red! I thought of you while grinding my colours. Hibiscus turns brown: you're worth more than hibiscus.
textes.Mon rêve ? Entrer dans le Cœur-de-Pierre: My dream? To get inside Stoneheart and draw what's in there. First you'd have to open the gate. And for that…
textes.Mon rêve ? Faire le tour de l'archipel e: My dream? To sail round the archipelago. The village, the jungle, the elves' island, the dwarves' mountain… they even say there's an island that flies.
textes.Mon rêve ? Je n'y ai jamais vraiment pen: My dream? I've never really thought about it.
textes.Mon rêve ? Ouvrir une paillote sur chaqu: My dream? Open a beach hut on every island. Even at the dwarves'. Especially at the dwarves', they're thirsty.
textes.Mon sabre corsaire, je le forge comme ma: I forge my corsair sabre the way my grandmother made pie: hitting hard and singing off-key.
textes.Mon sauveur ! Mon héros ! Mon Fernand !: My saviour! My hero! My Fernand!
textes.Mon sauveur ! Écoute, ce soir je joue «: My saviour! Listen, tonight I'm playing “The Azur Waltz” just for you.
textes.Mon secret ? Le champignon de braise. Il: My secret? The ember mushroom. It grows in the hot ash, near the fumaroles. It tingles, it warms, it heals.
textes.Mon secret ? Le miel sauvage. Les abeill: My secret? Wild honey. The bees of Bois-Doré feed on the Mother Tree: their honey is golden like its leaves.
textes.Mon secret ? Une goutte de miel des elfe: My secret? A drop of elf honey in the dough. Shh.
textes.Mon serré, Gisèle ! Le meilleur de l'arc: My short black, Gisèle! The best in the archipelago!
textes.Mon serré, Gisèle ! Le plus serré de l'a: My espresso, Gisèle! The strongest in the archipelago!
textes.Mon soufflet a un trou. Mon apprenti a u: My bellows have a hole. My apprentice has a hole in his head. Everything's leaking today.
textes.Mon sérieux préféré ! Toi qui dis tout f: My favourite straight face! You who say everything frankly: tell me frankly, do I look serious right now?
textes.Mon trésor de braise ! (Elle serre Pépin: My ember treasure! (She hugs Pépin so tight that his little horns turn red.) You, you come back to the market whenever you like: the chili peppers are yours, for life. Well, these ones. Here.
textes.Mon vieil ami ! Assieds-toi, enfin… il n: My old friend! Have a seat, well… there's no chair. Have a seat standing up.
textes.Mon village est à l'est, derrière la Sal: My village is to the east, behind the Bell Hall! Listen to the melody at the lectern, then play it again on the bells.
textes.Mon voyageur du village ! Votre petite c: My traveller from the village! Your little cross is still on my map. It seems to be doing very well.
textes.Mon voyageur venu de la mer ! Votre peti: My traveller from the sea! Your little wave is still in the corner of my map. With its question mark.
textes.Mon élève qui danse « plutôt bien » ! Le: My pupil who dances “pretty well”! The cat's waiting for you on the square. He wants to see your crab.
textes.Mon épée d'acier. Trois semaines de forg: My steel sword. Three weeks at the forge, tempered in seawater. Hold it tight: it's my masterpiece. Don't let it rust.
textes.Mon épée te va bien. Évidemment : c'est: My sword suits you. Of course it does: I forged it.
textes.Mon épée, c'est pour les combats qui vie: My sword is for the fights to come. Strange things happen at night in the jungle, {surnom}. Train on my dummies downstairs: three hits in a row, and the last one hurts.
textes.Mon étal ? Pommes, baies, et le miel de: My stall? Apples, berries, and forest honey, which Pomme-de-Pin climbs right to the top to fetch. I pay her in coins, obviously. I live with Lilas in the pond tree, and in the evening I dance behind her at the Circle. And between customers, I make fun of Bondi's three carrots. That's free. The only free thing on my stall.
textes.Monsieur Edmond ! Il a encore ronflé, ce: Monsieur Edmond! He was snoring again last night, on the fourth floor!
textes.Monsieur Edmond, c'est trente ans de réc: Monsieur Edmond is thirty years at reception and a moustache trimmed to the millimetre. He taught me everything. He says I talk too much. He doesn't talk enough, so it balances out.
textes.Monsieur Fil, le marchand de programmes: Mr Fil, the program seller of the Alleys, sold you his "Turbo-Adventure 3000" for a few coins. He copied it into your travel journal… and it was a virus! A fake one, luckily: it's part of the game. Glitch, the Arcade District hacker, is helping you get rid of it.
textes.Monsieur Fil, votre programme était un v: Monsieur Fil, your program was a virus!
textes.Monsieur Hulotte ! Vous voyez mon museau: Mister Hulotte! Can you see my snout?
textes.Monsieur Hulotte, il voit dans le noir,: Mister Hulotte can see in the dark, and he counts all the stars. He climbs the stairs really slowly, so I climb with him. He says I ask too many questions. He answers anyway.
textes.Monsieur Lisse range ses panneaux « BIEN: Monsieur Lisse is packing away his “COMING SOON” signs. He looks at the Hall. He taps his foot. In rhythm.
textes.Monsieur Prosper, le marchand de maisons: Mr Prosper, the house seller of the Upper Town, is selling the Wisteria Cottage: a bed, a fireplace, a trophy shelf and a front covered in wisteria. Three hundred coins. He exaggerates everything. Except the wisteria.
textes.Monsieur désire un café ? Il est brûlant: Would sir like a coffee? It is scalding. I know, I tasted it with my finger.
textes.Monsieur et Madame Térieur ont deux fils: Mr. and Mrs. Side have two sons. What are their names?
textes.Monsieur le Baron, vous êtes tout décoif: Baron, your hair is all over the place!
textes.Monsieur le maire est trop aimable. Si v: The mayor is too kind. If you're looking for a bed, our rooms are waiting for you. The night passes quickly here.
textes.Monsieur le maire, une holo-photo pour u: Mr. Mayor, a holo-photo for a tourist?
textes.Monsieur le maire. Vous avez fait vos vo: Mister Mayor. Done your vocal warm-ups?
Mister Thief. Tomorrow, I'll beat you.
textes.Mont Bolognaise — chemin de la Marmite\n:
Mount Bolognese — Cooking Pot path
Caution: unpredictable sauce eruptions.
Wear a bib.
textes.Mont Fumant. Il ronfle, il fume, il crac: Smoking Mountain. He snore, he smoke, he spit red. Never walk on red: red eat feet. Big-Beaks like fly above: hot air, they glide.
textes.Monte sur les passerelles, la vue est ma: Go up on the walkways, the view is magnificent. But don't look down.
textes.Monter au château du ciel et boire une b: To go up to the castle in the sky and share a fizz with the Sky Kings, as in my great-grandfather's day. A king talks better to a king. Especially over a fizz.
textes.Monter au sommet de la Flèche de Cristal: Fly to the top of the Crystal Spire (with the Star Glider) and give the Heart back its shards and its light
textes.Monter au sommet de la Tour Penchée en l: Levitate up to the top of the Leaning Tower (key 8 then V; in VR, left trigger) and ring the bell (E)
textes.Monter au sommet du Mont Fusain: Climb to the summit of Mount Charcoal
textes.Monter au sommet du Mont Fusain (le chem: Climb to the summit of Mount Charcoal (the path starts at the north exit of the clearing) and take the pot of purple at the foot of the cairn
textes.Monter dans le Village des Arbres-Maison: Climb up into the Treehouse Village
textes.Monter en haut de la Cascade d'Encre (pa: Climb to the top of the Ink Waterfall (by the Mount Charcoal path, then along the stream) and take the pot of orange by the water, on the Lip
textes.Monter jusqu'à la Marmite, en haut du Mo: Climb up to the Cooking Pot, at the top of Mount Bolognese
textes.Monter sur Astralys par le rayon d'accue: Go up to Astralys on the welcome beam (the glowing buoy, in the north-west of the archipelago)
textes.Monter vers le centre de l'île (à l'est: Go up towards the centre of the island (east of Carène) and examine the great gate at the foot of Stoneheart
textes.Monter voir Bucatini, le gardien de la M: Go up to see Bucatini, the keeper of the Cooking Pot, at the very top of Mount Bolognese (by the spiral path, in the daytime)
textes.Monter voir le soleil ! Et toucher un nu: Go up and see the sun! And touch a cloud, to find out if it's wet. And bite an apple. And climb a tree. And come back down and tell Mum everything. In that order.
textes.Monter à la Terrasse du Ciel, en haut de: Go up to the Sky Terrace, at the top of the Axiom Tower
textes.Monter à la surface et raconter l'Atlant: To go up to the surface and tell the people up there about Atlantis, a different version every night. After a year, they'll know a thousand Atlantises. The real one will be in there somewhere.
textes.Montjoie ! Ses tavernes, ses tourtes, se: Montjoie! Its taverns, its pies, its taverns…
textes.Montjoie est si jolie d'ici. On rentre b: Montjoie looks so pretty from up here. Are we going back soon?
textes.Montjoie, la ville fortifiée sur la Butt: Montjoie, the fortified town on the Hill
textes.Montjoie, la ville sur la Butte: Montjoie, the city on the Butte
textes.Montre-la à Ilyria, elle en fera une bro: Show it to Ilyria, she'll make an embroidery from it.
textes.Montre-moi ta lame. Tiens-la en main, qu: Show me your blade. Hold it in your hand, so I can see how you hold it.
textes.Montrer la fresque du tombeau à Céleste: Show the tomb's fresco to Céleste Lunette, the astronomer of Cliquetis (at her observatory)
textes.Montrer le pot d'orange à Achille (au pi: Show the pot of orange to Achille (at the foot of the waterfall in the daytime, near the Palette in the evening), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de bleu à Basile (au bord: Show the pot of blue to Basile (by the pond in the daytime, on the Brush Oak terrace at noon), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de jaune à Lili (sur la p: Show the pot of yellow to Lili (on the beach in the daytime, at the swing in the evening), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de rouge à Capucine (aux: Show the pot of red to Capucine (in the White Meadows in the daytime, on the Blotter Oak terrace at noon and in the evening), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de vert à Rosalie (à la l: Show the pot of green to Rosalie (at the edge of the wood in the daytime, on the Eraser Oak terrace at noon), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de violet à Gaspard (au B: Show the pot of purple to Gaspard (at the Lookout in the daytime), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer les cinq champignons à Mère Mori: Show the five mushrooms to Mère Morille (at her caravan, in the middle of the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Montrer les trois sceaux à la Dame de Pr: Show the three seals to the Lady of the Prow, the Léviathan's figurehead (right at the front of the deck, near the telescope)
textes.Montrer les étoiles de mer à Kevin, au p: Show the starfish to Kevin, at the lifeguard post
textes.Montrez voir, milord… Ah ! Ça, c'est le: Let's have a look, milord… Ah! That there is a mermaid's thimble.
textes.Morgane, je l'ai fait sauter sur mes gen: Morgane, I bounced her on my knees, and now she frowns at me. An admiral without a fleet, with the heart of a whole fleet. I laugh at her title, never at her.
textes.Mousse, c'est déjà bien. Je sais sonner,: Cabin boy's already good. I can ring, scrub and tie knots. Mostly scrub. I'm the best scrubber on the whole island, ask anyone.
textes.Mousse, puis pêcheur, puis charpentier :: Cabin boy, then fisherman, then carpenter: I tried everything, and I was average at all of it. The evening my grandfather died, the tavern stayed silent. Gwenola's mother put a mug in my hand and said: “You tell it.” I told the shipwreck. I've never stopped.
textes.Mousse. Qu'est-ce que tu vois, à l'horiz: Cabin boy. What do you see on the horizon?
textes.Moustache attend que le monde écrive, mo: Moustache waits for the world to write, I read what it has written. A fisherman and a tracker, it's the same trade. I don't believe in his King. But I love his patience.
textes.Moustache dit qu'il a vu un poisson d'or: Moustache says he saw a golden fish in the great pool. Big as a rabbit. He calls it “the King of the Pools”. He's never caught it. Maybe he's never seen it.
textes.Moustache m'a appris un nœud de pêcheur,: Moustache taught me a fisherman's knot, with the string from his rod. A real one! It tightens all by itself when you pull. Now I tie it everywhere: on my hazelnut bags, on Mochi's ribbon, on Pomme-de-Pin's laces. Moustache says I learn too well. That's a compliment, right?
textes.Moustache, c'est le pêcheur du ponton. I: Moustache is the fisherman on the jetty. He says that under the big pond lives the Pond King, and that he grows every time you talk about him. So I talk about him all the time, to see!
textes.Mrrr ! Toi. Tu sens le poisson. C'est un: Mrrr! You. You smell of fish. That's a compliment.
textes.Mrrr. Aujourd'hui, j'élève Myrtille, gri: Mrrr. These days, I'm raising Myrtille, grey like her father, who climbs everywhere except by the stairs. I keep an eye on Dad, who catches more colds than kings. I spoil my little sister Éclair. And I don't speak to Trèfle, the baker, any more. Well, I say hello: our daughters make us. It's tiring, being cross. Almost as tiring as making up.
textes.Mrrr. J'ai grandi sur le ponton de mon p: Mrrr. I grew up on my father's jetty, among the rods and buckets. He'd say “watch the float”, so I'd watch the float, and doze off in the sun. As a kitten, I believed in the Pond King, even stronger than Dad did. I'd save sardines for him. At twelve, I stopped believing. And started eating them myself. You grow up.
textes.Mrrr. Le rhume aussi est là, papa. Rentr: Mrrr. So is your cold, Dad. Come home.
Mrrr. Myrtille, come down from there.
Mrrr. Your skewer. The biggest one.
textes.Mrrr. Tant mieux pour toi. Tu me raconte: Mrrr. Good for you. Then you'll tell me what it's like. Slowly. With details. And without the waves.
Mrrr. You've got your letter-day face on.
textes.Mrrrou ! Course jusqu'au premier planche: Mrrrou! Race you to the first platform?
textes.Mrrrou ! J'ai sept ans. J'habite à la pê: Mrrrow! I'm seven. I live at the fishery with Mummy Caramel and Grandpa Moustache. My papa is Ardoise. He fishes in the sea, at Tazira, on a blue boat, and he sends letters that smell of salt. I'm grey like him, look! Mummy says I've got his eyes. Grandpa says I've got his tail. I say it's MY tail.
textes.Mrrrou ! T'as vu le Roi des mares ? Non: Mrrrow! Have you seen the King of the Pools? No? I nearly did.
textes.Mrrrou ! Toi qui viens de la mer… tu sai: Mrrrow! You come from the sea… can you swim?
textes.Mrrrou ! Trop fort ! Alors si le Roi des: Mrrrow! So cool! So if the Pond King comes by, you're the one who dives. I'll watch. I watch super well.
textes.Mrrrou ! Tu sens bizarre. Pas mauvais. B: Mrrrow! You smell funny. Not bad. Funny. I'm Myrtille. My grandpa is Moustache. He's looking for the King of the Pools. So am I, but I look better.
textes.Mrrr… Bonjour. Caramel, poissonnière. Po: Mrrr… Hello. Caramel, fishmonger. Pool fish in the morning, grilled skewers in the afternoon. And no, I don't taste the goods. Not much.
textes.Mrrr… Toi qui viens de la mer : la mer,: Mrrr… You come from the sea: doesn't it scare you, the sea?
textes.Mrrr… Tout le monde croit que je suis re: Mrrr… Everyone thinks I stayed for Dad. Or for Myrtille. No, {surnom}. I'm scared of the sea. I've never seen it, and I'm scared of it anyway. All that blue, with no edge. I'm ashamed. So when I write back to Ardoise, I send fish recipes. Seven recipes per letter. He must think all I think about is food.
textes.My dear Edmond ! Avez-vous réfléchi ?: My dear Edmond! Have you thought it over?
textes.My dear Fernand ! Et ce dragon, il morda: My dear Fernand! And that dragon, did it bite?
textes.My dear friend ! Quelles merveilles aujo: My dear friend! What marvels have you got today?
textes.Myrtille grimpe presque aussi bien qu'un: Myrtille climbs almost as well as a squirrel! It's brilliant, and I tell her all the time. She gets cross. I don't get why. And she believes in a king with a crown. Total nonsense.
textes.Myrtille, c'est ma copine. Elle croit au: Myrtille's my friend. She believes in the Pond King, with a crown. It's almost true. Our mummies are cross with each other, but we don't care. I give her my sardines, yuck, and she eats my cake.
textes.Mère Averse, Mamie Tournesol vous envoie: Mother Downpour, Granny Sunflower sends you these sunflowers.
textes.Mère Brasille, la jardinière des Jardins: Mère Brasille, the gardener of the Ash Gardens, would like five ember flowers for her flowerbeds. They only grow on the slopes of the Great Blaze.
textes.Mère Gwenola est la seule personne de Ca: Mother Gwenola is the only person in Carène who still calls me by my first name. She makes me eat by force. If she were gone, Carène would go out along with her stove.
textes.Mère Gwenola s'était fait vendre par des: Mother Gwenola had been sold red sand by some caravan traders, passed off as chilli. I took the sack to Aïcha. She tasted it, spat it out, swore in three languages, and gave me a real sack of chilli, free, “for the honour of spices”. Gwenola put some in the soup. Fañch is still crying.
textes.Mère Gwenola, c'est la seule personne de: Mother Gwenola is the only person in Carène I'm scared of. She let me touch her stove, once. It's the greatest honour of my life as a smith.
textes.Mère Morille, la sage de la Cathédrale d: Mother Morille, the wise woman of the Spore Cathedral, wants to teach you about the five fairy mushrooms that grow in the old gasholder: the Spring-Bolete, the Moonling, the Chatterbox, the Rainbow and the Little-Giant. They must be picked and shown to her. These are storybook mushrooms: in real life, you never eat a mushroom you don't know.
textes.Mère Morille, quels sont ces champignons: Mère Morille, what are these glowing mushrooms?
textes.Mère Sauge m'apprendra le sort de soin s: Mère Sauge will teach me the healing spell if I bring her three mushrooms from the Twisted Wood. Then I'll have to heal the injured owl that lives near Agathe's caravan.
textes.Mère-Lune ? Ma plus vieille amie, et la: Mother Moon? My oldest friend, and the most beautiful thing that ever happened to Ramure. She's been falling asleep during my stories for seventy years. I take it as a compliment.
textes.Mère-Lune dit que la lune parle aux pist: Mère-Lune says the moon speaks to trackers. That it spoke to her, at the edge of the world. I've been listening to it since I was eight, {surnom}. Every night. It's never said anything to me. Not a word. I read tracks, but I can't hear the moon. One day, someone will have to come after Mère-Lune. I'm not sure it's me. Don't tell her.
textes.Mère-Lune est la seule encore là à avoir: Mother Moon is the only one still here who tasted my grandmother's cake. Every evening, I take her a slice and hold my breath. Every evening, she says “almost”.
