textes.Remplir un pot de sauce à la Louche Sacr: Fill a jar with sauce at the Sacred Ladle (at the edge of the Cooking Pot), then ask Captain Rigatoni for the Golden Grater (his Houseboat, east of the Parmesan Beach)
textes.Rencontrer Lyra, l'elfe, au cœur de l'îl: Meet Lyra the elf in the heart of Village Island
textes.Rendre l'appareil photo à Gérard: Give the camera back to Gérard
textes.Rendre la Flamme Éternelle au Cœur-Brasi: Return the Eternal Flame to the Ember Heart (in the middle of the nave of the Forge Cathedral)
textes.Rendre la guitare et l'ampli à Rouille (: Give the guitar and the amp back to Rouille (at the Cannery in the morning, on the square in the afternoon, at the Howling Hall in the evening)
textes.Rendre le cerf-volant à Théo: Give the kite back to Théo
textes.Rendre le cochonnet à Raymond: Give the boules jack back to Raymond
textes.Rendre sa lumière au Cœur de la Flèche: Restore the light of the Spire's Heart
textes.Rendre visite au Capitaine Rigatoni, dan: Visit Captain Rigatoni in his Houseboat
textes.Rendre à l'Île Crayonnée toutes ses coul: Give Sketched Island back all its colours
textes.Rentre ce soir, ou c'est moi qui descend: Come home tonight, or I'm coming down.
Come home tonight. I'll make soup.
textes.Reprendre le ciseau d'argent à ce requin: To get the silver chisel back from that shark. I don't wish it any harm. Well, a little. One teeny red-coral bite, for honour's sake.
textes.Repêcher le gros mérou. Pas pour le mang: Catch the big grouper again. Not to eat him, eh! So he repeats his answer in front of witnesses. I'll carry him to the tavern in a bucket, and Gwenola won't be able to say I dreamed it.
textes.Rester. Juste ça. Et un jour, perdre mon: To stay. Just that. And one day lose my return ticket by accident, and not even look for it.
textes.Retiens ton souffle ! Sans masque, tu ne: Hold your breath! Without a mask, you can only last a few seconds underwater. Come up for air (Space).
textes.Retourner voir Coyotl, le potier (à son: Go back to Coyotl, the potter (at his workshop, or at the market at noon)
textes.Retourner voir Grand-Mère Aquarelle: Go back to see Grand-Mère Aquarelle
textes.Retourner voir Grand-Mère Aquarelle (dev: Go back to see Grand-Mère Aquarelle (in front of the Palette in the daytime, on the Council terrace at noon and in the evening)
textes.Retourner voir Nova (à la Serre des Espè: Go back to see Nova (at the Greenhouse of Species, in the north-east, past the Academy)
textes.Retourner voir Petit-Pierre (sur le quai: Go back to see Petit-Pierre (on the quay, by the crates, in the morning; at the fishing jetty in the afternoon; on the square in the evening)
textes.Retourner voir Pixel pour la fin de la p: Go back to see Pixel for the end of the game
textes.Retourner voir Père Gaubert (aux Champs: Go back to see Père Gaubert (in the Southern Fields, in front of his farm; in the yard at noon)
textes.Retourner voir Rosalie (à la poissonneri: Go back to see Rosalie (at the fishmonger's, on the harbour, in the morning; on a café terrace or the promenade in the afternoon)
textes.Retourner voir Rouille (à la Conserverie: Go back to see Rouille (at the Cannery in the morning, on the square or the quays in the afternoon, at the Howling Hall in the evening)
textes.Retourner voir l'archimage, dans la cour: Go back to the archmage, in the courtyard of the Great Crystal
textes.Retourner voir la Doyenne Astrée (à la S: Go back to see Elder Astrée (at the Council Hall, at the foot of the Spire; on her bench in the Agora during the auroras)
textes.Retourner voir le Révérend Père Farfalle: Go back to see Reverend Father Farfalle
textes.Retourner voir le maire, devant la mairi: Go back to the mayor, in front of the town hall
textes.Retourner à la pointe dorée, descendre j: To go back to the golden point, dive down to the rooftops, and this time not come up too fast. Listen to the song right to the end. And maybe sing along.
textes.Retraité, voisin de villa de Raymond, ce: Retired, and Raymond's next-door neighbour, which is a punishment. Pétanque in the morning, pétanque in the afternoon, on pitch two. The day the jack rolled off towards the fountain, we played with a pebble, sulking. Bernard runs circles round us going hup hup. And Hortense is convinced I'm the one leaving lavender on her bench. It's not me!
textes.Retrouver Ba Sidi, le conteur de Tazira: Find Ba Sidi, the storyteller of Tazira (on Lantern Square), who has the logbook of the Léviathan
textes.Retrouver Comète (au Spatioport, ou l'ap: Find Comète (at the Spaceport, or in the afternoon at the Zero-Gravity Garden)
textes.Retrouver Germaine-la-Terrible, la guita: Find Germaine the Terrible, Clou's guitar (at the robots' lair, in front of the gate of the Grey Factory, in the south-east, behind the Spore Wood)
textes.Retrouver Mamie Barricade (à la Conserve: Find Mamie Barricade (at the Cannery, in the assembly room on the roof, or in front of the entrance in the afternoon)
textes.Retrouver Pixel et Quark, cachés quelque: Find Pixel and Quark, hiding somewhere in Astralys (in a street corner, behind a giant plant, on a floating bench… Quark hums when he hides)
textes.Retrouver Plume-de-Nuage (une petite méd: Find Plume-de-Nuage (a little pink sky jellyfish, over by the Zero-Gravity Garden, to the west) and gently lead her back to the Greenhouse of Species: she follows you if you stay close to her
textes.Retrouver Rhubarbe au vieux camp abandon: Find Rhubarbe at the old abandoned camp (to the north-west, along the camp path), and call him at the foot of his perch with the seeds (E)
textes.Retrouver Sardine, le chien au bandana r: Find Sardine, the dog with the red bandana (at the Scrapyard, in the south-east of the island, among the car wrecks: listen carefully, he barks at the robots)
textes.Retrouver Truffe dans les bosquets au bo: Find Truffe in the thickets at the edge of the Southern Fields and ring his little bell: he'll come
textes.Retrouver Zénith (à l'Observatoire, au t: Find Zénith (at the Observatory, at the telescope, at night)
textes.Retrouver l'ampli à lampes (à la Casse,: Find the tube amp (at the Scrapyard, in the south-east, among the scrap heaps, near the Scrap dragon)
textes.Retrouver la carte volée par le chat rou: Find the map stolen by the ginger cat: he climbs onto the roofs of Tazira using crates, near the houses on the quay, east of the square
textes.Retrouver la clochette de Truffe (tombée: Find Truffe's little bell (it fell in the grass near Clovis's windmill, in the Southern Fields)
textes.Retrouver la pelote de laine rouge tombé: Find the ball of red wool that fell out of Pauline's basket (in the Grand Hotel garden)
textes.Retrouver la puce holographique envolée: Find the hologram chip that flew off during the explosion in Professor Quasar's laboratory (at the Academy of Sciences, east of the Agora)
textes.Retrouver le cerf-volant de Théo sur les: Find Théo's kite on the hills, west of the town
textes.Retrouver le chapeau à plume du Baron (l: Find the Baron's plumed hat (the wind blew it south: look on top of Clovis's windmill, in the Southern Fields)
textes.Retrouver le cochonnet, près de la fonta: Find the boules jack, near the fountain on the square
textes.Retrouver le quatrième cœur de la potion: To find the fourth heart of Grandmother's potion. I taste a new root every spring. One day it'll be the right one.
textes.Retrouver les baguettes de batterie (au: Find the drumsticks (at the Dry Dock, the skatepark, in the north-east of the town, next to the harbour)
textes.Retrouver les huit autres pots de couleu: Find the eight other paint pots and pour them into the Palette: the families know where six of them fell (Basile at the pond, Rosalie in the wood, Capucine in the meadows, Lili on the beach, Gaspard at the Lookout, Achille at the waterfall); as for the turquoise and the pink, Grandpa Augustin has a little idea
textes.Retrouver les trois fromages affinés cac: Find the three aged cheeses Biscotte has hidden around Port-Coutelas (between the crates on the quay, under the fishing jetty, near the well): follow your nose
textes.Retrouver les trois pages de la partitio: Find the three pages of sheet music (the beach, the square, the quay to the east)
textes.Retrouver les trois éclats du Cœur de la: Find the three shards of the Spire's Heart (one near the Observatory, to the north; one in the Greenhouse of Species, to the north-east; one high up in the Zero-Gravity Garden, to the west): they beat softly and sing a single note
textes.Retrouver trois pages de grimoire envolé: Find three spellbook pages that blew away around Montjoie (they glow a little: on the Great Square, in the Upper Town, in the Lower Town…)
textes.Revenir chaque année à Port-Azur, chambr: To come back to Port-Azur every year, room seven, on the same day. And one day, with a child who'll ask why daddy always checks his finger. I'll say it's an old habit. He won't believe me, I hope.
textes.Revenir voir Agrafe (à l'imprimerie de l: Go back to see Agrafe (at the Spinning Mill print shop, or in the evening at the Expression Wall)
textes.Revenir voir Brindille (à la poste du po: Go back to Brindille (at the port post office)
textes.Revenir voir Honorine (à la boulangerie,: Go back to see Honorine (at the bakery, in the Middle Town)
textes.Revenir voir Ionie au Spatioport: Go back to see Ionie at the Spaceport
textes.Reviens avec ton petit ballon, Pied-Lour: Come back with your little balloon, Heavy-Foot! I only transform things that already fly.
textes.Reviens vite. Et garde ton masque bien s: Come back soon. And keep your mask on tight.
textes.Reviens voir les gens souvent : à force: Come back and see people often: the more you chat, the more they'll tell you things they tell no one else.
textes.Reviens à six heures, on verra pour le r: Come back at six, we'll see about the record.
textes.Rhubarbe ? Ha ! Il ne descend pour perso: Rhubarbe? Ha! He won't come down for anyone. Except for this. (He hands you a little pouch.) Sunflower seeds roasted with salt. Show them to him, and don't look him in the eye: he hates that. And if he calls you a jellyfish head, it means he likes you.
textes.Rhubarbe te regarde de haut, ébouriffé :: Rhubarbe looks down at you, ruffled: “Jellyfish head!” He won't come down for nothing… Perroquet-Joe surely has something to lure him.
textes.Rhubarbe, le perroquet rouge de la capit: Rhubarbe, the red parrot of Captain Anne-Rose Corbeau, has flown off towards the old abandoned camp in the north-west of the island. Perroquet-Joe will know how to lure him back.
textes.Rhum ambré, eau chaude, miel et citron,: Hot water, honey and lemon, served steaming in a pewter mug. Corentin swears it cures everything. Restores one and a half hearts.
textes.Rien ! Juste un ver de terre, qui te reg: Nothing! Just an earthworm, looking at you in surprise.
textes.Rien ! Rien du tout ! … Pourquoi tu sors: Nothing! Nothing at all! … Why are you getting your quill out?
textes.Rien ? Oh, my dear… Mais vous êtes libre: Nothing? Oh, my dear… But you're as free as a seagull! I envy you. A little. I'd offer you an object, but it would spoil everything.
textes.Rien du tout. Le pirate grogne dans son: Nothing at all. The pirate grumbles in his sleep.
textes.Rien en vue pour l'instant. Explorez, re: Nothing in sight for now. Explore, meet people!
Nothing here. The treasure must be nearby.
Nothing for you, Lucas… Oh wait, here.
textes.Rien qu'avec moi ? C'est un compliment o: Only with me? Is that a compliment or a threat? Both, I hope. I love both.
textes.Rien que des cailloux. Ronds, plats, gri: Nothing but pebbles. Round, flat, grey, a little less grey… That one looks like my aunt. That one too, actually.
textes.Rien sous la tête… mais tu as l'impressi: Nothing under the head… but you get the feeling it snickered when you leaned over.
textes.Rien sur la mer. Le Cœur-de-Pierre, roug: Nothing at sea. Stoneheart, red, like yesterday.
textes.Rien à signaler. Et ne me demande pas de: Nothing to report. And don't ask me for details.
textes.Rien, Majesté ! Absolument rien ! Comme: Nothing, Majesty! Absolutely nothing! As usual!
textes.Rien, Majesté ! Enfin… des graines. Un p: Nothing, Your Majesty! Well… seeds. A few. Lots.
textes.Rien. Absolument rien. C'est très reposa: Nothing. Absolutely nothing. It's very restful.
textes.Rien. C'est déjà beaucoup. En surface, i: Nothing. That's already a lot. Up top, there's never nothing. There's always someone talking.
textes.Rien. Cette tête-là regarde l'horizon, d: Nothing. This head looks at the horizon, straight ahead; not at the clouds.
textes.Rien. Ils sont de pierre, ils parlent av: Nothing. They're made of stone, they talk with their… rocks. Er. Their relations. Anyway.
Nothing. I'm not hungry in the morning.
textes.Rien. Juste l'écho de ta propre main sur: Nothing. Just the echo of your own hand on the stone. In the beginning, there was…
textes.Rien. Mais le Cœur-de-Pierre était rouge: Nothing. But Stoneheart was red tonight. Redder than yesterday.
textes.Rien. Sauf peut-être… une petite vanille: Nothing. Except perhaps… a small vanilla.
textes.Rien. Tu peux vérifier. Je sais que tu v: Nothing. You can check. I know you're going to check.
textes.Rien… à part une vieille chaussette de p: Nothing… except an old pirate sock. Yuck.
textes.Rita m'a annoncé, l'œil mystérieux, que: Rita announced, with a mysterious look, that Gérard would find his camera thanks to “someone who walks a lot”. It's pretty, I'll admit. But the day before, she was on the promenade when Gérard came down from the lookout, empty-handed and looking like a lost dog. I saw her watching him. Just saying. Or not saying.
textes.Rita m'a dit que l'horloge sonnerait de: Rita told me the clock would chime again thanks to a stranger. I don't believe that nonsense. But I'm watching you, all the same.
textes.Rita me prédit un grand amour tous les a: Rita foretells a great love for me every year. She's wrong every year. I pay every year. Don't try to understand.
textes.Rita prédit à Colette un grand amour tou: Every year Rita foretells a great love for Colette, at the same price. For me, she foretold a stranger who'd make my clock ring. I told her: “Nonsense.” She replied: “You'll see.” Since then, that's how we greet each other, from one door to the other. “Nonsense.” “You'll see.”
textes.Rita, la voyante, m'a prédit un grand am: Rita, the fortune-teller, predicted a great love for me. She predicts it every year. I still pay.
textes.Roadie d'honneur du Festival du Larsen: Honorary roadie of the Larsen Festival
Round and happy! Like my belly.
textes.Ronflements. Sur le canapé, quelqu'un do: Snoring. On the sofa, someone sleeps under three plaid blankets. A black cat sleeps on top of him. Nobody moves.
textes.Ronron. Le chat se roule sur le dos. C'e: Purr. The cat rolls onto its back. It's a trap, everybody knows that.
textes.Rosalie Gomme, la jardinière, croit que: Rosalie Gomme, the gardener, thinks the pot of green (no. 2) rolled all the way to the Hollow Stump, the oldest stump on the island, deep in the Hatching Wood. She doesn't dare go there: a big owl lives there, and it gives her funny looks.
Rosalie has some lovely sea bream this morning.
textes.Rosalie chante en vidant le poisson, tou: Rosalie sings while she guts the fish, every morning, at her stall. One day, she lost her voice. My bouillabaisse was… fine. Fine! Mine! I ran to bring her honey and lemon. The next day she was singing, and so was my soup. Don't ask me to explain. Cooking isn't a science.
textes.Rosalie divise par deux toutes mes taill: Rosalie halves the size of all my fish. She's right, the rascal. I owe her a big one, and she knows it.
textes.Rosalie est à la lisière du Bois des Hac: Rosalie is at the edge of the Hatching Wood, Grandpa Augustin near the Palette.
textes.Rosalie vend le meilleur poisson du port: Rosalie sells the best fish in the harbour and repeats everything she sees. The fish, I buy. The rest, I leave to her.
textes.Rosalie, Brioche vient avec moi !: Rosalie, Brioche is coming with me!
textes.Rosalie, c'est ma poissonnière, ma chant: Rosalie is my fishmonger, my singer, and the biggest sulker in Port-Azur. Her voice puts heart into my soup. Her day-old sea bream, a lot less.
textes.Rosalie, c'est à qui, ce chat roux sur l: Rosalie, whose is that ginger cat on the roof?
textes.Rosalie, la poissonnière. Poisson excell: Rosalie, the fishmonger. Excellent fish, regrettable tongue. She undermines authority every day, out loud, in front of the whole harbour.
textes.Rosalie, ma belle ! Ce soir, la bouillab: Rosalie, my beauty! Tonight, the bouillabaisse is in your honour!
textes.Rosalie, voilà le pot de vert ! Le hibou: Rosalie, here's the pot of green! The owl didn't say a thing.
textes.Rosalie, vous cherchez quelque chose dan: Rosalie, are you looking for something in the wood?
textes.Rose a mis ma rose dans un vase, « en at: Rose put my rose in a vase, “in the meantime”. I like a florist waiting with me. She believes in happy endings, like Léa.
textes.Rose est une gentille fille, qui vend sa: Rose is a sweet girl, who sells her lavender to everyone. Which is exactly what complicates my investigation.
textes.Rose est une vraie fleuriste. Elle parle: Rose is a real florist. She talks to her bougainvillea, and it doesn't listen to her. Mine doesn't either. We understood each other straight away.
textes.Rose, c'est mon amie, ma jardinière et m: Rose is my friend, my gardener and my best supplier. Without her lavender, my herbal teas would be nothing but hot water.
textes.Rose, ma voisine. Ses bougainvilliers on: Rose, my neighbour. Her bougainvillea has invaded my roof, my ukulele invades her nights. We're even. Well, she says we're not.
textes.Rou ? Rou. Rouuu. (C'est très profond, e: Coo? Coo. Cooo. (It's very deep, in pigeon.)
Red! Ah, the hardest one to paint. An adventurous red, afraid of nothing. For you, I'll have to outdo myself.
textes.Rouge, jaune, bleu et vert, avec une lon: Red, yellow, blue and green, with a long knotted tail. It belongs to little Théo.
textes.Rouille ? Alors c'est la maison qui offr: Rouille? Then it's on the house. (She sets a lemonade in front of you with a rat-shaped straw.) Sirène's lemonade, lemon, mint and bubbles. Nothing that goes to your head: just enough to dance until midnight. There's a concert in the evening. Come. And bring your ears, Larsen takes care of the rest.
textes.Rouille m'envoie te dire bonjour !: Rouille sent me to say hello!
textes.Rouille t'envoie ? Alors tu fais partie: Rouille sent you? Then you're part of the family! Here, have a taste. (He holds out his giant ladle, full of soup.) No, not the whole ladle. Just a sip. … There. Now you know the taste of Boucan. Come back whenever you like: here, you pay what you can. Even zero. Especially if you're hungry.
textes.Rouille, la chanteuse des Rats de Cale,: Rouille, the singer of the Bilge Rats, wants you to get to know Port-Boucan. To start with: say hello to Lentille at the Pay-What-You-Can Canteen, to Rustine at the bike workshop and to Sirène at the Howling Hall bar.
textes.Rouille, pourquoi tout le monde fait cet: Rouille, why the long faces everywhere?
textes.Rouille, tu peux me présenter un peu la: Rouille, could you show me around town a bit?
textes.Rouleau quatre cent douze, Coralin. On a: Scroll four hundred and twelve, Coralin. We're nearing the end.
textes.Roux ? Un grand dadais de renard qui cue: Roux? A great lump of a fox who picks herbs in his sleep, apparently. He's made me laugh since we were five. It's exhausting. It's irreplaceable. Don't repeat the second word to him.
textes.Roux ? Un renard qui vend contre des piè: Roux? A fox who sells for coins on MY market! An insult to tradition. But a rival worthy of me, my friend: foxes and tanukis, it's the oldest quarrel in the forest.
textes.Roux dit que mon étoile tombée était une: Roux says my fallen star was a firefly who'd had too much tea. It's not funny. He plays the flute like nobody else. That's true. I won't tell him.
textes.Roux est encore rentré avec des feuilles: Roux came home with leaves in his tail again. He says he was gathering. I say he was sleeping under a tree.
textes.Roux joue de la flûte pendant que je dan: Roux plays the flute while I dance. He's the only one who can make me laugh in the middle of a step, and the only one I ask for advice. He answers with a joke, then with good advice.
textes.Roux raconte à tout le village que mon é: Roux tells the whole village that my star that fell into the big pond was “a firefly who'd had too much moon tea”. The children laugh. Fireflies don't fall, Roux. They don't drink tea either. I wrote him a poem to explain. He set it to music. That's worse.
textes.Roux, c'est le renard qui m'a appris les: Roux is the fox who taught me the rhythms of Tazira. Boom, boom-boom! Without him, I'd still be going boom, boom, boom. Like Bourru, but faster.
textes.Royalement bien. La bière est fraîche, l: Royally well. The fizz is cold, the forges are burning, the golems… hmm. Almost well.
textes.Royaume des fées : chez une fée: Fairy kingdom: at a fairy's home
textes.Rrriiiii ! Le larsen siffle encore. Les: Eeeeeee! The feedback squeals again. The Rainville crows fly off, offended.
Rrrrrr… pffff… (He's asleep. Deeply. There's moss on his shoulder.)
textes.Rrrr… non, pas les cailloux… rrrr…: Rrrr… no, not the pebbles… rrrr…
textes.Rubis, pièces d'or… et j'achète tout ce: Rubies, gold coins… and I buy anything that sparkles. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Rustine n'a plus de pièces de vélo : les: Rustine has run out of bike parts: Lisse's robots searched the Scrapyard to build themselves arms. There are three batches of parts left, hidden in the Scrapyard, to the south-east.
textes.RÈGLEMENT DU DONJON\nDES MILLE MARCHES\n:
RULES OF THE DUNGEON
OF A THOUSAND STEPS

1. Do not feed the slimes (they grow).
2. Do not pet the frogs (they swallow).
3. A chest that smiles is not a chest.
4. The blue crystals bring you back up here. The falls do not.

— Odon, keeper and step counter
textes.Réclamer la dette à Gontran Lestrange, d: Claim the debt from Gontran Lestrange, known as Jambe-de-Bois (on the Veuve Écarlate by day; at the Shark's Tooth in the evening)
textes.Récolter deux rayons de miel aux ruches: Gather two honeycombs from the fire bees' hives, in the Ash Wood (south-east of the city)
textes.Réconcilier Mamie Tournesol et Mère Aver: Make peace between Granny Sunflower and Mother Downpour
textes.Réconcilier le Grand Spaghetti Volant av: Reconcile the Great Flying Spaghetti with its followers
textes.Récupérer l'antenne de Radio Boucan (tou: Get back the Radio Boucan antenna (at the very top of the painted water tower, east of the town)
textes.Récupérer l'appareil photo de Gérard au: Get Gérard's camera back from the lookout (at the top of the hill path)
textes.Réparer le Léviathan, le remettre à l'ea: Fix the Léviathan, put her back in the water, and set sail with everyone on board. Everyone! Fañch and his boat on the deck, Gwenola and her stove, and my grandad right at the top of the crow's nest, like before. I'll carry him, if I have to.
textes.Répondre aux trois questions du Sphinx (: Answer the Sphinx's three questions (on the plateau of Ra, across the river, south of Per-Hâpy)
textes.Réponse de fée ! Prudente, maligne, et q: A fairy's answer! Cautious, clever, and says nothing at all. I'll write it in my big book, with your name beside it.
textes.Répète-le plus fort, qu'on l'entende jus: Say it louder, so they can hear it all the way to Octave's kapok tree.
textes.Résoudre l'énigme des serpents: Solve the riddle of the snakes
textes.Réunir une dernière fois les trois conte: To bring together the three storytellers of the big island one last time, Ba Sidi, Corentin and me, at the Moon Circle. Now that the Zéphyr links the towns, no more excuses! A whole night of stories…
textes.Réussir le rose. Le rose du port, le soi: To get the pink right. The pink of the port in the evening, when the lighthouse comes on. Just once. After that, I could paint notaries for the rest of my life, no problem.
textes.Réveiller les esprits de la forêt et ouv: Wake the forest spirits and open the root gate
textes.Réveiller les trois runes de la Crypte a: Wake the three runes of the Rune Crypt with the light spell (key 5 then V; in VR, left trigger): the crypt is above the garden, on the path to the Twisted Wood
textes.Révérend ! Il danse ! Il m'a touché l'ép: Reverend! He's dancing! He touched my shoulder!
textes.Révérend, pourquoi le Grand Spaghetti a-: Reverend, why does the Great Spaghetti look so sad?
textes.Révérend, voici les pâtes, la sauce et l: Reverend, here are the pasta, the sauce and the Golden Grater.
textes.Rêveuse. La mer était couleur de saphir: Dreamy. The sea was sapphire-coloured this morning.
textes.Rúmil ! Tu es en retard. Mes lanternes o: Rúmil! You're late. My lanterns are hungry.
textes.Rúmil dit que la lumière vient mieux qua: Rúmil says light comes more easily when someone sings. So every morning at dawn, I sing for his nets. He never says thank you. He leaves me the first ray.
textes.Rúmil est né trois minutes avant moi, et: Rúmil was born three minutes before me, and he reminds me every morning. He fishes the light, I keep it. Without him, my lanterns would be empty. Without me, he'd be asleep.
textes.Rúmil pêche la lumière à l'aube, comme s: Rúmil fishes for light at dawn, like his grandfather, like I saw it done nine centuries ago. It's a dying trade. He doesn't let it die: he listens.
textes.Rúmil vient au cercle des contes avec se: Rúmil comes to the storytelling circle with his nets to mend. He never looks up, he never asks a question, and he remembers everything, word for word. One day I got a name wrong in a six-hundred-year-old story. He just coughed. I corrected myself.
S to go down, W to go back up.
textes.S'il y avait du nouveau, tu y mettrais u: If there were, you'd put a question mark on it.
textes.S'inscrire à la Guilde des Aventuriers: Sign up at the Adventurers' Guild
textes.SARDINE ! (Le chien saute sur Tornade, l: SARDINE! (The dog leaps at Tornade, licks his whole face, then comes back to sit at your feet. Tornade looks at him, then at you, and sniffs.) ... He doesn't want to leave you, does he. I can see that. He chose you. (He rubs his eyes with his fist.) All right. You can keep him with you. But take good care of him, okay! He likes chew bones, he bites robots, and sometimes he brings back coins. Nobody knows where he finds them. Here, his chew bones. And bring him back to the skatepark once in a while. Promise?
textes.SORTIE DU PERSONNEL — TOURNIQUET\nformul:
STAFF EXIT — TURNSTILE
stamped forms required
textes.SPLOOOSH ! Le Mont Bolognaise crache sa: SPLOOOSH! Mount Bolognese spits out its sauce! Big red drops fly very high… and fall all over its slopes.
textes.SPLOTCH ! Une grosse goutte de sauce t'e: SPLOTCH! A big drop of sauce landed right next to you… You're splattered from head to toe. (It smells delicious.)
textes.STOP ! Toi… toi quoi ? Toi pas carré. To: STOP! You… you what? You not square. You all SMOOTH! Not one single pixel! Ougha never see thing like you. Where you come from? From sky? From big water? From belly of volcano?
textes.Sa cabane du bord de plage s'est effondr: His beach hut collapsed during one of Mistral's big tracks. I heard about it from Clou, who came home covered in sand. I sent him a bag of twenty nails, by Clou. He got eleven. Clou takes his commission.
textes.Sa carapace arrête tout ! Un vent assez: Its shell stops everything! A strong enough wind might knock it over…
textes.Sa cuirasse d'or est trop dure. Ses yeux: Its golden armor is too hard. Its eyes, though, fear fire…
textes.Sa flûte a une note de plus que les autr: His flute has one note more than the others, from the eighth hole, which Gland made while he was teething. Roux calls it “the squirrel note”. That's the one I spin on, in the middle of the dance. One evening he played it too early on purpose: I spun into thin air. He laughed so hard he missed the next one.
textes.Sa grand-mère Salicorne, je l'ai bien co: I knew her grandmother Salicorne well. I wrote: “Day 1: a seaweed cracker, dreadful, eaten by all.” Marée came to scratch out the word “dreadful” herself. I sat on the scroll. An hour like that. In the end, I added “weeping with joy”. She accepted.
textes.Sa grand-mère, Nanwë, était la meilleure: Her grandmother, Nanwë, was the best herbalist I've ever known. When she fell asleep beneath the Mother Tree, Aëlwen opened the shop the very next day, her eyes red. I went and sat in a corner and talked nonsense all day. She didn't laugh. But she didn't close.
textes.Sa grenouille a sauté dans ma soupe. J'a: Her frog jumped into my soup. I stepped back. One step. Just one. Ever since, the whole village says I'm scared of frogs. I'm not scared of frogs. I'm scared of what Nimiel does with them.
textes.Sa lame s'est plantée dans les dalles !: His blade is stuck in the flagstones! Strike now!
textes.Sa peau est très épaisse… Quand il RUGIT: Its skin is very thick… When it ROARS, it's going to charge: dodge, and let it smash into the rock of the hollow!
textes.Sa première lame, il me l'a apportée fie: He brought me his first blade, proud as a rooster. I looked at it, weighed it, and put it back in the fire. Melted. Without a word. He didn't say anything either. The next day, he forged another, better one. That's how you learn. That's how my father taught me.
textes.Sa première semaine, je lui ai montré le: Her first week, I showed her hospital corners. You pull, you fold, you tuck: the sheet must sit like a letter in its envelope. She did it thirty times while telling me the life story of the guests in room nine. By the thirtieth bed, the corners were perfect. So was the life story of the guests in nine, incidentally.
textes.Sa première vigie tout seul. J'étais en: His first watch alone. I was down below. I hear: “Alarm! Alarm! Something white, very fast!” I climb back up. Eighty steps. It was Bondi, training. I said: “A fast rabbit is not an alarm.” He answered: “For a runner, it is.” … He's not wrong. Don't tell him.
Wise decision. He never gives anything back.
textes.Sage décision. La dernière fois, j'ai pe: Wise decision. Last time, I lost my eyebrows. They grew back, but upside down.
textes.Sage. Très sage. J'ai passé quatre cents: Wise. Very wise. I've spent four hundred years knowing, and I sleep worse than Hilda's goats.
textes.Sage. Très sage. Plus sage que nous deux: Wise. Very wise. Wiser than the two of us put together, which isn't hard.
textes.Salomé ! Combien tu l'as vendu, mon dern: Salomé! How much did you sell my last sabre for?
textes.Salomé m'a proposé de me vendre une clé: Salomé offered to sell me a key for the Gate of the Four Seals. A key! For a gate with seals! She already sold me an ancient map, once. I don't want to talk about it.
textes.Salomé m'achète mes perles. Elle me paie: Salomé buys my pearls. She pays me a third of what they're worth, and smiles at me like she's giving me a present. I don't like haggling. She knows it.
textes.Salomé revend mes sabres aux caravaniers: Salomé resells my sabres to the caravanners for twice what I charge her. I know it, she knows I know it. But she brings me ore cheaper than anyone. We're square, I reckon.
textes.Salomé récupère mes chutes de toile, en: Salomé collects my canvas offcuts, turns them into “authentic sailor's bags” and resells them for three times the price. She'd sell the wind if you could put it in a bag. She's tried.
textes.Salomé vend des « baumes du désert » qui: Salomé sells “desert balms” that cure everything. I tried one: goat fat and cinnamon. It doesn't cure anything, but it smells nice. And that, I don't like.
textes.Salomé vend n'importe quoi à n'importe q: Salomé sells anything to anyone. Yesterday she sold a leaky bucket to a seagull.
textes.Salomé, ton baume, c'est encore de la gr: Salomé, is your balm goat fat again?
Salomé. No. I'm not buying a key.
textes.Salomé. Tes sacs d'algues, ce soir, tu l: Salomé. Your seaweed sacks. Tonight, you put them away.
textes.Saluer Edmond, à la réception du Grand H: Greet Edmond at the Grand Hotel reception
textes.Saluer Lentille à la Cantine à prix libr: Say hello to Lentille at the Pay-What-You-Can Canteen (on the ground floor of the Cannery, the big brick factory covered in murals, west of the Howling Hall)
textes.Saluer Odette à la capitainerie, sur le: Greet Odette at the harbour master's office, on the quay
textes.Saluer Rustine à l'atelier vélo (à la Fi: Say hello to Rustine at the bike workshop (in the Spinning Mill, the long brick shed with saw-tooth roofs, south of the Pallet Square)
textes.Saluer Sirène au bar de la Halle Hurlant: Say hello to Sirène at the Howling Hall bar (the old forge hall with the great glass roof, north-east of the Pallet Square)
textes.Saluer Toni au Perroquet Bleu: Greet Toni at Le Perroquet Bleu
textes.Salut ! Attention, je danse en faisant d: Hi! Careful, I dance with big arm movements, I've already knocked over two glasses and a Bastien.
textes.Salut ! Grisou ! Le prochain champion de: Hi! Grisou! The next Great Race champion! This time, I'm beating Bondi. I can feel it. I can feel it in my paws. My paws can feel it too.
textes.Salut ! Kevin, maître-nageur. Interdit d: Hi! Kevin, lifeguard. No swimming past the red flag, no running on wet sand, and no being more muscly than me.
textes.Salut ! Moi c'est Nina, j'ai sept ans et: Hi! I'm Nina, I'm seven and a half. What about you? Are you an adventurer? Have you got a sword? Will you show me?
textes.Salut ! T'entends ce son ? Viens, viens,: Hi! Hear that beat? Come on, come on, let's dance!
textes.Salut ! Toi aussi tu veux des bras comme: Hi! Do you want arms like these too? Come on, ten push-ups with me!
textes.Salut ! Tu flottes, toi aussi ? Non ? Ah: Hi! Are you floating too? No? Ah, Heavyfoots… Well, shall I turn gravity back on, or would you rather everything floated?
textes.Salut ! Tu tombes à pic : notre chanteur: Hi! You're just in time: our singer lost his voice. Literally. He's looked for it everywhere. Want to replace him?
textes.Salut ! Tu veux un bâton lumineux ? Ah,: Hi! Want a glow stick? Oh, I'm all out… Well, dance with your hands, that works too.
textes.Salut salut ! T'as vu, j'ai des lunettes: Hey hey! See, I wear sunglasses at night. It's a look.
textes.Salut, Barnabé. Tu as bu de l'eau ?: Hi, Barnabé. Have you drunk some water?
textes.Salut, Grégoire ! Combien de bateaux, au: Hello, Grégoire! How many ships today?
textes.Salut, Perlée ! Belle matinée pour un to: Hi, Perlée! Lovely morning for a lap of the Tree!
textes.Salut, Pépin ! Tu cours où, comme ça ?: Hi, Pépin! Where are you running off to?
textes.Salut, l'ami ! Assieds-toi. Je cherche l: Hey, friend! Sit down. I'm looking for the rest of my song. It's about a sunflower that falls in love with the moon… but never sees her, because it sleeps at night. Want to sing the chorus with me?
textes.Salut, l'étranger ! Roux. Je cueille, je: Hi, stranger! Roux. I gather, I find, I sell: feathers, ropes, little forest trinkets. And in the evening, I play the flute for the moon. She likes it.
textes.Salut, le terrestre ! Tu marches ? Comme: Hi there, landlubber! You walk? How… slow. Welcome!
textes.Salut, membre du club ! Toujours rien di: Hi, club member! Still haven't told anyone? Me neither. We're holding strong.
textes.Salut, membre du club des jamais-gagnant: Hello, member of the Never-Won Club! The day you pass the tenth arch in the lead, I'll strike you off the club. Gladly.
textes.Salut, toi. Fañch. Pêcheur. Ma maison, c: Hi there. Fañch. Fisherman. My house is the upturned boat on the beach, over there. It was shipwrecked before me, so we get on well.
textes.Salut, tonton ! J'ai fini la vigie !: Hi, Uncle! I've finished my watch!
Hi, Éclair! Running? I'm running. Lovely day, huh?
textes.Salut. Cette caisse s'appelle… une caiss: Hi. This crate is called… a crate. I'm making an effort, see.
textes.Salut. Fais attention où tu marches : le: Hi. Watch where you step: the roof leaks. In three places. I have three buckets, there, by the door, but I can't be bothered to get up… Would you put them under the drips?
textes.Salut. Lucie, plongeuse. Je ramasse ce q: Hi. Lucie, diver. I gather whatever the sea is willing to give: pearls, coral, and bits of the Léviathan that have fallen off over two hundred years.
Hi. Shift over, this crate's heavy.
textes.Salut… Je hoche la tête depuis une heure: Hi… I've been nodding my head for an hour, I think it's gone automatic.
textes.Sans blague ? Peuchère, enfin quelqu'un: No kidding? Well I never, somebody at last! Five o'clock, at the jetty, bring a jumper. The mackerel will be pleased. So will I.
textes.Sans commentaire ! Et la plus belle dess: No comment! And the nicest one on top, for the forces of law and order!
textes.Sans hésiter… Tu as de la chance. Moi, j: Without hesitating… You're lucky. I've been hesitating for three years. Maybe you hesitate less once you've already left once.
textes.Sans ma baguette, je me sens toute… norm: Without my wand I feel so… ordinary. It's horrible.
textes.Sans tache ? Ma doue, laisse-moi cherche: No blemish? Ma doue, let me look…
textes.Sardine a déterré quelque chose… Une piè: Sardine dug something up… A coin! He drops it at your feet.
textes.Sardine aboie de toutes ses forces : un: Sardine barks with all his might: a robot! He charges to bite its iron ankles.
textes.Sardine déboule en dérapant et te lèche: Sardine skids in and licks your hand. Mission: follow you.
textes.Sardine fait trois fois le tour de toi e: Sardine circles you three times, wagging his whole behind. It's decided: he's yours, and you're his.
textes.Sardine pose une pièce un peu baveuse à: Sardine puts a slightly slobbery coin at your feet and waits for praise.
textes.Sardine rentre à la maison en trottinant: Sardine trots home. He looks back twice to make sure you haven't changed your mind.
textes.Sardine revient en trottinant, une pièce: Sardine trots back, a coin in his mouth, very pleased with himself.
textes.Sardine s'allonge contre ta jambe et pou: Sardine lies down against your leg and lets out a big, happy dog sigh.
textes.Sardine saute dans la barque et se poste: Sardine jumps into the boat and takes up position at the bow, nose in the wind, like a true sea dog.
textes.Sardine, le chien au bandana rouge: Sardine, the dog with the red bandana
textes.Sardine, le chien de Tornade, un bâtard: Sardine, Tornade's dog, a happy mutt with a red bandana, followed one of Lisse's robots and hasn't come back. Chaussette thinks he went towards the Scrapyard, to the south-east.
textes.Satisfait. L'affaire des croissants est: Satisfied. The croissant case is closed.
textes.Sauter (ou E) : danser le pogo avec la f: Jump (or E): mosh with the crowd!
textes.Se faire inscrire au registre par Éclipt: Get Écliptique to enter you in the register (at the Council Hall, at the foot of the Crystal Spire, in the centre of the island; at noon at the Nebula Café)
textes.Se promener dans le Bois des Hachures: Take a walk in the Hatching Wood
textes.Secret professionnel. Comme vos cartes à: Trade secret. Like your postcards, one penny cheaper than mine.
textes.Sept heures, la capitainerie. Midi, le C: Seven o'clock, the harbour office. Noon, the Café de la Place, the table overlooking the harbour: I count sailboats while I eat. Afternoon, the register, Lucas and his crates, Yannick and his customers who can't swim. Seven in the evening, I lock up. On Sunday evenings, I take soup up to the lighthouse. Anselme doesn't say thank you. He eats it all.
textes.Sept pièces, mon ami. Les ressorts, ça s: Seven coins, my friend. Springs wear out. So do coins, but more slowly.
textes.Sept rubis sur huit brillent, Majesté. E: Seven rubies out of eight are shining, Majesty. Er… eight out of eight.
textes.Sept, demain. J'ai trouvé un bleu de plu: Seven, tomorrow. I've found one more blue.
Seven, tomorrow. I've seen a new blue.
textes.Sereine. Danser, c'est comme nager : on: Serene. Dancing is like swimming: you let yourself be carried.
textes.Sereine. Personne ne s'est cassé la jamb: Serene. Nobody broke a leg today. Ewen is in detention.
textes.Sereine. Pour une fois, tout est en ordr: Serene. For once, everything is in order.
textes.Serré. Comme le maire. Une personne de g: Short and strong. Like the mayor. A person of taste. I'll make it right away, nice and black.
textes.Ses crocs sont plantés dans la pierre :: His fangs are stuck in the stone: his head is on the ground, STRIKE!
textes.Ses fers plus légers ? Non. Jamais. … Hm: Lighter shoes for him? No. Never. … Hm. I might have changed his sole nails, the other evening. Finer ones. He thinks it's the training. Let him think so. Don't tell him anything, you.
Her letters always arrive wet. I dry them in the sun before reading them, and I keep the water in a little bottle. I have a hundred and forty of them, lined up on my windowsill. Every time she writes “I haven't lost anything”, the letter is wetter than the others.
textes.Ses pinces sont coincées dans la roche !: His claws are stuck in the rock! Strike now!
textes.Ses quarante pièces ?! Elle les aura qua: Her forty coins?! She'll get them when the sea runs dry! … What? You insist? Listen to me well, landlubber: either you pay my debt yourself, or you take it from me fair and square, with fists. No one has ever put Gontran Lestrange on the mat. No one.
textes.Ses trois cents noisettes dans le Chêne-: His three hundred hazelnuts in the Mother Oak: I help him look for them in the evening, when I've finished my bridges. We never find any. There are always two hundred and ninety-nine left. But he's happy, so I am too. Maybe that's the secret: looking together.
textes.Seulement mes pattes, petite. Sous la co: Only my paws, little one. Under the blanket.
Only when I hear a harp.
textes.Seulement si tu joues la note de l'écure: Only if you play the squirrel note.
textes.Sextant, Ionie a besoin d'une carte stel: Sextant, Ionie needs a star chart.
textes.Sextant, avez-vous vu une méduse de ciel: Sextant, have you seen a sky jellyfish?
textes.Si ! Un nouveau ! Presque pas de grenoui: I do! A new one! Hardly any frogs this time!
textes.Si : dans ta tête. C'est un très joli po: You can: in your head. It's a very pretty jar.
textes.Si fait. Celle d'une amirale qui ne riai: Indeed I have. The one about an admiral who never laughed.
textes.Si j'entends le mot baignoire, tu récure: If I hear the word bathtub, you'll be scrubbing the deck with Ewen.
textes.Si je cligne des yeux lentement, ça veut: If I blink slowly, it means I love you. Don't get used to it.
textes.Si je descends, tu m'apprends l'arc ?: If I get down, will you teach me archery?
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Je me souvien: Do I remember you? I remember all my customers. Especially the ones who don't pay.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Mais bien sûr: Do I remember you? But of course! My memory is a seashell: everything echoes inside it.
textes.Si je pose le sac, marraine, je ne me re: If I put the sack down, godmother, I'll never get up again.
textes.Si je vous prends en photo un jour, dite: If I take your photo one day, tell me: are you more of a front view, or a profile?
textes.Si le flotteur frétille juste un peu, ne: If the float just wiggles a little, don't move. That's a fish having a taste. Wait until it dives for real.
If we dance till then, sure.
textes.Si quelqu'un a l'air triste, va lui parl: If someone looks sad, go and talk to them. It always helps. Them and you.
textes.Si ton sac est plein, va vendre ce que t: If your bag is full, go and sell what you don't need at a merchant's.
If you have fish, we can talk.
textes.Si tu as faim, les croissants de Port-Az: If you're hungry, Port-Azur's croissants are the best. I take the boat just for them.
textes.Si tu chantes moins lentement que la der: If you sing less slowly than last time!
textes.Si tu coupes un arbre, plantes-en un aut: If you cut down a tree, plant another one. That's all we ask, we elves.
textes.Si tu devais rester quelque part pour to: If you had to stay somewhere forever, where would you choose?
textes.Si tu entends couiner dans ton oreille,: If you hear squeaking in your ear, that's me saying hello.
textes.Si tu grimpes les pitons, repose-toi sur: If you climb the rock spires, rest on the ledges. Even goats take breaks, and they don't have arms.
If you let me win, yes.
If you leave me the first ray.
textes.Si tu me regardes, je saute jusqu'à la l: If you're watching, I'll jump all the way to the moon!
textes.Si tu pouvais partir demain matin, n'imp: If you could leave tomorrow morning, for anywhere, without telling anyone… would you go?
If you promise not to drink the bay.
textes.Si tu restes sur l'estrade jusqu'au bout: If you stay on the stage till the end, this time.
If you want to make me happy, think of %s. But you didn't hear it from me.
textes.Si tu {le} croises, dis-lui bonjour de m: If you run into {le}, say hello from me.
textes.Si vous {le} croisez, dites-lui bonjour: If you run into {le}, say hello from me.
You are. The funniest one, in fact.
Sign here. And here. And there. Thank you.
textes.Signez ici. Non : lisez d'abord. TOUJOUR: Sign here. No: read first. ALWAYS read first. (You read.) “The undersigned promises to put books back in their place, not to dog-ear the pages, and to return good humor on the way out.” … You read to the very end. You're the first. Trial of the contract: passed.
textes.Signorina Ravioli m'a appris à chanter p: Signorina Ravioli taught me to sing to the tomatoes. They prefer nursery rhymes.
textes.Sigrun ! Ta bière a fait chanter la terr: Sigrun! Your fizz got the terrace singing last night.
Sigrun! A golden fizz. Same as yesterday.
textes.Sigrun ? Connais pas. … Bon. Une ancienn: Sigrun? Never heard of her. … Fine. A former apprentice. Forty years in my cellar, then off to make fizz at Dagna's. Her fizz is golden. Too golden. I've never tasted it.
textes.Sigrun brasse dans mon ancien four une b: In my old oven, Sigrun brews a golden barley fizz that smells of warm bread. The whole terrace drinks it. She deserves for the world to know. And for Ulfa to say so.
textes.Sigrun brasse la meilleure blonde de la: Sigrun makes the best golden fizz on the terrace, and she has a laugh that makes the barrels shake. I buy a mug from her every evening. Normally, I don't drink that much.
textes.Sire Orage est tombé, et sur la montagne: Lord Storm has fallen, and on the mountain the golems froze all at once, like statues. My people can finally sleep. You are a giant among giants, big one.
textes.Sire Orage lève son épée vers le ciel :: Sire Orage raises his sword to the sky: THE STORM BREAKS LOOSE! He'll charge in a gust: when he steps back glowing, move out of his path.
textes.Sire Orage pose un genou à terre… et se: Lord Storm drops to one knee… and dissolves into the wind. The storm calms, the sun returns to the Tower. Far away, on Fire Mountain, the golems fall still. A golden chest appears among the runes.
textes.Sire Orage, le Chevalier des Tempêtes: Lord Storm, the Knight of Storms
textes.Sire Tancrède de Tournevent raconte des: Sir Tancrède de Tournevent tells tales of magnificent feats. All imaginary. He'd finally like to live a real one, with a witness: defeat the goblin chief of the Goblin Wood and bring back his banner.
textes.Sire Tancrède, racontez-moi votre plus g: Sir Tancrède, tell me about your greatest exploit.
textes.Sire Tancrède, votre cape traîne encore: Sire Tancrède, your cloak is dragging in the mud again…
textes.Six bâtons, et droits en plus. Tiens, do: Six sticks, and straight ones too. Here, twelve coins. And your next shovel will cost you less: you're almost family.
Six hundred metres: the Glider has reached its ceiling. Above that is the realm of the stars.
textes.Six heures ! Je serai là à six heures !: Six! I'll be here at six!
textes.Six heures : les barques rentrent, le ph: Six o'clock: the boats come in, the lighthouse turns pink, and I unpack the ice. The grouper, sold before nine. In the afternoon, a coffee and a bench. In the evening, I have dinner at Paulo's, so he can see I'm cross. And between customers, I keep watch. The sergeant who stops at the ice-cream stand. Inès and her two Friday sea bream. Nothing gets past me.
textes.Six heures, je t'avais dit. Tu n'es pas: Six o'clock, I told you. You didn't come. The bowline's still waiting for you. So am I.
textes.Six pièces l'éclat de cristal. Dernière: Six coins a crystal shard. Final offer.
textes.Six pièces le hamac, couverture comprise: Six coins for the hammock, blanket included. My aunt doesn't give credit, and neither do I. Well… she doesn't let me.
textes.Six pièces, mon chou. Même les sorciers: Six coins, dearie. Even wizards pay for their bed. Especially wizards: they set the sheets on fire.
textes.Six sardines de l'aube grillées sur la b: Six dawn sardines grilled over the embers, with cumin and lemon, on the Tazira quay. Restores two hearts.
textes.Six, milord. Les plus dorés. Les mouette: Six, milord. The goldenest. The seagulls are waiting for you.
Six, my dear! The most golden, please.
textes.Sofia ! Tu m'as rapporté quoi, aujourd'h: Sofia! What did you bring me today?
textes.Sofia descend là où je ne peux pas aller: Sofia dives where I can't go and comes back up with the most beautiful shells on the island. My best necklaces are all thanks to her. And she never wants to be paid.
textes.Sofia m'a fredonné un chant de baleine q: Sofia hummed me a whale song she'd heard while diving. It went up, it went down, it went round in circles. I spent three nights recreating it on the decks. She listened to the end and said “almost”. Ever since, I've been looking for the rest of the “almost”. Tchoum tells everyone it's going to be huge.
textes.Sofia m'a rapporté un coquillage nacré g: Sofia brought me a pearly shell as big as my hand, found really deep down. I made the most beautiful necklace of my life with it. A very fancy gentleman from Port-Azur bought it for six coins. I gave the six coins to Sofia. She threw them into the sea, laughing, “for the fish”. I yelled her name for quite a while.
textes.Sofia m'apprend à plonger. Elle est calm: Sofia is teaching me to dive. She's calm like morning water, and she says dancing is like swimming. I tried the opposite: swimming the way I dance. It splashes.
textes.Sofia plonge, je rame. Elle a peur des p: Sofia dives, I row. She's been scared of the deep since the golden point, but she dives back in anyway. She's the bravest of us all. Even if she turns down five o'clock fishing.
textes.Sofia, c'est mon billet pour l'Atlantide: Sofia is my ticket to Atlantis. Well, the day she dares. She's heard the whales sing, and you can hear it in the way she dances.
textes.Sofia, demain matin, on regarde le lever: Sofia, tomorrow morning, shall we watch the sunrise from the water?
textes.Soigner ? Oh, mon petit, c'est la plus b: Healing? Oh, my dear, it's the most beautiful of all magic. But first you must learn to know what heals. Go and pick me three mushrooms in the Twisted Wood: the brown ones with white stalks, not the others. The others make you sing off-key.
textes.Soigner la chouette blessée du Bois Tors: Heal the injured owl in the Twisted Wood with the healing spell (key 0 then V, right next to her; in VR, left trigger)
textes.Sois franc, {surnom}. Ma dernière sculpt: Be honest, {surnom}. My latest sculpture, there: is it a fish or a sea urchin?
textes.Soixante ans de pêche. J'ai attrapé une: Sixty years of fishing. Once I caught a grouper so big it took two boats. I let it go: it looked older than me.
textes.Soixante ans de pêche. J'ai sorti un mér: Sixty years of fishing. I once landed a forty-kilo grouper. Well, thirty. Let's say twenty-five.
textes.Soixante, mon héros ! Et tu chantais en: Sixty, my hero! And you were singing at the same time.
textes.Son billet retour, jamais poinçonné, est: Her return ticket, never punched, is tucked into the frame of my compass, at the helm. It's gone yellow, the corner's dog-eared. Sometimes Lola comes aboard to give me a letter for her mother, she sees the ticket and says: “Keep it a while longer.” So I keep it. It's the only ticket in my life I've never wanted to punch.
textes.Son blindage arrête tout ! Attends qu'el: Its armor stops everything! Wait until it plants its bucket in the ground: its hoses will be exposed.
textes.Son dos est dur comme la pierre ! Frappe: Its back is hard as stone! Hit the head… or wait until it catches its breath after its tail swing.
textes.Son examen de pisteuse, à dix ans : retr: Her tracker's exam, at ten: find a mooncake hidden in the forest by Mère-Lune. Heh heh… I didn't know it was an exam! I was just following the smell, that's all. When Brume got there, half of it was missing, and my tracks were everywhere. She passed her exam. I got a tummy ache.
textes.Son fameux mérou de quarante kilos, Fern: His famous forty-kilo grouper — Fernand tells me about it every other morning. Each time, it's gained two kilos. I told him: “Odette weighed it, Fernand. Twenty-five.” He answered: “It lost weight from the emotion.” Since then, I divide everything of his by two. He pretends to be offended. It's our way of saying good morning.
textes.Son fromage des cendres est vivant. Je n: Her ash cheese is alive. I'm not joking: one morning, I left one on the table, and by evening it was at the other end. Hilda said: “It was cold.” So I put it in the stew, nice and warm. Nobody said a word. Bramm had seconds.
textes.Son grand-père marchait dans mon clan, l: His grandfather walked in my clan, the day we arrived. He had the same furrow between his eyes. Today Croc-Gris watches the forest from way up high, and I watch him. I don't tell him everything I see. He doesn't tell me everything he no longer sees.
textes.Son gâteau de lune est délicieux. Mais i: Her mooncake is delicious. But it's missing a herb: my nose is sure of it. Which one? I don't know. I suggested mint, sage, meadowsweet: she chased me out with her bread peel. My mushrooms have always been banned in her shop; now my herbs are too. I keep looking anyway. Outside.
textes.Son premier pont, c'était deux brindille: His first bridge was two twigs across a puddle, with a hazelnut in the middle. He showed it to me as if it were the west bridge. I blew on it, it danced. I told him it was a real bridge. It was true! He was so proud. Then he ate the hazelnut, and the bridge collapsed. He said it was for the winter.
textes.Son premier tableau, je l'ai accroché mo: Her first painting, I hung myself in the lobby, at eleven at night, once the last guest had gone up. A spirit level, a tape measure, a pencil. To the millimetre. I did it three times: the bubble was not satisfied. The next day, Mademoiselle Clémence stopped in front of it without a word. Then she ran upstairs.
textes.Son trident, je l'ai taillé la nuit des: I carved his trident on the night of the sharks, in one hour, from the first red coral that came to hand. I told him: “Careful, it bites.” He's held it for three hundred years without letting go. His calluses are like shells. He says it comes with the job.
textes.Sors de l'eau d'abord !: Get out of the water first!
textes.Sortir de Tazira par la porte du nord, s: Leave Tazira by the north gate, follow the three caravan markers to the north-east (they light up at night), open the tomb of the Walking Dune (the star, the dune, the sun) and take the Seal of Sands
To land a real forty-kilo grouper. A real one, weighed in front of Odette, no thumb on the scales. Forty. Not thirty-nine.
textes.Soucieuse ? Je grelotte, voilà ce que je: Worried? I'm shivering, that's what I am. Me! An archduchess of the underworld! The Ember Heart is dying out, little flame: it's no more than a blue glimmer, and the city is cooling. The cold rises from the Nine Circles, beneath the Forge Cathedral. The Frost Titan has awakened at the bottom of Cocytus, and he has taken the Eternal Flame. Brother Cinder keeps the key to the door. Go down, circle after circle… and bring us back our fire.
textes.Souffler une bulle de nacre assez grande: To blow a mother-of-pearl bubble big enough for Coralin to step inside. So he'd see it's solid. And say “not bad”. Just “not bad”. That would already be huge.
textes.Soulagée. Mes croissants restent dans le: Relieved. My croissants stay in their basket now.
textes.Sous cette salle, il y a la Forge Royale: Beneath this hall lies the Royal Forge, fed by the volcano's lava. Further down still… nobody goes.
textes.Sous l'eau, tu apprendras. La mer est pa: Underwater, you'll learn. The sea is patient.
textes.Sous l'eau, tu ne pourrais pas. C'est là: Underwater, you couldn't. That's where I like you best.
textes.Sous l'œil de Khépri, dans un coffret :: Beneath the eye of Khepri, in a small casket: a piece of Osiris!
textes.Sous la Lueur de lune, des lettres d'arg: Under the Moonglow, silver letters appear above the door: four moons, in order. Full, waning, new, waxing.
textes.Sous la Lueur de lune, un des beaux pont: Under the Moonglow, one of the beautiful slate bridges… fades away: it was only an illusion! And other bridges, made of light, appear where there was nothing.
textes.Sous la Poste, il y a un de ses ponts, a: Under the Post Office, there's one of her bridges, with singing-stones. When the east wind gets up, it sings, and it's nearly always the day the Zéphyr arrives with the post. I say the bridge announces the letters. Pomme-de-Pin says it's the wind. She doesn't argue too much. She's kind.
textes.Sous la Poste, à la cime, il y a un de m: Under the Post Office, at the treetop, there's one of my bridges, with singing-stones. When the east wind gets up, it sings, and it's often the day the Zéphyr brings the post. Plumette says it's the bridge announcing the letters. I say it's the wind. But I don't argue too much. It's prettier the way she tells it.
textes.Sous la grande mare, il y a un dragon !: Under the big pond there's a dragon! A real one! Mochi says it's a fish-dragon, but that's just silly.
textes.Sous la place, les racines de l'Arbre-Mè: Under the square, the Mother Tree's roots reach all the way down to the sea. Sometimes, at night, the fountain water sings.
textes.Sous la quille du Léviathan, il y a des: Under the Léviathan's keel there are carved signs. Not by castaways: it's too old, and it's cut into the stone, under the sand. The ship ran aground on something.
textes.Sous la tête, de la terre, une fourmi, e: Under the head, some earth, an ant, and the ant looks at you as if to say: “This is my home, you know.”
Beneath the Great Temple of Aztlán.
textes.Sous le Temple de Kukulkan s'ouvre le ch: Beneath the Temple of Kukulkan lies the road to Xibalba, the kingdom of the Lords of Death. Ix Kanul, the high priestess, would like someone to go down there like the Twins of the Popol Vuh, and bring back the Jade Mask of the kings of Yaxché.
textes.Sous le banc ! Marcel, il était sous le: Under the bench! Marcel, it was under the bench! … Thanks, kid. Here, a few coins. And whenever you like, we'll teach you how to play.
textes.Sous le beaupré, la Dame de Proue : une: Beneath the bowsprit, the Figurehead Lady: a woman of carved wood, leaning over the waves, her hands clasped over a closed shell. The blue paint of her dress is flaking. She has been watching the sea for two hundred years.
textes.Sous le capot d'une vieille voiture : de: Under the hood of an old car: some coins and two shiny springs. Ferraille had hidden them for a rainy day.
textes.Sous le coussin, tu trouves quelques piè: Under the cushion, you find a few coins, a broken drumstick and a note: “If you're reading this, don't wake me.” You leave the drumstick and the note, but he won't say a word about the coins.
textes.Sous le lit : trois moutons de poussière: Under the bed: three dust bunnies and a marble. Nobody.
textes.Sous nos pieds, la montagne est creuse c: Beneath our feet, the mountain is full of holes like a cheese. Tunnels, shafts, halls. And right at the bottom, the lava.
textes.Souvent ! Oh, vous me faites plaisir ! U: Often! Oh, that makes me happy! A letter is someone thinking of you long enough to find a stamp. Come and post them with me, I'll pick you the prettiest ones.
textes.Splendid ! Auriez-vous aussi des écaille: Splendid! Might you also have some mermaid scales?
textes.Splendid ! Je la prends. Et celle d'à cô: Splendid! I'll take it. And the one next to it, out of politeness.
Splendid! Let me listen to it.
textes.Splendid, comme toujours ! Hier j'ai acq: Splendid, as always! Yesterday I acquired a sea dragon's tooth. The fisherman gave me a jolly good price.
textes.Splendid. Je repasserai demain. Elle aus: Splendid. I'll come back tomorrow. So will it, I suppose.
textes.Splortch ! Te revoilà dehors, gluant de: Splortch! There you are, outside again, gooey from head to toe. The frog has the hiccups.
textes.Splotch ! Tu t'enfonces dans la boue du: Splotch! You sink into the mud of the Styx… and climb out, sticky, onto the bank. The bubbling slabs won't hold you!
textes.Stick droit : choisir Gâchette : répon: Right stick: choose   Trigger: answer   B: leave
textes.Stick droit : choisir Gâchette : utili: Right stick: select   Trigger: use   Grip: drop   Y: close
textes.Stick gauche : virer, monter, descendre: Left stick: turn, climb, descend; right trigger: faster, left: brake; A: land.
Left stick: turn, climb, descend; triggers: speed; A: land.
textes.Stick gauche pour virer et piquer, A pou: Left stick to turn and dive, A to land.
textes.Suis le rayon du regard : là où il touch: Follow the beam with your eyes: where it hits the wall, that's where it got lost!
textes.Suivre une trace jusqu'au bout. Une seul: Follow one trail to the very end. Just one. The round footprints at the big pond, all the way to whatever made them. Even if it's underwater.
textes.Super ! J'ai deux cents graines à trier: Great! I've got two hundred seeds to sort tonight!
textes.Super ! J'ai mangé un gâteau de lune. Ch: Great! I ate a mooncake. Shh.
textes.Super ! J'ai sonné la cloche trois fois: Great! I rang the bell three times this morning. Twice on purpose.
textes.Super ! J'ai vu un dauphin ce matin. Enf: Great! I saw a dolphin this morning. Well, maybe a big fish. But I'm saying dolphin.
textes.Super ! Ça fera un joli bruit sous le po: Great! They'll make a lovely sound under the south bridge!
textes.Super bien ! J'ai grimpé jusqu'à la troi: Super good! I climbed up to the third walkway with no hands! … Don't tell Aëlwen.
textes.Super bien ! J'ai vu une tortue par la f: Super good! I saw a turtle through the dome window!
textes.Super content ! Mon cerf-volant vole plu: Super happy! My kite flies higher than the lighthouse!
textes.Sur cette fresque, regarde : la cité sou: Look at this fresco: the city under its dome, the whale, and the three pearls. The whole story in one picture. It took me ten thousand scrolls.
textes.Sur l'autel de Serket, dans un coffret :: On the altar of Serket, in a small casket: a piece of Osiris, green as wheat growing back.
textes.Sur l'autel du Soleil des Jaguars : une: On the altar of the Sun of the Jaguars: a tablet engraved with a jaguar's head and four dots. The first sun, the one the jaguars devoured.
textes.Sur l'autel, sous la pluie de feu : la t: On the altar, beneath the rain of fire: the tablet of the Sun of the Rain of Fire, still warm.
textes.Sur l'île céleste vit Ventaile, un grand: On the sky island lives Ventaile, a great big bird. The only one who flies almost as fast as me. One day, I challenged him: three laps of the island. I lost by a feather. Just one! I kept that feather. I've got others now: I go for a rematch every year. And every year I lose. By a feather.
textes.Sur la Belle-Étoile, la nuit, Jules me m: On the Fair Star, at night, Jules would show me the stars. “That one's the Evening Star. Hortense's eyes are that colour.” And that one? “Hortense laughs like that, twinkling.” Every star in the sky, he'd sorted by Hortense. Even today, when I sail at night, that's how I recognise them.
textes.Sur la Mouette, Barnabé mesurait tout :: On the Seagull, Barnabé measured everything: the mast, the cook's soup, my beard. Eleven inches. He wrote it on his map, off a little islet: “Octave's beard, eleven inches”. The only accurate thing on that map. Just saying.
textes.Sur la Mouette, pendant trois jours de c: On the Seagull, during three days of dead calm, Octave carved me a walking stick from a bamboo cane. He engraved a little seagull on the handle, and my initials. Backwards: “C. B.”. I never pointed it out to him. It's my favourite walking stick.
textes.Sur la corniche, au sec : la tablette du: On the ledge, out of the wet: the tablet of the Sun of Water, engraved with waves. The sun of the great flood.
textes.Sur la plage noire, il y a des crabes de: On the black beach there are lava crabs. They're nice. Just a bit hot.
textes.Sur la porte, un écriteau : « NE PAS DÉR: On the door, a sign: “DO NOT DISTURB. (Since 1226.)”
textes.Sur la stèle, un soleil gravé et ces mot: On the stele, an engraved sun and these words: “I rise in the east, I burn in the south, I set in the west, and I sleep in the north. Relight my course, and the door will open.”
On the bowl, a label: “Fernand. Do not feed (he lies).”
textes.Sur le toit de Borin. Elle mange sa chem: On Borin's roof. She's eating his chimney.
textes.Sur les collines, il y a du thym, du rom: On the hills there's thyme, rosemary, lavender… and in the rocks of the point, a little yellow flower that heals burns. Don't pick it, it's rare.
textes.Sur les tables ! Comme le roi après la f: On the tables! Like the king after the Forge Festival! The big table still wobbles. You'll dance on the little one, it's sturdier.
textes.Sur ma carte des Anciens, à l'est, entre: On my Ancients' map, to the east, between the village and here, there's a patch of mist and a golden eye. I thought it was spilled coffee.
textes.Sur ma carte, j'ai barré le mot « NON »: On my map, I crossed out the word “NO” written three times and put your name there instead. Very small. There wasn't much room.
textes.Sur ma carte, la glace coco s'appelle la: On my menu, the coconut ice cream is called the “Bruno-Loco”. That way, everyone knows where it comes from. Bruno says it's free advertising. I say it's gratitude. The tourists ask whether a bruno is a jungle fruit.
textes.Sur ma flûte, il y a la note de l'écureu: On my flute there's the squirrel note, the one from the eighth hole. Lilas spins on it, in the middle of the dance. One evening, I played it too early on purpose, to see. She spun on nothing, shot me a dark look… and laughed in the middle of the step. The only laugh in the whole history of the moon dance. I'm proud of it.
textes.Sur quoi ? Je suis sourd, moi. C'est l'e: About what? I'm deaf, me. It's the anvil.
textes.Sur ton obsidienne, j'ai gravé les runes: On your obsidian, I carved the city's warding runes.
textes.Sur une ardoise : « Défense de goûter. S: On a slate: “No tasting. Except you, traveler. Just one. — The cheesemaker upstairs”
On a canvas. Just a canvas.
textes.Surtout, ne pleure pas au-dessus de la m: Whatever you do, don't cry over the pot!
textes.Survolté ! J'ai bu le jus de quatre noix: Supercharged! I drank the juice of four coconuts. I can see sounds. They're green.
textes.Sylvie dit que je photographie plus que: Sylvie says I take more pictures than I look. She's right. But photos, at least, don't go away.
textes.Sylvie jure qu'elle ne croit pas aux car: Sylvie swears she doesn't believe in the cards. And yet she's come back three times, always “just passing by”. Last time, I announced: “If you would come tomorrow, you would have a surprise.” She corrected me at once: “If you came, Madame Rita. No ‘would’ after ‘if’.” I let her. Even destiny needs a schoolteacher.
textes.Sylvie, c'est ma femme, la maman de Théo: Sylvie is my wife, Théo's mum, and the person who's always right. She says I photograph more than I look. It's exhausting, someone who's always right.
textes.Sylvie, la femme du photographe. Une ins: Sylvie, the photographer's wife. A schoolteacher: she believes in nothing, she corrects everything, and she still comes back to sit at my table. Sceptics make the best clients.
textes.Sylwen ! J'ai un nouveau couplet sur ta: Sylwen! I have a new verse about your brioche.
textes.Sylwen ! Le miel du jour. Tilleul et trè: Sylwen! Today's honey. Lime and clover.
textes.Sylwen ! Ton four a l'air de bonne humeu: Sylwen! Your oven seems in a good mood.
textes.Sylwen ! Ton pain de miel a traversé la: Sylwen! Your honey loaf crossed the mist, you know.
textes.Sylwen ! Ça sent le pain au miel jusqu'à: Sylwen! You can smell the honey bread all the way to the fountain!
textes.Sylwen a goûté ma chanson sur le pain. E: Sylwen heard my song about bread. She said “nice”. Coming from her, that's a triumph.
textes.Sylwen a raté son pain ce matin. Elle di: Sylwen ruined her bread this morning. She says it's the oven. It's always the oven.
textes.Sylwen dit bonjour à mes abeilles, maint: Sylwen says hello to my bees now. From a distance, but she says it. They like her. Her bread tastes of their work: that's the finest thank-you there is.
textes.Sylwen est le meilleur public du Bois-Do: Sylwen is the best audience in the Bois-Doré. She listens while kneading, she laughs at the right moment, and when she says “pretty”, it's a triumph. Her bread, now, that's a song.
textes.Sylwen fait le meilleur pain du monde, e: Sylwen makes the best bread in the world, and she never tells Mummy anything. Well, hardly ever. She forgave me for the door and the frog. I love her loads.
textes.Sylwen jure que je me suis endormie au d: Sylwen swears I fell asleep at the twelfth verse of the song he sang me last summer. I wasn't asleep. I'd closed my eyes to listen better. But if I admit it, he'll write forty more.
textes.Sylwen me garde la croûte du premier pai: Sylwen saves me the crust of the first loaf of every batch. In exchange, I tell her oven a story while it bakes: according to her, it rises better when you talk to it. It's already heard two thousand of my stories. It's my warmest listener.
textes.Sylwen me laisse façonner un petit pain,: Sylwen lets me shape a little bread roll on Saturdays. Mine always comes out a funny shape. Once it looked like Button. Sylwen baked it anyway and put it on the stall with a label: “Frog-bread, not for sale.” Everyone came to see it!
textes.Sylwen nourrit le Bois-Doré depuis deux: Sylwen has been feeding the Bois-Doré for two centuries. When she was little, I told the children about banquets so they'd forget they were hungry. She preferred to make bread. She was right.
textes.Sylwen nourrit tout le Bois-Doré et se v: Sylwen feeds the whole of Bois-Doré and takes offence if you don't have seconds. I always have seconds. It's a matter of diplomacy.
textes.Sylwen raconte à tout le monde que ma pl: Sylwen tells everyone my plank creaked on the day of the forty loaves. She doesn't even hold it against me: she laughs about it. That's worse. I wish she'd hold it against me a little.
textes.Sylwen. Elle me laisse un pain tous les: Sylwen. She leaves me bread every morning at the foot of my tower. I never see her put it there. Me, who sees everything. I don't ask her anything. I eat it.
textes.Sylwen. J'ai refait toutes les planches: Sylwen. I've redone all the planks on the north side.
textes.Sérieusement ? {dernier_cadeau} ? Tu te: Seriously? {dernier_cadeau}? Are you making fun of me, {surnom}?
textes.Sœur Pétronille, la prêtresse du Temple: Sister Pétronille, the priestess of the Temple of Dawn, was praying by the Frog Lake when the biggest giant frog in the lake swallowed her sun rosary. Without it, she doesn't dare go adventuring any more.
textes.Sœur Pétronille, vous voulez que je vous: Sister Pétronille, would you like me to read you something?
textes.T'as de la sauce sur le nez !: You've got sauce on your nose!
textes.T'as essayé, le château ? Si ça a cassé,: Did you try the castle? If it broke, it's ruins. Ruins are good too.
textes.T'as pas d'oreilles ! Enfin si, mais ell: You haven't got any ears! Well, you have, but they're teeny, on the sides! That's funny! I'm Mochi. My mum makes the bread.
textes.T'as renversé mon verre, là. Tu vas me l: You knocked over my glass, there. You're going to pay for it.
textes.T'as toujours pas vu de dauphin ? Viens: Still haven't seen a dolphin? Come to the end of the quay tomorrow morning. I'll save you a spot.
textes.T'as une queue d'écureuil, c'est de la t: You've got a squirrel tail, that's cheating.
textes.T'as vu mon château ? Il a quatre tours: Seen my castle? It's got four towers and a moat. The sea made the moat.
textes.T'es le meilleur ! Punch ce soir, c'est: You're the best! Punch tonight, it's on me!
textes.TE PRÉSENTER ? Avec plaisir ! Bon, je ne: INTRODUCE YOU? With pleasure! Well, I can't introduce you to everyone, there are too many of us and Tapage would talk for three days. So start with the three pillars of Boucan: Lentille, who feeds everyone at the Canteen, on the ground floor of the Cannery; Rustine, who keeps everything with wheels rolling, at the bike workshop in the Spinning Mill; and Sirène, who quenches everyone's thirst, at the bar of the Howling Hall. Tell them Rouille sent you. They'll give you a… noisy welcome.
textes.TING ! … Dans le berceau : « HIHIHI ! EN: DING! … In the cradle: “HEEHEEHEE! AGAIN! AGAIN! DING!”
textes.TOI AS CHASSÉ GROSSE-DENT ! (Ougha lève: YOU HUNTED GROSSE-DENT! (Ougha raises his arms. The whole Clan cheers.) Tonight, big feast! Ocre paint this on wall. You… you now of the Clan. Clan of Squares… and one Smooth!
textes.TOUCHÉ ! Hi hi hi ! On a gagné ! On reco: TAGGED! Hee hee hee! We won! We can go again whenever you like.
textes.TOUS LES TROIS ?! (Tom saute sur la tabl: ALL THREE?! (Tom jumps on the table and plays until his strings nearly snap.) ♪ And then came a stranger, with fists as hard as bronze, he put all three on the mat: long live the King, the king of fists! ♪ … Here, the King's belt: it belonged to the last champion, forty years ago. No one has worn it since.
textes.TROISIÈME FOIS DANS L'ANNEAU ! Les Seign: THIRD TIME IN THE RING! The Lords of Xibalba are defeated at the ball game, just as the Twins once beat them. “Go then… to the House of Bats.” The door at the back opens.
textes.TROP vite ! Ils vont se décrocher la mâc: TOO fast! They'll dislocate their jaws!
textes.TU AS GAGNÉ ! Devant Bondi ! Bondi a les: YOU WON! Ahead of Bondi! Bondi's ears are all flat, look at him! I'll paint your name at the very top of the board, in lantern letters. Here, the Great Race cup: it's made of Mother Oak wood, and it hasn't left Bondi's side in three years. It'll have a lot of fun with you.
textes.TU AS PÊCHÉ LE POISSON-LUNE DORÉ ?! Gast: YOU CAUGHT THE GOLDEN SUNFISH?! Gaston, fall off your perch, now's the time! You're a legend, {surnom}!
textes.Ta Chanson du Roi de la Bagarre… il lui: Your Song of the Brawl King… is it missing a verse?
textes.Ta barbe pousse encore de travers, Griml: Your beard's still growing crooked, Grimli.
textes.Ta barque peut s'amarrer au petit ponton: Your boat can moor at the little wooden jetty, next to mine. It's free. Well, for you.
textes.Ta barque va bien ? Gertrude te dit bonj: How's your rowboat? Gertrude says hello. Well… I say hello for her.
textes.Ta bière fume, Ulfa. Les runes n'aiment: Your fizz is fuming, Ulfa. The runes don't like it.
Your goat's on my shoulder again.
textes.Ta fleur à nectar a bien poussé, dis don: Your nectar flower's really come along, hasn't it.
textes.Ta hache sent la sève fraîche. Combien d: Your axe smells of fresh sap. How many trees was it again? {nb_arbres}? Leave me one for the shade.
textes.Ta halle tient debout sans toi ?: Is your hall still standing without you?
textes.Ta lavande est coupée, Amélie. Trois bot: Your lavender's cut, Amélie. Three bunches.
textes.Ta mère a raison. Prends-en un troisième: Your mother's right. Have a third.
textes.Ta pelle heurte de la pierre… Une trappe: Your shovel strikes stone… A trapdoor engraved with a serpent, with a bronze ring!
Your octopus scares off my sardines, Lulu.
Your pickaxe is on my goat.
textes.Ta porte aussi, Bramm. Elle ne bouge pas: So is your gate, Bramm. It doesn't move on its own, you know.
textes.Ta première fête, c'était ici. Tu la rac: Your first party was here. How do you tell it now? Polished up a bit already? Good. That's how it's done.
textes.Ta queue cachée, elle va bien ? Chut, j': How's your hidden tail? Shh, I didn't tell anyone! … Well, just Myrtille. And Gland. And Uncle.
Your railing, under my threads, Taeron.
textes.Ta réponse est dans mon grand livre : «: Your answer is in my big book: “Depends on the mystery.” Page one hundred and twelve. Between two “hmphs”.
textes.Ta tisane, Mère-Lune. Et pas de mares ce: Your tea, Mother Moon. And no ponds tonight.
textes.Ta épaule, c'est le meilleur poste de vi: Your shoulder is the best lookout post in the archipelago!
textes.Tac. Tac. Tac. Un nain creuse dans le mu: Tap. Tap. Tap. A dwarf is digging through the wall of his own living room.
textes.Tad-kozh ! La lanterne est allumée, bien: Tad-kozh! The lantern's lit, nice and straight!
textes.Taeron ! Ta passerelle du nord est solid: Taeron! Is your north footbridge sturdy, at least?
textes.Taeron ! Ta planche du milieu soupire, c: Taeron! Your middle plank is sighing tonight.
textes.Taeron construit les passerelles et répa: Taeron builds the footbridges and mends everything, even my door. But he swears the plank didn't crack on the day of the forty loaves. It cracked. I was there. So was he.
textes.Taeron entend ses planches comme j'enten: Taeron hears his planks the way I hear my flames. Up there, we each watch over our own things. He made me hooks for my lanterns. He doesn't make them for anyone else.
textes.Taeron pose les planches, je tisse les v: Taeron lays the planks, I weave the sails. He says his planks hold up the footbridge. I say my threads hold up his planks. We're both right, except him.
textes.Tailler la pierre parfaite. Sans un défa: To cut the perfect stone. Not a flaw, not a bubble. Just one, in my whole life. And show it to nobody. Except you, maybe. For a small fee.
textes.Taillées par Coralin dans du corail et d: Carved by Coralin from coral and shark teeth, ribbed with mother-of-pearl. As long as they're in your bag, you swim one and a half times faster.
textes.Tant mieux pour toi. Ça rend méfiant. On: Good for you. It makes you wary. You start watching the night more than the day. Keep your eyes at peace.
textes.Tant mieux. Ici, on aime les gens qui s': All the better. Around here, we like people who get along.
textes.Tant mieux. J'ai une corbeille de pétale: Good. I've got a basket of petals, just in case.
textes.Tant mieux. J'ai une pleine corbeille de: Good. I've got a whole basket of petals, just in case.
textes.Tant pis pour toi ! Enfin… tant mieux po: Too bad for you! Well… lucky for you, maybe. Hehe. The offer still stands!
textes.Tant pis. Mais tu rates quelque chose !: Too bad. But you're missing out! Well… the neighbors say not, but you are.
Oh well. It can be glued back together… maybe.
textes.Tant que l'Usine Grise de Lisse & Fils f: As long as the Lisse & Sons Grey Factory keeps building robots, the raids will go on. Mamie Barricade knows that the plans for the Lisse-Center are kept at the very bottom of the factory, underground, guarded by Mr Lisse's favourite machine: the Great Digger. You need to go down the five floors, defeat the machine and bring back the plans.
textes.Tata ! Je t'ai vue courir cette nuit !: Auntie! I saw you running last night!
