textes.Tata m'apprend à courir. Elle dit qu'il: Auntie's teaching me to run. She says you have to “wait for the bend”: start gently, wait, wait, and at the bend, hop, give it everything. I said: “Like Grandpa with the float?” She gave me a funny look, for a long time, and said: “… Yes.” I think I said something clever.
textes.Tazira, le pont de la Murène Noire: Tazira, the deck of the Murène Noire
textes.Tazira, le port des sables — la criée, l: Tazira, the port of sands — the fish auction, the souk, and the Murène Noire at the quay
textes.Tchoum ! Tu m'as dit bonjour en premier: Tchoum! You said hello first! I'm writing that down!
textes.Tchoum avait un coup de soleil sur le cr: Tchoum had sunburn on his scalp, bright red. He didn't complain, he never complains. I had a green beanie knitted in Port-Azur and put it on his head. He said: “Yeah.” He's worn it every day since. Even when it's hot. Especially when it's hot.
textes.Tchoum connaît toutes les enceintes par: Tchoum knows all the speakers by their first names, and he knows they have feelings. He pretends not to believe it. Germaine told me everything, though.
textes.Tchoum et moi, on hoche la tête côte à c: Tchoum and I have been nodding our heads side by side for five years. We hardly talk. We don't need to. He's my calmest friend, and my most loyal.
textes.Tchoum ne parle presque pas, mais il con: Tchoum hardly talks, but he knows every speaker by its first name. He does, really.
textes.Tchoum ne parle presque pas, mais quand: Tchoum hardly talks, but when he does, everyone goes quiet to listen. He knows every speaker by its name. Except one, which he refuses to tell me.
textes.Tchoum, Germaine ronronne fort, aujourd': Tchoum, Germaine is purring loudly today.
textes.Tchoum, c'est la moitié de ce mur. Il di: Tchoum is half of this wall. He says three words a day and all three are right. Without him, the party would be noise with sand in it.
Tchoum is a mystery with a beard. He can hear a crab in a speaker before the crab knows it's there. Well… almost. That one time, I was the one who heard it.
textes.Tchoum, il ne grésille pas, c'est la mer: Tchoum, it's not crackling, that's the sea.
Stitch you up? There's nothing to stitch. Come back after your next brawl. It shouldn't be long.
textes.Te revoilà ! Le village parle de toi, tu: You're back! The village talks about you, you know.
textes.Te revoilà ! Où en étais-je ? Ah oui. La: You're back! Where was I? Ah yes. The night the Léviathan struck land…
You're back! The whole city is talking about you.
textes.Te revoilà ! Tu as aimé notre cuisine, h: You're back! You liked our cooking, huh? Come back whenever you like!
Back in the fairy kingdom again.
textes.Te revoilà parmi nous. Yggdrasil murmure: You are among us again. Yggdrasil whispers your name, you know.
textes.Te revoilà, {surnom} ! J'ai du nectar to: You're back, {surnom}! I have fresh nectar, picked at dawn. Well, fairy dawn: when the waterfall lights up.
textes.Te revoilà, {surnom} ! Le vent est bon,: You're back, {surnom}! The wind is good, the sea is like glass. We cast off whenever you like.
textes.Te revoilà, {surnom}. La brume m'avait d: You're back, {surnom}. The mist told me you would return.
textes.Te revoilà, {surnom}. Le dôme frissonne: You're back, {surnom}. The dome shivers when you pass through the Tide Gate. It likes you.
textes.Te revoilà, {surnom}. Les feuilles t'ont: Here you are again, {surnom}. The leaves announced you before your footsteps did.
textes.Te revoilà. Tu ne grandis pas, au moins: You're back. You're not getting any taller, at least?
textes.Te voilà, l'ami des poissons ! {nb_poiss: There you are, friend of the fishes! {nb_poissons} catches, according to Gaston. He counts everything, that bird.
textes.Te voilà, {surnom} ! Assieds-toi, j'ai u: There you are, {surnom}! Sit down, I've got a crêpe on the griddle.
textes.Te voilà, {surnom} ! Django va bientôt j: There you are, {surnom}! Django's about to play.
textes.Te voilà. Montre-moi ces égratignures… H: There you are. Show me those scratches… Hmm. You'll live.
textes.Te voilà. Tu vois, Ramure t'attendait. M: There you are. You see, Ramure was waiting for you. So was I, a little.
textes.Temple-Passoire\nEntrez, la porte est ou:
Colander Temple
Come in, the door is open (everything is open: it's a colander).
Quiet, please, we're draining.
textes.Tenez, Gédéon. Ces baguettes vous attend: Here, Gédéon. These sticks were waiting for you.
textes.Tes bâtons ont fait de belles flèches. T: Your sticks made fine arrows. You have an eye for wood. For a human.
textes.Tes champignons de braise ont fait le ra: Your ember mushrooms made the stew of the century.
textes.Tes champignons ont soigné la toux de to: Your mushrooms cured the whole village's cough.
textes.Tes coups le traversent ! Il faudrait un: Your blows go right through it! You'd need a light to reveal what's hiding… (the Moonglow)
textes.Tes coups rebondissent sur le bronze ! S: Your blows bounce off the bronze! If only its gears would jam…
Your magma hearts light up my tunnel. It doesn't get lost anymore.
textes.Tes genoux, Nono, ils ont battu la mesur: Your knees, Nono, kept the beat the whole track.
Your pearls shine on my party dress. Everyone asks me where they come from.
textes.Tes pieds deviennent légers, légers… Ici: Your feet grow light, so light… Here, gravity is taking a nap. Jump!
textes.Tes rayons de miel ont fait le meilleur: Your honeycombs made the best bread of the year.
textes.Tes roses sont sur le chemin de mes abei: Your roses are in my bees' way, Miriel.
textes.Tes rêves aussi font boum-boum. On les e: Your dreams go boom-boom too. We can hear them from up above.
textes.Thalassa ! Les laminaires sont arrivées,: Thalassa! The kelp's in, long as the canal!
textes.Thalassa m'a tissé un tablier pour l'éta: Thalassa wove me an apron for the stall, with my name embroidered on it. I wanted to pay her, she refused, twice. So I slip a cracker into her basket every morning. I don't think she eats them. Ondine makes boats out of them for the canal. Apparently they float very well. I don't know if I should be proud.
textes.Thalassa me prend toutes les longues lam: Thalassa takes all my long kelp for her weaving. She pays on the nail, never haggles. It's almost insulting.
textes.Thalassa. Des laminaires, à côté du méti: Thalassa. Some kelp, beside the loom.
textes.Thalassa. Elle tisse ce que je fais pous: Thalassa. She weaves what I grow. We understand each other without talking. Especially me.
textes.Thalion ! Aujourd'hui, tu m'apprends l'a: Thalion! Are you teaching me archery today?
textes.Thalion ! Tu as mangé ton pain ?: Thalion! Did you eat your bread?
textes.Thalion ! Tu es encore monté sans dire b: Thalion! You went up again without saying hello.
textes.Thalion ? Il garde une porte fermée depu: Thalion? He's been guarding a closed door for three centuries, and he thinks it's my harp that makes noise. A little music wouldn't hurt him. And he sings out of tune, which doesn't help.
textes.Thalion a peur des grenouilles. C'est vr: Thalion is scared of frogs. It's true! I saw it!
textes.Thalion dit que ma harpe l'empêche de mo: Thalion says my harp stops him keeping watch. He only says that because he sings out of tune.
textes.Thalion grimpe chez les abeilles d'en ha: Thalion climbs up to the top bees like a bear, without saying hello, and comes back down with their honey. He calls it training. My bees call it something else.
textes.Thalion m'a surprise une fois à viser un: Once Thalion caught me aiming at an apple with a stick and a bit of string. I thought he was going to tell me off. He looked at me for ages, then he said: “Your elbow's too high.” And he left. I didn't get it at first. It was a lesson! A real one!
textes.Thalion m'a tout appris. Deux siècles pl: Thalion taught me everything. Two centuries later, he still checks my arrows one by one. I respect him more than anyone. He exasperates me more than anyone, too.
textes.Thalion me demande où je vais dix fois p: Thalion asks me where I'm going ten times a day. I'm a messenger: I go everywhere. He knows that. He asks anyway. One day I'll tell him the truth, just to see his face.
textes.Thalion surveille la place d'en bas, moi: Thalion watches the square from below, I watch it from above. He thinks he's the only one who sees everything. He doesn't see half of what I see. And he never misses an apple, alas.
textes.Thalion surveille tout le monde et oubli: Thalion keeps an eye on everyone and forgets to eat. So I keep an eye on him. Every morning, a honey loaf at the foot of his tower. He pretends not to know where it comes from.
textes.Thalion t'a encore demandé où tu allais: Did Thalion ask you where you were going again?
textes.Thalion t'a à l'œil. Ne lui en veux pas: Thalion has his eye on you. Don't hold it against him: he has his eye on everyone.
textes.Thalion va me chercher le miel sauvage t: Thalion fetches me the wild honey from the very top of the Mother Tree, where the bees are the most golden. For him it's an exercise, like archery. He comes down covered in stings, jaw clenched, and hands me the comb without a word. I give him the first loaf. He eats it with his back to me.
textes.Thalion, c'est le meilleur archer du mon: Thalion's the best archer in the world! But he won't teach me. He says “later”, “never” or “ask Sylwen's door”. And he's scared of frogs. He is, he is!
textes.Thorgal chante faux, danse mal et perd s: Thorgal sings off-key, dances badly and loses his crown while it's on his head. He's the best king we've ever had. And he can't tell I water down his fizz. Well… I think.
textes.Thorgal est un bon roi, mais il croit qu: Thorgal is a good king, but he thinks my crows exist to bring him cheese at midnight. My crows aren't kitchen boys. Neither am I.
textes.Thorgal porte la plus belle couronne du: Thorgal wears the most beautiful crown in the world. I should know: I made it. He still owes me half of it. Ninety years of half a debt weighs heavy on a crown.
textes.Thorgal vient me demander l'avenir comme: Thorgal comes to ask me about the future the way you'd ask the time. He doesn't want to know: he wants to be reassured. I do my best not to lie to him.
textes.Théo cherche son cerf-volant. Il l'a vu: Théo's looking for his kite. He saw it fly off towards the hills, to the west. I haven't got the legs to climb up there.
textes.Théo est mon meilleur critique. Il regar: Théo is my best critic. He watches, he asks questions, and he says “you don't paint fast”. He's right.
textes.Théo est né il y a six ans, un mardi, pe: Théo was born six years ago, on a Tuesday, during a storm. Gérard took forty photos of the window and none of the baby. Since then, I've been watching over two children: Théo, who wants to touch everything, and Gérard, who wants to photograph everything. The first is growing up very fast. The second, I'm not so sure.
textes.Théo, c'est mon fils, six ans, construct: Théo is my son, six years old, builder of sandcastles. The best subject in the world. He never stops moving, so all my photos of him are blurry.
textes.Théo, c'est mon petit architecte. Six an: Théo is my little architect. Six years old, and already building castles with four towers and a moat. One day, he'll build a town. And I'll run the beach hut in it.
textes.Théo, c'est un bébé. Il a six ans et il: Théo is a baby. He's six and he cried for days and days over his kite. But he makes really, really good sandcastles. I have to say that.
textes.Théo, le garçon de l'hôtel, il a perdu s: Théo, the boy at the hotel, lost his kite. He cries all the time. He's a baby.
textes.Théo, mon fils. Six ans, une imagination: Théo, my son. Six years old, the imagination of a sixty-year-old, and a kite that flew away and broke his heart. He builds castles bigger than himself. I can't wait to see what he'll build later on.
textes.Théophraste Filandre m'apprend la téléki: Théophraste Filandre is teaching me telekinesis. Four of his books flew away during the great storm and are stuck where no one can climb: I have to bring them back down.
textes.Tic. Tac. Tic. Tac. Des horloges partout: Tick. Tock. Tick. Tock. Clocks everywhere… and not one shows the same time.
textes.Tiens : une pour maintenant, une pour la: Here: one for now, one for the road. And remember: herbal tea is meant to be sipped slowly, while looking at something beautiful.
textes.Tiens bon, on tangue un peu !: Hold on tight, we're rocking a bit!
textes.Tiens, Barbe-de-Fer. Toujours à refondre: Well, well, Barbe-de-Fer. Still melting down other people's work?
textes.Tiens, des pièces, et deux jarres de la: Here, some coins, and two jars of Mérit's date juice. And if one day you want to fish, my boat is yours.
textes.Tiens, des pièces, et du copal pour le t: Here, some coins, and copal for the temple: they say the gods love the smell of flowers and copal together.
textes.Tiens, des pièces. Des vraies, des ronde: Here, some coins. Real ones, round ones. And a patch, just in case. You never know when you'll get a flat. A tyre, I mean.
Here, keep this one as a souvenir.
textes.Tiens, goûte. … Alors ? Je le savais. Le: Here, taste. … Well? I knew it. The saffron comes from Aïcha's, the preserved lemon from my mother's, and the sea bream… from yours. Take one for the road, and these few coins. And come back on Friday.
textes.Tiens, le passager ! Toujours en bateau: Well, the passenger! Still going by boat? Do me a favour: the steps of the quay, at a run. Hop!
textes.Tiens, le supporter de Raymond. Tu viens: Well, if it isn't Raymond's supporter. Come to see a real champion, or did you get the wrong pitch again?
textes.Tiens, mon amateur de vanille ! Ta boule: Well, my vanilla fan! Your scoop is waiting for you. In my mind, still. But for real too, if you drop by.
textes.Tiens, mon chou : deux potions de mana,: Here, dearie: two mana potions, for your trouble. They're surely magic. These ones, I'm almost sure.
textes.Tiens, mon retardataire. À l'heure, aujo: Well, if it isn't my latecomer. On time, today? No? I only said it to encourage you.
textes.Tiens, quelques pièces, et deux bols de: Here, a few coins, and two bowls of soup to take away. They're in jars, with a lid. Copeau made the lids. Out of pallets, of course.
textes.Tiens, revoilà la jeunesse. Tu viens m'a: Well, look who's back, young blood. Come to help me untangle, or just to listen to my stories?
textes.Tiens, te revoilà, {surnom} ! Ça fait {a: Well, look who's back, {surnom}! It's been {absence}. Gaston thought the crabs had eaten you.
Here, hold the pot. … (You hold the pot. He gets paint everywhere. Mostly on you.) … Perfect! Here, for the helping hand.
textes.Tiens, tiens… Toi qui réfléchis : tu pré: Well, well… You're a thinker: would you rather know the answer, or keep the mystery?
textes.Tiens, tiens… Un humain. Je suis Cardamo: Well, well… A human. I'm Cardamome. I love riddles, secrets and people who think. Do you think?
textes.Tiens, tiens… Venez donc m'expliquer, vo: Well, well… Come and explain yourself, you.
textes.Tiens, tiens… Viens donc m'expliquer, to: Well, well… Come and explain yourself, you.
textes.Tiens, toi. L'eau est bonne, aujourd'hui: Oh, it's you. The water's lovely today. Coming in?
textes.Tiens, un gâteau de miel de Bobor, que j: Here, a Bobor honey cake that I was saving for myself. I'm giving it to you: you did the hardest part, I only did the planting.
Here, a corn cake from Ix Chab.
textes.Tiens, une petite carte de ton portrait,: Here, a little card of your portrait, as a souvenir!
textes.Tiens, une petite fusée de remerciement…: Here, a little thank-you rocket… no, some coins, rather. Rockets are for the party.
textes.Tiens, {dernier_cadeau}. Hmm. Merci, je: Well, {dernier_cadeau}. Hmm. Thanks, I suppose. I'm sure I'll find a use for it.
textes.Tiens, {surnom} ! Monte, j'ai du neuf. E: Well, {surnom}! Come on up, I've got new stock. Well, the same stock.
Here. Hang it above your bed. And if you ever have a nightmare, come tell me: I'll strengthen the net.
textes.Tiens. Des pièces, et trois flacons de m: Here. Some coins, and three flasks of my tonic: honey, fever grass, syrup and a secret. One sip, and you get back up from any brawl. Well, almost any.
textes.Tiens… on se connaît ?: Well now… do we know each other?
textes.Tilleul ! Et alors, cette louve, elle l': Tilleul! So, that she-wolf, did she fish the moon out?
textes.Tilleul ? Le premier qui m'ait raconté u: Tilleul? The first one who told me a story in Ramure, and the only one who's never told me the end of one. My oldest friend. His paws creak as much as mine.
textes.Tilleul, le conteur de Ramure. Un ours,: Tilleul, the storyteller of Ramure. A bear, a real one, with ears. He tells stories better than me, but he falls asleep before the end. In Carène, nobody believes me when I talk about him.
textes.Tisane de brume pour dormir, de lune pou: Mist tea for sleeping, moon tea for dreaming. Every evening I take Mother Moon hers, and I sew the fox ears she gives to travellers who help her. Roux comes home with leaves in his tail and swears he was picking herbs. And Trèfle's tarts, I can smell them a hundred paces off: I walk past just as they come out of the oven. How? The nose, of course.
textes.Tisser à Ondine une robe couleur de sole: To weave Ondine a sun-coloured dress, for the day she goes up there. I'd need yellow thread. Under the sea, there's only the gold of the crown, and the queen is rather attached to it. Will you bring me some?
textes.Titou ! Ta pirouette, elle compte pas do: Titou! Your pirouette doesn't count double.
textes.Titou a inventé le crabe amoureux, je le: Titou invented the lovestruck crab, I admit it. But he danced it badly: too many arms, not enough hips. I fixed it, called it the “sentimental crab” and I teach it. He's demanding his name on my poster. I offered him a teeny little line at the bottom. He said: “Thank you, Miss.” I couldn't tell if that was mean.
textes.Titou compte les versions de mes histoir: Titou counts the versions of my stories and imitates my dancing on the square, in front of all the kids. “The elegant seal.” Cheeky. And he forgets the shoulder move, on top of it.
textes.Titou dit qu'il en est à dix-sept versio: Titou says he's up to seventeen versions of my party in the mine. He writes them down in a journal. One evening he read me version seven, the one with the dragon. I didn't remember telling it. It was very good. I served it up again to Gaspard the next day, polished a little.
textes.Titou dit qu'une pirouette compte double: Titou says a pirouette counts double. That's not in the rules! There aren't any rules, but it's not in the rules. Apart from that, he's my jumping brother.
textes.Titou est adorable, drôle, généreux… et: Titou is adorable, funny, generous… and I haven't got a single sharp photo of him in three years. Not one. And on top of that, he's the one who lost my last glow sticks.
textes.Titou fait le dauphin dans son spectacle: Titou plays the dolphin in his show on the square, to make fun of me. He jumps, he goes “kik-kik”, he ends up in a bucket of water. The kids scream with laughter. I went to watch, ready to grumble. I laughed so hard I gave every kid a necklace. His dolphin cost me fifteen necklaces.
textes.Titou me pique mes élèves, mes idées et: Titou steals my pupils, my ideas and my side of the fountain. He's funny, that's the worst part. His lovestruck crab, I kept it in my class, under a better name.
textes.Titou, l'épaule. On roule l'épaule, comm: Titou, the shoulder. You roll the shoulder, like this.
textes.Titou, ton pas de danse, là, c'est quoi: Titou, that dance step of yours, what is it?
textes.Titou, tu es encore de mon côté de la fo: Titou, you're on my side of the fountain again.
textes.Titou. Une photo. Tu ne bouges pas. D'ac: Titou. One photo. You don't move. OK?
Tobias! My roof's leaking, on the north side.
textes.Tobias ! Ta galette, dans ta poche, comm: Tobias! Your crêpe, in your pocket, as usual.
textes.Tobias a cloué une casserole au plafond: Tobias nailed a saucepan to the ceiling of his workshop, right under my anvil. Every time I strike, it rings. He says it's so I hear what he hears. So I hung a saucepan under my anvil too, which rings at the same time. Now it makes music. He doesn't find it funny.
textes.Tobias bouche les trous du bateau depuis: Tobias has been plugging the holes in the ship for thirty years and never has time to eat. So every morning, I put a crêpe in his pocket. He says thank you the way other people say sorry.
textes.Tobias dit que je suis ses yeux sous la: Tobias says I'm his eyes under the hull. I tell him where it's seeping, where the wood's soft. He listens without sighing, which is rare for him. And his daughter is my friend.
textes.Tobias dit que la coque tiendra encore c: Tobias says the hull will hold for another hundred years. Tobias has been saying that for thirty years.
textes.Tobias me dit que la coque tiendra encor: Tobias tells me the hull will hold another hundred years. He's been telling me that for thirty years. I know what it means: he'll spend his life on it. No one is more faithful to this ship.
textes.Tobias recalfate ma barque-maison chaque: Tobias re-caulks my boat-house every autumn and won't let me pay him. He takes a mackerel, he sighs, he leaves. Gloomy as a windless day, but a good lad.
textes.Tobias se plaint de tout, et surtout de: Tobias complains about everything, and especially about me. He says one day I'll go straight through the deck. He's the grumpiest man in Carène, and I owe him more than he'll ever say.
textes.Tobias se plaint du bruit. Tobias se pla: Tobias complains about the noise. Tobias complains about everything.
textes.Tobias soupire chaque fois que je parle: Tobias sighs every time I talk about putting the Léviathan back in the water. He sighs when I don't talk about it too. But he's the one who knows how to plug the holes, so I keep coming back.
textes.Tobias, le calfat, doit reboucher une vo: Tobias, the caulker, has to patch a leak in the hull of the Léviathan. He needs good timber.
textes.Tobias. Tribord, sous la troisième membr: Tobias. Starboard, under the third frame, it's seeping.
textes.Toc toc ! … Ah non, c'est toi qui frappe: Knock knock! … Oh no, you're the one knocking. Shall we start over?
textes.Toc toc toc ? Hé, c'est MOI qui fais les: Knock knock knock? Hey, I'M the one who tells the jokes around here!
textes.Toc toc… (Une voix ensommeillée, derrièr: Knock knock… (A sleepy voice, behind the door.) “Who's there? … Ah, it's you. We're asleep, it's night! Come back tomorrow, we'll look for the colours together.”
textes.Toc toc… La Maison du Conseil est fermée: Knock knock… The Council House is closed. A poster: “Extraordinary meeting: WHERE HAVE OUR COLOURS GONE? Everyone is asked to search everywhere.”
textes.Toc toc… Personne : de jour, tout le mon: Knock knock… Nobody: by day, everyone is out looking for the colour pots.
textes.Toc toc… Personne. Sur la porte, un peti: Knock knock… Nobody. On the door, a little note: “Gone to find the blue of the sky. Back soon! — the Brush family”
textes.Toc toc… Personne. Un mot un peu taché :: Knock knock… Nobody. A slightly smudged note: “Gone to find the red of the poppies. Please water our flowers, thanks! — the Blotter family”
textes.Toc toc… Personne. Un petit mot : « Part: Knock knock… Nobody. A little note: “Gone to find the green of the leaves. Don't erase anything while we're away! — the Rubber family”
textes.Toc, toc, toc. Une petite voix, derrière: Knock, knock, knock. A little voice, behind the door: "
textes.Toc, toc. Le seul qui répond, c'est la p: Knock, knock. The only one answering is the rain on the roof: tic, tic, tic…
textes.Toc, toc. Rien… Un écriteau peint : « En: Knock, knock. Nothing… A painted sign: “Meditating. Come back in an hour, or in a lifetime.”
textes.Toc, toc… Personne. Sur la porte, un pet: Knock, knock… Nobody. On the door, a little note: “Gone to pick poppies. Come back whenever you like, the door of the heart is always open (this one, not so much).”
textes.Toc, toc… Rien. Puis, de très loin dans: Knock, knock… Nothing. Then, from deep inside the yurt, a sleepy voice: “… It's not time for rehearsal yet…”
textes.Toi ! Ne crois pas que je ne sais pas ce: You! Don't think I don't know what you did.
textes.Toi ! Toi trop maigre ! Pas assez de car: You! You too skinny! Not enough squares! Eat, eat. Fern flatbread, Granny Silex recipe. Nice and crunchy.
textes.Toi ! Tu as l'air affamé. Entre donc !: You! You look starving. Come on in!
textes.Toi ! Tu sais manier la hache ?: You! Can you handle an axe?
textes.Toi ! Tu tombes bien ! Dis-lui, toi :: You! Just in time! Tell him, would you:
textes.Toi ? Dans les Neuf Cercles ? (Le vieux: You? Into the Nine Circles? (The old guardian looks at you for a long time, then unhooks a big black key from his belt.) The Key of the Ember. The door is at the back of the nave. Listen well: a coin for Charon, honey cakes for Cerberus, good answers for Minos. And take a coat, little one. Cocytus is no joke.
textes.Toi ? Dans une mine ? Je rentre !: You? In a mine? I'm coming home!
textes.Toi ? Peur de la mer ? Mais tu es venu j: You? Scared of the sea? But you came all the way here! … So you can be scared and go anyway? Oh. That changes everything.
textes.Toi ?! Sur MA scène ? … D'accord. Vas-y,: You?! On MY stage? … Fine. Go ahead, the audience is hot. Well, warm. Well, it's made of stone.
textes.Toi aussi, tu as eu peur de la mer, et t: You were scared of the sea too, and you came anyway. I think about it every time I look up.
textes.Toi aussi, tu as peur de la mer. Je ne l: You're scared of the sea too. I won't forget. That makes us two pond cats.
You heard it too, the song. There are two of us. It does me good to know that.
textes.Toi aussi, tu perds le compte. On devrai: You lose count too. We should start a club. There'd be four thousand two hundred and twelve of us. Or thirteen.
textes.Toi aussi, tu pleures, quelquefois. Je l: You cry sometimes too. I kept it to myself. If it ever happens to you here, come and find me. I know the good spots.
You too. I mean… have a nice evening.
textes.Toi aussi. À ton enclume. Et aux pierres: You too. With your anvil. And with stones.
You no move! Ocre look at you.
textes.Toi du Clan. Toi toujours bienvenu au fe: You of the Clan. You always welcome at fire.
textes.Toi encore. Bien. Tant que tu respectes: You again. Good. As long as you respect the ship, you're welcome.
textes.Toi et ta fête de village… j'y repensais: You and your village party… I was thinking about it. There was an old fellow in a beanie dancing, wasn't there? No? Pity.
textes.Toi et ta harpe… Caelan a joué jusqu'à q: You and your harp… Caelan played until four. I thought of you. I looked behind me.
textes.Toi et ton poisson grillé… j'ai essayé u: You and your grilled fish… I tried a sardine with ember mushroom. It sneezed. So did I.
textes.Toi grandir. Toi devenir carré comme nou: You grow. You become square like us!
textes.Toi l'amateur de mystères, je t'ai gardé: You lover of mysteries, I've saved you a riddle with no answer. Don't solve it too fast.
textes.Toi le chanteur ! Le roi demande si tu r: Hey, singer! The king's asking if you're coming back tonight. He says he needs someone to drown out his voice.
textes.Toi non plus, tu n'as jamais vu la balei: You've never seen the whale either. Shall we start a club? Two members already makes a watch.
textes.Toi que les bêtes escaladent, je t'ai mi: You whom the animals climb all over, I've put aside a thick old cloak for you. Hooves leave marks.
textes.Toi qui adores le bateau… tu me raconter: You love boats… will you tell me about Port-Azur? With details. I want to know everything, without going.
textes.Toi qui aimes la cuisine douce, j'ai mis: For you who likes it mild, I put less rouille in your portion. My pot hasn't spoken to me since.
textes.Toi qui aimes le silence, ce soir je fer: You who love silence, tonight I'll leave a pause between two songs. A long one. You'll know why.
textes.Toi qui aimes les belles histoires, j'en: You, who love beautiful stories, I've got a brand-new one. It isn't true at all. It's magnificent.
textes.Toi qui aimes les deux… Il était deux fo: You who like both… Twice upon a time, {surnom}. See? You're smiling already.
textes.Toi qui aimes les histoires vraies : cel: You who like true stories: this one really happened. Twice, in fact. Sit down.
textes.Toi qui aimes les lames légères… j'ai pe: You who like light blades… I thought of you this morning while thinning an edge. By a hair. A dwarf's hair, mind, which is already a lot.
textes.Toi qui aimes écouter : j'ai trois histo: You who love to listen: I've got three brand-new stories for you. One of them's about Orsik. Shh!
textes.Toi qui arrives toujours en avance… tu n: You who always arrive early… couldn't you lend me your secret? For one letter. Just one.
textes.Toi qui as compté les étoiles : ce soir,: You who've counted the stars: tonight, count again with me. Two of us will make fewer mistakes. Or twice as many.
textes.Toi qui as des amis pour moitiés… combie: You who have friends for halves… how many do you have now? I count. It's my job.
textes.Toi qui as jamais peur du noir, tu me ra: You who are never scared of the dark, will you tell me how you do it? Slowly. With some fireflies around, though.
textes.Toi qui as oublié ta première fête… je t: You, who forgot your first party… I made one up for you. There were dwarves. You danced a lot.
textes.Toi qui as pas de queue, t'as fait des s: You with no tail, did you do happy eyebrows today? Show me!
textes.Toi qui as peur du noir : la forge reste: You who are scared of the dark: the forge stays red till midnight. Drop by.
textes.Toi qui as plusieurs maisons… Ramure en: You who have several homes… Is Ramure one of them now? Don't answer. I'll feel it.
textes.Toi qui as reconnu mon poisson, viens vo: You recognised my fish, so come and see the next one. I think it's a fish too. Maybe.
textes.Toi qui as un peu peur de la mer : moi a: You who are a little scared of the sea: me too, a little. All right. A lot. But that stays between us.
textes.Toi qui as un peu peur du fond, comme mo: You, who are a bit scared of the deep, like me: breathe slower than the fear. It works for dancing too.
textes.Toi qui as un peu peur du noir… j'ai dem: You who are a bit scared of the dark… I asked a firefly to follow you tonight. If you see a little light, that's her.
textes.Toi qui as vu des dauphins, tu crois que: You've seen dolphins, so do you think mine was a real one? Say yes.
textes.Toi qui as vu du pays, dis-moi francheme: You've seen the world, so tell me honestly: can a map be wrong?
textes.Toi qui as vu tant d'îles… Si tu aimais: You who've seen so many islands… If you'd loved someone for a hundred years, how would you tell them?
textes.Toi qui as vu une lumière que personne n: You who saw a light nobody else saw: if it comes back, come and get me. I'll believe you.
textes.Toi qui avais un peu peur la première fo: You were a bit scared the first time: would you come with me on the Swallow? One day. Not today.
textes.Toi qui bois des litres, je te fais conf: You drink gallons, I trust you. But drink anyway. Just to make me happy.
textes.Toi qui caches des choses vraies dans te: You who hide true things in your jokes… made one this morning? I'm suspicious now.
textes.Toi qui crois aux fées… elles le savent,: You believe in fairies… they know, you know. Last time, up there, I talked about you. They smiled.
textes.Toi qui crois l'avenir écrit : ce matin,: You who believe the future is written: this morning, a rune moved as you went by. I won't tell you which one.
textes.Toi qui dansais comme un pied… je t'ai v: You with the two left feet… I saw you the other night. At least one right foot now. We're getting there!
textes.Toi qui danses avec les pieds, j'ai mont: You dance with your feet — I turned the bass up a bit tonight. Just for your ankles.
textes.Toi qui danses dans ta tête… alors, ça s: You dance in your head… so, is it coming out a little now? I saw you tapping your foot the other night.
textes.Toi qui danses quand personne ne regarde: You, who dance when nobody's watching: I'm not watching. Promise. Well, just a little, as a teacher.
textes.Toi qui danses sur les tables : j'ai fai: Hey, table-dancer: I've had the little one reinforced, with Borin's iron. It's waiting for you!
textes.Toi qui danses… Ce soir, tu viens ? Je t: You who dance… Are you coming tonight? I've saved you a spot behind me, near Grelot.
textes.Toi qui demandes ton chemin : demande-mo: You who ask for directions: ask me, then. I've still got corners of the map to show you.
textes.Toi qui dis merci aux racines. J'ai véri: You say thank you to the roots. I checked. The east one squeaks less. Hmph.
textes.Toi qui dis qu'on peut gagner en arrivan: You, who say you can win by coming second: I won again! Well… second. So, won!
textes.Toi qui dis qu'une bonne carte ne se tro: You, who say a good map is never wrong… you're my only ally on this island. Along with Gaston, on the days he agrees.
textes.Toi qui dis qu'une dette, ça se paie tou: You say a debt always gets paid: you still owe me one visit a week. I'm writing it down.
textes.Toi qui dis que seul le premier gagne… t: You, who say only first place wins… you'll see. This time's the one. My paws agree with you now.
textes.Toi qui dis tout en face… non, rien. Je: You who say everything to people's faces… no, nothing. I wanted to ask your advice. Later. The usual?
textes.Toi qui disais qu'une dette, ça se pardo: You said a debt can be forgiven… I'm thinking about it. Slowly. Don't rush me: iron doesn't like that either.
textes.Toi qui donnes l'alerte : si tu vois que: You who raise the alarm: if you see something, you climb the Lookout. You shout. I come down.
textes.Toi qui dors comme une souche, garde ce: You who sleep like a log, keep that gift. And don't tell Faelar: he'd turn it into a contest.
textes.Toi qui dors mal… tes yeux vont mieux ?: You, the poor sleeper… are your eyes any better? No? Come back and see me, I've got fresh mist.
textes.Toi qui entends ton cœur sous l'eau : re: You who hear your heart underwater: stay a little longer next time. After the heart, there's the rest.
textes.Toi qui es du matin et du soir, comme mo: You're a morning AND a night person, like me… so when exactly do you sleep? Not on the Swallow, OK? That's my spot.
textes.Toi qui es déjà parti une fois, tu ne re: You who've already left once, no regrets? No… I can see you have no regrets.
textes.Toi qui es souvent en retard… je ne te f: You who are often late… I won't lecture you. I was too, once. Just once. That was enough for me.
textes.Toi qui es tombé deux fois de mon hamac: You who fell out of my hammock twice: good news, I've put a cushion underneath. A small one.
textes.Toi qui fais des villes, regarde : j'ai: You who make towns, look: I've started a street. There are three houses and a dog. The dog's a pebble.
textes.Toi qui fais encore des bêtises, on en f: You still get up to mischief, so shall we do some together? A little one. A nice one.
textes.Toi qui fais réparer par les autres : tu: You who get others to fix things: you wouldn't have any wood, by any chance? Good wood. Not driftwood.
textes.Toi qui faisais des tas de bêtises… tu m: You used to get up to loads of mischief… will you tell me about one? Just one? I won't tell Mummy!
textes.Toi qui gardes tes souvenirs, je ne t'en: You who keep your memories, I won't ask you for one. But if one day you've got one to spare…
textes.Toi qui le dirais « tout simplement »… J: You who would tell them “simple as that”… I tried, yesterday. I said “hello”. It's a start, isn't it?
textes.Toi qui lis les cartes avant de partir :: You who read maps before setting off: I've fixed the swamp. Well, I think so. Tell me if you fall in.
textes.Toi qui m'as demandé si j'oserais… J'y p: You asked me whether I'd dare… I think about it every night. Don't tell anyone. Especially not the spiders.
textes.Toi qui m'as dit oui pour la pêche : cin: You said yes to fishing: five o'clock, the jetty, don't forget. I'm still waiting for you. So are the mackerel.
textes.Toi qui manges ce que tu trouves : tu as: You who eat whatever you find: did you find anything today? No? Then EAT.
textes.Toi qui manges du poisson le matin, je t: You eat fish in the morning, so I've saved you a savoury loaf. Just for you. Don't tell the oven.
textes.Toi qui marchandes toujours, approche !: You who always haggle, come closer! I've raised my prices just for you. Now you can bring them down.
textes.Toi qui me crois pour le dauphin ! Tu es: You believe me about the dolphin! You're family now. Have you still got your necklace?
textes.Toi qui montres tes bobos tout de suite,: You, who show your scrapes straight away, let me see those hands… Hmm. You'll live, as usual.
textes.Toi qui n'aimes pas les photos : je n'en: You don't like photos: I haven't taken a single one of you. Well, just one, in my head. It came out nicely.
textes.Toi qui n'as jamais rien vu d'étrange :: You who've never seen anything strange: look at Stoneheart one night. Just one. Then you tell me.
textes.Toi qui n'as pas de moitié… j'ai donné t: You who have no other half… I gave your name to a drop. It's on a flower, near the pond.
textes.Toi qui n'as pas peur de la mer… raconte: You who aren't scared of the sea… tell me again. The colour. The sound. Not the waves.
textes.Toi qui n'as pas peur du fond… tu me rac: You, who aren't scared of the deep… will you tell me what's down there? Take your time. I'm in no hurry.
textes.Toi qui n'as pas peur du noir : si tu cr: You who aren't scared of the dark: if you come across a lantern gone out in a tunnel, it's probably mine. Light it again.
textes.Toi qui n'as peur de rien. Hm. Tiens ce: You who fear nothing. Hm. Hold this hot iron, then. … No. Joking.
textes.Toi qui n'as « pas le temps de dormir »,: You who have “no time to sleep”, you look like a dried mushroom. Sit down. Three breaths.
textes.Toi qui n'entends rien sous l'eau, tu as: You who hear nothing underwater, you're lucky. Silence is rare. Hold on to it.
textes.Toi qui nages un peu : tu m'apprendras ?: You who swim a little: will you teach me? Not in the big pond. In a teeny tiny puddle.
textes.Toi qui ne crois pas aux fées… tu as vu: You don't believe in fairies… have you seen the little lights in the dune, at night? No? Look harder.
textes.Toi qui ne danses jamais… viens ce soir: You who never dance… come tonight anyway. Feet always make up their minds in the end.
textes.Toi qui ne dors jamais assez… je sens qu: You who never get enough sleep… I can smell you've been running about again. A nap, {surnom}. Doctor's orders.
textes.Toi qui ne manges rien le matin… Tu as m: You don't eat anything in the morning… Have you eaten today? Don't lie, I've got a sharp eye.
textes.Toi qui ne marchandes jamais, je t'ai fa: You who never haggle, I gave you a discount. Without saying a word. Don't repeat it, I have a reputation.
textes.Toi qui ne me crois pas… le dauphin est: You don't believe me… the dolphin came by again yesterday. OK, I wasn't there. But it came by again, for sure.
textes.Toi qui ne rapportes jamais rien… Une ca: You who never bring anything back… A postcard weighs nothing, let me remind you. A penny and a half.
textes.Toi qui ne sais pas attendre. Assieds-to: You who can't wait. Sit down anyway. We start with one minute. Shh.
textes.Toi qui ne sais pas jongler : tu as trav: You, who can't juggle: have you practised your fall? I want a lovely fall, with a little yelp.
textes.Toi qui ne sais plus d'où tu viens… j'ai: You who don't remember where you come from… I found a seed that looks like you. Well, a bit. It looks lost too.
textes.Toi qui ne savais pas nager… tu as essay: You, who couldn't swim… did you try floating? The sea holds you up, I told you.
textes.Toi qui ne suis jamais les ordres, je ne: You who never follow orders, I won't give you any. I'll ask you. It's not the same.
textes.Toi qui ne te retournes jamais… Je l'ai: You never look behind you… I did it for you last night. Nothing to report. Good.
textes.Toi qui oublies tes rêves… Perlée en a t: You forget your dreams… Perlée found one in the pond this morning. It was shaped like you. I've kept it.
textes.Toi qui paies sans discuter… je n'ai pas: You pay without haggling… I haven't raised my prices for you. Well, hardly.
textes.Toi qui parles à tes affaires en cachett: You who talk to your things in secret, you know how to keep a secret. So do I. We keep ours, the two of us.
textes.Toi qui partirais sans hésiter, dis-moi: You who'd leave without hesitating, tell me: how does it feel, the first morning, when the coast disappears?
textes.Toi qui passes partout, dis-moi franchem: You go everywhere, so tell me honestly: will Caelan ever dare?
textes.Toi qui pleures en cachette… si tu veux,: You cry in secret… if you like, my house is a good hiding place. Nobody comes. Except Grommelot, but he doesn't look.
textes.Toi qui préfères les chèvres : la petite: You who prefer goats: the little black one recognised you just now. She tried to eat your sleeve. That's a good sign.
textes.Toi qui préfères les vagues… viens sur l: You who prefer the waves… come to the jetty at sunset. We'll play together, them and me.
textes.Toi qui préfères nager : je te garde une: You'd rather swim: I'll keep a towel for you by the dance floor. And a banana, for afterwards.
textes.Toi qui préfères écrire… tu crois qu'une: You'd rather write… do you think a letter counts as much as words said face to face? Say yes.
textes.Toi qui regardes tes pieds : j'ai resser: You who look at your feet: I've tightened two ropes on the south bridge. It dances more calmly now. Just for you.
textes.Toi qui rendrais la baguette à sa fée… j: You'd give the wand back to its fairy… I've put you in my book, on the page for good people. There's only you and Brindille.
textes.Toi qui resterais ici pour toujours… tu: You, who'd stay here forever… see, you're still here. So am I. We're holding on!
textes.Toi qui répares : si tu as une heure, il: You who mend things: if you've got an hour, there's a leak under the forge. No, I'm joking. Almost.
textes.Toi qui rêves les yeux ouverts, viens t': You dream with your eyes open, so come and sit by the pond. Yggdrasil grows upside down in it. It's a good place for dreaming.
textes.Toi qui sais attendre : le ponton est li: You who know how to wait: the jetty's free. Sit down. The King likes patient folk.
textes.Toi qui sais faire des châteaux, viens v: You know how to make castles, come and see mine! It's got five towers now. You can do the moat.
textes.Toi qui sais faire le nœud de chaise : t: You who can tie a bowline: here, mend this bit of net for me. I trust you.
textes.Toi qui sais nager ! Tu plongeras cherch: You can swim! You'll dive for the King, won't you? I'll hold your towel.
textes.Toi qui suis les lanternes : tes bottes: You who follow the lanterns: your boots smell of bridge mushrooms. Good. You listened.
textes.Toi qui suis toujours les ordres, en voi: You who always follow orders, here's one: get some rest. … See, that wasn't hard.
textes.Toi qui t'intéresses à ton passé… je l'a: You, who are interested in your past… I looked at it again last night. It's bigger than you, your past.
textes.Toi qui t'orientes bien : tes bottes son: You with the good sense of direction: your boots went past the same spot twice yesterday. I'm not saying anything. I'm reading.
textes.Toi qui te caches. Bien. Cache-toi derri: You who hide. Good. Hide behind the Lookout: I can see you. Well. I will see you.
textes.Toi qui te lèves avec le soleil : la deu: You who get up with the sun: the second batch has just come out. Just for you. And for the sun.
textes.Toi qui te perds exprès : tu t'es perdu: You who get lost on purpose: where have you got lost since last time? Tell me, I've got my pencil.
textes.Toi qui te souviens de tous tes rêves… r: You remember all your dreams… tell me one, some day. Up here, dreams are news.
textes.Toi qui vas voir de plus près. Hm. Si tu: You who go for a closer look. Hm. If you see something, tell Brume. Then me. In that order.
textes.Toi qui veux des histoires vraies : cell: You, who want true stories: tonight's one, I swear it's true. Almost entirely.
textes.Toi qui veux le vrai et le beau en même: You, who want the true and the beautiful at the same time, you're in for a treat. Sit down: it's always both.
textes.Toi qui veux toujours la réponse… j'en a: You always want the answer… I've got one for you today. But first you'll have to find the question.
textes.Toi qui viens d'une île lointaine… tu n': You who come from a faraway island… you wouldn't have a seed from home at the bottom of a pocket? Look carefully.
textes.Toi qui viens de la mer… tu n'aurais pas: You who come from the sea… you haven't come across a seaweed seed, have you? I've already made room for it.
textes.Toi qui voulais connaître ton avenir… il: You who wanted to know your future… is it unfolding nicely? The cards are asking after you.
textes.Toi qui voulais danser jusqu'à cinq heur: You wanted to dance till five and fish afterwards… The boat has a corner for sleeping, I'm warning you.
textes.Toi qui voulais visiter toutes les îles,: You wanted to visit every island, and it looks like you've come a long way. Will you tell me about the ones I don't know?
textes.Toi qui voyages : quand tu arrives quelq: You, the traveller: when you arrive somewhere, do you look at the map first, or do you get lost on purpose?
textes.Toi qui voyages… qu'est-ce qui brille le: You who travel… what shines brightest, on the other islands?
textes.Toi qui étais très sage… Je ne te crois: You were very good… I still don't believe you. Neither does Button.
You too skinny. Not enough squares.
textes.Toi à qui personne ne racontait d'histoi: You, whom nobody told stories to… I save one for you every time. You've got catching up to do.
textes.Toi, au moins, tu paies en pièces ! Mon: You, at least, pay in coins! My favourite customer. Don't tell my uncle, he'd disown me.
textes.Toi, c'est l'eau fraîche, je sais. Avec: You're the cool-water one, I know. With the umbrella. I'm not judging. Well, a little.
textes.Toi, l'enfant des histoires de pirates !: You, the child of pirate stories! I've found one in my memory: a pirate who was scared of water. Sit down.
textes.Toi, l'expert de l'œil ! Regarde ma daur: You, the eye expert! Look at my sea bream: it's giving you the eye, isn't it? Caught this morning.
textes.Toi, l'humain ! Tu as l'air fatigué. Vie: You there, human! You look tired. Come and see my potions!
textes.Toi, l'épée à une main. Montre ton poign: You, the one-handed sword. Show me your wrist. … Hm. Looser. Always looser.
textes.Toi, la personne du matin ! Passe au Pai: Hey, morning person! Drop by the Pain Doré at six, I'll keep the first croissant for you. Piping hot.
textes.Toi, le fan de coco… tu es allé goûter c: You, the coconut fan… did you go and try Kiki's? Traitor. Just kidding. So, which one's better?
textes.Toi, le mangeur de noix de coco ! J'ai r: Ah, the coconut eater! I made my coconut brioche again. The oven didn't sulk for a second.
textes.Toi, le marcheur ! Tu sais quoi ? Dans l: You, the walker! Know what? On the hills, walking's not so bad. Between you and me.
textes.Toi, le poète qui trouve que la mer bril: You, the poet who thinks the sea shines: got any coins today? No? I thought as much.
textes.Toi, le roi de la bière pour tous : Ulfa: You, the king of fizz-for-all: Ulfa sends her regards. She says if you ever take a throne, she's moving out.
textes.Toi, le vertige. Hrmm. Je tire doucement: You. Scared of heights. Hrmm. I pull gently. Promise.
textes.Toi, le « pas encore » ! Alors, c'est po: Well, if it isn't “Not Yet”! So, when's it going to be? The starting arch hasn't moved, and neither has my stopwatch.
You did. Him, I don't know.
textes.Toi, sois honnête : tu marchandes ?: You there, be honest: do you haggle?
textes.Toi, t'as une tête qui ne me revient pas: I don't like the look of you.
You, talk too much. Like before.
textes.Toi, tu as assez bu pour aujourd'hui. Un: You, you've had enough to drink for today. A glass of water, and off to bed!
textes.Toi, tu as dit que je n'aurais jamais pe: You said I'd never be scared. I told the crystal, and Abyssos wrote it down. It's official.
textes.Toi, tu as quelqu'un qui est un peu ta m: Do you have someone who's a bit like your other half? A brother, a sister, someone far away?
textes.Toi, tu as vu la baleine. Immense. Je te: You've seen the whale. Enormous. Sometimes I look at you and think: those eyes have seen it.
textes.Toi, tu boudes moins depuis que tu mange: You sulk less since you started eating breakfast.
textes.Toi, tu frappes aux portes. Bien. C'est: You knock at doors. Good. That's rare. The others dig underneath. Hmph.
textes.Toi, {surnom}… Pas de hop, cette fois. L: You, {surnom}… No hop, this time. The cup from two years ago, I turned it to face the wall of my room. I'm ashamed I didn't stop for Éclair. Grisou, he shouted “you OK?”. And I'm scared. Not of losing the race: of not knowing who I am any more, if I'm not the champion. Bondi running at the back, who's that?
textes.Toi, ça fait longtemps que je voulais te: You, I've been wanting to tell you this for ages!
textes.Toi. Quand tu arrives devant une porte f: You. When you come to a closed door, what do you do?
textes.Toi. Tu as déjà vu une lumière que perso: You. Have you ever seen a light that nobody else saw?
You… come here and let me archive you.
textes.Tom le Violoneux chantera la gloire de c: Tom the Fiddler will sing the glory of whoever knocks down the port's three champions with their fists: Gros-Louis of the Requin Borgne, the Mute of the Veuve Écarlate and Belle-Humeur of the Morue Enragée.
textes.Tom va en faire une chanson !: Tom's going to make a song out of this!
textes.Tombée d'un cocotier abattu. Son lait re: Fallen from a felled coconut palm. Its milk restores one heart.
textes.Ton ami. Hmpf. Chacun ses fréquentations: Your friend. Hmph. Each to their own company. As long as you pay…
textes.Ton bateau ! Évidemment. Un bateau, ça a: Your boat! Of course. A boat has a name, that's the law. Mine's called Gertrude. Your rowboat and Gertrude might cross paths in the harbour. They'd better get along.
Your bowl, Bramm. Careful, it's hot.
textes.Ton carnet de voyage a rencontré un prob:
Your travel journal ran into a problem.
A “cheap” program turned everything upside down.
textes.Ton carnet est très, très lent. Clique i: Your journal is very, very slow. Click here to speed it up (promise).
textes.Ton carnet garde tout ce qu'on te demand: Your journal keeps track of everything you're asked. Read it again when you don't know where to go.
Your coal, Brunna. Dry. Bone dry.
textes.Ton chat a besoin d'une mise à jour. Tu: Your cat needs an update. You don't have a cat? It needs one anyway.
textes.Ton chat… je peux le chercher ?: Your cat… can I look for it?
textes.Ton cidre aussi, Salomé. Le thé d'abord,: So has your apple juice, Salomé. Tea first, we'll quarrel later.
textes.Ton cœur bat fort et ton souffle est ple: Your heart beats strong and your breath is full. Ra has nothing to give you today… except his light, and that one is free.
Your duty has gravy in its beard.
Your kapok tree is laughing, you know.
textes.Ton gros poisson, j'y ai repensé. C'étai: I thought about your big fish again. It was a dolphin. I'm sure. Almost sure.
textes.Ton livre ? Il dort chez moi depuis soix: Your book? It's been sleeping at my place for seventy years. It's picked up the accent.
textes.Ton miel ! Le pain de cette semaine a le: Your honey! This week's bread tastes of sunshine. The whole village wants the recipe.
textes.Ton moustique… tu me le prêterais ?: Your mosquito… would you lend it to me?
textes.Ton pantalon, je lui parle, moi. Il dira: Your trousers? I'll have a word with them. They'll say yes.
textes.Ton passé ? Tiens, original. Tu es arriv: Your past? Well, that's original. You arrived by sea, you carry a sword, and you look like you've seen things no one here has ever seen. No need for cards for that, traveller.
textes.Ton perroquet… je peux le chercher ?: Your parrot… can I look for it?
textes.Ton portrait est sur le mur, dans la Gro: Your portrait on wall, in the Cave of Paintings. Whole Clan come see. They laugh. But nicely.
textes.Ton professeur qui nous cherche… J'ai co: Your professor who's looking for us… I've started a scroll about him. There's only his job in it so far, but it's a start.
textes.Ton record, c'est {record} ? Moi, une fo: Your record is {record}? I once caught a whale. Well, it was a rock. But it looked like a whale.
textes.Ton rouleau, je vais le tailler en poiss: Your scroll? I'm going to carve it into a fish.
textes.Ton sac déborde, {surnom}. Range-le comm: Your bag's overflowing, {surnom}. Pack it like a mine: well propped.
textes.Ton sac déborde. Fais de la place, et re: Your bag is overflowing. Make some room, then come back.
textes.Ton sac est plein ! Fais de la place ava: Your bag is full! Make some room before opening the chest: its contents will wait for you.
Your bag is full! Make some room before opening the chest.
textes.Ton sac est plein ! Fais de la place pou: Your bag is full! Make room for the Pearl of Light.
Your bag is full! Make room for the wand.
Your bag is full! Make room for the flower.
textes.Ton sac est plein ! Fais un peu de place: Your bag is full! Make a little room for the fragment.
Your bag is full! Make a little room for the seal.
Your bag is full! Make a little room, then come back.
Your bag is full! Make a little room.
textes.Ton sac est plein ! Trocante rit : « Alo: Your bag is full! Trocante laughs: “Then give something first!”
textes.Ton sac est plein : Lentille te fait boi: Your bag is full: Lentille has you drink the soup right there, from the ladle. It does you good.
textes.Ton sac est plein : fais-y un peu de pla: Your bag is full: make a little room for the colour pot.
textes.Ton sac est plein : le sifflet des compa: Your bag is full: the Companions' Whistle is waiting for you. Make some room!
textes.Ton sac est plein de virus ! (Ça, c'est: Your bag is full of viruses! (That one's true. It's me.)
textes.Ton sac est plein à craquer : fais-lui u: Your bag is bursting: make a little room for the cloth.
Your bucket? The blue one? Never seen it, bro.
Your short black, Aristide. Don't touch anything.
textes.Ton sort pour voler avance ! Pour l'inst: Your flying spell's coming along! For now, it makes spoons levitate. It's a start.
textes.Ton épée naine ! Prends-en soin : graiss: Your dwarven sword! Take care of it: grease the blade, and never lend it to an elf.
textes.Ton épée à deux mains. La poignée, elle: Your two-handed sword. The grip, is it holding? Show me. … Hm. It's holding.
Your island is pretty. Noisy, but pretty. The trees here are young: they don't talk much yet.
textes.Toni ! Un verre pour un collègue ?: Toni! A drink for a colleague?
textes.Toni est un artiste. Son punch est divin: Toni is an artist. His punch is divine, absolutely divine, whereas the tea on this island is a tragedy. He never has change, but he always has a smile. That's far rarer.
textes.Toni et moi, on a souvent parlé d'organi: Toni and I have often talked about holding a big punch contest: the Perroquet against the Coco Loco, in front of the whole town. We never dared. The night we talked about it most seriously, we tasted each other's punch for practice, and ended up singing together on the terrace. Contest postponed.
textes.Toni m'a donné une scène, un repas et un: Toni gave me a stage, a meal and a wage. I'm grateful to him. The wage is what bothers me.
textes.Toni n'a plus de noix de coco pour son c: Toni has run out of coconuts for his famous punch.
textes.Toni, c'est mon copain et mon concurrent: Toni is my pal and my competitor. He makes the second-best punch in Port-Azur. In the evening, it's his place I go to for a drink. That way, I keep an eye on the competition.
textes.Toni, c'est mon patron, et un peu mon on: Toni is my boss, and a bit of an honorary uncle. He hired me the very first evening. He teases me about Lucas every day. I pretend not to hear.
textes.Toni, my friend ! Un punch, s'il vous pl: Toni, my friend! A punch, please. Divine, as usual.
textes.Toni. Bon bar, bonne bière. Il me paie l: Toni. Good café, good fizz. He's been paying for the sign in fizz for twenty years. Suits me. Don't tell Colette, she'd charge me for the air.
textes.Tonton Bondi, c'est le plus rapide du mo: Uncle Bondi is the fastest in the whole wide world! He eats three carrots, not one more. I'll be a runner too, like him. But with cakes instead of carrots.
textes.Tonton m'apprend le départ comme une flè: Uncle teaches me the arrow start, in Grandpa and Granny's vegetable patch. We crouch between the carrots, he says “Hop!” and off we go. I go before the hop. He says that's cheating. I say it's a very fast arrow. Granny says we're squashing the leeks.
textes.Tordue ? Sur quoi tu couds, sur une coqu: Bent? What are you sewing on, a hull?
textes.Toujours ? Comme ça, droit dans les yeux: Always? Just like that, straight in the eye? I'm impressed. Won't you give me lessons? I'll pay in punch.
Always BOOM. At least it's consistent. Science marches on!
textes.Toujours au top ! Le soleil brille, les: Always top-notch! The sun's shining, people are thirsty, and I've got ice.
textes.Toujours aucune lettre ? Je vous ai mis: Still no letters? I've put an envelope aside for you. Empty. Waiting for you to fill it.
textes.Toujours bonne ! Un patron de bar triste: Always good! A sad café owner is like an empty bottle.
Always in the other direction, eh.
textes.Toujours de passage ? Je vous ai inscrit: Still passing through? I put you down in pencil. It hasn't rubbed off yet, mind you.
textes.Toujours deux. Je les ai comptés, comme: Still two. I counted them, like Grégoire.
textes.Toujours jamais malade ? Je note. Je not: Still never ill? I'm making a note. I note everything, you know. The day you sneeze, I'll be there.
textes.Toujours les affaires. La barque t'atten: Always business. The boat's waiting for you, you know.
textes.Toujours moi, Croc-Gris. Pas de monstre,: Still me, Croc-Gris. No monster tonight.
textes.Toujours pas d'épée ? Hm. Je t'ai mis un: Still no sword? Hm. I've put a blade aside for you. Not free. But aside.
textes.Toujours pas de légendes, pour vous ? Je: Still no legends for you? I'm noting your position. I'll refute it one day, with evidence in hand.
textes.Toujours pas de nom pour ta lame ? Elle: Still no name for your blade? It's waiting, you know. Iron is patient.
textes.Toujours pas de romans d'amour ? Je vous: Still no romance novels? I'll lend you one. You'll read it in secret, like everyone.
textes.Toujours pas de sommeil ? Je vous ai mis: Still no sleep? I've put a cup of tea aside for you. The management understands. It, too, sometimes…
textes.Toujours pas dit merci aux racines, hein: Still haven't thanked the roots, eh? Hmph. They kept you standing anyway. That's how they are.
textes.Toujours pas parlé à ton épée ? Essaie u: Still haven't talked to your sword? Try one evening, very quietly. I'm sure it has things to say.
textes.Toujours pas. Et tu me dois toujours tro: Still not. And you still owe me three bottles.
Still no. But I've got beetroot.
textes.Toujours rien de précieux ? Vous voyagez: Still nothing precious? You travel light. I need three porters just to go and have tea.
Still nothing to declare? … Very well. I'm watching you. Discreetly. Don't turn round.
textes.Toujours rien à vous reprocher ? Je véri: Still nothing to reproach yourself with? I'm just checking, that's all. Pure routine. Good day, model citizen.
textes.Toujours sans un sou, {surnom} ? Ta gout: Still penniless, {surnom}? Your free drop is waiting. Just one, mind. I have a reputation.
textes.Toujours sur mon dos, Bedaine. Et elle y: Still on my back, Bedaine. And there it stays.
textes.Toujours tes cailloux ? Apporte-les-moi,: Still your pebbles? Bring them to me, I'll paint them blue for you. Pebble rate, very low. Very low for me.
textes.Toujours trop chaud ? Votre platane est: Still too hot? Your plane tree is under review. Before the end of the year. Don't tell Hortense.
textes.Toujours une boule pour l'inventrice, pa: Always a scoop for the inventor, boss!
textes.Toujours {manque} champignons à trouver,: Still {manque} mushrooms to find, {surnom}. Damp undergrowth, at the foot of the big trees.
textes.Toujours {manque} cœurs de magma à trouv: Still {manque} magma hearts to find, {surnom}. The elementals prowl the edge of the crater. They burn: strike fast, step back fast.
textes.Toujours {manque} dents de requin à trou: Still {manque} shark teeth to find, {surnom}. The sharks circle the reef. Wait for them to charge, then strike!
textes.Toujours {manque} runes de golem. Monte: Still {manque} golem runes. Climb towards the crater: they guard the black slopes. Strike when they raise their big arms… after, not before.
textes.Toujours {manque} éclats d'obsidienne, {: Still {manque} obsidian shards, {surnom}. The black glass, at the edge of the crater.
textes.Toujours, Majesté ! Enfin… presque toujo: Always, Your Majesty! Well… almost always.
Always, Majesty. Only real ones here.
textes.Toujours, Nono. Mais lentement, mon appa: Always, Nono. But slowly, my camera's tired.
Always, down to the tiniest detail.
textes.Toujours, madame. C'est une politique de: Always, madam. It is house policy.
textes.Toujours, maître Borin. Et toujours un p: Still, Master Borin. And still a little less well than you.
textes.Toujours, petit. Les baleines ont leurs: Always, lad. Whales have their habits.
Always. Even if it's the lullaby.
textes.Toujours. Rejouez la note grave. Pour le: Always. Play the low note again. For the violet.
Always. Come in, I've made coffee.
textes.Tourne les cristaux ! Chacun renvoie la: Turn the crystals! Each one sends the light in the direction it points.
Turn around. No, the other profile.
textes.Tous les ans, Borin et moi, on demande à: Every year, Borin and I ask Hilda to judge our beards. She stands us side by side, walks around us, tugs a hair here, a hair there. Then she says: “I win.” Croâ caws to applaud. We try again the next year. We always lose.
textes.Tous les ans, à la fête de la Forge, je: Every year, at the Forge Festival, I challenge Bramm to arm-wrestling. Every year, I lose. He doesn't even break a sweat. Last year, I held out for eleven seconds. He said nothing. But Kalda told me that on the way home, he muttered: “Eleven.” Just that. I'm training for twelve.
textes.Tous les après-midi, quand je fais ma lo: Every afternoon, when I do my lap of the bay, Bernard runs along the beach, right level with me. “By chance.” If I speed up, he speeds up. If I float on my back, he stops to retie his shoelace. We never talk about it. Between sportsmen, we understand each other.
textes.Tous les chats accourent ! La dame est r: All the cats come running! The lady is delighted: “You've been adopted. By them. It's an honor!”
textes.Tous les dimanches, Fernand mange ma bou: Every Sunday, Fernand eats my bouillabaisse, mops it up to the last drop, then puts down his spoon and says: “Something's missing.” Every Sunday! Something! It keeps me up at night. I change the saffron, the garlic, the fennel… he always says the same thing. One day I'll find that something. And that day, he's doing the washing-up.
textes.Tous les jours à midi, Dagna traverse la: Every day at noon, Dagna crosses the terrace with a steaming bowl and sets it on the stone next to me. I say “Hmph”. She says “You're welcome”. We've been talking like that for a hundred and fifty years. It's the longest conversation of my life.
textes.Tous les jours à onze heures, je passe g: Every day at eleven, I drop by to taste the stew. One ladleful. For the salt. Dagna pretends not to see me, and the ladle is always resting on the edge of the cauldron, handle turned my way. Always. I say nothing. Neither does she. And I go back for thirds.
textes.Tous les jours, en allant au Perroquet,: Every day, on my way to the Perroquet, I walk under the clock and look up. One day, Madame Hortense was on her bench. She saw me look up. She said nothing. Neither did I. Cost me more than a good telling-off.
textes.Tous les jours, je monte quarante sacs d: Every day, I carry forty sacks from the city stores up to the terrace forges. Three hundred steps. A big'un carried with me for three years, once: Hector, Borin's apprentice. He puffed like a bellows with a hole in it, but he never gave up. Coal is heavy. The terrace is warm thanks to us.
textes.Tous les jours, je vais à la poste achet: Every day I go to the post office to buy a stamp. Just one. Nadine asks me: “Again?” I say I have a lot of mail. I've got three hundred stamps in a drawer and nobody to write to. If I stuck them all on one letter, it would go round the whole archipelago. One day, maybe. For now, I just chat.
textes.Tous les matins, Dwalin descend un chaud: Every morning, Dwalin takes a cauldron of my stew down to the Blazing Mug. Ulfa sells it on for twice what I charge. I know it, she knows it. At every Forge Festival, she gives me back the difference in an embroidered purse, with a little note: “For the salt.” She's teasing Borin, of course.
textes.Tous les matins, maman a de la farine su: Every morning, Mum has flour on her nose. I don't tell her. The customers smile, and she thinks it's because of her bread. One day I'll tell her. Or not. She looks pretty with it.
textes.Tous les matins, quand je passe devant l: Every morning, when I go past the lifeguard post, he starts doing push-ups. On purpose. He counts out loud: “Four hundred and ninety-eight! Four hundred and ninety-nine!” So I do an extra lap. He does a hundred more push-ups. One day, one of us is going to crack. It won't be me. Well, I don't think so.
textes.Tous les matins. On s'est habitués l'un: Every morning. We've got used to each other.
textes.Tous les printemps, je trouve un bouquet: Every spring, I find a bouquet on my counter, tied with a golden thread. Nobody in the village spins that kind of gold, except one. I've never thanked her. She's never confessed. One morning I left a cup of tea beside it, with a note: “For the wind.” The cup was empty by noon.
textes.Tous les quatre ! Le traité des nuages,: All four! The treatise on clouds, the herbal of shadows, the grammar of ravens and… “Berthe's Recipes, Volume Two.” I'd forgotten that one. Thank you. Truly. Here, some coins. And you may borrow any book you like, whenever you like. Without dog-earing it.
textes.Tous les soirs après la garde, je monte: Every evening after my watch, I go up to the terrace to buy a mug of golden fizz from Sigrun. I drink it very slowly, so I can stay. Yesterday, she said: “Gunnar, you've been drinking the same mug for three years.” She's right: I top it up with water so it lasts. She laughed. I blushed.
textes.Tous les soirs, Barnabé agite son chapea: Every evening, Barnabé waves his hat towards our mist from his beach. Thalion says we don't answer humans. One evening I took a lantern and flashed it three times from the top of the highest platform. Barnabé jumped on the spot and danced. His parrot must have told him it was a firefly. Don't tell Thalion.
textes.Tous les soirs, Kiki rentre de la paillo: Every night, Kiki comes back from the beach hut at midnight on the dot and plays three songs under my window. He thinks I like it. So at midnight on the dot, I close my shutter. Clack. He takes it for applause. The next day he asks me: “Did you hear the new one?” I heard. All the new ones.
textes.Tous les soirs, Ori compte mes rubis ave: Every evening, Ori counts my rubies with me and writes them one by one in the big ledger. Every evening, one is missing. Ori writes: “one ruby, out”. Not “stolen”. “Out.” I asked him why. He said: “Because it comes back.” That lad is wiser than his great-uncle.
textes.Tous les soirs, au ponton, Bastien m'att: Every evening, at the jetty, Bastien waits to carry my baskets. He says he's checking the tides. At seven in the evening. Every evening. Empty-handed. One day I gave him the most golden croissant of the batch. He held it like treasure. He didn't eat it in front of me. Funny boy.
textes.Tous les soirs, j'agite mon chapeau vers: Every evening, I wave my hat towards the mist. Nobody ever answers. Except once: a lantern blinked three times, high up in the trees. Gaston says it was a firefly. Me, I'm sure it was Faelar. Old folks understand each other.
textes.Tous les soirs, j'écoute grand-père Till: Every evening I listen to Grandpa Tilleul at the Circle. The other little ones fall asleep before the end. Not me! Never! I ask “And then?”, and he starts another story. He's got loads. Under the big pond there's a dragon, I'm sure of it, and one day he'll tell me its very own story. Mochi says a dragon-fish. Myrtille says a king. Both total nonsense.
textes.Tous les soirs, je monte sur ma plus hau: Every evening, I climb onto my highest branch and look across to the other side of the island. I check that the smoke from his hut is rising. If it is, I climb back down. I don't know why I do it. Neither does Clou.
textes.Tous les soirs, mademoiselle ! Un jour,: Every evening, miss! One day, someone will answer.
textes.Tous les soirs, maman me raconte une his: Every night, Mummy tells me a story she makes up. They're the best in the world. Yesterday it was Captain, my bear, who went off on a boat to find my kite. He found it on an island made of clouds. I fell asleep before the end. This morning I asked for the end. Mummy said it's a secret. Mummies have loads of secrets.
textes.Tous les soirs, quand L'Hirondelle accos: Every evening, when the Swallow docks, I'm at the jetty to carry Fanny's baskets to the dance floor. One evening she gave me the most golden croissant of the batch. I didn't eat it right away. I looked at it for a long time, sitting in my boat. It was all squashed the next day. Silly, isn't it.
textes.Tous les soirs, une lanterne de nacre ar: Every evening, a mother-of-pearl lantern drifts down the canal, right in front of my bridge. I pretend to believe it's the current. But the current flows the other way, {surnom}. I know perfectly well who blows those lanterns. I'm waiting for him to tell me himself. It's been thirty years. I'm patient. Well, less and less.
textes.Tous les trois ! Et chauds encore, je pa: All three! And still warm, I bet. You're a darling, my little one. Here, some coins, and a nice warm honey bread. That one, you're allowed to eat on the way.
textes.Tous trouvés ! Tu es le champion du cach: All found! You're the hide-and-seek champion!
All of it? Very well: {prix} coins for the lot.
textes.Tout ? {prix} pièces le lot. Et je suis: All of it? {prix} coins for the lot. And I'm being generous.
Very softly, then. Close your eyes.
textes.Tout ce qui arrive sur l'île passe par m: Everything that arrives on the island goes through my arms. Margaux's bread, Toni's bottles, the jewellery shop's dresses.
textes.Tout de suite, chef ! Combien, aujourd'h: Right away, boss! How many today?
textes.Tout de suite, milord. Mais je n'ai touj: Right away, milord. But I still don't have change.
textes.Tout en haut de la grotte ! Les gros cha: Right at the top of the cave! The big mushrooms bounce: climb on, and boing!
textes.Tout en haut du tableau, champion. Il s': Right at the top of the board, champ. It's getting a bit bored.
textes.Tout est beau ici. Même quand on est tri: Everything is beautiful here. Even when you're sad.
textes.Tout est cher à Port-Azur, parce que tou: Everything's expensive in Port-Azur, because everything comes by boat. But my prices are fair. Well, nearly.
Everything's too close to you, lad. Hmph. Again.
Everything is for sale! … Well, almost.
textes.Tout flotte ! La table, les chaises, les: Everything floats! The table, the chairs, the books… even the houseplant, which looks delighted.
textes.Tout l'hiver, il m'a appelée « la grande: All winter, he called me “the big hairy one”. “Big hairy one, sweep! Big hairy one, stand back!” I swept. I watched. He refused to teach me the runes. I didn't ask twice. Tempering, I learned by watching him. He knows, I think. He grumbled, the day I left. A good grumble.
textes.Tout le monde croit que Grimli dort dans: Everyone thinks Grimli sleeps in the mine because I snore. I snore, fine. But that's not why. He forgets things, {surnom}. Real things. He's afraid I'll see it. So I embroidered both our names inside his cap. He hasn't noticed yet.
textes.Tout le monde parle de ce que tu as fait: Everyone's talking about what you did for {qn}.
textes.Tout le monde parle de ce que vous avez: Everyone's talking about what you did for {qn}.
Everyone knows I'm scared of heights. What nobody knows is why I'm cross with Thalion. Not because he shakes the bees up there. Because he can climb up and see them, and I can't. I hear them singing on windy days. I've never seen them. Not once.
textes.Tout le monde sait que tu as offert {obj: Everyone knows you gave {objet} to {qn}. Around here, news travels faster than the wind.
textes.Tout le monde sait que vous avez offert: Everyone knows you gave {objet} to {qn}. Around here, news travels faster than the wind.
textes.Tout le reste. Mais on a des amis partou: All the rest. But we've got friends everywhere now.
textes.Tout le temps ! Ha ha ! Tu es un renard: All the time! Ha ha! You're a fox in disguise, admit it! … All the time, eh. It gets tiring, in the long run. I know.
textes.Tout là-haut, au sommet du Mont Fusain,: Way up, at the summit of Mount Charcoal, beside the cairn: a little glint. Purple. A pot!
Everything looks lovely to me today.
textes.Tout près, hein. Pour qu'il la voie bien: Really close, eh. So he can see it properly. He'd say “Hm.” But a proud “Hm”. I know those, I've heard two.
textes.Tout simplement… Tu dis ça comme si c'ét: Simple as that… You say it as if it were simple. For humans, maybe: you live fast, you talk fast. I should take lessons.
textes.Tout tourne… Tu ferais mieux de t'arrête: Everything's spinning… you'd better stop there!
textes.Tout ça ? D'accord. {prix} pièces le lot: All that? Alright. {prix} coins for the lot. You're getting a good deal, and I'm getting a better one.
textes.Toute la caverne chante, d'une seule voi: The whole cavern sings, with one low, soft voice. The veins of the rock light up all the way to the ceiling… At the back of the room, the great slab sinks into the floor. “The Heart of the Song is yours, friend of the Moai.”
textes.Toute la forge se tait. Borin et Nori le: The whole forge falls silent. Borin and Nori the Runecarver engrave the armour for an entire night. By morning, the runes beat softly, like a heart. “The finest I've ever made.”
textes.Toute la forêt, tonton ! Surtout la part: The whole forest, Uncle! Especially the part with the arches.
textes.Toute la place a entendu. Le trente-sixi: The whole square heard. The thirty-sixth verse was pretty.
textes.Toute légère ! Les fleurs boivent, les f: Light as air! The flowers are drinking, the fairies are singing.
textes.Toute ma vie, j'ai cherché la cité englo: All my life, I've searched for the sunken city. The texts speak of a great crystal that gave air and light. If one day you find that city, if you see that crystal shining… come back and tell me about it. I beg you.
textes.Toute petite ourse, pendant mes histoire: When she was a tiny bear cub, during my stories, she'd bang on the pots with a spoon. Bing! when the dragon came. Bang! when the storm broke. Her mother wanted to hush her. Me, I understood that night she'd be a blacksmith. Old Charbon took her on as an apprentice at ten. He said she struck true.
textes.Toute petite, Lumi passait ses journées: When she was tiny, Lumi spent her days trying to light herself up, like the fireflies who saw her born. One evening, she came and cried on my lap. I told her: “You don't need to glow, Lumi. You make the others glow.” The next day, I put her in charge of the fireflies.
textes.Toutes ? Et combien de détours ?: All of them? And how many detours?
textes.Toutes ? Il en faudrait peut-être quatre: Every one? There may be four hundred… But I like your answer. You have human feet and the heart of a migrating bird.
textes.Toutes ? Même celle qui ne craquait pas: All of them? Even the one that didn't creak?
textes.Toutes ? Même… la reine ? Oh ! J'ai les: All of them? Even… the queen? Oh! I have tears in my eyes. You carried a little of my heart to the end of the world. Take a little of mine: it's big, I have too much.
textes.Toutes les couleurs de l'île: All the colours of the island
textes.Toutes les heures, Gaspard pose une gour: Every hour, Gaspard puts a bottle of spring water on my table. If I don't drink, he stays there, looking at me, nodding. Once, I held out for four minutes. I drank it in one go, laughing, and improvised a track for him. I called it “Water Bottle”. He's never found it funny. He dances to it anyway.
textes.Toutes les journées sont belles, au Bois: Every day is lovely, in Bois-Doré.
textes.Toutes les yourtes sont vides… Où sont d: All the yurts are empty… Where have the people of Larsen Island gone? It looks like they're preparing something.
textes.Toutes mes passerelles sont solides, Syl: All my footbridges are sturdy, Sylwen. All of them.
textes.Toutes mes versions sont vraies, ma puce: All my versions are true, sweetheart. Especially the best ones.
textes.Toutes, Majesté ! Un record ! Fffiou !: Every one, Your Majesty! A record! Fffwoosh!
textes.Toutes… Toutes les couleurs. (Elle regar: All… All the colours. (She looks at the clearing, the giants, the houses, the sky in the pond, for a long time, saying nothing.) The Council met this morning. Well, Gaspard, Augustin and I, on the terrace. We voted. From now on, you will be the Colourist of Sketched Island. Keep the Brush: it's yours now. And if one day it rains too hard, you'll know what to do. Here, also: a honey cake from Rosalie, and a little from the Council's fund. It was only used for buying paint.
textes.Tout… Vous avez un grand cœur. Ou beauco: Everything… You have a big heart. Or a lot of practice. A ring in the sand should be easy to forgive, shouldn't it? So why is it so hard?
textes.Tranquille, Barnabé. Plancher, murs, toi: Chill, Barnabé. Floor, walls, roof. And a bottle of water.
textes.Tranquille. Le son est bon, l'eau est fr: Chilled. The sound is good, the water is cool.
textes.Tranquille. Tu veux de l'eau ? J'ai touj: Chill. Want some water? I've always got water.
textes.Traverser le Lac Miroir sur un chemin de: Cross Mirror Lake on a path of ice (frost spell, key 7 then V, facing the islet; in VR, left trigger) and touch the Frost Crystal (E)
textes.Trente ans de réception. J'ai accueilli: Thirty years at reception. I've welcomed princes, pirates and a performing bear. The bear was the most polite.
textes.Trente ans en haut du Guet. Par tous les: Thirty years at the top of the Lookout. In all weathers. The zip line, I strung it up to get down fast in an alarm. The children use it. And Grisou. From up there, I see the forest, and the forest knows I see it. That's the job. Being seen seeing. So nobody gets up to mischief. Almost nobody.
textes.Trente ans facteur à Port-Azur. Je conna: Thirty years as Port-Azur's postman. I knew every letterbox, every dog, every creaky step. At Hortense's I'd stop by even with no letter. For my last year, they gave me an apprentice, Nadine. I taught her everything. She remembered everything. Except the route: she made it shorter. That one still sticks in my throat.
