I got up, opened the door, waited on the doorstep in my nightshirt. He turned up at nine, walking. He said he'd had a pebble in his shoe. I went back in without a word. I slept badly anyway.
textes.Un matin, il répétait son grand air sur: One morning, he was rehearsing his big aria on his balcony, above the port. A high note, very high, very long. Every seagull in the port took off at once. Every one. The fishermen thought a storm was coming. He took a bow. I was playing down below, on the jetty. I played louder, out of solidarity with the seagulls.
textes.Un matin, il s'est accoudé au comptoir e: One morning, he leaned on the desk and studied me at length through a magnifying glass. Then: “My dear Edmond, I'll buy your moustache. For my collection, next to the admiral's.” I replied that it was not for sale, and that I very much doubted the admiral had been consulted. He laughed. He hasn't given up.
textes.Un matin, j'ai dit à Hortense que l'horl: One morning, I told Hortense the clock would ring again thanks to a stranger. She answered “Nonsense” and shut her door in my face. Ten seconds later, she opened it again, just a crack, to ask: “What sort of stranger?” Then she shut it before I could answer.
textes.Un matin, j'ai décidé de le rattraper po: One morning, I decided to catch up with him to serve him notice of the sign. I ran. With the kepi, the belt and the notebook. After twenty metres, I was red as a lobster, and Bernard was at the lighthouse. He waited for me there, doing stretches. I didn't fine him. I needed my breath.
textes.Un matin, j'ai envoyé Croâ lui porter un: One morning, I sent Croâ to take him a bit of bark. I'd carved on it: “Smile.” Croâ came back with the bark cut neatly in two. On the half he gave back, Bramm had carved: “No.” I still have it. It's the only letter he's ever written me.
textes.Un matin, j'ai posé une brochette sur so: One morning, I put a skewer on his bench. One of Caramel's. Still warm. No note. … He looked at it all day. He didn't eat it. He thought it was a trap. … By evening, it was cold. I ate it. Cold. … It doesn't matter.
textes.Un matin, j'ai pêché un mérou plus lourd: One morning I caught a grouper heavier than Clou. I hauled it up to the cheese shop with a rope. Octave looked at it, weighed it in his hands, and paid without haggling. Without haggling! I told the whole party about it, twice. Mistral made a track out of it, “Octave's Grouper”. Octave has never listened to it. He hears it anyway, from up there.
textes.Un matin, j'ai recompté derrière elle. T: One morning, I recounted after her. Stalk by stalk. Two hours. There was one too many. I kept it in my pocket all week to show her. She said: “It's a little one, it counts as half.” Hmm. I replanted it. Seaweed doesn't haggle.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé dans la vase des t: One morning, I found fresh cat tracks in the mud, circling the jetty three times and stopping right at the edge. I thought I was onto something. I followed them, measured them, drew them. They were his, from the night before. He'd come back in secret. He said: “Shh. I was checking.”
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé un panneau sur la: One morning, I found a sign on the lighthouse door: “People sleep here.” Hand-painted, in enormous letters. I knocked anyway, twice, but ever so gently, with my fingertips. Tap… tap. I've knocked like that ever since. He says it's worse. I'll never understand that man.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé un pédalo jaune am: One morning, I found a yellow pedalo tied to my bollard. Mine, in front of the harbour office. Yannick spent twenty minutes explaining that this pedalo had a name, a history and a personality. All I took in was the knot. It was wrong.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé une brochette sur: One morning I found a skewer on my bench at the foot of the Lookout. No note, nothing. One of Caramel's skewers, still warm. And across the bridge, Éclair, watching me. I thought it was a trap! I kept an eye on it all day without touching it. In the evening it was cold, and Éclair looked disappointed. Why disappointed?
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé une chèvre sur mon: One morning, I found a goat on my throne. She was chewing my red velvet cushion and looking at me as if I were the intruder. I thought: there's a beast with a feel for power. I sent for her shepherdess and put her in charge of my ravens. I've never regretted it. The cushion, I do.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé une jolie pierre r: One morning, I found a pretty red stone on my anvil. I took it for ore and put it in the fire. It shattered. Kalda came by right after. She looked at the empty anvil, she looked at the fire, and she left without a word. Hilda says I'm a donkey. I still don't know why.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé une noisette sur l: One morning, I found a hazelnut on the steps of my throne. Zéphyr swore he hadn't done it on purpose. The shell cracked, and a teeny tiny fairy poked her head out to ask: “Are there any seeds around here?” That was her first word. It was not her last.
textes.Un matin, j'ai vidé son sac par terre en: One morning, I emptied his sack on the floor, shouting: “Wet!” He shouted: “Dry!” An hour of arguing, right in front of Borin. In the end, Borin threw a lump on the fire. Pfff. Wet. Dwalin never owned up. But the next day, his coal was dry, and he brought me a slice of Dagna's cake.
textes.Un matin, j'avais la voix cassée. Rúmil: One morning I'd lost my voice. Rúmil cast his nets anyway. Nothing. Not one ray. He waited an hour, then looked at me: “Whistle, then.” I whistled. Three rays came. Ever since, he claims the light prefers whistling. He's lying, and he knows it.
textes.Un matin, j'avais une nouvelle figure da: One morning I had a new figure in my head, and I tried it in the kitchen. Oh… I spun, my tail swept the shelf, and two jars of honey broke. Grelot came in, looked at the honey on the floor and said: “That pirouette's four coins.” Then she helped me clean up, laughing.
textes.Un matin, j'entends gratter sous la viei: One morning I hear scratching under the old root. A fairy. From the sky. With a shovel. She'd dug a hole as big as… as her. She said: “Just one seed!” I chased her with my broom all the way to the garden. She was laughing. She had the seed. Hmph.
textes.Un matin, j'ouvre une caisse de sardines: One morning, I open a crate of sardines for the stall: hazelnuts. Everywhere, between the fish. Gland had put them there “to keep cool”. I yelled so loud Dad dropped his rod. Myrtille laughed so hard she fell off the bench. The worst part: the sardines had a little hazelnut taste. I sold them for more.
textes.Un matin, je lui ai demandé l'air qu'on: One morning, I asked her for the tune they used to dance to in the square when she was twenty. She hesitated, then hummed it, very softly, eyes closed. I played it. At the second verse, she stood up and walked off, very upright, without a word. I didn't finish the tune. I've never played it in front of her again.
textes.Un matin, je lui ai demandé trois fois o: One morning I asked him three times where he was going. Three times he said “nowhere”. The third time, I followed him. He did indeed go nowhere: to the end of the jetty, to look at the mist, for a whole hour. I went back. We've never spoken of it since.
textes.Un matin, je me retourne : plus de Fanny: One morning, I turn round: no Fanny. She was standing against the warm oven, arms crossed, eyes shut, hair full of sand. Asleep on her feet, like a horse. I let her be for ten minutes. When she woke up, she said: “I dreamed I was making croissants.” She had flour up to her eyebrows.
textes.Un matin, je me suis cachée derrière une: One morning, I hid behind a flower to listen to Perlée talking to her drops. She was telling them the weather forecast! “You'll get sunshine. You, a little wind. Sorry, that's Zéphyr.” I couldn't help laughing. She pretended not to hear me.
textes.Un matin, je portais une caisse de citro: One morning I was carrying a crate of lemons along the edge of the quay. Odette shouted “Lucas!” behind me. I jumped, I dropped the crate. A hundred lemons in the harbour. She didn't scold me. She took a landing net, I took another, and we fished them out together for an hour. Without talking. Three are missing. The seagulls, I think.
textes.Un matin, je suis parti faire un petit t: One morning I went out for a little stroll. I followed a golden heron, then a stream, then the edge of the mist. When I got back, the whole village was in tears: nine days had gone by. Orophin had searched the entire island. I thought I'd been gone a morning. I brought Nimiel back a feather.
textes.Un matin, ma barque avait disparu. Momo: One morning, my boat had vanished. Momo had taken it to go and find his dolphin. He came back at noon, swimming, pushing the boat in front of him: he'd lost both oars. No dolphin. He made me a shell necklace to say sorry. I wear it. Don't you dare tell him.
textes.Un matin, maman a ouvert une caisse de s: One morning, Mum opened a crate of sardines, and there were hazelnuts all through it! She screamed so loud that Grandpa dropped his rod. It was Gland, he'd put them there “to keep cool”. I laughed so much I fell off the bench. Mum said the sardines smelled of hazelnut. She sold them anyway.
textes.Un matin, mon pétrin a fait « croa ». J': One morning my dough trough went “croak”. I plunged my hands into the dough and pulled out a frog covered in flour, looking very pleased with itself. Nimiel was at the window. She said: “He was cold.” The dough, I threw away. The frog, I gave back. And I didn't tell Miriel. That time.
textes.Un matin, pour balayer dessous, j'ai sou: One morning, to sweep underneath, I lifted his anvil. On my own. Borin stopped talking. A whole minute. The dwarves put down their hammers. Silence. First time all winter. Then he said: “Put it down. Gently.” I put it down. He started talking again. Quieter.
textes.Un matin, pour gagner un aller-retour, j: One morning, to save a round trip, I took both flour sacks at once, one on each shoulder, and ran the whole south bridge. I arrived white from my ears to my tail, a proper rabbit ghost. Mochi screamed. Trèfle just said: “Morning, Pépin.” She'd recognised me by the way I puff.
textes.Un matin, très tôt, j'ai trouvé Thalion: Very early one morning, I found Thalion sitting alone on the harp bench, plucking a string. Just one. Always the same one. He jumped and said: “Inspection.” Since then I always leave the harp tuned to that note. He doesn't know. He mustn't know.
textes.Un matin, un garçon timide est entré et: One morning, a shy boy came in and bought a bouquet “for his mother”. The next day too. And the day after. A whole year like that. One day, his mother came to see where all those bouquets were coming from: she sneezed eleven times. Hay fever. On the three hundred and sixty-fifth morning, Hugo held the bouquet out to me over the counter. He said: “Here.” It was perfect.
textes.Un matin, une araignée de cristal s'est: One morning a crystal spider shattered against my root. A heap of shards, right outside my place. She came flying, with her purse. I sat on them. She said six coins a shard. I said no. There was a blue one. She'd have melted it. Melted! A blue shard like that.

One morning a crystal spider shattered against a root, right outside his place. A heap of shards! I came flying, Grommelot came running. He sat on them. I offered six coins a shard, he said “not for sale”. The whole lot went into his fireplace. For the warmth, apparently. It sparkles like a shop window, his warmth.
textes.Un matin, une fuite s'est ouverte sous l: One morning, a leak opened under the hold, and I had nothing to stuff it with while I waited for the oakum. I used what I had in my pocket: Gwenola's pancake. It held for two hours, nicely buttered. Gwenola found out, I don't know how. She reminds me every morning. That was twelve years ago.
textes.Un matin, une plume de lune s'est envolé: One morning, a moon feather flew off my counter, so light, so shiny. I chased it up the stairs, then across three bridges, then all the way to the treetop. It landed right on the Post Office counter. Plumette picked it up and gave it back to me: “Hoo. It wanted to go by post.” I was as out of breath as a rabbit.
A thank you! I'm writing that down.
textes.Un midi, elle s'est levée d'un bond, la: One lunchtime, she leapt up, fork in hand, and ran off towards the quay. A badly moored sailing boat was banging against the jetty. She retied the knot with the fork between her teeth. Then she came back, sat down and finished her cold plate without a word. I offered to warm it up. “No need.” She ate the lot.
textes.Un minuscule carré de cristal. Quand on: A tiny square of crystal. When you blow on it, a little hologram pops out and takes a bow.
textes.Un minuscule champignon féerique bleu, t: A tiny blue fairy mushroom, very proud, puffing out its cap. "Munch": you suddenly grow big and hit harder (for a while). A storybook mushroom: in a real forest, you must NEVER eat a mushroom you don't know.
textes.Un monstre ! Je prie, je prie très fort: A monster! I'm praying, I'm praying really hard!
textes.Un morceau d'amulette en jade, gravé d'u: A piece of jade amulet, engraved with an ancient symbol. You need three to open the Serpent Gate, deep inside the Sunken Temple.
textes.Un morceau de fromage qui a beaucoup voy: A piece of cheese that has travelled a lot, with a golden rind and a… brave smell. For a rat, it's a treasure.
textes.Un morceau de lumière tombé du ciel une: A piece of light fallen from the sky on a clear night, pale and warm. Aurélien Lumen needs it to teach the light spell.
textes.Un mot sur la table : « Cher voleur, il: A note on the table: “Dear thief, there's nothing to steal here except the dirty dishes. Help yourself.”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « Le plombier pass: A note on the table: “The plumber will come on Tuesday. Or Wednesday. Or never. Put a basin under the leak.”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « Liste de courses: A note on the table: “Shopping list: bread, eggs, a dragon (small), cheese. Don't forget the cheese.”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « Ne pas toucher a: A note on the table: “Don't touch the cake. Signed: Mum.” Below, in different handwriting: “What cake?”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « Partis à la plag: A note on the table: “Gone to the beach. If it's you, Gérard: the cat has ALREADY eaten. Don't listen to him.”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « RAPPEL : demain,: A note on the table: “REMINDER: tomorrow is Uncle's birthday. Buy a present. NOT socks.”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « Recette de la so: A note on the table: “Granny's soup recipe: water, vegetables, and lots of patience. Especially patience.”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « Si tu lis ce mot: A note on the table: “If you're reading this, you're in my house. While you're at it, water the plants. Thanks!”
textes.Un moteur à cristal… Seuls les Lumens d': A crystal engine… Only the Lumens of Astralys, the island floating in the sky, know how to make those crystals sing. You'd have to go and visit them.
textes.Un moteur à vapeur, j'aimerais bien… mai: A steam engine, I'd love to… but I'd need the plans from the inventors of Cliquetis, the city of gears, on the great eastern island. Go and pay them a visit!
textes.Un moustique dans une petite calebasse f: A mosquito in a little gourd closed with a leaf stopper. Kinich swears its name is Xan, like the Twins' one, and that it stings liars.
textes.Un mérou ! Un vrai, un gros ! Je vais le: A grouper! A real one, a big one! I'll be eating it for a week. Or mapping it.
textes.Un mérou… Je vais le fumer au-dessus de: A grouper… I'll smoke it over the forge. Come back for a taste.
textes.Un nain n'oublie jamais un visage. Ni un: A dwarf never forgets a face. Or a debt. Or an insult.
textes.Un naufragé ne se perd jamais : il est d: A castaway never gets lost: he's already lost. It's very restful.
textes.Un navet fuyard ! Il ne mord pas… il cou: A runaway turnip! It doesn't bite… it runs. Catch up by running (Shift) and give it a little tap: it's yours.
textes.Un navet fuyard des Champs du Sud, attra: A runaway turnip from the Southern Fields, caught during an alert: it's golden, it has little arms, and it's sulking. The Guild buys it back; so do Babette and Ulric (for soup).
textes.Un nectar ! Bois-le d'un trait, c'est me: A nectar! Drink it in one go, it's better. And it heals better.
textes.Un nid de pie était caché dans les branc: A magpie's nest was hidden in the branches!
textes.Un nid de tagliatelles dorées, faites à: A nest of golden tagliatelle, handmade this morning by Mamma Lasagna, "while singing". For the Great Reconciliation dish. Don't squash it, don't break it, don't eat it on the way.
textes.Un nouveau ! Génial ! Viens, je te montr: A new one! Brilliant! Come on, I'll show you: there, the dormitory, Oscar snores; over there, the Duelling Ground, Pyra shouts; down below, the Chaudron Fumant, Berthe bakes pies; and up there, the Observatory, Lumen sleeps by day. Six masters, six spells! Me, I have zero. But soon one!
textes.Un ondin, un esprit de l'eau ! Il se gon: An undine, a water spirit! It swells up before pouncing: step aside. The Gust (key 1) scatters it.
textes.Un os à mâcher qui sent bon le jambon, d: A chew bone that smells deliciously of ham, from Chaussette's shop. For Sardine, the dog with the red bandana: "Give" when he's with you.
textes.Un oursin ! Hmpf. Bon. Je vais lui ajout: A sea urchin! Hmph. Fine. I'll add some spines, then you'll be right. The customer decides. Even when he doesn't pay.
A tool… Fine. A tool's honest. But you'll see: one day it'll save your skin, and that day, you'll find it a name. All by yourself.
textes.Un pain assez grand pour tout le village: A loaf big enough for the whole village, at the Dawn Festival! One single loaf in the middle of the square, and everyone takes a piece. I'll need a bigger oven. Mine's going to sulk.
textes.Un pain que tout l'archipel connaîtrait: A bread the whole archipelago would know: “Azur bread”, with honey. Eaten by the dwarves, by the elves, under the sea if need be. And people would say: that comes from Margaux's.
textes.Un pain rond et plat, cuit contre la par: A round, flat loaf, baked against the wall of Mérit's oven, with a little sand in it (everyone has sand in their bread in Per-Hâpy). Restores two hearts.
textes.Un panier d'osier des Jardins Partagés :: A wicker basket from the Shared Gardens: leeks, squashes, potatoes, and a carrot with a tiny bite taken out of it. For everyone's soup.
textes.Un parapluie noir, comme tous ceux de Ra: A black umbrella, like all the ones in Rainville… but underneath, when you open it, there are painted sunflowers. Mother Downpour made it fifty years ago, for her best friend.
textes.Un parapluie rouge surmonté d'une hélice: A red umbrella topped with a propeller. When you open the umbrella, the propeller spins. It's no use at all, but it's very pretty.
textes.Un parapluie… avec des tournesols peints: An umbrella… with sunflowers painted underneath. So that, even in the rain, I can see the sun. (She opens it; she laughs; she cries a little.) She promised it to me, the summer of our quarrel. Fifty years… Well. It's time two old ladies stopped being silly.
textes.Un parchemin roulé, un sceau rouge, une: A rolled-up parchment, a red seal, a little cottage drawn in the corner: "The Wisteria Cottage, Montjoie Upper Town, now belongs to its new owner. Wisteria included." Signed: Mr Prosper.
textes.Un parchemin roussi aux coins, scellé de: A parchment singed at the corners, sealed with red wax: "Bachelor of Flames, with the (slightly burnt) congratulations of the jury". Signed: Professor Malachar.
A passenger saw whales, up north.
textes.Un pavillon à la poupe : six dessins au: A flag at the stern: six designs to choose from, to change whenever you like.
textes.Un perroquet ! La prochaine fois, je t'e: A parrot! Next time, I'll make you two. One for him.
A parrot ate half of it.
textes.Un petit ? Un tout petit tour ?: A little one? A teeny little lap?
textes.Un petit Moaï surveille un tas de feuill: A little Moai watches over a pile of smoking leaves. “Don't step on it! It's dinner!”
textes.Un petit Moaï te fait signe : « Psst ! T: A little Moai beckons to you: “Psst! Do you know '1, 2, 3, Moai'?”
textes.Un petit air, pour rester éveillé ?: A little tune, to help you stay awake?
textes.Un petit champignon des mares de Ramure,: A little mushroom from the ponds of Ramure, with a pale blue cap, that glows softly at night. Mère-Lune puts them in the bridge lanterns.
textes.Un petit chien blanc dort derrière mes c: A little white dog sleeps behind my crates, at the end of the quay. I'd seen a snout. I didn't say anything. Nina found him and named him Brioche. So I made him a kennel out of an empty crate and an old blanket. I wrote on it in chalk: “Brioche”. The crate's called Brioche now too.
textes.Un petit croc jaune, perdu par un gobeli: A small yellow fang, lost by a goblin from the Goblin Wood (he has others, and a stolen sock in each pocket). Master Hugues makes necklaces with them.
textes.Un petit diablotin te tapote la joue : «: A little imp pats your cheek: “Up you get! The circles won't go down by themselves.”
textes.Un petit démon plonge sous la table en t: A little demon dives under the table when he sees you. “MOOOMMY! A HUMAN!”
textes.Un petit museau rose sort d'entre les pl: A little pink snout pokes out from between the planks of the jetty, next to the hull of the Requin Borgne… and ducks straight back in. You'd need to put down something that smells very, very good: the aged cheese!
textes.Un petit piment rouge et luisant, du mar: A small, shiny red chilli from Zébuline's market. Demons crunch them like cherries. You're going to cry. Restores one heart (smoke out of the ears included free).
textes.Un petit pot de peinture en fer-blanc, c: A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "1". Inside, the blue of Sketched Island (the Rubbed-Out Pond, the sky in the water, the streams). To be poured into cup no. 1 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "2". Inside, the green of Sketched Island (the leaves, the grass, the moss of the Hatching Wood). To be poured into cup no. 2 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "3". Inside, the red of Sketched Island (the poppies of the White Meadows). To be poured into cup no. 3 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "4". Inside, the yellow of Sketched Island (the sand of the White Strand). To be poured into cup no. 4 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "5". Inside, the brown of Sketched Island (the wood of the village, the earth of the clearing). To be poured into cup no. 5 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "6". Inside, the purple of Sketched Island (the heather of Mount Charcoal). To be poured into cup no. 6 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "7". Inside, the orange of Sketched Island (the Ink Waterfall at sunset). To be poured into cup no. 7 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "8". Inside, the turquoise of Sketched Island (the Dotted Stream, all the way to the sea). To be poured into cup no. 8 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "9". Inside, the pink of Sketched Island (the flowers of the south-western meadows). To be poured into cup no. 9 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.
textes.Un petit pot de sauce tomate, puisé à la: A small jar of tomato sauce, scooped with the giant ladle from the Cooking Pot of Mount Bolognese: tomato, garlic, basil, a pinch of sugar. Still warm. Restores two hearts.
textes.Un petit robot-nettoyeur te passe la ser: A little cleaning robot mops your forehead: “Please do not faint in traffic areas. Thank you.”
textes.Un petit sifflet en os sculpté, avec un: A little carved bone whistle, with a dog, a cat, a rat and a pig engraved all around it. "Use": choose which companion comes with you.
textes.Un petit slime te tapote la joue d'une g: A little slime pats your cheek with some very cool jelly: “Blop?” (That means “get up”.)
textes.Un petit sort de bulle : l'air de la mai: A little bubble spell: the air in the house is a bit damp, just enough for them. You don't feel a thing. Except maybe a little dampness in your hair.
textes.Un petit tour, ou neuf jours ?: A little stroll, or nine days?
textes.Un petit tour. Tu viens avec moi ?: A little stroll. Coming with me?
textes.Un petit trésor ! Le coffret contient :: A little treasure! The box contains:
textes.Un peu ? Il parle à un perroquet ET à de: A bit? He talks to a parrot AND to seashells. You, now, you're someone sensible.
textes.Un peu ? Tu en as perdu combien, en rout: A little? How much did you lose on the way?
textes.Un peu de graisse de chèvre. Très peu. P: A bit of goat fat. Very little. Hardly any.
textes.Un peu de lumière de l'Aube, et hop !: A little light of the Dawn, and presto!
textes.Un peu de vertige. Hrmm. La rambarde. Pa: A bit scared of heights. Hrmm. The rail. Not the wicker. Remember?
textes.Un peu ensommeillée… Les chouettes, le j: A bit sleepy… Owls in the daytime are like rabbits at night.
textes.Un peu fatigué. J'ai dansé toute la nuit: A little tired. I danced all night beneath the Mother Tree.
textes.Un peu inquiet. Le cristal pâlit…: A little worried. The crystal is fading…
A bit lost, to be honest.
A little more in tune, please.
textes.Un peu triste. La harpe s'est tue cette: A little sad. The harp fell silent last night. … I won't say I miss it.
textes.Un peu triste. Le cristal pâlit, et ma m: A bit sad. The crystal is fading, and my mum says it's serious.
textes.Un peu triste. Sans ma rosée, les fleurs: A little sad. Without my dew, the village flowers are thirsty.
textes.Un peu, c'est bien. Ça fait marcher douc: A little is good. It makes you tread carefully. The miners who are never scared, they're the ones you find at the bottom of holes. Me, for instance.
textes.Un peu, c'est déjà beaucoup ! Moi, un pe: A little is already a lot! Me, a little… um… I can put one paw in the water. That's a start, right? Mrrrow.
textes.Un peu, c'est honnête. Moi aussi, le pre: A little is honest. Me too, the first winter. Look at the lighthouse when it takes hold of you. It turns for you too.
textes.Un peu, c'est sage. Une mer, c'est une m: A little is wise. A sea is a pond that doesn't know when to stop. You have to be wary of it. A little. Mrrr.
textes.Un peu, c'est un début. Conseil de pro :: A bit is a start. Pro tip: breathe out slowly, don't fight the water, and don't think about sharks. There aren't any. Hardly any.
A little. Thanks to the chocolate.
textes.Un peu. Hrmm. Comme tout le monde. Tiens: A bit. Hrmm. Like everyone. Hold the rail. Not the wicker.
A little. I've noted it, Admiral.
textes.Un peu. Moins qu'avant. Grâce à votre te: A bit. Less than before. Thanks to your tenon.
textes.Un peu… D'accord. Un peu, je peux. C'est: A bit… OK. A bit, I can do. It's a lot I can't do. Will you hold my hand, for the bit?
textes.Un piano enrhumé, des bulles en forme de: A piano with a cold, heart-shaped bubbles and an offended automaton. Exactly what I thought: they've all won. I'll create three prizes. Thank you, juror! You deserve your title. And take this watch: it runs backwards, but it's accurate… backwards.
textes.Un pirate ronfle dans son hamac. Sur son: A pirate snores in his hammock. On his perch, a red parrot looks at you… and is very, very eager to chat.
textes.Un plateau de cuivre, une théière d'arge: A copper tray, a silver teapot, colored glasses: it's tea time.
textes.Un pogo à la Halle Hurlante: A mosh pit at the Howling Hall
textes.Un poing de fer ? Pour toi ? … Hm. Il me: An iron fist? For you? … Hm. I need three crocodile teeth. Not dog teeth, not shark teeth: crocodile from the Drowned Marsh, to the west. They're as hard as steel. I'll set them in the metal, and your fists will hit like hammers. But the crocodiles, they bite like anvils. Watch out for the water.
textes.Un poisson frais ! Gaston, sors la poêle: A fresh fish! Gaston, get out the frying pan! Well… the flat stone.
textes.Un poisson noble qui se défend bien. Ren: A noble fish that puts up a good fight. Restores one and a half hearts.
textes.Un poisson-perroquet ! Ne le dis pas à G: A parrotfish! Don't tell Gaston, he'd think it's a cousin.
textes.Un poisson. Non. Un oursin. Ne bouge pas: A fish. No. A sea urchin. Don't move, I'm thinking.
textes.Un pont de Ramure jusqu'au Cœur-de-Pierr: A bridge from Ramure all the way to Cœur-de-Pierre! Really long, really high, dancing the whole way. You'd hear the stones singing all the way to Cliquetis!
textes.Un pont de corde, il faut qu'il danse av: A rope bridge has to dance with the wind. A stiff bridge breaks. A dancing bridge lasts a hundred years. Like old squirrels.
textes.Un pont jusqu'à la lune ! Je commencerai: A bridge all the way to the moon! I'll start it all by myself, with twigs, and Pomme-de-Pin will help with the last bit. The last bit's the hardest: it wobbles because of the stars.
textes.Un pont qui sonne comme une caisse. Enfi: A bridge that rings like a till. Finally some common sense.
textes.Un pot de gelée verte, tremblotante, qui: A jar of wobbly green jelly that goes "bloop" when you shake it. Aubin, the apothecary, makes ointments with it; Madame Olga, potions; the children, mischief.
textes.Un poulpe entre dans une taverne. Il com: An octopus walks into a café. He orders eight drinks. One per arm!
textes.Un printemps, Nimiel s'est cachée sous m: One spring, Nimiel hid under my cloak, at the bottom of my boat, to go and see the humans. She sneezed right in the middle of the mist. I had to turn back. She sulked for a whole day, which is her record. The next day, she was already planning her next hiding place.
textes.Un printemps, j'ai cueilli tout le pré d: One spring, I picked the whole clover meadow for the Dawn festival crowns. The next day, Gilwen came to see me with a hundred furious bees around her head: “They're looking for you.” I had to put half the crowns back in the meadow. Half the village danced bareheaded.
textes.Un printemps, j'ai suivi la côte jusqu'à: One spring, I followed the coast all the way to Tazira. Three days' walk, sea spray all over my whiskers. Over there, on a square full of sand, drums all night, and people dancing like happy goats. I came home with sand in my tail for a month, rhythms for Pépin, and steps for Lilas. The sand, I kept for myself.
textes.Un printemps, je me suis cachée sous la: One spring I hid under Lyra's cloak, at the bottom of her boat, to go and see the humans. I sneezed right in the middle of the mist. Atchoo! Lyra turned back. I sulked for a whole day, that's my record. Next time I'll bring a hanky.
textes.Un prix ? C'est déjà un prix. Le fer coû: A discount? That IS the discount. Iron costs, charcoal costs, Clou costs. No.
textes.Un prix honnête, Jos ! Pour un sabre his: An honest price, Jos! For a historic sabre.
textes.Un problème ? Une catastrophe ! Marcel a: A problem? A catastrophe! Marcel played like a beginner and the jack shot off towards the fountain. No way to find it. No jack, no pétanque. No pétanque, no life.
textes.Un professeur ! Qui nous cherche ! Par l: A professor! Looking for us! By the tides… A colleague. An archivist from up there. I'll write to him. Tell me, how does one send a scroll upwards? Do you let go of it, and it floats?
textes.Un programme pour que mon frigo me dise: A program so my fridge says hello to me… Cheap… Hm.
textes.Un ptéranodon (Grand-Bec) ! Il tourne au: A pteranodon (Big-Beak)! It circles above you, screeches… then dives. Roll aside! It climbs back slowly, very low: that's your moment to strike.
textes.Un punch coco à la paillote: A coconut punch at the beach hut
textes.Un punch que tout l'archipel viendrait b: A punch the whole archipelago would come to drink at the Perroquet: the dwarves with their beards in the glass, the elves dipping their lips in it, the folk from under the sea, if there are any. A punch that everyone would agree on.
A punch. Without a ladle in it.
textes.Un rayon de miel trouvé dans un arbre cr: A honeycomb found in a hollow tree. Restores two hearts.
A register in order for a whole season. Not one line crossed out, not one boat without a name. I don't believe it, but you asked me for a dream.
textes.Un ressort tout brillant, tombé d'un rob: A shiny spring that fell off one of Lisse's robots. It goes "boing" when you let go of it. Ferraille puts them in her sculptures; Cradoc in his shoes.
textes.Un rhum de la Balafre au comptoir: A Balafre dark tonic at the counter
textes.Un robot ! Il fait une révérence, perd u: A robot! He bows, drops a bolt, picks it up, and bows again.
A robot! Shall I bite it? I'M BITING IT.
textes.Un robot déménageur de Lisse & Fils ! Tr: A Lisse & Fils mover robot! Very polite… and very heavy. When it raises its pincers, it's going to shove you: step aside, then strike. It falls apart into bolts and springs.
textes.Un robot soudeur ! Son arc bleu ne porte: A welder robot! Its blue arc doesn't reach far: stay out of range when the sparks fly, then strike while it cools down.
textes.Un rocher. Un vrai. Il a l'air un peu ve: A rock. A real one. It looks a little offended that someone lifted it.
textes.Un roi a beaucoup à dire, Ori !: A king has a lot to say, Ori!
textes.Un ronceux ! Ce paquet de ronces marche: A bramblekin! This bundle of brambles walks toward you and raises its thorny arms before striking: parry (F) or back off, then cut it to pieces.
textes.Un rouage ? Pour l'horloge ? … Bon. Appo: A cog? For the clock? … Fine. Bring me two logs to heat the forge, and three stones for the mould. I'll do the rest.
textes.Un rouage neuf forgé par Hector pour l'h: A new cogwheel forged by Hector for the town hall clock. It shines like a gold coin.
A cog has broken in the mechanism. Hector, the armourer, could forge a new one. But he always says he has no time. Would you mind talking to him?
textes.Un rouleau de toile épaisse, tissée serr: A roll of thick, tightly woven canvas that smells of salt and hemp. For ships' sails… and the wings of flying machines.
textes.Un rubis tout neuf, Orsik ! Combien ?: A brand-new ruby, Orsik! How much?
textes.Un rubis… Il brille comme ma forge un so: A ruby… It glows like my forge on a winter evening. {prix} coins, and I won't ask where it came from.
textes.Un sablé en forme d'engrenage, au beurre: A gear-shaped shortbread, with butter and cinnamon. The teeth are crunchy. Restores two hearts.
textes.Un sac de facteur qui irait partout. Le: A postbag that could go anywhere. The village, the jungle, the elves, the dwarves, the flying island, and under the sea, with a waterproof satchel. I'd knock on every door in the archipelago.
textes.Un sac de toile plein de chaînes, de péd: A canvas bag full of chains, pedals, spokes, brake pads, and a bell shaped like a rat. Ferraille had hidden them for Rustine.
textes.Un sceau de pierre barré de chaînes de b: A stone seal barred with bronze chains. Behind it, an icy breath… You would need the key of the Ancients.
textes.Un second saut en plein vol (Espace, ou: A second jump in mid-air (Space, or A in VR, a second time in the air).
textes.Un secret ! Bravo. Plus on est nombreux: A secret! Well done. The more people keep it, the faster it flies away.
textes.Un secret ! Ooooh ! J'adore les secrets: A secret! Ooooh! I love secrets! I'll keep it, promise, cross my heart, on my mooncake. Nobody will know. Shh!
textes.Un secret ! Vous me torturez. Bon. J'écr: A secret! You're torturing me. All right. I'll write “terra incognita” in the corner. That's what the old cartographers wrote when they didn't know. It suits you very well.
textes.Un secret : le coffre de paie de la Moue: A secret: the Seagull's pay chest was made of ironwood, bound with copper. If your shovel hits metal, call me. We'll split it. Sixty-forty. My way.
textes.Un secret de cartographe : les jarres de: A cartographer's secret: the jars in your village put themselves back together. Nobody knows why. Me neither. But I pretend I do.
textes.Un secret de cartographe : sur ma carte,: A cartographer's secret: on my map, I'd marked the Seagull's pay chest. On the sea side, about twenty paces from Octave's great kapok tree, between three flat stones. He lives right next to it and has never found it. He doesn't read my maps. Take a shovel.
textes.Un secret, puisque tu as l'air de savoir: A secret, since you look like you can keep quiet. A hundred years ago, I carried Églantine's letter to the queen. On the way, I ran into Ventaile, and I wanted my rematch. Three days of racing. When the letter arrived, the brambles were already closing everything off. Since then, I fly fast. I'm catching up three days. I never manage.
textes.Un secret, {surnom}, et tu le gardes. Si: A secret, {surnom}, and you keep it. Sigrun, my little apprentice: I tell everyone I don't know her. Every spring, she sends me a barrel with no name. I taste it alone, door shut. It's better than mine. There. I'm so proud of her I could cry, and I don't know how to tell her.
textes.Un secret, {surnom}. Au fond du bassin,: A secret, {surnom}. At the bottom of the basin, there's an old boat everyone thinks is rotten. I've been caulking it at night for two years, plank by plank. For Nolwenn. I know she wants to leave, I've always known. The day she leaves, I want her to leave in a boat that doesn't take on water. That's all I know how to do.
textes.Un secret, {surnom}. La nuit, quand Bori: A secret, {surnom}. At night, while Borin sleeps, I light the little forge and make a spearhead for Kalda. It's a bit crooked. Very crooked, actually. I've redone it seven times. I've never given it to her. I'm scared she'll laugh. Or worse: that she'll use it.
textes.Un secret, {surnom}. Le jour où j'ai ouv: A secret, {surnom}. The day I opened Marie-Jeanne, she was still loaded. Two hundred years of powder, dry as sand. I was about to light my first fire in there. It was Tobias who sniffed, who stopped my hand, who drowned the lot in a bucket, and who never said a word about it. So when he complains about the noise, I hit softer. A bit.
textes.Un secret, {surnom}. Les corbeaux, je ne: A secret, {surnom}. I only half understand the crows. The other half, I make up. One day, to save a goat that had eaten the king's cloak, I translated a message from Croâ: “The king is the handsomest of dwarves.” Croâ had said nothing of the sort. Thorgal had it carved above the throne.
textes.Un secret, {surnom}. Les yeux de mon gra: A secret, {surnom}. My great-uncle's eyes are failing. He reads the runes with his fingertips when he thinks nobody's watching. So every evening, I read him the others out loud, “for practice”. I get the easiest ones wrong on purpose, so he can correct me. He must never know.
textes.Un septième bleu ! Je l'ajoute à la lége: A seventh blue! I'll add it to the key.
textes.Un serre-tête avec deux oreilles de rena: A headband with two red felt fox ears with black tips. A gift from Mère-Lune: in Ramure, they take you for one of their own.
Just one? There are five missing, Titou.
textes.Un seul, matelot. Gaston, note l'heure !: Just one, sailor. Gaston, write down the time!
textes.Un seul. Et cinq minutes de conversation: Just one. And five minutes of conversation.
textes.Un sifflet qui ne fait aucun bruit. L'in: A whistle that makes no sound at all. The inventor insists it's perfect for calling fish.
textes.Un signe ! Oui ! Mais lequel ? Elle a so: A sign! Yes! But which one? She smiled this morning. She sighed yesterday. She closed her window the day before. Those are all signs. But of what?
textes.Un slime ! Une petite gelée qui rebondit: A slime! A little jelly that bounces. When it squashes down flat, it's about to jump on you: step aside, then strike. The blue and pink ones are tougher.
textes.Un soir d'hiver, on est restées près du: One winter evening, we stayed by the fire, she and I, from nightfall till midnight. She said: “Cold.” I said: “Yes.” She said: “Good.” Three words in all. On her way to bed, she hugged me, very quickly, without looking at me. It's one of my loveliest evenings.
textes.Un soir d'hiver, un seul client au Perro: One winter evening, just one customer at the Perroquet, a sailor crying into his glass. Django played for him. Two hours, without stopping. The sailor left smiling. And Django always puts his hat at the edge of the stage, like his grandfather. I fill it on the sly, at closing time. He doesn't know. Well, I think he doesn't.
textes.Un soir d'hiver. Le feu. Brume et moi. D: A winter evening. The fire. Brume and me. From nightfall to midnight. … I said: “Cold.” She said: “Yes.” I said: “Good.” … Three words. It was a lovely evening. One of the best.
textes.Un soir de brouillard, je suis rentré à: One foggy night, I came home at three in the morning following his lantern. Grégoire was at the bow, all alone, stiff as a mast. I shouted to him: “How many ships have you counted?” He said: “One. Yours. It was late.” And he went to bed without saying goodnight.
textes.Un soir de brouille, Paulo a posé entre: One evening when we'd fallen out, Paulo set a single slice of tiramisu between Léa and me, with two spoons, and walked off whistling. We didn't touch it. The tiramisu looked at us all evening. At the end, Paulo took it away with a sigh: “Not even my tiramisu can do it.”
textes.Un soir de brume épaisse, on a gratté à: One evening of thick mist, something scratched at my door. A little she-wolf of eight, soaked to the ears: she had followed my tracks from the big pond, all alone. I gave her a blanket and a lesson: “A track is a sentence.” She fell asleep repeating it. The next day she was my pupil.
textes.Un soir de fête, une terrasse qui débord: A festival evening, the terrace spilling out all the way to the fountain. Django playing, the clock striking, and everyone ordering at once.
textes.Un soir où Léa regardait la mer, Paulo s: One evening while Léa was looking at the sea, Paulo leaned over to me: “The day you take her hand with your ring on your finger, I sing. At your table. In Italian. Very loud.” He chose the song that night, one of his nonna's, and rehearsed it in the kitchen all week. The whole quay heard it. Léa pretended not to smile.
textes.Un soir où le Zéphyr débarquait douze vo: One evening when the Zéphyr landed twelve travellers, Salomé planted herself at the breach with a sign: “Seaweed beds, two coins, no risk of falling”. She got eight, I got four. The next day, her eight came begging me for a hammock, covered in sea fleas. I charged them double. I'm not proud of it. Well, a bit.
textes.Un soir où mon four boudait, Lyra lui a: One evening when my oven was sulking, Lyra sang it a bark lullaby. The bread rose. Pure chance, obviously. But ever since, when the oven's in a mood, I go and fetch Lyra. Also by chance.
textes.Un soir où son four boudait, je lui ai c: One evening when her oven was sulking, I sang it a bark lullaby. The bread rose. Sylwen swears it was luck. And yet, ever since, she comes to fetch me every time her oven is in a mood.
textes.Un soir, Bourru était enrhumé ; il est r: One evening Bourru had a cold; he stayed home with honey and one of Pivoine's teas. Pépin drummed alone. And me… I couldn't find the step. Not once. I stumbled twice in front of the whole Circle. The next day his drum came back, and so did my feet. Grelot went “hrmm” for a week.
textes.Un soir, Caelan est entré dans la boutiq: One evening, Caelan came into the shop clutching his chest: “Aëlwen, I'm dying.” I examined him for an hour. Ilyria had said hello to him. Just hello. I gave him a camomile and the bill. He wanted to pay in song. I refused the song.
textes.Un soir, Fanny a fait un grand geste. Ya: One evening, Fanny made a big gesture. Yaya landed in my arms. Just like that. All of a sudden. I said: “… You okay?” She said yes. I didn't let go right away. Three seconds. Maybe four. The whole dance floor saw. Nobody talks about it. … Good.
textes.Un soir, Hugo et Léa ont dîné chez moi s: One evening, Hugo and Léa had dinner here without saying a word to each other. He was looking at his finger, she was looking at the sea. I served them a single slice of tiramisu with two spoons. They each ate their half, sitting very straight, without touching. Never seen such a sad tiramisu. There was a mystery, I could feel it.
textes.Un soir, Lola a écrit sur l'ardoise : «: One evening, Lola wrote on the chalkboard: “Sweethearts' Punch”. I didn't even know we had one. She'd doubled the recipe: twice the coconut, twice the sugar. Lucas drank three. He went home singing, the big shy lump. I didn't say a thing. I left the line on the board. It's still there.
textes.Un soir, Lucas a joué sa casquette. Il l: One evening, Lucas bet his cap. He lost it, of course: he had three aces in his hand and his eyes on Lola. I kept it for a week. Then I gave it back to him “on rental”: one coffee a week. He's still paying. To make it up to him, I slip him a painted shell now and then. We've never done the sums.
textes.Un soir, Lucas est entré pendant que je: One evening, Lucas came in just as I was bringing Django his punch. Django saw and slowed his waltz down. So much that I had to cross the Perroquet in slow motion, in time with the music, with my tray, like in a dream. The whole room was watching me. Lucas too. I've never walked so slowly in my life.
textes.Un soir, Lulu est revenue de chez ses fé: One night, Lulu came back from her fairies with golden pollen on her cheeks. She climbed onto the stage and whispered: “Softer, they're sleeping.” I played the calmest set of my life, all night. Tchoum fell asleep standing up. The next day, Lulu thanked me on behalf of the queen.
textes.Un soir, Marley a glissé une banane dans: One evening, Marley slipped a banana into my basket, “so your boss can taste it”. During the crossing, I sat on it without seeing it. The next day's batch had a faint taste of banana, who knows how. Margaux looked at me for a long time. I said it was an experiment. We sold them. I never confessed to Marley.
textes.Un soir, Pépin a tapé si fort, au moment: One evening Pépin drummed so hard, just as the moon was lifted out of the pond, that the skin of his drum burst. Boom… pfft. Nothing more. I finished the dance to the big drum alone. Slowly. Oh… it was the loveliest evening of the year. Pépin doesn't understand why I said that. I won't explain.
textes.Un soir, Pépin était enroué. Plus de voi: One evening, Pépin was hoarse. No voice. No pep. He left his drum. I played alone. Slowly. The whole Circle danced in slow motion. Even Gland. Even Mère-Lune, under her blanket. Good. Very good. Pépin says: longest evening of the year. Hrmm. Same thing.
textes.Un soir, Roux est monté à la cime avec s: One evening, Roux came up to the treetop with his flute, “to help me count”. He played a slow tune, with the squirrel note in the middle, and I listened. I forgot to count. When he left, I didn't know if I was at twelve or thirteen. Since that evening, it's twelve or thirteen. It was very beautiful. That's exactly the problem.
textes.Un soir, Sofia m'a demandé un collier qu: One evening Sofia asked me for a necklace we'd never sell. With a single pearl, found near the golden point, to the south-west. She wouldn't say why that pearl mattered. I asked her only one question: “Blue thread or gold thread?” Blue. I ask Sofia just one question a day. That's our rule.
textes.Un soir, Tchoum cherchait depuis une heu: One night, Tchoum had spent an hour trying to work out why Raoul was crackling. Me: “It's the sea.” Bastien, passing by: “It's a crab.” Tchoum opened the speaker: a crab, making itself at home. Tchoum still hasn't forgiven Bastien for being right before him. And me, ever since, I check. While pretending not to check.
textes.Un soir, absorbée par mon roman, j'ai te: One evening, absorbed in my novel, I held the newspaper upside down for an hour. Gisèle walked by, turned it the right way up without stopping, and said out loud: “The weather reads better the right way up, Colette.” Nobody understood. I did. I blushed behind the weather forecast.
textes.Un soir, au Cercle, il y avait un gâteau: One evening, at the Circle, there was a mooncake all alone on a bench. Nobody around. I tasted it. To check. Mrrr… It was… good. Very good, even. I finished it. If you tell Trèfle, {surnom}, I'll say you're lying. And I'll charge you double for your skewers.
textes.Un soir, avec Bernard, on a calculé. Tre: One evening, Bernard and I did the maths. Thirty years on the round, twenty kilometres a day, six days a week… We worked it out on the back of one of Gisèle's receipts. Result: I walked three times round the whole archipelago. Bernard checked twice. He said: “No stopwatch, doesn't count.” It counts.
textes.Un soir, c'est grand-père qui s'est endo: One evening Grandpa fell asleep before me! Right in the middle of the story, snore. So I finished it myself, for the other little ones. With a dragon in it. A huge one. They loved it. Grandpa woke up and asked “Where was I?”, and everyone shouted: “THE DRAGON!”
textes.Un soir, depuis la cime, dans le noir, j: One evening, from the treetop, in the dark, I saw Mochi way down at the Circle. I called out: “You've got cake on your snout!” She jumped so hard her ears shot up. She thinks I can see in the dark. I can a little, it's true. But mostly, Mochi always has cake on her snout.
textes.Un soir, elle a mordu dans mon gâteau, e: One evening, she bit into my cake, closed her eyes, and opened her mouth as if to say “that's it”. I dropped the plate. And… she coughed. A crumb went down the wrong way. I patted her back, gave her water, and when she could talk, she said: “Almost.” I nearly cried. Or laughed. Both, I think.
textes.Un soir, elle a regardé par ma fenêtre p: One evening she looked through my window while I was looking at my shards. Next day, the whole village knew I was “smiling”. I wasn't smiling. I had a cramp. In my mouth. It happens.
textes.Un soir, elle m'a apporté sept gâteaux d: One evening she brought me seven different cakes. Seven! More honey, less honey, baked longer, a pinch of who-knows-what… I tasted all seven, very seriously, and said “almost” seven times. The next day I had a tummy ache, and she already had an eighth attempt.
textes.Un soir, en cueillant mes herbes dans le: One evening, picking my herbs in the hotel garden, I heard sniffling behind the thyme. It was the young bride from room seven, sitting on the ground. She asked me if I had anything for husbands. I said I had lime blossom. It's a start.
textes.Un soir, en essuyant les verres derrière: One evening, drying glasses behind the bar, she started singing the chorus with me. Very softly. She sings well, she doesn't know it. Lucas looked up from his cards. She stopped dead and dropped a glass. I carried on with the chorus alone, louder, to cover for her. That's what neighbours are for.
textes.Un soir, en plein morceau, elle a levé l: One evening, in the middle of a song, she raised her hand: “Play the low note again, please. For the colour.” For the colour! I played it again. She closed her eyes and said: “Violet.” The whole room turned to look at me. I played it again. Ten times. I don't know why I obeyed.
textes.Un soir, en revenant de là-haut, j'ai de: One night, coming back from up there, I asked Mistral to play more softly, because the fairies were asleep. He didn't ask a single question. He played the gentlest set in the world, all night long. Tchoum fell asleep standing up. The fairies slept well — the queen told me. I'll never forget it.
textes.Un soir, il a déposé le filet devant la: One evening, he left the net at the lighthouse door. Folded nice and square, my brother's lead weights inside. I found it on my way down, at dawn. I carried it to his door, on the quay, and went back up. Without a word. He thought that was what I wanted. That's not how you give back a net.
textes.Un soir, il a parlé de la grande mare, e: One evening he talked about the big pond, and I asked questions about the dragon. How many teeth, how many legs, does it like hazelnuts, can it swim upside down… Forty-seven questions! Pomme-de-Pin counted. Grandpa said: “Twice upon a time…” and started another story. I think he knows too much.
textes.Un soir, il a parlé si longtemps que le: One evening, he talked so long the forge fire went out. All by itself. He didn't notice. He was telling me about his race, bend by bend. Ten arches. Twice. I went to bed. He finished the story to the anvil.
textes.Un soir, il faisait tout noir, et monsie: One evening it was all dark, and Mister Hulotte, way up at the treetop, said to me: “Mochi, you've got cake on your snout.” IN THE DARK! From way up there! I wiped it, but it was too late, Mummy had heard. Since then I wash my snout before I go under the Post Office. Just in case.
textes.Un soir, j'ai décidé d'en finir : je lui: One evening, I decided to settle it once and for all: I brought her seven different cakes. More honey, less honey, baked longer, more chestnut, a pinch of salt… She tasted all seven, very seriously, and said “almost” seven times. Seven almosts! The next day, Pivoine took her up a tea for her tummy. I felt very guilty.
textes.Un soir, j'ai fredonné à Mistral un chan: One evening I hummed Mistral a whale song I'd heard while diving, to make him happy. He spent three nights recreating it with his machines. When he played it for me, it was almost right. I said “almost”. He looked so disappointed I nearly said “exactly”. He's still working on it.
textes.Un soir, j'ai laissé une couronne de feu: One evening, I left a crown of golden leaves on his big black speakers, to thank him. He wore it until dawn. He tells everyone he has a secret admirer. That's not untrue.
textes.Un soir, j'ai mordu dans son gâteau, et: One evening I bit into her cake, and for a second I saw Luzerne's kitchen again. I opened my mouth to say “that's it”… and coughed instead. Trèfle patted my back, all pale. It wasn't quite it yet. It was already something else. I didn't know which of the two to tell her.
textes.Un soir, j'ai oublié des coquilles au pi: One evening, I left some shells at the foot of the tower, in the crystal's warmth. By morning, they were soft as wax. I blew into them through a hollow reed, and a bubble of mother-of-pearl was born, round, perfect. I ran to show Coralin. He said: “That's cheating.” I left that very evening.
textes.Un soir, j'ai parlé de pêche à Tchoum pe: One evening I talked fishing with Tchoum for two hours. Tides, bait, the moon. He said three words, one of which was “Right.” At the end, he shook my hand. I think it was the best conversation of my life. As for him, I think he's still tired from it.
textes.Un soir, j'ai parlé du dragon de la gran: One evening, I mentioned the dragon of the big pond. One sentence, just one. Gland asked me forty-seven questions. How many teeth? Does it eat hazelnuts? Does it have a mummy? Where does it sleep in winter? After the forty-seventh, I had to make up a dragon story that answered the questions. He asked ten more.
textes.Un soir, j'ai plié le filet du père Vass: One evening, I folded old Vasseur's net, nice and square, with Marius's lead weights inside, and I left it outside the lighthouse door. I told myself: there, it's given back. The next morning, it was outside my own door. Folded exactly the same. Not a word. I didn't understand. I still don't.
textes.Un soir, j'ai raté un croquis : sa guita: One evening, I botched a sketch: his guitar looked like a pear. A real pear, stalk and all. Toni found it so funny he pinned it up behind the bar. Django now plays every night under a pear. He hasn't forgiven me.
textes.Un soir, j'ai recompté les hamacs : tren: One evening, I recounted the hammocks: thirty-one. I searched the lower deck until midnight, questioned the guests, suspected Ewen. The next day, there were thirty-two again. My aunt said: “You must have miscounted.” I'd counted right. I know it was her. She knows I know. We don't talk about it.
textes.Un soir, j'ai sorti mon chronomètre de C: One evening, I took out my Cliquetis stopwatch right in the middle of the party: “One boom every two seconds, Bourru! It's measured!” He looked at me. He played one boom. He waited. After four seconds, he said: “Hrmm.” I wrote it down: one hrmm every four seconds. That's a rhythm, at least.
textes.Un soir, j'ai trouvé l'Amirale seule à l: One evening, I found the Admiral alone in the harbour office, bent over my map, a candle in her hand. She was tracing the route of my crossing with her finger. She didn't hear me come in. She said very quietly: “He went everywhere, the idiot.” I slipped out without a sound. I think it was a compliment.
textes.Un soir, j'ai voulu danser avec elle, po: One evening, I wanted to dance with her, to see what it's like on the other side of the drum. I trod on her hooves. Twice. The second time was in rhythm, at least. She laughed, kindly. Since then, I stay behind my drum: it's better for everyone, especially her hooves.
textes.Un soir, j'ai écrit : « Rien à signaler,: One evening I wrote: “Nothing to report, except one very large sunfish.” Abyssos turned up at the Gate at midnight, out of breath, with three blank scrolls. The sunfish had gone. He made me describe it for two hours. Since then I only write “Nothing to report”. It's more restful for everyone.
textes.Un soir, j'avais dessiné la cité telle q: One evening, I had drawn the city as I imagine it: a dome, towers, and in the middle the great crystal. I slipped it under my pillow, like a child. The next day, Pauline made my bed. The day after, on the café terrace, the mayor asked me if my crystal was “pretty in real life”. I thought I would die.
One evening, I had a cold. Stuffed nose. Pépin drummed alone. Lilas danced. Badly. Couldn't find the step. Tripped twice. Next day, I came back. She danced like the moon. Hrmm. Pépin says it's a coincidence. Hrmm.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai surprise derrière la be: One evening, I caught her behind the sheepfold, deep in conversation with Croâ. She was saying: “No, not tonight.” He said: “Croak.” She answered: “I know, but no.” At midnight, the king sent for cheese. She'd refused in advance! I heard it, I'm telling you!
textes.Un soir, je l'ai trouvée cachée derrière: One evening I found her hiding behind my workbench. She'd heard me saying good night to the sculptures. I expected the whole city to laugh at me. The next day, there was a little piece of seaweed laid on every sculpture, like a blanket. I left them there.
textes.Un soir, je lisais tout haut l'histoire: One evening, I was reading the history of the surface out loud to the shelves, as usual: nobody else listens to me. At the end, someone sneezed behind the wheat scroll. It was Ondine, who'd been asleep there since the afternoon. She said: “Again.” Nobody had ever said “again” to me.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai demandé comment on fa: One evening, I asked her how you let someone know you like them, without saying it. She answered: “Like goats do. You climb all over them.” I tried a stone instead. It didn't work: he threw it in the fire. Hilda laughed all the way to the goat pen.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai fait mon rapport : «: One evening I gave him my report: “Forest quiet.” He said: “Too quiet?” I said: “No, just quiet.” He went to check for himself. He came back at dawn, covered in dew, and said: “Quiet.” Then he checked my arrows. All of them. Again.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai montré mon croquis de: One evening, I showed him my sketch of the village coast, drawn from three passengers' accounts. He put his big finger on the beach and slid it north: “Higher. And the hermit's hut, there.” Then he tapped a rock: “That one, I hit once.” I corrected it. I drew the rock bigger.
textes.Un soir, je me suis cachée derrière son: One evening I hid behind his workbench. I heard him say good night to all his sculptures, one by one, even the fish-urchin. His voice was all soft, not grumpy at all. The next day I put a little piece of seaweed on each one, like a blanket. He didn't say anything. He left them there.
textes.Un soir, je me suis endormie sur mon trô: One evening, I fell asleep on my throne. Noisette took the chance to plant a seed in my crown, “just to see”. By morning, a little shoot was standing between two of its flowers. The fairies didn't dare tell me. I kept it: it has two leaves now. Noisette comes to water it in secret. Very badly in secret.
textes.Un soir, je suis monté à la cime avec ma: One evening, I went up to the treetop with my flute, to help him count: “Music keeps the rhythm!” He was at four thousand two hundred and twelve. I played the squirrel note. He said “thirteen?”, then “twelve?”, then he shut his notebook. Since then, it's been twelve or thirteen. He's never asked me back. But he hasn't chased me off either.
textes.Un soir, la reine a planté une fleur en: One evening, the queen secretly planted a flower, to see whether I'd notice. I found it before dawn. I went to tell her: “Four thousand three hundred and two, Your Majesty. Yesterday it was four thousand three hundred and one.” She laughed. I named the flower Oriane. It gets the first drop every morning.
textes.Un soir, la reine s'est endormie sur son: One evening, the queen fell asleep on her throne. I planted a seed in her crown, just to see. By morning, there was a little shoot between two of its flowers! Nobody dared tell her. She kept it. It has two leaves now. I'm the one who waters it, in secret.
textes.Un soir, le Lord m'a demandé un verre d': One evening, the Lord asked me for a glass of water. A glass of water! And he put a gold coin on the counter, with the profile of a great-grandfather with a big nose. I said: “Milord, that's worth a hundred glasses of water.” He said: “Keep the rest.” So I opened a tab just for him. I owe him ninety-nine glasses of water. I don't know how you settle that.
textes.Un soir, le plancher de ma cuisine s'est: One evening, my kitchen floor lifted up and a head popped out, right under my table. I grabbed whatever was handy: a bellows. Bonk. It was Grimli. I patched him up and made him soup. A year later, we were married. We kept the hole. It's the cellar trapdoor.
textes.Un soir, on a fait le calcul sur une nap: One evening, we did the sums on a paper tablecloth at the Perroquet. Thirty years of rounds, the hill, the stairs, the dogs… with the mailbag. Result: Marcel has walked round the archipelago three times. Me, with my forty marathons, twice. He kept the tablecloth. He says he's going to frame it.
textes.Un soir, penchés sur ses cartes, il m'a: One evening, bent over his charts, he said to me: “I can't swim.” I said: “I get seasick.” We looked at each other. I burst out laughing: “The two greatest explorers in the archipelago… who've never left!” He laughed too. Then he pencilled a cross to the south-west of the village. We believe in it.
textes.Un soir, pendant qu'il lisait ses runes: One evening, while he was reading his runes by the fire, I tasted his famous moon water. Yuck! Cold pebbles and dust. He saw me. He said nothing. He just jotted something in his journal. Ever since, I've been wondering what he wrote. It's eating at me. It's eating at me a lot.
textes.Un soir, pendant un gros morceau de Mist: One night, during a big Mistral track, my test hut collapsed. The next day, Clou turned up with a bag of nails, from Octave. Eleven nails. The bag said twenty. I rebuilt it with them. It still leans, but it holds: that's where Zoé sleeps. I've never dared ask where the other nine went.
textes.Un soir, pour la taquiner, j'ai planté u: One evening, to tease her, I secretly planted one extra flower in the clearing. The next day, before the sun was even up, Perlée came to find me: “Four thousand three hundred and two, Your Majesty. Yesterday it was four thousand three hundred and one.” She named the flower “Oriane”. She still gives it the first drop.
textes.Un soir, sur l'ardoise du Perroquet, il: One evening, on the Perroquet's slate, it said: “Dish of the day: for Lucas, on the house.” Toni said it was a mistake. Lola wiped it off really fast with her sleeve. But I'd read it. I ate the dish of the day. I paid anyway. I don't know why. I was all flustered.
textes.Un soir, sur la plage, elle m'a pris l'a: One evening, on the beach, she took the camera out of my hands and put it away in her bag. “Look.” The sun went down. My hands kept reaching for the shutter button on their own. Ten minutes of looking, doing nothing. She asked: “Well?” I said: “A bit overexposed.” She pinched my arm.
textes.Un soir, sur le ponton, j'ai failli tout: One evening, on the pontoon, I nearly told Lucie everything, about the sail. I opened my mouth. She looked at me and said: “Not now. When you're sure.” Then she dived in. She always knows when someone's carrying a secret. She never asks which one.
textes.Un soir, une de mes lanternes a dérivé j: One evening, one of my lanterns drifted right up to her feet while she was dancing. She picked it up, raised it towards the crystal, and danced with it until the tide turned. I was hiding behind a column. I forgot to breathe. For a glassblower, that's serious.
textes.Un soir, une lanterne de nacre est arriv: One evening, a mother-of-pearl lantern landed at my feet while I was dancing. I held it up to the crystal and danced with it till the end of the tide. Behind a column, someone gasped, very loudly. I didn't need to turn round. There's only one blower in the dome.
textes.Un soir, à La Rose des Vents, penchés su: One evening, at the Compass Rose, bent over the big seabed chart, Félix took a pencil and drew a little cross south-west of the village. He said: “There.” I said: “There.” We stayed a minute without speaking, looking at the cross. Then he rubbed it out, to be safe. You can still see the mark. We still look at it.
textes.Un sorbet de fruits rouges et de cannell: A sorbet of red berries and fire cinnamon, served in an obsidian cup: hot inside, ice-cold outside (or the other way round, nobody agrees). Restores one and a half hearts.
textes.Un souci à trois têtes… non, à trois chi: A three-headed problem… no, a three-dog problem. Wild hellhounds, on the lava field, east of the volcano. They're not bad, just ill-mannered. They spit fire at passersby. My guard is busy guarding. Will you take care of it? When the jaws glow red, step aside.
textes.Un souffle de mécanique : il remet en ma: A mechanical breath: it restarts old mechanisms from afar and paralyses automatons.
textes.Un souffle glacé : les ennemis se figent: An icy breath: enemies freeze; on a lake, a path of ice.
textes.Un souffle glacé sort de l'antre. Au bou: An icy breath comes out of the lair. At the end of the corridor, an immense flooded cavern… Get ready.
textes.Un soufflet sans trou. Un seul. Et un ma: A bellows without holes. Just one. And a husband who sleeps at home, even if I snore. Especially if I snore.
textes.Un souvenir… Hé hé, bonne réponse. Les s: A memory… Heh heh, good answer. Memories can't be swapped: they're for telling. Ask Tilleul. But not too late in the evening.
textes.Un squelette de pirate ! Il lève son cou: A pirate skeleton! It raises its cutlass before striking: parry (F) or roll (Ctrl), then strike. Bones break, you know.
textes.Un tableau pour la semaine, mademoiselle: A painting for the week, mademoiselle?
textes.Un tanuki entre au Marché aux trocs avec: A tanuki walks into the Barter Market with a leaf on its head. Bedaine says: “I'll swap you two leaves for it!” The tanuki agrees. It was Bedaine.
textes.Un temple, sous l'île… Si tu croises des: A temple, under the island… If you run into critters down there, don't come crying to me: buy my sword first.
textes.Un thé bleu nuit où flottent des paillet: A midnight-blue tea with flecks of gold floating in it, served at the Nebula Café. It tastes of mint, rain and something else that no one can quite name. Restores one heart.
textes.Un thé à la menthe sur la terrasse: A mint tea on the terrace
textes.Un tiers de parchemin jauni, déchiré en: A third of a yellowed parchment, torn in a zigzag, covered in dotted lines, arrows and stains: a piece of Barbe-Sanglante's map.
textes.Un tireur ! Comme Marcel… Bon, tu n'y es: A shooter! Like Marcel… Well, it's not your fault. Shooting is fine when it hits. The rest of the time, it's just noise. Come on, I'll teach you to point, that'll cure you.
textes.Un touriste de l'espace ? Vert ? Gélatin: A space tourist? Green? Jelly-like? (She bursts out laughing.) He can come in for a drink, he won't be the weirdest one in the room! Right, the photo. Hold on. (She spits in her hand, smooths her hair, strikes a pose with her fists on her hips.) Like this. With the Crâne Fendu behind me. So everyone can see it's a respectable tavern. Click! … I look small in there. And all shiny. I like it. Tell your jelly we pay BEFORE we brawl.
textes.Un touriste de l'espace qui a peur de de: A space tourist who's afraid to come down? (She puts down her knitting.) Tell him that here in Boucan, everyone is welcome. Punks, reformed robots, rats, dogs in bandanas… A green jelly was all we were missing. (She raises her fist, standing very straight, with a big smile.) Click! You tell him: “The door is open. It fell down in 1998, but it's open.”
textes.Un touriste demande à Fernand : « Il y a: A tourist asks Fernand: “Are there sharks here?” Fernand replies: “No, the dolphins ate them.” The tourist goes for a swim. Fernand adds: “We ate the dolphins.”
textes.Un tout petit peu ! Hm. Je ne veux pas s: A tiny bit! Hm. I don't want to know what. Yes, I do. No. I'll let it go this time. But I've got my eye on you. My left eye, the stricter one.
Just a tiny bit. Round the edges.
textes.Un tricorne de feutre noir galonné d'or,: A black felt tricorn trimmed with gold braid, a red feather stuck in the side: Barbe-Sanglante's own, which Old Silas kept for a hundred years for the heir to the treasure.
textes.Un tricératops (Corne-Sur-Nez) ! Quand i: A triceratops (Nose-Horn)! When it scratches the ground with its foot, it's going to CHARGE straight ahead: step aside… and if it hits a rock or a tree, it sees stars. Strike then!
textes.Un vendredi, j'ai remarqué que le timbre: One Friday, I noticed the stamp on my letter had a little heart drawn in the corner. Nadine said: “Oh? Pure chance.” The next week, another heart. And the week after. I told her to stop. She swore she couldn't help it, the stamps just came out like that. The stamps. Of course.
textes.Un vendredi, pour la faire taire, j'ai a: One Friday, to shut her up, I bought three sea bream. Rosalie shouted: “Three?! How many of you are there?” The whole fish shop turned round. I ate the third one on Saturday, alone, telling myself you're never smarter than a fishmonger.
textes.Un vent du large qui repousse les ennemi: A sea wind that pushes enemies back, flips shells over, turns sails and windmills.
textes.Un vent furieux tourbillonne autour de l: A furious wind swirls around the Citadel: Ventaile refuses to go near. Land on the Wind Perch, south of the island.
A furious wind swirls around the Citadel: you can't get near it. Land on the Wind Field, south of the island.
textes.Un ver de terre, vexé d'avoir été dérang: An earthworm, offended at being disturbed. It leaves with a sigh (for a worm).
textes.Un verre de rhum de la Murène: A glass of La Murène dark tonic
textes.Un verrou de moins ! Regarde-le, il comm: One lock down! Look at it, it's starting to sweat.
textes.Un vieil ampli à lampes, lourd comme un: An old tube amp, heavy as a donkey, with knobs that go up to eleven. When you switch it on, it purrs. When Clou plays, it roars.
textes.Un vieux coffre cerclé de fer, fermé par: An old iron-bound chest, shut with a chain of bones. It won't give. On the lid, engraved: “To whoever carries my map. B.S.”
textes.Un vieux coquillage, apporté là par un o: An old seashell, brought here by a mischievous bird. This head looks at the sea, not the sky.
textes.Un vieux parchemin offert par Églantine,: An old parchment given by Églantine, the freed Bramble Queen. It shows the passage through the reefs and the ashes, to the west, all the way to the dwarves' volcanic island.
textes.Un vieux parchemin taché de rhum : une c: An old stained parchment: a coastline, dotted lines, a red cross. Captain Salazar Croc-de-Sel cares about it more than his wooden leg.
An old professor is looking for you.
textes.Un virus ? Dans MES programmes ? Impossi: A virus? In MY programs? Impossible! They're guaranteed. Guaranteed… something. (He looks away.) Go see little Glitch: she knows about… about things. Mornings and evenings, she hangs around near the Arcade Station; in the afternoon, in the arcade hall. Me, I have an appointment. Very far away. Right now.
textes.Un virus ? Dans MON programme ? (Il devi: A virus? In MY program? (He turns all red, then all purple, to match his hat.) Well. All right. Maybe. I bought it from a dealer even cheaper than me, and I hadn't tried it… I'm giving you your coins back, with an apology on top. And I make you a promise: from now on, Monsieur Fil will only sell verified programs! Verified by Glitch. She said yes. Well, she said “we'll see”. It's almost yes.
textes.Un visage de roi fait de centaines de pe: A king's face made of hundreds of little squares of jade, with eyes of mother-of-pearl and obsidian. The mask of the kings of Yaxché, kept deep in Xibalba. Its place is on the Altar of the Three Suns.
textes.Un visiteur ! D'où viens-tu ? Non, atten: A visitor! Where are you from? No, wait, let me guess… from the west, by sea, eh? Matthias, cartographer. I've been drawing this island for fifteen years and it still isn't finished.
textes.Un visiteur ! À inscrire ! Au registre !: A visitor! To be registered! In the register! (He opens an immense book, which falls on his foot.) Ahem ahem. According to article twelve, I write your name in lumen letters... There. According to article thirteen, you must now curtsy. No, not like that. Not like that either. According to article fourteen... Ah, there is no article fourteen. Well. You're registered. Congratulations. That was very protocolary.
A sailboat flies away very easily.
textes.Un vrai ! Les pieds, c'est la base : le: A real one! Feet are the foundation: the kick comes up through the sand and out through your knees. Stand in front of Raoul, the big speaker, and you'll get it.
textes.Un vrai ! Punch du héros pour le héros !: A real one! Hero's punch for the hero!
textes.Un vrai chapiteau sur la place du villag: A real big top on the village square, red and yellow, with benches for every kid on the island. And Yaya's cat in the front row. He'll pay in purrs.
textes.Un éboulement bloque la galerie. Au-delà: A rockfall blocks the gallery. Beyond it, you can hear water flowing… You'll have to find another way. (Work in progress!)
textes.Un éclat de cristal qui bat doucement, c: A shard of crystal that beats gently, like a heart. It is warm, and it sings a single, very pure note.
textes.Un éclat de glace bleue qui ne fond jama: A shard of blue ice that never melts, even in your hand, even in Pandémonia. It comes from the Cocytus, the frozen lake of the Ninth Circle.
textes.Un éclat de la grande lentille s'est dét: A shard of the great lens broke off during the storm. It fell into the sea, at the foot of the point, on the seaward side. Six metres down, maybe. I'm too old to dive. Without it, my lighthouse no longer lights the night.
textes.Un éclat rose et tiède, laissé par une a: A pink, warm shard, left behind by a crystal spider. Grommelot the sprite collects them; Mélisse buys them.
textes.Un écusson brodé : un rat à crête verte: An embroidered patch: a yelling green-crested rat, and "BILGE RATS" in red letters. Velours sews them herself, one by one, for the true fans.
textes.Un élixir doré qui pétille comme un ciel: A golden elixir that sparkles like a summer sky. It restores all your magic, and two hearts. Gustave won't say what he puts in it.
textes.Un élémentaire de magma ! Quand il gonfl: A magma elemental! When it swells up and glows red, it's going to leap at you: step aside, then strike while it cools.
textes.Un étal à Tazira, juste à côté de celui: A stall in Tazira, right next to Aïcha's, so we can steal each other's customers face to face. It would be wonderful. Every evening we'd both close up with less money and more stories.
textes.Un été, il n'a pas plu pendant deux mois: One summer, it didn't rain for two months. My plants were frying on the hill. So I carried water up, bucket by bucket, morning and evening. On the third day, Amélie, the herbalist, saw me go by and picked up a bucket, without a word. She came up with me all summer. My lavender survived, and so did her thyme. And I gained a friend.
textes.Un été, j'ai pisté vers l'ouest. Plus lo: One summer, I tracked westward. Further than ever. All the way to the foot of Stoneheart, in the centre of the island. There, the tracks of all four peoples arrive: boots, hooves, paws, wheels. All very old. Then nothing. I sat a whole night in front of that nothing. I understood that the world was bigger than Ramure. And that it had forgotten something.
textes.Un œil d'or et de lapis-lazuli, l'œil qu: An eye of gold and lapis lazuli, the eye the god Horus lost fighting Set and that Thoth healed: the sign of the light that always comes back. Brought back from the depths of the Pyramid of Ra. Its place is on the Altar of the Three Suns.
textes.Un œil de pierre… Les petits Moaïs du pl: A stone eye… The little Moai on the plateau might know who it belongs to. (The eldest, Granny Basalte, knows all the legends.)
textes.Un, deux, trois… Vas-y, je suis prêt !: One, two, three… Go on, I'm ready!
textes.Une Grande Course qui ferait le tour de: A Great Race that went all the way round the island! Then a wolf would win, for sure. I can feel it in my paws. And I'd put the cup right at the top of the watch post, right next to my uncle.
textes.Une Grande Course, elle est passée devan: One Great Race, she went past the jetty, in the lead, so fast the water shivered. I stood up. Me. I shouted her name. My rod went into the pond, with the line and the float. I never found it. The King must have it. He can keep it. It was a good day.
textes.Une Grande Lanterne éteinte, aussi haute: An unlit Great Lantern, as tall as a giant's street lamp. To light it, you'd need a flame from a living ember: Lumina, the lantern-keeper, keeps some in her lantern.
textes.Une Série Z… « Voix numéro zéro ». La to: A Z Series… “Voice number zero”. The city's very first android voice. Cargo kept it all this time. (He cleans it, blows on it, examines it through the lens of his monocle.) It works. I set Zéro up on my workbench, he was waiting. Click. There. Go and see him… I think he has something to tell you.
textes.Une VILLE ? Toute une ville ? Avec des m: A TOWN? A whole town? With houses and everything? Kiki says I'll make one too. Will you teach me? I'll give you my coconuts.
